intro.heading: Two grading systems, one Year 11: what makes this school's route unusual
paragraphs: Emirates International School Jumeirah is among the longest-established IB schools in the UAE, and it runs the continuum from the Primary Years Programme upward. What makes a search for an IB IGCSE tutor for Emirates International School Jumeirah students in Dubai different from a generic Dubai tutoring search is the overlap in the middle. The Middle Years Programme ends in Year 11. So does the IGCSE course. A student in that year can be judged by criterion descriptors marked internally and by an external examiner working to a published mark scheme, and the two reward different behaviour.

Confirm with the school which route your child's cohort takes, subject by subject. Dubai schools revise option blocks and entry patterns regularly, and the number of external subjects a year group sits is a decision the school makes on its own evidence. The head of secondary and the examinations officer are the authority there. What this page can tell you reliably is what each route demands once the decision is made, and how tuition should differ between them.

Criterion marking rewards the visible process. A Middle Years science task is marked against descriptors covering inquiry, knowledge, processing and reflection, and a student who reaches the right conclusion without showing the reasoning will score below a weaker student who shows it. External IGCSE marking rewards the opposite discipline: concise, complete answers in the command term's own language, with no reward for narrating the thinking. A student who is strong at one is frequently weak at the other, and that is the single most common thing families on this page ask us to fix.

The second thing that shows up repeatedly is the Diploma coursework load in Year 12. Each Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher against named criteria and moderated by the IB. Add Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay and a student is running six or seven pieces of long-form work against school-set internal deadlines that all sit earlier than the examination timetable. Tutoring that only addresses examination content misses most of where the marks are.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video, held at a Gulf Standard Time hour that fits a Dubai school day. In-home visiting is a service IB Gram runs only in India, not in the UAE, and this page says so rather than leaving it ambiguous. Every number below carries the name of whoever published it, and where a date could not be verified from the examining board itself, the page says that instead of guessing. That applies to IB examination dates in particular: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date for the Diploma appears anywhere on this page. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator, who works from the official timetable.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-emirates-intern.programmesIntro: Three assessment systems run at this school at once, and a Year 11 student may be inside two of them. Here is what each measures and what that implies for a Dubai family planning tuition.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, ending in Year 11
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by boundaries the IB publishes. Schools may enter candidates for on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to an IB certificate, with the Personal Project required alongside. There is no linear external paper in the Cambridge sense and no tiering.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route sits inside a market where UK curricula carry 37 per cent of private-school enrolment against roughly seven per cent on IB programmes. The consequence for a Jumeirah family is practical: a tutor who has taught criterion descriptors is scarcer locally than one who has taught GCSE papers, which is the main reason online matching widens the choice so much.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years ending in external written papers graded A* to G by Cambridge or 9 to 1 by Pearson. Cambridge syllabuses tier into Core and Extended in most subjects; Pearson Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher while the Pearson international sciences are single-tier. Practical skills are assessed in a written paper, not by coursework.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE grade set is the qualification the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency route counts for British-curriculum students: five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that five. Verify the current wording on the Ministry's own channel; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of attestation.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component, typically around a fifth of the grade, marked against named criteria and externally moderated. The score runs to 45 points including up to three from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is growing: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them running International Baccalaureate programmes, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More places does not mean more Higher Level specialists, which is why specialist supply remains the binding constraint in this city.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-emirates-intern.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Jumeirah families ask about most. Each description names the component that decides the grade, because the component is where tuition earns its money.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level runs three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent with the exploration at 20. Paper 3 carries two long structured investigations, and the first mark depends on reading an unfamiliar context correctly rather than on recall. Proof by induction and complex numbers in polar form are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The data-handling and modelling route, often the right choice for a student heading into business, design or the social sciences. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and statistical inference. Students chosen badly into this course are usually those who found Analysis and Approaches algebra hard rather than those who prefer context.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 at half the grade each. The content that reliably costs marks is composite and inverse function notation, histograms with unequal class widths, and column vectors. Core candidates cannot be awarded above grade C, so the tier decision is a grade-ceiling decision taken in Year 10.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0620 or 4CH1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic is the largest single source of lost marks at IGCSE Extended and returns as the quantitative spine of Diploma energetics and equilibrium. At Higher Level, organic mechanisms are marked on curly-arrow placement and intermediate charge, so a right product with a wrong mechanism scores partially.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0625 or 4PH1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 Extended runs a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper at 20. That practical paper tests graph scales, significant figures and conclusion wording, which do not improve by revising content and improve quickly with technique work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0610 or 4BI1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Accessible content, unforgiving marking. IGCSE Extended rewards exact command-term response, so a student who explains when asked to describe loses marks on knowledge they hold. The Diploma scientific investigation carries a fifth of the grade and is marked on research design and evaluation rather than on tidy data.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral asks for a ten-minute structured argument linking a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract. Wide readers still score poorly because this is argument, not discussion. IGCSE First Language 0500 rewards directed writing that holds register, which responds well to drilling.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment at 800 words each, and the diagram carries the marks. Students write careful prose around a diagram that does not show the effect described. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and templated, making it the fastest paper on which to add points.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school and streamed by first-language status, with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requiring that classes for Arab and non-Arab students are organised separately rather than combined. Support is reading fluency and script confidence, and it works best in short, frequent sessions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects against an internal prompt. Students lose marks by writing about the topic rather than about how knowledge in that area is justified. Sessions here are structural: finding the knowledge question inside the title before any writing begins.

sections.heading: eAssessment or IGCSE: the two ways a Year 11 here can be certificated
paragraphs: This is the decision that makes the school distinctive and it is poorly explained almost everywhere online. A Middle Years Programme student can be entered for IB on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, graded 1 to 7 against criteria, with the Personal Project sitting alongside. An IGCSE candidate sits external linear papers set and marked by Cambridge or Pearson. Some students do both in different subjects. The school decides the pattern, and it changes, so confirm your child's own entry list with the examinations officer rather than assuming.

The two routes reward different work and therefore different tuition. Criterion assessment is marked on the visible process, which means a student has to be taught to write their reasoning down even when they can see the answer. External papers are marked on the finished response in the command term's own language, which means a student has to be taught to stop narrating. A tutor who only knows one route will give advice that actively costs marks in the other, and this is not a hypothetical problem; it is the most common complaint that brings families to this page.

There is also a pacing difference. Criterion assessment is continuous, so a weak term shows up in the final grade. External papers are terminal, so a weak term can be recovered if the recovery starts early enough. A family choosing when to begin tuition should know which clock their child is on. For a continuous system, the useful intervention is early and steady. For a terminal system, a concentrated block in the spring can still move a grade.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson for the same subject: codes, papers and what differs
paragraphs: Parents routinely treat IGCSE as one qualification. It is two, from two boards, with different paper structures and different tiering, and the differences are large enough to change how a student should revise. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended, with Extended candidates sitting Papers 2 and 4. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher over two two-hour papers with no multiple choice, so stamina matters more and the short-answer paper disappears.

In the sciences the gap widens. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each carry a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper worth a fifth of the grade. The Pearson international sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers and are single-tier, so the full grade range sits on one route. A student moving between a Cambridge entry and a Pearson entry is not simply learning different content; they may be losing or gaining a whole paper.

The tutoring consequence is specific. A Cambridge science candidate needs dedicated work on graph scales, significant figures and conclusion wording, because a fifth of the grade is decided by those habits. A Pearson candidate needs that technique too, but embedded, and gains more from structured long-answer practice. Matching a tutor to the code rather than to the subject name is the difference between a useful term and a pleasant one. The mathematics difference bites in a similar way: a Cambridge Extended candidate must switch between a fast short-answer paper and a slower structured one, while a Pearson Higher candidate writes for two hours twice and needs pacing rather than gear-changing. Ask the school for the code per subject and hand it to the tutor before the first session.

sections.heading: The cost question answered monthly, because that is how a school budget works
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is sold and monthly totals are how families decide, so take the monthly view first. Published monthly packages in this market include an online plan at AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist support in an examination year.

Translate that into a decision. One weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor, at the AED 150 to 300 band Unitors publishes for IGCSE and IB, is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Two weekly hours with a specialist at the AED 200 to 450 band that TutorChase and Bestimate publish is closer to AED 1,600 to 3,600. In-home delivery adds travel: the in-home band runs AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end published by EdFlik.

Context helps. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A frozen fee and a rising tuition bill is a real household arithmetic problem, and the sensible response is to buy specialist hours only where the component actually carries the marks rather than across every subject.

sections.heading: What a Dubai inspection report tells you, and what to read instead of the band
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are inspected by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection outcomes are published on a six-band scale from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. Parents treat the band as a school's score. It is better understood as a summary of many separate judgements, several of which have nothing to do with your child's subject.

This page does not publish any school's rating, including this one's, because a rating should be read from the regulator's own site on the day you read it rather than from a tutoring page written earlier. What is worth saying is how to use the report once you open it. Skip the headline. Go to the subject-level commentary and the section on provision for different groups of students, because that is where a report says something actionable about whether your child's particular need is being met.

The scale of the sector is worth holding in mind too. Dubai's 2024-25 figures record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, American at 14 and International Baccalaureate at about seven. A school can be strong overall and still be thin in one Higher Level subject simply because the cohort taking it is small. That is a supply problem rather than a quality problem, and it is exactly the gap private tuition fills.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the international curriculum
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. This is a federal requirement in substance: private schools are not obliged to follow a particular curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority's own guidance required its current mandatory-subject arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

The streaming rules are specific and worth knowing before you book anything. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and the authority states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language.

There is also a content constraint that limits honest marketing. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. That means no tutor can legitimately offer an alternative Arabic or Islamic Education curriculum, and anyone advertising one is describing something they should not be doing. Support in these subjects is reading fluency, vocabulary, script confidence and examination familiarity within the school's own material. One further detail is checkable and worth asking about at the school: the authority requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate approval from it to teach those subjects. That requirement sits on schools rather than on private tutors, and knowing the difference keeps a parent from being sold a credential that does not exist.

sections.heading: Diploma internal assessment: the criterion letters and what each is worth
paragraphs: This is the single largest gap in the pages competing for this search. Nobody names a criterion. Yet a Diploma student's internally assessed component is typically about a fifth of the subject grade, it is marked against descriptors the IB publishes, and a student who has never read those descriptors is guessing. Confirm the current allocation with your child's teacher or the subject guide the coordinator issues, because the IB revises subject guides on a cycle and a figure from an old guide is worse than none.

The mathematics exploration is the clearest example of why the letters matter. Marks are distributed across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Two of those criteria are about writing rather than mathematics, and they are the ones Dubai students score lowest on, because a cohort trained on efficient IGCSE answers reads reflection as padding. It is not padding. Teaching a student to write honestly about a method that failed is a specific, learnable skill worth real marks.

Word and page limits are the other thing families get wrong, usually by treating a limit as a target. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 and the exhibition commentary at 950. An economics commentary runs to 800 words. Writing to the cap is not a virtue; examiners read the first words that count and stop where the limit says. A tighter piece that hits every criterion beats a longer one that hits most.

sections.heading: Online delivery, honestly compared with a tutor in the room
paragraphs: A tutor in the room is a real product and it has real advantages. They can see an exercise book without being shown it, read hesitation that a video call flattens, and remove any question of a student quietly doing something else. For a younger child, or one who needs physical presence to stay on task, that is worth the premium. Any page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising.

The costs are travel and supply. The in-home band in this market runs AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the gap is time the tutor cannot sell twice. Supply is the larger issue. A tutor who must physically reach Jumeirah by five can serve a handful of students a day, so your child's choice narrows to whoever is both qualified and close. For Higher Level sciences in Dubai that is a short list, and it does not always contain the subject you need.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is an India-only service, and the UAE offer is one-to-one live video. The result for a Jumeirah family is that the question changes from who lives nearby to who is free at your hour. Many families end up splitting the problem sensibly: online one-to-one for the specialist subject, and a local arrangement for general homework supervision where expertise matters less.

sections.heading: When a Jumeirah session can realistically start, and what that costs you
paragraphs: Scheduling looks like a detail and is actually the most common reason tuition fails. A Dubai secondary day starts early and ends in the hottest part of the afternoon. A student collected at half past two, driven home through the Al Wasl and Jumeirah Beach Road squeeze, and sat down at three, is a tired student. Families who book that slot because it looks convenient tend to conclude after a term that tutoring does not work for their child, when what did not work was the hour.

The slots that hold are later. Between five and eight in the evening, Gulf Standard Time, a student has eaten, decompressed and done the urgent homework, and can give a focused hour. That window is only reliably available when the tutor has no journey to make, because an in-home tutor pricing an evening slot in Jumeirah is pricing a return trip through the same traffic. Online removes the journey from both sides of the hour.

Two seasonal adjustments matter here. During Ramadan, school days shorten and household routines move later, and most students shift their slot to after Iftar for the month; with no travel involved that shift is simple to arrange. Over the long summer, families either pause or buy a short block aimed at one named gap, which is the pattern we see most from Year 11 students heading into the Diploma. Either way, tell us a fortnight ahead and the slot is held or released.

process.title: Send the year group, the entry codes and the component that is costing marks
process.description: Specific beats general. Year 11 Cambridge 0620 Extended with moles unresolved, or Year 12 economics with two commentaries written and no diagram marks, both produce the right tutor. A subject name on its own produces a generalist, which is rarely what the problem needs.

process.title: We match one tutor and run a free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a real teaching hour on the student's own work rather than a sales call. The student decides afterwards, because the student is the one who has to turn up each week. If the pairing does not work we match again rather than asking anyone to persevere.

process.title: Fix the hour in Gulf Standard Time and hold it

process.title: Teach from the school's own sequence

faqs.question: Does Emirates International School Jumeirah enter students for IGCSE or for IB on-screen assessment?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because the pattern varies by subject and by cohort and schools revise it. Some subjects are entered externally with Cambridge or Pearson while others are assessed against Middle Years criteria, and a student can be inside both systems in the same year. The answer changes how tuition should work: criterion marking rewards visible reasoning, external papers reward concise finished answers in the command term's own language. Once you have the entry list, matching a tutor to it is straightforward, because the paper structure follows from the code.

faqs.question: Is a Middle Years Programme grade comparable to an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and treating them as equivalent causes real planning mistakes. A Middle Years grade of 1 to 7 is built from criterion marks converted by published boundaries, while an IGCSE grade is awarded on external papers against a mark scheme. A student can hold a strong criterion grade and still be unprepared for a timed external paper, or the reverse. Use each grade for what it measures, and ask the school's coordinator how they read the two together when making Higher Level recommendations, because that reading is the one that affects your child.

faqs.question: How much does one weekly tutoring hour cost a Dubai family per month?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai estimates put a single weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 in the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Published packages in the market include an online plan at AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are the market's own figures rather than IB Gram's price list. Decide which band the component actually needs before buying hours across every subject.

faqs.question: What do the criterion letters on my child's Diploma coursework mean?
faqs.answer: Each internally assessed component is marked against named criteria with their own mark allocations, and the letters are how teachers and moderators refer to them. On the mathematics exploration the marks are spread across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. On a scientific investigation they cover research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Ask your child's teacher for the current descriptors from the subject guide the coordinator issues, because the IB revises guides on a cycle and working from an outdated version is worse than working from none.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach an Extended Essay for an Emirates International School Jumeirah student legitimately?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is easy to state. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain how the criteria are applied, read a draft the student wrote and mark it against the descriptors, question an argument until the student can defend it, and teach the referencing convention. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a draft into its submitted form, or choose the research question. The most valuable hour is the earliest, stress-testing the student's own question, because an essay built on a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words stalls however well it is written.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child in Jumeirah actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so it should never appear in a UAE plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so ask the school which zone your centre sits in.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Jumeirah or on Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Stating that plainly is more useful than letting you discover it later. What you gain is supply: the tutor no longer has to be within driving distance of Jumeirah at five in the afternoon, so the pool is set by who is free at your hour rather than by who lives nearby. For Higher Level sciences in Dubai that difference is substantial rather than cosmetic.

faqs.question: Why does my non-Arab child study Arabic at an IB school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because it is mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, alongside Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. Arabic is streamed by first-language status, and the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requires that classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies are organised separately, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and the authority advises no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

faqs.question: How do I read the school's published inspection report usefully?
faqs.answer: Skip the headline band and read the subject-level commentary plus the sections on provision for different groups of students. Dubai schools are judged on a six-band scale from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak, and a single band summarises many separate judgements about teaching, outcomes, leadership and provision. Read the report on the regulator's own website on the day you need it, rather than from a summary on a tutoring page. A school can be strong overall and still thin in one small Higher Level cohort.

faqs.question: Is a permit required for anyone tutoring my child privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the ministry's smart app and e-services, with a published completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Analysis and Approaches and a Higher Level science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because the overlap is real. The quantitative handling that decides a Higher Level chemistry or physics grade is the same algebraic fluency that decides a mathematics paper, so a tutor strong in both can teach the skill once and apply it twice. Where no single tutor covers both to the depth needed, two separate pairings are better than one stretched one. We say which situation applies rather than matching a generalist to a Paper 3 problem and hoping.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 and has not started revising. Is a spring block worth it?
faqs.answer: For external papers, yes, because the assessment is terminal and a concentrated block can still move a grade. The work should be timed papers rather than content revision: sit a paper cold, mark it during the session, identify the two or three repeating error types and drill those. In Cambridge sciences the written practical paper is usually the fastest fifth of the grade to improve, because scales, precision and conclusion wording are technique. What a spring block cannot change is a criterion-marked component already submitted.

faqs.question: How does a Jumeirah family's weekly tutoring slot change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Most families move it to after Iftar for the month and keep everything else the same. School days shorten and household routines shift later, so an afternoon slot stops working while an evening one starts working better. Because delivery is over live video there is no journey to reschedule around, which makes the change simple to arrange and simple to reverse. Tell us roughly a fortnight ahead and the new hour is held for the month, then the original slot resumes without the student losing continuity with the same tutor.

faqs.question: What if the first tutor we try for our Jumeirah student is the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Say so and we match again. The free trial lesson exists precisely so that this decision gets made after an hour of real teaching rather than after a term of fees, and the student's view carries the most weight because the student is the one attending. A wrong match is usually about pace or explanation style rather than competence, which is information worth having for the second attempt. There is no package to commit to before the trial and nothing to unwind if the answer is no.

intro.heading: The fork in the road a Meadows family is usually standing at
paragraphs: Emirates International School Meadows runs an IB continuum with external IGCSE examinations inside it, which gives a student here two credible routes out of Year 11 and a mathematics decision that shapes university options years later. That is why a search for an IB IGCSE tutor for Emirates International School Meadows students in Dubai so often comes from a parent planning rather than panicking. The question is not usually how to rescue a grade. It is which Higher Level list is realistic and what has to be true by August for it to work.

Confirm the detail with the school. Dubai schools revise option blocks, examination boards and entry patterns on their own timetable, and the number of external subjects a cohort sits is a decision the school makes on its own evidence. The head of secondary and the examinations officer are the only reliable source for your child's actual entries. What this page can do is set out what each route demands once the decision exists, and where tuition changes an outcome rather than just filling an evening.

The mathematics decision deserves naming first because it is the one most often made for the wrong reason. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-proof route; Applications and Interpretation is the data-and-modelling route. Students pick Applications because Analysis looks hard, and then discover a degree they want specifies Analysis. Students pick Analysis Higher Level because it sounds stronger, and then lose points across two years on a course that does not suit how they think. Both mistakes are expensive and both are avoidable with one honest conversation in Year 11.

The second thing a Meadows household underestimates is the coursework load. Each Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated externally, and Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit on top. Those deadlines are school-set and they land earlier than any examination timetable. A family that starts tuition when the examination dates appear has already passed the window where a fifth of each grade was still movable.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video at a Gulf Standard Time hour. In-home visiting is a service we run only in India, not in the UAE, and this page states that plainly rather than leaving it to be discovered. Every figure below names whoever published it. No IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a planning page is worse than no date at all. Your child's Diploma coordinator works from the official timetable and is the right person to ask for those dates.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two linear years ending in external papers, graded A* to G by Cambridge or 9 to 1 by Pearson. Cambridge syllabuses tier into Core and Extended in most subjects, with Core candidates capped at grade C. Pearson Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher while the Pearson international sciences run on a single tier across the full grade range.

They are the qualification the Ministry of Education equivalency route counts on the British track, where five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required and Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside that count. programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component of roughly a fifth of the grade, teacher-marked against named criteria and externally moderated. The total runs to 45 points, three of which come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority route in Dubai, at roughly seven per cent of private-school enrolment against 37 per cent on UK curricula in the 2024-25 figures. programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. A student has to learn to read the criterion descriptors and write the reasoning down. subjects.description: The algebra, calculus and proof route. Higher Level runs three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent with the exploration at 20. Paper 3 is the component Dubai students under-prepare, because its first marks depend on reading an unfamiliar investigation correctly rather than on recall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The data, statistics and modelling route, with graph theory and matrices added at Higher Level. It is not an easier course; it is a different one, and a student who finds algebra hard will still find Higher Level Applications demanding because the modelling work assumes algebraic confidence.

subjects.description: Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 at half the grade each. The marks that go missing are in composite and inverse function notation, histograms with unequal class widths, and column vectors. subjects.levels: IGCSE 0625 or 4PH1, IB HL and SL

Fixing the research question in the first fortnight is worth more than weeks of later redrafting, and it is entirely legitimate coaching.

subjects.description: IGCSE 0478 splits into computer systems and algorithms, and the algorithm paper is marked on pseudocode discipline rather than on whether code would compile. sections.heading: Where a Meadows student's Year 11 grades actually go next
paragraphs: A set of IGCSE grades is read by three different audiences and a family that knows which one matters to them makes better decisions. The Diploma coordinator reads them as a prediction of whether Higher Level requests are realistic. A sixth form reads them as entry criteria. The Ministry of Education equivalency route reads them as a count of five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that five.

Those three readings pull in different directions. The equivalency count rewards breadth: five subjects passed at a modest threshold. A Higher Level recommendation rewards depth in a narrow set: a strong grade in the specific subject requested, and in mathematics, Extended-tier algebra rather than a general pass. A student optimising for one can quietly undermine the other, and the most common version of that is dropping a science to protect an overall average and then wanting Higher Level chemistry.

The practical move is to write down the destination before Year 11 starts. If the Diploma is the plan, the question becomes which three Higher Level subjects and what each one assumes from IGCSE. If a sixth form outside the school is the plan, the question becomes which grades that institution publishes as its threshold. If the family may relocate within the UAE, the equivalency count becomes the thing to protect. All three are answerable in an afternoon with the school, and none of them is answerable from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: how to choose honestly
paragraphs: This is the decision with the longest tail and the worst available advice. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebra, calculus and proof. Applications and Interpretation is built on data, statistics and modelling, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Neither is a reduced version of the other. The mistake families make is treating Applications as the easier course, which it is not: Higher Level Applications still assumes algebraic confidence and its modelling work is unforgiving of a student who cannot manipulate an expression.

The decision should be driven by two things. The first is how the student thinks, which is visible in their marked work rather than in their opinion of themselves: a student who enjoys a proof and dislikes an open-ended investigation belongs in Analysis, and the reverse belongs in Applications. The second is prerequisites. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many computer science programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, design, the social sciences and most life-science routes usually accept either.

Check the prerequisite on the programme's own published requirements rather than on anything written about it elsewhere, including here. University requirements change between admissions cycles, they differ between faculties inside the same institution, and they differ between an engineering degree in the UAE and the same degree abroad. A Meadows family with a shortlist can resolve this in an hour of reading. A family that assumes will discover the problem in Year 13, when nothing can be changed.

sections.heading: Where Diploma science marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Science grades at Diploma level are lost in three predictable places, and none of them is content coverage. The first is the investigation, worth about a fifth of the subject grade and marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students who have come through IGCSE have never been assessed on research design, because at IGCSE the method is given. Asked to produce their own, they build something that generates data but cannot answer the question they set, and no amount of later analysis repairs that.

The second is quantitative handling. Diploma chemistry runs on moles arithmetic the way a building runs on its foundations, and a student who passed IGCSE by pattern-matching calculations will stall in the first energetics unit. Physics is the same story with algebraic rearrangement. These are fixable in a handful of sessions, but only if the diagnosis is right; a student who says they find chemistry hard is usually saying they find the arithmetic inside chemistry hard.

The third is the command-term discipline that transfers straight from IGCSE and then changes slightly. Diploma papers use a published set of command terms with specific demands, and the difference between outline, describe and explain is worth marks on every paper. A student who writes a thorough explanation in answer to state has produced a correct response that earns nothing extra and spent four minutes doing it. Tutors on this page keep a running error log so these patterns surface rather than being rediscovered each term.

sections.heading: What Dubai tutoring costs, starting from the cheapest option available
paragraphs: Build the budget upward rather than downward, because the cheapest option in this market is genuinely useful for some problems. Online platforms using university-student tutors publish the lowest rates: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For a Year 9 student who needs someone to sit with them through homework and explain a topic again, that band is appropriate and anything more is overspending.

Step up when the problem becomes a mark scheme rather than a concept. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200, which is one of very few published numbers in this market. Three of the six strongest pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in.

Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upward. The premium tier starts around AED 500, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home visiting is a separate band at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the rate. None of these is IB Gram's price and this page publishes no price list; what it offers is the shape of the market so a family can buy the band the problem actually needs.

sections.heading: Five regulators, seven emirates: what changes if your family moves
paragraphs: Expatriate families in Dubai move within the UAE more often than they expect to, and private-school regulation is not federal in practice. According to u.ae, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. In Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education there, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The practical differences are larger than the names suggest. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval rather than inspection alone sits with the emirate. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the press, prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the national tutoring permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

For tuition planning, the useful consequence is that the only element that genuinely travels with the family is the qualification. A Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE entry and an IB Diploma registration are board-level, not emirate-level, so a move does not restart the course. What changes is the inspection regime, the fee-approval route and the school supply. A tutor working over live video continues unaffected, which is one of the few genuinely practical arguments for online delivery in a mobile population.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what an IGCSE student has to be able to show
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which a foreign school certificate is recognised in the UAE, and it matters for a student applying to a UAE institution or needing the certificate recognised locally. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details are routinely got wrong. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects, so a student who counts them is a subject short. And at least one site ranking for queries in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. For the American track the published requirement includes English proficiency at a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT mathematics test.

No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears on this page, and that absence is deliberate. The source that sets out the British and American tracks does not state one, and publishing an unverified points figure on a page a parent plans around would be worse than leaving a gap. Check the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel or with the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of equivalency or attestation, and no tuition is required for any of it.

sections.heading: What the drive out to The Meadows costs, and why the evening slot wins
paragraphs: An in-home tutor is a real product with real advantages. Someone in the room sees an exercise book without being shown it, reads hesitation a video call flattens, and removes any question of a student quietly doing something else. For a younger child or one who needs presence to stay on task, that is worth paying for. The costs are travel and supply, and in a community like The Meadows both are larger than they look.

Travel first. The published in-home band runs AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the difference is time the tutor cannot sell twice. A trip out past Emirates Hills at half past four and back at seven is most of an afternoon for one hour of teaching, which is why evening in-home bookings in these communities sit at the upper end of the band rather than the lower.

Supply is the bigger constraint. A tutor who must physically reach The Meadows by five can serve three or four students a day, so the choice available to your child narrows to whoever is both qualified and nearby. For Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 in Dubai, that is a short list and it frequently does not include the subject you need. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is an India-only service, and the UAE offer is one-to-one live video at the hour you choose.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on internally assessed work
paragraphs: Some sites competing for this search sell completed internal assessments outright. That is not tutoring and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the whole diploma rather than one subject grade. A page aimed at Meadows parents should say so directly, because the offer is easy to find and the risk is not advertised alongside it. Submitting work the student did not produce is academic misconduct under IB rules, and there is no version of it that is safe.

The legitimate boundary is specific and genuinely valuable. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain what each named criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and mark it against the descriptors, question an argument until the student can defend it, and teach the referencing convention the subject requires. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a draft into its submitted form, choose the research question outright, or process the data on the student's behalf.

In practice the earliest session is the most valuable, before any writing starts. A mathematics exploration built on a question that cannot generate enough mathematics scores poorly however well it reads, and an Extended Essay on a question with no accessible sources stalls at the research stage. Half an hour stress-testing the question saves weeks, and the student leaves having made the decision themselves. Sessions on this page are documented with a note of what was taught and what the student changed afterwards, in their own words, so a family asked about support can answer honestly.

process.description: A Higher Level list, a sixth-form shortlist or a mathematics route decision all change which tutor is right. process.description: The trial is a real teaching hour on the student's own work rather than a consultation. The student decides afterwards, because the student is the one attending every week. If the pairing is wrong we match again instead of asking a family to persevere with it.

process.description: Most Meadows and Springs families settle between five and eight in the evening, Gulf Standard Time. We hold that hour across the term so it survives the activities timetable, and move it for mock weeks, Ramadan and travel when you tell us in advance.

process.description: The tutor asks for the current unit or the coursework deadline each half term and teaches to it rather than running a parallel syllabus. That keeps the hour useful this week and stops the student carrying two competing versions of a topic into a paper.

process.description: Every session ends with a written note of what was taught, what went wrong and what to practise. Across a term the repeating errors become the real diagnosis, and they are almost always narrower and more fixable than the worry that prompted the first enquiry.

faqs.question: Should an Emirates International School Meadows student take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Decide from marked work and from prerequisites, not from which course sounds harder. Analysis is algebra, calculus and proof; Applications is data, statistics and modelling, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Applications is not a reduced Analysis, and its Higher Level still assumes algebraic confidence. Engineering, physics and mathematics programmes commonly specify Analysis, often at Higher Level, while business, design and social sciences usually accept either. Check the requirement on the programme's own published pages, because faculties differ inside one institution and requirements change between admissions cycles.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Meadows student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five, which is the detail families most often get wrong. One site ranking in this market publishes a six-subject figure that does not match the rule. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of equivalency.

faqs.question: Which exam board does Emirates International School Meadows use for its IGCSE entries?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because schools in Dubai run different boards in different subjects and revise entries between cohorts. The difference changes revision: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended with Papers 2 and 4 at Extended, while Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher over two two-hour papers with no multiple choice. Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper worth a fifth of the grade; the Pearson international sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers instead.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor out to The Meadows or The Springs?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly is more useful than letting it surface later. What you gain is choice: the tutor no longer has to drive out past Emirates Hills by five, so availability is set by who is free at your hour rather than by who lives nearby. For Higher Level sciences and Analysis Paper 3 work in Dubai, that is a material difference.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible tutoring option in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For homework company and re-explaining a topic, the budget online band is appropriate: Tutopiya publishes from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. That band is genuinely useful for a Year 8 or Year 9 student and anything more is overspending. The step up matters when the problem becomes a mark scheme rather than a concept, where qualified subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: My child's Diploma science grade dropped. Where should we look first?
faqs.answer: At the investigation and the arithmetic, in that order. The internally assessed investigation is worth about a fifth of the subject grade and is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, none of which IGCSE assessed, so students build something that produces data but cannot answer the question set. The second place is quantitative handling: a student who passed IGCSE chemistry by pattern-matching moles calculations stalls in the first energetics unit. Both are fixable in a handful of sessions once the diagnosis is right rather than general.

faqs.question: Which regulator would apply if we moved from Dubai to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah?
faqs.answer: A different one in each case, because private-school regulation sits with the emirate. According to u.ae, Dubai is overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, while the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. The qualification itself travels with the student, since board registration is not emirate-level.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose my Meadows child's exploration topic?
faqs.answer: A tutor may stress-test the student's own ideas against the criteria and explain why one question will generate more mathematics than another, and that is the most valuable session available because it happens before any writing. A tutor may not hand over a question for the student to adopt, write or rewrite passages into the submitted version, or process the data. The student keeps a note of the decision and their reasoning, and the tutor's session note records what was taught, so support can be described honestly if the school asks.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition in Year 10 rather than waiting for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for one specific reason: the Cambridge tier decision is taken on the school's evidence late in Year 10, and a Core placement caps the grade at C and leaves roughly a term of algebra to acquire before Higher Level mathematics becomes workable. Work in Year 10 that secures an Extended placement is cheaper and far less stressful than work in Year 12 bridging the consequence. If the tier is already secure, Year 10 support is better spent on one weak subject than spread thinly across several.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge February series available to UAE candidates, or only in India?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers the February and March series to India only, so it should never appear in a UAE revision plan. UAE candidates sit the June series, with November available as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so ask the school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a tutor for a Meadows family?
faqs.answer: For the common Extended-tier IGCSE subjects and Standard Level Diploma subjects, usually within a few days, because the pool is broad. For a Higher Level science at Paper 3 depth or a less common subject, it can take longer and sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour. In that case the options are a different hour, a short wait, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, all disclosed with the rate before anything is booked rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two children in the same Springs household?
faqs.answer: Often yes within a subject family, and consecutive one-to-one slots on the same evening is the arrangement most households with two secondary-age children settle on. Separate hours are kept, because two students at different stages are graded against different schemes and a shared hour serves neither well. A chemistry specialist who teaches both IGCSE Extended and Diploma chemistry can also tell the younger child which skill the older one wishes they had secured earlier, which is useful and free.

faqs.question: What does the school's published inspection band tell a parent about one subject?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents assume. Dubai schools are judged on a six-band scale from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak, and the band summarises many separate judgements about teaching, outcomes, leadership and provision. Read the subject-level commentary and the sections on provision for different groups instead, on the regulator's own website rather than from a summary elsewhere. A school can be strong overall and still thin in one Higher Level subject purely because the cohort taking it is small.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a Meadows student need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the ministry's smart app and e-services, with a published completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

intro.heading: The frequency question comes before the rate question
paragraphs: Parents usually ask what a tutor costs per hour. The more useful first question is how many hours, because frequency drives the monthly total far more than the rate does. A specialist at AED 300 once a week costs less per month than a mid-market tutor at AED 180 three times a week, and the two plans are suited to completely different problems. Deciding the shape first and the rate second is the way to avoid buying the right rate for the wrong plan.

The published monthly bands make the point. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those all assume one session a week. Double the frequency and the monthly figure doubles; the hourly rate has not moved at all.

Session length is the second lever and it behaves differently. A 90-minute session is not simply one and a half times as useful as a 60-minute one. For paper practice and Internal Assessment drafting it often is, because a full paper or a full draft review does not fit into an hour. For habit work such as writing method out or drilling command words, an hour twice a week beats ninety minutes once, because the repetition is what installs the habit rather than the duration.

There is a third lever most families never consider: how long the plan runs. A four-session block with a defined end and a re-test is a different financial commitment from an open-ended weekly slot, and it is the one that answers the question of whether tutoring is the right purchase at all. Open-ended arrangements have a way of continuing because nobody set a point at which to decide.

A GEMS International School Al Khail family sits along a corridor where journey times shape everything. Al Khail Road moves well outside the peak and badly inside it, and the residential communities on either side are spread out. For an in-home arrangement that means the plan's shape is partly decided by somebody else's drive. Removing the journey removes that constraint, which is worth more than it sounds when you are trying to run two sessions a week.

A note on independent work, because it changes the frequency answer. Sessions are not the only hours in the week, and a plan that ignores what happens between them will always look as though it needs more of them. A student doing thirty minutes of targeted practice between sessions makes one weekly hour behave like two; a student doing nothing between sessions makes two weekly hours behave like one. Ask what the between-session task is and whether anyone checks it, because that is the cheapest lever in the whole arrangement and it is usually left unpulled.

Delivery is stated once and holds throughout. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below is the market's, attributed and dated, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment scored out of eight under lettered criteria, with no terminal examination. One session a week is almost always enough at this stage, because the work is habit formation rather than content coverage and the school is carrying the syllabus itself.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-internatio.subjectsIntro: What frequency and session length suit each subject, and why. These are the courses most often requested along the Al Khail corridor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency is built by repetition, so two shorter sessions a week beats one long one for most students. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation marked on written reasoning, and that component does need a full ninety minutes to practise properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling with technology use assumed throughout. Calculator technique is an assessed skill and benefits from short, frequent practice. One weekly session is usually sufficient, which makes this a cheaper subject to support than Analysis and Approaches at the same rate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Quantitative work rewards frequency: moles, energetics and significant figures become reliable through repetition rather than explanation. Mechanism notation needs teaching once and practising often, which is the classic case for two sessions a week over a short block.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Deriving relationships from plotted data is a contained skill that four or five sessions usually settles, so a short block at any frequency works. Full past-paper practice under timed conditions needs a session long enough to sit the paper, which an hour rarely is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-word discipline is the common failure and it responds to frequency, not duration: short drills on answer shapes, repeated. Content volume tempts families into long sessions, which usually produces passive coverage rather than active recall.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Draft feedback and Individual Oral rehearsal both need length. A sixty-minute session rarely accommodates reading a piece of work and discussing it usefully, so this is the subject where ninety minutes most clearly earns the extra cost.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is drilled in short bursts; Higher Level evaluation is taught in longer ones, because it needs a full essay plan discussed end to end. A mixed pattern works well here and most providers will accommodate it if asked at the start.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study technique requires working through stimulus material, which takes time, so longer sessions less often suits it. Quantitative tools at Higher Level are marked on method shown and are better drilled in short, frequent sets.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Tier sets the grade ceiling, with Core capped at 5 and Extended reaching 9, so the first purchase is two timed papers rather than a term of sessions. Afterwards, habit work on writing method out responds best to twice-weekly short sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so confirm the stream before buying any sessions. Language work favours frequency strongly over length.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of frequency, in AED
paragraphs: Bestimate's published Dubai monthly estimates all describe one weekly hour: AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. That is the unit most families are quoted and the one most families then exceed without noticing, because the plan quietly becomes twice a week in the term before an examination.

Run the comparison properly and the result is often counter-intuitive. One specialist session a week at the upper end of the mid-market band costs less per month than three sessions with a budget tutor, and for a diagnosed component it will usually do more. Conversely, if the problem is a habit that needs installing, three cheaper sessions a week may genuinely beat one expensive one, because the mechanism is repetition rather than insight. The rate is not the variable that decides this. The nature of the failure is.

The monthly packages visible in this market encode the same trade. AED 799 for eight online sessions works out around AED 100 a session, which places it in the budget band however it is described, and eight sessions a month is twice a week. AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour including travel, at one session a week of double length. Both are reasonable products. They are not the same product.

The table below sets the frequencies against the monthly bands so a family can see what each shape costs before choosing a provider. The figures are the market's, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

sections.heading: Sixty minutes or ninety: what the extra half hour buys
paragraphs: Session length is treated as a budget decision and is really a pedagogical one. The honest answer is that it depends entirely on what is being worked on, and the two categories behave in opposite directions. Work that has to be done in one piece needs the length. Work that has to become automatic needs the frequency.

Things that need ninety minutes: sitting a full past-paper component and reviewing it in the same session, reading an Internal Assessment draft and discussing it criterion by criterion, rehearsing a language Individual Oral, planning and critiquing a full Higher Level essay. Trying to do any of these in sixty minutes produces half the work and a session that ends mid-thought, which is the most common complaint families have about hourly tutoring and is a shape problem rather than a tutor problem.

Things that are better twice a week at sixty minutes: algebraic fluency, command-word drills, writing method out so it can be credited, vocabulary and language retrieval, calculator technique. In each case the student needs to do the thing repeatedly with feedback between attempts, and a single long session gives one attempt with a lot of discussion around it.

For younger students the calculation is different again. Attention rather than content is the constraint, and two thirty-minute sessions a week will usually achieve more than one sixty-minute session at the same cost. Not every provider will split an hour, which is worth asking about before signing rather than discovering afterwards.

sections.heading: The rate bands, and what a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Once the shape is decided, the rate matters. The published Dubai bands run from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, through AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, to AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists on Bestimate's table, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and AED 650 at BartyED for examiner-led work.

Three of the strongest pages competing for this search publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars, which is a currency UAE families do not transact in. Knowing the band is therefore most of the value: a quote at AED 400 an hour for Year 8 homework support is identifiable as mispriced only if you know the market, and so is a quote at AED 60 for Higher Level Paper 3 coaching.

What a parent can genuinely verify is narrower than what gets claimed, and it is worth knowing which is which. Verifiable: whether the tutor teaches that subject at that level weekly, whether marking is included in the rate, who teaches each session by name, what a cancelled session costs, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Not verifiable from a website: examiner status, a self-published star rating, or a claimed average improvement.

On that last point, one provider in this market displays two conflicting review totals on the same page, and another shows a five-star average from twenty reviews alongside a student-numbers claim several orders larger. Treat self-asserted ratings as marketing. The MoHRE permit, by contrast, is a real thing, is granted free of charge for two years, and can simply be asked about.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit along the Al Khail corridor
paragraphs: In-home tutoring deserves a fair statement of its merits. A tutor in the room holds the attention of a younger or more distractible student more easily, written working is visible without a camera trick, and some families prefer a person present as a matter of preference rather than argument. The market prices that at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's figures and up to AED 500 from independent home tutors.

Along the Al Khail corridor the premium is mostly the drive, and the drive is unusually consequential here because the communities are strung out rather than clustered. A tutor coming from Jumeirah or Mirdif can realistically teach two sessions in an evening instead of four, and the rate reflects that lost capacity. More importantly for a frequency-led plan, twice-weekly in-home sessions are rarely sustainable: the second one lands too late in the evening to be useful.

The second cost is the shortlist. A family in Al Quoz or Al Khail Gate choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from whoever will make that drive on a weekday, which for a mainstream subject may be a decent list and for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3 may be nobody. Geography sets that limit and more money does not move it.

IB Gram removes the journey rather than discounting it. Lessons are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nothing here suggests otherwise; home visits are an India-only service. For a plan that needs two sessions a week, that is the difference between a schedule that works and one that does not.

sections.heading: Five ways Dubai families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: These are the patterns that recur, and each has a one-sentence remedy. The first is buying before diagnosing. A plan agreed without anybody reading a marked script is a guess, and a guess at the right hourly rate is still a guess. One timed paper marked against the published scheme costs an hour and determines every hour after it.

The second is running subjects in parallel. A Diploma student with three weak subjects whose family buys three weekly slots is paying three times the monthly band and asking the student to absorb three habit changes at once. Sequencing them, in order of how many marks each is costing, holds the cost near one band and usually produces more movement.

The third is the open-ended slot. A weekly session with no end date and no re-test continues because nobody set a point at which to decide, and families discover at results that nothing changed. The remedy is a block with a defined end and a fresh paper at the close. The fourth is the mismatched tutor: four sessions spent reading the specification is several hundred dirhams of no teaching, and the question that prevents it is whether the tutor teaches this subject at this level weekly.

The fifth is late buying. Help in the final six weeks is the most expensive version of the purchase because only timing and technique can still move; content gaps are no longer repairable at that point. That is not an argument for panic buying earlier, it is an argument for one cheap diagnostic paper a term, which is what makes early intervention possible at all.

sections.heading: The examination calendar, and why the deadline is not the exam
paragraphs: Families plan around the examination and are caught by the entry deadline, which sits months earlier. By the time the papers arrive the decisions that mattered have already been taken: which subjects, which tier, which board. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates are cited because they can be checked. For any future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than a restated date.

One administrative point costs more than any tutoring decision if it goes wrong. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Get the zone in writing from the exams officer.

For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no IB examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date is worse than none on a page a family schedules around. The dates that actually govern the year are the school's own internal Internal Assessment deadlines, which sit ahead of the IB's.
