sections.heading: Permits, premises and what nobody is approved to say
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit is free of charge, no provider can present licensing as a cost justifying a higher rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to a parent by anybody, and a figure circulating in this market could not be verified.

Premises are a separate licence. A tutoring operation with staff and a location in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, beginning with initial approval, allowing a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requiring annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved.

Dubai private schools themselves are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. A regulator inspects schools; it does not endorse tutoring companies, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked for a permit number.

sections.heading: What no number of sessions can buy
paragraphs: A page about frequency should be clear that some outcomes are not purchasable at any frequency. Nobody can promise a grade, and a provider offering a guaranteed score or a specific improvement is making a commercial claim rather than a professional judgement. What can be stated honestly is what sort of change is available over what period, and what the evidence at the end of a block will be.

The harder boundary concerns coursework. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and the mechanism is a risk transfer: the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money. No number of sessions and no fee makes that a reasonable purchase.

The legitimate version is specific. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score to a draft and quote the descriptor behind it, help narrow a research question until it fits the limit, confirm a data collection plan is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit until the sentences stop being the student's. Nor should a tutor distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are linked at source. If feedback could be shown to the school's coordinator without discomfort, it is on the right side of the line.

sections.heading: Availability, and what to ask before booking a frequency
paragraphs: Frequency depends on availability, and availability is finite. The scarcest combinations are the ones families most often want twice a week: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, a less commonly taught Diploma language, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is itself worth noticing.

The position here is that a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives, including waiting. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred from a contact number. For an online lesson it makes no practical difference, but a parent is entitled to know.

Three questions are worth asking before committing to a frequency. Can this slot be held for the whole term, or does it move each week? Will the same named tutor teach every session, or is there a rota? And if two sessions a week are agreed, is the second one at a time the student can actually use, or is it a late slot nobody wants? A rota destroys continuity and a bad second slot wastes half the plan.

The free trial lesson is one session, free with no card required, taken with the specialist who would actually teach. It exists so a mismatch costs an hour rather than a term. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed; if nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly rather than worked around.

process.title: Decide the shape before comparing rates
process.description: Work out whether the problem needs repetition or needs length. Habits such as writing method out and command-word discipline want two shorter sessions a week. Drafting, full papers and oral rehearsal want ninety minutes. Comparing hourly rates before deciding this is how families buy the right price for the wrong plan.

process.title: Buy one marked timed paper
process.description: A past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, sat under exam conditions and marked against the published scheme, with a written diagnosis naming the failing component. This is the cheapest hour in the plan and it frequently shortens everything that follows, because it rules out whole categories of work.

process.title: Confirm codes and entry details with the school
process.description: One email to the exams officer for the board, the syllabus codes, the tiers and the centre's Cambridge administrative zone. All four are free to obtain and each prevents a specific expensive error, the worst of which is a missed paper through using the wrong zone timetable.

process.title: Take the free trial, then fix the frequency
process.description: One free session with the specialist who would teach, no card required. Use it to agree the shape as well as the fit: how many sessions a week, how long, and whether the slot is held for the term. Agreeing the frequency vaguely is how a once-weekly plan becomes a twice-weekly bill.

process.title: Re-test at the end of the block, then decide
process.description: A fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the first. Either the component moved or it did not. If it did not, change the plan rather than extending it; if it did, decide deliberately whether to continue or stop. An open-ended slot with no re-test is the most common way money goes nowhere.

whyPoints.title: Shape first, rate second
whyPoints.description: The frequency and length of sessions move the monthly total more than the hourly rate does, and they are decided by the kind of failure rather than the budget. A plan built in that order is cheaper and more effective than one built by comparing hourly prices across providers.

whyPoints.title: Twice weekly is actually schedulable
whyPoints.description: Because no journey is made, a second session in the week lands at a usable time rather than after seven o'clock. Along the Al Khail corridor that is the practical difference between habit work being possible and being theoretical, and habit work is where most of the available marks sit.

whyPoints.title: Short sessions for young students
whyPoints.description: Two thirty-minute sessions a week usually achieve more than one sixty-minute session for a primary-age child, at the same cost, because attention rather than content is the constraint. Not every provider will split an hour; online delivery makes it straightforward.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names who published it and when it was read. Three of the strongest pages in this market publish no price and two quote United States dollars. A parent cannot identify a mispriced quote without knowing the market.

whyPoints.title: An end date and a re-test
whyPoints.description: Blocks have a defined close and a fresh paper at the end, so continuing is a decision rather than a default. Open-ended weekly slots are the commonest way a Dubai family spends steadily for a year and finds out at results that nothing moved.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable the tutor's location is disclosed, and there is no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a GEMS International School Al Khail student start with?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, after a marked timed paper has produced a written diagnosis. One weekly session is enough when the school is carrying the syllabus and the work is a single diagnosed component. Two a week is justified when the problem is a habit that needs repetition, such as writing method out so it can be credited, drilling command words or building algebraic fluency, and then only for a short block of four to six weeks. Starting at three a week before anybody has read the student's work is how families triple a monthly cost without improving the plan.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute session better value than an hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on the task, not the price. Ninety minutes earns its cost when the work cannot be split: sitting a full paper component and reviewing it, reading an Internal Assessment draft and discussing it criterion by criterion, or rehearsing a language Individual Oral with feedback. An hour is better when the work needs repeating with feedback between attempts, which covers fluency drills, command-word practice and calculator technique. For a primary-age child neither is right, and two thirty-minute sessions a week will usually do more at the same cost.

faqs.question: What does two sessions a week cost in Dubai at mid-market rates?
faqs.answer: Roughly double the published monthly band, since Bestimate's Dubai estimates of AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above specialist all assume a single weekly hour. Two mid-market sessions a week therefore runs around AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month. The monthly package figures in the market are consistent with that: AED 799 for eight online sessions is about AED 100 a session, which is budget tier at twice-weekly frequency. These are market figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Can the second weekly session be scheduled at a useful time?
faqs.answer: Online, yes, which is most of the reason twice-weekly plans work at all. With an in-home arrangement along the Al Khail corridor the second session usually lands after seven in the evening, because the tutor has to drive between households and the corridor moves badly in the afternoon peak. A session a tired student cannot use is money spent for nothing. Ask any provider, before agreeing a frequency, exactly when both sessions would be, and whether both slots are held for the full term rather than being rescheduled each week.

faqs.question: Should we run three Diploma subjects at once if three are weak?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Three weekly slots costs three times the monthly band and asks the student to absorb three habit changes simultaneously, which rarely works. Sequencing them, starting with whichever is costing the most marks on the evidence of marked work, holds the monthly figure near one band and generally produces more movement. Begin the second subject once the first component has been re-tested on a fresh paper. The order should come from the scripts rather than from which subject the student finds least pleasant, which is the usual basis for the decision.

faqs.question: Will a cheaper tutor three times a week beat a specialist once a week?
faqs.answer: For habit installation, sometimes yes, because the mechanism is repetition and a competent tutor supervising repeated practice delivers that. For a diagnosed component such as extended-response method marks or Internal Assessment criterion work, no, because the budget tier generally cannot read a marked script and name what is failing. The decision follows from the diagnosis rather than from the arithmetic. One timed paper marked against the published scheme tells you which of the two situations you are in, and it costs a single hour.

faqs.question: Does GEMS International School Al Khail run IGCSE as well as the IB?
faqs.answer: Confirm the programme and the entry details with the school directly rather than with any tutoring provider, including this one, because provision changes and an outdated answer on a website is worth nothing. What matters for a tutoring plan is narrower anyway: which board and syllabus codes your child is actually entered for, which tier where tiering applies, and the centre's Cambridge administrative zone. The exams officer can confirm all of that in one email, and those four facts determine what a tutor should be teaching and from which specification.

faqs.question: Can sessions be split into two shorter ones for a younger child?
faqs.answer: Online, yes, and for a primary-age student it is usually the better shape. Attention is the binding constraint well before sixty minutes, so two thirty-minute sessions a week typically achieve more than one hour at the same total cost. In-home arrangements rarely allow it because two journeys for one hour of teaching is uneconomic for the tutor, which is a logistics limit rather than a teaching judgement. Ask before committing, because some providers price and schedule strictly in whole hours and will not split them whatever the age of the student.

faqs.question: What happens to the schedule during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Timing moves and the rate does not. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar slots for the month and return to the usual time afterwards with the same tutor. Because delivery is online there is no journey to re-plan and no travel cost to re-price, which is why Dubai families generally find an online schedule easier through the month than an in-home one. School days are shortened, so some families use the earlier afternoon instead and keep evenings clear. Decide which shape you want before the month begins rather than part-way through it.

faqs.question: How long should a block of tutoring run before we judge it?
faqs.answer: Four to six weeks for a habit or technique problem, eight to twelve for a content gap, with a fresh unseen paper at the end under the same conditions as the first. That close is the point of the block. Either the diagnosed component moved or it did not, and both answers are useful: if it did not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should change rather than extend. An arrangement with no end date and no re-test continues by default, and families usually discover at results that nothing shifted.

faqs.question: Is marking included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies by provider and it changes the real cost significantly. Marking a full past paper properly against the published scheme takes time, and if it is charged separately or simply not done, the evidence trail the whole plan depends on does not exist. The related questions worth asking at the same time are who teaches each session by name, whether a cancelled session is credited or billed, and what happens if the tutor leaves mid-term. Those terms vary more between providers than the headline hourly rates do.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The market does offer in-home tutoring at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's figures and up to AED 500 from independent tutors, and for a younger or easily distracted student there is a real case for it. For a twice-weekly plan along the Al Khail corridor the scheduling usually defeats it, which is the practical reason online suits this shape.

faqs.question: Does a higher frequency mean faster results?
faqs.answer: Only where repetition is the mechanism. Fluency, command-word discipline and retrieval respond to frequency because the student needs repeated attempts with feedback in between. Content understanding does not: a second session in the same week often arrives before the student has done anything with the first, and the time goes on re-explanation. The honest answer is that frequency should follow the diagnosis. Where the diagnosis is a content gap, one good session a week plus independent work usually beats two sessions and no independent work.

faqs.question: What should we do first if exams are only a few weeks away?
faqs.answer: Work from the student's own most recent marked mock rather than starting new content, and accept what that window can and cannot change. In six weeks, timing, paper order, method shown and command-word reading can all move, and those are real marks often worth a grade boundary. A topic never properly learned will not become secure in that time, and a plan that tries to cover everything thinly moves nothing. Two or three sessions a week on technique is a reasonable shape here; it is also the most expensive point at which to start, which is the argument for a diagnostic paper each term.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-internatio.closingHeading: Decide the shape, then the rate
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-internatio.closingBody: For a family at GEMS International School Al Khail, the two decisions that actually set the cost are how often and how long, and both follow from what is failing rather than from a budget. Habit problems want two shorter sessions a week for a short block. Drafting and full papers want ninety minutes. One marked timed paper, read against the published scheme, tells you which you are dealing with and usually shortens the plan. intro.heading: Primary results are measurements, not verdicts
paragraphs: A Jumeirah parent holding a page of primary assessment results is usually looking at three or four different kinds of number without being told which is which. Some are teacher judgements against year-group expectations. Some are raw scores on an internal test. Some are standardised scores, where the figure has been adjusted for age and compared against a reference group. Each answers a different question, and treating them as one picture is how a family concludes their child is behind when the data says something narrower.

GEMS Jumeirah Primary School teaches the English National Curriculum through the primary years on the Jumeirah side of the city, so the assessment a family meets is largely internal. That is not a weakness in the information; it simply means the question to ask changes. Instead of 'what grade is this', the useful questions are what skill was being tested, whether the result is consistent with the last one, and whether the gap is in the skill or in the way it was assessed.

The pattern we see most often in Dubai primary work is a child who is strong on one half of a subject and weak on the other, with the overall score hiding it. In mathematics, arithmetic fluency and mathematical reasoning are genuinely separate skills: a child can retrieve number facts instantly and still stall on a word problem, and another can reason beautifully and be slowed by every calculation. A single maths score averages those two into a figure that tells a parent nothing about what to do next.

Reading splits the same way. A comprehension score combines retrieval, which is a scanning and attention skill, with inference, which is a reasoning and vocabulary skill. They fail for different reasons and respond to completely different teaching. Writing splits again, into sentence structure, punctuation accuracy, vocabulary range and the ability to hold a structure across a page. Any of the four can be the brake while the other three are fine.

Separating those parts is the first job of a first session, and it is usually the cheapest useful thing a family buys. A combined score split into its components tells a parent where to put effort, and it frequently shows that the half they were worried about is fine. Families should also confirm current year-group provision with the school directly, since Dubai schools extend their age range often and the sector is growing quickly.

The families who contact us about IGCSE and IB support for pupils at a Jumeirah primary are usually thinking ahead to the secondary years, or dealing with both stages at once because of an older child. Both are handled here. Lessons for Dubai families run online, one-to-one, over live video, with the child's own work shared and annotated on screen. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India, and the comparison later on this page states that trade plainly.

sections.heading: What each kind of primary assessment is designed to detect
paragraphs: Three kinds of number arrive home from a Dubai primary, and they are not comparable. A teacher judgement places a child against year-group expectations using everything the teacher has seen, which makes it the broadest and the least precise. A raw score on an internal test measures performance on that test on that day, which makes it precise and narrow. A standardised score adjusts for age and compares against a reference group, which makes it useful for spotting an outlier and poor at describing a specific skill.

Each is answering a different question, so each supports a different decision. If a family wants to know whether their child is broadly where the school expects, the teacher judgement is the right source. If they want to know whether last term's work on fractions landed, a repeated raw score on the same task is the only thing that will tell them. If they want to know whether a difficulty is unusual for the child's age rather than typical, the standardised measure is the one to read.

The common mistake is reading a standardised score as a mark out of a hundred, which produces unnecessary alarm in both directions. The second common mistake is comparing scores from two different tests and treating the difference as progress. A new test can move for a dozen reasons that have nothing to do with the child, which is why a repeat of the same measure is worth more than a more sophisticated new one.

The practical habit worth building is simply to ask, each time a result arrives, what this instrument was designed to detect. Schools answer that question readily when asked directly. With the answer in hand a parent can tell whether a number deserves a response at all, and a great deal of tutoring in this city is bought in response to numbers that never needed one.

sections.heading: The number half of maths, and the reasoning half
paragraphs: Arithmetic fluency means retrieving a number fact rather than working it out. The difference is not speed for its own sake; it is attention. A child who computes seven times eight by counting is using working memory on the calculation, and the lesson's actual idea, whether that is area or equivalence or division with remainders, arrives into a mind that has no capacity left for it. This is why fluency gaps look like comprehension gaps.

It is measured honestly in two minutes with a sheet of known facts, repeated six weeks later. The sheet should be the same sheet, which feels like cheating and is the whole point: the only variable that has changed is the child. Progress here is unambiguous in a way that very little else at primary level is, and it tends to move quickly once practice is short, frequent and tracked.

Reasoning is a different animal. A word problem asks a child to read a situation, decide what is being asked, choose an operation and then calculate. Most failures happen in the first three steps and get recorded as a maths error. The teaching is therefore structured reading: underline what is given, state what is wanted, name the operation, then calculate. Practising more calculations does not improve any of the first three steps.

A session that treats these as one subject wastes half its time. We separate them from the first lesson, measure them separately, and report them separately, because the parent's next decision depends on which one is weak. A fluency gap is a short, dull, highly effective piece of work. A reasoning gap is slower, more interesting, and needs talk rather than worksheets.

sections.heading: Writing is marked against criteria, not against length
paragraphs: Children in Dubai primaries are frequently praised for writing more, and they reasonably conclude that length is the measure. Marking criteria say otherwise. They reward sentence variety, accurate punctuation used for effect, precise vocabulary and an organisation that holds across the piece. A long piece with repetitive sentence openings and drifting structure scores below a shorter piece that controls all four.

Separating the four strands changes what practice looks like. Sentence structure improves by writing the same content three different ways and choosing. Punctuation accuracy improves by proofreading someone else's work, which removes the author's blindness to their own text. Vocabulary improves through reading and through deliberate replacement of a general word with a precise one. Organisation improves by planning in four boxes before writing anything.

The honest measure is two pieces, months apart, marked against the same criteria, with the first piece kept. This is the single most convincing evidence a parent can hold, and it is also the one most families never have, because the first piece went home in a bag and was lost. Keeping it costs nothing and makes every later conversation concrete.

At IGCSE this becomes directly transferable. First-language English rewards register and structure on the directed-writing task, and second-language English rewards a mechanical approach to the summary question. Both are versions of the same primary skill: write to the criteria rather than to the page. A child who learns that in Year 5 is not learning a primary trick; they are learning the thing that will earn marks in Year 11.

sections.heading: What the IGCSE years will ask for, and what carries forward
paragraphs: Parents of primary children are entitled to know what the examined years actually demand, because it changes what is worth practising now. IGCSE grades come from external written papers marked by an examiner who has never met the student, applying a published scheme to the words on the page. Three habits decide a great deal of the outcome, and all three can be started years earlier.

The first is answering to the mark allocation. If a question offers three marks, the answer needs three distinct creditable points, and most students write one well-expressed sentence instead. The second is command-term discipline: explain requires a causal link, describe does not, evaluate requires a judgement with a reason. The third is working shown on the page, so that method marks survive an incorrect final answer.

Three skills carry forward from primary in order of practical impact: arithmetic automaticity, reading stamina on dense text, and the ability to produce extended writing to a deadline. None of them is content. All three are built by practice distributed over years rather than crammed in Year 10, which is the honest argument for primary tuition that is not about remediation at all.

What does not carry forward is the habit of being rewarded for effort and presentation alone. That shift catches many students out in Year 10, and it catches out the strongest ones hardest, because they have never had to think about how an answer is credited. Naming it early makes the transition a technical adjustment rather than a confidence shock.

sections.heading: What one session can honestly fix at primary level
paragraphs: Some things genuinely change in a single session, and a family deserves to know which, because it affects how much they need to buy. Structured reading of a word problem is one: underline what is given, state what is wanted, name the operation. A child who has never been shown that sequence can apply it the same afternoon, and the effect on word-problem accuracy is often immediate and large.

Punctuation accuracy in a child's own writing is another, because the fix is procedural rather than conceptual. Reading the piece aloud to find missing full stops, then proofreading a classmate's text to see errors they are blind to in their own, produces a measurable change within a session or two. The same applies to layout habits in maths, such as one step per line and the equals signs aligned.

Other things take months and should be described that way. Arithmetic automaticity is built by short, frequent, distributed practice over a term. Inference in reading grows with vocabulary and with talk about text, which is slow and cumulative. Sustained written organisation across a long piece develops with maturity as much as with teaching, and no amount of weekly tuition compresses it.

The reason to say this plainly is that families are often sold the slow things as though they were fast, and then conclude that tutoring does not work when the fast things were never attempted. A first session spent on diagnosis usually finds at least one immediate win, which buys the patience the slower work needs.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on a British timetable
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. This is a federal requirement implemented through KHDA in the emirate, and the authority's guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Jumeirah family it means the timetable carries subjects that appear on no Cambridge specification and still produce report grades.

KHDA sets out how these classes must be organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab pupils, while non-Arab pupils are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the appropriate approval from KHDA, which is a concrete credential point a parent can ask about.

For tutoring there is a real constraint here. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support has to work from the school's own material and the Ministry's curriculum rather than substituting an alternative scheme. That makes coordination with the class teacher more important in these subjects than in any other.

sections.heading: What this costs in Dubai, and what the money buys at primary level
paragraphs: Published market figures, read in October 2026, give four bands. A budget online tutor or university student runs from about AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase quoting AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are their figures, not an IB Gram price list.

At primary level the tier question looks different from the examined years, because the subject content is not where the difficulty lies. What a parent is paying for is diagnostic skill: the ability to look at a combined score and say which half of it is weak, and then to teach that half specifically. That is a judgement skill rather than a content one, and it is not reliably available at the bottom of the market.

Session length also behaves differently. For a seven-year-old, a shorter session more often beats a full hour weekly, because attention is the binding constraint. Paying for sixty minutes when a child can concentrate for thirty-five is one of the quieter ways money leaves a tutoring budget in this city. Ask how long sessions actually run for the child's age before comparing any hourly figure.

In-home tuition sits outside the online bands because travel is priced into the hour, with published in-home figures of AED 180 to AED 500. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and no tutor is sent to a Jumeirah address. For primary work the online format needs a quiet room, headphones and a document camera or tablet so handwriting is visible as it happens.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's help stops, for an older sibling's coursework
paragraphs: Families with a primary child and a Diploma student need the boundary stated once, clearly. A tutor may teach what each assessment criterion rewards and how marks are allocated across the lettered criteria, discuss a research question the student has proposed, read a draft the student has written and identify where it falls short, and coach the process of collecting, presenting and referencing evidence.

A tutor may not write any part of a submitted text, may not edit a draft into its final state, and may not supply a topic, a data set or a conclusion for the student to adopt. The distinction is not a technicality. One Dubai operator advertises completed IB Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules with the consequence falling on the student rather than the seller.

The same boundary covers IGCSE coursework components, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. It also covers the boards' documents: syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, so a tutor cites and links the official source rather than distributing copies of it.

Stating this on a primary-facing page is deliberate. The families most exposed to the completed-coursework market are the ones under time pressure with an older child, and the price gap between real support and a purchased document is exactly what makes the shortcut tempting. Knowing in advance what legitimate help looks like makes the offer easy to recognise and easy to refuse.

faqs.question: What does a standardised score on my GEMS Jumeirah Primary child's report actually mean?
faqs.answer: It compares performance against a reference group of the same age, so it answers the question of whether a result is unusual rather than typical. It is not a mark out of a hundred, and reading it that way causes unnecessary alarm in both directions. It is good for spotting an outlier and poor at telling you which specific skill is weak. Ask the school what instrument produced it and what the instrument was designed to detect; schools answer that readily, and the answer often means no response is needed at all.

faqs.question: Why is my child quick at sums but stuck on word problems?
faqs.answer: Because those are two different skills and one score usually hides the split. A word problem asks the child to read a situation, work out what is being asked, choose an operation and only then calculate. Most failures happen in the first three steps and get recorded as a maths error. The teaching is structured reading of the question rather than more calculation practice: underline what is given, state what is wanted, name the operation, then compute. Children who have never been shown that sequence often apply it the same day.

faqs.question: Is it worth working on times tables in Year 4 when the content has moved on?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is attention rather than arithmetic. A child who calculates seven times eight instead of retrieving it spends working memory on the calculation, so the lesson's actual idea arrives into a mind with no capacity left for it. Fluency gaps therefore present as comprehension gaps. Practice should be short, frequent and tracked with the same two-minute sheet repeated six weeks apart, because the repeat is what proves anything moved. It is dull work and among the highest-return things available at primary level.

faqs.question: How should a primary writing piece be judged if not by how much the child wrote?
faqs.answer: Against four separate strands: sentence structure, punctuation accuracy, vocabulary precision and organisation held across the piece. A long piece with repetitive openings and drifting structure scores below a shorter piece that controls all four. Each strand improves through a different activity, so treating writing as one skill wastes most of the practice. Keep the first piece of work, mark a later piece against the same four strands, and the comparison becomes concrete rather than a matter of impression.

faqs.question: Which primary skills actually matter for IGCSE grades later?
faqs.answer: Three, in order of practical impact. Arithmetic automaticity, because it frees attention for the new idea in every maths and science lesson. Reading stamina on dense text, because source questions, case studies and data responses demand sustained attention to the final question. And producing extended writing to a deadline, since every written paper is time-limited. None of the three is content, and all three are built by practice distributed across years rather than compressed into Year 10 revision.

faqs.question: What changes about assessment when my child reaches Year 10?
faqs.answer: Credit stops being awarded for effort and presentation and starts being awarded strictly against a published scheme by an examiner who has never met the student. Three habits decide a lot of the outcome: answering to the mark allocation, so three marks get three distinct points; command-term discipline, since explain requires a causal link and describe does not; and showing working so method marks survive a wrong final answer. Strong students are often hit hardest, because they have never needed to think about how an answer is credited.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a six or seven-year-old?
faqs.answer: Usually thirty to forty-five minutes rather than a full hour, segmented into short tasks. Attention is the binding constraint at this age, not ability, and paying for sixty minutes when a child concentrates for thirty-five is a quiet way to waste a tutoring budget. A good short session opens on the child's own work, teaches one thing, has the child do it unaided while the tutor watches, and ends with a short task to be marked before next time. Ask any provider what length they actually run before comparing hourly rates.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell the difference between a retrieval problem and an inference problem in reading?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing worth establishing. Retrieval questions ask the child to locate information, and errors come from reading too fast, losing place on a long passage, or answering the expected question rather than the printed one. Inference questions ask the child to reason from what the text implies, and errors come from unfamiliar vocabulary or reluctance to commit. Retrieval responds quickly to technique; inference grows slowly through vocabulary and discussion about text. One comprehension score hides which of the two you are facing.

faqs.question: Do Jumeirah primary pupils need separate support for Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because those subjects sit outside the English National Curriculum and still carry report grades. Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies whatever curriculum they are licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Instructional time runs in 40-minute lesson units. Support must work from the school's own material, since using different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: What should I keep now that will be useful at the Year 7 transfer?
faqs.answer: A baseline and a first piece of writing. At the move into Year 7 the child usually changes school, so no teacher carries their history across and the new subject specialists start from nothing. A kept two-minute fluency sheet with its date, a reading measure recorded the same way twice, and one early piece of writing marked against fixed criteria give the next teacher something concrete. It costs nothing to keep and it is the single most useful file a Dubai family can hand over at a transfer.

faqs.question: Which problems can realistically change in one tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Structured reading of a word problem, working layout in maths such as one step per line, and proofreading procedure in writing. All three are procedural rather than conceptual, so a child who has never been shown the sequence can apply it immediately. What does not change in a session is arithmetic automaticity, inference in reading, or sustained organisation across a long piece: those take months of distributed practice. A first diagnostic session usually finds at least one immediate win, which buys patience for the slower work.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for primary tuition in Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026 put a budget online tutor from about AED 33 to AED 150 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, and a qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are the providers' own figures. At primary level the premium is for diagnostic judgement rather than subject content, since the maths itself is not the hard part. Ask about session length before comparing any hourly rate.

faqs.question: Is online tuition sensible for a young child, or does it need someone in the room?
faqs.answer: It works when the setup is right and fails when it is not, and the setup is simple: a quiet room away from a television, headphones, and a tablet or document camera so the tutor sees handwriting as it is produced rather than after the fact. Sessions must be shorter and more segmented than an adult's. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, since that service exists only in India, so the free trial exists to test the format honestly before any money moves rather than to argue for it.

faqs.question: What will a tutor not do if my older child needs help with an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Write any part of it, edit a draft into its final state, or supply a topic, data set or conclusion. What a tutor will do is teach what each lettered criterion rewards, explain how marks are allocated across them, discuss a research question the student has proposed, read a draft the student wrote and name where it falls short, and coach referencing and presentation of evidence. One Dubai operator advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting purchased work is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-jumeirah-p.closingHeading: Send the result that worried you
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-jumeirah-p.closingBody: The most useful first message is not a request for a tutor but a copy of the result that prompted the search, with the year group beside it. Often the first answer is about what that assessment was designed to detect, and it saves a family from buying a term of lessons in response to a number that needed no response. Where there is a real gap, the free trial session splits the combined score into its parts and tells you in writing which half is weak. From there you can decide whether you need a few weeks of work or something longer.

intro.heading: Four science routes, and the one nobody explains
paragraphs: Science is the only part of an IGCSE timetable where the structure of the qualification itself, rather than the grade, decides what a pupil can do next. A pupil with a grade 6 in English has a grade 6 in English. A pupil with a grade 6 in Combined Science and a pupil with grade 6s in Biology, Chemistry and Physics are in materially different positions when they apply for a sixth-form science course, and the difference is in the route rather than the attainment.

Cambridge offers four of them. Combined Science, code 0653, is a single award: reduced content from all three sciences reported as one grade. Coordinated Sciences, code 0654, is a double award covering more content and reporting two grades. And the three separate sciences - Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 - are three full qualifications reported as three grades. Pearson Edexcel offers an equivalent set with its own codes. Each route has Core and Extended tiers where tiering applies, which multiplies the options again.

Options evening rarely conveys this clearly, and not through any bad faith. The choice is usually framed as how much science a pupil wants to do, which is true and incomplete. The part that goes unsaid is the consequence: several Dubai sixth forms treat Combined Science as below the entry requirement for A Level Chemistry or Physics, and some degree routes assume separate sciences at 16 without saying so. Those are facts a family can check in Year 9 and discover in Year 12.

The decision is also not purely academic. Separate sciences occupy three slots on a timetable, which means something else comes off it - often a second language, a creative subject or a humanity. On a nine or ten subject timetable that trade is real, and it interacts with other requirements. The UAE Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, which makes the shape of a timetable a practical matter as well as an academic one.

This page therefore sets out what each route contains, how the grades work, what each one keeps open, which pupil each suits, and when it is still possible to change. It also says plainly what tutoring can and cannot do about a route decision, which is less than families often hope: an outside provider can produce evidence and close a specific gap, and it cannot change which specification a centre enters its pupils for or persuade a sixth form to accept a qualification it does not accept. Tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge IGCSE 0653)
subjects.description: A single award covering reduced content from biology, chemistry and physics, reported as one grade. A sensible route for a pupil whose strengths lie elsewhere, and a constraint on A Level science entry at several Dubai sixth forms.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge IGCSE 0654)
subjects.description: A double award with more content than Combined Science and two grades reported. The middle route, and the most commonly overlooked: it keeps considerably more open than 0653 while occupying fewer timetable slots than three separate sciences.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: A full separate qualification. High content volume, lower conceptual difficulty, and the science where marks go to imprecise terminology and command-term mismatches rather than to misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: A full separate qualification where moles and organic chemistry decide the Extended-tier grade. The content most frequently reduced in the Combined and Coordinated routes is also the content A Level Chemistry assumes first.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: A full separate qualification, and the science where mathematical fluency matters most. Rearranging equations, unit conversion and sensible precision are examined inside physics questions, which is why a maths gap shows up here first.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The subject every science route depends on. A pupil on Extended-tier science with Core-tier mathematics is carrying a mismatch that will show up in the quantitative parts of chemistry and physics long before anyone names it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
subjects.description: Pearson offers separate sciences and a double award with its own codes and no tiering, which removes the ceiling question and raises a different one about accessing the whole paper. A pupil transferring mid-course needs the specifications reconciled.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Relevant to science because extended-response marks are writing marks. A pupil who cannot structure a six-mark explanation loses the same marks in physics as in English, and the repair transfers between them.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: Frequently chosen in the slot that separate sciences would have occupied. Worth knowing that it does not substitute for a science in any Dubai sixth-form science entry requirement, whatever its own merits.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Mandatory provision in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, under KHDA's requirements. Relevant to timetable planning because Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the MoE's five-subject equivalency count.

sections.heading: The four routes, and what the choice actually is
paragraphs: The question at options evening is usually posed as how much science a pupil wants to take. The question that will matter in two years is what the award structure is, because that is what a sixth-form admissions page refers to. Combined Science 0653 produces one grade from reduced content across the three disciplines. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award with more content and two grades. The separate sciences produce three grades from three full qualifications.

That structural difference has three consequences. First, timetable space: separate sciences take three option slots, Coordinated Sciences typically takes two, and Combined Science takes one. Second, the certificate: a pupil with three separate science grades has three subjects on their certificate where a Combined Science pupil has one. Third, admissions: a requirement expressed as 'grade 7 in Chemistry' is satisfied by 0620 and is a different question entirely for a 0653 candidate.

Tiering layers on top of all of it. The Cambridge science routes offer Core and Extended tiers, and Core entry caps the grade scale regardless of how well the papers are answered. So a pupil can be on the right route at the wrong tier, or the right tier on a route that does not open the door they want. Those are two separate conversations and they are routinely merged into one vague worry about science being difficult.

The practical instruction is to establish, in writing, exactly what your child is entered for: the code, the award type and the tier. Then look up the sixth-form science entry requirements for the schools you would plausibly consider. Those two pieces of information answer most of the anxiety in this area, and both are available for the cost of an email. Always confirm the current structure on the live Cambridge or Pearson documentation, because specifications are revised.

sections.heading: What Combined Science covers, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Combined Science is not a watered-down version of each separate science; it is a selection from each. The syllabus takes core material from biology, chemistry and physics and omits the parts that are most demanding and, not coincidentally, the parts that A Level courses assume first. The specific omissions vary by series and must be read from the live syllabus, but the pattern is consistent: the quantitative and the abstract go first.

In chemistry that typically means reduced treatment of the mole and of organic chemistry, which are the two topics A Level Chemistry builds on in its opening weeks. In physics it means reduced treatment of the more mathematical areas, which are the same areas A Level Physics assumes. In biology the reduction is more in breadth than in depth, which is part of why a Combined Science pupil moving to A Level Biology usually has a smaller gap than one moving to A Level Chemistry.

That asymmetry is worth knowing because it changes the advice. A pupil on Combined Science who later wants A Level Biology is in a recoverable position with a summer of work. The same pupil wanting A Level Chemistry or Physics faces a larger gap in content that is also conceptually harder, and a sixth form may reasonably decline the application rather than set them up to struggle. This is not gatekeeping for its own sake.

None of this makes Combined Science a poor choice. For a pupil whose strengths and intentions lie in languages, humanities, creative subjects or business, it is a sensible way to hold a science qualification without surrendering three option slots to it. The error is choosing it while intending a science route later, and that error is made at options evening by families who were never told the two were connected.

sections.heading: The grade arithmetic: one, two or three grades
paragraphs: A certificate is a list, and the length of the list matters in ways families do not anticipate. A pupil taking nine subjects with three separate sciences has nine entries of which three are sciences. A pupil taking nine subjects with Combined Science has nine entries of which one is a science, and two of the freed slots went elsewhere. Both are nine-subject pupils; their certificates look quite different to anyone reading them.

The UAE adds a specific reason to think about this. The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. For most pupils with a full timetable this is comfortably met either way. For a pupil on a thinner timetable it is arithmetic worth checking, and how a double award is counted for that purpose is a question for the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority rather than for a tutoring page.

There is also a risk-spreading argument that cuts both ways. Three separate science grades mean a bad day in one paper affects one grade. One Combined Science grade means the whole science outcome rests on a smaller number of papers, which is lower exposure in some respects and higher concentration in others. Neither is obviously safer, and families who think about it usually conclude that the sixth-form consequence outweighs the risk profile.

The useful discipline here is to write the actual certificate out. List the nine or ten subjects your child will have, with the science route named by its code and award type, and then read that list as an admissions officer or an attestation clerk would. Anything that looks thin on paper is worth reconsidering while the choice is still open, which is a Year 9 conversation and not a Year 11 one.

sections.heading: Sixth-form consequences, subject by subject
paragraphs: Dubai sixth forms publish science entry grades and they apply them, which makes this the part of the decision with the hardest edges. A requirement stated as a grade in Chemistry is straightforwardly satisfied by Chemistry 0620 and is a matter of departmental discretion for a Combined Science candidate. Some departments accept a strong Coordinated Sciences double award; some do not; several publish their position explicitly.

Science departments also frequently publish a mathematics requirement alongside the science one, and that catches families out more often than the science rule does. A pupil with a strong Chemistry grade and a weak Extended-tier mathematics grade is a weaker A Level Chemistry candidate than the grades suggest, because the quantitative work in Year 12 assumes the mathematics. Some departments say so; others simply decline the application.

For the IB Diploma the position is different in form and similar in substance. A pupil takes one or two sciences at Higher or Standard Level within the group structure, and Higher Level sciences assume secure Extended-tier content. A Combined Science background is a thinner base for Higher Level Chemistry than a separate Chemistry qualification is, and the first term of the course will reveal that rather than forgive it.

The only reliable action is to look the requirements up while the options decision is still open. Pick two or three sixth forms you would plausibly consider, find their published science entry grades for the courses your child might want, and note any mathematics requirement attached. That exercise takes an afternoon in Year 9 and removes almost all the uncertainty that otherwise arrives in Year 12.

sections.heading: Coordinated Sciences as the middle route
paragraphs: Coordinated Sciences 0654 is the route fewest families consider and the one that resolves the most dilemmas. It is a double award: more content than Combined Science, two grades reported rather than one, and typically two timetable slots rather than three. For a pupil who wants to keep a science route open without giving three option slots to science, it is the obvious candidate and it is frequently not mentioned at all.

Its strength is coverage. The content is substantially closer to the separate sciences than Combined Science is, which means a pupil arriving at a Higher Level or A Level science from this route has a smaller gap to close. Its weakness is recognition: because it is less common than either alternative, individual sixth-form departments vary in how they treat it, and a family cannot assume it will be accepted for a specific A Level course without asking.

That makes the action straightforward. If Coordinated Sciences is on the table at your child's school, ask the two or three sixth forms you would consider whether a double award at a stated grade satisfies their A Level science entry requirement. The answers will be specific and they will differ. With those answers in hand the route becomes either an excellent compromise or a route to avoid, and either way the decision is informed.

One caveat worth stating. Not every Dubai school offers all four routes, and a school with a growing secondary phase may offer two. If the route that suits your child is not available at their school, that is a fact to weigh in a school decision rather than a problem tutoring can solve. No amount of outside support changes which specification a centre enters its pupils for.

sections.heading: Which pupil suits which route
paragraphs: The right route is a function of three things and none of them is how hard the pupil finds science. The first is intention: what post-16 and degree routes are plausibly in view. The second is the pupil's actual profile across the three disciplines, which is frequently uneven in ways reports do not show. The third is timetable pressure, meaning what would have to be given up to accommodate three sciences.

Where a pupil is strong across all three disciplines and intends a science route, separate sciences is the answer and the conversation is short. Where a pupil has no science intentions at all and strong interests elsewhere, Combined Science is the answer and that conversation is short too. The difficult cases sit in the middle: a pupil strong in biology and chemistry and weak in physics, or a pupil with no settled intentions at fourteen, which describes most fourteen-year-olds.

For the uneven pupil, the question is whether the weak discipline is weak for a fixable reason. Physics is the usual culprit and the usual cause is mathematical rather than physical: a pupil who cannot rearrange an equation fluently will find physics hard in a way that looks like a lack of aptitude. That is testable in a single session and fixable in a term if caught in Year 9, which can change what route is realistic.

For the pupil with no settled intentions, the general principle is to keep doors open where the cost of doing so is bearable. Coordinated Sciences, or two separate sciences with one dropped, keeps more open than Combined Science at a smaller timetable cost than three. That is a defensible default, and it is better than choosing the narrowest route at fourteen on the basis that nothing has been decided.

sections.heading: Moving between routes, and when that stops being possible
paragraphs: There are two deadlines and they are different. The options deadline, internal to the school, fixes what a pupil is taught from the start of Year 10. The examination entry deadline, set by the board and administered through the centre, fixes what they sit. In between there is a window where a change is sometimes possible and always awkward, because a pupil moving from Combined Science to separate sciences part-way through has missed content the class has already covered.

The practical reality is that a change in the first term of Year 10 is usually feasible with support. A change in the second year is rarely sensible even where it is administratively possible, because the content gap is substantial and the time is not. A change of tier within the same route is a different and easier matter, and it can often be made as late as the autumn of Year 11 if the department is persuaded.

What persuades a department is evidence in the form it uses. A timed Extended-tier paper from the relevant separate science, marked against the published mark scheme, showing the pupil reaching the content, is a document a head of science can read in five minutes. Parental conviction, however well founded, cannot be acted on the same way. Ask the department directly what evidence it would want and when its internal deadline falls.

Where a change is genuinely not possible, the honest plan is to work with what exists. A Combined Science pupil intending A Level Biology can prepare properly over the summer and present a case. One intending A Level Chemistry needs to have a frank conversation about whether that course is the right one, and about alternatives that lead to similar destinations. Pretending the gap is smaller than it is serves nobody and costs a term of Year 12.
