sections.heading: What a tutor can and cannot do about a science route
paragraphs: Tutoring can do three useful things here and it cannot do the fourth. It can produce the evidence that informs or challenges a route recommendation, by having the pupil sit separate-science questions under timing and marking them properly. It can close the specific gap - usually mathematical - that made one discipline look weaker than it is. And it can prepare a pupil on a reduced route for the content a post-16 course will assume.

What it cannot do is change what a centre enters a pupil for, or make a sixth-form department accept a qualification it does not accept. Those are institutional decisions and no outside provider influences them. A page that implies otherwise is overselling, and a provider who takes money to prepare a pupil for an entry requirement they cannot meet has sold something other than teaching.

The honesty line applies here as everywhere. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including a school practical write-up contributing to an internally assessed mark. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate.

Nor should board material be handed over as files. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides, and the correct behaviour is to link the official page so a family reads the current version. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and makes no such claim. There is no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and getting started
paragraphs: All four Cambridge science routes and the Pearson equivalents are covered in this set at both tiers, and a match is usually quick for the common combinations. Thinner briefs exist: Coordinated Sciences 0654 specifically, rather than the separate sciences, and mid-course reconciliation between a Cambridge route and a Pearson one. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free, and that is better stated than filled with a generalist.

So a Metropole science enquiry ends in one of three ways, and a family is entitled to be told which one. Either the route brief is covered, and a trial lesson goes into the diary within days. Or it is covered by a specialist teaching into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is said out loud rather than concealed behind a local-looking telephone number. Or nobody currently holds that brief, in which case it is named as uncovered instead of handed to a generalist who last opened a Coordinated Sciences specification years ago. The third answer is the one worth trusting a provider for, because it is the one that costs them the booking. Where a tutor happens to sit makes no difference to the rate.

There is one credential a parent can genuinely verify, so verify that rather than a badge on a homepage. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Its eligibility list is wide enough to explain the range of people offering science help around a school of this size: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school pupils aged fifteen to eighteen. A sixth-former who did well in the separate sciences can hold that permit entirely legitimately. Whether that person should be advising on a route decision with sixth-form consequences attached is a different question, and the permit does not answer it. Tutoring with no permit at all attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no schedule of amounts has been published, treat any figure quoted to you as invented.

Starting is small. A free trial lesson is one session, with no card details required, and the useful things to bring are the specification code and award type from the examinations officer, your child's last marked science script, and the published science entry grades from two sixth forms you would consider. With those three, the route question can usually be answered within the hour rather than carried for two years.

process.title: Establish the code and the award type
process.description: Ask the examinations officer in writing which science specification your child is entered for and what kind of award it is: 0653 single, 0654 double, or the separate 0610, 0620 and 0625. A prospectus saying 'IGCSE Science' has not answered the question, and the answer determines everything else on this page.

process.title: Look up two sixth forms' science entry rules
process.description: Find the published science entry grades for the A Level or Diploma courses your child might plausibly want, at two or three schools you would consider, and note any mathematics requirement attached. This afternoon of work in Year 9 removes almost all the uncertainty that otherwise arrives in Year 12.

process.title: Test whether a weak discipline is fixable
process.description: Physics is usually the discipline that pushes a pupil towards a reduced route, and the cause is usually mathematical rather than physical. A single session of equation rearranging and unit work establishes which it is. If it is mathematical, it is fixable in a term and the route calculation changes.

process.title: Ask about the school's own options deadline
process.description: The internal deadline that fixes what a pupil is taught is earlier and less visible than the board's entry deadline. A route change in the first term of Year 10 is often feasible; the same change a year later rarely is. Knowing the date is what makes the difference between a decision and a regret.

process.title: Buy the practical component block regardless of route
process.description: Every science route examines a practical or alternative-to-practical component worth around a fifth of the grade, and it tests written method rather than laboratory skill. Six to eight sessions on it raises marks across every science the pupil takes at once, which makes it the best-value science purchase on any route.

whyPoints.title: Routes named by code and award type
whyPoints.description: Work starts from 0653, 0654, 0610, 0620 or 0625 and the tier on the entry, because those are the terms a sixth-form admissions page and an attestation authority use. A conversation about science being hard cannot answer a question about award structures.

whyPoints.title: Sixth-form consequences stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Each post-16 science course is listed with what it normally requires at 16, where Combined Science usually sits, and the mathematics requirement families most often miss. Those are checkable facts rather than general encouragement to do more science.

whyPoints.title: The middle route brought into the conversation
whyPoints.description: Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award that keeps considerably more open than Combined Science at a smaller timetable cost than three separate sciences, and it is the route fewest families are told about. Whether local sixth forms accept it is a specific question with a specific answer.

whyPoints.title: The physics question tested rather than assumed
whyPoints.description: A pupil pushed towards a reduced route by weak physics is usually weak for mathematical reasons, which is testable in one session and fixable in a term when caught in Year 9. That single test sometimes changes which route is realistic.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a brief such as Coordinated Sciences 0654 has no specialist free, that is named rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what tutoring cannot change
whyPoints.description: No provider influences which specification a centre enters its pupils for, or whether a sixth form accepts a qualification. Tutoring produces evidence, closes gaps and prepares for what a course assumes. Anything beyond that is overselling, and so is any claim of regulator or board approval.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Combined Science and separate sciences at GEMS Metropole School?
faqs.answer: The award structure, which is what sixth forms actually read. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is a single award: reduced content from biology, chemistry and physics reported as one grade, taking one option slot. The separate sciences - Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 - are three full qualifications reported as three grades across three slots. A requirement expressed as a grade in Chemistry is satisfied directly by 0620 and becomes a matter of departmental discretion for a Combined Science candidate, which is the difference that matters.

faqs.question: What is Coordinated Sciences 0654 and why has nobody mentioned it?
faqs.answer: It is a double award sitting between the two usual options: more content than Combined Science, two grades reported, and typically two timetable slots rather than three. It is less common than either alternative, which is probably why it gets less attention at options evening, and its content is substantially closer to the separate sciences. The catch is recognition: individual sixth-form departments vary in whether they accept it for A Level sciences, so the useful action is to ask two or three directly before choosing it.

faqs.question: Does Combined Science close off A Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: At several Dubai sixth forms, effectively yes, and the position is usually published rather than hidden. Combined Science typically reduces the quantitative chemistry, including the mole, and the organic depth - which are precisely the areas A Level Chemistry builds on in its opening weeks. A department declining the application is not gatekeeping for its own sake; it is avoiding setting a pupil up to struggle. A Level Biology is more often negotiable with a strong Combined grade and a prepared summer, because the reduction there is more in breadth than depth.

faqs.question: Which sciences are most reduced on the Combined route?
faqs.answer: Chemistry and physics, in the areas that are most quantitative and most abstract. In chemistry that generally means the mole and organic depth; in physics, the more mathematical treatment throughout. Biology is reduced more in breadth than in depth, which is why a Combined Science pupil moving to A Level Biology usually has a smaller gap than one moving to Chemistry or Physics. The exact omissions vary by series, so read them from the live Cambridge syllabus for your child's entry rather than from any summary.

faqs.question: Can my child switch from Combined Science to separate sciences part-way through?
faqs.answer: In the first term of Year 10, usually yes with support. In the second year, rarely sensibly, even where it is administratively possible, because the content gap is substantial and the remaining time is not. A tier change within the same route is a different and easier matter and can often be made as late as the autumn of Year 11. Ask the school about its internal options deadline, which is earlier and less visible than the board's entry deadline, and ask what evidence the department would want.

faqs.question: Is my child's weak physics a reason to take Combined Science?
faqs.answer: Only after you have tested why it is weak, because the usual cause is mathematical rather than physical. A pupil who cannot rearrange an equation fluently, convert units confidently or give a sensible precision will find physics hard in a way that looks exactly like a lack of aptitude. That is testable in a single session: three Extended-tier calculations and watching what happens in the first thirty seconds. If the cause is mathematical, it is fixable in a term when caught in Year 9, and the route calculation changes substantially.

faqs.question: How many option slots do the different science routes take?
faqs.answer: Three separate sciences take three slots, Coordinated Sciences typically takes two, and Combined Science takes one. That is a real trade on a nine or ten subject timetable: what comes off is often a second language, a creative subject or a humanity. The decision is therefore not only about science, and it is worth writing out the whole prospective certificate before choosing. A list that looks thin on paper is worth reconsidering while the choice is still open, which is a Year 9 conversation.

faqs.question: Does the science route affect the UAE equivalency subject count?
faqs.answer: Potentially, through the shape of the timetable. The Ministry of Education's British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. For a pupil with a full timetable this is comfortably met on any science route. For a thinner timetable it is arithmetic worth checking, and how a double award is counted for that purpose is a question for moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority rather than for a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Do sixth forms also set a mathematics requirement for science courses?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and this catches families out more often than the science rule does. The quantitative work in Year 12 chemistry and physics assumes Extended-tier mathematics, so a pupil with a strong science grade and a weak maths grade is a weaker candidate than their grades suggest. Some Dubai departments publish a mathematics requirement explicitly alongside the science one; others simply decline the application without explaining. Ask the department directly in Year 10, because the mathematics gap is usually the cheaper of the two to close.

faqs.question: Is the practical paper worth preparing for on every route?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the best-value science purchase available whichever route a pupil is on. Every science route examines a practical or alternative-to-practical component worth around a fifth of the grade, and it tests written precision rather than laboratory skill: describing a method with quantities and instruments stated, identifying variables, reading scales, tabulating, plotting, interpreting and suggesting a specific improvement. Six to eight sessions on it raises marks across every science a pupil takes at once, which no amount of single-subject content work can do.

faqs.question: What if our school does not offer the route that suits our child?
faqs.answer: Then it is a fact to weigh in a school decision rather than a problem tutoring can solve, and that is worth saying plainly. A centre enters its pupils for the specifications it has chosen to teach, and no outside provider changes that. A school with a growing secondary phase may offer two of the four routes rather than all of them. Dubai's market is deep enough that the question is answerable at the point of choosing a school: KHDA counted 227 private schools in the emirate, with seven more joining the 2026-27 intake.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a school science practical write-up on any of these routes?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the write-up needs and give feedback on the pupil's own draft, naming what the mark scheme wants that is missing. A tutor cannot write it, supply paragraphs for it, or edit it to completion, and no price makes that acceptable - particularly where the write-up contributes to an internally assessed mark that must represent the pupil's own work. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice risk rather than a service.

faqs.question: Do you send science tutors to Motor City or Arabian Ranches addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For science that works well, because the highest-value work - practical paper methods and extended-response rewriting - is the pupil writing while the tutor marks live on a shared screen. It also means the tutor is chosen for the specification and award type rather than for living within a drivable radius.

faqs.question: What should we bring to a first conversation about the science route?
faqs.answer: Three things. The specification code and award type from the examinations officer, in writing. Your child's last marked science script, not the report grade. And the published science entry grades from two or three sixth forms you would plausibly consider, including any mathematics requirement. With those, the route question can usually be resolved within the hour rather than carried as a worry for two years. The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-modern-aca.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach CBSE subjects at Class IX to XII and IB Diploma subjects at Higher or Standard Level. Crossing work between the two is a distinct request and is matched to somebody who has taught inside both systems rather than one.

intro.heading: The content carries across; the assessment does not
paragraphs: GEMS Modern Academy at Nad Al Sheba runs the Indian curriculum with the International Baccalaureate Diploma available in the senior years, which puts a particular crossing in front of a lot of households here. A student completes Class X on a system built around terminal board examinations marked out of a hundred per subject, and then enters a programme where twenty to thirty per cent of every subject grade is produced away from the examination hall, against published criteria, over several months. The content overlaps substantially. Almost nothing else does.

That mismatch is the most under-supported moment in an Indian-curriculum household's school career, and it is widespread: Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with the Indian curriculum accounting for twenty-six per cent of enrolment, second only to the UK curriculum at thirty-seven. A large number of families make this crossing every year, and the advice available to them is mostly about prestige rather than about what actually changes.

What changes is specific and listable. Six subjects instead of four or five, across six prescribed groups rather than a chosen stream. An internal assessment in every subject, which is independent research rather than a prescribed practical. A core consisting of an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge course examined through an essay of up to 1,600 words and an exhibition commentary of up to 950, and CAS, which carries no points but blocks the diploma if incomplete. And command terms that specify what an answer must do, with mark schemes built around that specification.

A CBSE-trained student arrives with genuine strengths for this. The content load in Class XII sciences and mathematics is heavy, the computational fluency is usually strong, and the habit of sustained preparation for a terminal examination transfers directly to the Diploma papers. What is missing is independent research design, writing against criteria rather than for a model answer, and the project-management capacity that a 4,000-word essay and three internal assessments demand simultaneously.

IB Gram supports families at this school with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that position appears on every country page this site publishes. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, read in October 2026. No IB session or results date appears here, because none could be verified from the organisation's own site; take every date from the school. The same caution applies to the weightings and criteria quoted below, which were read from the current subject guides: guides get revised, and your child's coordinator holds the version that governs their cohort, so treat the figures here as a map of where the marks sit rather than as the authority for them.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-modern-aca.programmesIntro: Four stages, and the crossing sits between the second and the third. Knowing which one your child is in determines whether tutoring should be teaching content or teaching a new way of being assessed.

programmes.name: CBSE Classes IX and X
programmes.description: Culminating in Class X board examinations, with internal assessment forming a defined portion of the mark in several subjects and the rest coming from terminal papers marked out of a hundred. Mathematics is offered at more than one level, and that choice has consequences for the stream available afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: The decision at the end of Class X is the real one: stream for Class XI and XII, or cross into the Diploma. Families often treat it as a single question when it is two, because a student can be well suited to the Diploma's structure and poorly suited to carrying six subjects, or the reverse. Both deserve asking separately.

programmes.name: CBSE Classes XI and XII
programmes.description: A chosen stream of four or five subjects, with Class XII board examinations marked out of a hundred per subject and practical components in the sciences. Aggregate percentage is the headline figure most admissions processes read, which concentrates the pressure on a single examination season.
programmes.countryNote: The tutoring pattern here is intensive and content-led, because the assessment is content-led. That is a genuinely different job from Diploma support, and a tutor experienced in one does not automatically transfer. Ask any prospective tutor which system they have actually taught, and for how long, before matching.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum and up to three bonus points from the core matrix. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject.
programmes.countryNote: For a CBSE-trained student the papers are the familiar part and the internal assessment is not. The first term of support should therefore be weighted towards research design, criteria and project management rather than towards content, which is the opposite of what most families expect to buy.

programmes.name: IGCSE, where a student crosses to a British school
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with tiering into Core and Extended on Cambridge or Foundation and Higher on Pearson Edexcel, and a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. Closer to CBSE in shape than the Diploma is, but with different tiering and different practical assessment.
programmes.countryNote: A CBSE student moving to IGCSE finds the assessment logic familiar and the administration unfamiliar. Establish the syllabus code immediately, because Cambridge sciences carry a practical component worth twenty per cent while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam at all, and tiering decides the grade ceiling before teaching starts.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-modern-aca.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject with the specific thing that changes between CBSE and the Diploma. The content overlap is usually large; the note names what is genuinely new.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A CBSE-trained student usually arrives with strong computational fluency and less practice at written justification. Standard Level is two papers at forty per cent each plus the Exploration at twenty; Higher Level adds Paper 3 at twenty, an extended-response problem paper unlike anything in a board examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure, with modelling and statistics in place of the heavier pure content. The new demand is written interpretation in context: an answer that states a number without saying what it means in the situation scores below its potential.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content overlap with Class XII physics is substantial. What is new is uncertainty handling, unfamiliar graph analysis in the Paper 1 data section, and an independent investigation capped at 3,000 words rather than a prescribed practical with a known method.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Again heavy overlap, with energetics and organic mechanisms as the Higher Level separators. The investigation is the genuine novelty: the student designs it, which is a research skill no board practical requires because the method is given.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content load is comparable to Class XII and the command-term discipline is tighter. A student used to writing everything they know about a topic loses marks in the Diploma for answering a different question from the one asked, which is a habit rather than a gap.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level Paper 1 at thirty per cent, Paper 2 at forty, portfolio at thirty; Higher Level adds a third paper and reduces the portfolio to twenty. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each on real published articles, which has no CBSE equivalent.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for the Higher Level paper that can be worked months in advance. The shift from a content-recall examination to applying a concept to a specific described business is the adjustment that takes longest.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level Paper 1 at thirty-five per cent, Paper 2 at thirty-five, Individual Oral at thirty; Higher Level adds the HL Essay at twenty. The oral component is new to most CBSE students and is rehearsable, which makes it good value per hour.

subjects.name: Hindi and other language options
subjects.levels: HL, SL, B and ab initio
subjects.description: Language group placement matters more than families expect, because a language studied as a first language and the same language studied as an acquisition course are different qualifications with different ceilings. Ask the coordinator which placement is proposed and on what basis.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A solution-development internal assessment where documentation is assessed alongside the working product. Students with strong programming from a CBSE background routinely lose marks on documentation, because the criteria reward evidence of a design process rather than code that runs.

sections.heading: The CBSE to Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: One competitor in this market has a single subheading on curriculum transition. Nobody publishes a structured subject-by-subject version, which is odd given that the Indian curriculum accounts for twenty-six per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment. The gap is not a general increase in difficulty, and in several subjects the CBSE content is heavier. It is a specific set of things the Diploma assumes a student can already do, and the set differs by subject.

In mathematics the computational fluency transfers well and the written justification does not. CBSE rewards a correct method and a correct answer; the Diploma also rewards explaining why the method applies, and at Higher Level the third paper asks for sustained reasoning across an extended problem. A student who has drilled hundreds of questions arrives fast and accurate and loses marks on the parts that ask for an argument rather than a result.

In the sciences the content overlap with Class XII is substantial and the investigation is genuinely new. A CBSE practical has a prescribed method; a Diploma investigation requires the student to design one, and research design is one of four criteria carrying six marks each out of twenty-four, with the whole piece capped at 3,000 words. It is also the only one of the four that cannot be repaired once data has been collected, which makes a planning conversation before any practical work the highest-value single session in the subject.

In the humanities and in English the shift is from content recall to argument and analysis. A Diploma extended-response answer rewards a judgement supported by evidence; an answer that covers the topic comprehensively without reaching a position scores in a lower band. And across every subject there are command terms, a small closed vocabulary specifying what an answer must do, with mark schemes built around that specification. That is the cheapest thing to fix and the thing nobody teaches explicitly.

sections.heading: What each system actually rewards
paragraphs: Set the two side by side and the difference stops being about reputation. CBSE Class XII concentrates the grade in terminal board examinations marked out of a hundred per subject, with practical components in the sciences, and the headline figure most admissions processes read is an aggregate percentage. That rewards comprehensive content coverage, computational accuracy, and the ability to sustain preparation across a single intense examination season.

The Diploma distributes the grade. Each of six subjects produces a grade from one to seven, built from timed papers plus an internal assessment worth typically twenty to thirty per cent, and the total out of 45 includes up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. That rewards breadth, deadline management across two years, and the ability to write against published criteria. It also forgives a weak patch in a way a single examination season does not, and punishes a disorganised autumn in a way CBSE does not.

There is a further structural difference worth naming. CBSE allows a chosen stream of four or five subjects, so a student can concentrate on what they are good at. The Diploma requires one subject from each of six groups by design, which means a student who is sharply uneven carries their weakest area for two years. For some students that breadth is valuable and for others it is a standing tax, and the honest comparison depends on which kind of student yours is rather than on which qualification sounds better.

Neither system is harder. They are differently shaped, and the shape suits different students. A student who struggles with deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way that no amount of subject tutoring repairs. A student who performs poorly under single-season examination pressure will find the Diploma's distributed assessment a relief. That is the comparison to make, and the evidence for it already exists in how your child handled Class IX and X.

sections.heading: Mathematics: from CBSE into one of four Diploma courses
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a crossing student and the one most often made without information. CBSE offers mathematics at more than one level at Class X, and the Diploma offers two distinct courses — Analysis and Approaches, and Applications and Interpretation — each at Higher and Standard Level, which makes four destinations from one starting point. They are different courses rather than difficulty settings, and some university programmes specify one of the two.

A CBSE-trained student typically arrives with an advantage in pure technique. Algebraic manipulation, trigonometric identities and calculus procedures are drilled more thoroughly in a CBSE Class XI and XII sequence than in most systems, which means Analysis and Approaches content is often less alarming than it looks. The difficulty appears in two places: proof, which is examinable in the Diploma in a way it is not in a board examination, and the extended-response problem paper at Higher Level, which asks for sustained reasoning rather than the application of a known method.

Applications and Interpretation is not the easier route and should not be chosen as one. It emphasises modelling and statistics, and it requires written interpretation in context: an answer that produces a number without saying what the number means in the situation described scores below its potential. For a student who is strong computationally and weak at written explanation, Applications can be the harder of the two, which is the opposite of the usual assumption.

The decision should be made on university prerequisites read from those universities' own pages, not from any tutoring site including this one. Prerequisites change, they vary by institution and country, and some engineering and mathematics programmes name a specific course and level. Check before the subject form is signed, because changing after the first term is disruptive and at some schools not possible.

sections.heading: The internal assessment habit nobody has needed yet
paragraphs: A CBSE practical has a method. The student follows it, records results, and writes up against a known format. A Diploma internal assessment has a criterion list and nothing else: in the sciences the student chooses a research question, designs the investigation, controls the variables, collects enough data, analyses it with uncertainties carried through, concludes against the scientific context and evaluates with realistic improvements proposed. The piece is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four, six marks for each of research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

That is a research skill rather than a study skill, and it is the single largest novelty in the crossing. The most common failure is not laziness or weak science. It is a research question too broad to be answered with the data that can realistically be collected in the available time, which is a planning error made in week one and discovered at the first draft. Because research design cannot be repaired after the data exists, that error is terminal for six of the twenty-four marks.

The same pattern repeats across the other internal assessments. The mathematics Exploration needs a question of appropriate scope. The Economics portfolio needs three commentaries of no more than 800 words each on real published articles, each tightly focused. The Extended Essay at 4,000 words needs a question the available sources can actually support. In every case the highest-value intervention is one session at the planning stage, and in every case families buy support at the drafting stage instead.

What legitimate help looks like is narrow and should be stated before work begins. A tutor may explain each criterion in the board's published wording, help turn a broad question into a researchable one, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work; submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice and the finding lands on the student.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the fastest marks in the crossing
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject guide publishes a list of command terms with definitions, and every paper uses them deliberately. State, outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, justify and compare each specify what an answer must do, and the mark scheme is built around that specification rather than around the topic. An answer that is entirely true but addresses the wrong command scores a fraction of the marks available.

This is where a CBSE-trained student loses most avoidable marks in their first Diploma year, and the reason is structural rather than a failing. A board examination rewards comprehensive coverage: writing everything relevant about a topic is a sensible strategy when the marking rewards content. In the Diploma that strategy loses marks, because an examiner marking an explain question is looking for a mechanism and will not award credit for a description however thorough.

It is also the fastest thing to fix in the entire crossing. An hour spent sorting past-paper questions by command term, writing only the first sentence of each answer, and comparing those sentences against the mark scheme moves more marks than an hour of new content at almost any point in the two years. Two or three sessions on it usually produces visible change on the next marked script, which makes it the sensible first target rather than an afterthought.

The test to apply to any prospective tutor is short. Ask what the difference is between describe and explain in your child's subject, and what it is worth. Somebody who has taught the Diploma answers with an example from a paper in under a minute. Somebody whose experience is content-led will answer in the abstract, which tells you they will teach material where the marks are being lost on question analysis.

sections.heading: Languages and the group structure
paragraphs: The Diploma's six-group requirement produces one decision that Indian-curriculum families regularly get wrong, and it concerns languages. Group one is studies in language and literature, taken as a first language. Group two is language acquisition, with ab initio for a genuine beginner, B at Standard Level for a working speaker and B at Higher Level for someone approaching fluency. A language studied as a first language and the same language studied as an acquisition course are different qualifications with different ceilings and different work.

The error that costs most is placing a student with real home fluency into an acquisition course a level or two below their ability. It produces a comfortable grade, teaches almost nothing, and consumes a sixth of the Diploma for two years. The opposite error, placing a partial speaker at Higher Level B, produces two years of unnecessary difficulty. Both are avoidable with a short assessment and a conversation with the coordinator before the subject form is returned.

There is also a UAE requirement running underneath all of this that affects the week rather than the Diploma grade. Private schools in the emirate must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside whichever curriculum they are licensed for, with classes organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes strictly prohibited because the expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit.

One rule limits what a tutor can honestly offer in those subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means tutoring works from the school's own material rather than from a parallel scheme. Anyone selling a separate curriculum for Arabic or Islamic Education is describing something the regulations do not permit.

sections.heading: Deciding at the end of Class X, on evidence
paragraphs: The decision at the end of Class X is really two questions, and treating it as one is where households go wrong. The first is whether the Diploma's structure suits the student: six subjects across six prescribed groups, internal assessment in every one, a core with deadlines spread across two years, and a score assembled rather than earned in a single season. The second is whether the student's academic profile suits it: are they broadly capable, or sharply stronger in two or three areas?

A student who is broadly strong and reasonably organised does well in the Diploma, and the breadth is a genuine benefit rather than a tax. A student who is sharply uneven carries their weakest group for two years, and a chosen CBSE stream lets them avoid that entirely. A student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing regardless of ability, because CAS carries no points but blocks the diploma if incomplete, and the Extended Essay and internal assessments are internally deadlined in clusters.

The evidence for all of that already exists in how Classes IX and X went, and it is more useful than any comparison of the two qualifications' reputations. Did the student keep on top of work set over weeks, or produce it the night before? Did they handle the internal assessment components of Class X subjects or only the terminal papers? Were their marks even across subjects or concentrated? Those three answers predict the Diploma experience better than a percentage does.

Where a short block of tutoring genuinely helps is in making that comparison concrete: two or three sessions walking through the actual courses under consideration with somebody who has taught inside both systems, built from the student's own record rather than from general advice. It is an unusual purchase and frequently the best-value tutoring a crossing household ever buys, because it operates on a decision that shapes two years rather than a topic that shapes a term.

sections.heading: Materials, authorship and the position of this site
paragraphs: Subject guides, specifications, past papers, mark schemes, board question papers and grade-boundary tables belong to the bodies that publish them. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. Reference and link so that a parent reads the authoritative document. Everything factual on this page about weightings, criteria and caps should be confirmed against the current guide through the school.

On assessed work the line is authorship and it is not a matter of degree. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. A useful test is to ask what they would do if your child requested one written paragraph; a refusal with an explanation is the right answer.

On permits, the cost is zero, which removes an excuse. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

And position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, has no arrangement with any school named on this page, and makes no claim about any university's admissions decisions.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from CBSE Class X into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Larger in assessment than in content, and the content is sometimes heavier on the CBSE side. What changes is six subjects across six prescribed groups instead of a chosen stream, an internal assessment worth twenty to thirty per cent in every subject, a core consisting of the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and command terms that specify what an answer must do. A CBSE-trained student arrives strong on content and preparation stamina and short on independent research design.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to homes in Nad Al Sheba?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, read in October 2026. For crossing work the useful person is somebody who has taught inside both systems, which has nothing to do with distance.

faqs.question: Why does a CBSE student lose marks on IB papers despite knowing the content?
faqs.answer: Because command terms specify what an answer must do and the mark scheme is built around that specification. A board examination rewards comprehensive coverage, so writing everything relevant about a topic is a sensible strategy there. In the Diploma an examiner marking an explain question is looking for a mechanism and will not credit a description however thorough. Correcting that is the fastest mark movement in the entire crossing and usually shows on the next marked script.

faqs.question: What is the IB internal assessment, compared with a CBSE practical?
faqs.answer: A CBSE practical has a prescribed method to follow and write up. A Diploma investigation has only a criterion list: the student chooses the research question, designs the investigation, controls variables, collects enough data, analyses it with uncertainties carried through, concludes against the science and evaluates with realistic improvements. It is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four, with research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carrying six marks. That is a research skill, not a study skill.

faqs.question: Which IB mathematics course suits a CBSE-trained student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree they are aiming at, and the prerequisites should be read on those universities' own pages. CBSE students usually arrive strong in algebraic technique, which makes Analysis and Approaches content less alarming than expected, with proof and the Higher Level extended-response paper as the real gaps. Applications and Interpretation is not the easier option: it requires written interpretation in context, and a student strong computationally but weak at explanation can find it harder.

faqs.question: When should a crossing block be taken?
faqs.answer: Over the summer between Class X and the start of the Diploma, finishing before term begins rather than running alongside it. Six to ten sessions on research design, writing against criteria rather than for a model answer, and the project-management habit a 4,000-word essay demands, with one subject as the worked example. A student who arrives already familiar with the new assessment language starts slightly ahead instead of catching up from week three.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment criterion is most urgent to get right?
faqs.answer: Research design, because it is the only one of the four that cannot be repaired once the data has been collected. It covers the research question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned, and it carries six of the investigation's twenty-four marks. The usual failure is a question too broad to be answered with the data realistically collectable in the time available, made in week one and discovered at the first draft.

faqs.question: Should my child stay on CBSE or move to the IB Diploma after Class X?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions rather than one. Does the structure suit them: six subjects across six groups, internal assessment in every one, and a core deadlined across two years? And does their profile suit it: are they broadly capable or sharply stronger in two or three areas? A chosen CBSE stream lets an uneven student avoid their weakest area entirely. A student who misses deadlines finds the Diploma core punishing regardless of ability.

faqs.question: What evidence should the Class X decision be based on?
faqs.answer: How Classes IX and X actually went, rather than the aggregate percentage. Did work set over several weeks get done across those weeks, or the night before? Did the internal assessment components of Class X subjects go as well as the terminal papers? Were marks even across subjects or concentrated in two or three? Those three answers predict the Diploma experience better than any percentage, and they are all already available to you.

faqs.question: Can my child take Hindi in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Language options vary by school, so confirm what is offered with the coordinator. The important distinction is between group one, where a language is studied as a first language, and group two language acquisition, where ab initio is for a genuine beginner, B at Standard Level for a working speaker and B at Higher Level for someone approaching fluency. The same language studied in those two ways is a different qualification with a different ceiling, so placement deserves a short assessment before the form.

faqs.question: What happens to Arabic and Islamic Education lessons alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: They continue, because private schools in the emirate must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside whichever curriculum they are licensed for. Classes must be organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Tutoring in those subjects must work from the school's own material, because additional content without ministry permission is prohibited.

faqs.question: Is Diploma tutoring the same job as CBSE Class XII tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two is a common and costly mistake. CBSE Class XII support is content-led and intensive, because the assessment is content-led and concentrated in one season. Diploma support should be component-led, aimed at a named part of the grade with a published weighting, and much of it is criteria-based rather than content-based. Ask any prospective tutor which system they have taught and how recently, before matching rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How much does a tutor cost for a family at this school?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, a named specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits including travel at roughly AED 180 to 500, and budget platforms between AED 45 and 150. Monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. Those belong to the providers that published them; ours follows the free trial lesson and depends on subject, level and frequency.

faqs.question: What should the first Diploma term's tutoring concentrate on?
faqs.answer: Not content, which is the opposite of what most crossing families expect to buy. Command terms first, because a student trained to cover a topic comprehensively is using an actively losing strategy and correcting it shows on the next script. Then research design, before any internal assessment data is collected, because that criterion cannot be repaired afterwards. Then the core deadline calendar, which the school sets and which arrives in clusters rather than evenly.

intro.heading: Progress you can see on paper, not progress you are told about
paragraphs: Parents at GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis rarely arrive asking for a tutor in the abstract. They arrive holding something: a Year 10 mock paper with 41 out of 80 on it, a science practical write-up marked down for the wrong reason, a progress report that moved from a 6 to a 5 with no explanation attached. The useful question is never whether tutoring helps in general. It is what this specific script says about this specific student, and what the next four weeks should fix first.

That is the premise of this page. The tutoring described here is built around a visible record: the work your child produces, the marks a tutor puts on it against the published criteria, and a dated note of what changed between one Tuesday and the next. If a tutor cannot show you the paper and point at the line where three marks went, the tutoring is not evidence-led, whatever the weekly email says.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India — so nobody is quoted a travel premium and nobody waits for a tutor stuck on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. A Silicon Oasis family gets a Chemistry specialist who marks Paper 4 every week rather than whichever graduate lives twenty minutes away, and the saved travel time goes back into the session.

The school sits in Dubai Silicon Oasis and draws from Academic City, Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif and the Ras Al Khor side of the city. It runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE and offers a sixth form; confirm the exact current offer and subject list with the school, because option blocks change year to year. What does not change is the shape of the assessment: terminal papers in a June or November series, a small number of coursework-style components, and grade boundaries that move by a few marks each sitting. One practical consequence of a Silicon Oasis timetable is that the compulsory Arabic and Islamic Education blocks sit alongside the IGCSE option subjects, so the week has fewer free periods than the option sheet suggests. Count them before agreeing to two sessions a subject, because a plan the student cannot physically sit through is the commonest reason tutoring quietly stops after six weeks.

Everything on this page is written for a parent who wants to check it. Fee and rate figures are the Dubai market's, attributed where they came from, not an IB Gram price list. Regulatory statements come from u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Exam-series information comes from Cambridge International and Pearson. Where a figure could not be verified — IB session dates among them — it is left out rather than guessed, because a date a parent acts on has to be right.

Each lesson leaves a dated note naming the topic, the marks lost and the next task

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-wellington.programmesIntro: GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis families usually need help at one of four points: the two IGCSE years, the Diploma that follows for some students, the middle-years run-up, or the A Level route taken by others in the same cohort. Each has a different assessment logic, so each gets a different kind of session.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal written papers. Most subjects split into a Core tier capped at grade C or 5 and an Extended tier reaching A* or 9, and the tier decision is usually made in Year 10 on the strength of end-of-unit tests. Sciences carry a practical-skills paper assessed in writing rather than in a lab. Maths at Extended level adds functions, transformations of graphs and vectors that the Core paper never asks for.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a Silicon Oasis parent reading an Indian revision blog will see dates that do not apply to their child. Entries are made by the school as the exam centre, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The grade jump that catches students out is not the content; it is the shift from answering questions to producing extended work under criteria they have to read for themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai reports International Baccalaureate as the curriculum of roughly 7% of its private-school pupils, against 37% on a UK curriculum, so a Diploma student here is in a smaller cohort than the school assembly suggests. IB session dates are not restated on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every deadline with the school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment in which each subject is marked against four criteria, A to D, on an eight-point scale. Students arriving from a numerical-mark system find the conversion opaque: a 6 on criterion B is not 75%, and a best-fit judgement across a semester is not an average. Tutoring here is mostly about reading the criterion descriptors and writing to them.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools within a short drive of Silicon Oasis run MYP rather than IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, so cousins and neighbours in the same community are assessed on entirely different logic. A student transferring between the two mid-key-stage needs a bridging plan, not catch-up.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken in depth, assessed by written papers with some subjects offering a staged AS and A2 structure. Content depth rises sharply from IGCSE: A Level Chemistry assumes the 0620 Extended syllabus as a floor rather than a starting point. Students who coasted to a 7 at IGCSE without writing anything down are the ones who stall in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education do not count towards those five.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-wellington.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Silicon Oasis families request most often, with what each one actually assesses and the place marks go missing. A tutor who cannot tell you which paper carries the weighting is not a specialist in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Two papers at each tier. Extended adds functions, graph transformations, vectors and conditional probability. Marks disappear in method lines left out of non-calculator working and in bearings questions where the diagram is never drawn. Working shown earns method marks even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Multiple choice, a theory paper and the alternative-to-practical paper. The practical paper is where Extended candidates lose most: it asks for sources of error, improvements and table headings with units, and those are learned by doing past practicals, not by revising content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for a large share of lost marks every series. Students can recite V = IR and still fail to read a series-parallel circuit. Sessions work through circuit diagrams on a shared screen until the student redraws them correctly without prompting.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. The six-mark extended-response questions want named processes in sequence, not a general description. Osmosis, transpiration and enzyme practicals are the usual gap, and they recur in the alternative-to-practical paper.

subjects.name: English Language (Pearson Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise reference to the text; the transactional writing task rewards a controlled register and a clear structure. Most lost marks are structural, not grammatical. Tutoring is largely marking a student's own responses against the band descriptors line by line.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, Paper 2 is calculator-permitted, and HL adds Paper 3 as an extended problem-solving component. HL proof by induction and complex numbers are the common wall. The exploration is twenty per cent and rewards a genuine personal engagement with a mathematical idea.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where HL students lose ground, and the scientific investigation asks for a research question with a measurable independent variable. Most weak investigations fail at the design stage, weeks before any data is collected.

subjects.name: Economics (IB DP)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks that content knowledge does not rescue. Axes must be labelled, shifts must be drawn in the right direction, and the evaluation sentence has to do real work. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit.

subjects.name: Business Management (IB DP)
subjects.description: Case-study response under time pressure, with HL adding an extension topic and the pre-released case study for Paper 2. Students who know the tools and cannot apply them to the stimulus lose the application marks, which are the bulk of the paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support focuses on the school's own scheme of work rather than any outside material.

sections.heading: What a GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis parent is actually asking for
paragraphs: The literal search is for a tutor attached to one school. What the search usually means is narrower: my child is in Year 10 or Year 11 at a British-curriculum school in Dubai Silicon Oasis, a subject has slipped, and I want someone who knows the exact paper they will sit rather than someone who knows the subject in general. Those are different people. A graduate chemist can explain redox; only a tutor who marks 0620 Paper 6 every week knows that the alternative-to-practical paper is where the grade is actually decided.

The second thing in the question is timing. Year 10 is when tier decisions get made and when a weak foundation in algebra or electricity is still cheap to fix. Year 11 is when it is expensive. A student who arrives in September of Year 11 with a 4 in Maths needs a different plan from one who arrives in February with a 6 and wants a 7, and both plans should be written down before the first lesson rather than discovered by week six.

The third thing, usually unspoken, is scepticism. Parents in this market have been sold tutoring before and have been told their child is making progress with nothing to look at. So the whole structure here is built to be audited: the diagnostic paper from week one stays on file, each session note is dated, and the same paper or its equivalent is sat again at the end of a block. If the marks have not moved, that is visible to you at the same moment it is visible to us, which is the only honest way to run it.
bullets: Name the board and paper, not just the subject, when you enquire
Send the most recent marked script rather than a grade

sections.heading: The evidence file: what gets kept on your child and why
paragraphs: Evidence-led tutoring means a small set of artefacts that exist whether or not anyone asks to see them. The diagnostic script is the baseline. The weekly session note is the narrative. The marked papers are the proof. The re-sit of a comparable paper at the end of a block is the test of whether any of it worked. None of this is sophisticated; it is simply what a school department does and what most private tutoring does not.

The reason to keep it is that memory is a poor instrument for measuring progress. A parent who feels reassured after a good week and anxious after a bad one has no way of telling drift from noise. A column of marks on comparable papers, with the error types tallied beside them, separates the two in about thirty seconds. It also makes the uncomfortable conversation possible: if six weeks of sessions have produced no movement, the honest response is to change the approach or the tutor, and that conversation needs numbers rather than impressions.

The table below sets out what each artefact is, when it appears and what it can actually prove. The limits matter as much as the uses. A school report is a judgement, not a measurement, and two reports from different teachers are not directly comparable. A marked past paper is a measurement, but a paper sat untimed at the kitchen table measures something different from one sat to time. Treating those as the same number is how families end up surprised in August.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision made in Year 10
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier a student is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade before the paper is even sat. Core caps at grade C in the letter system or 5 in the numbered one. Extended reaches A* or 9 but carries more content and harder papers. Schools make the call during Year 10 on the strength of end-of-unit assessments, and a student who looks weak in October because of one bad half-term can be placed on a tier that follows them for two years.

This is the single most consequential decision in the IGCSE years and the one parents are least often consulted about in detail. It is worth asking the department directly which tier their current data points to, what the threshold is, and what would have to change to move it. A tutor's job in that window is narrow and specific: close the content gaps that are pulling the internal data down, in time for the decision rather than after it.

The comparison below is drawn for Mathematics and the sciences, where tiering bites hardest. In English Language and in most humanities the structure differs and there is no tier to choose. Confirm your child's actual entry with the school, because entry patterns vary by subject within the same cohort and a student can sit Extended Maths alongside Core in a second language. Ask for the tier entry in writing once the school has set it, because Cambridge marks against the code on the entry form rather than the name of the set your child sits in.

sections.heading: Where Year 10 and Year 11 marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across marked scripts the losses cluster in a handful of places, and almost none of them are content ignorance. In Mathematics the largest single category is unwritten method: a student does three steps mentally, writes the answer, gets it wrong by an arithmetic slip and collects nothing where two method marks were available. The fix is mechanical and unglamorous. Write the line. It takes four sessions of nagging and is worth more than a month of new topics.

In the sciences the cluster sits in the practical paper. Candidates who can describe an experiment cannot name a source of error, suggest an improvement that is actually testable, or head a results table with the unit in brackets. These are learnable in a fortnight because the question types repeat, but they are rarely taught explicitly in a crowded Year 11 scheme of work. Electricity is the content exception: series and parallel circuits defeat students who have genuinely learned the formulae, because the difficulty is reading the diagram rather than recalling the relationship.

In English the losses are structural. A reading response that paraphrases instead of referring, a transactional task that ignores the audience named in the question, a timed essay that spends half its words on the introduction. None of those are fixed by reading more; they are fixed by writing to the band descriptors with someone marking against them. The common thread across all three subjects is that the marks are lost in technique, which is why the first session is a marked paper rather than a lecture.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Silicon Oasis, by the month
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a household budget actually feels. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package pricing in this market runs from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions up to AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The gap between those two packages is mostly travel.

Converted to an hourly figure, the market bands look like this. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit in the AED 150 to 300 range; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500, and named or examiner-tier tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are the market's figures and the providers' own published rates, not IB Gram's price list.

Two things are worth knowing before you compare. First, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the following academic year, under an economics incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so tutoring is the line in the education budget that is actually moving. Second, ask whether a quoted rate is per hour or per lesson and whether VAT is included, because the two most common billing surprises in this market are a 45-minute lesson priced as an hour and a tax line added later. For IB Gram's own arrangement, start with the free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a rate card.

sections.heading: The June series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, which is a detail worth holding on to, because a great deal of IGCSE revision content online is written for Indian candidates and quotes dates that are wrong for a child in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Counting backwards from the exam is more useful than counting forwards from today. Entries are made by the school as the exam centre, months before the papers are sat, and they are the hinge: once an entry is submitted at a tier, the ceiling is fixed. Before that sit the mock window and the internal coursework deadlines, which is where most of a tutor's work is actually timed to. After the exam come results, then the window for an enquiry about results or a remark, then the resit entry for the next series.

Dates get revised, so the only responsible thing a page like this can do is name the milestones and send you to the official timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and are there to show you the shape of the gap, not to be read as next year's calendar.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the time they take
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A family moving within the UAE moves between regulators, and inspection language does not translate directly across them.

The practical consequence for a Silicon Oasis timetable is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Those subjects occupy real timetable minutes. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support in these subjects has to work from the school's own scheme of work. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate approval from the authority to teach those subjects — a credential a parent can ask the school about directly. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA and does not claim any.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE coursework, a Diploma internal assessment, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay all have to be the student's own work, and the student signs to that effect. The consequence of getting this wrong is not a telling-off; it is a malpractice finding that can cost a candidate the qualification. That makes the boundary worth stating plainly rather than leaving to inference, particularly in a market where at least one provider openly sells completed internal assessments.

What a tutor may do: teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, read a draft the student has written and give criterion-referenced feedback on it, model the technique on a different example, and help plan a timeline backwards from the school's deadline. What a tutor may not do: write any part of the work, dictate sentences, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, supply a research question as a finished product, or hand over a worked exemplar to be adapted. IB Gram does not write, complete or produce assessed work of any kind, and will not take an instruction to do so.

There is also a boundary around materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards. We reference them and link to the official source — cambridgeinternational.org, qualifications.pearson.com, ibo.org — rather than reproducing or distributing them. And a note on who may tutor at all: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Whatever emirate you are in, your child's own class teacher is not the right private tutor for them.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in the UAE, and how to check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The enforcement position is equally clear and equally worth knowing: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody, and a figure circulating online as a specific sum is not something a provider can substantiate. If a tutor tells you tutoring in Dubai is unregulated, they are wrong, and that is useful information about them.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which runs from initial approval through permit and licence steps with annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit is what a claim of KHDA approval properly refers to, and it is the single most frequently misused phrase in this market. IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute, holds no such permit, has no UAE premises, and delivers one-to-one lessons online. Ask any provider which category they fall into and what they can show you.
