sections.heading: Online from Silicon Oasis: the practical case, and the honest limits
paragraphs: The argument for online delivery in this part of Dubai is not that screens are better than rooms. It is supply. The number of tutors who mark Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 weekly and are also free at 17:00 within a twenty-minute drive of Silicon Oasis is small. Remove the drive and the pool becomes every specialist available in that slot. For a mainstream Maths request the difference is modest; for Economics HL, Further Maths or a second-language subject it is the difference between a specialist and whoever is nearest.

The second argument is time. An in-home arrangement prices travel into the rate, which is visible in the market bands above, and it prices it into the evening too: a tutor arriving at 17:40 because of traffic on the Al Ain Road interchange eats twenty minutes of a sixty-minute lesson. Online, the lesson starts when it says it starts, work can be marked and returned on a shared screen, and a session can be moved to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan without a tutor crossing the city twice.

The honest limits are worth stating too. A younger student who cannot yet sit at a desk unsupervised needs a parent in earshot for the first few weeks. Practical science cannot be done over video, which is why the alternative-to-practical paper is the right focus and why school lab time stays irreplaceable. And if no specialist is free in the slot you need, the right answer is to say so and offer a different slot or a different tutor, not to fill the gap with a generalist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and pretending otherwise would be the easiest way to lose a family's trust in week one.

process.title: Send the evidence, not the summary
process.description: Share the most recent marked script, the last report and the subject's exam board. Two marked papers tell a tutor more in five minutes than a long phone call does in thirty. If you have a mock paper, send it even if the mark is poor; particularly if the mark is poor.

process.title: A diagnostic paper, sat to time
process.description: Before teaching starts, the student sits a full paper under exam conditions. The tutor marks it against the published scheme and writes up the topics that are empty, the method marks lost and the question types that collapsed. This is the baseline every later mark is read against.

process.title: A written plan with a date on it
process.description: You get a short plan naming the topics in order, the number of sessions each should take, and when the next measured paper falls. It is deliberately specific enough to be wrong, because a plan that cannot be wrong cannot be checked either.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a note each time
process.description: One-to-one, live over video, same slot and same tutor. Work is marked before the lesson, the lesson covers the lost marks, and a dated note goes out afterwards naming what was taught and what the next task is. Those notes accumulate into the record you can read backwards.

process.title: Re-measure, then decide
process.description: After six to eight sessions the student sits a comparable paper to time. The marks either moved or they did not. If they did not, the approach changes or the tutor does, and that decision is made on the numbers rather than on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: The paper comes before the opinion
whyPoints.description: Every judgement on this page traces back to a marked script. A tutor who has read your child's actual Paper 2 can say which four topics to spend the next month on; one who has only read the report can say that revision is important.

whyPoints.title: Boards and codes named in full
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610; Pearson 4MA1 and 4EA1. A Cambridge and an Edexcel paper in the same subject differ in structure and tiering, and a tutor working from the wrong one wastes a term. We confirm the board before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: Written records you keep
whyPoints.description: Dated session notes, marked papers and the diagnostic script stay available to you. If you change tutor, change school or move emirate, the file goes with the student rather than evaporating with the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Market rates shown, our own quoted plainly
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are the Dubai market's, attributed to the providers who published them. We do not pretend they are ours and we do not hide behind a contact form: the free trial and the consultation are where our own arrangement is set out.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line held, in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. Nobody here writes an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or any assessed work. That is stated on the page rather than buried, because the student is the one who carries the risk.

whyPoints.title: Online, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and movable for Ramadan. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE and does not have a Dubai office, so nothing on this page depends on a tutor's commute.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor is actually helping my child at Wellington Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: Ask for three things. A baseline paper, sat to time and marked against the published scheme, from before teaching started. A dated note from each session naming what was taught and what was wrong. A comparable paper sat again after six to eight sessions. If the second mark has not moved, the tutoring has not worked yet, whatever the sessions felt like. Reports and verbal reassurance are judgements rather than measurements, and two reports from different teachers are not comparable numbers. The point of keeping a file is that the awkward conversation becomes possible: you can see the same thing we can, at the same time.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child sit at a British-curriculum school in Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject within the same school, which surprises most parents. A cohort can sit Cambridge IGCSE in the sciences and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in English in the same year. The papers differ in structure, tiering and syllabus code, so the board has to be confirmed before any tutoring starts. The school's subject information sheet or the head of department will tell you, and the code is usually printed on the front of any past paper your child has been given. Send us a photo of that front page and the question is answered in a minute.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10. Is it too early to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest place to fix a problem and the point at which the tier decision gets made. Schools place students on the Core or Extended tier during that year on the strength of internal assessments, and that choice sets a grade ceiling for two years. A student whose algebra or circuit work is shaky in October can be lifted before the decision; the same student in February of Year 11 is working against a fixed entry. If you are weighing timing, Year 10 support is usually better value per session than an emergency block later.

faqs.question: What does the alternative-to-practical paper test for a Wellington Silicon Oasis science student?
faqs.answer: It tests practical reasoning in writing rather than laboratory skill. Candidates are asked to identify sources of error, suggest improvements that are genuinely testable, read apparatus diagrams, head a results table with units, plot and interpret data, and explain why a method controls a variable. The question types repeat series after series, which makes this the most trainable paper in the sciences and the one where Extended candidates most often leave marks behind. Two or three weeks of working through past practical papers with feedback typically shifts more marks than the same time spent re-reading content notes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Diploma internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the content, explain what each criterion is asking for, read a draft the student has written and give criterion-referenced feedback on it, model the technique on a different example, and plan the work backwards from the school's deadline. A tutor cannot write any part of it, dictate sentences, rewrite a paragraph into final form or supply a research question as a finished product. The student signs that the work is their own, so the student carries the risk. IB Gram does not produce assessed work and declines requests to.

faqs.question: Why is there no home-visit option for families living in Dubai Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The reason is supply rather than policy for its own sake. The pool of tutors who mark a specific IGCSE paper weekly and are also free at a given hour within a short drive of one Dubai community is small, and the market prices the travel into the rate anyway — in-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online. Removing the commute widens the choice of specialist and removes the traffic risk from the start time.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly budget for exam-year support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market run from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are the market's published figures, not IB Gram's price list. Before comparing, check whether a rate is per hour or per lesson and whether tax is included.

faqs.question: When do UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: In the June series and the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so revision guides and timetable posts written for Indian candidates quote dates that do not apply to a child in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Entries are made by the school as the exam centre, months ahead of the papers. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards UAE equivalency for a British-curriculum student?
faqs.answer: No. The British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. The same route requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary at the same grade. One competing site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry of Education, not by any tutoring provider, and should be confirmed on the ministry's own channel before you plan around it.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic if they are on a UK curriculum?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA's requirements. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so any support has to work from the school's own scheme of work rather than from outside material.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and can I check one?
faqs.answer: They do. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services, with a two-working-day completion time. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with scepticism.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we see a mark move?
faqs.answer: Technique losses move fastest. Unwritten method lines in maths and table-heading or error-source marks in the practical papers often show up within three or four sessions, because the student is already capable and is simply not writing what the scheme rewards. Content gaps take longer: a missing topic block in Extended Maths is realistically six to eight sessions before it holds under timed conditions. We re-measure on a comparable paper after six to eight sessions rather than guessing, and no honest tutor will put a number of grades against a number of weeks in advance.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school mocks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. Many families shift to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan, and because lessons run over video there is no commute to rebuild around — the slot simply moves. Around mocks and study leave the shape changes rather than the frequency: sessions become paper-marking rather than new teaching, so the student sits full papers to time and the lesson covers only what lost marks. Coursework blocks are planned backwards from the school's internal deadlines, so those weeks are blocked out before the term starts where possible.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right match for our Wellington Silicon Oasis student?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change it, without a case having to be made. A mismatch is usually about pace or manner rather than competence, and it shows up in the first two or three sessions. Because the evidence file travels with the student — the diagnostic paper, the plan, the session notes — a new tutor starts from the record rather than from scratch, which is the main practical argument for keeping the file at all. Ask any provider this question before you book, and ask what it costs you when it happens.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring workable for a Year 11 student who learns better face to face?
faqs.answer: For most Year 11 students, yes, with two caveats. The session has to be worked rather than watched: a shared screen with the student's own script on it, annotated live, is a different experience from a lecture over video. And a younger or easily distracted student benefits from a parent in earshot for the first few weeks until the habit sets. What online cannot replace is laboratory time, which is the school's job, and that is precisely why written practical papers are the right focus for science support.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-wellington.closingHeading: Send one marked paper and we will tell you what it says
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-wellington.closingBody: If your child is at GEMS Wellington Academy Silicon Oasis and a subject has slipped, the fastest useful step is not a phone call about tutoring in general. Send the most recent marked script, the subject's exam board and the term you are working towards. A specialist in that paper reads it, names the topics that are actually empty and the marks being lost to technique, and writes back with a plan that has dates on it. The first lesson is a free trial, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the diagnostic paper from it becomes the baseline everything afterwards is measured against.

intro.heading: Start at the cheap end and work upwards
paragraphs: Most pricing conversations in this market begin at the premium end, which flatters the seller and tells a parent nothing. So begin at the other end. Published market rates read in October 2026 put budget online platforms and university-student tutors between roughly AED 45 and 150 an hour, with some platform entry rates quoted from AED 33. That is a real option for a student who needs company and accountability rather than specification depth, and for a Year 9 student working on arithmetic fluency it is often sufficient.

Above that sits a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Then a named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, one agency publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500. At the top a single provider publishes AED 650 an hour. Each of those figures belongs to the provider that published it, and quoting one is neither an endorsement nor a judgement.

The reason to lay the ladder out in that order is that families habitually buy one rung above what the problem requires. A student whose marked script shows command-term misreading and unwritten method does not need a premium specialist; those are behaviours and a competent subject tutor fixes them. A student attempting Higher Level mathematics Paper 3 does need somebody who has taught the course. Matching the rung to the diagnosis is the single largest saving available, and it requires a marked script rather than a conversation.

The bigger money question at this school is structural rather than hourly. GEMS Wellington International School runs the British curriculum through IGCSE and offers a sixth form where families choose a post-16 route; confirm the current provision with the school, since offers change. Six Diploma subjects plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS is a different tutoring budget from three or four A Levels, and nobody models that difference before the decision. This page does, in dirhams and in household hours.

IB Gram supports Wellington families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India. Two things are deliberately absent from this page: any statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none here, and any fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, because the ministry published no schedule and the circulating figure could not be verified. Both gaps are deliberate, and they are the kind of gap worth looking for on any page that quotes money at you, because a provider willing to publish one figure it cannot source will publish others.

sections.heading: What each post-16 pathway costs a household over two years
paragraphs: Nobody models this before the decision, and it is modellable. The Diploma is six subjects plus an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge course examined through an essay of up to 1,600 words and an exhibition commentary of up to 950, and CAS, which carries no points but blocks the diploma if incomplete. A Levels are three or four subjects taken deeper, with no core. Those structures produce different tutoring demand patterns, not simply different amounts.

On the Diploma the demand is wide and shallow. Six subjects means six places a problem can emerge, each carrying an internal assessment worth twenty to thirty per cent, plus the core with its own deadlines that need process coaching rather than subject teaching. A household on this pathway typically finds itself buying several short blocks across two years — an investigation planning session here, an oral rehearsal there, a Theory of Knowledge essay structure conversation — rather than one long engagement.

On A Levels the demand is narrow and deep. Three subjects means a weak one cannot be carried, because there is no sixth subject to absorb it, so when tutoring becomes necessary it tends to be sustained weekly support in one subject rather than a scatter of blocks. Totals vary enormously by household, but the pattern holds: the Diploma spreads spending across more items and the A Level route concentrates it in fewer.

The table below models both using the published market monthly bands rather than invented figures: roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget support at one weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-range qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. It is a shape for planning, not a quote, and the point of it is that a household can see the pattern before choosing rather than discovering it in the second year.

sections.heading: The hours, which are as finite as the money
paragraphs: Dirhams are the visible budget and hours are the one that actually binds. A Dubai school week is longer than its international equivalent, because Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in every private school in the emirate, and the afternoon commute in this catchment takes what it takes. Against that sits homework in six subjects or three, internal assessment work arriving in bursts, CAS in the evenings, and whatever a tutoring arrangement adds.

The arithmetic is worth doing once. A single weekly tutoring session is not one hour of household time. It is the session, plus the work set between sessions, plus the rescheduling when something collides, plus the parent's attention in reading whatever comes back. Two subjects at two sessions a week is not four hours; it is closer to eight or nine once the work between sessions is counted, and it sits on top of a week that was already full.

That is the real reason two subjects at once usually produces two half-improvements. The money is affordable and the hours are not, and the hours give way first — the work between sessions stops being done, the sessions become revision of unattempted homework, and the arrangement quietly becomes two expensive conversations a week. Sequencing avoids it: the subject with the shortest diagnostic list first, banked, then the hours move.

On the Diploma specifically, the hours constraint is tightest in the autumn of the final year, when internal assessment finals, the Extended Essay submission and mock examinations collide. A household that has agreed in advance what sessions will contain during that cluster — process coaching on the piece that is due, rather than subject teaching that competes with it — keeps the arrangement. One that has not usually cancels and never restarts.

sections.heading: Matching the rung to the diagnosis
paragraphs: The largest single saving available in this market is not negotiating a rate. It is buying the right rung on the ladder for the problem you actually have, and that requires a marked script. A lost mark has six possible causes: content not known, content known but not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method correct but not written out, and time ran out. Four of those six are behaviours or techniques rather than knowledge gaps.

Behaviours and techniques do not require a premium specialist. Command-term misreading is fixed by the command-term list and an hour sorting past questions by it. Unwritten method is fixed by enforcement on every piece of marked work. Misread questions are fixed by slower reading, practised. Pacing is fixed by section timing targets and full papers to time. A competent subject tutor at the middle of the published band does all four as well as anybody charging double.

What does justify the specialist rung is genuine content depth in a course with a small teaching pool: Higher Level mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level chemistry mechanisms, a minority Diploma subject, or an A Level module where the board's approach differs from the textbook's. There the person's experience of the specific course is the product, and the rate reflects scarcity rather than polish.

So the sequence that saves money is: get the marked script, count the causes, then choose the rung. Families who choose the rung first and the diagnosis afterwards routinely pay specialist rates to fix a notation habit, which works and costs twice what it needed to. Nobody in this market will point that out, because the incentive runs the other way.

sections.heading: Siblings and the five-year view
paragraphs: Households in this catchment frequently have two or three children in school at once, which turns tutoring from a purchase into a recurring line. Looked at over five years rather than one term, two conclusions follow that are invisible from inside a single decision.

The first is that early support is cheaper than late support for every child, every time. The Year 9 options form fixes the subject list and usually the tier, and a Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C, closing post-16 routes that need a B. Producing the evidence that reopens that — Extended-only content taught, then a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme — costs a handful of sessions in Year 9 and a whole term in Year 11. A household with three children will face that decision three times, and getting it right the first time changes the five-year total more than any rate negotiation.

The second is that the exam-year surge compounds. Published monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run from roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, the highest band in the country, and a significant share of it is spring scarcity rather than teaching quality. A household that habitually engages in February rather than the previous autumn pays that premium once per child per examination year, which over three children and two examination stages each is six instances of an avoidable cost.

Set against those, the saving from using a cheaper tutor is small. The rate difference between the middle and the top of the band is real but bounded; the difference between early and late engagement, and between a tier decision taken well and badly, is not. A household budgeting over five years should spend its planning effort on timing and on the Year 9 form, and relatively little on comparing hourly rates.

sections.heading: The questions that settle a price, and what free should mean
paragraphs: Five questions, answered in writing, settle almost any price conversation. Does the figure include VAT. Is the rate per hour or per session, and how long is a session. What happens if we stop after one month. Who marks work between sessions, against what, and is that time inside the rate. And what happens if the matched tutor becomes unavailable, including whether the written risk list hands over.

The marking question is the one that separates arrangements which generate evidence from those that generate a pleasant relationship. A piece of work annotated away from the student against the official mark scheme is a document that can be compared with next month's. The same correction made verbally in the room leaves nothing behind, and a household then has no way of knowing whether the hours worked until results arrive.

On anything described as free, the condition belongs on the same screen as the word. A trial lesson should be free without a commitment, a card requirement or a minimum booking appearing later. Ours is one lesson with the matched tutor before anything is paid, with the parent able to listen in, and its purpose is to test whether your child can follow this person's explanation rather than to conduct a sales conversation.

And if any provider states a rating, a satisfaction percentage or a student count, ask for the sample size, the date and the method. Several pages researched in this market publish figures with none of the three; one shows two different ratings and review counts in the same document, and another pairs a five-star figure from twenty reviews with a claim of 2,500 students taught. A figure without an n and a date is not evidence of anything.

sections.heading: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: No statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because making one responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none here. No fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, because the ministry published no schedule and the figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. No IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency, because none could be read on an official source; the British-track figures are published and appear elsewhere on this site, and the IB figure does not. No IB examination or results date, because the organisation's own site could not be checked. No star rating, satisfaction percentage or student count.

On permits, the cost is zero. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

On assessed work, the cheapest-looking purchase in this market is the most expensive item on any menu. A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work at a fixed price. Submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the board's rules and the consequence lands on the student's qualification. A tutor may teach, explain criteria in the board's wording, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses. A tutor may not write the internal assessment or draft the Extended Essay.

And position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, and has no arrangement with any school named on this page. Every rate quoted belongs to the provider that published it.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-acad.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover what a Dubai IB family most often funds: Diploma subject specialists across the six groups, Middle Years support, and separate Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching, which is a different budget line from exam preparation.

intro.heading: The price, and the four things that actually move it
paragraphs: Dubai has the densest private-school market in the UAE — 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, on KHDA's own published figures. A market that size should produce transparent tutoring prices. It does not. Of the six competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026, three published no price whatsoever, one asks the cost question in its own frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency Dubai families pay anything in.

So here are the figures in dirhams, with the source of each. Budget online tutoring with a university-student tutor runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey reaching 450 or more. An in-home one-to-one visit costs AED 180 to 500, Bestimate putting it at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Premium named tutors run AED 500 to 650 or above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly, because that is how a household budgets: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of these are IB Gram prices. We publish no price list on these pages, because an honest number depends on subject, level and availability, and a figure invented for a web page is worse than a conversation.

Four things move the number in this emirate specifically, and only one of them is the tutor's experience. The first is format: an in-home visit in Dubai carries a drive across one of the region's heaviest afternoon road networks, and that drive is inside the hourly rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. The second is timing: specialist demand peaks before the May session and the June series, and the slots that fill first are exactly the late-afternoon ones a Dubai school run forces. The third is precision: a tutor matched to the subject rather than the specification delivers teaching rather than marks. The fourth is sequence, which is the largest of all and the one nobody prices.

The rest of this page is built around the number. There is a table of what each band buys, a table setting tutoring against the rest of a Dubai education bill with KHDA's fee freeze as the anchor, the in-home travel premium priced out for Dubai traffic, coursework coaching treated as its own budget line, a note on reading your school's KHDA inspection report before spending anything, a list of what nobody should be charging you for, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rules for both the British and American tracks.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-acad.programmesIntro: An IB continuum family funds support at three different stages, and the cost per unit of improvement is not the same in any two of them. Knowing which stage you are in is most of the budgeting problem.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, organised around units rather than subjects, reporting against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages. Parents arriving from a marks-based system often cannot tell whether a child is behind, which is why primary tutoring here is frequently bought on anxiety rather than on evidence.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest and most useful purchase at this stage is a short diagnostic rather than a standing weekly hour: number fluency, reading stamina and written structure assessed against age expectations. Those three predict Middle Years performance, and fixing them in Year 4 costs a fraction of repairing them in Year 9 at Dubai specialist rates.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. There is no external paper before the optional eAssessment, so a student can go years without an externally benchmarked mark while school reports look reassuring.
programmes.countryNote: MYP5 into DP1 is where Dubai families spend most unnecessarily, because the help is bought after the step rather than before it. A student who has never sat a timed external paper meets Paper 1 under clock pressure in DP1. The spring term before DP1 is the cheap window, and it is the term almost nobody funds.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, reaching A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is untiered in most subjects and awards 9 to 1. Codes carry real cost consequences: 0580 and 4MA1 are different exams with different mark schemes, and a mismatch buys a term of the wrong preparation.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, and most run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. For a household moving between a British and an IB pathway inside Dubai, the IGCSE grades and the pathway decision are both worth a short diagnostic spend rather than a term of weekly hours.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE matrix. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in most sciences the HL extension sits on its own paper.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. The dates that bind a Dubai Diploma household are the coordinator's internal coursework deadlines, which fall through DP1 and into DP2. That has a direct budget consequence: coursework coaching has to be funded before paper technique, because a missed internal deadline cannot be bought back at any rate.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-gems-world-acad.subjectsIntro: Subjects a Dubai IB family funds most often, with a note on which carry a coursework cost on top of exam preparation. That second line is the one most budgets miss.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Carries an internal exploration as well as papers, so budget two lines. HL Paper 3 is a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the grade and the most expensive gap to leave open, because it responds to practice rather than explanation and practice takes weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Also carries an exploration. The recurring loss is interpretation rather than calculation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means collects the calculation marks only. Cheap to fix once diagnosed, costly to leave because it recurs on every paper.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice under tight timing; Paper 2 is extended response, where a numerically right answer with no reasoning chain loses the explanation marks. The internal assessment needs real uncertainty treatment, which is coursework coaching rather than subject teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium carry the weight in Paper 2 and organic mechanism notation is the most common hidden gap. The IA rewards a genuinely personal investigation; discovering late that a reproduced textbook experiment sits mid-band is among the costlier surprises in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked as a precision subject rather than a recall one. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different answer shape. Genetics and homeostasis are the usual collapse points and both respond quickly enough to be cheap.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IA is three 800-word commentaries on news articles the student finds, and a badly chosen article wastes a fortnight of student time plus paid coaching time. HL adds Paper 3, which is arithmetic under time pressure rather than deeper theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question; Paper 2 is comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract and is internally assessed, externally moderated. Weak ones fail on the global issue.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study decides the grade, and application to the named business is the assessed skill. One of the cheapest improvements in the Diploma, because candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus are losing marks for a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: No coursework component, so the entire budget goes on paper technique. Marks are lost on transformations, bounds and the final part of multi-step problems where method marks were available for working that was never written down.

subjects.name: Sciences (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The practical or alternative-to-practical paper is a separate preparation cost from the theory papers, and Cambridge Paper 6 rewards apparatus precision no textbook summary supplies. The board split halves the available specialist pool, so confirm the code first.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring means supporting the school's own prescribed material.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Central, well connected and dense with schools, so the in-home travel premium is at its lowest here and the local tutor pool at its largest. Even so, an afternoon drive across Al Khail Road at 16:00 is not the drive the map promises.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Established, villa-heavy and close to several large schools. In-home supply is good and so is the premium, because tutors can fit two visits into an afternoon here in a way they cannot further out along the Expo corridor.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Apartment density means a tutor can serve several households in one tower block, which should in principle lower the premium. Parking and building access often cancel that out, and a 16:30 arrival is frequently a 16:50 one.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and the Emirates Road corridor
regions.note: Villa communities with a longer run from the central school cluster. In-home quotes here sit higher for identical teaching, and a cancelled session wastes a substantial journey that is usually charged either way.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: East of the creek, with its own school cluster and a different traffic profile. Families here often find the tutor pool thinner than the central areas and the quotes correspondingly higher at the in-home end.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Further out, with university campuses nearby that broaden the budget end of the tutor pool. Specialist Diploma supply is thinner than in Al Barsha, which pushes an in-home specialist quote towards the top of the published band.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village and the Expo corridor
regions.note: Rapidly growing residential areas with newer schools. The commute is the variable: a tutor crossing from Jumeirah to JVC in the late afternoon spends more of their day travelling than teaching, and prices accordingly.

sections.heading: What each AED band actually buys in Dubai
paragraphs: An hourly rate is a bundle, not a quality score, and the bundles differ. Working up from the cheapest band shows what each additional dirham is purchasing, which is the only way to judge whether a Dubai quote is good value or merely expensive.

At AED 45 to 150 an hour you are buying availability. A university-student tutor can keep a capable child moving, explain homework and hold a routine, and in a city with Academic City campuses the budget end of the Dubai pool is genuinely deep. What you are not buying is specification knowledge, and at Diploma level that is usually what separates a 5 from a 6. At AED 150 to 300 you are buying subject training and familiarity with the course. At AED 200 to 450 and above you are buying level-specific and paper-specific experience: somebody who can name the failure modes on HL Paper 2 without looking them up.

At AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit you are buying presence plus a Dubai drive. Presence is real value for a younger child. The drive is pure cost, and in this emirate it is a larger cost than the distance suggests, because the hours a school run dictates are the hours the roads are worst. At AED 500 to 650 and above you are buying reputation, and any examiner claim should be evidenced rather than accepted: examiner status is unverifiable from a website and is often used to imply access to marking standards, boundaries or paper content that nobody outside the process has.

The practical test is to price the pieces rather than compare the totals. Two quotes of AED 250 and AED 320 are not comparable if the second includes travel: the second is cheaper on teaching and dearer overall. And a quote of AED 200 from somebody who teaches a different board is not a bargain at any price, because what you are buying is the mark scheme.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against the rest of a Dubai education bill
paragraphs: A tutoring quote means little in isolation. Set against the cost of the schooling it supplements, the decision becomes a question of proportion, and proportion is what makes AED 250 an hour either reasonable or absurd.

The anchor is KHDA's own announcement. On 22 May 2026 KHDA confirmed there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family already paying international school fees, that confirmation means a tutoring budget set the previous year has not been squeezed from the school side.

Against an international school bill, the published tutoring bands read differently. A weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor at Bestimate's AED 600 to 1,200 a month is a marginal addition rather than a second school fee. A specialist exam-year arrangement at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month is a genuine commitment, and it is usually temporary — concentrated into two or three terms rather than spread across the whole Diploma. The published AED 799 monthly package for eight online sessions is the cheapest structured option in the market as read in October 2026.

Supply is moving too, which matters over a five-year horizon. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB places means more IB students, which over time means more IB teachers and a deeper tutoring pool. That is a reason to expect the specialist end of this market to get easier rather than harder to buy.

sections.heading: The Dubai travel premium, priced out
paragraphs: Dubai looks like the one emirate where an in-home arrangement should be cheap, because the city is dense and the schools are close together. The arithmetic says otherwise, and it says so for a reason specific to this city rather than to tutoring in general.

A tutor delivering a one-hour in-home session has to travel to it and away from it, and the hours a school run dictates are the hours Dubai's roads are least cooperative. A crossing that takes twenty minutes at 11:00 takes forty-five at 16:30. So a single taught hour consumes two to two and a half hours of the tutor's working day, and a rate that makes that sustainable has to price all of it. That is why the in-home band at AED 180 to 500 sits above the online qualified band at AED 150 to 300 even when it is the same person teaching.

What online delivery removes is not only the cost but the risk. The appointment no longer has to be fixed against an arrival time nobody can predict, so a late school bus costs ten minutes rather than a wasted journey that is usually charged regardless. A 19:00 slot costs exactly what a 16:00 slot costs, because nobody is driving, and that matters in a household where the afternoon is already full. Past papers screen-share and annotate live, and a session can be recorded and rewatched the night before a paper, which no kitchen-table lesson produces.

The case where the premium earns its keep is a younger child who genuinely needs an adult physically present to stay on task. That is a real need and worth paying for. It is not the situation of a DP2 student losing marks on Paper 2 extended response, where the thing worth paying for is somebody who knows Paper 2. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Coursework is a separate budget line, and most households miss it
paragraphs: The most common budgeting error in a Dubai Diploma household is treating tutoring as one thing. It is two things with different costs, different timing and different providers of value, and funding only the visible one is how families end up paying twice.

Exam preparation is the visible one: weekly hours, past papers, technique. Coursework is the other: the Extended Essay research question, Internal Assessments in nearly every subject, the TOK exhibition and essay. Coursework deadlines are set by the school's IB coordinator rather than the exam board, and they fall through DP1 and the first half of DP2, which means they bind before any exam does. A household that funds paper practice while an Internal Assessment sits unstarted has spent money in the wrong order, and the deadline cannot be repurchased.

What coursework coaching legitimately contains is worth stating, because this is the part of the market where the boundary is abused. A tutor can explain what each assessment criterion rewards and in what proportion, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of the descriptors, triage a research question that cannot be answered inside the word limit, and teach the statistics a Biology investigation or the testing documentation a Computer Science solution requires. All of that is feedback on the student's own work.

What a tutor may not do is write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to submission standard any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not and declines the request. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price; that is not expensive tutoring, it is a transaction whose downside is the Diploma, and the student carries it rather than the seller. The test is free: a legitimate session ends with your child holding a list of changes, not with a cleaner document in a parent's inbox.

sections.heading: Read the inspection report before you spend anything
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The reports are published. They are also, for a parent about to spend money on tutoring, the single best free targeting document available, and almost nobody reads them that way.

An inspection report does not just award a headline band. It reports attainment and progress by subject and by phase, which means it names the year groups and subjects where a school's own students are doing least well. If your child's school shows weaker progress in secondary mathematics than elsewhere, that is a stronger signal about where to direct tutoring money than any provider's marketing. If attainment is strong across the board, the honest conclusion may be that paid tutoring is not the first thing to buy.

Two cautions about how those reports get used in this market. First, a band is a school-level judgement across hundreds of students and says little about one child's needs; a report is a targeting tool, not a diagnosis. Second, no tutoring provider should be presenting a school's rating as a reason to buy, and none should imply any relationship with the school. Writing "students we support attend" is accurate where true; implying partnership is not, and several competitor pages list twenty or more schools as though they were clients.

Read your own school's report alongside your child's marked work, and the targeting question usually answers itself. That combination costs nothing, takes an evening, and routinely saves a term of misdirected hours. It is also why we ask for marked papers before quoting anything rather than selling a package off a page.

sections.heading: Where Dubai households overspend
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the waste in this city, and all four are visible in advance.

The first is paying the travel premium and receiving availability. The in-home band at AED 180 to 500 overlaps the specialist band at AED 200 to 450, so a household can pay specialist money for a tutor selected because they were willing to make a particular drive at 16:30. Nobody sets out to buy that, and it is rarely discovered before week three.

The second is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. Six sessions of general revision at published mid-band rates is roughly AED 900 to 1,800 and changes little, because nobody established where the marks were going. Three or four sessions marking past papers against the official scheme and sorting every lost mark by cause — content not known, method not shown, command term misread, units and notation, time ran out — tells you what the next twenty hours should contain. The distribution is almost always lopsided and almost no family has seen it.

The third is starting in the DP2 spring, when specialist demand peaks, the late slots are gone and everything outstanding has to be repaired rather than built. The fourth, specific to a city with this many providers, is buying on presentation. A page with a self-asserted star rating, a fabricated satisfaction percentage or a tutor count that nobody can evidence is telling you something about how it will treat your invoice. Of the competitor pages examined for this project, one shows two different review figures on the same page and another shows a five-star rating from twenty reviews alongside a claim of thousands of students.

sections.heading: What nobody should be charging you for
paragraphs: Several things are on sale in Dubai's tutoring market that cannot legitimately be supplied. Recognising them protects a budget more effectively than negotiating an hourly rate.

Regulator approval is not for sale. KHDA oversees private education quality in Dubai; ADEK handles licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain; SPEA regulates Sharjah; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of those bodies approves or accredits a tutor or a tutoring platform. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit is not for sale either. Introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted should be treated as unverified. A tutor cannot reasonably attribute a higher rate to licensing costs.

Nor should anybody be charging for a promise about a grade, for completed coursework, for board syllabus documents and mark schemes as downloads, or for handling Ministry of Education equivalency. The first is not deliverable, the second risks the qualification, the third belongs to the boards, and the fourth is a Ministry process that we describe and point you to rather than perform. One more worth adding in a city this competitive: a school's own teacher tutoring your child privately may be barred from doing so, and nobody should be marketing that arrangement.

sections.heading: Equivalency on both tracks, and why it costs nothing to understand
paragraphs: A Dubai student applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It costs nothing to understand, and understanding it early prevents expensive subject-choice mistakes. It is also a Ministry process rather than a service a tutoring provider performs, so nobody should be charging you to handle it.

On the British track the published rules are specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. At least one ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and a household funding a sixth subject's tuition on that basis is spending for no reason.

On the American track, English proficiency requires 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma specifically, this page publishes no points threshold, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. An invented figure would be one a family plans two years of spending around, so ask the Ministry, the emirate attestation authority, or your school's university counsellor.

One caution with a direct cost implication: tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process in order to sell hours, and in a market with 227 schools' worth of demand, that tactic is common enough to be worth naming.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the monthly shape
process.description: Whether you are thinking in hours a week or dirhams a month changes the honest answer. A monthly figure lets us say what it will and will not cover at published market rates, rather than quoting an hourly number that sounds reasonable and then needing twice the hours to do anything.

process.title: Read your school's KHDA report first
process.description: It is free, published, and it names the subjects and phases where attainment and progress are weakest. Read it alongside your child's marked work and the targeting question usually answers itself, often more precisely than a tutoring consultation would.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis before the hours
process.description: Send four marked past papers if you have them. Three or four sessions sorting lost marks by cause costs far less than twenty hours of general revision and determines what those hours should contain. The distribution is almost always lopsided and almost no household has seen it.

process.title: Take the free trial with no condition attached
process.description: One session, no minimum booking, no card required, at the hour you would genuinely use rather than a convenient weekend one. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures in the first twenty minutes, because that is exactly what the later hours are paying for.

process.title: Review the spend against marks every six weeks
process.description: Compare what has been paid against what has moved: school assessment marks, past-paper scores by question type, coursework feedback. If nothing has shifted on what you targeted, change the plan or the tutor and say so early. A rematch in week two costs an hour; one in week ten costs a term.

whyPoints.title: The price question answered rather than deflected
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages examined publish no price at all, one asks the cost question in its own FAQ and declines to answer, and two quote US dollars. This page leads with sourced AED bands, names who published each, and states plainly that they are market figures rather than ours.

whyPoints.title: The Dubai travel premium made visible
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor crossing the city at 16:30 spends two to two and a half hours of their day to deliver one, and the hourly rate prices all of it. We remove the line rather than discounting it, because nobody is driving anywhere.

whyPoints.title: Coursework costed as its own budget line
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK are different work from exam preparation, and their deadlines bind first. A household that funds paper practice while an IA sits unstarted has spent in the wrong order, and no rate recovers a missed internal deadline.

whyPoints.title: The free targeting document named
whyPoints.description: KHDA publishes annual inspection reports naming attainment and progress by subject and phase. That is better targeting information than any provider's marketing, it costs nothing, and we would rather you read it before spending than after.

whyPoints.title: No approval claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK or SPEA, no Ministry accreditation and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. You will find no satisfaction percentage, star rating or student count here, because we cannot produce the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: Advice against our own short-term interest
whyPoints.description: The cheapest Diploma support starts in DP1, and the cheapest IGCSE support starts in Year 10 with a decision rather than a term of hours. Saying that to a household calling in the DP2 autumn means selling fewer hours, and it is still the honest answer.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost for a Dubai school student?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, budget online tutoring from around AED 45, and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour with a qualified tutor. Those are market figures from providers' own pages and surveys, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why will nobody in this market tell me the price?
faqs.answer: Because a quoted figure invites comparison and most providers would rather have the conversation first. Of the six competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026, three published no price at all, one asks what tutoring costs in its own frequently asked questions and then declines to answer, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. Publishing the sourced market bands, as this page does, is the simplest form of honesty available here.

faqs.question: What makes one Dubai tutoring quote higher than another?
faqs.answer: Four things, and only one is experience. Format: an in-home visit carries a Dubai afternoon drive inside the rate. Timing: specialist demand peaks before the May session and the late-afternoon slots fill first. Precision: a tutor matched to the subject rather than the specification delivers teaching instead of marks. And sequence: help bought in DP2 costs more per point than the same help bought in DP1, because the cheap options have expired.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor worth the premium in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For a younger child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, often yes. For an exam-year Diploma student, rarely. The premium prices the drive: a one-hour visit consumes two to two and a half hours of the tutor's day at the time of afternoon the roads are worst. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, so the travel line does not appear on our bills at all.

faqs.question: Did Dubai school fees go up for 2026-27?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is useful context for a tutoring budget: the school side of the bill has not moved, so a figure set the previous year has not been squeezed from that direction.

faqs.question: How should we split a budget between exams and coursework?
faqs.answer: Fund coursework first in DP1 and the DP2 autumn, then exam technique. The coordinator's internal deadlines for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK fall before any exam, and a missed internal deadline cannot be bought back at any hourly rate. Paper practice funded ahead of an unstarted IA is money spent in the wrong order, and it is the most common budgeting error we see in Dubai IB households.

faqs.question: Can the KHDA inspection report help us decide what to buy?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports, which give attainment and progress by subject and phase rather than only a headline band. That names the subjects and year groups where your school's own students do least well, which is better targeting information than any provider's marketing. Read it alongside your child's marked work.

faqs.question: Is a group class a sensible way to cut the bill?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes: a topic can be taught to four students about as efficiently as to one, and the per-student cost drops. What a group cannot do is work through one student's marked paper and the specific reasons that student loses marks, which is where most recoverable marks sit in an exam year. Ask what the actual group size is, because two and six are sold under the same word and behave very differently.

faqs.question: Does the rate rise before the May session?
faqs.answer: In this market it often does, because specialist demand peaks and the late-afternoon slots a Dubai school run forces are the first to fill. That is one reason the DP1 year is the cheap window. Ask any provider directly whether their rate moves with the calendar, because a September figure that rises in February is a materially different proposition and the difference is rarely volunteered until it applies.

faqs.question: Which fees tend to appear after the quote in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and they are rarely offered up. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session and how long a session runs, whether it includes VAT, what a cancellation inside 24 hours costs on either side, whether the rate rises before an exam session, and whether matching, session notes or progress reports carry a fee. Our own position: no charge for the match, no minimum booking on the trial, session notes every time.

faqs.question: How much does a tutor's UAE permit cost?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. So no tutor can reasonably attribute a higher rate to licensing. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

faqs.question: Should we consider our child's own class teacher for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Check the rules before anything else, because it may be barred. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. An independent specialist with no conflict avoids the question entirely, and no provider should be marketing that arrangement to you.

faqs.question: Can anybody sell us regulator approval or an accredited tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and the offer should end the conversation. KHDA oversees private education quality in Dubai, ADEK handles licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi, SPEA regulates Sharjah, the RAK Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None approves tutors. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises, which IB Gram does not hold.

faqs.question: Is Dubai's tutoring market getting cheaper or dearer?
faqs.answer: Supply is growing, which should help at the specialist end over time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB places eventually means more IB teachers and a deeper tutoring pool. In the short term, demand before the May session still sets the price in the specialist bands.

faqs.question: If we can fund only one subject, which should it be?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level subject with the heaviest unstarted internal assessment and the weakest current marks, in that order. HL and SL points are worth the same towards the Diploma total, so a point gained at HL costs no less and is usually harder to get unaided. Where coursework is both heavily weighted and not begun, that is the subject to fund, because a deadline missed cannot be recovered at any rate you pay later.

intro.heading: Six ways to buy the same hour, at six different prices
paragraphs: A Dubai family looking for tuition is not choosing between tutors so much as between business models, and the models price very differently for reasons that have little to do with teaching. A specialist agency, an international marketplace, an independent freelance tutor, a tuition centre running small groups, a school's own after-hours support and an online platform are six distinct propositions. Comparing their hourly rates without comparing what sits inside the hour is how families end up surprised.

The published numbers give a reasonable map. Unitors lists IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and budget online provision lower again, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner-led end. Monthly, the market shows AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What those numbers do not show is the replacement policy when a tutor leaves mid-term, whether the person named at sign-up teaches every session, whether marking is included or extra, and whether a missed session is credited or billed. Those terms vary more between models than the headline rates do, and across a Diploma they can matter more. A family paying AED 200 an hour with free reschedules may spend less across a year than one paying AED 150 with sessions lost to traffic and illness.

Greenfield International School families sit in a part of Dubai where this matters more than average. Dubai Investments Park and the southern communities around it are a long way from the city's tuition supply, which is concentrated in Jumeirah, Al Barsha and the Marina corridor. An in-home tutor willing to drive to Dubai Investments Park on a weekday evening is either charging for the journey or is the only person who offered, and neither is a strong negotiating position for a parent.

One rule applies throughout and does not change anywhere on this page. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That removes the journey from the cost and from the shortlist, which in this part of the city is the larger of the two effects.

The sections below compare the models on published terms, set out the extras that sit outside the hourly rate, and show where spending early is cheaper than spending late. The figures are the market's, attributed and dated. None of them is an IB Gram price list; for that, the free trial lesson and the consultation are the right conversation.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-greenfield-inte.programmesIntro: Greenfield International School runs the IB continuum, so the shape of a family's spend is set by the stage. The Primary Years Programme costs little to support, the Middle Years Programme is where early money is best spent, and the Diploma is where most of it is actually spent.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based learning with no external examination, so there is no mark scheme for a tutor to work against. Support at this stage is skill-specific: reading fluency, number facts, sentence construction, English as an additional language. Short blocks of eight to twelve sessions in the lower market bands are the appropriate purchase, and a standing weekly slot usually is not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families commonly start paying for tuition earlier than the need justifies, which inflates lifetime spend without changing outcomes. For a Dubai Investments Park family the useful first step is asking the class teacher whether the gap is developmental timing or a genuine skill shortfall, and buying a short diagnostic block rather than committing to a term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment with scores out of eight against lettered criteria. There is no terminal examination, so costs stay moderate, but this is where cheap and unfocused help wastes most money. A tutor who cannot say what criterion D rewards will teach content the student already holds and the report will not move.
programmes.countryNote: This is where a Greenfield International School family can spend least and gain most. Securing algebraic fluency in Year 9 removes the expensive Diploma rescue work that otherwise arrives in Year 12. Market rates for a tutor who knows the criteria sit around the AED 150 to 250 band, which is a fraction of exam-year specialist pricing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Spending concentrates here because several Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay and three Higher Level courses arrive in overlapping windows, and families buy help for more than one at a time rather than sequencing them.
programmes.countryNote: Bestimate's specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month assumes a single subject at one session a week. Two Higher Levels plus Internal Assessment coaching is a multiple of that figure. UAE schools sit the May session; no IB date appears on this page because ibo.org blocks automated verification, so confirm each deadline with the school's coordinator.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-greenfield-inte.subjectsIntro: Which subjects absorb the budget, and why. Request volume from IB continuum schools across southern Dubai follows a consistent pattern, and so does the reason families buy help in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest-volume request at Diploma and the most expensive to leave late, because Higher Level builds vertically on algebra. Paper 3 is an extended investigation marked on reasoning and the pool of tutors who have taught it to final assessment is small, which is reflected in rates at the upper end of the specialist band.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Often chosen as the lighter option and then found heavy in statistics and modelling, with technology use assumed throughout. Typically needs fewer hours than Analysis and Approaches, so the total spend is lower even at the same hourly rate, provided the calculator technique is taught as an assessed skill.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms fail when bonding was never secure, which makes late help costly because the repair runs backwards through the course. Marks also go to units and significant figures as routinely as to chemistry, and that part is cheap to fix if diagnosed.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Recall is usually sound and the losses cluster in graph-based and extended-response questions, where a relationship has to be derived from plotted data. That is a contained skill of four or five sessions rather than a term, so the efficient purchase here is small and specific.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes families buy long blocks when the actual loss is command-word discipline. Distinguish, outline and evaluate demand different structures, and correcting that is among the cheapest grade movements available in the Diploma. Re-teaching the whole syllabus is neither cheap nor usually necessary.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The cost driver is draft feedback, which is time-intensive per session rather than per week. Individual Oral preparation, marked on sustained analysis of a global issue, gives more movement per hour than general essay practice and should be bought as a short focused block.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks prose cannot recover; an unlabelled axis loses the point whatever the argument says. Higher Level evaluation is a separate taught skill with its own allocation, and teaching it is the single cheapest available grade movement in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward application to the stimulus, and students who recite theory without touching the company in front of them lose marks consistently. Quantitative tools at Higher Level, including break-even and investment appraisal, are marked on visible method.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: For families transferring into a British-route school, tier sets the ceiling: Core caps at grade 5 and Extended reaches 9. The cost of establishing which tier a student can collect marks at is two timed papers, which is trivial against the consequence of guessing.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so the stream has to be confirmed before an hour is bought or the material will be wrong.
