sections.heading: The six provider models, compared on what they publish
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself against an unnamed set of other platforms, which is not a comparison. A useful one compares models rather than brands and quotes only rates the providers themselves have published, with the month they were read. The six models a Dubai family can actually buy from are a specialist agency, an international marketplace, an independent freelance tutor, a tuition centre running small groups, school-run after-hours support, and an online one-to-one platform.

The differences that matter are mostly contractual rather than pedagogical. Does the person named at sign-up teach every session, or is there a rota? Is marking included in the hour or charged separately? What happens when a tutor leaves mid-term, and who finds the replacement? Is a session missed through illness credited or billed? Across a two-year Diploma those terms can be worth more than fifty dirhams an hour, and they are rarely on the pricing page.

Two further checks are worth making whatever the model. First, ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Because it costs nothing, no provider can present licensing as a reason for a higher rate. Second, treat any self-published star rating with scepticism: one provider in this market displays two conflicting review totals on the same page, which tells you what the number is worth.

sections.heading: The extras that sit outside the hourly rate
paragraphs: Families budget for the hour and are then caught by everything around it. Some of these costs are unavoidable and some are entirely avoidable, but almost none of them appear on a tutoring price page. Naming them in advance is the difference between a plan a family can sustain for two years and one abandoned in the second term because the total was never counted.

The largest avoidable cost is a wasted entry. A subject entered at the wrong tier, or a resit required because an entry decision was made without evidence, costs a full entry fee and a term of preparation. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, so the decision is taken while a family may not even realise it is being taken. Asking the exams officer in writing which subjects and tiers the child is entered for is free and prevents the most expensive surprise available.

The second is the cost of material. Official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards and should be read at source; a tutor who offers to supply a folder of them is creating a copyright and malpractice exposure rather than saving you money. Textbooks and revision guides are real costs and must match the correct syllabus code, or they teach content that will not be examined.

The third is time rather than money, but it converts. A session lost to traffic with an in-home tutor is usually billed. A standing slot that runs through the school's own mock weeks competes with the thing it is meant to support. A tutor matched to a subject they do not teach weekly spends the first four sessions reading the specification. Each of those is a cost with no corresponding benefit, and each is avoidable by asking one question at sign-up.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys in Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: In-home tutoring has genuine merits worth stating before any comparison. A tutor in the room holds a younger or more distractible student's attention with less effort, written working is visible without a document camera, and some families simply prefer a person present. Those are legitimate reasons, and the market prices them at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500.

In Dubai Investments Park the premium buys something smaller than it does in Jumeirah, because the journey is longer and the supply is thinner. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Dubai Investments Park in the afternoon spends most of an hour each way and can teach perhaps two sessions in an evening rather than four. The rate carries that lost capacity, and the family is also choosing from an unusually short list: not the strongest Higher Level Chemistry teacher available, but whoever will make that drive on a Tuesday.

For a mainstream subject at a mainstream level the short list may still contain good people. For Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, or Internal Assessment feedback in a less commonly taught subject, it may contain nobody at all. That is the part of the premium a family cannot buy its way out of, because the constraint is geography rather than price.

IB Gram removes the journey rather than discounting it. Lessons are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nothing on this page suggests otherwise; home visits are an India-only service. The gain in southern Dubai is larger than in the centre, because the local pool is smaller to begin with.

sections.heading: Spending early in the Middle Years Programme versus rescuing late in the Diploma
paragraphs: The cheapest intervention in the entire IB continuum is securing algebraic fluency during the Middle Years Programme, and the most expensive is repairing it in the first Diploma term. The two are the same piece of learning. The difference in cost is entirely a function of when it happens, because by Year 12 the repair has to run backwards through material the student is simultaneously being taught.

This is easy to miss at a continuum school, because the Middle Years Programme produces no external mark and so nothing forces the issue. A student can sit comfortably on criterion scores of five and six for three years with an algebraic weakness that never becomes visible, then meet Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and appear to collapse. Nothing collapsed. The gap was always there and the assessment finally asked about it.

The practical remedy costs very little. One timed paper a term, from the board the student will eventually sit, marked honestly against the published scheme, gives a family an external reference point years before the first real examination. If it shows a method or fluency problem, four to six sessions in Year 9 settle it. The same problem addressed in Year 12 is a term of work bought at specialist exam-year rates, which Bestimate places at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month.

The same logic applies to command-word discipline and to writing method out so it can be credited. Both are habits, both take weeks rather than months to establish, and both get more expensive to install the closer they are to an examination, because by then they are competing with revision for the same hours.

sections.heading: The examination calendar read as a budget document
paragraphs: The session dates are the only fixed points in a tutoring year, which makes the calendar a budgeting tool. Help bought in the final six weeks is the most expensive version of the same purchase, because only timing and technique can still move. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates are cited so they can be checked. For any future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site, since provisional timetables are revised and a restated date goes stale without anyone touching it.

There is also an administrative cost worth avoiding. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A missed paper is a resit entry and a lost series, which is the largest single avoidable cost in this whole document.

For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears here because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date on a page a family budgets against is worse than none. Work from the school's internal Internal Assessment deadlines, which sit ahead of the IB's and are the dates that actually govern the term.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge a Dubai family for tutoring
paragraphs: Price is not the only thing to verify. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences follow for a budget. Because the permit is free of charge, no tutor can reasonably present licensing as a cost to be passed on. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, which means no amount should be quoted to a parent by anybody. A figure circulating in this market could not be verified against an official source and is not repeated here.

Anything with premises is a separate matter. A tutoring operation with staff and a location in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and does not describe itself or any tutor as KHDA-approved. Any provider using that phrase should be asked for the permit number.

One further point concerns school staff. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy, but do not approach a child's own teacher for paid lessons on the assumption it is permitted.

sections.heading: What should never be bought at any price
paragraphs: A page about cost has to name the purchase that should not be made. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and so is the mechanism: it is a risk transfer, because the academic-honesty finding attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money. Priced against a withdrawn result and a university offer, it is the most expensive thing in this market.

The legitimate alternative is specific enough to hold a tutor to. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score to a draft, help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, confirm a data collection plan is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit a draft until the sentences stop being the student's. Nor should a tutor distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are linked at source. Reproducing them is a copyright matter, and unreleased material is a malpractice exposure.

A practical test for a parent weighing a quote: if the work being offered could be shown to the school's Diploma coordinator without discomfort, it is on the right side of the line. Criterion feedback passes that test. A returned draft with new paragraphs in it does not. Ask where a prospective tutor's line sits before paying, and treat an accommodating answer as the answer.

sections.heading: Availability and what a straight answer sounds like
paragraphs: No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is itself a finding. Specialist supply is finite, and the combinations families most often need urgently are the scarcest: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, a less commonly taught Diploma language, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. An immediate yes to every request is either a guess or a generalist.

The honest version is a realistic timescale and the alternatives, including the alternative of waiting. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed rather than concealed behind a contact number. It makes no practical difference to an online lesson, but a parent is entitled to know it before booking rather than to infer it later.

This matters commercially as much as ethically. A family in Dubai Investments Park matched to a generalist spends the first four sessions paying for someone to read the specification, which at the mid-market band is several hundred dirhams for no teaching. Asking whether the tutor teaches this subject at this level weekly is the cheapest piece of diligence available and it takes one sentence.

The free trial lesson exists so a mismatch costs an hour rather than a term. It is free with no card required, and the only condition is that it is a single session with the specialist who would actually teach the subject. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed. If nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly, because sending a family elsewhere is cheaper for them than taking their money.

process.title: Count the whole cost, not the hourly rate
process.description: Before comparing providers, write down the hourly rate, whether marking is included, what a missed session costs, who teaches each week, and what happens if the tutor leaves mid-term. Across a two-year Diploma those terms can outweigh fifty dirhams an hour, and none of them appears on a pricing page.

process.title: Confirm the syllabus codes in writing
process.description: Email the school's exams officer for the board, the syllabus codes and the tiers your child is entered for. It is free, it takes one message, and it prevents the two most expensive errors available: revision bought for the wrong specification, and an entry decision discovered after the deadline has passed.

process.title: Buy one marked timed paper first
process.description: A past paper under exam conditions, marked against the published scheme, with a written diagnosis naming the failing component. This is the cheapest useful hour in the whole plan because it determines every hour after it, and it often shortens the plan considerably.

process.title: Take the free trial, then sequence the subjects
process.description: One free session with the specialist who would teach, no card required. If more than one subject is weak, start with the one costing most marks and add the second only when the first has been re-tested. Sequencing holds the monthly cost near one subject's band instead of three.

process.title: Re-test, then stop or continue on purpose
process.description: At the end of the block the student sits a fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the first. Either the component moved or it did not. If it did not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes. Extending an unchanged plan is how families spend steadily and move nothing.

whyPoints.title: Models compared, not brands
whyPoints.description: The comparison on this page is between business models on terms a family can verify, with rates attributed to whoever published them and the month they were read. Every competitor in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing they can act on.

whyPoints.title: No journey inside the hour
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, nothing in the rate pays for a drive to Dubai Investments Park. In southern Dubai that is a larger share of the in-home premium than it is in Jumeirah or Al Barsha, so removing it saves more here than it would closer to the centre.

whyPoints.title: The specialist pool rather than the local one
whyPoints.description: An in-home arrangement in Dubai Investments Park means choosing from whoever will drive south on a weekday. Online, the choice is whoever teaches that component weekly. For scarce components the difference is not a matter of degree; it is the difference between someone and nobody.

whyPoints.title: Extras named before you commit
whyPoints.description: Entry fees at the wrong tier, resit entries, textbooks for the wrong syllabus code, sessions billed and lost to traffic, marking charged separately. Each is a real cost that sits outside the hourly rate, and each is avoidable with one question asked before signing rather than after.

whyPoints.title: Permit position stated accurately
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free of charge for two years, so licensing is not a cost to be passed on. No fine amounts are published and none are quoted here. IB Gram holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, operates no UAE centre, and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for the component you need at the time you need it, you are told, with a realistic timescale. Being told no quickly is cheaper for a family than paying a generalist to read the specification for four sessions, which is the usual alternative.

faqs.question: Which tuition model is best value for a Greenfield International School family?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem rather than the price. A tuition centre running small groups to a fixed scheme is reasonable value for broad content coverage and poor value for one diagnosed component. An independent in-home tutor at AED 200 to 500 is buying you a person in the room and a short local shortlist. An online one-to-one specialist at AED 150 to 450 and above buys subject depth with no travel priced in. Compare the contractual terms as well: who teaches each session, whether marking is included, and what a missed session costs across a two-year Diploma.

faqs.question: Is small-group tuition cheaper than one-to-one in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per student, almost always, because the tutor's hour is shared. Whether it is better value depends entirely on whether the students share the same problem. A group working through a scheme of work suits three students with the same content gap and suits nobody whose issue is method, timing or command-word reading, since those are individual habits. Ask what the group size is, whether it is fixed for the term, and how the scheme was chosen. A centre with premises in Dubai also needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is worth confirming.

faqs.question: What should I budget for a full IB Diploma at Greenfield International School?
faqs.answer: Using published market figures rather than ours: one subject at one weekly session runs roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month at mid-market rates, or AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above in the specialist exam-year band, per Bestimate's Dubai estimates. Across a ten-month year that is AED 6,000 to 20,000 for one subject. Two Higher Levels plus Internal Assessment coaching multiplies it. Sequencing subjects rather than running them in parallel is the single largest saving available, and it usually produces more movement because a student can absorb one habit change at a time.

faqs.question: What costs do parents in Dubai forget to budget for?
faqs.answer: Four recur. An examination entry made at the wrong tier, which costs a full entry fee and a term. A resit entry in a later series when an entry decision was taken without evidence. Textbooks bought for the wrong syllabus code, which teach content that will not be examined. And sessions billed but lost, which happens with in-home arrangements when an afternoon drive goes wrong. Marking charged separately from the hour is a fifth. None of these appears on a pricing page, and all five are avoidable by asking the exams officer and the provider one question each.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor more expensive in Dubai Investments Park than in Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is longer and the local supply is thinner. A tutor driving from Al Barsha or Jumeirah to Dubai Investments Park in the afternoon spends most of an hour each way and can teach perhaps two sessions in an evening instead of four, and the rate carries that lost capacity. The second effect is less visible: the family is choosing from whoever is willing to make that drive, which for scarce components may be nobody. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case, so the journey is removed rather than negotiated.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in the Middle Years Programme or wait for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Far cheaper to start when the problem appears, which at a continuum school is usually in the Middle Years Programme even though nothing external flags it. Securing algebraic fluency in Year 9 takes four to six sessions at mid-market rates. The same gap met in Year 12 is a term of work at specialist exam-year rates, running backwards through material the student is being taught at the same time. A cheap way to see it coming is one timed paper a term from the board the student will eventually sit, marked honestly against the published scheme.

faqs.question: Do group classes at a tuition centre need a licence in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes. The process begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is different from the MoHRE private tuition work permit an individual tutor holds, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. If a centre describes itself as KHDA-approved, asking for the permit number is reasonable.

faqs.question: Can we reduce cost by using one tutor for two children?
faqs.answer: With an in-home tutor it usually does reduce cost, because one journey covers two sessions, and that is much of the reason families arrange it. Online there is no journey to share, so the saving largely disappears, and what is traded instead is subject fit. A tutor strong in Higher Level Chemistry is not automatically right for a Year 8 mathematics gap. Separate specialists in separate slots costs more per hour and generally less per mark moved. If budget is the binding constraint, sequencing the two children's blocks is a better lever than sharing a tutor.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a better tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Rate reflects scarcity, level taught, travel and the claim being made. A tutor at the specialist band should be able to read a marked script and name the failing component, which is the capability worth paying for. A rate at the examiner-led end, which BartyED publishes at AED 650, is pricing a credential, and a parent should ask for evidence of current status rather than accepting the label. Examiner status should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Ask what the extra hundred dirhams an hour specifically buys.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we book to start with?
faqs.answer: Four to six, as a block with a defined end, after a marked timed paper has produced a written diagnosis. That is enough to shift a method, timing or command-word problem and short enough that a wrong diagnosis costs little. Do not open with a term-long standing commitment, and be wary of a provider that requires one. The block should end with a fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the first, so the decision to continue is made against evidence rather than against the impression that sessions have been going well.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during school holidays and family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and because lessons are online a pause costs nothing on either side; no journey has been committed and the same tutor and slot can resume. Some Dubai families prefer the opposite and use the summer for a concentrated block, which works well for content rebuilding when the school term is not competing for the same hours. Sessions can also follow a student who is travelling, since the only requirement is a connection and a workable time zone offset. Decide which shape you want before the holiday rather than during it.

faqs.question: Will my child's own teacher at Greenfield International School tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: You should not plan on it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify against current policy, but the direction is clear and no reputable provider should market a child's own teacher as a private option. An independent subject specialist avoids the question entirely.

faqs.question: Does tutoring help with UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly, and it is not a requirement for it. Equivalency is a process the Ministry of Education runs, and no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or accelerates it. What is published for the British track is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so verify any IB figure on moe.gov.ae directly.

faqs.question: What does a mismatched tutor cost us before we can change?
faqs.answer: That is what the free trial is for. It is a single session, free, with no card required, taken with the specialist who would actually teach the subject, so a mismatch costs an hour rather than a term. If the fit is wrong afterwards, say so early and a different specialist is proposed. The question worth asking any provider at sign-up is who teaches each session by name, because a named match that quietly becomes a rota is the most common version of this problem in Dubai and the hardest to spot from an invoice.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-greenfield-inte.closingHeading: Compare the terms, then buy one marked paper
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-greenfield-inte.closingBody: For a family at Greenfield International School weighing tuition options, two steps come before any spending. Write down each provider's terms as well as its rate: who teaches each session, whether marking is included, what a missed session costs, and what happens if the tutor leaves. Then buy one marked timed paper from the correct board and syllabus code and read the written diagnosis. Between them those two things tell you which model you need and for how long, which is the difference between a plan that lasts two years and one abandoned in the second term. Lessons run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time, with no journey priced into the hour.

intro.heading: The question a tutoring record has to answer
paragraphs: Three months into a tutoring arrangement, a parent should be able to answer a simple question without asking anybody: what has changed. Not whether the sessions feel productive, not whether the student likes the tutor, but what specifically is different in the work. Most arrangements in Dubai cannot answer it, because nothing was written down at the start and nothing has been marked and kept since. The sessions happened and left no trace.

The alternative is a record, and it is not elaborate. A dated note each week saying what was worked on, what the marked work showed and what the next task is. A baseline document at the start naming the failing component. A closing document at the end testing whether it moved. For Diploma students, a kept sequence of drafts showing how a piece of work developed. None of that requires special software and all of it can be read by a parent who does not know the subject.

Hartland International School families have a particular reason to care about the record, because the school runs a British route into the sixth form with an IB Diploma option. That means a student can sit IGCSEs marked question by question against a published scheme and then, two years later, be assessed against lettered criteria on work they produce themselves. The evidence that counts changes shape at that transition, and a family who has been collecting one kind suddenly needs another.

There is also a harder reason. Diploma work that a student produces independently has to be defensible as their own, and a documented drafting trail is what makes it defensible. A student with three dated drafts showing a question narrowing, data arriving and an argument forming is in a strong position if anyone ever asks. A student with one polished file and no history is not, even when the work is entirely their own.

So this page is about documents rather than promises. What a weekly record should contain. How to read a mock grade against the mock script, which tell you different things. What evidence a school actually uses when it forms a predicted grade. What a drafting trail looks like at each stage. And where the published examination dates sit, so the record has fixed points to measure against.

One caution about records, since they can be done badly. A log full of topic names proves only that somebody wrote a log. The entries that matter are the ones carrying a number: marks out of a total, a count of marks lost to a named cause, a criterion score with its descriptor. Those can be compared with next week's entry, and a comparison is the only thing that constitutes evidence. Everything else is a description of an hour that may or may not have achieved anything.

Delivery, once: tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one, live, over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a record-based plan this helps, because marked scripts, dated notes and draft versions accumulate in one shared place instead of in a folder somebody left at school.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-hartland-intern.programmesIntro: Hartland International School families need evidence of three kinds: progress in Key Stage 3, mark-scheme evidence through IGCSE, and criterion evidence in the Diploma. The documents differ at each stage.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examination, so school assessments are the only evidence available and they vary in form between subjects. The useful habit at this stage is collecting one timed paper a term from the board the student will eventually sit, which gives an external reference point years before it matters and costs almost nothing.
programmes.countryNote: At a Dubai British-curriculum school this is where method habits are cheapest to install. Writing working out so it can be credited, and reading command words precisely, are both habits rather than knowledge, and both take weeks in Year 8 and months in Year 11 when they compete with revision.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers graded 9-1 or A*-G, marked against a published scheme with marks allocated question by question. This is the cleanest evidence in school education: every lost mark attaches to a question, so a script shows exactly which topic, which method and which command word failed.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the June series as the main window and November as the resit route. Tiering in several subjects caps the available grade before the paper is written, and the decision is made by the school on internal evidence, which is a reason to generate evidence at both tiers in Year 10 rather than accepting an assumption.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal Assessments are marked against lettered criteria with published descriptors; final papers are externally marked. The evidence is therefore half script and half draft trail, which is a different filing problem from IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears here, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date on a page a family schedules around is worse than silence. Confirm each one with the school's Diploma coordinator, whose internal deadlines sit ahead of the IB's.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-hartland-intern.subjectsIntro: What the evidence looks like in each subject: what a marked script shows, and what a draft trail should contain. These are the courses most often brought by families in Sobha Hartland and the surrounding communities.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE and Diploma)
subjects.description: Scripts show whether method was written out, because method marks cannot be awarded for an unwritten step. The clearest before-and-after evidence in any subject: the same question type, before and after four sessions of enforced written working, with the mark difference visible.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Evidence of improvement shows in units, significant figures and completed mechanism arrows rather than in whether the chemistry is understood. The Internal Assessment draft trail should show a research question narrowing and an uncertainty analysis appearing, which is what the criteria reward.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Recall questions usually score well while graph and extended-response questions cluster the losses, which is visible on a script as a geographic pattern rather than a topic one. Progress evidence is a second script with the same cluster filled in.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-word failure is the most legible thing on a biology script: accurate content answering a different question from the one printed. Four sessions of answer-shape drills produces one of the most visible mark changes available, which makes it good first evidence that a plan is working.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IGCSE and Diploma HL and SL
subjects.description: Progress is read from annotated drafts rather than scripts. The measurable change is whether quotations are interrogated or merely placed, and whether a summary task selects well. Both are visible to a parent comparing two drafts side by side.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram errors repeat identically across a script, which makes them easy evidence: an unlabelled axis or a shift drawn the wrong way, three or four times. Higher Level evaluation has its own mark allocation and its appearance in a draft is a documented change.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study scripts show whether the stimulus was used at all. A paper of accurate theory with no reference to the company is a specific documented failure, and the improvement is countable: references to the case per answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode to the specification style is a documented skill distinct from writing working code, and trace tables show reasoning explicitly, which makes them unusually good evidence. A script reveals immediately whether a student is answering in the specification's notation.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall and data-response technique are separately assessed, and a script shows which is missing. Fieldwork or Internal Assessment components need a draft trail showing method decisions, which is also the protection against any authorship question.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so the stream must be confirmed before a plan is written or the material will be wrong.

sections.heading: What a weekly tutoring record should actually contain
paragraphs: A record is only useful if a parent who does not know the subject can read it. That rules out lesson plans full of topic names and it rules out reassurance. Four items do the work: the date, what was worked on, what the marked evidence showed, and what the student is doing before the next session. Written honestly, that fits in five lines a week and accumulates into something genuinely informative by week six.

The entry that matters most is the second one, because it is the one that can be checked. Saying that a student worked on quadratics is a description of the hour. Saying that the student scored eleven of twenty on a set of extended-response questions with nine marks lost to unwritten method is a measurement, and the following week's entry can be compared with it. The first kind of note can be written without the session happening; the second cannot.

The fourth item, the between-session task, is where most of the available progress actually comes from and where most arrangements are silent. A plan that assumes all the learning happens in the paid hour will always look as though it needs more hours. Thirty minutes of targeted practice between sessions makes one weekly hour behave like two, and the record is what makes it visible whether that practice is happening.

A monthly summary on top of the weekly notes is worth asking for, because it forces a judgement rather than a log. One paragraph naming what has changed, what has not, and whether the original diagnosis still looks right. A tutor who cannot write that paragraph after four weeks has not been measuring anything, which is useful information in itself.

sections.heading: A mock grade and a mock script answer different questions
paragraphs: Mock season produces a grade, and the grade is the least informative thing in the envelope. It tells a family roughly where the student stands against a boundary that may itself be provisional, and it tells them nothing about why. The script tells them why, and most families never see it because nobody asks. Schools generally return scripts on request, and the request is free.

Read side by side, the two documents support different decisions. The grade supports a conversation about subject choices, tiering and whether a target is realistic. The script supports a decision about what to do on Tuesday. A family holding only the grade can worry accurately and act vaguely, which is the state most Dubai parents are in during the mock term.

There is a specific trap worth naming. A mock grade that is one boundary below target invites a plan of broad revision, which is usually the wrong response. If the script shows nine marks lost to unwritten method and six to a single topic, the efficient plan is four sessions of enforced working plus a topic rebuild, not a general sweep through the syllabus. The same grade can require quite different work depending on the script behind it.

The second trap is reading one mock as a trend. A single paper under unfamiliar conditions is a data point, not a trajectory, and students who are nervous in a hall produce scripts that understate them. Two papers under the same conditions, a few weeks apart, is the minimum for a trend, which is another argument for a termly timed paper rather than waiting for the school to produce one.

sections.heading: How schools form a predicted grade, and what evidence influences it
paragraphs: Predicted grades matter because university applications depend on them, and they are formed by teachers from the evidence in front of them: internal assessments, mock performance, coursework drafts and classroom work. They are a professional judgement rather than a calculation, which means the evidence a student generates in the months before the prediction carries real weight.

This is a place where a tutoring record has a practical use beyond the sessions themselves. A parent arriving at a conversation about a prediction with a kept history of marked work and measured improvement is making a factual contribution. A parent arriving with the view that their child has been working hard with a tutor is making an assertion, and teachers hear a great many of those.

What a tutor must not do is issue a predicted grade of their own. No tutor has the body of evidence a school has, and a competing prediction from outside helps nobody; it also tends to anchor a family's expectations to a number with no standing. What a tutor can legitimately provide is an honest indicative score against published criteria or a mark against a published scheme, which is a measurement rather than a forecast.

The timing point is simple and often missed. Evidence produced after a prediction is formed cannot influence it. If the prediction is made in the autumn of the final year, the work that shapes it happened in the preceding spring and summer, which is the argument for starting a record early rather than in the term when it would be most useful to have one.

sections.heading: The drafting trail on Diploma coursework, stage by stage
paragraphs: Diploma coursework has to be the student's own work, and a documented drafting trail is both the best way to produce good work and the best protection if authorship is ever questioned. The stages are the same across Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay: a question, a plan, a first draft, a revision, a submission. Keeping each stage dated costs nothing and produces a history.

The first stage is where most of the marks are won or lost. A question broad enough to feel interesting is usually too broad to answer within the word limit, and the consequence appears at the end, when the data is collected and the argument will not fit. Narrowing a question takes a conversation. Narrowing it after the work is done means discarding work. This single stage is the highest-value hour in the whole process.

At draft stage, legitimate feedback is an honest indicative score against each lettered criterion, the published descriptor that justifies it, and the questions an examiner would ask about the student's own claims. Does this graph show what the sentence says. Is this limitation weighed or merely listed. Is the conclusion supported by the data presented. The student answers those questions in writing; the tutor does not answer them for them.

What the trail demonstrates, read later, is the shape of genuine work: a question that narrowed, data that arrived and then surprised, an argument that changed in response. Fabricated work does not have that shape. A student with three dated drafts is in a strong position if anybody asks, and a student with one polished file and no history is not, even when the work is entirely their own.

sections.heading: The examination calendar as the record's fixed points
paragraphs: A record needs dates to hang on, and the examination calendar supplies them. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November, and any page giving a UAE parent a March window is giving them a date they cannot use.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates are cited precisely because they are checkable. For any future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site, since provisional timetables are revised.

There is one administrative risk larger than any tutoring decision. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The zone belongs in the record, in writing, from the exams officer.

For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session, and no IB examination or results date appears on this page because ibo.org blocks automated verification. The dates that actually structure a Year 13 record are the school's internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines, which sit ahead of the IB's. Get those in writing at the start of the year and build the drafting trail backwards from them.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection evidence and the limits of a rating
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education.

As evidence, an inspection band is coarse. It describes a whole school across all phases and subjects, and a parent deciding what to tutor needs something finer. The valuable section is the subject and phase commentary, which names attainment and progress by area and is written by inspectors rather than by a school's marketing team. A line stating that attainment in secondary mathematics is below expectations is independent evidence worth more than any provider's claim.

Two regulatory facts sit alongside. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes strictly prohibited. The use of different or additional content in those subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, which constrains how tutoring in them can work.

And on approval claims: a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved or IB-approved. A regulator inspects schools; it does not endorse tutoring providers.

sections.heading: Why the record is also the honesty protection
paragraphs: The academic-honesty boundary and the evidence trail are the same subject viewed from two sides. Work that is genuinely the student's leaves a history, and a history is what demonstrates authorship. That is the practical reason to keep dated drafts quite apart from the quality benefit, and it is worth explaining to a student in those terms, because it makes the rule feel like protection rather than suspicion.

The context in this market makes it more than theoretical. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and the mechanism is a risk transfer: the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money. A purchased piece of work also has no drafting history, which is exactly the absence that invites a question.

The legitimate boundary is specific. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score and quote the descriptor behind it, help narrow a question until it is answerable in the word limit, confirm a method is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit until the sentences are no longer the student's. A tutor should also not distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are linked at source. The useful test for a parent is whether the whole record, including every draft and every piece of feedback, could be handed to the school's coordinator without discomfort.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what a straight answer on availability sounds like
paragraphs: The first step produces a document rather than a lesson: the most recent marked work, and a timed paper from the correct board and syllabus code sat under exam conditions and marked against the published scheme. From that comes a written diagnosis naming the component, the topic and the command words, with no predicted grade in it. If the proposed plan does not visibly follow from that document, that is the moment to ask why.

After that the shape is a block with a defined end, dated weekly notes, marked work returned, and a closing re-test on an unseen paper under the same conditions as the first. Either the component moved or it did not. If it did not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than extends, and the record is what makes that conclusion available by week four instead of at results.

Specialist supply is finite and the scarcest combinations are the ones families need most urgently: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, a less commonly taught Diploma language, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is worth noticing when every request receives an immediate yes.

Here a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before booking. The free trial is one session, free with no card required, with the specialist who would actually teach and mark. Lessons are one-to-one online; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: Ask the school for the script, not the grade
process.description: Request the marked mock or assessment paper itself. Most Dubai schools return them when asked. The grade supports a conversation about targets; the script supports a decision about what to do next week, and only one of those is actionable. If no script exists for a subject, ask what evidence the grade was formed from.

process.title: Sit one timed paper and keep it
process.description: A past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, under exam conditions, marked against the published scheme. This is the baseline document, and it is the only thing that makes a later claim of progress checkable. File it; a plan without a baseline cannot be evaluated at any point in its life.

process.title: Agree what the weekly record will contain
process.description: Date, what was worked on, what the marked evidence showed, and the task before the next session. Agree it at the start rather than hoping for it later. A tutor who declines to keep a four-line note each week is telling you something about how the sessions will be evaluated.

process.title: Take the free trial with the tutor who will mark the work
process.description: One session, free, no card required, with the specialist who would actually teach and mark. Ask what they made of the baseline paper and listen for specifics: a topic, a command word, a count of marks lost to method. Encouragement without a measurement is the signal to keep looking.

process.title: Re-test, read the record, then decide
process.description: At the close of the block a fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the baseline, read alongside the weekly notes. Either the component moved or it did not, and the record will usually have shown which by week four. If it did not, the plan changes rather than runs on.

whyPoints.title: A record a parent can read
whyPoints.description: Four lines a week: date, what was worked on, what the marked evidence showed, and the task before next time. Written that way it can be read by someone who does not know the subject and compared week to week, which is the whole point of keeping it.

whyPoints.title: Marked by the person who taught
whyPoints.description: The tutor who teaches the session marks the work and returns the script. A different marker each week makes the marking incomparable, which destroys the evidence trail even when every individual session is good. One named specialist throughout is what makes a record mean anything.

whyPoints.title: Draft trails that document authorship
whyPoints.description: Diploma coursework is staged and dated: question, plan, first draft, revision. That history is both how good work gets made and what demonstrates it was the student's. Purchased work has no history, and the absence is exactly what invites a question later.

whyPoints.title: No competing predicted grades
whyPoints.description: No tutor here will issue a predicted grade. Schools form predictions from a body of evidence no outsider holds, and a competing number anchors a family's expectations to something with no standing. An honest indicative score against a published scheme is a measurement and is offered instead.

whyPoints.title: The honest entry when nothing moved
whyPoints.description: If a block closes and the component has not shifted, the record says so and the plan changes rather than extending. That entry is the one most arrangements never produce, and producing it is the difference between a term that cost something and a year that did not.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable the tutor's location is disclosed, and there is no UAE office or centre to attend.

faqs.question: What record will we get of my child's tutoring at Hartland International School?
faqs.answer: A dated note each week containing four things: what was worked on, what the marked evidence showed in measurable terms, the error pattern seen, and the task to be done before the next session. On top of that, a written diagnosis at the start of the block, the marked scripts themselves returned rather than described, and a short monthly paragraph naming what has changed and what has not. Ask for this at the outset rather than hoping for it. A tutor who will not keep four lines a week is telling you how the sessions will be evaluated.

faqs.question: How do I get my child's mock script rather than just the grade?
faqs.answer: Ask the subject teacher or head of department directly; most Dubai schools return scripts on request and there is no cost. The grade places a student roughly against a boundary and supports conversations about targets and tiering. The script shows which topic failed, whether method was written out so marks could be awarded, how far the student got before time ran out, and whether command words were read correctly. Those four facts determine what the next four sessions should contain, and none of them is visible from a grade alone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me what grade my child will get?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of one who offers. Schools form predicted grades from a body of evidence that includes internal assessments, mocks, coursework drafts and classroom work, which no outside tutor holds. A competing prediction anchors expectations to a number with no standing and can complicate a conversation with the school. What a tutor can legitimately give you is a measurement: a mark against a published scheme, or an honest indicative score against each published criterion with the descriptor that justifies it. That is checkable, which a forecast is not.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring record help with predicted grades at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Indirectly but genuinely. Predictions are a teacher's professional judgement from the evidence in front of them, and a parent who brings a kept history of marked work and measured improvement is contributing something factual rather than an assertion. Teachers hear a great many assertions about how hard a child is working. One timing point matters: evidence produced after a prediction has been formed cannot change it, so if the prediction is made in the autumn of the final year, the work shaping it happened the preceding spring and summer.

faqs.question: Why keep dated drafts of an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and the second surprises people. The first is quality: narrowing a research question early, before data is collected, is the highest-value hour in the whole process, and a staged trail forces that to happen. The second is protection. Work that is genuinely a student's own leaves a history, with a question that narrowed, data that arrived and sometimes surprised, and an argument that changed in response. A student with three dated drafts is in a strong position if authorship is ever queried. One polished file with no history is harder to defend even when it is entirely honest.

faqs.question: What does legitimate feedback on a Diploma draft look like?
faqs.answer: An honest indicative score against each lettered criterion, the published descriptor that justifies it, and the questions an examiner would ask about the student's own claims: does this graph show what the sentence says, is this limitation weighed or merely listed, is the conclusion supported by the data presented. The student answers those in writing themselves. Nothing is inserted into the draft, nothing is rewritten and no sentence in the submitted work belongs to anyone else. A reasonable test is whether the feedback and every draft could be handed to the school's coordinator without discomfort.

faqs.question: My child's mock grade was one boundary below target. What now?
faqs.answer: Read the script before planning anything, because the same grade can need quite different work. If nine marks went to unwritten method and six to one topic, the efficient plan is four sessions of enforced written working plus a topic rebuild, not a general sweep through the syllabus. A broad revision plan is the usual response to a near-miss grade and usually the wrong one. Also treat a single paper as a data point rather than a trend: students who are nervous in a hall produce scripts that understate them, so a second paper under the same conditions is worth having.

faqs.question: What evidence should we be collecting in Years 7 to 9?
faqs.answer: One timed paper a term from the board the student will eventually sit, marked honestly against the published scheme and filed. It costs an hour and it gives an external reference point years before anything counts, which is the only way to notice a method or fluency problem while it is still cheap to fix. Writing working out so it can be credited, and reading command words precisely, are habits rather than knowledge, and they take weeks to install in Year 8 and months in Year 11 when they compete with revision for the same hours.

faqs.question: How does the evidence change between IGCSE and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It changes shape entirely. IGCSE evidence is a script: marks attached to individual questions against a published scheme, so a lost mark has an address. Diploma evidence is half script and half draft trail, because Internal Assessments are marked against lettered criteria on work the student produces over months. A family who has spent two years collecting marked papers suddenly needs to collect dated drafts instead. Both are readable by a parent, but the filing habit has to change at the transition, and the time to set it up is the start of Year 12.

faqs.question: Who marks the work if sessions are online?
faqs.answer: The tutor who taught the session, personally, with the marked script returned to the family rather than summarised. This is worth confirming with any provider, because marking passed to a different person each week makes the marking incomparable, and a record built from incomparable marking is not evidence of anything. Ask who teaches each session by name and who marks. A named match at sign-up that quietly becomes a rota is the most common version of this problem in the Dubai market and the hardest to spot from an invoice.

faqs.question: What if the record shows nothing has changed after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Then the diagnosis was probably wrong, and the plan should change rather than extend. That is the entry most tutoring arrangements never produce, because nothing was measured at the start and so nothing can be shown not to have moved. The common causes are a misread failure pattern, a content gap larger than the block allowed for, or an underlying reading or processing issue that needs the school rather than a subject tutor. Extending an unchanged plan because the sessions feel productive is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: Do you provide tutoring at homes in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a record-based plan this is an advantage rather than a compromise: marked scripts, dated notes and draft versions accumulate in one shared place instead of in a folder left at school. It also means the tutor is chosen for the component in question rather than for willingness to drive into Mohammed Bin Rashid City at four in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Can the record be shared with my child's teachers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually worth doing. The record belongs to the family, and a subject teacher who can see a baseline paper, four weeks of measured notes and a closing re-test has something concrete to weigh rather than a parental impression. It also removes a suspicion that occasionally attaches to private tutoring, which is that work being submitted has had more help than it should. A complete, shareable record is the straightforward answer to that, which is another reason to keep the drafts and the feedback together.

faqs.question: How quickly should the first evidence of change appear?
faqs.answer: For a technique or command-word problem, within three or four sessions, because answer-shape habits respond fast and the change is countable on a script. For fluency work such as algebraic manipulation, expect six to twelve sessions before a measurable shift, since automaticity is built by repetition over weeks. For a genuine content gap, longer, and the first visible change should be in the specific topic rather than in the overall mark. If a plan predicts no visible change for a whole term, ask what intermediate measurement it offers instead.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-hartland-intern.closingHeading: Start the record before you start the sessions
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-hartland-intern.closingBody: For a family at Hartland International School, the useful first move is to collect two documents: the most recent marked script from the school, and one timed past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, marked against the published scheme. Together they form a baseline, and without a baseline no later claim about progress can be checked. Agree what the weekly record will contain before the first session, keep the drafts dated for any Diploma coursework, and set a closing re-test at the start rather than at the end. Book the free trial with the specialist who would teach and mark; lessons run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-horizon-english.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach primary English and maths through to IGCSE and IB subject level, so a family with children at different stages can keep one record rather than two. Choose a subject, read what the tutor covers, and take a trial lesson first.

intro.heading: How a family actually knows tuition is working
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in Dubai are judged on feel. The child seems happier about maths, the tutor is pleasant, homework arguments have quietened, and the family continues for a year on that basis. Sometimes the feel is right. Often it is measuring the relationship rather than the learning, and the first hard evidence arrives with a school report that nobody can connect back to any particular week of work. The alternative is to decide, at the start, what counts as evidence and then collect it.

Horizon English School teaches the English National Curriculum through the primary years in Al Safa, so families here are rarely dealing with examination papers yet. That makes the evidence question harder rather than easier, because there is no external grade to point at. What exists instead is specific and perfectly usable: a reading level measured the same way twice, a timed arithmetic sheet repeated after six weeks, a piece of writing marked against the same criteria in September and in January, and a spelling pattern that stops recurring.

The families who contact us about IGCSE and IB support for Horizon pupils generally fall into two groups. The larger group is looking ahead, usually at the Year 6 to Year 7 transfer into one of the secondary schools in this part of Dubai, and wants to know what should be secure before a child meets a secondary scheme of work. The smaller group has an older sibling already in Years 10 and 11 elsewhere and wants one provider keeping one record across both children, which is a reasonable thing to want and surprisingly hard to buy.

Families should confirm current year-group provision directly with the school, since Dubai schools extend their age range often and the sector is still growing quickly. Both groups get the same discipline. Every session produces a short written note: what was worked on, what the student produced, what changed, and what is set before next time. Every fourth session produces a review that compares a repeated measure against its baseline. Nothing in that record is a prediction, and none of it is a promise about a grade; it is simply what happened, written down, so that a decision to continue or stop is made on evidence rather than on habit.

Lessons for Dubai families run online, one-to-one, over live video, with the child's own work on a shared screen and a document camera or tablet showing their handwriting as they work. That format matters for the evidence question specifically, because the annotated work is saved rather than handed back in a bag. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India, and the comparison later on this page sets out that trade honestly.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-horizon-english.programmesIntro: A Horizon family touches three stages in sequence: the primary years now, the secondary key stage that follows the transfer, and then the examined years. The evidence that counts changes completely at each step, which is the main reason progress feels harder to read as a child gets older.

programmes.name: English National Curriculum, primary years
programmes.description: Teacher assessment against year-group expectations in reading, writing and mathematics, supported by internal testing. There is no external grade, so progress has to be shown through repeated measures: the same reading assessment twice, the same timed arithmetic sheet after six weeks, the same writing criteria applied to two pieces months apart.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private primary sector is large and varied, with 227 private schools offering 17 curricula across the emirate and UK-curriculum schools accounting for the largest share of enrolment. That variety matters at transfer, because two British curriculum schools in Al Safa can still be at different points in a scheme of work.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, the years before IGCSE
programmes.description: The stage where subject specialists replace a class teacher and the volume of written work rises sharply. Evidence shifts from year-group expectations to subject assessments, and gaps that were manageable in primary become visible because nobody is tracking the whole child any more.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 6 to Year 7 move in Dubai usually involves a change of school and sometimes a change of operator, so no single teacher carries the history. A family's own record of what was secure at the end of Year 6 is genuinely useful at that point, and almost nobody keeps one.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two linear years assessed by external written papers. Evidence becomes hard and countable: component marks, mark-scheme credit, timed-paper pace. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended, which sets different grade ceilings in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: UAE centres enter candidates for the Cambridge June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and publishes a provisional timetable ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the reference.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria, so a draft is itself a piece of evidence that can be read against a rubric rather than judged by impression.
programmes.countryNote: IB programmes account for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, and the 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven openings. UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-horizon-english.subjectsIntro: For each subject below the note names the measure that is worth repeating. A measure you can run twice is worth more than a sophisticated one you run once, because only the repeat tells you whether anything moved.

subjects.name: Primary mathematics
subjects.description: Timed number fluency is the repeatable measure: the same sheet of arithmetic under the same two minutes, six weeks apart. Reasoning questions are assessed separately, because a child can be fluent and still unable to decode a word problem, and the two need different teaching.

subjects.name: Primary reading and comprehension
subjects.description: A standardised reading measure applied the same way twice is the only honest evidence here. Comprehension is tracked by question type, since inference questions and retrieval questions fail for different reasons and a single score conceals which one is weak.

subjects.name: Primary writing
subjects.description: The same criteria applied to two pieces several months apart, with the first piece kept. Sentence structure, punctuation accuracy and vocabulary range are recorded separately so improvement in one is not hidden by a plateau in another.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Evidence becomes component marks. Extended Paper 4 is where method marks live, and the recurring loss is working the student did mentally and never wrote down, which turns a nearly correct answer into no marks at all.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Track the practical or alternative-to-practical component separately from theory. Marks there go on axes, scales, units, significant figures and anomalous points, which is presentation discipline and moves quickly once it is measured.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles fluency is the leading indicator: weakness there surfaces as errors in topics that look unrelated. A short moles diagnostic repeated after a month is one of the most predictive measures available in the subject.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Measure terminology precision, not understanding. Most lost marks come from describing the right process in everyday words. A simple count of marks lost to wording, tracked across three papers, usually falls faster than families expect.

subjects.name: English Language

sections.heading: What a week-by-week record actually contains
paragraphs: An evidence record is useless if it is long, so ours is short and the same every week. Four lines: what was worked on, what the student produced, what changed, and what is set before the next session. The second line is the one that matters, because it names an artefact. 'Worked on fractions' is an activity. 'Completed eight equivalent-fraction questions, six correct, two errors both in simplifying' is evidence, and a parent can read it in five seconds.

By the fourth session there is enough material to compare. That is when the repeated measure comes out: the same timed arithmetic sheet, the same reading assessment, the same writing criteria applied to a new piece. A repeat is harder to argue with than anything else available, because the only variable that changed is the child. New measures invented each month feel more thorough and prove nothing, since a different test can move for a dozen reasons.

The record also captures what did not work, which is the part most providers leave out. If a method was tried and abandoned, it goes in the note. If a session was spent on something that turned out to be already secure, that goes in too, because it is information about where the real gap is. A record that only contains successes is a marketing document pretending to be evidence.

Over a term that produces roughly twelve notes and three reviews, which is enough to see shape. The useful judgement is not whether every week improved, since no child learns in a straight line, but whether the repeated measures moved and whether the same error keeps returning. A recurring error after six weeks of teaching means the teaching is wrong, not that the child needs more of it, and the record makes that visible rather than arguable.

sections.heading: Measuring progress in the primary years, where no grade exists
paragraphs: Primary progress is genuinely harder to evidence than examination progress, and most tutoring in this band avoids the problem by not trying. There is no external mark, year-group expectations are broad, and a child can look fine on a Tuesday and lost on a Thursday. The answer is not a more elaborate assessment; it is a small number of narrow measures used repeatedly and recorded honestly.

In mathematics the most reliable measure is timed number fluency, because it is unambiguous and it predicts a great deal. The same sheet of arithmetic under the same time limit, six weeks apart, tells you whether automaticity is building. Reasoning is measured separately, since a fluent child can still be unable to decode a word problem, and a child who decodes well can be slowed by arithmetic. Treating them as one number hides the half of the work that needs doing.

In reading, a standardised measure applied the same way twice is the only defensible evidence, and comprehension should be tracked by question type rather than as a single percentage. Retrieval questions and inference questions fail for different reasons: one is a scanning and attention problem, the other is a reasoning and vocabulary problem, and the teaching for each has almost nothing in common. A combined score conceals exactly the distinction a tutor needs.

In writing, keep the first piece. Nothing else is as convincing to a parent, or as useful to a child, as two pieces side by side with the same criteria marked on both. Track sentence structure, punctuation accuracy and vocabulary range as separate lines, because progress usually arrives in one of the three first and a single overall impression will miss it entirely while the family waits for the other two.
bullets: Few measures, used repeatedly, beat many measures used once
