sections.heading: Academic honesty across the continuum
paragraphs: The honesty boundary applies at every stage of the continuum, not only in the Diploma, and it is worth teaching a student explicitly in the Middle Years Programme so that it is already familiar when the stakes rise. The Personal Project, every Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are all the student's own work, and the IB treats breaches as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student.

This matters commercially in Dubai because at least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The transaction is a risk transfer: the fee is paid once and the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record. No grade is worth that exposure, and no page should present the option neutrally.

What a tutor may legitimately do is well defined. Teach the content the assessment rests on. Explain what each published criterion rewards. Assign an honest indicative score to a draft and quote the descriptor behind it. Help narrow a research or project question until it is answerable within the limit. Confirm a data collection plan is viable. Read what the student wrote and ask the questions an examiner would ask. Teach referencing conventions properly.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit until the sentences stop being the student's. A tutor should also not distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are linked at source. A useful parental test is whether the feedback could be shown to the school coordinator without discomfort.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when a specialist is not free
paragraphs: The first step is to get the criterion breakdown or the marked script, whichever the student's programme produces. For a Middle Years student that means asking the subject teacher which criteria the scores sit under; for a Diploma student it means a Diploma-style question set or a marked assessment. Either way the plan should follow from a document rather than from a conversation about how the student feels about the subject.

From there the shape is short and testable: a written diagnosis naming the criterion or the component, a block of four to twelve sessions depending on the gap, and a re-test against comparable work at the end. If the identified criterion has moved, continue or stop deliberately. If it has not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes rather than extends. That is the whole mechanism and it is unglamorous on purpose.

Specialist supply is finite and the scarcest combinations are the ones families need most urgently: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, a less commonly taught Diploma language, Visual Arts process portfolio support. Where nobody suitable is free, a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives rather than matched to a generalist who will read the syllabus alongside the student.

Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred. The free trial lesson is a single session, free with no card required, taken with the specialist who would actually teach, so a mismatch costs one hour instead of a term. Lessons are one-to-one online; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: Ask for the criterion breakdown
process.description: Request the per-criterion scores from the subject teacher rather than working from the summary grade. A 5 built on a strong A and a weak D is a different student from a 5 built on even scores, and the two need different work. Most Dubai schools will share the breakdown on request even when the report does not show it.

process.title: Get a piece of work with marks on it
process.description: A marked assessment, an annotated draft or a Diploma-style question set, depending on the stage. The document is what a plan is built from. A conversation about whether the student enjoys the subject is useful context and tells a tutor nothing about which criterion or component is failing.

process.title: Read a written diagnosis before agreeing anything
process.description: The diagnosis should name the criterion, the component or the technical gap, and should not contain a predicted grade. If the proposed plan does not visibly follow from the diagnosis, ask why at that point rather than after six sessions have been paid for.

process.title: Take the free trial with the subject specialist
process.description: One session, free, no card required, with the person who would actually teach at that level. Ask during the trial what they made of the criterion breakdown or the marked work, and listen for something specific. Encouragement without specifics is the signal to keep looking.

process.title: Re-test against comparable work
process.description: At the end of the block the student does comparable work under comparable conditions. Either the criterion or the component moved or it did not, and both answers are useful. If it did not move, the plan changes rather than runs on, which is the difference between a term that cost something and a year that did not.

whyPoints.title: The criteria explained, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Middle Years Programme reports are written in a vocabulary most parents were never taught, and most tutoring in Dubai works around that rather than through it. A plan here starts by naming which criterion is weak and what its descriptor actually asks for, which turns an opaque report into a task.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma gap named per subject
whyPoints.description: Describing the step up as a jump in workload is accurate and useless. The real gap is a specific technical expectation in each subject, and naming it converts a vague worry into a defined block of six to twelve sessions taken at the point when it is still cheap to close.

whyPoints.title: Evidence before a subject choice
whyPoints.description: Higher Level and Standard Level choices made in Year 11 constrain university options two years later. A short block of Diploma-style questions, marked honestly, gives a family more to decide on than a predicted grade, and it works equally well as a reason not to take a Higher Level course.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line drawn early
whyPoints.description: The boundary that matters in the Diploma is worth teaching during the Personal Project, when the stakes are lower. A tutor questions, explains criteria and teaches referencing; a tutor does not design a project, write a report or supply text. That is stated before the first session.

faqs.question: What do the MYP criterion letters on a Jumeirah Baccalaureate School report mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, scored out of eight. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, closest to a conventional test of content. Criterion B is investigating patterns in mathematics or inquiring and designing in the sciences. Criterion C is communicating, which rewards correct notation, terminology and a logical structure a reader can follow. Criterion D is applying the subject in real-life or unfamiliar contexts. The summary grade from 1 to 7 averages them, so a student can score 7 on A and 3 on D and appear unremarkable. Ask the subject teacher for the breakdown and work on the lowest letter.

faqs.question: Which of the four MYP criteria best predicts Diploma performance?
faqs.answer: Criterion D, applying the subject in unfamiliar contexts, is the most predictive. It asks a student to use a technique somewhere it was not taught, which is exactly what Diploma papers do constantly. A student who holds every procedure in the course but has only ever met them inside the question types that announce them will score well on criterion A and poorly on D, and that profile is the one most likely to find the first Diploma term difficult. Criterion C runs a close second, because every Diploma subject rewards a visible chain of reasoning and penalises an unjustified assertion.

faqs.question: Why does a student with sixes and sevens at MYP find Diploma term one hard?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma assumes a technical fluency the Middle Years Programme never explicitly demanded. In mathematics a student can explain differentiation clearly and still lose the marks when the algebra in the middle of the question breaks down. In chemistry, moles and significant figures become marked content rather than arithmetic to tidy up later. In physics, deriving a relationship from plotted data is a distinct skill from knowing the relationship. None of this is a collapse in ability and none of it is a surprise once named. It is a defined gap, usually six to twelve sessions, cheapest to close before Year 12 begins.

faqs.question: When is the best time to close the MYP to Diploma gap?
faqs.answer: The summer before Year 12, or the first few weeks of it. At that point the gap is small, nothing else is urgent and the work does not compete with the Diploma course itself. The same gap addressed in the second term of Year 12 has to be closed while the student is being taught new content and managing an Internal Assessment, which is why it costs several times as much in hours and in money. If a student is already mid-year, the order of work matters more: fix the one technical skill the rest of the subject depends on before attempting broad revision.

faqs.question: How is the MYP Personal Project assessed, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It is assessed against published criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the marks go to the process rather than to the object produced. A modest outcome with clearly evidenced thinking scores above an impressive outcome documented thinly. A tutor may help narrow the question so it is achievable, check the plan, explain what each criterion rewards, read what the student has written and ask the questions an assessor would ask, and teach how to log decisions as they happen. A tutor may not design the project, write the report or produce the outcome.

faqs.question: Should my child take a subject at Higher Level or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence rather than ambition, and check the university requirement before the choice is locked. Higher Level covers additional topics, carries more teaching hours and usually adds a paper, and it is commonly required by name for science, engineering and economics courses. The best signal from the Middle Years Programme is not the summary grade but criterion D: a student with transfer ability handles the Higher Level course better than their grade suggests, and a student carried by recall is exposed by it. A short block of Diploma-style questions, marked honestly, is worth more here than any prediction.

faqs.question: Is the Middle Years Programme harder or easier than IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Neither, usefully. They are assessed by different machinery and they reward different things. IGCSE grades come almost entirely from terminal papers marked against a published scheme question by question, which rewards paper technique, timing and writing method out so it can be credited. Middle Years Programme grades come from criterion-referenced judgements across the year, which reward inquiry, communication and application. A student strong in one is not automatically strong in the other, and a family holding a child in each system should expect different conversations rather than a single comparison.

faqs.question: My child is moving from Jumeirah Baccalaureate School to an IGCSE school. What changes?
faqs.answer: The assessment style changes more than the content does. Nothing in criterion-referenced work requires a student to write method out so that method marks can be awarded, to allocate time across a long terminal paper, or to read command words with the precision a published mark scheme demands. All three are needed from the first mock. Expect the first IGCSE assessment to look worse than the Middle Years Programme reports did, and expect that to be assessment literacy rather than a drop in ability. It is usually four to six sessions of enforced habit change plus timed practice.

faqs.question: Where should a Jumeirah Baccalaureate School family get Diploma deadlines from?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and that is as specific as this page will be, because ibo.org returns an error to automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. An unverified date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date. Confirm every Diploma deadline with the school's IB coordinator, whose internal calendar sits ahead of the IB's and is what actually governs the year. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and are cited here with their sources.

faqs.question: Could one specialist take two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within a subject group, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A specialist who teaches both Chemistry and Biology at Higher Level exists; one who credibly teaches Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and English A Language and Literature is rare enough to be worth questioning. The test is whether they teach each subject at that level weekly and can discuss its specific components. Two subjects with one tutor saves scheduling effort and risks depth. If budget is the reason, sequencing the subjects one after another is usually the better lever.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around the IB at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it as a requirement. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes strictly prohibited. Teachers of these subjects must hold appropriate KHDA approval. Because the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, tutoring in these subjects must work within the prescribed curriculum rather than substituting other material. Confirm which stream your child sits in first.

faqs.question: What should we do if the first term of Year 12 has gone badly?
faqs.answer: Get the marked work and identify whether the problem is the technical gap, the volume, or the Internal Assessment running alongside the course. Those are three different problems and the triage matters more than the hours. If it is the technical gap, a focused block on the one skill the subject rests on is the efficient move, not broad revision. If it is volume, the honest conversation may be about dropping a Higher Level to Standard Level while that is still possible. Ask the school what the deadline for that change is before planning around it.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to homes in Al Safa or Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence in Al Safa and Jumeirah is that a family chooses a specialist in the exact component causing trouble rather than whoever can reach the house by five o'clock, which matters most for the scarcest combinations such as Higher Level Paper 3 work or Visual Arts process portfolio support. There is also no UAE office or centre to attend.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a transition block usually take?
faqs.answer: Between six and twelve, depending on the subject and the gap. Command-word discipline in biology is at the short end, often three to five sessions, because it is an answer-shape habit rather than knowledge. Algebraic fluency for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches is at the long end, because automaticity is built by repetition over weeks rather than taught in a lesson. Quantitative handling in chemistry sits in between, around eight to twelve. The block should end with comparable work under comparable conditions, so the decision to continue or stop is made against evidence rather than impression.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-jumeirah-baccal.closingHeading: Start with the lowest letter on the report
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-jumeirah-baccal.closingBody: If something is not right for a student at Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, the first move costs nothing: ask the subject teacher for the criterion breakdown rather than reading the summary grade, and find the lowest letter. A weak criterion C is a different piece of work from a weak criterion D, and in the Diploma they lead to different problems. From there a written diagnosis, a block with a defined end and a re-test against comparable work is enough to know whether the plan is right. Book the free trial with the specialist who would teach the subject, and lessons run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-jumeirah-colleg.tutorsIntro: These tutors take IGCSE and A Level work for families across Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim. Each teaches one named subject at one named level, and each plan names the paper and its weighting before a single topic is scheduled.

intro.heading: Which paper, and what is it worth
paragraphs: The most useful sentence a tutor can say in a first conversation is something like: Paper 4 carries the extended-response questions and most of your lost marks are method marks the examiner could not award. The least useful is that they will cover the syllabus. The difference is not presentation. One statement implies that somebody has read the student's work against a published scheme and knows the component weightings; the other implies nobody has.

At a selective British-curriculum school like Jumeirah College the question is sharper than usual, because the problems are rarely about ability. A student in a strong cohort can be working hard, understanding the content and still sitting two boundaries below where they should be, because the losses are concentrated in a component nobody has looked at. In that situation a general revision plan is almost the worst response available: it spends the hours uniformly across material the student mostly knows.

This page is therefore organised around the structure of the qualifications rather than around reassurance. It sets out the science award routes, because whether a student is entered for three separate science IGCSEs or a combined award changes both the grade outcome and the revision load. It compares the maths options above the standard syllabus, because Additional Mathematics is a different animal from the main course and is often taken by exactly the students who need the least help with it. And it names what each paper tests and roughly what it is worth, because that is what decides where an hour should go.

There is a second reason to be specific. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects with different codes, different paper structures and different tiering rules, and a revision guide bought for the wrong board teaches content that will not be examined in that form. The school's exams officer can confirm every code in a single email, which is the cheapest piece of diligence available and the one most families skip.

What this page will not do is state component weightings as though they were fixed forever. Specifications are revised, and the authoritative figures live on the board's own site for the exact syllabus year the student is entered for. The percentages here are the shape of the assessment and the right way to think about priority; the precise numbers should be read from the live specification rather than from any tutoring site, this one included.

Delivery, once: tutoring for UAE families is one-to-one, live, over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a component-level plan that is an advantage, because the tutor is chosen for the specific paper rather than for proximity to Al Safa at five o'clock.

The decisions that matter are the science route, whether to take a second language, and whether Additional Mathematics is on offer. Each has a consequence that is hard to reverse once entries are made.
programmes.countryNote: In a strong Dubai cohort there is pressure to take the most demanding version of everything, which suits some students and quietly damages others. The useful evidence is a timed paper at the level under consideration rather than a current grade, because performance on the actual assessment is what the decision should rest on.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers graded 9-1 or A*-G, marked against a published scheme with marks attached to individual questions. The components differ in what they reward: a calculation paper, an extended-response paper and a written practical-method paper demand three distinct skills, and a student can be strong in one and weak in another within the same subject.

Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and the correct zone timetable must be used; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth, with assessment that expects a student to link topics without prompting and to argue rather than organise. The IGCSE habits that produced strong grades, particularly answering the question type a topic announces, stop being sufficient.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-jumeirah-colleg.subjectsIntro: What each subject's components actually test, and which one usually holds the lost marks. These are the courses most often brought by families around Al Safa and Jumeirah.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Content volume is high and the losses are usually command words rather than knowledge. Describe, explain, compare and suggest each demand a different answer shape, and accurate biology in the wrong shape earns nothing. Transport in plants and human physiology repay drawing and labelling over re-reading.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry hold the widest mark spread at Extended, followed by organic reaction pathways. Units and significant figures are assessed alongside the arithmetic. Qualitative analysis tables are recall and are free marks for a student who drills them.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism produce the widest spread. Circuit questions fail when a series-parallel diagram cannot be read quickly under pressure. Calculations lose marks to missing units as often as to method, which is a cheap fix once identified.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: A single or double award covering all three sciences in less depth, with its own paper structure rather than a reduced version of the separate papers. Revision material written for the separate sciences overshoots, which wastes hours on content outside the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 reward written method, and the commonest loss at the top of the cohort is a correct answer with no visible working. Setting out working in labelled lines is a habit worth four to six sessions and real marks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0606)
subjects.description: Covers calculus, trigonometric identities and series beyond the main syllabus, and functions as preparation for A Level Mathematics. It is a separate grade and a separate paper load, and it is usually a poor choice for a student who is not already secure on Extended algebra.

subjects.name: English Language (IGCSE 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: The summary task is marked on selection, not on fluency, so a student who writes well and selects badly plateaus. Directed writing rewards register, audience and form before content. Both are identifiable from one marked paper.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Marks follow close reading and frequent writing, which makes this a subject where a short block on essay structure helps and a long weekly arrangement rarely does. Quotation used as evidence rather than decoration is the measurable difference.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: For students moving to an IB Diploma sixth form elsewhere in Dubai. Higher Level assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic so calculus and proof have room, and Paper 3 is an extended investigation marked on written reasoning rather than on speed.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so the stream must be confirmed before any plan is written.

sections.heading: Triple award, combined or coordinated: what the science route decides
paragraphs: The science decision taken at the end of Year 9 is one of the most consequential on a British-curriculum timetable and one of the least discussed with parents. Separate sciences produce three distinct IGCSE grades, one each in Biology, Chemistry and Physics, with three full syllabuses and three sets of papers. Combined or coordinated award routes cover all three disciplines in less depth and produce fewer grades, with their own paper structure rather than a shortened version of the separate papers.

That last point matters practically and is routinely missed. A student on a combined award who revises from separate-science material is studying content outside their syllabus, which wastes hours and produces anxiety about topics that will never be examined. Equally, a student on separate sciences using combined-award resources is under-prepared on depth. The first question any tutor should ask about a science plan is which award route, and the second is which syllabus code.

The route also has a sixth-form consequence. Separate sciences are the conventional preparation for science A Levels and for IB Higher Level science courses, and some sixth forms expect them for entry to those subjects. A combined award does not close every door, but it narrows the conversation, and a family should ask the school directly what its own sixth form and its typical destinations require before the options form is signed.

Where tutoring contributes is evidence rather than persuasion. A timed paper from the separate-science syllabus, marked honestly against the published scheme, tells a family whether a student is collecting marks at that depth. If they are, the case for separate sciences makes itself. If they are not, the family is choosing on information rather than on the general feeling that the harder route is better.

sections.heading: What each science component tests, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Within a science subject the components are not three versions of the same examination. A multiple-choice or short-answer paper tests breadth of recall under time pressure. A structured or extended-response paper tests the ability to build an argument across several marks and to show reasoning. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental method in writing: identifying variables, describing how a reading was taken, naming sources of error and explaining how a result could be made more reliable.

A student can be strong on one and weak on another, which is why a subject-level grade hides the diagnosis. The commonest pattern in a strong Dubai cohort is solid recall with weak extended response, because the student knows the content and has never been taught to construct a six-mark answer. The second commonest is a weak practical-method paper, because it is the component that feels least like the subject and is therefore least revised.

The practical-method paper is the most tutorable component in school science, and it is almost entirely neglected. Its marks go to a specific written vocabulary that can be learned in four sessions: control variables described rather than named, uncertainty discussed rather than mentioned, improvements that address the actual source of error rather than generic suggestions about repeating the experiment. Because the assessment is written rather than laboratory-based in most centres, online delivery costs nothing on this component.

Exact weightings belong to the live specification for the student's syllabus year, and that is where they should be read, because specifications are revised. The shape, however, is stable enough to plan from: the extended-response paper usually carries the largest single share, and the practical-method paper carries enough that neglecting it entirely costs a grade boundary on its own.

sections.heading: The mathematics options above the standard syllabus
paragraphs: In a strong cohort there is usually a route above the main mathematics syllabus, and families are often unsure what it is for. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics, syllabus 0606, is a separate qualification covering calculus, trigonometric identities, series and functions beyond the Extended syllabus, and it exists largely as preparation for A Level Mathematics. It produces its own grade and its own paper load.

It is the right choice for a specific student: one who is already secure on Extended algebra, finds the main syllabus comfortable, and intends to take mathematics further. It is the wrong choice for a student who is working hard to hold a grade 7 on the main syllabus, because the additional course assumes the algebra underneath is automatic and will expose any weakness there while consuming hours the main grade needs.

The decision is often made on the wrong signal. A student with a strong current grade in a well-taught set may be scoring on familiar question types rather than on transferable fluency, and those two profiles look identical on a report. The distinguishing evidence is performance on unfamiliar algebraic manipulation under time pressure, which a timed paper shows and a grade does not.

There is a related consideration for students heading to an IB Diploma sixth form elsewhere in Dubai rather than staying for A Levels. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic so that calculus and proof have room, which is the same underlying requirement Additional Mathematics develops. A student who found the additional course manageable is generally well placed for that route; one who struggled with it should take the signal seriously.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go in English and the humanities
paragraphs: In English Language the single most useful fact is that the summary task is marked on selection rather than on expression. A student who writes elegantly and selects the wrong points plateaus around a middle grade and cannot understand why, because every piece of feedback they receive praises their writing. The fix is mechanical: identify the required content points first, then write. It takes two or three sessions and lifts a component that otherwise resists effort.

Directed writing rewards register, audience and form before content. A letter that reads like an essay loses marks that have nothing to do with the quality of the argument. This is highly teachable and routinely untaught, because it feels like a formality rather than a skill. Composition, by contrast, improves mostly through volume of reading and writing, which is work the student has to do and not something an hourly rate can substitute for.

In the humanities the split is between recall and technique. Case-study content and chronology are the student's own revision work. Source handling, data response and the structure of an evaluative answer are teachable and carry their own marks. Most families buy the reverse, paying an hourly rate for content coverage that a textbook delivers adequately and leaving the technique untaught.

English Literature deserves a blunt note. Essay quality follows from close reading of the set texts and from writing often with feedback, and an hour of weekly discussion does not substitute for either. A short block on essay structure and on using quotation as evidence rather than decoration is worth having before mocks. A two-year weekly arrangement generally is not, and saying so costs bookings.

sections.heading: Boards, codes and why the specification is the only authority
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects, with different codes, different paper structures and different tiering vocabulary. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson's equivalent is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher. Cambridge Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Computer Science 0478, English First Language 0500 or 0990. Those codes are what identify the specification a student is actually being examined against.

A revision guide bought for the wrong board teaches content in a structure that will not appear, and past papers from the wrong board train the wrong instincts. This is the commonest unforced error in Dubai household revision and it is prevented by one email to the exams officer asking for the board, the syllabus codes and the tiers. The reply is also what lets a parent read the official specification themselves rather than relying on any tutoring site.

On weightings specifically: this page gives the shape of each assessment and declines to publish precise percentages, because specifications are revised and a stale number on a page a family plans around is worse than none. The live document on the board's own site, for the student's syllabus year, is the only authority. The same applies to past papers and mark schemes, which should be read at source rather than received as a folder from a tutor; reproducing board material is a copyright matter and unreleased material is a malpractice exposure.

One administrative point sits alongside. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The zone comes from the exams officer in writing, not from a search result.

sections.heading: The examination calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November, and any page quoting a March window to a UAE parent is giving them a date they cannot act on.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Verifiable past dates: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For a future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than any restated date, because provisional timetables are revised.

Counted backwards, the decisions that matter sit far earlier than families expect. Tier and award-route decisions are taken on internal evidence around two terms before the papers. Final entry deadlines sit months ahead. That means the evidence informing them has to be generated earlier still, which is why a timed paper in Year 10 is worth more than three in the spring of Year 11.

For a student heading into an IB Diploma sixth form, UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date on a page a family plans around is worse than silence. Confirm each one with the receiving school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the regulator and claims to distrust
paragraphs: For a student applying to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking in this market states six, which the Ministry's own clarification does not support.

That has a bearing on the subject and award decisions above. A student taking separate sciences produces three of the five counted subjects in one discipline area, which is comfortable; a combined award produces fewer grades and the arithmetic should be checked rather than assumed. Equivalency is a Ministry process in any case: no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or accelerates it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Alongside any licensed curriculum, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and combined classes strictly prohibited.

Two claims should be distrusted on sight. One is regulator approval: a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, and IB Gram holds none, operates no UAE centre and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved. The other is examiner status used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, which no provider should assert and no parent should pay a premium for without evidence.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework and what they may not
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are now assessed by terminal papers, but coursework and controlled assessment survive in some subjects and in the IB Diploma, and the boundary matters in both. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and the mechanism is a risk transfer: the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money.

A tutor may teach the subject content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score to a draft and quote the descriptor that justifies it, help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, confirm a method is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit a draft until the sentences stop being the student's. Nor should a tutor distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are cited and linked at source.

A useful test for a parent is whether the feedback could be handed to the student's head of department without anybody being uncomfortable. Annotated criterion feedback passes it easily. A returned draft with new paragraphs in it does not. Ask a prospective tutor where their line sits before the first session, and treat an accommodating answer as the answer.

sections.heading: Getting the right specialist, and what happens when there is not one
paragraphs: A component-level plan needs a component-level specialist, and the supply is narrower than the demand. The scarcest combinations are predictable: Additional Mathematics 0606, A Level Further Mathematics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style, and a less commonly taught language. No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is worth noticing when every enquiry receives an immediate yes.

The question that most reliably sorts a specialist from a generalist is whether they teach that subject at that level every week, followed by what they made of the marked script you sent. A generalist can answer the first question vaguely and cannot answer the second at all. Four sessions spent reading the specification is several hundred dirhams of no teaching and is the commonest way tutoring money disappears.

Here a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives rather than being matched to whoever is free. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred from a contact number. For an online lesson it makes no practical difference, but it should be said.

The free trial is one session, free with no card required, with the specialist who would actually teach. It exists so a mismatch costs an hour rather than a term. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed; if nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly. Lessons are one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram offers no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: Get the board, the codes and the award route
process.description: One email to the exams officer asking for the board, the syllabus codes, the tiers and whether the sciences are separate or combined. Those four facts determine which specification a tutor should be planning against and which past papers are the right ones, and getting them wrong wastes a term of household revision.

process.title: Sit the specific component, not a general paper
process.description: If the suspicion is extended response, sit that paper. If it is the written practical-method component, sit that one. Marked against the published scheme for the correct code, it shows whether the suspicion was right. A general assessment averages across components and hides the thing you are looking for.

process.title: Read the diagnosis against the weightings
process.description: A written diagnosis naming the component, the topics and the command words, read alongside the component weightings in the live specification. Ten marks recoverable in a heavily weighted paper is worth more than twenty in a lightly weighted one, and that comparison is what sets the priority.

process.title: Take the free trial with the component specialist
process.description: One free session, no card required, with the person who would actually teach. Ask what they made of the marked component and listen for specifics: a command word, a mark-scheme point, a named topic. Encouragement without a mark-scheme reference is the signal to keep looking.

process.title: Re-sit the component and compare
process.description: At the close of the block, the same component again, unseen, under the same conditions. Either the marks moved on that paper or they did not. Comparing a specific component before and after is far more informative than comparing subject grades, which move for many reasons.

whyPoints.title: Plans named by paper, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A plan that says Paper 4 extended response and names the topics is checkable against the specification and against the marked script. A plan that says it will cover the syllabus cannot be checked at all, which is why the first kind takes longer to write and is worth more.

whyPoints.title: Award routes treated as a real decision
whyPoints.description: Whether a student sits separate sciences or a combined award changes the grades produced, the revision load and the sixth-form conversation. It is decided at the end of Year 9 and is hard to reverse, and it deserves a timed paper as evidence rather than a general preference for the harder route.

whyPoints.title: The practical-method paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: The written alternative-to-practical component is the most tutorable part of school science and the least revised, because it feels least like the subject. Its marks go to a specific vocabulary that can be learned in four sessions, and neglecting it entirely can cost a grade boundary.

whyPoints.title: Weightings read from the live specification
whyPoints.description: This page gives the shape of each assessment and declines to publish exact percentages, because specifications are revised and a stale figure is worse than none. The board's own document for the student's syllabus year is the only authority, and a family can read it themselves.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where tutoring helps least
whyPoints.description: English Literature and content recall repay a long weekly arrangement poorly, because the work that moves those grades is reading, writing and memorising the student must do. Naming that costs bookings and is the reason the rest of the advice on this page can be trusted.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable the tutor's location is disclosed, and there is no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: Should a Jumeirah College student take separate sciences or a combined award?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence rather than on a general preference for the harder route. Separate sciences produce three distinct IGCSE grades with three full syllabuses and are the conventional preparation for science A Levels and IB Higher Level courses. A combined or coordinated award covers all three disciplines in less depth with its own paper structure and frees an option slot. Sit a timed separate-science paper, marked honestly against the published scheme, and see whether the student is collecting marks at that depth. Also ask the school directly what its sixth form expects, before the options form is signed.

faqs.question: Can revision material for separate sciences be used for a combined award?
faqs.answer: No, and this is one of the commonest wasted-effort errors in Dubai households. A combined or coordinated award has its own syllabus and its own paper structure; it is not a shortened version of the separate-science papers. A student revising from separate-science material is studying content that will not be examined and generating anxiety about topics outside their course. Confirm the award route and the syllabus code with the exams officer, then buy resources that match that code exactly. The same applies in reverse: combined-award material under-prepares a separate-science candidate on depth.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how is it tutored?
faqs.answer: In most Dubai centres the science practical component is assessed by a written paper rather than a laboratory examination. It is marked on experimental method: identifying independent and controlled variables, describing how a reading was taken, naming sources of error, and explaining how a result could be made more reliable. The marks go to a specific written vocabulary, which is learnable in about four sessions and is almost always the least revised component in the subject. Because it is a written assessment, online delivery costs nothing here. Confirm with the school which component your child is entered for.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics worth taking?
faqs.answer: For the right student, yes. Syllabus 0606 covers calculus, trigonometric identities, series and functions beyond the Extended syllabus and serves as preparation for A Level Mathematics, producing its own grade and its own paper load. It suits a student already secure on Extended algebra who finds the main syllabus comfortable and intends to continue with mathematics. It is a poor choice for a student working hard to hold a strong grade on the main syllabus, because it assumes the underlying algebra is automatic and will consume hours that grade needs.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child is ready for Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Not from the current grade, which in a well-taught set can reflect scoring on familiar question types rather than transferable fluency. The distinguishing evidence is performance on unfamiliar algebraic manipulation under time pressure, which a timed paper shows and a report does not. A student who handles rearrangement, fractional and negative indices and multi-step substitution without slowing down is ready. One who understands each step but works slowly through it will find the additional course consumes the time the main syllabus needs. Two timed papers settle the question cheaply.

faqs.question: Why does my child write good answers and still lose marks in English Language?
faqs.answer: Most often because the summary task is marked on selection rather than on expression. A student who writes elegantly and identifies the wrong content points plateaus around a middle grade while receiving feedback that praises their writing, which is both accurate and unhelpful. The fix is mechanical and takes two or three sessions: identify the required content points first, then write. Directed writing has a parallel issue, where marks go to register, audience and form before content, so a letter that reads like an essay loses marks unrelated to the quality of its argument.

faqs.question: Which component usually holds the lost marks in a strong cohort?
faqs.answer: The extended-response paper, followed by the written practical-method component. In a strong Dubai cohort the pattern is consistent: recall is solid because the content has been well taught and revised, and the losses concentrate where a student has to construct a multi-mark argument or write about experimental method. Both are skills rather than knowledge, which is why they resist more revision and respond quickly to targeted work. Identifying which of the two is the problem needs the marked script rather than the subject grade, since the grade averages across the components.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish exact paper weightings on this page?
faqs.answer: Because specifications are revised and a stale percentage on a page a family plans around is worse than no figure at all. What is stable enough to plan from is the shape: the extended-response paper usually carries the largest single share, and the written practical-method component carries enough that ignoring it can cost a grade boundary. The authoritative numbers live in the live specification on the board's own site for the exact syllabus year your child is entered for, and a parent can read that document directly once they have the code from the exams officer.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board and syllabus codes my child sits?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer and request the codes rather than the board name alone. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects with different paper structures and different tier vocabulary, so a revision guide bought for the wrong board teaches content in a form that will not appear. The reply should give you something like 0580 for Cambridge Mathematics or 4MA1 for Pearson. While you are asking, request the tiers, the science award route and the centre's Cambridge administrative zone, since all four affect planning.

faqs.question: Does a strong school cohort mean tutoring is unnecessary?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it does change what tutoring should be for. In a strong cohort the content is usually well taught and the losses are concentrated in a component nobody has examined: the extended-response paper, the written practical method, the summary task's selection. A general revision plan is close to the worst response, because it spreads hours across material the student already holds. The right purchase is narrow, identified from a marked script, and often only four to six sessions. A standing weekly slot booked out of caution is the expensive alternative.

faqs.question: What changes between IGCSE and A Level in the same subject?
faqs.answer: The expectation that a student links topics without being prompted, and in the essay subjects the shift from an organised answer to an argued one. IGCSE questions tend to announce which topic they are testing; A Level questions frequently do not, and a student who scored well by recognising question types finds that skill stops working. The efficient response is a short diagnostic block early in Year 12 aimed at that specific gap, rather than a standing weekly slot covering content the school is already teaching well.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Al Safa or Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a component-level plan this is an advantage: the tutor is chosen for the specific paper rather than for proximity to Al Safa at five o'clock, which matters most for the scarcest components such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or specification-style pseudocode. There is also no UAE office or centre to attend.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades does UAE equivalency actually require?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market states six, which the Ministry's own clarification does not support. This bears on the science award decision, since separate sciences produce three counted grades and a combined award produces fewer. Verify with the Ministry before planning entries around it.

faqs.question: What should we have in hand after the first paid hour?
faqs.answer: A document rather than a lesson: the specific component sat under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme for the correct syllabus code, and a written diagnosis naming the topics and command words costing marks. Read alongside the component weightings in the live specification, that tells you where an hour is worth spending, because ten recoverable marks on a heavily weighted paper outrank twenty on a lightly weighted one. A first session that produces only a pleasant impression of the subject has told you nothing a plan can be built on.

intro.heading: Dubai has the deepest tutoring market in the country and the least transparent pricing
paragraphs: Research for this market fetched and read sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026, and the pricing finding was consistent. Three of the six pages competing for queries like this one publish no price at all. The two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family at an Arabian Ranches school pays school fees in or budgets a month in. One agency's own frequently asked questions poses the cost question and then declines to answer it. That is not an accident of layout; it is a strategy, and it works because a parent with no reference range cannot compare anything.

So this page leads with money and keeps its sources attached. The market bands by provider model, with who publishes what. What an hour of tutoring actually contains, which matters because an hourly rate is not a unit of teaching. The Dubai-specific factors that move a quote, which are different from the factors in a smaller emirate. The exam-season surge, which is the largest avoidable cost available to a family in this city. And the five questions that settle a price in writing.

What makes Dubai distinctive is depth of supply. The emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian twenty-six, American fourteen and the International Baccalaureate seven. A sector that size employs a great many subject teachers, which pushes rates down at the ordinary end and makes genuine scarcity rarer than in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. It also means the top of the market has room to charge whatever reputation will bear, and one provider publishes AED 650 an hour.

IB Gram supports Arabian Ranches families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that statement appears on every country page this site publishes. The Dubai in-home market is substantial and publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. A later section breaks that premium into its parts community by community, because in a city where the afternoon commute is the real variable, what the premium buys differs by postcode.

Two things are deliberately absent. No statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because making one responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and this page has none; ask any provider in writing whether a quoted figure is inclusive. And no fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, because the ministry published no schedule and the figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. Both absences are deliberate, and they are the kind of absence worth looking for on any page that quotes money. A provider willing to publish a number it cannot source will publish others, and a parent then has no way to tell which figures on that page were read from a document and which were estimated into existence.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects assessed by terminal paper, with tiering and a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. The widest specialist supply of any stage in Dubai, which keeps rates nearest the middle of the published band.
programmes.countryNote: The pricing decision at this stage is usually how many subjects, and the honest answer is normally fewer than families start with. Two subjects at two sessions a week is four sessions plus four sets of homework on top of nine certificates, and the common result is two half-improvements at double the monthly cost of one completed one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the minimum. Higher Level subjects draw on a smaller pool than IGCSE, so rates sit higher and booking earlier matters more than it does lower down.
programmes.countryNote: Published market monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run from roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, the highest band for any tutoring in the country. programmes.name: AS and A Level, where that route is taken
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken deeper with no compulsory core. Confirm the current sixth-form provision with the school, since offers change. Where a choice exists it also changes the tutoring budget, because fewer subjects concentrate the spend.
programmes.countryNote: A Level support is often cheaper in total than Diploma support for the same household, simply because there are three subjects rather than six and no core to coach. That is a budgeting fact rather than an argument for the route, and it should not decide a choice that shapes the next four years.

programmes.name: The years before the options form
programmes.description: The cheapest tutoring in the whole school career and the stage most families skip. Nothing is yet being repaired against a deadline, the specialist requirement is lower, and a weakness identified here costs a handful of sessions rather than a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Higher Level subject in the Gulf, which makes autumn booking materially easier than spring booking. Standard Level runs two papers at forty per cent each plus the Exploration at twenty; Higher Level adds Paper 3 at twenty and rebalances the rest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Less requested than Analysis and Approaches, which usually means a shorter wait rather than a lower rate. Modelling questions need written interpretation in context, and calculator technique is examinable in its own right.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Reasonably available in Dubai and scarce almost everywhere else in the country, which is a direct illustration of why emirate matters to price. Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, investigation at twenty with a 3,000-word cap.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Comparable availability to Chemistry. The hidden cost driver is algebraic fluency: a Physics student who is also weak in mathematics needs more hours, and a good tutor says so in the first fortnight rather than the third month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The widest supply of the three sciences and the heaviest content load, so the hours tend to be more numerous and individually less specialised. Most of the gain comes from retrieval practice, which is cheap per unit of improvement.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Efficient to tutor because diagram accuracy is a narrow teachable skill carrying a disproportionate share of the marks. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each on real published articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Wide availability keeps rates mid-band. The Individual Oral, worth thirty per cent at Standard Level, is where hours convert fastest, because rehearsal against published criteria is a dependable technology.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Available and inexpensive relative to the sciences. The pre-released case for the Higher Level paper is the single best use of booked hours, because it can be worked through months before the examination and usually is not.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics and Sciences
subjects.description: The deepest supply and therefore the most competitive pricing of anything on this list. Confirm the syllabus code first: Cambridge sciences carry a twenty per cent practical component while Pearson Edexcel sciences have no separate practical exam.

subjects.name: Computer Science and Design Technology
subjects.description: Scarcer than the mainstream subjects even in Dubai, so availability rather than rate is usually the binding constraint. Both pair theory with an internal assessment where documentation is marked alongside the product.

sections.heading: The market bands, and which provider model charges what
paragraphs: Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online platforms and university-student tutors between roughly AED 45 and 150 an hour, with some platform entry rates quoted from AED 33. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, and one agency publishes AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500. At the top, a single provider publishes AED 650 an hour.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those two look comparable and are not: the second buys eight hours of contact time, the first buys eight sessions of unstated length. Convert every package to a cost per contact hour before putting it next to an hourly rate, because that single step resolves most of the confusion in this market.

Each figure belongs to the provider that published it, and quoting one is neither an endorsement nor a comment on quality. They appear here because an Arabian Ranches parent needs a reference range and the pages competing for this search decline to supply one. IB Gram's own figure is not in the table, because a single number would mislead: it depends on subject, level and frequency, and it follows the free trial lesson.

One instruction before comparing anything. Ask every provider, this one included, whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and require the answer in writing. This page states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees because doing so responsibly needs a Federal Tax Authority citation, and there is none here. What a parent can always do is make the inclusive or exclusive position explicit in the quote itself.

sections.heading: What an hour actually contains, and why the rate alone is meaningless
paragraphs: An hourly rate implies that the unit being bought is an hour of talking, and for some providers that is exactly what it is. For others the hour sits on top of work done outside it: marking what the student produced since last time, planning the session against the school's scheme, and writing something a parent can read. Two providers at the same nominal rate can therefore be selling quite different things, and nobody in this market itemises it.

Marking is the part that matters most and is least visible. A piece of work annotated properly away from the student, against the official mark scheme, produces a document that can be compared with next month's. The same correction made verbally in the room leaves nothing behind. If marking is not included in the rate, the arrangement generates no evidence, and a family discovers whether it worked at results rather than in week five.

Planning is the second invisible component. A session built against the school's scheme of work, so that the student meets a topic shortly before or after their class does, is worth more than the same hour spent on whatever the student mentions first. That alignment requires knowing what the school is covering, which requires asking, which takes time outside the session.

The practical move is to ask the question directly: of this rate, how much is contact time, who marks work between sessions and is that time included, and what will I receive in writing after four weeks. A provider that answers plainly is giving you more than any of the pages competing for this search. A provider that treats the question as unusual has answered it.

sections.heading: The travel premium, community by community
paragraphs: In-home and online bands overlap, which makes the comparison look like taste. Split the in-home figure into its parts and it stops being a preference. A travelling tutor is paid for teaching, for the journey, and for the scarcity of people willing to make that journey at that hour. In Arabian Ranches itself the journey is short and the premium is mostly genuine convenience. In Mudon, Damac Hills or Jumeirah Golf Estates the journey is long enough that a meaningful share of the rate is a car on the Dubailand corridor at five in the afternoon.

There is a second cost that nobody prices and everybody experiences: drift. An arrival is not a start time. A session booked for 17:00 that begins at 17:20 and ends on time has lost a third of itself, and the part that gets cut is always the end, where the review happens and the next week's work is set. Over a term that converts a weekly arrangement into something closer to fortnightly at weekly cost, and the family concludes the tutoring is not working when what is not working is the traffic.

The honest counterweight is that presence matters for some students, particularly younger ones who need supervision as much as teaching, and for anyone whose attention has to be externally managed. The mitigations for a screen are specific rather than reassuring: shorter sessions with a break, a shared document the tutor writes on live so the student watches working appear, a visible worked page rather than a talking head, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks.

For a Year 11 or Diploma student in this catchment the arithmetic usually favours online, and not because of the headline rate. It favours online because a fixed slot and marked work between sessions produce evidence, and an arrival window on a busy corridor produces a pleasant relationship with no document at the end of it.

sections.heading: Tutoring against the other education lines in a Dubai household
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest education line in a household in this catchment, which is exactly why it is the line that gets examined. Seeing it in proportion changes how it is decided. Fees dominate. Examination entry as a private candidate is a real cost families forget until the invoice arrives. And a two-year commitment at one session a week is a different kind of obligation from a four-session block, even at an identical hourly rate.

On fees, the context is unusually clear in Dubai right now. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting across a year, a flat fee line makes the discretionary lines easier to plan and harder to justify loosely.

The supply picture is also expanding, which matters for scarcity and therefore for price over time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. More International Baccalaureate places means more Diploma teachers in the city over time, which is the structural reason Dubai rates for Higher Level subjects sit below those in emirates where the pool is thin.

The planning conclusion is unexciting and correct. Set the annual tutoring line in the household education budget before choosing a provider, then pick the arrangement that fits it. A family that decides it can spend the mid-range monthly band on one subject for a year makes better decisions than one that starts with two subjects at two sessions a week and revisits the figure when it becomes uncomfortable in March.

sections.heading: The exam-season surge, and how not to pay it
paragraphs: The largest avoidable cost in Dubai tutoring is not a provider's margin. It is timing. Published market estimates put specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for a weekly hour, the highest band for any tutoring in the country, and a substantial part of that is scarcity in the spring rather than any difference in teaching quality. In February every family in the Gulf is looking for the same Higher Level specialists, and the specialists are choosing.

The same person booked in the autumn of the first Diploma year, or in Year 10 rather than Year 11, costs less per month, is actually available, and has four times as long to work in. That is not a marketing claim; it is the structure of a market with seasonal demand. The analogy is unglamorous but exact: you are not buying better teaching in the spring, you are buying the last seat on a flight.

There is a second-order effect that matters more than the money. A specialist engaged late is engaged for repair, and repair has a ceiling. Content gaps close at roughly two to four weeks per topic, which means a student with gaps across a syllabus eight weeks out cannot close them all and should be told so honestly rather than sold a plan that assumes otherwise. The same hours spent a year earlier would have been teaching rather than triage.

Avoiding the surge takes one decision made once: fix the tutoring line in the budget at the start of the school year rather than at the first crisis, and engage in the autumn for whichever subject the previous year's evidence flagged. Families who do this spend less in total and get more, and they also stop competing with the whole city for the same fortnight in February.

sections.heading: Where families in this catchment waste money
paragraphs: Five patterns account for most wasted spend, and none involves a bad tutor. The first is the surge above. The second is buying hours before a diagnostic: if nobody has sat a timed paper, marked it against the official scheme and attributed every lost mark to a cause, the plan is a guess and the hours go wherever the student's anxiety points. The six causes — content not known, content not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method not written out, time ran out — need different remedies, and five of six are not fixed by more teaching.

The third is spreading across subjects. Two subjects at two sessions a week each is four sessions plus four sets of homework on top of a full Dubai school week, which is longer than it looks because Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in every private school in the emirate. Sequencing produces better results for the same money: the subject with the shortest loss list first, banked, then the hours move.

The fourth is paying for presence a student does not need, analysed community by community above. The fifth is the quietest: never reviewing. An arrangement that made sense in October is rarely examined in February. What to ask for is the written risk list from the diagnostic, updated monthly, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work behind it. An item unchanged after three weeks is a conversation. Three unchanged after two months means something should change.

There is also a sixth pattern worth naming because it is specific to a deep market. In a city with 227 private schools and a large tutoring sector, there is always somebody cheaper and always somebody more expensive, and families churn between them. Each change costs a diagnostic, a relationship and usually a month. Changing because the evidence says the arrangement is not working is rational; changing because a cheaper rate appeared is usually not.

sections.heading: Five questions that settle a price, in writing
paragraphs: Most price conversations in this market are vague because nobody asks precisely. Five questions, answered in writing, settle almost everything and take one message to send. They also sort providers quickly, because a provider who answers all five plainly is offering more transparency than any of the pages competing for this search.

First: does the figure include VAT. This page deliberately asserts nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation. What a parent can always do is require the inclusive or exclusive position in the quote. Second: is the rate per hour or per session, and how long is a session. A package of eight sessions is not eight hours unless somebody says so.

Third: what happens if we stop after one month. Notice periods and minimum commitments are legitimate and should be stated before payment, not discovered afterwards. Fourth: who marks work between sessions, against what, and is that time inside the rate. This is the question that separates an arrangement which produces evidence from one that produces a pleasant relationship. Fifth: what happens if the matched tutor becomes unavailable, and is there a handover of the written risk list.

Two more are worth adding for anything described as free. A trial should be free without conditions that appear later, and any condition attached to the word free belongs on the same screen as the word. And if a provider states a rating, a satisfaction percentage or a student count, ask for the sample size, the date and the method. Several pages in this market publish figures with none of the three, and one shows two different ratings in the same document.
