sections.heading: What this page will not claim, and why that is the point
paragraphs: A page about money in this market is exactly where the overclaims live, so here is what is absent and why. No statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation. No fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, because the ministry did not publish a schedule and the number circulating online could not be verified. No IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency, because no official source for one could be read. No star rating, no satisfaction percentage, no student count, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method attached.

On permits, the relevant cost is zero. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

On assessed work, the cheapest-looking purchase in this market is the most expensive thing on any menu. A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work at a fixed price. Submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the board's rules, and the consequence falls on the student's qualification rather than the seller's business. Measured against two years of work and a university offer, nothing else in this market costs as much.

And position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, and has no arrangement with any school named on this page. Every rate quoted belongs to the provider that published it, and ours arrives after a trial lesson rather than before one.

process.title: Fix the annual tutoring line before choosing a provider
process.description: Decide what the household can spend across the year, then choose the arrangement that fits. Families who pick a provider first and discover the annual figure in March make worse decisions than those who commit to the mid-range monthly band on one subject for a year.

process.title: Engage in the autumn on last year's evidence
process.description: The spring premium is scarcity, not quality. The same specialist booked in the autumn of Year 10 or the first Diploma year costs less per month, is actually available, and has four times as long to work in. One decision made once removes the largest avoidable cost in this market.

process.title: Send the subject, level or tier, and the syllabus code
process.description: Level and subject scarcity are two of the drivers that move a quote, and the syllabus code determines the papers. Cambridge sciences carry a twenty per cent practical component; Pearson Edexcel sciences have no separate practical exam. Guessing costs the first two sessions.

process.title: Take the trial lesson before discussing money
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, with you able to listen in. If the explanation does not land with your child the price is irrelevant. If it does, the quote can be judged against the market bands published on this page rather than against nothing at all.

process.title: Ask the five price questions in writing
process.description: VAT inclusion. Per hour or per session and the session length. Cancellation after a month. Who marks work between sessions and whether that is inside the rate. What happens if the tutor becomes unavailable. Answers in writing are the whole point of asking.

process.title: Insist on a diagnostic before buying a block
process.description: A timed paper marked against the official scheme with losses attributed to six causes. A short specific list makes a concentrated spend rational; a long diffuse one tells you to spread the work over a longer period instead, which is a cheaper and more honest plan.

whyPoints.title: A published band, with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price and two quote in dollars. Every figure here is a market rate read in October 2026, attributed to the provider model that published it, so an Arabian Ranches parent has a reference range rather than a conversation with no anchor.

whyPoints.title: The hour itemised
whyPoints.description: Contact time, marking, planning against the school's scheme, written reporting, the diagnostic, and the handover if a tutor becomes unavailable. Two providers at the same nominal rate can be selling very different things, and nobody in this market breaks it down.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium priced by community
whyPoints.description: Short from Arabian Ranches itself, substantial from Mudon, Damac Hills or the Marina at peak. Drift is the cost nobody quotes: a session starting twenty minutes late and ending on time has lost the part where next week's work gets set.

whyPoints.title: The seasonal surge named
whyPoints.description: Exam-year specialist support is the highest published band in the country, and much of the spring premium is scarcity rather than quality. Engaging in the autumn buys the same person for less, with four times as long to work in.

whyPoints.title: Dubai context rather than generic context
whyPoints.description: 227 private schools, 387,441 students, seventeen curricula, no fee increase for 2026-27 confirmed in May 2026, and seven new schools adding 16,846 places. Depth of supply is why Dubai rates sit below thin-market emirates, and it is a real planning fact.

whyPoints.title: Nothing asserted that cannot be sourced
whyPoints.description: No VAT treatment, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation. No fine amount, because none was published. No equivalency points threshold, no star rating, no satisfaction percentage. The absences on a money page are the most informative part of it.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost for a JESS Arabian Ranches family?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, a named IB specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits including travel at roughly AED 180 to 500, and budget platforms between AED 45 and 150. One provider publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those belong to the providers who published them and are not IB Gram prices; ours follows a free trial lesson and depends on subject, level and frequency.

faqs.question: Why are Dubai tutoring rates lower than in the smaller emirates for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Depth of supply. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, and a sector that size employs a great many subject teachers. Scarcity premiums for Higher Level sciences and mathematics are therefore rarer here than in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, where the number of people who have taught a given course recently can be close to zero. The expansion continues: seven new schools for 2026-27 add 16,846 places.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying hourly?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what a session is, so convert the package to a cost per contact hour first. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The second buys eight hours of contact; the first buys eight sessions of unstated length. Ask how long a session runs before comparing either figure against an hourly rate.

faqs.question: What is actually included in an hourly tutoring rate?
faqs.answer: It varies far more than families expect. Contact teaching time always; marking of work between sessions sometimes; planning against the school's scheme of work rarely stated; written reporting to the parent rarely included; and a handover if the tutor becomes unavailable almost never mentioned. Marking is the element that matters most, because a properly annotated script is a document you can compare with next month's, while a verbal correction in the room leaves nothing behind.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium make sense from Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: It is the fairest place in this catchment to compare the formats, because the journey to the school's immediate area is short, so the premium is mostly genuine convenience rather than travel. From Mudon, Damac Hills, Jumeirah Golf Estates or the Marina at peak, a large share of the rate is a car on a busy corridor. The cost nobody quotes is drift: a session starting twenty minutes late and ending on time loses the end, where next week's work is set.

faqs.question: Should an Arabian Ranches parent ask whether a tutoring quote is VAT inclusive?
faqs.answer: Ask whoever is quoting, in writing, and require the answer before paying. This page deliberately states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none on offer here. Making the inclusive or exclusive position explicit in the quote is something a parent can always insist on, and it belongs alongside session length, cancellation terms and whether marking time is inside the rate.

faqs.question: How do I avoid the exam-season price surge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Engage in the autumn rather than the spring. Published monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run from roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, the highest band for any tutoring in the country, and much of that premium is scarcity in February when every family in the Gulf wants the same Higher Level specialists. The same person booked a year earlier costs less per month, is available, and has four times as long to work in.

faqs.question: How much should I budget monthly for one Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for a single weekly one-hour session put budget options at roughly AED 240 to 600, a mid-range qualified tutor at roughly AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. The mid-range band across the first Diploma year is the lowest cost per grade gained, because the work is developmental rather than repair. Set that line in the household budget before choosing a provider.

faqs.question: Is two subjects at once good value for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Rarely as a starting point. Two subjects at two sessions a week is four sessions plus four sets of homework on top of a Dubai school week that already includes Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside the licensed curriculum. The usual outcome is two half-improvements at double the cost of one completed one. Sequencing works better: the subject whose diagnostic shows the shortest loss list first, banked, then the hours move.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest genuinely useful purchase for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: A defined block of four to six sessions on one named component with a published weighting: the internal assessment plan, the Individual Oral at thirty per cent, the pre-released business case, or Paper 3 at Higher Level mathematics. Priced as a block rather than monthly, with a visible finish. Many families would do better with two of those a year than with an open-ended weekly arrangement nobody re-examines after the first term.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze affect what I should spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, by making the year easier to plan. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A flat fee line makes the discretionary lines easier to budget and harder to justify loosely, which argues for setting the annual tutoring figure deliberately rather than by accumulation.

faqs.question: Should I change tutors if I find a cheaper rate?
faqs.answer: Only if the evidence says the current arrangement is not working. In a city with 227 private schools and a large tutoring sector there is always somebody cheaper and always somebody more expensive, and each change costs a diagnostic, a relationship and usually a month of progress. Changing because the written risk list shows three items unchanged after two months is rational. Changing because a lower figure appeared generally is not.

faqs.question: What does the UAE tutoring permit cost, and does it affect price?
faqs.answer: It costs nothing, so it should not affect any quote. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Because it is free and fast there is no reasonable explanation for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Why does this page not publish IB Gram's own rate?
faqs.answer: Because a single number would mislead. What we charge depends on the subject, the level, how often you meet and whether the engagement is a defined block or an open commitment, and those produce genuinely different figures. Publishing one rate would mean either overstating the cost of a simple arrangement or understating a complex one. The market bands here give you a reference range, the trial lesson is free, and the quote follows it rather than preceding it.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-jumeirah-englis.closingBody: For a family in this catchment the sequence matters more than the provider. Decide the annual tutoring line first. Take the free trial lesson and judge the explanation rather than the enthusiasm. Then ask, in writing, whether the figure includes VAT, whether it is per hour or per session, what happens if you stop after a month, who marks work between sessions, and what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-al.tutorsIntro: These tutors take IGCSE and A Level work for families across Al Barsha, Barsha Heights and the Umm Suqeim side of the city. Each teaches one subject at one level, and no part of the hourly cost pays for a journey.

intro.heading: The spend is decided by subject count, not by rate
paragraphs: A Year 11 student at a British-curriculum school in Dubai is sitting eight or nine IGCSEs. If a family decides to tutor four of them at mid-market rates, the monthly cost is four times Bestimate's published band of AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour, which is AED 2,400 to 4,800 a month. If they tutor one, it is AED 600 to 1,200. The hourly rate is identical in both cases. The decision that moved the number by a factor of four was which subjects, and almost nobody makes it deliberately.

The usual pattern is that tutoring follows anxiety. The subject a student complains about most gets a tutor, then the subject that produced the worst mock grade, then the subject a friend's child is being tutored in. None of those is a bad instinct and none of them is evidence. What produces a sensible list is a different question: in which subjects would four to six focused sessions move more marks than the same hours spent anywhere else.

That question has an unfashionable answer. Some subjects repay paid tutoring very reliably, usually because their losses are technique rather than knowledge: mathematics, where method marks go uncollected, and the sciences, where command words and alternative-to-practical method language cost marks a student could easily collect. Others repay it poorly, because the work that moves the grade is reading, writing and revision the student has to do themselves, and an hour a week with an adult does not substitute for it.

There is a second filter specific to the UAE. The Ministry of Education counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 and above for British-track equivalency, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. A family tutoring a ninth subject toward a grade nobody will ever require is spending money on a line that does not appear in any requirement. Knowing which five matter changes the list.

Kings' School Al Barsha families sit in one of the better-supplied parts of Dubai for tutoring, which has its own effect on price. Al Barsha is central, the drive is short from several directions, and the in-home market is therefore competitive here in a way it is not in Dubai Investments Park. That makes the comparison on this page closer than it would be further out, and it is set out honestly rather than slanted.

Delivery, stated once: tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below belongs to whoever published it, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-al.programmesIntro: Kings' School Al Barsha families typically need help at one of three points: the IGCSE years, the step into A Level, or an IB Diploma route taken elsewhere for sixth form. Each has a different cost profile.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external examination, so this stage is where paid tutoring is both cheapest and most often unnecessary. Where it earns its cost is habit installation: writing working out so method marks can be awarded, and reading command words precisely. Both are habits rather than knowledge and both are far cheaper to install here than in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families commonly buy tutoring at this stage out of a general wish to stay ahead, which rarely changes an outcome. A better use of the same money is one timed paper a term from the board the student will eventually sit, marked honestly, which gives an external reference point at a fraction of the cost of weekly sessions.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, each graded 9-1 or A*-G from terminal papers. Because grades come from papers marked against a published scheme, the subjects where technique is the problem respond quickly to tutoring, which makes the selection question unusually answerable from evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the June series as the main window and November as the resit route. Tiering in several subjects caps the grade before the paper is written, and entry deadlines sit months ahead, so the tier decision is taken while there is still a great deal of course left to learn. It should be taken on timed-paper evidence.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with university offers hanging on them. The cost profile inverts: fewer subjects, higher stakes per subject, and tutoring concentrated in one or two rather than spread across a timetable. Rates sit at the specialist end because the pool of tutors teaching to A Level standard is smaller.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE to A Level step catches students who scored well on technique and never had to think independently about a subject. That gap is specific per subject rather than general, which is why a short diagnostic block at the start of Year 12 is a better purchase than a standing weekly slot booked out of caution.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-al.subjectsIntro: Which subjects repay paid tutoring, and roughly how quickly. The judgement in each case is about where the marks are actually lost, because that determines whether an adult in a session can move them.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Repays tutoring more reliably than any other subject, because the commonest loss is method not written out, which is a habit an adult can enforce. Four to six sessions typically converts correct-but-unmarked answers into marked ones. Tier choice between Core and Extended is worth two timed papers on its own.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Repays tutoring well. Circuit reading and the alternative-to-practical paper both respond fast, because the losses are a specific skill and a specific vocabulary rather than broad understanding. Electricity produces the widest mark spread of any topic in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Repays tutoring for the quantitative parts: moles, stoichiometry, units and significant figures are drillable and worth real marks. Qualitative analysis recall is pure memorisation and is cheaper for the student to do alone than to pay someone to supervise.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Repays a short block and rarely a long one. Command-word discipline is the usual failure and three to five sessions settles it. The large content volume is learning the student must do themselves, and paying an adult to watch them do it is poor value.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Repays tutoring at Higher Level more than almost anything else, because algebraic fluency and Paper 3 investigation technique both need expert feedback. Also the most expensive to leave until the final year, since fluency is built over weeks.

subjects.name: English Language (IGCSE 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Repays a focused block on the summary task and directed writing, where marks go to selection and register rather than fluency. Repays a long weekly arrangement poorly, because improvement in composition comes from writing and reading volume the student has to supply.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Repays tutoring least reliably of the core subjects. Essay quality follows from reading the texts closely and writing often, and an hour of discussion a week does not substitute for either. A short block on essay structure before mocks is the efficient version.

subjects.name: Computer Science (IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: Repays tutoring strongly and is widely under-tutored. Pseudocode to the specification style and trace tables are narrow, learnable and worth marks that students with real programming ability routinely lose by answering in working code instead.

subjects.name: Business and Economics
subjects.description: Repays a focused block on technique: diagram accuracy, case-study application and the evaluation paragraph each have their own mark allocation and each is teachable. Content recall is not worth paying for at an hourly rate.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Repays frequency over length; confirm which stream applies before buying anything.

sections.heading: The subject-count arithmetic, in AED
paragraphs: Bestimate's published Dubai estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those bands are per subject. Multiply by the number of subjects being tutored and the real monthly figure appears, which is the number most families only discover in the third month.

Running the multiplication changes decisions. Two mid-market subjects is AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month. Four is AED 2,400 to 4,800. Across a ten-month year, four tutored subjects at mid-market rates is AED 24,000 to 48,000, which for most families is a materially different commitment from the AED 6,000 to 12,000 that one subject costs. Nobody sets out to spend the larger figure; it accumulates one anxious decision at a time.

The alternative is to decide the list on evidence and hold it. Sit timed papers in the three or four subjects causing concern, have them marked against the published schemes, and rank them by recoverable marks rather than by current grade. A subject sitting two boundaries below target with nine marks going to unwritten method has more recoverable marks than a subject one boundary below where the losses are spread evenly across content.

Then tutor the top one, or at most two in sequence, and leave the rest to the school and to the student's own revision. That is an uncomfortable recommendation because it involves declining to buy help for a subject a child is worried about, but it is the version that produces the most movement per dirham and the only one that stays affordable across two years.

sections.heading: Which subjects repay paid tutoring, and which do not
paragraphs: The useful test is whether the marks being lost are the kind an adult in a session can move. Where losses come from technique, notation, command-word reading or a specific drillable skill, an hour of expert attention is worth a great deal and the effect appears within weeks. Where losses come from not having read the texts, not having learned the content or not having practised enough, an hour a week with an adult is an expensive form of supervision.

Mathematics is the clearest case for tutoring. The single commonest loss at IGCSE is method not written out, which is a habit an adult can enforce and a student almost never changes alone. The sciences follow, for similar reasons: command-word discipline in biology, circuit reading in physics, moles and significant figures in chemistry, and the alternative-to-practical paper's specific vocabulary across all three. Computer Science is strongly under-tutored relative to how well it responds, because pseudocode in the specification's style is narrow and learnable.

English Literature is the clearest case against, and saying so is unpopular. Essay quality comes from close reading and frequent writing, and a weekly discussion does not substitute for either. A short block on essay structure before mocks is worth having; a two-year weekly arrangement generally is not. Content-heavy recall subjects fall into the same category: paying an adult at AED 200 an hour to watch a student memorise is poor use of both.

There is a middle group where a short focused block works and a long arrangement does not. English Language responds to work on the summary task and directed writing, because marks go to selection and register. Economics and Business respond to diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph. In all of these the right purchase is four to six sessions on the technique, then stopping.

sections.heading: The five subjects the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: A UAE-specific filter sits on top of the selection question and it is routinely missed. For British-track equivalency, the Ministry of Education's published requirement is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five.

That number is worth stating plainly because one page currently ranking in this market says six, and a family acting on the wrong figure may push a child through an extra subject and lose the hours it consumes. It is five, from the Ministry's own clarification, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education from the count.

The practical effect on spending is immediate. A student sitting nine IGCSEs does not need all nine to be strong for UAE equivalency purposes, and tutoring a ninth subject toward a grade no requirement mentions is money spent on a line nobody will read. University admissions elsewhere may have their own requirements, and those should be checked individually on each institution's published pages rather than assumed, but the equivalency floor is published and specific.

None of that means a weak subject is unimportant to the student, and it is not an argument for neglect. It is an argument for knowing which subjects are load-bearing before deciding where several thousand dirhams a month should go. Equivalency itself is a Ministry process: no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or accelerates it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit in Al Barsha
paragraphs: This comparison is closer in Al Barsha than almost anywhere in Dubai, and that should be said rather than glossed. Al Barsha is central, the drive is short from several directions and more independent tutors live within range than in the outer communities, so the in-home market here is genuinely competitive on both price and quality. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

The merits of a tutor in the room are real: a younger or more distractible student stays on task with less effort, written working is visible without a camera, and some families prefer it as a matter of preference rather than argument. For a Year 8 student needing supervised practice, an in-home tutor from the local Al Barsha market may well be the right purchase.

Where the comparison still favours online is depth and scheduling. Even in a well-supplied area the local pool thins sharply at the top of a subject: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, A Level Further Mathematics, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. And the second weekly session, which is what habit work needs, is hard to schedule when somebody has to drive to it twice.

IB Gram's position is fixed regardless of how the comparison falls. Lessons are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nothing on this page suggests otherwise; home visits are a service offered only in India. In Al Barsha the honest summary is that the in-home option is competitive for mainstream work and still thin at the specialist end.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to A Level step, and where the money moves
paragraphs: The cost profile inverts at sixteen. Instead of eight or nine subjects with a selection problem, a student has three or four with high stakes attached to each, and tutoring concentrates rather than spreads. Rates sit at the specialist end because fewer tutors teach credibly to A Level standard, and the consequence of a weak grade is a withdrawn university offer rather than a line on a certificate.

The gap itself is specific per subject and routinely described too vaguely. In mathematics it is that A Level questions assume IGCSE technique is automatic and spend their difficulty elsewhere. In the sciences it is the quantity of independent reading and the expectation that a student will link topics without being prompted. In the essay subjects it is that a good IGCSE answer is organised and a good A Level answer is argued, which is a different thing and has to be taught as one.

The efficient purchase is therefore a short diagnostic block early in Year 12 rather than a standing weekly slot booked out of caution in September. Eight sessions in October aimed at the one skill the rest of the course depends on is worth more than thirty sessions spread across the year covering content the school is already teaching. Many families do the second because the first requires knowing what the gap is.

One subject-selection point carries real financial weight. A Level choices made at sixteen constrain university courses two years later, and the requirements are specific rather than general: particular subjects named, sometimes a particular mathematics route. Checking each target university's published entry requirements before the choice is locked costs nothing and prevents the most expensive academic error available, which is a year of study in the wrong subject.

sections.heading: The calendar, the tier decision and the cost of getting it wrong
paragraphs: The most expensive error available in the IGCSE years is not a tutoring decision at all. It is an entry made at the wrong tier or in the wrong subject, because it costs an entry fee, a term of preparation and sometimes a resit series. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which means the decision is taken while a great deal of the course is still to be learned.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

Verifiable past dates are worth citing. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For a future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than a restated date, since provisional timetables are revised. And every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable.

The tier point deserves its own line. In tiered Cambridge subjects, Core entry caps the result at grade 5 while Extended reaches grade 9 across a harder paper. The decision is normally taken by the school in Year 10 or early Year 11 on internal evidence, and it is not reversible after the entry deadline. Two timed papers, one at each tier, marked honestly, is a very small purchase against a consequence that lasts.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and claims nobody is entitled to make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit costs nothing, no provider can present licensing as a reason for a higher rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to a parent by anybody, and a figure circulating in this market could not be verified against an official source.

Premises are a separate licence entirely. A tutoring operation with staff and a location in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, beginning with initial approval, allowing a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requiring annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved.

Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, with ADEK covering Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covering Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covering Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and combined classes strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: What should not be on any subject list
paragraphs: A page about choosing where to spend should name the purchase that belongs on no list. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and the mechanism is a risk transfer: the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money. Measured against a withdrawn result, it is the most expensive line item in this market.

The legitimate alternative is specific enough to hold any tutor to. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score to a draft and quote the descriptor behind it, help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, confirm a data collection plan is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit until the sentences are no longer the student's. A tutor should also not distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are linked and cited at source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and unreleased material is a malpractice exposure.

Nor should a grade be promised. No tutor can honour a guaranteed score or a specific improvement, and any provider leading with one is making a commercial claim rather than a professional judgement. What can be offered honestly is a measurement against a published scheme and a statement of what kind of change is available over a given period.

sections.heading: Availability, and the one question that saves the most money
paragraphs: Specialist supply is finite, and the scarcest combinations are the ones families most often want at short notice: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, A Level Further Mathematics, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is worth noticing when every enquiry receives an immediate yes.

The question that saves the most money is simple: does the person who would teach my child teach this subject at this level every week? A tutor who does not will spend the first three or four sessions reading the specification, which at mid-market rates is several hundred dirhams of no teaching and is the commonest way tutoring money disappears in Dubai. The question takes one sentence and the answer is usually audible.

Here a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives, including waiting. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred from a contact number. For an online lesson it makes no practical difference, but it should not be concealed.

The free trial is one session, free with no card required, with the specialist who would actually teach. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed; if nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly. Lessons are one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: List the subjects, then rank them by recoverable marks
process.description: Not by current grade and not by how worried the student is. Sit timed papers in the three or four causing concern, have them marked against the published schemes, and count the marks lost to a fixable cause. A subject with nine marks going to unwritten method outranks one where losses are spread evenly.

process.title: Confirm the board, codes and tiers in writing
process.description: One email to the exams officer for the board, the syllabus codes, the tiers your child is entered for and the centre's Cambridge administrative zone. All four are free and each prevents a specific expensive error, the worst being a missed paper from using the wrong zone's timetable.

process.title: Buy one subject, not four
process.description: Start with the top of the ranked list as a four to six session block with a defined end. Four subjects at mid-market rates is AED 2,400 to 4,800 a month and is almost never justified by evidence. If a second subject genuinely needs work, take it in sequence after the first has been re-tested.

process.title: Take the free trial with the subject specialist
process.description: One free session, no card required, with the person who would actually teach at that level. Ask what they made of the marked paper and whether they teach this subject at this level weekly. A generalist spending four sessions reading the specification is the commonest way money disappears here.

process.title: Re-test, then decide whether to buy more
process.description: At the close of the block a fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the first. Either the component moved or it did not. If it did, decide deliberately whether to continue or to switch to the next subject on the list. If it did not, change the plan rather than extending it.

whyPoints.title: The selection question answered first
whyPoints.description: The spend is set by how many subjects are tutored, not by the hourly rate, and most families never make that decision deliberately. Ranking subjects by recoverable marks rather than by current grade is what keeps a plan affordable across two years of IGCSE.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where tutoring does not help
whyPoints.description: English Literature and content-recall subjects rarely repay a long weekly arrangement, because the work that moves the grade is reading, writing and memorising the student has to do themselves. Saying so costs us bookings and saves families money, which is the point.

whyPoints.title: The five-subject equivalency floor
whyPoints.description: The Ministry counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. A page currently ranking in this market says six. Knowing the published figure changes which subjects are load-bearing.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it and the month it was read. Three of the strongest pages competing for this search publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars, which is a currency no UAE family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: A fair comparison, not a slanted one
whyPoints.description: In Al Barsha the in-home market is genuinely competitive for mainstream subjects, and this page says so. Online wins on specialist depth, on scheduling a second weekly session, and on cost certainty, which is a narrower claim than the usual one and a true one.

faqs.question: How many subjects should a Kings School Al Barsha student be tutored in?
faqs.answer: One at a time in almost every case, chosen on evidence rather than on which subject causes most worry. Bestimate's published Dubai bands of AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a mid-market weekly hour are per subject, so four tutored subjects is AED 2,400 to 4,800 a month and AED 24,000 to 48,000 across a year. Sit timed papers in the subjects causing concern, have them marked against the published schemes, and rank by marks lost to a fixable cause. Then tutor the top one, and take a second in sequence only if the first has been re-tested.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Those where marks are lost to technique rather than to not having learned the material. Mathematics is the strongest case, because the commonest loss is method not written out and an adult can enforce the habit a student will not change alone. Physics, Chemistry's quantitative parts and Computer Science pseudocode follow. Biology repays a short block on command words. English Literature and content-recall subjects repay a long weekly arrangement least, because the work that moves those grades is reading, writing and memorising the student has to do themselves.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring English Literature at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For a short block before mocks, often yes, aimed at essay structure and how to use quotation as evidence rather than decoration. For a two-year weekly arrangement, usually not. Essay quality follows from close reading of the set texts and from writing frequently with feedback, and an hour of discussion each week does not substitute for either. If a student has not read the texts closely, no amount of paid discussion fixes the grade. Spend the money where the losses are technique, and spend the time on the texts.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a Dubai student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market states six, which is not supported by the Ministry's own clarification. Individual universities may require more or specific subjects, so check each institution's published pages directly.

faqs.question: Should we tutor a subject my child is not going to need?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the question is worth asking explicitly because it is where several thousand dirhams a month quietly goes. For UAE equivalency, five accredited IGCSE subjects carry the requirement, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education. A ninth subject tutored toward a grade no requirement mentions is money spent on a line nobody reads. That is not an argument for neglect, and a student may have good reasons of their own to care about the subject. It is an argument for knowing which subjects are load-bearing before committing a budget.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring competitive in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: More so than in most of Dubai, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. Al Barsha is central, the drive is short from several directions and more independent tutors live within range than in the outer communities, so the local in-home market at AED 180 to 500 is genuinely competitive for mainstream subjects. Where it still thins sharply is at the top of a subject: Higher Level Paper 3 work, A Level Further Mathematics, specification-style pseudocode. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; lessons are one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What does the Core and Extended tier decision cost if it goes wrong?
faqs.answer: A capped grade or a paper the student cannot score on, and it is not reversible after the entry deadline. Core entry in tiered Cambridge subjects caps the result at grade 5; Extended reaches grade 9 but covers supplement content and asks longer, less scaffolded questions. Schools decide in Year 10 or early Year 11 on internal evidence, and entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Two timed papers, one at each tier, marked honestly against the published schemes, is a very small purchase against a consequence that follows the student into sixth form.

faqs.question: When should we start thinking about A Level support?
faqs.answer: Early in Year 12, as a short diagnostic block rather than a standing weekly slot booked in September out of caution. The gap is specific per subject: mathematics assumes IGCSE technique is automatic and spends its difficulty elsewhere, the sciences expect independent reading and topic linking without prompting, and the essay subjects want an argued answer rather than an organised one. Eight sessions in October aimed at the one skill the rest of the course rests on is worth more than thirty spread thinly across the year covering content the school is already teaching.

faqs.question: Will a cheaper tutor do for a mainstream IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is what the marked script shows. If a student needs supervised practice and content recap, budget provision at AED 45 to 150 an hour may be entirely adequate and good value. If the diagnosis is that extended-response method marks are going uncollected, or that alternative-to-practical answers describe the wrong thing, the budget tier generally cannot see that in a script and the hours will not move it. Sit one timed paper, have it marked against the published scheme, and let the diagnosis decide which band of provision the problem needs.

faqs.question: Would putting two of my child's IGCSE subjects with one tutor reduce the bill?
faqs.answer: Within a subject group it is sometimes genuine: a specialist who teaches both Physics and Chemistry at IGCSE exists. Across groups it usually means a generalist, and a generalist spending the first sessions reading two specifications is the most expensive thing a family can buy at a reasonable hourly rate. The saving is also smaller than it looks, since two subjects is two hours whoever teaches them. If the budget is the constraint, sequencing the subjects one after another is a better lever than combining them under one tutor.

faqs.question: How quickly should we see something change after starting?
faqs.answer: For technique and command-word work, within three or four sessions, because answer-shape habits respond fast and the change is countable on a script. For algebraic fluency, six to twelve sessions, since automaticity is built by repetition over weeks rather than taught in a lesson. For a genuine content gap, longer, and the first visible change should appear in the specific topic rather than in the overall mark. A plan that offers no intermediate measurement for a whole term is not a plan you can evaluate.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Al Barsha or Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The local in-home market does exist and is competitive in this area at AED 180 to 500 an hour by published figures, and for a younger student needing supervision there is a real case for it. What online delivery adds is specialist depth, a second weekly session that lands at a usable time, and no session billed and lost to traffic.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor before paying for the first block?
faqs.answer: Four things. Do you teach this subject at this level every week? What did you take from the marked script we sent? Is marking included in the hourly rate? And who teaches each session by name. The first question prevents the commonest waste in Dubai, which is paying a generalist to read the specification for three or four sessions. The last prevents a named match quietly becoming a rota, which destroys continuity. Vague answers to any of the four are themselves the answer.

faqs.question: Does a free trial lesson have conditions attached?
faqs.answer: One: it is a single session, so both sides can judge fit. It is free, no card is required, and it is taken with the specialist who would actually teach the subject rather than with a different member of staff. The purpose is narrow and worth stating, because the alternative is a family discovering a mismatch three months and several thousand dirhams in. If the fit is wrong afterwards, say so and a different specialist is proposed; if no suitable specialist exists for the component, that is said plainly.

intro.heading: Budget by the month, because that is how the money leaves
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutoring is advertised and monthly totals are how it is paid for. The gap between those two framings is where most Dubai tutoring budgets go wrong. An hourly figure of AED 250 sounds like a considered decision; the same arrangement across two subjects for nine months of the academic year is close to AED 18,000, which is a different kind of decision and one most families would have taken differently had anyone put it that way at the start.

The monthly view also makes visible the things an hourly view hides. A month contains four sessions, sometimes five, occasionally three when a holiday lands badly. A month may or may not include the marking of work between sessions. A month may be billed in advance with no rollover, or it may be billed for sessions used. Two providers quoting the same hourly rate can produce monthly invoices that differ by a third, and the difference is in the terms rather than in the teaching.

The published monthly figures in this market are worth knowing before any conversation starts, and they come from providers and surveys rather than from us. Packages circulating in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to over 2,000 for specialist exam-year support.

Against that sits a useful piece of Dubai-specific context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are therefore a known monthly figure for the year ahead. Tutoring is the variable, and it is the one worth modelling properly because it is the one you control.

So this page is built around the monthly number. What each monthly band contains. What falls inside a package and what is billed on top. How the arithmetic changes with two children in the house. Which months of a Dubai academic year are worth buying and which are better skipped. And what no monthly invoice should ever cover. Tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

A word on what this page deliberately does not do. It does not publish an IB Gram price list, because the sensible first step is a free trial lesson and a conversation about what the diagnosis actually requires, and a headline figure quoted before that is a guess dressed as a quote. Every AED number below belongs to the provider or survey named beside it, and is given so that whatever you are quoted can be placed against the market rather than accepted on its own.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, nine or ten subjects, and the point at which monthly costs peak if nobody plans. The sensible shape is uneven: a heavier autumn in Year 10 to install habits, light middle months with a monthly paper instead of weekly sessions, and a concentrated final quarter in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit June and November, so the expensive months for a Dubai family are February to April ahead of the June series. Specialist availability tightens in that window and rates at the upper end firm up, which means the same teaching costs more in March than it did in September.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Monthly costs are lumpier than at IGCSE, because internal assessment deadlines cluster. A family may need two intensive months around an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay window and nothing at all for the two after it. Buying a flat monthly arrangement across two years overpays considerably.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private-school sector keeps adding IB places, with three of the seven schools joining the 2026-27 intake offering the International Baccalaureate among 16,846 new places. For a family moving from IGCSE, the budgeting shift is from weekly rhythm to deadline-driven blocks.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Fewer subjects and higher rates per subject, because the specialist pool is thinner. The published AED 200-450 specialist band applies, and premium named tutors advertise up to AED 650. Monthly totals for one subject at the specialist end sit comfortably above AED 1,000 in an examination year.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai family with a Year 13 candidate and a Year 11 candidate in the same house faces its heaviest combined months in the spring, since both series fall close together. Sequencing those two children's blocks rather than running both at once is the single largest saving available.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-na.subjectsIntro: Monthly cost varies by subject, mostly because the specialist pool differs. Each entry names the specification code and notes what tends to drive the monthly figure up or down.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The best-supplied subject, which keeps monthly rates near the middle of the published band. Short targeted blocks work well here, so a two-month arrangement aimed at written method is often all that is needed.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Similarly well supplied. The monthly figure only differs if the brief includes reconciling a mid-course board change, which adds three or four sessions once rather than raising the ongoing rate.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Extended-tier physics sits at the upper end of the specialist band because the pool is thinner than for mathematics. A practical-paper block serves all three sciences at once, which lowers the effective monthly cost substantially.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: A narrow and defined brief - moles and organic - keeps the monthly commitment short. An open-ended chemistry arrangement with no stated end point is the commonest way a monthly figure quietly becomes permanent.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: The cheapest science to support, because much of the content gap is closable with a revision guide and a schedule. What justifies paid months is terminology marking, which is a few weeks of work rather than a term.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Priced in the middle band and unusually efficient per month, because three or four marked and rewritten pieces often move a grade. Buying nine months of English discussion is a far worse use of the same money.

subjects.name: Literature in English (Cambridge 0475 and 0992)
subjects.description: Monthly cost depends on the school's text list, because an unusual set text narrows the specialist pool. Worth confirming the list before a monthly arrangement is agreed, since it affects both match time and rate.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Mid-band, and efficient when aimed at evaluation writing specifically rather than at content coverage. Pupils who know the definitions and lose the evaluation marks need weeks, not terms.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: A thinner specialist pool, particularly for Cambridge pseudocode conventions, which lengthens match time and pushes the monthly figure towards the upper band. Worth asking about availability before budgeting.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Sits alongside the Arabic provision Dubai private schools must deliver under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements whatever the licensed curriculum. Progress is measurable monthly, which suits a short defined arrangement.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-na.regionsTitle: Where the household budgets on this page are set
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-na.regionsIntro: Communities around the Nad Al Sheba corridor differ in what an in-home arrangement would cost in practice, because the travel premium inside the published AED 180-500 band is a function of the journey. These notes cover that.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba 1 to 4
regions.note: Closest to the corridor, so the travel component of an in-home monthly package is at its smallest here. Even so, a provider prices a round trip, and the monthly in-home figure of AED 1,599-1,799 reflects that rather than extra teaching.

regions.name: Meydan and Meydan Avenue
regions.note: Apartment and townhouse stock with a short run to the corridor and a slow one towards Downtown. Monthly packages here are often bought for two children at once, which is where the per-child arithmetic matters most.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City and District One
regions.note: Large villa plots where the premium named-tutor band of AED 500-650 an hour finds a market. At that rate a single subject in an examination year passes AED 2,000 a month, which is worth stating before it is committed to.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba Gardens and Al Barari
regions.note: Quiet residential communities with long internal distances, so even a nearby tutor spends time inside the community itself. The monthly in-home premium here buys that time rather than any additional teaching.

regions.name: Al Quoz 3 and Al Khail Heights
regions.note: Short distances with awkward peak traffic, which pushes an in-home session to a 5.30pm start or later. An online slot at the same hour carries no travel component in the monthly figure at all.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Slow on the Al Khail approach at school-run time, so a travelling tutor commits ninety minutes to deliver sixty. Over a month that is six hours of somebody's time priced into four lessons.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Established districts with a cross-city run to the corridor. Families here frequently use weekend sessions, which are easier to fit into a monthly package than a weekday evening and cost the same.

schoolClusters.city: The Nad Al Sheba and Meydan corridor
schoolClusters.note: Newer British-curriculum schools with growing secondary phases, where families are often budgeting for a first IGCSE cohort with no older sibling's experience to draw on. That is precisely where an hourly quote gets mistaken for a monthly plan.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Quoz, Dubai Hills and Jumeirah belt
schoolClusters.note: Established schools within a short radius, with a wide spread of fee levels and therefore of tutoring budgets. Households here are often running two children at different stages, which changes the monthly arithmetic more than the subject does.

sections.heading: The monthly bands, and who published each figure
paragraphs: IGCSE tutoring in Dubai costs between roughly AED 240 and AED 2,000 or more per month for one subject, depending on tier, format and who is teaching. That is a wide range and it is not arbitrary: each band corresponds to a different kind of arrangement, and knowing which band you are being quoted from is more informative than any conversation about quality.

The figures that follow are market rates published by the providers and surveys named, not an IB Gram price list. Packages seen in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, working out near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is about AED 200 to 225 an hour. The Bestimate survey for Dubai gives monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions of AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to over 2,000 for specialist examination-year support.

Converting between the two framings is the useful discipline. An AED 799 package of eight sessions is cheaper per hour than a mid-band weekly arrangement, because eight sessions a month is twice the frequency; the monthly figure is higher and the hourly figure lower. An in-home package at AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits delivers eight hours, the same as the online package, at more than double the price, and the difference is travel rather than teaching.

None of these bands comes with published outcome data. No ranking provider in this market publishes a statistic with a sample size, a date and a method, which means a higher monthly figure is a claim about positioning rather than evidence of effect. The table sets out the bands with their sources so a quote can be placed against them before anything is agreed.

sections.heading: What is inside a month, and what gets billed on top
paragraphs: Two monthly invoices for the same hourly rate can differ by a third, and the difference lives in the terms. The first question is how many sessions a month contains. Four is the usual assumption, five happens in long months, and three happens when a holiday lands badly. A provider billing a flat monthly figure regardless is charging for five sessions in some months and three in others, and over a year that is not neutral.

The second question is marking. A session spent going through a paper the pupil sat the previous week implies somebody marked it, and marking takes time. In some arrangements that time is inside the monthly figure; in others it is billed separately or simply not done, in which case the session is spent marking live and the teaching hour has become a marking hour. Asking directly is a thirty-second conversation that materially changes value.

The third is what happens to unused sessions. A package bought in advance with no rollover means a month disrupted by illness, travel or a school trip is a month partly paid for and partly used. A month that rolls over, or a month billed for sessions taken, behaves differently. Neither arrangement is wrong, but a family that has not asked will discover the answer in the month it matters.

The fourth is notice. The commonest leak in a Dubai tutoring budget is a notice period on an arrangement that has stopped being useful: a month's notice on a monthly commitment means paying for a month of sessions nobody wants. Ask what notice applies, in writing, before the first invoice. The table lists the items worth settling and what a good answer sounds like.

sections.heading: Two children in the same house, one budget
paragraphs: The sibling arithmetic is where Dubai monthly budgets most often break, and it is rarely discussed because providers price per child. A household with a Year 11 candidate and a Year 9 pupil running two mid-band weekly arrangements is looking at AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month before anything intensive happens. Running both at full intensity through the same spring is the most expensive version of every plan available.

The lever is sequencing rather than sharing. The Year 11 candidate has a fixed external deadline; the Year 9 pupil does not. Front-loading the younger child's work into the autumn and the following summer, while the older child's months are concentrated into the spring, flattens the peak without reducing what either receives. It requires a plan for the household rather than a plan per child, which is the thing nobody sells.

Sharing a session is the other option and it should be understood honestly. Small-group rates in Dubai run around AED 100 to 150 per pupil, against AED 200 to 450 for one-to-one specialist work, so the saving is real. What is lost is diagnosis: a session pitched between two children's gaps addresses neither precisely, and the whole argument for specialist rates is that the hour targets one pupil's specific lost marks. It works for siblings genuinely at the same tier in the same subject and poorly otherwise.

One more point specific to a two-child household. The expensive overlap is not two IGCSE candidates; it is a Year 13 and a Year 11, because both series fall close together and A Level specialist rates sit higher. A family facing that combination in the same academic year should model the whole year in advance, because discovering it in February leaves no room to sequence anything. sections.heading: Tutoring against the school fee, month by month
paragraphs: Context changes how a monthly tutoring figure feels, and Dubai supplies an unusually clear anchor. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning the year ahead, that means the largest line in the education budget is a known quantity.

The emirate's scale is worth knowing too, because it explains the spread of tutoring prices. KHDA counted 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven more schools creating 16,846 places. That depth produces genuine competition on tutoring rates, which is why the published monthly range is so wide and why a quoted figure is more negotiable than it would be in a thin market.

Set against a monthly school fee, a mid-band tutoring arrangement is a meaningful but not dominant addition. Set against two such arrangements plus an intensive final quarter, it stops being marginal. The useful exercise is to write the monthly education total for the year ahead - fees, transport, tutoring, examination entries where a pupil sits any paper as a private candidate - and then decide what the tutoring line should be rather than letting it accumulate.

The last item on that list catches families out. Entry fees for examinations are normally handled through the school for a registered candidate, but a pupil sitting a paper as a private candidate, including a November retake arranged outside their school, may face separate charges through a centre. Ask the examinations officer rather than assuming, because it is a cost that arrives in a specific month and is not part of any tutoring quote.

sections.heading: Packages: the arithmetic, and the conditions that matter more
paragraphs: A monthly package is not automatically better or worse value than paying per session. It is a different instrument with different risks, and the arithmetic should be done before the conditions are considered. An AED 799 package for eight online sessions is close to AED 100 an hour, which is genuinely cheaper per hour than most mid-band weekly arrangements. Whether it is cheaper in practice depends on whether eight sessions a month is what the pupil needs.

That is the first trap. Eight sessions a month is twice the frequency of a weekly arrangement, and for a narrow technique repair it is more than the work requires. A pupil who needs five sessions of written-method insistence does not need sixteen sessions across two months, and a package that delivers them has sold a low hourly rate attached to a high monthly total. Frequency should follow the diagnosis rather than the pricing structure.

The second trap is rollover. A package bought in advance assumes a month runs smoothly, and Dubai school calendars include trips, long weekends, examination weeks and in some years a Ramadan reshaping of the evening. A package with no rollover converts every disruption into a loss. A package that rolls over, or a monthly arrangement billed for sessions taken, does not. This is worth more than a modest discount on the headline figure.

The third is the exit. A notice period on a monthly package means paying for a month that is no longer useful, and the useful question is not whether notice exists but what it costs. A week is reasonable. A month, on a monthly product, means the arrangement can only ever be left at full price. Settle it in writing before the first invoice, because it is the single commonest leak in a Dubai tutoring budget.

sections.heading: The in-home monthly premium, from the Nad Al Sheba side
paragraphs: An in-home monthly package in Dubai at AED 1,599 to 1,799 delivers eight hours across four two-hour visits. An online package at AED 799 delivers eight hours across eight sessions. The teaching time is the same and the price differs by more than double, so it is worth being precise about what the difference buys, because part of it is genuine and part of it is traffic.

The genuine part is the convenience of a single longer visit and the presence of an adult in the room. For a younger pupil who will not settle to work alone, that has value. The traffic part is substantial and specific: a tutor travelling into the Nad Al Sheba corridor or across to Dubai Hills at four in the afternoon spends between forty and seventy minutes each way, so a two-hour lesson is a four-hour commitment. Over a month that is eight hours of somebody's time inside four lessons.

The second cost is selection, and it does not appear on any invoice. An in-home tutor must live within a drivable radius, so the pool for Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 within twenty minutes of a given community is small and sometimes empty. When it is empty the arrangement becomes whoever is available rather than whoever is right, and the family is paying the in-home premium for a generalist. That is the worst value combination in the market.

Removing the car changes both. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Dubai households over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which means the tutor is chosen for the specification and tier rather than for a postcode. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India only. The table compares the two monthly shapes on the terms that actually differ.

sections.heading: Which months to buy, and which to skip
paragraphs: A Dubai academic year is not uniform, and a flat monthly arrangement pays the same amount for months of very different value. The autumn of Year 10 is high value and cheap, because habits install easily and specialist availability is loose. The middle terms are low value for weekly sessions and high value for a single marked paper a month. The final quarter of Year 11 is the highest-value and most expensive window in the sequence.

Two Dubai-specific factors shape that further. Specialist availability tightens from January as the June series approaches, so the same teaching costs more and is harder to book in February than in September. And in some years the spring revision window overlaps Ramadan, when school days shorten and evenings restructure around Iftar. A family that moves sessions to a post-Iftar slot keeps the most valuable quarter intact; a family that pauses loses six weeks.

The long summer is the most underused month in the whole calendar. A pupil going into Year 11 with a known content gap is far better served by four sessions in August, when the topic can still be taught properly, than by twelve in February, when there is only time to revise what is already there. August availability is loose, rates are not firmed up, and the work is more useful. Almost nobody books it.

Mock season deserves its own line because it produces a free diagnostic. The school has already administered a timed paper under proper conditions, and the script is the most valuable document in the process. One month built round reading those scripts properly, across all subjects, often prevents two months of misdirected work. The table sets out the year as a buying plan rather than as a calendar.

sections.heading: What no monthly invoice should cover
paragraphs: Some things should never appear on a tutoring invoice at any monthly figure. Written, edited or supplied coursework is the clearest. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger rather than a service, and the exposure falls on the candidate whose qualification is at stake. A tutor teaches, questions, models and marks the pupil's own work.

Files of past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents should not be supplied either. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own that material, and the correct behaviour is to link the official page. A provider offering a folder of mark schemes as part of a package has told you how it treats rules in general, which is worth knowing before a monthly commitment is made.

Nor should an invoice rest on claims nobody can substantiate. No provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so a satisfaction percentage or a claim about the proportion of pupils reaching top grades is a marketing figure rather than evidence. A promise of a specific grade is a reason to walk away. And 'KHDA-approved tutors' is the most dangerous phrase in Dubai tutoring advertising: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, and no online matching platform holds one.

What a family is entitled to check is the permit that genuinely exists. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a provider citing licensing costs in its rate has misread its own paperwork. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.
