sections.heading: Coverage, VAT and the first month
paragraphs: Mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist: Computer Science 0478 with Cambridge pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, or an unusual literature text list. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free, and that is better said than filled with a generalist at the same monthly figure.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies before any month is agreed. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named. Rates do not change because a tutor is based outside the UAE.

On tax: this page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so would require a Federal Tax Authority citation and the position turns on the provider's own registration and the nature of the service. What a family can reasonably require is a quoted monthly AED figure with a plain statement of whether VAT is included, excluded or not applicable, plus a tax registration number if the provider holds one. A provider who will not put that in writing has answered a different question.

The first month is deliberately small. A free trial lesson is one session, with no card details required, and the useful thing to bring is your child's last marked paper rather than a description of the problem. From there the honest shape is a single diagnostic month with no automatic continuation, ending in a written recommendation that states how many further months are justified, in which subject, and at what monthly figure. If that recommendation is 'none', that is a legitimate and valuable outcome.

process.title: Convert every quote into a monthly figure
process.description: Ask for the hourly rate, the number of sessions a month contains, and whether marking sits inside the rate. Then multiply. A quote that cannot be turned into a monthly number in thirty seconds is a quote designed not to be compared, and the comparison is the only protection a household budget has.

process.title: Settle the terms before the first invoice
process.description: Sessions per month, rollover of unused sessions, notice period, whether holiday months are billed, and whether the figure is fixed for the agreed months. All in writing. The commonest leak in a Dubai tutoring budget is a month's notice on a monthly product, which means leaving always costs full price.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic month, not a term
process.description: Three or four sessions with a written output: a marked timed paper, lost marks counted by type, and a recommendation stating how many further months are justified. At the mid band that is roughly AED 600 to 1,200, and it is the month that prevents the unnecessary ones from being bought at all.

process.title: Plan the household, not the child
process.description: Write down the monthly education total for the year ahead across every child: fees, transport, tutoring, examination entries. Then sequence the intensive months so that two children's peaks do not collide. A Year 13 and a Year 11 in the same spring is the most expensive shape available and the easiest to avoid with notice.

process.title: Spend unevenly across the year
process.description: Heavy in August and the autumn of Year 10, light in the middle terms with one marked paper a month, concentrated in the final quarter of Year 11. The same annual total buys considerably more distributed that way, and booking the spring months in January protects both the slot and the rate.

whyPoints.title: Priced as months, with the sources named
whyPoints.description: Every monthly band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, stated as a market range rather than as our price. Three of the highest-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai household transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Terms settled before the first invoice
whyPoints.description: Session count, marking, rollover, notice and holiday months agreed in writing at the start. Two providers at the same hourly rate can invoice a third apart on terms alone, and the terms are where a monthly budget quietly overruns.

whyPoints.title: One diagnostic month, no automatic continuation
whyPoints.description: The first commitment is a single month ending in a written recommendation that states how many further months are justified and in which subject. A recommendation of none is a legitimate outcome, and an arrangement that renews by default is a standing order rather than a repair.

whyPoints.title: The household modelled, not just the child
whyPoints.description: Two children at different stages, with two series falling close together, is where Dubai monthly budgets break. Sequencing the intensive months rather than running both at once is the largest saving available and nobody sells it, because providers price per child.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a minority subject has no specialist free, it is named rather than filled with a generalist at the same monthly figure.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted ratings, and no suggestion that KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB has approved, accredited or partnered with IB Gram. There is no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: What should a Kings School Nad Al Sheba family expect to pay a month for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: For one subject, between roughly AED 240 and AED 2,000 depending on tier and format. The Bestimate Dubai survey puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to over 2,000 for specialist examination-year support. Packages circulating in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures from published sources, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a tutoring month actually contain?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it varies and the answer changes the effective rate substantially. Four is the usual assumption, five happens in long months, and three happens when a school holiday or examination week lands badly. A provider billing a flat monthly figure regardless is charging for five sessions in some months and three in others, which over a year is not neutral. The cleaner arrangement is a stated session count billed as used, so a disrupted month costs what it delivered.

faqs.question: Is marking included in the monthly rate or billed separately?
faqs.answer: It differs by provider and it matters more than most families expect. If a session is spent going through a paper the pupil sat last week, somebody marked it, and marking takes time that has to be paid for somewhere. In some arrangements it sits inside the monthly figure; in others it is billed on top, or simply not done, in which case the lesson hour becomes a marking hour and the teaching disappears. One thirty-second question in writing settles it.

faqs.question: Does an AED 799 monthly package work out cheaper than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Eight sessions for AED 799 is close to AED 100 an hour, which undercuts most mid-band weekly arrangements. Whether it is cheaper in practice depends on whether eight sessions a month is what the pupil needs, because that is twice weekly frequency and a narrow technique repair rarely requires it. A pupil needing five sessions of written-method insistence does not need sixteen sessions across two months. Frequency should follow the diagnosis rather than the pricing structure.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions we cannot use in a given month?
faqs.answer: Ask before the first invoice, because Dubai school calendars guarantee disruption: trips, long weekends, examination weeks, and in some years a Ramadan reshaping of the evening. A package bought in advance with no rollover converts every disruption into a loss. A package that rolls over, or a monthly arrangement billed only for sessions taken, does not. Rollover is worth more to a household than a modest discount on the headline monthly figure, and it is the term providers are least likely to volunteer.

faqs.question: What notice period should we accept on a monthly arrangement?
faqs.answer: A week, or none. A month's notice on a monthly product means the arrangement can only ever be left at full price, which is the commonest leak in a Dubai tutoring budget: a family that has decided the work is not landing still pays for four more sessions nobody wants. The question is not whether notice exists but what leaving costs, and it should be settled in writing before the first invoice rather than discovered in the month you want to stop.

faqs.question: How do we budget when two children both need support?
faqs.answer: Sequence rather than share. A household running two mid-band weekly arrangements is looking at AED 1,200 to 2,400 a month before anything intensive happens. The younger child usually has no fixed external deadline, so front-loading their months into the autumn and the following summer while the older child's months concentrate into the spring flattens the peak without reducing what either receives. The expensive collision is a Year 13 and a Year 11 in the same academic year, and that needs modelling before January.

faqs.question: Is putting two siblings in one session a real saving?
faqs.answer: A real saving and a real compromise. Small-group rates in Dubai run around AED 100 to 150 per pupil against AED 200 to 450 for one-to-one specialist work, so the monthly difference is substantial. What is lost is precision: a session pitched between two children's gaps addresses neither exactly, and the whole case for specialist rates is that the hour targets one pupil's specific lost marks. It works where siblings are genuinely at the same tier in the same subject and works poorly otherwise.

faqs.question: With school fees frozen for 2026-27, should the tutoring line go up?
faqs.answer: It fixes the other side of the budget rather than this one. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. Tutoring is a separate, unregulated private market with rates set provider by provider. The practical benefit is planning: with the largest line known, the tutoring line becomes the one you can actually model and decide on rather than absorb.

faqs.question: Which months of the year are worth paying for?
faqs.answer: August before Year 11, the autumn of Year 10, and the final quarter before the June series. August is the most underused month in the calendar: a known content gap can still be taught properly then, where in February there is only time to revise what is already there. The middle terms are poor value for weekly sessions and good value for one marked paper a month. Specialist availability tightens from January, so the same teaching costs more in March than in September.

faqs.question: Does a monthly in-home package justify costing double the online one?
faqs.answer: Decide it as a travel question. An in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 delivers eight hours across four two-hour visits; an online package at around AED 799 delivers the same eight hours. A tutor travelling into the Nad Al Sheba corridor or across to Dubai Hills at four in the afternoon spends forty to seventy minutes each way, so the month contains about eight hours of travel inside four lessons. The genuine value is an adult in the room for a younger pupil. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai.

faqs.question: Will the monthly figure change closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: At the specialist end, usually yes. Demand for IGCSE support in Dubai concentrates between January and April ahead of the June series, and the people who can mark an Extended-tier script properly are booked out in that window, which firms up rates. Buying the same teaching in September costs less and is easier to schedule. If you know a final-quarter block is coming, agree the months and the figure in writing in January rather than negotiating in March when neither slots nor rates are in your favour.

faqs.question: Does the monthly price include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider to state it in writing before the first invoice. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that would require a Federal Tax Authority citation and the position depends on the provider's own registration and the nature of the service. What a household can reasonably require is a quoted monthly AED figure with a plain statement of whether VAT is included, excluded or not applicable, plus a tax registration number where one is held. A provider who avoids that question has answered a different one.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Nad Al Sheba or Mohammed Bin Rashid City addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The monthly consequence is direct: the travel priced into the published AED 1,599-1,799 in-home packages is not in the figure at all, and the tutor is chosen for the specification and tier rather than for living within a drivable radius of your community.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-na.closingHeading: Write the monthly number down before you agree anything
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-kings-school-na.closingBody: Take any quote you have been given, ask how many sessions a month contains, whether marking is inside the rate, whether unused sessions roll over and what notice ends the arrangement, then multiply it out. Compare that figure against the published Dubai bands on this page. Then decide which months of the year you actually want to buy, rather than agreeing to all of them by default. A free trial lesson is one session with no card details required, and the honest first commitment is a single diagnostic month ending in a written recommendation. intro.heading: The marks are in specific places, and the places are published
paragraphs: Nord Anglia International School Dubai runs the British curriculum through IGCSE and the International Baccalaureate Diploma in the sixth form, which means a family can hold two entirely different assessment systems in the same household and sometimes in the same child's five-year arc. Most tutoring conversations in that situation stay at the level of the subject: maths is hard, chemistry is going badly. That is not where the marks are. The marks are in components with published weightings, assessed against published criteria, and the loss points are specific enough to name.

This page names them. For every Diploma subject group, what the assessment actually rewards and how the weight is distributed. For the sciences, each paper and what it tests. For mathematics, the four distinct routes available across IGCSE and the Diploma and how they differ. For English and the languages, the components nobody rehearses and which are worth the most. And for IGCSE, the paper structure per subject with the board difference flagged, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are not interchangeable.

The point of publishing all of it is that it converts a vague worry into a decision about where hours go. A component worth forty-four per cent and a component worth twenty deserve different amounts of attention. An untimed, criteria-marked component is usually the fastest place to gain marks because the criteria are published and there is no clock. Yet the conversation at home almost always starts from the topic a student dislikes rather than from the component carrying the most marks, and the hours follow the anxiety.

IB Gram supports Nord Anglia families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and that statement appears on every country page this site publishes. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For a component-level problem the thing that matters is whether the tutor has taught that component, which is a narrower question than who will drive to Al Barsha South.

Two cautions before the detail. No IB session or results date appears anywhere here, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project; Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session and every specific date should come from the school. And the weightings quoted below were read from the current subject guides, but guides are revised, so treat them as a map of where the marks sit and confirm the governing version with your child's coordinator or exams officer. Everything else on this page is either a published weighting, a loss point that recurs across cohorts and is visible on a marked script, or a market rate read from a named source in October 2026. Where a figure could not be verified it has been left out rather than estimated into existence.

sections.heading: The six Diploma groups, and why they are not assessed alike
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes one subject from each of six groups, and families treat those six as six instances of the same thing. They are not. The groups distribute marks across fundamentally different kinds of task, which means an hour of tutoring buys a different amount of grade movement depending on where it is spent. Knowing the distribution is the single most useful planning fact available, and it is published.

In the sciences, roughly four-fifths of the grade comes from two written papers and one-fifth from an independent investigation that is untimed and criteria-marked. In mathematics the proportion is similar but the third Higher Level paper changes the shape. In language and literature a substantial slice comes from an oral component that can be rehearsed. In language acquisition the grade is split across receptive, productive and interactive skills, so a weakness in one skill can cost a quarter of a grade while the student appears broadly competent. In the individuals and societies group, extended-response writing carries almost everything, and evaluation is the band-deciding skill.

The planning consequence is straightforward once stated. The untimed, criteria-marked components are usually the fastest marks available, because the criteria tell you exactly what is wanted and there is no clock introducing a second variable. The rehearsable oral components are next, because rehearsal is a reliable technology. The timed written papers are slowest, because they combine content, technique and pacing, which have to be fixed separately.

That ranking is almost the opposite of how families allocate hours. The default is to pour time into the written paper of the subject the student finds hardest, which is the slowest-moving target in the slowest-moving category. Spending the first block on an internal assessment or an oral component in the same subject frequently produces more grade movement in less time, and it also builds the confidence that makes the paper work possible.

sections.heading: The sciences paper by paper, and what each one is testing
paragraphs: The Diploma sciences share one structure across Physics, Chemistry and Biology, and it is worth knowing in detail because it is where most Nord Anglia tutoring enquiries land. Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent and contains both multiple-choice questions and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and is extended response. The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent, is capped at 3,000 words, and is marked out of twenty-four across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each.

Each of those tests something different. The multiple-choice section rewards elimination technique, which is a teachable skill in its own right and is almost never taught; a student who can reliably discard two plausible distractors converts guesses into marks across the whole section. The data-analysis section rewards practice on unfamiliar graphs rather than recall of familiar ones, which means revising notes does nothing for it. Paper 2 rewards command-term compliance and the ability to sustain a multi-step explanation.

The investigation is the component where a tutor adds the most value per hour and where the authorship boundary is tightest. Research design covers the question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned, and it cannot be repaired once the practical work has been done, which makes a single planning session before data collection the highest-value hour available in the subject. Data analysis is usually about uncertainty and processing rather than arithmetic. A weak conclusion states a result without linking it to the science. A weak evaluation lists limitations without proposing remedies.

A tutor may explain each of those criteria in the guide's published wording, show how a comparable investigation is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it. A tutor may not write the investigation, draft the evaluation, or edit a piece to completion so the sentences become theirs. The 3,000-word cap is a limit rather than a target, and a tightly written 2,200-word investigation routinely outscores a padded one at the cap.

sections.heading: Four mathematics routes, one decision
paragraphs: Across IGCSE and the Diploma a Nord Anglia student passes through up to four distinct mathematics routes, and families often do not realise these are different courses rather than different difficulty settings. At IGCSE, Cambridge offers 0580 at Core and Extended plus 0606 Additional Mathematics and 0607 International Mathematics, while Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher tier. In the Diploma, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses, each at Higher and Standard Level.

The consequential decisions are two. The first is the IGCSE tier, taken by the school in Year 10, usually on Year 9 evidence. A Cambridge Core entry is assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C, which closes the Diploma Higher Level and A Level routes that require a B. That decision is easier to revisit in Year 10 than in Year 11, and what reopens it is evidence: Extended-only content taught, then a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme.

The second is the Diploma course. Analysis and Approaches is heavier on pure content, with calculus and proof, and is the larger step from Extended IGCSE by a wide margin. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling and statistics, and demands written interpretation in context rather than a bare answer. The weighting structure is identical: two papers at forty per cent each plus the Exploration at twenty at Standard Level; three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty plus the Exploration at twenty at Higher Level. Some university programmes expect one course specifically, so check prerequisites before the subject form is signed.

0607 International Mathematics deserves a mention because schools feeding into the IB often prefer it and it carries an investigation paper that exists on no other maths syllabus. For a student heading towards the Diploma Exploration that is useful preparation. Across every one of these routes, one behaviour carries marks: writing the method out. A correct method with an arithmetic slip keeps most of its marks; a correct answer with no working loses marks the student had already earned.

sections.heading: English and the languages: the components nobody rehearses
paragraphs: Language subjects contain the most reliably recoverable marks in the Diploma and attract the least tutoring, because the problem does not present as a crisis. A student who writes fluently looks fine on a report and may be losing a third of a component to one specific habit. The habits are identifiable and the components are rehearsable, which is an unusual combination.

In English A: Language and Literature, Standard Level runs Paper 1 at thirty-five per cent, Paper 2 at thirty-five and the Individual Oral at thirty; Higher Level adds the HL Essay at twenty and rebalances the rest. Paper 1 is guided textual analysis, and the dominant loss is identifying a technique rather than analysing its effect on a reader. That is a sentence-level change, visible immediately in a script, and among the fastest improvements available anywhere in the Diploma.

The Individual Oral is the component families most overlook. It requires a global issue traced through two texts, it is worth thirty per cent at Standard Level, and it is rehearsable in a way that no written paper is. A student who has practised it four times with feedback performs differently from one who has thought about it, and the difference is worth more than most content revision. The HL Essay is similarly tractable because it is untimed and criteria-marked.

In language acquisition the grade divides across receptive, productive and interactive skills, which means a student can appear broadly competent while one skill carrying a quarter of the grade sits well below the others. Speaking is usually that skill, because it is the least practised in a classroom and the most uncomfortable to practise alone. It is also the most improvable in a short run of focused sessions. The first thing to check, though, is placement: being in the wrong course or phase is a common and entirely fixable cause of apparent underperformance.

sections.heading: IGCSE paper structure, with the board difference made explicit
paragraphs: At a school running the British curriculum through IGCSE, the board matters subject by subject and is not always announced at home. A school may enter Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson Edexcel for mathematics, or the reverse, and a student can sit two boards across one certificate set. The code is on the entry confirmation and the exams officer can give it in a sentence. It is the first question to settle, because the structural differences change the preparation entirely.

In the sciences the divergence is largest. Cambridge carries a practical component worth twenty per cent, sat either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, with the school choosing which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam; the same skills are examined inside two written papers. A term of alternative-to-practical preparation for a candidate not sitting that component is a term gone, and the mistake is invisible until results arrive.

The tiering language differs too. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Pearson Edexcel splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher tier. These are not interchangeable in content or in difficulty profile, and a tutor who has only taught one will approximate the other. Grade reporting also varies: some Cambridge syllabuses report 9-1 and others A*-G depending on the version entered, and the two scales are not interchangeable on a university application.

On series, both boards run a November sitting alongside the main summer one, which makes a single-subject resit a matter of months rather than a year. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Work from the exams officer's copy and nothing else.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go in the four biggest subjects
paragraphs: Across cohorts the same loss points recur, because they are the places where a plausible wrong method produces a plausible wrong answer. A student sitting mathematics and three sciences typically has four to seven identifiable items carrying most of their lost marks, not a general weakness spread evenly. That is why a diagnostic paper is worth more than a revision plan: it converts an anxiety into a list with seven entries.

In mathematics, at both IGCSE and Diploma level, the recurring items are bounds and accuracy, algebraic fractions, vector geometry, the final parts of structured questions where method must be written, and at Higher Level the unpractised Paper 3. In Physics they are circuit behaviour under load, sign conventions in anything directional, moments where the pivot is not where the student assumes, and the difference between a quantity and its unit. In Chemistry they are two-step mole conversions, the exact wording of ion and gas tests, charge-balanced ionic equations and organic reaction conditions.

In Biology the largest single item is not a topic at all. It is command-term compliance: answering describe where the paper asked explain, which costs marks on answers that are entirely true. The same fault appears across every extended-response subject and it is the fastest of all the loss points to fix, usually inside two weeks, because it is a reading and writing habit rather than a knowledge gap.

Two items on that list are worth more than any individual topic and are almost never taught. The first is written method, which earns marks across every structured question in mathematics and the quantitative sciences. The second is multiple-choice elimination on the boards and papers that use it, where thirty per cent or more of a grade sits. Ranking loss points by marks at stake rather than by discomfort usually puts both near the top, and surprises families who expected the hardest topic to matter most.
bullets: Mathematics: bounds, algebraic fractions, vectors, written method, Paper 3 at HL
Physics: circuits under load, sign conventions, moments, quantity against unit
Chemistry: two-step moles, ion and gas tests, charge balance, organic conditions

sections.heading: Materials, authorship and the position of this site
paragraphs: Subject guides, specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge and Pearson. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. Reference and link so that a parent reads the authoritative document. No grade-boundary figure appears on this page for that reason, and because a boundary quoted second-hand will eventually be wrong.

On assessed work the line is authorship. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. The caps are 4,000 words on the Extended Essay, 1,600 on the Theory of Knowledge essay, 950 on the exhibition commentary, 3,000 on the sciences investigation and 800 per Economics commentary.

A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work at a fixed price. Submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the board's rules and the finding lands on the student, not the seller. A useful test for anybody offering coursework help is to ask what they would do if your child requested one written paragraph. A refusal with a description of the alternative is the right answer; treating it as negotiable tells you what happens the week before a deadline.

And position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, has no arrangement with any school named on this page, publishes no star rating and quotes no statistic without its source and date.

sections.heading: Putting it to work: choosing the component to attack first
paragraphs: With the weightings in front of you the planning takes ten minutes. List the components of the subject in question with their percentages. Mark which are timed and which are not. Mark which are rehearsable. Then ask where the student's marks are currently going, which requires a marked script rather than an impression, and pick the intersection of high weighting and fast movement.

In a science that intersection is usually the investigation, because it is twenty per cent, untimed, criteria-marked, and a single planning session before data collection can change the research design mark that cannot be repaired later. In language and literature it is usually the oral component, worth thirty per cent at Standard Level and rehearsable. In mathematics it is written method, which is worth marks across every paper and costs one habit change. In business management it is the pre-released case, which can be worked months ahead.

What it is almost never is the hardest topic in the hardest paper, which is where families instinctively start. That target is slow-moving, combines three variables, and frequently absorbs a whole term for a modest return. Attacking it second, after a faster component has produced visible movement, works better for an additional reason that has nothing to do with marks: the student now believes the arrangement does something, and belief changes how they spend the hours between sessions.

Then measure. Ask for a marked piece from two different weeks, with the loss points counted and compared. If a count has fallen, something happened. If nothing has moved after three weeks on a fast-moving target like command-term compliance or written method, the remedy is not being enforced on marked work, and that is a specific conversation rather than a vague dissatisfaction.

process.title: Get the component list with its weightings
process.description: For a Diploma subject, from the coordinator or the subject guide. For IGCSE, the syllabus code from the exams officer, which determines the papers and whether a practical exam exists. Ten minutes of asking replaces two sessions of discovery and prevents the most expensive mismatch available.

process.title: Ask for a marked script, not a predicted grade
process.description: A prediction compresses every cause into one letter. A script shows where the marks went. The most recent mock or internal assessment with its mark breakdown is enough to identify which component is carrying the losses, which is what the plan should target.

process.title: Pick high weighting crossed with fast movement
process.description: Usually the untimed criteria-marked component or a rehearsable oral, not the hardest topic in the hardest paper. The hardest topic is slow-moving and combines content, technique and pacing, which have to be fixed separately and rarely are inside one term.

process.title: Test the tutor on the component, not the subject
process.description: Ask what Paper 1 contains besides multiple choice, or which investigation criterion cannot be repaired after data collection, or what the Individual Oral requires. A specialist answers in a sentence. An answer about teaching philosophy is itself the information you needed.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep
process.description: The real weekday and hour, not a convenient demonstration time, because a Dubai afternoon commute is the actual constraint on whether an arrangement survives a term. Listen for whether the tutor asks which board or which level before teaching anything.

process.title: Compare counts monthly, not percentages termly
process.description: Two marked pieces from different weeks with the loss points counted and compared. Command-term compliance and written method should move inside a fortnight. If a fast-moving target has not moved in three weeks, the remedy is not being enforced on marked work.

whyPoints.title: Weightings published, not described
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, the investigation at twenty. Those numbers decide where hours should go, and most families have never been shown them. A component worth double another deserves double the attention, which sounds obvious and almost never happens.

whyPoints.title: Loss points named, subject by subject
whyPoints.description: Two-step mole conversions, circuit behaviour under load, bounds and algebraic fractions, command-term compliance. Marked scripts usually show four to seven items carrying most of the losses, and the same ones recur across cohorts because of how the questions are built.

whyPoints.title: The fastest component identified first
whyPoints.description: Untimed criteria-marked work and rehearsable orals move faster than timed papers, because they involve one variable rather than three. Starting there produces visible movement, which also changes how a student spends the hours between sessions.

whyPoints.title: Four mathematics routes separated
whyPoints.description: Core, Extended, International Mathematics, then Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at two levels. These are different courses, not difficulty settings, and the IGCSE tier decision can close a Diploma route two years before the student reaches it.

whyPoints.title: The board difference flagged before it costs a term
whyPoints.description: Cambridge sciences carry a practical component worth twenty per cent; Pearson Edexcel sciences have no separate practical exam. A term spent preparing a component your child is not sitting is invisible until results, and the syllabus code prevents it in one question.

whyPoints.title: Only sourced numbers, and the absences stated
whyPoints.description: No IB examination date, because none could be verified from the organisation's own site. No grade boundary figure, because boundaries move and belong to the boards. No accreditation claim, no school arrangement, no UAE premises, no star rating.

faqs.question: What does Paper 1 contain in the IB sciences at Nord Anglia Dubai?
faqs.answer: Both multiple-choice questions and a data-analysis section, together worth thirty-six per cent of the subject grade, with Paper 2 at forty-four per cent and the investigation at twenty. The two sections of Paper 1 test different things: the multiple-choice part rewards breadth of recall plus elimination technique, and the data-analysis part rewards practice on unfamiliar graphs rather than revision of familiar ones. Confirm the current structure with your child's coordinator, since subject guides are periodically revised.

faqs.question: Which IB component gives the fastest grade movement?
faqs.answer: Usually the untimed, criteria-marked one, because the criteria state exactly what is wanted and there is no clock adding a second variable. In the sciences that is the investigation at twenty per cent; in language and literature it is the Individual Oral at thirty per cent at Standard Level, which is rehearsable in a way no written paper is. Families instinctively start with the hardest topic in the hardest paper, which is the slowest-moving target available.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For a component-level problem the relevant question is whether the tutor has taught that component, which is narrower than who will drive to the school's catchment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths Analysis and Applications?
faqs.answer: They are separate courses sharing an identical weighting structure. Analysis and Approaches is heavier on pure content, with calculus and examinable proof, and is the larger step from Extended IGCSE by a wide margin. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling and statistics and requires written interpretation in context rather than a bare answer. Some university programmes expect one specifically, so check the prerequisites for the courses under consideration before the subject form is signed.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 at Higher Level mathematics cause trouble?
faqs.answer: Because it is an extended-response problem paper worth twenty per cent, it does not resemble Papers 1 and 2, and schools generally reach it last in the teaching sequence. The result is that it is the least practised component in the Diploma while carrying a fifth of the grade. A Higher Level student who has never sat it under timed conditions is carrying avoidable risk, and it should be drilled separately and early rather than in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my child's subjects are entered on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code on the entry confirmation. Cambridge codes are four digits such as 0580 or 0625; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. Schools choose board by board, so Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics in the same certificate set is normal. The code determines the papers, the tiering language and whether a separate practical exam exists, which makes it the first question before any tutoring is arranged.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the board. Cambridge science syllabuses carry a practical component worth twenty per cent of the grade, taken either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam; practical understanding is examined inside the written papers instead. Those are genuinely different preparations, so confirm the component before arranging any tutoring around it.

faqs.question: Which investigation criterion is the most urgent to get right?
faqs.answer: Research design, because it is the only one of the four that cannot be repaired once the data has been collected. It covers the research question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned. That makes a single planning session before any practical work the highest-value hour available in the subject. The other three criteria — data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — carry eighteen of the twenty-four marks and can still be improved at drafting stage.

faqs.question: Why is the Individual Oral worth tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because it carries thirty per cent of English A: Language and Literature at Standard Level, it requires a global issue traced through two texts, and it is rehearsable in a way that written papers are not. A student who has practised it four times with feedback against the published criteria performs differently from one who has only thought about it. Rehearsal is a reliable technology, which makes this one of the most dependable returns on tutoring hours in the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: My child writes fluently but loses marks on Paper 1. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because they are identifying techniques rather than analysing their effect on a reader. Naming a metaphor is not analysis; saying what it does to the reader's understanding is. That is a sentence-level change, visible immediately in a script, and among the fastest improvements available anywhere in the Diploma. Paper 1 carries thirty-five per cent at both levels, so the return on fixing one habit is disproportionate to the effort involved.

faqs.question: What should I check first in a language acquisition subject?
faqs.answer: Placement, before anything else. The grade divides across receptive, productive and interactive skills, so a student can look broadly competent while one skill carrying a quarter of the grade sits well below the others. Being in the wrong course or phase is a common and entirely fixable cause of apparent underperformance. After placement, speaking is usually the weakest and the most improvable, because it is least practised in class and most uncomfortable to practise alone.

faqs.question: Which loss points are worth more than any single topic?
faqs.answer: Two. Written method, which earns marks across every structured question in mathematics and the quantitative sciences, so an unwritten method loses marks the student had already earned. And multiple-choice elimination on the boards and papers that use it, where thirty per cent or more of a grade can sit. Ranking loss points by marks at stake rather than by how uncomfortable they feel usually puts both near the top, which surprises most families.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover a Diploma science and a Diploma language?
faqs.answer: Rarely well. The component structures differ completely: one is two timed papers plus an independent investigation, the other is written papers plus a rehearsable oral assessed on different criteria. A tutor strong in one is approximating in the other, and the session that suffers is whichever they are less current in. Two specialists on two evenings generally costs the same and works better, with one asked to keep sight of the overall deadline calendar.

faqs.question: How soon should a component-targeted plan show something?
faqs.answer: It depends on the target. Command-term compliance and written method are behaviours and should move on the next marked script, inside one to two weeks. Rehearsable oral components improve visibly across three or four rehearsals. An investigation criterion moves between drafts, so a second draft in a higher band is the evidence. Timed paper performance is slowest at four to six weeks, because pacing and stamina develop only through full papers under timing.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-nord-anglia-int.closingHeading: List the components, then pick the one worth attacking
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-nord-anglia-int.closingBody: For a Nord Anglia family the planning is short once the numbers are visible. Get the component list with its weightings from the coordinator, or the syllabus code from the exams officer. Ask for the last marked script rather than the last prediction. Pick the component where high weighting meets fast movement, which is usually untimed criteria-marked work or a rehearsable oral rather than the hardest topic in the hardest paper. Then test the tutor on that component specifically. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to a Dubai address.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-north-london-co.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects, one-to-one over live video. Every arrangement starts from your child's own marked work and reports progress against it rather than against a feeling.

intro.heading: How you will know, and how you will know to stop
paragraphs: Tutoring is unusually hard to evaluate. The sessions happen, the child seems calmer, the tutor is encouraging, and three months later the grade is where it was. By then AED 3,000 has gone and nobody can say what it bought, because nothing measurable was ever produced. This is the normal outcome rather than the exceptional one, and it is a failure of instrumentation rather than of effort. Nobody set up anything that could have shown movement or its absence.

The alternative is not complicated, and it does not require a parent to understand the subject. It requires artefacts: a timed script marked against the real mark scheme at the start, a count of lost marks by type, a named target, and a repeat of the same instrument at four, eight and twelve weeks. Those documents either show marks moving on the questions that were being worked on, or they do not. A conversation about confidence cannot be checked. A mark count can.

This matters more at a selective school than at a less demanding one, because the margins are smaller. A pupil at a 6 who needs a 7 is chasing perhaps eight to twelve marks across two papers. That is a precise, countable target, and it is entirely possible to establish within a fortnight whether the work is finding those marks. It is also possible to establish that it is not, which is the information families are least often given and most need.

There is a second reason to insist on evidence in this market specifically. Nobody ranking for these queries publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method. Competitor pages carry satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and claims about the proportion of students reaching top grades, none of it accompanied by anything checkable. One page shows a rating of 5.0 from twenty reviews sitting beside a student figure orders of magnitude larger, and the two cannot both be meaningful. If a provider's own numbers cannot be interrogated, your own child's marked scripts are the only reliable instrument available, and conveniently they are also free.

So this page is about measurement. What a report grade can and cannot tell you. The full list of evidence that exists and who holds each piece. How to read a marked script in twenty minutes without knowing the subject. What should exist after four, eight and twelve weeks. What a mock grade actually predicts. And the signals that mean the arrangement should end. Tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

One caution before any of that. Measurement is a tool for deciding where to spend and when to stop, not a stick. A pupil who knows every session is being scored can become more anxious rather than more accurate, and anxiety costs marks of its own. The instrument belongs to the adults: the baseline is sat once, the repeats are framed as practice papers, and the mark counts are a conversation between the parent and the tutor rather than a weekly verdict delivered to a fifteen-year-old.
bullets: A report grade gives a position; a marked script shows which marks are available
The baseline instrument must be repeatable, which means a timed past paper
Lost marks sort into content, method, arithmetic or selection, precision and timing
A target of eight to twelve marks across two papers is countable and checkable
No ranking competitor publishes outcome data with a sample size, date and method
A stop rule agreed in advance is the thing that protects the budget

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-north-london-co.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different at each stage, because the instruments available differ. Below is what can actually be measured at each point and what it is worth.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: No external examination, so the available evidence is internal assessment and the pupil's own written work. That makes progress harder to measure and cheaper to achieve, because a habit installed here costs a fraction of what the same habit costs in Year 11. The measurable artefact at this stage is usually a piece of written work before and after, side by side.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set and stream from Year 7 or 8 in many cases, and the set a pupil occupies at the end of Year 9 often decides the IGCSE tier they are entered for. A set change is therefore a measurable event with a two-year consequence, and it is worth asking what evidence drove it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: The best-instrumented stage in school, because past papers and published mark schemes exist in quantity. A pupil can sit the same kind of paper repeatedly under the same conditions and the marks are directly comparable. Nothing else in a child's education offers that, and most families never use it.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit June and November. For measurement purposes the school's mock season is the most valuable fixed point in the year, because it produces a marked script under conditions nobody had to arrange. Asking for the script rather than the grade is the single highest-return request available to a Dubai parent.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mixed internal and terminal assessment, which means the evidence includes draft feedback against published criteria as well as timed papers. Internal assessment criteria are lettered and carry stated mark allocations, so a draft can be scored against them explicitly rather than discussed in general terms.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private-school sector continues to add IB places, with three of the seven new schools joining the 2026-27 intake offering the International Baccalaureate among 16,846 new places. For a pupil bridging from IGCSE, the measurable unit shifts from a paper mark to a criterion letter.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Largely terminal, so timed past papers remain the primary instrument and comparison across attempts stays clean. The complication is that content accumulates fast, so an early paper covers a small part of the course and a later one covers much more. Compare like with like or the measurement misleads.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms publish subject entry grades, which turn an abstract worry into a numeric target. A pupil told they need a 7 for A Level Chemistry has been handed the most useful piece of measurement infrastructure in the system, and it should be used rather than merely worried about.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-north-london-co.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the evidence that actually measures progress in it, because the right instrument differs. A maths grade and an English grade do not move in the same observable way.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The cleanest subject to measure. Timed past papers, marked against the published scheme, with lost marks sorted into content, method, arithmetic, precision and timing. Movement shows within four weeks if the work is aimed at the right column.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Same instrument, different papers and calculator rules. The measurement only works if the practice papers match the code on the entry, so confirm that with the examinations officer before any baseline is taken.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Measure the theory paper and the practical component separately, because they fail independently. A pupil can be improving on explanation questions while flat on method writing, and a single grade conceals both facts completely.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Moles give a binary test that takes two minutes: three Extended-tier calculations, and whether the pupil writes a balanced equation first. That is a cleaner instrument than any report comment about chemistry being difficult.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Measured by terminology precision rather than by content recall. Count how many marks were lost to imprecise language against command-term mismatches, because the two need different work and neither needs more revision guides.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Measured against assessment objectives, not overall impression. A marked reading answer shows whether the loss is selection or analysis; a marked writing task shows whether it is form or accuracy. Those are four different repairs.

subjects.name: Literature in English (Cambridge 0475 and 0992)
subjects.description: Timed essays on the school's own set texts, scored against the real criteria. Improvement appears as argument structure and quotation economy before it appears as a grade, so measure those directly.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge IGCSE 0470)
subjects.description: Source questions are scored on select, attribute, infer and evaluate, which makes them unusually diagnosable. A pupil improving in English reading analysis usually shows movement here within weeks, and that can be measured.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Separate the data-response marks from the evaluation marks when measuring. Pupils strong on content often lose the whole evaluation allocation, and an overall grade hides which half of the paper is actually failing.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Runs alongside the Arabic provision Dubai private schools must deliver under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements whatever the licensed curriculum. Script accuracy and reading fluency are both directly measurable week to week.

regions.note: Newer villa developments where the household routine is still forming, so a fixed weekly slot holds better than a flexible one. A fixed slot is also what makes four-weekly measurement comparable.

regions.note: A slow approach on the Al Khail Road at school-run time, which pushes most families to a 5.30pm or later start. Full timed papers are better placed at a weekend here than on a weekday evening.

regions.name: Al Barari and Nad Al Sheba Gardens
regions.note: Quiet villa communities with space for a pupil to sit a paper undisturbed, which matters more for measurement than it sounds. A timed script produced in a noisy room is not comparable with one produced in a quiet one.

regions.name: The Villa and Dubailand
regions.note: Longer journeys on routes that behave badly at the wrong hour, so an in-home arrangement becomes a ninety-minute commitment for a sixty-minute lesson. Removing the car removes both the premium and the cancellation risk.

regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial, with short runs to the corridor but awkward peak traffic. Pupils are generally home by five, and early-evening sessions work well for marking and rewriting rather than for fresh timed work.

regions.note: A cross-city commute, so pupils arrive home late and tired. Measurement sessions here are better taken at a weekend, because a timed paper sat at seven in the evening understates what the pupil can do.

sections.heading: What a report grade cannot tell you, and what a script can
paragraphs: A school report compresses a term into a letter and a sentence, and the compression destroys exactly the information a parent needs. 'Working at grade 6, needs to show more detail in extended answers' is a true statement that is consistent with at least four different underlying situations, each of which costs a different amount to repair. The report is not at fault; it was never designed to be a diagnostic instrument.

The script is. A marked paper shows which questions were attempted, which were abandoned, whether the working was written, whether the method was right and the arithmetic wrong, whether the command term was read, and whether the back page was reached. Those are facts rather than judgements, and a parent can read most of them without knowing the subject at all. The annotations cluster, and where they cluster is the diagnosis.

This is why the most valuable request a Dubai parent can make is for the marked script rather than the grade. Most schools will release it. Ask for the mock paper, the marked internal assessment, the annotated essay. Then look at where the marks went, not at how many. A pupil who lost fourteen marks to unshown method and three to content is in a far better position than a pupil with the same grade who lost seventeen to content.

The table below lists the report comments Dubai parents most often receive and what each one might actually mean, with the specific thing to look for in a script to resolve it. It is worth going through this exercise once before buying anything, because the most expensive tutoring purchase available is a term of teaching bought to fix a habit.

sections.heading: The evidence ledger: what exists and who holds it
paragraphs: More evidence exists than families realise, and almost all of it is already held by somebody. The school holds marked mocks, internal assessment records, set allocations and the reasons for them, the specification codes on the exam entries, and in many cases the department's own published entry thresholds. None of that is confidential and most of it is available on request.

The boards hold past papers and mark schemes, published on their own sites for anyone to download. This is the resource that makes IGCSE the best-instrumented stage of school, and it is free. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own this material, so the correct behaviour is to use it from the official site rather than to accept files from a tutor, and a provider offering to supply mark schemes as downloads has told you something about how they treat rules.

The tutor should hold a growing file of the pupil's own marked work with dates, plus the count of lost marks by type at each measurement point. That file belongs to the family rather than to the provider, and it should be shareable at any moment. An arrangement where the evidence lives only in the tutor's memory is an arrangement that cannot be evaluated, and that is usually not an accident.

What nobody holds is reliable outcome data about tutoring providers in this market. No ranking page publishes a statistic with a sample size, a date and a method. Satisfaction percentages, star ratings and claims about the proportion of students reaching top grades appear without anything checkable behind them, and one page shows a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim about far larger numbers. Treat all of it as marketing and rely on your own child's scripts instead.

sections.heading: Reading a marked script in twenty minutes without knowing the subject
paragraphs: A parent does not need to understand Extended-tier chemistry to read a chemistry script usefully. The procedure is mechanical and takes about twenty minutes. Start at the back. If the final questions are blank while comparable earlier questions were answered, the pupil ran out of time, and that is a timing problem regardless of what the subject is. If the final questions were attempted and wrong, it is not a timing problem.

Next, look for questions where marks were awarded partway through. In mathematics and the sciences this shows as method marks earned with the accuracy mark missing, which means the approach was right and a number went wrong. In essay subjects it shows as a tick for a point made with no credit for development, which means the pupil stopped where the mark scheme wanted more. Both are narrow, cheap repairs.

Then count. Put every lost mark into one of five buckets: content not known, method not shown, arithmetic or selection error, precision or terminology, and time not reached. You do not need to judge which bucket perfectly; an approximate count is sufficient to see the shape. One bucket is almost always much larger than the others, and that bucket is what the money should be aimed at.

Finally, look at the annotations rather than the marks. Teachers write where the problem is, repeatedly, in the margin. 'Explain' circled three times is a command-term problem. 'Units?' written twice is a precision problem. 'Evidence?' in an essay is a selection problem. The marker has already done the diagnosis; it is simply written in a form nobody collects. Twenty minutes with a highlighter converts it into a plan.

sections.heading: What should exist after four weeks, eight weeks and twelve
paragraphs: Progress has a shape and it is worth agreeing in advance what that shape looks like, because without it every outcome can be narrated as success. At four weeks the pupil should have produced at least three pieces of timed work, each marked, and the second repeat of the baseline instrument should be scheduled. The habit being targeted - written method, the analysis sentence, the units check - should be visible in the pupil's work even if the mark has not moved yet.

At eight weeks the mark should have moved on the specific questions that were being worked on. Not the overall grade, which is a noisy measure over eight weeks, but the marks on the question types in the targeted column. If method marks were the target, the method marks should be there. If they are not, the work has been aimed at the wrong thing or the pupil is not doing the between-session work, and both of those are findable rather than mysterious.

At twelve weeks there should be a decision rather than a renewal. Either the target has been met, in which case the arrangement should end or move to a new target, or it has not, in which case the honest conversation is about why. A provider who proposes continuing at twelve weeks without producing a comparison against the baseline is asking for a subscription rather than reporting on a repair.

The table below sets this out as a schedule. It is deliberately unforgiving, because the alternative is the default: pleasant sessions, a vaguely positive report, and a grade in June that nobody predicted. Agreeing this schedule at the start costs one conversation and it is the single most protective thing a family can do with a tutoring budget.

sections.heading: Mock grades and what they actually predict
paragraphs: Mock results are the most over-interpreted number in a British-curriculum school year, in both directions. A disappointing mock is routinely treated as a forecast and a strong one as a guarantee, and neither is justified. A mock is a single performance on a particular paper, under conditions that differ from the real series, at a point when the course is not finished. What it reliably indicates is where marks are currently being lost, which is far more useful than what it predicts.

There are specific reasons a mock understates. The syllabus is often incomplete, so questions on untaught topics are unanswerable rather than wrong. Mocks are frequently sat in a normal classroom rather than in examination conditions. And schools sometimes mark mocks harshly on purpose, to create urgency. Each of those depresses the number without telling you anything about June.

There are also reasons it overstates. A mock covering only the first two thirds of the specification is an easier paper than the real one. A pupil who has revised intensively for a known date may not sustain that across a full series of eight or nine subjects. And a generous boundary applied internally is not the boundary the board will apply.

The useful move is therefore to stop reading the mock grade and start reading the mock script. Which questions were lost, in which category, and were they topics that had been taught? That question separates the signal from the noise entirely. And it is free: the school has already run the diagnostic and produced the document, and most families read the headline and file the rest.

sections.heading: Signals that tutoring is not working, and when to stop
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a stop rule, which is understandable and not in a family's interest. A stop rule is simply a condition agreed in advance under which the arrangement ends, and having one converts tutoring from an open commitment into a bounded project. It also removes the awkwardness of the conversation, because the condition was set when everyone was optimistic rather than when someone is disappointed.

The clearest signal is the repeated instrument not moving. If the same paper under the same conditions at eight weeks shows the same marks lost in the same category, the work is not landing. That might be the wrong diagnosis, the wrong tutor, or the pupil not doing the between-session work, and all three are addressable, but none of them is addressed by buying another term and hoping.

There are softer signals worth noticing. No artefact exists: the sessions happen and nothing written is produced or marked. The reporting is adjectival: 'more confident', 'engaging well', with no reference to a question or a mark. The target has drifted: the arrangement began about method marks in Maths and is now general support across three subjects. And the pupil cannot say what the current goal is, which usually means there is not one.

Stopping is not a failure and it is sometimes the correct outcome of a diagnostic. A pupil with a content gap across a third of the specification in March cannot be rescued by weekly sessions, and a provider who says so has behaved well. Equally, a pupil whose script shows the marks are already there and the problem is nerves needs something other than teaching. The table lists the signals and the right response to each.

sections.heading: Evidence a school will act on
paragraphs: Parents often want a school to change something: a tier entry, a set, a predicted grade, the amount of feedback a pupil receives. Schools respond to evidence and not to concern, and the difference between those two is the difference between a productive meeting and an uncomfortable one. A timed script marked against the real mark scheme is evidence. A parental impression that the child is capable of more is not, however accurate it may be.

The strongest document is an independent measurement using the same instrument the school uses. A pupil who has sat a Cambridge or Pearson past paper under timing, marked against the published scheme, with the lost marks categorised, has produced something a head of department can read in five minutes and act on. It speaks the school's own language and it does not require the school to take anyone's word for anything.

Timing matters as much as content. A tier change request in the autumn of Year 11 can still be actioned; the same request in March cannot, because the entry has closed. A set review at the start of a year is a normal conversation; the same conversation in May is a complaint. The useful principle is to produce the evidence a full term before the decision it is meant to influence.

It is also worth asking the school what evidence it would find persuasive, which is a disarming question and usually gets a straight answer. Departments have internal thresholds and internal processes, and they will often tell you exactly what they need to see. That turns an adversarial exchange into a specification, and specifications can be met.

sections.heading: What not to accept as evidence, and coverage
paragraphs: Some things look like evidence and are not. A satisfaction percentage with no sample size, date or method is a marketing figure. A star rating a provider has asserted about itself, with no countable attributable reviews behind it, is not a measurement and is against Google's structured-data policy when shipped in schema. A claim about the proportion of students reaching top grades, with no underlying data available, is unverifiable by construction.

Nor should anyone accept a grade promise. No tutor can promise a particular grade, score or improvement, and a provider willing to put that in writing has told you they will say whatever closes the sale. The same applies to any suggestion that tutors are approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. IB Gram holds none of those and makes no such claim; it has no office or centre in the UAE.

Parents are entitled to check the one credential that does exist. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure circulating online is unverified.

On coverage: mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist, and in a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free. Where a specialist is working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, that is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number, and the rate does not change. A free trial lesson is one session, with no card details required, and the right thing to bring is a marked script.
