process.title: Ask for the script, not the grade
process.description: Request your child's last marked mock paper in the subjects you are considering. Most Dubai schools release it. A grade is a position; a script shows which marks were available and which were not, and the annotations are a diagnosis the marker has already written in the margin.

process.title: Count the lost marks into five buckets
process.description: Content not known, method not shown, arithmetic or selection error, precision or terminology, and time not reached. An approximate count is sufficient to see the shape, and one bucket is almost always much larger than the rest. That bucket is where the money should go.

process.title: Agree a target and a stop rule before buying a term
process.description: The target is a number of marks on named question types. The stop rule is the condition under which the arrangement ends - typically the same instrument flat at eight weeks. Setting both while everyone is optimistic removes a difficult conversation later and bounds the spend.

process.title: Repeat the same instrument every four weeks
process.description: The same kind of paper, under the same conditions, marked the same way. Comparability is what makes measurement possible, and it is destroyed by switching to easier papers or by marking generously. The repeat is the point of the whole arrangement, not an optional extra.

process.title: Decide at twelve weeks instead of renewing
process.description: Either the target has been met, in which case stop or set a new one, or it has not, in which case the conversation is about why. A provider proposing continuation without a side-by-side comparison against the baseline is asking for a standing order rather than reporting on a repair.

whyPoints.title: Progress reported in marks, not adjectives
whyPoints.description: Every report names the question types worked on and the marks recovered on them, compared with a dated baseline. 'More confident' is not a measurement and cannot be checked in June, which is exactly why it is the most common thing a family is told.

whyPoints.title: A stop rule agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: The condition under which the arrangement ends is set before any term is bought. No ranking competitor publishes one, which is understandable and not in a family's interest. A bounded project is cheaper and more honest than an open commitment.

whyPoints.title: The evidence file belongs to you
whyPoints.description: A dated record of your child's marked work and the mark counts at each checkpoint, shareable at any moment. An arrangement where the evidence lives only in the tutor's memory is one that cannot be evaluated, and that is rarely an accident.

whyPoints.title: Official materials used from source
whyPoints.description: Past papers and mark schemes are downloaded from Cambridge, Pearson or the IB rather than handed over as files, because the boards own them. A provider offering a folder of mark schemes has told you how it treats rules in general.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a brief has no specialist free, it is named rather than filled with a generalist at the same rate.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be interrogated
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted ratings, no proportion-reaching-top-grades claims, no grade promises, and no suggestion that KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB has approved or partnered with IB Gram.

faqs.question: How will we know whether tutoring is working for our North London Collegiate School Dubai child?
faqs.answer: By repeating one instrument. Have the pupil sit a timed past paper at the tier they are entered for, marked against the published scheme, before anything is bought. Count the lost marks by type and name a target in marks on specific question types. Then repeat the same paper type under the same conditions at four, eight and twelve weeks. Either the marks move on the questions being worked on or they do not. A conversation about growing confidence cannot be checked; a side-by-side mark count can, and it costs nothing but the hour.

faqs.question: What exactly should we ask the school for?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of which schools normally provide. The last marked mock script in the subjects you are considering, not the grade. The specification code and tier on your child's exam entry, from the examinations officer and preferably in writing. The reason behind any set allocation, from the department. And, if sixth form is in view, the published entry grades for the courses your child wants plus any underpinning subject requirement. None of that is confidential and all of it changes what tutoring is worth buying.

faqs.question: Can a parent read a marked script without understanding the subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the procedure takes about twenty minutes. Start at the back: blank final questions where comparable earlier ones were answered means time ran out. Look for partial marks, which mean the approach was right and something narrow went wrong. Then count every lost mark into five buckets - content, method, arithmetic or selection, precision, timing - approximately rather than perfectly. Finally read the margin annotations, because the marker has already written the diagnosis repeatedly. One bucket is almost always much larger than the others.

faqs.question: What should exist after four weeks of sessions?
faqs.answer: Three pieces of the pupil's own timed work, each marked, and the targeted habit visible in their writing even if the overall mark has not moved yet. If written method was the target, working should be appearing. If the analysis sentence was the target, it should be present. The overall grade is a noisy measure over four weeks and should not be the test. What should not exist at four weeks is nothing: sessions that have happened with no artefact produced cannot be evaluated at eight weeks either.

faqs.question: What is a reasonable stop rule to agree in advance?
faqs.answer: The simplest workable one is that if the baseline instrument, repeated at eight weeks under the same conditions, shows the same marks lost in the same category, the arrangement ends. That gives two months, which is long enough for honest work to show movement on narrow targets. Agreeing it at the start, while everyone is optimistic, removes a difficult conversation later and bounds the spend. No ranking competitor page publishes a stop rule, which is understandable from their position and not from yours.

faqs.question: How much should we trust a disappointing mock result?
faqs.answer: As a diagnosis, considerably. As a prediction, much less. A mock is one performance on one paper, often covering an incomplete syllabus, sometimes sat in a classroom rather than under examination conditions, and sometimes marked deliberately harshly to create urgency. Each of those depresses the number without telling you about June. What the script reliably shows is where marks are currently being lost and in which category, and that is more useful than any forecast. Read the questions rather than the headline.

faqs.question: Can a mock result overstate how well a pupil will do?
faqs.answer: Yes, in three recognisable ways. A mock covering two thirds of the specification is an easier paper than the real one, because the untaught third cannot be examined. A pupil who revised intensively for one known date may not sustain that effort across eight or nine subjects in a full series. And an internally applied generous boundary is not the boundary the board will apply. The remedy is the same as for an understated mock: look at which questions were answered and which topics had actually been taught.

faqs.question: What evidence will a Dubai school actually act on?
faqs.answer: Measurement in its own language. A timed board past paper, marked against the published scheme, with lost marks categorised, is a document a head of department can read in five minutes and act on, because it does not ask them to take anyone's word for anything. Parental impression, however accurate, is not evidence in that sense. Timing matters equally: a tier change can be actioned in the autumn of Year 11 and cannot in March, so produce the evidence a full term before the decision it is meant to influence.

faqs.question: Should we accept a provider's satisfaction percentage as proof of anything?
faqs.answer: No, unless it arrives with a sample size, a date and a stated method, which in this market it never does. Ranking pages in UAE tutoring carry satisfaction figures, self-asserted star ratings and claims about the proportion of students reaching top grades, none accompanied by anything checkable. One page shows a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim about far larger numbers. Ask for the n, the date and the collection method. The response to that question is itself informative, whichever way it goes.

faqs.question: What are the soft signals that an arrangement has quietly stopped working?
faqs.answer: Four recur. No written artefact after four weeks, which means nothing measurable is being produced. Reporting that is purely adjectival, with no reference to a question or a mark. Scope creep, where an arrangement that began about method marks in one subject has become general support across three. And the pupil being unable to say what the current goal is, which usually means there is not one. Any of those is a reason to return to a single target and a single instrument rather than to fund the wider arrangement.

faqs.question: Is stopping tutoring ever the right recommendation?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and a provider who says so has behaved well. A pupil whose script shows a content gap across a third of the specification in March cannot be rescued by weekly sessions, and the honest plan is to narrow to what can still move and accept the rest. A pupil whose marks are already there and whose problem is examination nerves needs something other than teaching. A pupil who has met the named target should stop rather than continue by default, which is how a budget quietly doubles.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's coursework or internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can score a draft against the published criteria and say which criterion is unmet, which is feedback the student can act on and repeat. A tutor cannot write, co-write or edit any submitted piece to completion, and no price makes that acceptable, because the mark has to represent the student's own work. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate. Nobody should hand over mark schemes or board documents as files either; the official page is linked instead.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Nad Al Sheba, Meydan or Dubai Hills addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For measured work this suits the method, because the session is spent annotating the pupil's own marked script on a shared screen and re-answering the questions where marks were lost. It also removes the travel premium inside the published AED 180-500 in-home band and the cancellation risk of a peak-hour journey.

faqs.question: How do we check that a tutor in Dubai holds the required permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a tutor claiming their rate reflects licensing costs has misread their own paperwork. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-north-london-co.closingHeading: Set up the instrument before you buy anything
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-north-london-co.closingBody: Ask the school for your child's last marked script, spend twenty minutes counting the lost marks into five buckets, and write down a target in marks on the question types in the largest bucket. Then agree a stop rule: if the same paper type at eight weeks shows the same losses, the arrangement ends. intro.heading: What a Raffles World Academy family is actually buying when they book a tutor
paragraphs: Raffles World Academy sits in Umm Suqeim 3, and it runs one of the less common routes through a Dubai secondary school: an IB continuum underneath, IGCSE examinations at the end of Year 11, and the IB Diploma Programme on top. That combination is why a search for an IB IGCSE tutor for Raffles World Academy students in Dubai is not the same search as one for a straight British school. A student here can move from Middle Years criterion marking to a Cambridge grade scale and then back to Diploma criterion marking inside thirty months. Each of those three systems rewards something different, and a tutor who does not know which one your child is being graded against this term will teach the wrong thing competently.

Confirm the exact subject list with the school before you book anything. Schools in Dubai revise their option blocks every few years, and the number of IGCSE subjects a cohort sits, the boards they sit them with, and which subjects run as Middle Years courses instead, all change. The school's own curriculum page and the head of secondary are the authority on that, not a tutoring site. What does not change is the shape of the problem: Year 11 produces a set of letter grades that the Diploma coordinator reads as a prediction, and Year 12 then asks for a different kind of writing within weeks of those grades arriving.

The gap between those two things is where most of the tutoring demand on this page comes from. An Extended-tier IGCSE paper asks a student to execute a known method under time pressure. A Diploma Higher Level paper asks the same student to choose a method, justify the choice, and comment on its limits. A child who scored a 7 at IGCSE by being fast and accurate can lose two grade points in the first Diploma term without doing anything wrong, because speed and accuracy are now the floor rather than the ceiling. That is a teachable transition, and it is far cheaper to teach in Year 11 than to repair in Year 12.

IB Gram matches one tutor to one student and keeps that pairing. Sessions run over live video with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and a written note at the end of each hour. We do not send a tutor to a Dubai address; in-home visiting is a service IB Gram offers only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than pretending otherwise. The practical effect for an Umm Suqeim family is that the pool is no longer limited to whoever can reach Umm Suqeim 3 by four in the afternoon.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raffles-world-a.programmesIntro: A Raffles World Academy student may be sitting any of four different assessment systems depending on their year group. These are the four, with what each one measures and what it means for a Dubai family planning tuition around it.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses ending in external written papers, graded A*-G on the Cambridge scale or 9-1 on the Pearson scale. Cambridge syllabuses tier into Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher while the Pearson sciences are single-tier. Nothing in a Cambridge IGCSE science is coursework any more, so the practical skills are assessed in a written paper.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, the IGCSE grade set does double duty. It is the qualification the Ministry of Education equivalency route counts, where five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required and Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from that count. It is also the evidence a Diploma coordinator uses when deciding whether a Higher Level request is realistic.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked against named criteria by the teacher and moderated externally. The final score runs to 45 points including up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's Diploma cohort is a small slice of a very large private sector. International Baccalaureate programmes accounted for about seven per cent of private-school enrolment in the 2024-25 figures published by Dubai's media office, against 37 per cent on UK curricula. That minority position is exactly why a specialist Higher Level tutor is harder to find locally than a general maths tutor, and why online matching widens the pool so much.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no final examination in the Cambridge sense. Students are judged on inquiry, communication, critical thinking and reflection, which is a different skill set from executing a known method under timed conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families moving a child into a continuum school mid-year often arrive from a CBSE or American system where marks come from tests. The adjustment is to criterion language: a Year 9 student who writes a correct answer with no reasoning can score well below a weaker student who shows their thinking. Tutoring here is largely about teaching the student to read the criterion descriptors.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in every Dubai private school. Arabic is streamed by first-language and additional-language status, and Islamic Education is streamed for Arab and non-Arab students, with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requiring that classes for the two groups are organised separately rather than combined.
programmes.countryNote: The authority's guidance calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. It also prohibits the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission, which limits how any tutor may describe Arabic or Islamic Education support.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raffles-world-a.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubai families most often ask about at Extended tier and at Higher Level. Each line names what the assessment actually rewards, because that is where the grade is won rather than in topic coverage.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level runs three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent with the exploration at 20 per cent. Paper 3 is the one Dubai students under-prepare: two long structured investigations where the first mark depends on reading an unfamiliar context correctly. Proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form and the Maclaurin series are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended tier sits Papers 2 and 4, each worth half the grade, one short-answer and one structured. The Extended-only content that costs marks is function notation with composite and inverse functions, histograms with unequal class widths, and vectors in column form. Core candidates cannot be awarded above grade C, which makes the tier decision a grade ceiling decision.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0625 or 4PH1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 Extended runs a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 per cent and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper at 20 per cent. The written practical paper is where Dubai candidates lose the most: it tests graph-plotting discipline, significant figures and the wording of a conclusion, none of which improve by revising content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0620 or 4CH1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic is the single largest source of lost marks at IGCSE Extended, and it reappears at Diploma level as the quantitative thread through energetics and equilibrium. At Higher Level, organic mechanisms are marked for curly-arrow placement and intermediate charge, so a correct product with a wrong mechanism scores partially and a student rarely knows why.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IGCSE 0610 or 4BI1, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: The content is accessible and the marking is not. IGCSE Extended rewards precise command-term response, so a student who explains when asked to describe loses marks on knowledge they clearly hold. At Diploma level the scientific investigation carries a fifth of the grade and is marked on research design and evaluation rather than on how clean the data looked.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL; IGCSE 0500 and 0510
subjects.description: The Diploma individual oral asks a student to link a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract in ten minutes. Dubai students who read widely still score poorly here because the oral is a structured argument, not a discussion. IGCSE First Language 0500 rewards directed writing that holds register, which is a drillable skill.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment, 800 words each, and the diagram is the mark. Students write good prose around a diagram that does not show the effect they describe. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and heavily templated, which makes it the fastest paper on which to gain points with a tutor.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level internal assessment is a research project on a real organisation, and the most common failure is a question that cannot be answered with the evidence a sixteen-year-old can actually obtain in Dubai. Fixing the research question in the first fortnight is worth more than any amount of later redrafting.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: IGCSE 0478 splits into computer systems and algorithms, and the algorithm paper is marked on pseudocode discipline rather than on whether the logic would compile. At Diploma level the Higher Level extension covers object-oriented programming and abstract data structures, where tracing a recursive call by hand is the skill that opens up the paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Non-Arab students in Dubai private schools take Arabic as an additional language throughout their schooling, and the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requires the stream to be taught separately from the first-language stream. Support here is reading fluency and script confidence rather than examination technique, and it benefits from short, frequent sessions.

sections.heading: What this search actually means for a Year 11 or Year 12 student here
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor for Raffles World Academy students in Dubai is, in practice, a tutor who can hold two mark schemes in mind at once. Year 11 is being graded by Cambridge or Pearson examiners against a published mark scheme that rewards the right answer by the right method. Year 12 is being graded against criterion descriptors that reward judgement and reflection. A tutor who only knows one of those systems will give advice that is correct for the wrong year group.

The practical test when you speak to a tutor is simple. Ask what the command word describe requires that explain does not, and then ask what criterion A on the mathematics exploration is actually called. A tutor who answers both quickly has taught both systems. A tutor who answers one well and talks around the other has not, and that is worth knowing before a term's fees are committed.

Timing matters as much as subject knowledge. Raffles World Academy students begin early, and the school day ends in the heat of the afternoon. A session that starts at three is a session with a tired student in it. Most families on this page settle on a slot between half past five and eight, which is only possible when the tutor does not have to drive anywhere. That single constraint is why online delivery is not a compromise here but the thing that makes a specialist slot available at all.

The last element is continuity. A student who sees a different tutor each month restates the same problem each month. IB Gram holds the pairing for as long as it works, and changes it on request rather than on rotation. The free trial lesson exists so that the decision about whether the pairing works is made by the student after an hour of real teaching, not by a parent after reading a profile.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that sets a grade ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses offer two tiers in most subjects, and the choice is made by the school on the school's evidence, usually late in Year 10. It is not a presentational difference. A Core candidate in Mathematics 0580 sits Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C. An Extended candidate sits Papers 2 and 4 and is in contention for A*. The content overlaps substantially, but the Extended-only material is the part that appears in every Diploma prerequisite conversation afterwards.

Pearson works differently and parents mix the two up constantly. Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher, with Higher covering grades 9 to 4 and a grade 3 allowed below it. The Pearson international sciences are single-tier, so a candidate sits one route to the full 9-1 range. That means a child who moves between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course is not simply changing syllabus codes; they may be changing whether a tier decision exists at all.

For a student heading into the Diploma, the tier question is really a question about Higher Level. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes the Extended-tier algebra and functions content as a starting point, not as something to be met for the first time in Year 12. A student placed on Core in Year 10 who then wants Higher Level mathematics has roughly a term of algebra to acquire that their classmates already have, and that is the most common piece of catch-up work this page is asked for.

The honest advice is to have the tier conversation with the school in the first term of Year 10, not the last. Schools move students between tiers on evidence, and the evidence is the work produced in that first year. Tuition in Year 10 that secures an Extended placement is cheaper and less stressful than tuition in Year 12 trying to bridge the consequence of a Core placement.

sections.heading: Where Raffles World Academy students lose marks, subject by subject
paragraphs: Lost marks cluster, and they cluster in the same places across Dubai cohorts because the causes are structural rather than personal. In IGCSE Extended mathematics, the cluster is function notation. A student who can solve an equation flawlessly will mishandle a composite function written as fg of x, because the notation reads right to left and almost nothing else in school mathematics does. Three sessions on notation alone routinely move a paper mark more than three sessions on new content.

In the Cambridge sciences, the cluster is the practical paper. Paper 6 asks for a conclusion in the mark scheme's own language, a graph drawn with a sensible scale, and readings quoted to a consistent precision. None of that is content, so revising content does not fix it, and a student who has only ever been marked on content will not know it is being assessed. This is the most reliable twenty per cent of a Cambridge science grade to improve with a tutor.

At Diploma level, the cluster moves to reflection. Mathematics exploration criteria allocate marks to personal engagement and reflection, and these are the criteria Dubai students score lowest on, because they read as padding to a student trained on IGCSE efficiency. They are not padding; they are a quarter of the exploration marks. Teaching a student to write a genuine reflective paragraph about a method that did not work is a specific, learnable skill.

The fourth cluster is command terms, and it runs across every subject and both systems. A student who writes an excellent explanation in answer to a question that said state has produced a correct response that scores nothing extra and burned four minutes. Tutors on this page keep a running error log per student precisely so these patterns become visible rather than being rediscovered each term.

sections.heading: From IGCSE to the Diploma: the gap Year 11 does not close
paragraphs: The transition into Year 12 is the most expensive moment in this whole page if it goes wrong, and the most avoidable. The reason is that IGCSE finishes in May or June and the Diploma starts in late August, so the handover happens across a summer when nobody is teaching. A student who leaves Year 11 with a specific, named gap arrives in Year 12 with the same gap plus eight weeks of forgetting on top of it.

The gaps are predictable by subject. In mathematics it is algebraic fluency and the habit of working symbolically rather than numerically. In the sciences it is quantitative handling: moles at IGCSE becomes the arithmetic spine of Diploma chemistry, and a student who guessed their way through it will stall in the first unit. In the essay subjects it is the move from a structured answer to a sustained argument with a thesis that survives three paragraphs.

A short summer block is unusually cost-effective here because it is short. Six to eight hours spread across July and August, aimed at one named gap, is a far smaller commitment than a term of remedial work in Year 12 while the new syllabus is also being taught. Families who do this tend to report that the first Diploma unit test stopped being the shock it was for their older child.

Where a student is moving into the Diploma from outside the school's own Middle Years route, the gap list is different again and needs reading individually. A student arriving from a CBSE Class 10 has strong procedural mathematics and little experience of extended writing. A student arriving from an American middle school has the opposite. Neither profile is a problem, but both are badly served by a generic bridging course.

Those figures are real and they buy real help with homework and content gaps. What they do not usually buy is someone who has marked a Higher Level paper against the criteria.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor working online, broadly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Above that sit IB and IGCSE specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and beyond. TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards. The premium tier runs from AED 500, with BartyED at AED 650. None of these are IB Gram's prices and this page does not publish a price list. What a Dubai family should take from the table is the shape of the market: the gap between a content-help rate and a specialist rate is roughly threefold, and the gap between an online specialist and an in-home specialist is mostly travel. Set your budget against the band you actually need, then take a free trial lesson before paying for anything.

sections.heading: Online or a tutor in the car: what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Set the two options side by side honestly, because an in-home tutor is a genuinely good product for some families and pretending otherwise is not useful. A tutor in the room can see a child's exercise book without being shown it, can read body language that a video call compresses, and removes any question of a student quietly doing something else. For a younger child or a student who needs physical presence to stay on task, that is worth paying for.

The cost is twofold and both parts are hidden. The first is money: the in-home band starts at AED 180 and the online specialist band starts at AED 150, and the difference is travel time the tutor cannot sell to anyone else. The second is supply. A tutor who must physically reach Umm Suqeim 3 by half past five can serve perhaps three or four students a day. That constraint means the pool of people available to your child is whoever is both qualified and geographically close, which for Higher Level mathematics in Dubai is a short list.

Online delivery inverts that. The question becomes whether the right specialist is free at your preferred hour, not whether they happen to live on this side of Sheikh Zayed Road. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visiting is an India-only service, and the UAE offer is one-to-one live video. That is a real limitation and it is stated here rather than buried.

The practical answer most families on this page reach is a hybrid of their own making: online one-to-one for the specialist subject where the pool matters, and whatever local arrangement works for general homework supervision. That is a sensible split, and no part of it requires paying a travel premium on the subject where expertise is scarcest.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Almost no competing page in this search names an examination series at all, which is strange, because the calendar is the thing that determines when tutoring is useful. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026. For a sense of how long results take, the June 2026 Pearson results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are published, checkable dates, which is why they appear here with their years attached.

One Cambridge administrative detail is worth more to a Dubai parent than any revision tip. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable, not from a generic one found online.

Counting backwards is the useful exercise. Final entries close months before the papers. Internal deadlines for Diploma coursework sit earlier still, because the school needs time to mark and moderate. A family that starts tutoring when the examination timetable is published has missed the window where the internal assessment components, which are a fifth of each Diploma grade, could still be improved.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an exploration or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the section where the search results in front of you divide into two groups, and it is worth being direct about why. At least one site ranking for queries like this one sells completed internal assessments. That is not tutoring. Submitting work a student did not produce is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the diploma rather than the subject. No page should be vague about this, so this one is not.

The legitimate boundary is well defined and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the subject content the student needs, explain what each named criterion rewards, read a draft the student wrote and mark it against the descriptors, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and teach the referencing convention. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into the final version, choose the research question outright or handle the data analysis on the student's behalf.

In practice the most valuable hour is the earliest one, before writing starts. A mathematics exploration built on a question that cannot generate enough mathematics will score poorly regardless of how well it is written, and an Extended Essay on a question with no accessible sources will stall at the research stage. Half an hour spent stress-testing the question saves weeks. That conversation is entirely legitimate because the student leaves it having made the decision themselves.

Expect your tutor to keep a record of what they did. Sessions on this page are documented with a note of what was taught and what the student changed afterwards, in the student's own words. If a school ever asks what support a student received, that record is the answer, and a family that can produce it is in a far stronger position than one that cannot.

faqs.question: Which exam board does Raffles World Academy use for IGCSE, Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, because schools in Dubai run different boards in different subjects and revise their entries. Some enter Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics; others use one board throughout. The difference matters: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended with Papers 2 and 4 at Extended, while Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher over two two-hour papers. The examinations officer or the head of secondary will confirm the code per subject. Once you have the codes, matching a tutor becomes straightforward, because the paper structure and the practical assessment follow from the code.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 at Raffles World Academy and wants Higher Level maths. Is that realistic?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on tier and on algebraic fluency rather than on current grade. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes the Extended-tier algebra and functions content as a starting point. A student sitting Extended with secure function notation and confident symbolic manipulation is in a good position. A student on Core, or one who works numerically rather than symbolically, has roughly a term of algebra to acquire. That is bridgeable, and the cheapest time to bridge it is the spring of Year 11 and the following summer, not the first term of Year 12.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our villa in Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. That is a real limitation and it is better stated than discovered later. What you gain is the thing the travel premium was paying for: the tutor does not have to be within driving distance of Umm Suqeim 3 at half past five, so the pool of available specialists is set by who is free at your hour rather than by who lives nearby. For Higher Level sciences in Dubai that difference is substantial.

faqs.question: What does a specialist IGCSE or IB tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The market splits into bands. Budget online platforms publish from AED 33 to 65, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visiting is AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are the market's own published figures, not IB Gram's price list; ask for a trial lesson before committing to anything.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematics exploration without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear enough to describe in a sentence. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student wrote and mark it against the descriptors, and question a weak argument. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a draft into its final form, or choose the research question outright. The most valuable session is the earliest one, stress-testing the student's own question before writing starts, because an exploration built on a thin question scores poorly however well it is written.

faqs.question: Which months do UAE IGCSE candidates actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so it should never appear in a UAE revision plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so ask the school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Raffles World Academy student need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. One competing site publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel before acting, and note that IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of the equivalency process.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting tuition six weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the work changes shape. Six weeks is too short to acquire missing content across a whole syllabus and long enough to fix paper technique, which is often where the marks are. An intensive block sits a timed paper cold, marks it during the session, and drills the two or three repeating error types that surface. In Cambridge sciences the practical paper is usually the fastest twenty per cent to improve, because scales, precision and conclusion wording are technique rather than knowledge. What six weeks cannot do is change an internally assessed component that is already submitted.

faqs.question: What does the Knowledge and Human Development Authority inspection rating of a school actually tell me?
faqs.answer: Dubai private schools are inspected on a six-band scale running from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. The band is a judgement about the school as a whole across teaching, outcomes, leadership and provision, not a prediction about one subject or one child. Read the published report rather than the headline band, because the subject-level commentary inside it is far more useful for planning tuition. The reports sit on the authority's own website, which is where you should read them rather than relying on a summary elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does my non-Arab child still have to take Arabic in a Dubai IB school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Arabic is streamed by first-language and additional-language status, and the Knowledge and Human Development Authority requires that classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies are organised separately, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and the authority advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with Raffles World Academy students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, applications are made through the ministry's smart app and e-services, and the published completion time is two working days. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover both my children if one is in Year 10 and one in Year 12?
faqs.answer: Often yes within a subject family, and it is usually a good idea. A chemistry specialist who teaches Cambridge 0620 Extended and Diploma chemistry sees the same quantitative thread running through both, and can tell the younger child exactly which skill the older one wishes they had secured earlier. Separate one-to-one sessions are still held, because the two students are being graded against different schemes and a shared hour serves neither well. Scheduling them back to back on the same evening is the arrangement most families settle on.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject at Raffles World Academy?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than matching a generalist to it. Some Diploma combinations are genuinely thin on specialist supply, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Paper 3 level are the usual pressure points in this market. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour, the options are a different hour, a short wait for a slot to open, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. All three are disclosed up front, with the rate, before anything is booked.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and the Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan and family routines move later, so most students shift their weekly slot to after Iftar for the month. Because delivery is over live video there is no travel to reschedule around, which makes that shift easy to arrange. Across the long summer break, families either pause entirely or use a short block aimed at one named gap ahead of the new year, which is the pattern we see most from Year 11 students heading into the Diploma. Tell us which you want a fortnight ahead and the slot is held or released accordingly.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raffles-world-a.closingHeading: Start with one honest hour on the work your child actually has in front of them
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-raffles-world-a.closingBody: The useful first step is not a brochure call. Send the year group, the board and syllabus code, and the two topics or papers that are costing marks, and we will match a tutor who teaches that code and that level. The first session is a free trial on the student's own work, over live video, at a Gulf Standard Time hour that suits a Dubai school day. Afterwards the student says whether the pairing works. If it does, we hold the slot for the term. If it does not, we match again. Nothing on this page is a price list, and no figure here is published without naming where it came from.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-repton-school-d.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are matched to one subject at one level or tier. The first thing any of them should produce is a marked script with the losses counted, because that document is what makes everything afterwards measurable.

intro.heading: Most tutoring is bought on trust and never measured
paragraphs: A Repton School Dubai family hiring a tutor usually gets a reasonable experience and almost never gets evidence. Sessions happen, the student reports that they are helpful, a term passes, and the next data point is a mock or a real result. If the grade moved, the tutoring is credited. If it did not, the conclusion is usually that the child needs to work harder. Neither inference is supported by anything, because nobody measured.

This is fixable with two documents and a monthly habit, and it costs nothing. The first document is a marked script from a paper sat under genuine timing, with every lost mark attributed to a cause rather than listed by topic. The second is a risk list built from it and updated monthly, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work that justifies the marking. That is the entire apparatus. It takes a tutor ten minutes a month to maintain if they are working from it and cannot be produced at all if they are not.

The reason to insist on causes rather than topics is that a lost mark has six possible origins and they need different remedies. Content not known. Content known but not recalled under pressure. Question misread. Command term misread. Method correct but not written out. Time ran out. A student told to revise more will apply the wrong remedy to five of those six, and a tutor who starts teaching before knowing the mix is guessing with your money and your child's term.

Repton School Dubai sits at Nad Al Sheba with a second campus in Al Barsha, runs the British curriculum through IGCSE, and offers a sixth form where families choose between routes; confirm the current provision directly with the school, since school offers change. That structure makes the evidence question sharper, because a student crossing from IGCSE into the Diploma inside one institution changes assessment system without changing building, and the measurements that worked in Year 11 do not transfer unchanged to Year 12.

IB Gram supports Repton families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, stated the same way on every country page here. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. What the online format adds to an evidence-led arrangement is specific: a slot that is a start time rather than an arrival window, and work marked between sessions rather than glanced at in the room. Marking between sessions is the part that produces the evidence, because a script annotated properly away from the student is a document you can read, while a correction made verbally across a table in the room leaves nothing behind for anybody to check a month later.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-repton-school-d.programmesIntro: Three stages, and the evidence changes at each one. What counts as proof in Year 10 is not what counts in the final Diploma year.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with tiering into Core and Extended on Cambridge or Foundation and Higher on Pearson Edexcel, and a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. Almost everything is measured at the end, which makes interim measurement entirely the family's responsibility.
programmes.countryNote: The evidence at this stage is a timed past paper marked against the official scheme. Nothing else is comparable to the real thing, because a question attempted without a clock measures knowledge rather than performance, and the gap between those two is where most of the lost marks in a Repton cohort's scripts actually sit.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, which gives a second, independent kind of evidence to track.
programmes.countryNote: Here the evidence is two-track: timed papers on one side and marked drafts on the other. A marked draft is the better early signal because the criteria are published and the work is untimed, so a weakness shows up cleanly rather than being tangled with pacing. Ask for both, from the first month.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, where that route is taken
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken deeper, with no compulsory core and limited coursework. Entry is gated on IGCSE grades in the same subject, usually at a B or better, which is the real reason Year 10 tier decisions reach forward two years.
programmes.countryNote: Evidence on this route is almost entirely paper-based, which makes it the simplest of the three to measure and the easiest to leave unmeasured. A student taking three subjects should have one timed, marked paper per subject per term at minimum, and the lost marks counted by cause each time rather than summarised.

programmes.name: The crossing at sixteen
programmes.description: Moving from Extended IGCSE into Higher Level Diploma or into A Level is a real step, and it is different in each subject. Mathematics is the largest: calculus arrives properly and proof becomes examinable, which a strong Extended grade does not guarantee readiness for.
programmes.countryNote: For a Repton student the crossing happens inside one school, which hides it. The curriculum changes while the corridors do not, and families therefore plan for it less than families who are also changing institution. A summer block of six to ten sessions in the subject with the largest gap is the cheapest intervention available at this point.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-repton-school-d.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the note names the evidence that shows whether tutoring is working. It differs by subject more than families expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Evidence is method marks earned on structured questions, visible in the script even where the final answer is wrong. Weightings: Standard Level two papers at forty per cent each plus the Exploration at twenty; Higher Level three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty with the Exploration at twenty.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Evidence is a written interpretation in context rather than a bare answer, because that is what the scheme rewards. Calculator technique is examinable in itself, so a script showing the steps the screen produced is worth more than one showing only the output.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Evidence splits: performance on the Paper 1 data-analysis section, which rewards practice on unfamiliar graphs, and sign-convention accuracy on extended calculation. Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 forty-four, and the investigation twenty.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Evidence is recall items closing fast and mechanisms closing slowly. Organic conditions and ion tests should disappear from a risk list within three weeks; energetics calculation takes longer and should not be expected to move at the same rate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Evidence is command-term compliance. Count how many marks were lost on a script to answering describe where the question asked explain, then count again a month later. It is the single largest avoidable loss in the subject and it is measurable to the mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evidence is diagram marks, which are awarded individually for labelled axes, correct initial position, correct shift direction and the new equilibrium. Count them on two scripts a month apart. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Evidence is a sentence about effect where there was previously a sentence about technique. That change is visible in the text and is the whole of Paper 1 analysis, worth thirty-five per cent at both levels. The HL Essay adds twenty per cent at Higher Level.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580; Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Evidence is written method on the final parts of structured questions. A student who shows a correct method and slips on arithmetic keeps most of the marks; one who writes only an answer loses marks already earned. The split between the non-calculator and calculator papers differs by board.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences (0625, 0620, 0610; Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Evidence depends on the board. Cambridge carries a practical component worth twenty per cent, sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson Edexcel has no separate practical exam. Count losses separately per component rather than per subject.

subjects.name: IGCSE English and Humanities
subjects.description: Evidence in English is register and audience control on directed writing, and own-words compliance on the summary question. In history and geography it is use of provenance and named examples with figures, both of which are countable on a marked script rather than impressionistic.

sections.heading: The six causes of a lost mark, and why the distinction is the whole thing
paragraphs: Take a marked script and go through it mark by mark. Every lost mark has a cause, and in practice there are six. The student did not know the content. The student knew it and could not retrieve it under pressure. The student misread what the question was asking. The student read the question correctly but answered a different command — described where the paper said explain. The student had the right method and did not write it down, so the method marks were never available. Or the student ran out of time.

Those six have nothing in common as problems. Content not known needs teaching. Content not retrieved needs retrieval practice, which is a different activity involving low-stakes testing rather than explanation. A misread question needs slower reading and underlining, which is a behaviour. A misread command term needs the command-term list and an hour sorting past questions by it. An unwritten method needs a habit change and nothing else. Running out of time needs section timing targets.

Now consider what happens when a family is told simply that their child must revise more. That instruction is the correct remedy for exactly one of the six, and the wrong one for five. It is also what most tutoring defaults to, because teaching is what tutors are set up to do and the other five remedies look less like a lesson. A tutor who hands you a count across the six categories after the first paper has told you more in one document than most arrangements produce in a term.

For a Repton student this is particularly worth doing before a sixth-form route decision. A student losing marks mainly to pacing and unwritten method will do better in a system with more components and more internal assessment; a student losing marks mainly to content gaps needs those closed whichever route they take. The count is a better input to that decision than a predicted grade, because a predicted grade compresses all six causes into one letter.

sections.heading: Using the mock cycle as a measurement instead of a verdict
paragraphs: Mocks arrive, a percentage is reported, the household reacts, and the information is thrown away. That is a waste of the single best measurement opportunity in the school year, because a mock is the only occasion on which a student sits a full paper under something close to real conditions with somebody else marking it. The reaction is understandable and the discard is not.

Start by reading the percentage correctly, which means not reading it as a grade. Grade boundaries are set by the board after each series has been marked, taking account of how the cohort and the paper performed, and are published afterwards. A mock graded against a previous series' boundaries is an estimate. A student two marks below a boundary is not two marks from a grade in any dependable sense, because the boundary will move. Treating a mock percentage as a verdict is therefore reading a number as something it is not.

What the mock actually provides is a script. Ask for it back, with the mark breakdown, and go through it for causes. That is a one-hour job and it produces the baseline for everything afterwards. It also lets you compare the school's marking with a tutor's, which is worth doing once: significant disagreement early is information, and discovering it in June is not.

The cycle then has a shape worth planning around. Pre-mock, the work is coverage and technique. The mock itself is the measurement. Post-mock is the most productive fortnight in the school year, because the evidence is fresh and specific and the student's attention is available. Families routinely spend that fortnight on recovery from the emotional reaction and start the useful work three weeks later, when the specificity has faded.

sections.heading: What a marked internal assessment draft tells you that a paper cannot
paragraphs: For a Repton student in the Diploma there is a second evidence stream that is cleaner than paper performance, and families underuse it. An internal assessment draft is untimed, criteria-marked and written over weeks, which means a weakness in it is not tangled up with pacing or exam nerves. If a draft scores in a low band on a published criterion, that is a direct statement about a specific skill, and it is actionable immediately.

In the Diploma sciences the investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Those four names do most of the diagnostic work. A low research design mark is a planning failure that cannot be repaired once the data exists, which makes the planning conversation the highest-value single session available. A low data analysis mark is usually about uncertainty and processing. A low conclusion mark means a result was stated without being linked to the science. A low evaluation mark means limitations were listed without remedies.

The evidence of improvement here is unusually clean: a second draft scoring in a higher band on the same criterion, with the change visible in the text. That is a document a parent can read without any subject knowledge, because the criterion wording tells you what was being looked for and the two drafts show whether it appeared. Ask for both drafts and the criterion wording, not a summary of the feedback.

The authorship line matters more here than anywhere else, and should be stated before the work starts. A tutor may explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so the sentences become theirs. A page in this search result sells finished assessed work, and the consequence of that falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: Week by week: what should change, and when you would see it
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement should produce visible change on a known schedule, and the schedule differs by cause. Knowing it prevents both impatience and complacency: a parent who expects content gaps to close in a fortnight will panic unnecessarily, and a parent who waits a term for command-term discipline to improve has waited ten weeks too long.

The fastest movers are command-term discipline and unwritten method. Both are behaviours rather than knowledge, both are visible on the very next marked script, and both should show up within one to two weeks. If they have not moved after three, the tutor is not enforcing them on marked work, and that is a specific thing to raise rather than a vague dissatisfaction.

Retrieval failures take two to three weeks of frequent short testing. Misread questions take one to two weeks of deliberate slow reading. Pacing takes three to six weeks because stamina develops slowly and only through full papers to time. Content gaps are the slowest at two to four weeks per topic, which is also why a student with gaps across a syllabus eight weeks before a series cannot close them all and should be told so honestly rather than sold a plan that assumes otherwise.

The practical instruction is to ask, at the first review, which causes are expected to move first and by when. A tutor who gives you that forecast has committed to something checkable. One who says progress takes time has not, and the second answer is far more common than it should be in a market where nobody measures anything.

sections.heading: The sixth-form route decision, made on evidence rather than reputation
paragraphs: At a school offering more than one post-sixteen route, the choice gets made on conversation, sibling precedent and reputation. It can be made on evidence instead, and the evidence already exists in the Year 11 scripts. Confirm the current sixth-form provision with the school before planning around it, because offers change, but the reasoning below holds wherever a genuine choice exists.

The Diploma is six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge course examined through an essay of up to 1,600 words and an exhibition commentary of up to 950, and CAS, which carries no points but blocks the diploma if incomplete. It is scored out of 45 with 24 as the minimum and up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. A Levels are three or four subjects taken deeper with no core and limited coursework.

Now read the cause count against that. A student whose losses are mainly pacing and unwritten method does relatively better where more of the grade comes from untimed, criteria-marked internal assessment, which favours the Diploma. A student whose losses are content gaps in two subjects and nothing elsewhere does relatively better concentrating on three subjects, which favours A Levels. A student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way that no amount of subject tutoring repairs, and that is the single strongest signal in either direction.

The mathematics decision sits inside the Diploma option and deserves separate attention. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation share component weightings and differ in content, and some university programmes expect one specifically. Check the prerequisites for the courses under consideration before the subject form is signed, because changing after the first term is disruptive.

sections.heading: What should not count as evidence, however sincerely reported
paragraphs: Four things get reported as progress that are not progress. They are usually reported honestly, they are often genuine precursors to improvement, and none of them is a mark. A parent who accepts them as evidence has no way of knowing whether the arrangement is working until results, which is precisely the position this page is written to avoid.

The first is improved confidence. Real, pleasant, and not measurable. The second is better engagement: the student now does the homework, attends willingly, asks questions. Also real, also not a grade. The third is a completed stack of past papers, which measures volume rather than performance unless each was sat to time and marked against the official scheme — and in most cases they were not, which is why forty papers can produce no movement at all. The fourth is a risen predicted grade, which is somebody's estimate against boundaries that will move.

The replacement for all four is the same and it is cheap. Marked work under timing, from two different weeks, with the lost marks counted by cause and the counts compared. If the count on a given cause has fallen, something happened. If it has not, something should change, and the change is not always the tutor: it may be the subject being prioritised, the frequency, the slot, or the remedy being applied to the wrong cause.

Ask for it monthly rather than termly. A term is long enough for an arrangement to drift entirely, and by the time a term-end report arrives the time remaining before the series has shrunk. Monthly reviews with two scripts catch both common failure modes early: the wrong content, and a slot that has quietly stopped working because the Dubai afternoon commute moved.

sections.heading: Materials, honesty and the position of this site
paragraphs: Specifications, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge and Pearson. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference and link so a parent reads the authoritative document. No grade-boundary figure appears on this page for that reason, and because a boundary quoted second-hand is a number that will eventually be wrong.

On assessed work the line is authorship and it is not a matter of degree. Teach the content, explain the criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, teach them to fix it. Do not write the internal assessment, do not draft the Extended Essay, do not edit a piece to completion so the words become the tutor's. The caps are 4,000 words on the Extended Essay, 1,600 on the Theory of Knowledge essay, 950 on the exhibition commentary, 3,000 on the Diploma sciences investigation and 800 per Economics commentary.

There is also a UAE rule a Dubai parent should know before approaching a teacher privately. Private tutoring is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school.

Finally, position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, has no arrangement with Repton School Dubai or any school named here, publishes no star rating and quotes no statistic without its source and date.

faqs.question: What evidence should a Repton School Dubai family ask a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Two documents. A full paper sat under genuine exam timing, marked against the official scheme, with every lost mark attributed to one of six causes and the counts written down. Then a risk list built from it, updated monthly, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work attached. That is the whole apparatus. It takes a tutor ten minutes a month to maintain if they are working from it, and cannot be produced at all if they are not.

faqs.question: What are the six causes of a lost mark?
faqs.answer: Content not known; content known but not recalled under pressure; question misread; command term misread; method correct but not written out; and time ran out. They have nothing in common as problems, and the instruction to revise more is the right remedy for only one of them. A tutor who hands you a count across all six after the first paper has told you more than most arrangements produce in a term, and it also tells you what not to spend hours on.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our home in Nad Al Sheba or Meydan?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Dubai's in-home market is large and publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For an evidence-led arrangement the online format adds a slot that is a start time rather than an arrival window, and work marked between sessions.

faqs.question: Why should I not read my child's mock percentage as a grade?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries are set by the board after each series has been marked, taking account of how the cohort and the paper performed, and published afterwards. A mock graded against a previous series' boundaries is an estimate, and a student two marks below a boundary is not two marks from a grade in any dependable sense. The useful output of a mock is the script and the distribution of lost marks by cause, which is stable information you can act on.

faqs.question: How quickly should I expect to see something change?
faqs.answer: It depends on the cause, which is why the count matters. Command-term discipline and unwritten method are behaviours and should move on the next marked script, within one to two weeks. Retrieval failures take two to three weeks of short frequent testing. Misread questions take one to two. Pacing takes four to six because stamina develops slowly. Content gaps are the slowest at two to four weeks per topic, which also sets a limit on what eight weeks can achieve.

faqs.question: What is the most productive fortnight in a Repton student's year?
faqs.answer: The two weeks immediately after a mock. The evidence is fresh and specific, the student's attention is briefly available, and the exact causes of lost marks are visible on a script somebody else marked. Families routinely spend that fortnight recovering from the emotional reaction to a percentage and begin the useful work three weeks later, when the specificity has faded and so has the willingness. Ask for the script back and go through it in the first week.

faqs.question: How do I use a marked internal assessment draft as evidence?
faqs.answer: Ask for both drafts and the criterion wording rather than a summary of the feedback. An internal assessment is untimed and criteria-marked, so a weakness shows up cleanly rather than tangled with pacing. In the Diploma sciences the investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. A second draft scoring in a higher band on the same criterion is readable without any subject knowledge.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment criterion cannot be fixed later?
faqs.answer: Research design, in the Diploma sciences investigation. It covers the research question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned, and once the practical work has been done it cannot be repaired. That makes the planning conversation before any data collection the highest-value single session available in the subject. The other three criteria — data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — carry eighteen of the twenty-four marks and can still be improved at drafting stage.

faqs.question: Can the Year 11 evidence help decide between the Diploma and A Levels?
faqs.answer: Yes, more usefully than reputation does. A student whose losses are mainly pacing and unwritten method tends to do better where more of the grade comes from untimed criteria-marked internal assessment. A student with concentrated content gaps in two subjects does better concentrating on three subjects taken deeper. A student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way subject tutoring cannot fix, and that is the strongest single signal either way.

faqs.question: What should I refuse to accept as progress?
faqs.answer: Four things, however sincerely reported. Improved confidence. Better engagement. A stack of completed past papers, unless each was sat to time and marked against the official scheme. And a risen predicted grade, which is an estimate against boundaries that will move. All four are pleasant, often genuine precursors to improvement, and none is a mark. The replacement is two marked pieces from different weeks with the cause counts compared.

faqs.question: Does the syllabus code matter if my child is at a single school?
faqs.answer: Very much, because schools choose their board subject by subject. Cambridge science syllabuses carry a practical component worth twenty per cent, sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper at the school's choice, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam at all. A term of preparation for a component your child is not sitting is wasted, and the mistake is invisible until results. The exams officer can confirm the code in a sentence.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child actually sit?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families imagine, used properly. One paper sat under genuine timing, marked against the official scheme and analysed for causes is worth more than five worked through casually, because the second method produces familiarity rather than improvement. In the final stretch the pattern that works is one full paper a week under timing, marked, with the counts compared against the previous week, and no new content at all in the last fortnight.

faqs.question: What if the tutor's marking disagrees with the school's?
faqs.answer: Find out why in week two rather than in June. Significant disagreement is information: it may mean the tutor is working from a different specification, applying a different mark scheme, or marking more or less generously than the examiner would. Any of those is worth resolving early, and the resolution is to compare the two markings against the official scheme for the same question. A tutor confident in their marking will welcome that comparison rather than deflect it.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule is published, so no amount is quoted.
