intro.heading: A grade is a symptom; the paper tells you the cause
paragraphs: A Year 10 report from a British curriculum school in Dubai gives a grade and a comment, and the comment is almost always true and almost never actionable. 'Needs to show more working' and 'should revise more thoroughly' describe the outcome rather than the mechanism. The mechanism is in the script: which questions were attempted, which were abandoned, which earned the first mark and lost the second, and which were answered correctly in a form the mark scheme does not accept. That distinction is the entire reason a specialist session looks different from a homework club.

At Safa British School, students move through the English National Curriculum and into the International GCSE years, where assessment changes shape rather than simply getting harder. Up to Year 9 the work is largely teacher-assessed against internal criteria, with coursework and projects carrying weight. From Year 10 the grade is decided by terminal written papers marked by an external examiner who has never met the student, applying a published scheme to the words on the page. Students who were rewarded for understanding now have to be rewarded for demonstrating it in a specific format.

That shift produces three recognisable failure modes. The first is the student who understands the physics and writes two sentences where the mark scheme wants three distinct points for three marks. The second is the student who can solve a problem but cannot set one up, so a question phrased as a context rather than an equation stalls them before the mathematics starts. The third is pace: a student who is accurate but slow loses the last question on every paper, which in Extended Mathematics is often where the highest-tariff marks sit.

There is a fourth pattern that only shows up in the sciences, and it is the one families least expect. A student can be strong on the structured theory paper and weak on the practical or alternative-to-practical component, and the overall grade hides that completely. Marks there go on axis choice, scales that ignore the grid, missing units, significant figures and anomalous points left unmarked. That is measurement and presentation discipline rather than subject knowledge, and it is almost never practised deliberately because it does not look like revision.

None of those three is fixed by covering the syllabus again. They are fixed by marking the student's own attempts against the scheme and showing them, mark by mark, where the examiner stopped awarding credit. That is slow, specific work, and it is what a weekly online session is for. IB Gram delivers tuition for Dubai families online, one-to-one, over live video, with the student's scripts on a shared screen; we do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Linear two-year courses assessed by terminal written papers, usually two or three per subject. Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is untiered in several subjects. Each paper has its own structure, duration and weighting, and the specification code on the front decides all three.

Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with inquiry and reflection built into the grade. Students arriving from MYP into the IGCSE years typically have good investigative habits and little experience of a closed-book timed paper, which is a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap.

The practical work is mapping what has already been covered against the specification and finding the topics that were never examinable in MYP.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment is criterion-marked by letter, and the written papers reward command-term precision more strictly than IGCSE. Higher Level adds a third paper in several sciences.

UAE schools sit the May session. No IB exam or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The usual sixth-form continuation for a British curriculum student. Three or four subjects in depth, with AS and A2 structures varying by board. The gap between a strong Extended grade and an A Level A is larger than the labels suggest, particularly where algebraic fluency is assumed rather than taught.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 carries the long multi-step questions where method marks live. The recurring loss is working that exists in the student's head and not on the page, so an incorrect final answer earns nothing where it should have earned most of the marks.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Circuits and electricity cost more Extended marks than any other topic. The data-handling paper is marked on axes, scales, units and significant figures, which means a student can draw a correct graph and still lose two marks on presentation.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry gate the rest of the course, so weakness there shows up as apparently unrelated errors later. Paper 4 asks for explanation in chemical language; an answer that is right in everyday words scores nothing on the explanation marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Almost all lost marks are vocabulary rather than concept. Transport, homeostasis and genetics crosses need the exact term. Students also need the habit of counting the marks and writing that many separate points, which is a technique taught in minutes and practised for months.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The summary question on the second-language paper has a mechanical scheme: find the content points, compress them, do not comment. The directed-writing task on first language is scored on audience and register. Both are coachable in a way that general reading is not.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Marks come from the level descriptors, which reward a sustained argument about how a writer creates an effect. Plot retelling, however accurate, sits in the bottom bands. The highest-yield work is building one paragraph properly and then repeating its shape under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application marks require the case study in front of the student, not a memorised firm, and evaluation marks require a judgement with a reason. Many students write good analysis and stop short of the judgement, which is the single most recoverable mark on the paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode notation, trace tables and the board's exact definitions carry the marks. Fluent Python coders often underperform because the paper wants the specification's notation rather than working code, which is a short, finite piece of work.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case studies plus skills. The extended-response question is where the level descriptors apply, so structure and a line of argument earn bands that accurate fragments cannot reach. Map and graph skills are quick wins that students rarely practise deliberately.

subjects.name: Arabic as a second language
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under KHDA's rules. Support here works from the school's own material, because substituting content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

modes.title: Weekly diagnostic hour
modes.description: One hour a week that opens on a marked piece of the student's own work. The tutor shows where credit stopped, teaches the specific technique that would have earned it, and sets one short task to be marked before the next session. Most Al Safa families start here.

modes.title: Timed paper and review pairing
modes.description: A 90-minute session in which a paper section is attempted under exam conditions, followed by a session spent marking it line by line against the published scheme. This pairing is what moves science and maths grades, because it produces evidence rather than impressions.

Line-by-line marking against the scheme
Pace measured, not guessed

modes.description: A defined number of sessions ending at a stated date, booked for the weeks before a series or around an IB Internal Assessment window. The scope is agreed in writing first, so the cost is known rather than open-ended across a term.

sections.heading: What each IGCSE component is actually built to test
paragraphs: A paper is not a random selection of questions from the syllabus. Each component has a declared job: one tests recall and short application, another tests extended reasoning, another tests experimental and data skills. A student revising for 'Chemistry' rather than for 'Chemistry Paper 4' revises the content twice and the skill not at all, which is why so much revision produces so little grade movement.

The structure below is the common Cambridge pattern for the sciences and maths at Extended tier. Exact durations and weightings vary by subject and by series, so the school's own specification copy is the reference; what does not vary is the division of labour between components. The multiple-choice paper rewards breadth and precision under time pressure. The structured theory paper rewards explanation. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper rewards method, measurement and graph discipline, and it is the component most often left unpractised.

Knowing the split changes how a session is spent. If a student's mock breakdown shows a strong theory paper and a weak practical paper, the useful work is graph axes, tabulated results, anomalous points and the language of variables, not another pass through the topic list. That diagnosis takes one session with the component marks in front of the tutor, and it frequently halves the amount of tuition a family thought they needed.

It also changes what the student practises alone. A multiple-choice paper is trained by doing many questions quickly and reviewing the wrong ones by elimination logic rather than by topic. An extended theory paper is trained by writing fewer answers and rewriting them to the scheme's shape. Treating those as the same activity is why so many students revise diligently and see the same component mark return twice in a row.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a ceiling decision, not a difficulty setting
paragraphs: Cambridge splits mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended tiers, and families routinely treat the choice as a judgement about how hard the child should be pushed. It is better understood as a ceiling. A Core entry caps the achievable grade, and no amount of excellent performance inside Core lifts a student above that cap. An Extended entry removes the cap and adds content, and a student entered at Extended who cannot access the harder material can finish with a lower grade than they would have earned in Core.

The decision is usually taken during Year 10, which means it is taken on partial evidence. The useful inputs are not confidence or effort but specific: can the student handle algebraic manipulation without a calculator, can they set up a problem from a written context, and do they finish a paper section inside the time. Those three can be measured in two sessions, and the measurement is far more reliable than a prediction made from classwork.

Where a student sits close to the boundary, the honest answer is often that the tier is the wrong lever. Moving to Core to secure a pass is a legitimate choice if the subject is not a prerequisite for the student's sixth-form plan. If it is a prerequisite, the work is to close the specific gap rather than to lower the ceiling, and that work has to start early enough in Year 10 to change the entry decision. The table sets out what actually differs.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks they quietly control
paragraphs: Every examined subject has a small vocabulary of instruction words, and each one has a defined expectation behind it. 'State' wants a fact with no reasoning. 'Describe' wants what happens without why. 'Explain' wants a causal link, and an answer without the link scores nothing however correct the description. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement supported by both sides. Students who have never been taught this read every question as an invitation to write what they know.

The cost is measurable. In a structured science paper, a six-mark question answered as description rather than explanation can lose four marks while containing no errors at all. In Business Studies, an analysis paragraph without a judgement loses the evaluation marks entirely. In Geography and History, the level descriptors on extended responses reward a sustained line of argument, so a student who writes five accurate but unconnected points sits in a lower band than one who writes three connected ones.

Some terms are board-specific, which is why the board matters even here. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own command-term expectations, and the same word can carry a slightly different demand between them. A tutor working from the correct specification teaches the definition the student's examiner will apply rather than a generic version of it, and that is a small distinction that shows up in the top band of a long answer.

This is one of the fastest things to fix, which is why it leads the work in most first terms. The method is mechanical: take the student's own answers, identify the command term, state what the term required, and rewrite one answer together to the required shape. Repeat across a handful of questions and the pattern transfers. It is not a term's work; it is usually three or four sessions, and it frequently produces the clearest single jump in a mock breakdown.
bullets: State: a fact, no reasoning, no padding
Describe: what happens, in sequence, without causes
Explain: a causal chain, which is where most marks are lost
Compare: both subjects in every sentence, not two separate accounts
Evaluate: a judgement with a reason, not a summary of both sides

sections.heading: What one session fixes, and what honestly takes a term
paragraphs: Families deserve a straight answer about scale before they commit money. Some problems are technique problems with a short tail. Answering to the mark allocation, reading command terms, laying out working so method marks survive a wrong answer, drawing a graph to the practical paper's standard, and planning the order in which to attempt a paper are all learnable inside a few sessions, because the student already holds the knowledge and is losing credit on presentation.

Other problems are content problems and they take real time. A gap in algebraic fluency underneath a maths course, an unlearned moles foundation underneath Chemistry, or two terms of missed work after a mid-year transfer cannot be compressed. Those are a term or more of weekly work, and any provider promising otherwise is describing a schedule rather than a method. The useful thing a first session does is tell you which of the two categories you are in.

Telling the two apart is not difficult once a script is on screen. A technique problem looks like correct thinking that stops earning credit partway through an answer. A content problem looks like questions left blank or started and abandoned, clustered around particular topics. The pattern is usually visible inside ten minutes, which is why we spend the first session reading evidence instead of teaching.

The third category is pace, and it sits between the two. A student who knows the material and runs out of time is not short of content or technique; they are short of fluency, which is built by repeated timed practice with marking in between. That takes weeks rather than months, but it cannot be done in a single long sitting, because fluency comes from distributed practice. Scheduling matters as much as teaching here.
bullets: Short tail: mark allocation, command terms, working layout, graph discipline
Long tail: missing algebra, missing moles, a mid-year transfer gap
Medium tail: pace, which needs distributed timed practice and marking
A first diagnostic session tells you which category applies

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: same subject, different paper
paragraphs: Dubai schools use both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, sometimes within the same building for different subjects. The subject names match and the papers do not. Tiering, the number of components, how practical skills are assessed and whether a modular route exists all vary, and a tutor working from the wrong board's past papers will teach well and prepare the student for the wrong examination.

The first thing to establish, then, is not the subject but the code. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610. Pearson's equivalents are 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1. The code appears on the front of every past paper and on the school's exam entry information. Ask the subject teacher or the exams officer, and write it down for each subject separately, because one student can sit two boards in one series.

The practical consequence for revision is specific. Past papers must match the board and the tier, or the practice misleads in both directions: a Pearson paper worked by a Cambridge Extended candidate can feel deceptively comfortable, and a Cambridge Extended paper worked by a Pearson Foundation candidate can destroy confidence for no reason. Checking the code once, at the start, removes a problem that otherwise runs quietly for a whole year.

Series availability differs too. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE centres, with the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. The Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates show the rhythm; always work from the live official timetable.

sections.heading: Mocks, past papers, and marking against the scheme
paragraphs: A past paper that is completed and not marked is practice in writing, not in examination. The value sits in the marking, and specifically in the student seeing why a sentence earned nothing. Most students in Dubai have done more past papers than they have had marked properly, which is why a mock result often surprises a family that believed revision was going well.

The productive routine is narrow. Attempt a section under genuine time pressure, with no notes and no restarts. Mark it against the published scheme, awarding only what the scheme allows, which usually feels harsh. List every lost mark by cause rather than by topic: not 'lost two marks on osmosis' but 'described where explanation was required'. Then teach to the causes, which are always fewer than the topics.

Mock season in Dubai's British curriculum schools falls in the term before the series, and it is the best diagnostic a family gets for free. Ask the school for the component breakdown rather than the overall grade. A 6 made of a strong theory paper and a weak practical paper needs different work from a 6 made of two middling papers, and the overall grade hides that completely.

Two conditions make a mock worth reading. The paper should be a real past paper rather than a teacher-written approximation, and it should be sat under genuine conditions, including the full duration. A shortened mock tells you nothing about pace, which is one of the three things it exists to measure. Where a school runs a shortened version for timetable reasons, a full paper sat at home under supervision fills the gap.

After the mock, the single most useful habit is a one-page error log kept by the student rather than by the tutor. Each entry names the question, the cause in the student's own words, and the correction. Reviewing that log before the next paper takes five minutes and catches repeat errors, which in most subjects account for more lost marks than new material does.
bullets: Attempt under real time pressure, then mark strictly to the scheme
Record lost marks by cause, not by topic
Ask the school for component breakdowns, not just the overall grade
Two identical grades can need completely different teaching

sections.heading: What the work costs, read from the bottom of the market up
paragraphs: Starting at the cheapest end is the honest way to read this market. A budget online tutor or university student in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya publishing from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, and the published bands reach about AED 150. That tier supervises homework and revises content, which helps a student who is simply not working, and does little for a technique problem on an Extended paper.

A step up, a qualified subject tutor working online sits in a market band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table landing at AED 200 to AED 450 plus. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those figures belong to the providers named; they are not an IB Gram price list.

In-home visits sit apart from that ladder because travel is inside the fee, with published bands of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tuition is a service offered only in India, and no tutor is sent to an Al Safa address. For a diagnosis-led approach the online format also has a practical advantage: the student's scripts, the mark scheme and a shared working surface sit on one screen, annotated and saved, so the record of what was fixed survives the session.
bullets: Budget tier from AED 33-65, reaching about AED 150, for supervision rather than technique
Qualified subject tutor roughly AED 150-300 online
IB and IGCSE specialist AED 200-450 and above
In-home bands AED 180-500 because the drive is inside the fee

sections.heading: Coursework, Internal Assessment and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: Part of this market sells finished work. One Dubai operator advertises completed IB Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting a purchased document is malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student, and the exposure extends to the Diploma itself. Any page discussing assessment has a duty to name that, because families comparing prices are sometimes comparing two entirely different products without realising it.

The legitimate boundary is specific and it is not restrictive in practice. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards and how marks are allocated across the letters, discusses a research question the student has proposed, reads a draft the student has written and identifies where it falls short of a criterion, and coaches the process of collecting and presenting evidence. A tutor does not write any part of a submitted text, does not edit a draft into a final version, and does not supply a topic, data set or conclusion.

The same applies to IGCSE coursework components, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. It also applies to the boards' material: syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright documents, so a tutor cites and links the official source rather than distributing copies. A provider whose offer removes the student's work rather than improving it is not cheaper; it is selling a different thing under the same name.

In scheduling terms this shapes how coursework support is booked. A useful Internal Assessment block is three to five sessions spread across the drafting window, because the student must write between them for the feedback to have anything to act on. Compressing it into one long sitting produces a conversation rather than a draft, and that is the point at which some families reach for the shortcut this section exists to warn against.
bullets: Teaching criteria and mark allocations by letter: yes
Feedback on a draft the student wrote: yes
Writing, completing or finalising any submitted text: never
Supplying a topic, data set or conclusion to adopt: never

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description
process.description: The fastest route to a useful first session is a recent mock or class paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it. The grade tells us little; the pattern of lost marks tells us almost everything. Include the subject, the specification code and the paper number.

process.title: Get the component diagnosis in writing
process.description: After the trial lesson we set out which components are weak, whether the cause is content, technique or pace, and roughly how many sessions each category needs. That written read is yours whether or not you continue, and it is specific enough to discuss with the school.

process.title: Choose the format that matches the cause
process.description: Technique problems suit a weekly diagnostic hour. Pace problems need the timed paper and review pairing. Content gaps need sustained weekly work across a term. Matching the format to the cause is what stops a family paying for the wrong kind of help.

process.title: Review against the school's own calendar
process.description: We set a review point four sessions ahead, timed to the next school assessment rather than to a month boundary. If the component marks have moved, we continue; if they have not, we change the approach or the tutor rather than continuing out of habit.

process.title: Say when the work is finished
process.description: A technique fix ends. We will tell you when the remaining gap is small enough that school teaching and independent practice will close it, because a provider that never reaches that point is not reading the evidence.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session is spent on the student's own marked work, establishing whether lost marks come from content, technique or pace. Those three need different teaching, and treating them as one is the most common reason a term of tuition changes nothing.

whyPoints.title: Specification and mark scheme, not a textbook
whyPoints.description: Tutors work from the published Cambridge and Pearson specifications and from the schemes' own wording, including the command-term definitions. The paper is what the student faces, so the paper is what the session is built around.

whyPoints.title: Component-level reporting
whyPoints.description: Feedback names the component and the cause: explanation marks lost to description on the structured paper, two marks lost to graph presentation on the practical. That is specific enough for a parent to raise at a parents' evening.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice that treats the cap as a cap
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended set different grade ceilings, and the entry decision has consequences for sixth-form prerequisites. We measure fluency, problem setup and pace rather than offering an opinion about potential.

whyPoints.title: Published boundary on coursework
whyPoints.description: Teaching criteria, explaining mark allocations and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. Never writing, completing or supplying assessed work. The boundary is written down because a nearby part of this market sells the other thing.

whyPoints.title: Online only, and said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Dubai run one-to-one over live video, with scripts, schemes and a shared working surface on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and no page here implies otherwise.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board my Safa British School child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the subject teacher or the school's exams officer for the specification code, subject by subject, because one student can sit two boards in a single series. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry, 0625 for Physics and 0610 for Biology. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1. The code appears on the front of every past paper. Booking a tutor without it risks excellent teaching aimed at the wrong paper structure, which wastes some of the money and some of the time.

faqs.question: Should my Year 10 be entered for Core or Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a ceiling decision rather than a difficulty setting. A Core entry caps the achievable grade whatever the student scores, while an Extended entry removes the cap and adds content. The useful evidence is measurable: algebraic manipulation without a calculator, the ability to set up a problem from a written context, and finishing a paper section inside the time. Two timed sessions measure those reliably. Also check whether the sixth-form course your child wants requires an Extended grade, because a Core entry can close that route quietly.

faqs.question: Why did my child score well in class and badly in the mock?
faqs.answer: Usually because classwork rewards understanding and the paper rewards demonstrating it in a specific format. Three patterns account for most of the gap: writing one point where the mark allocation offers three, answering a question that says explain as though it said describe, and running out of time before the high-tariff questions at the end. None of the three is a knowledge problem, and all three are visible in the script within a few minutes. Ask the school for the component breakdown rather than the overall grade, since that is where the cause shows.

faqs.question: What is the quickest technique fix available before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Answering to the mark allocation. If a question offers three marks, the answer needs three distinct creditable points, and most students write one well-expressed sentence instead. The habit transfers across every written subject and takes one session to teach and a few weeks to embed. The second quickest is command-term discipline: knowing that explain requires a causal link and that an answer without one scores nothing on those marks. Together they routinely account for a visible shift in a mock breakdown without any new content being learned.

faqs.question: How many marks do students really lose on the practical or alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Enough that it often decides the grade, and it is the least practised component. Marks go on axis choice and labelling, scales that do not use the grid, missing or inconsistent units, significant figures, tabulated results in the wrong order, and anomalous points left unmarked. None of that is physics, chemistry or biology knowledge; it is measurement and presentation discipline. A student can understand the experiment completely and still lose several marks on a page, which is why we practise this component separately rather than folding it into topic revision.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if my child transferred into Year 11 from an IB school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a common piece of work in this city, because several Dubai schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11. The first task is mapping what has been covered against the specification and finding the topics that were never examinable in MYP. The second is timed-paper stamina, which MYP rarely demands. Students arriving from MYP usually have strong investigative habits and little experience of closed-book papers under clock pressure, so the work is technique and selected content rather than starting the course again.

faqs.question: Is it worth doing more past papers if the grade is not moving?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. A completed, unmarked past paper is practice in writing rather than in examination, and most students have done more papers than they have had marked properly. The value sits in strict marking against the published scheme and then listing lost marks by cause instead of by topic. Recording 'described where explanation was required' is useful; recording 'lost marks on osmosis' is not. Teach to the causes, which are always fewer than the topics, and then return to papers to confirm the change held.

faqs.question: What does an online IGCSE session actually look like for an Al Safa student?
faqs.answer: The student's marked script is shared on screen alongside the relevant mark scheme, and a working surface such as a tablet or document camera shows the student's own handwriting as they work. The tutor annotates the script where credit stopped, teaches the one technique that would have earned it, then has the student redo a comparable question live. A short marked task follows before the next session. The annotated file is saved, so the record of what was fixed survives the hour rather than evaporating with it.

faqs.question: Does Safa British School's assessment calendar matter for scheduling tuition?
faqs.answer: It should drive the scheduling entirely. A British curriculum year in Dubai has three concentrated stretches: the autumn assessment window, the mock season in the new term, and the run to the June series. Work booked to land just before one of those produces evidence you can read; work booked to a calendar month does not. We set review points to the school's next assessment rather than to a date, which also makes it obvious when the tuition has done its job and can stop.

faqs.question: How does an examiner mark an explanation question differently from a description question?
faqs.answer: An explanation scheme awards credit for causal links, so each mark usually corresponds to one step in a chain of reasoning. A description scheme awards credit for the correct sequence of observable events. The practical consequence is that an answer which lists accurate facts can score zero on an explanation question while containing no errors. Students fix this by learning to write because and therefore into their answers deliberately, then checking that the number of links matches the number of marks offered on the line.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series can a Dubai candidate actually enter?
faqs.answer: The June series and the November series. Cambridge offers the February/March series to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, and any page quoting a February exam window to a Gulf parent is giving them a date that does not apply. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Work from the school's own timetable copy.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my child's Extended Essay draft without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clearer than most families expect. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain how marks are allocated, discuss a research question the student has proposed, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short of a criterion, and coach the process of finding and presenting evidence. A tutor may not write any part of the submitted text, edit a draft into its final state, or supply a topic, data set or conclusion. One Dubai operator advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is malpractice and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: What do the mandatory UAE subjects mean for a British curriculum timetable?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are taught in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for, so they appear on the timetable and in reports without appearing on any Cambridge specification. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arab students in those subjects. Instructional time runs in 40-minute lesson units, and content cannot be substituted without prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: How much tuition does a technique problem actually need in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. Answering to the mark allocation, reading command terms, laying out working so method marks survive a wrong answer, and practical-paper presentation are learnable in a handful of sessions, because the student already holds the knowledge. Content gaps are different: missing algebraic fluency or an unlearned moles foundation is a term or more of weekly work. Pace sits between the two and needs distributed timed practice with marking in between. A first diagnostic session tells you which of the three you are paying to fix.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-safa-british-sc.closingHeading: Send the script and get the cause named
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-safa-british-sc.closingBody: The useful next step is not a conversation about grades, it is a look at a paper. Send a recent marked script with the subject, the specification code and the paper number, and take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the subject. You will get the component breakdown, the cause of each cluster of lost marks, and an honest estimate of how much work each cause needs, including the frequent answer that one of them needs almost none. From there you can decide whether to book weekly, book a block, or simply take the diagnosis back to the school.

intro.heading: Bilingual study changes the tutoring question and the price of it
paragraphs: Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits at Al Jaddaf and runs the International Baccalaureate as a continuum with bilingual streams, which produces a tutoring problem no monolingual school generates. A student may be studying a science in a second language, taking two languages at A level of the programme rather than one, or carrying a language acquisition course that is well below or well above where their actual fluency sits. None of those is a difficulty with the subject. They are structural, they are diagnosable, and the market prices them very differently from mathematics.

That is the first thing worth saying about cost. Subject tutoring in Dubai has deep supply and therefore competitive pricing: published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Language work inside a bilingual programme has thinner supply, because the pool is not people who speak French or German but people who have taught a Diploma language A course or a Diploma science in that language. That narrows the field sharply, and scarcity shows up as a longer wait more often than as a surcharge.

The second thing is that the bilingual route has a real academic prize attached and families often do not know what it requires. A Bilingual Diploma can be awarded on more than one basis, and the routes involve either two languages studied at A level of the programme, or a group three or group four subject completed in a language other than the student's language A. The exact current requirements should be confirmed with the school's coordinator, because they are specific and they decide whether a subject choice made in Year 11 produces the award or not.

IB Gram supports SISD families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that statement appears on every country page this site publishes. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. For a boarding student or a weekly commuter the comparison barely applies, which is one of the reasons this page treats boarding as its own section rather than a footnote.

Two absences, both deliberate. No statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because making one responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none here; ask any provider in writing whether a figure is inclusive. And no IB session or results date, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project. Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session; take every date from the school rather than from any tutoring page, this one included.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-swiss-internati.programmesIntro: A continuum school with bilingual streams produces four distinct tutoring situations. The price and the availability differ across all four, which is why naming the situation precisely matters before anything is booked.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme, bilingual
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examinations, ending in the Exhibition. In a bilingual stream a child is building literacy in two languages simultaneously, which is a strength over time and produces temporary asymmetries that look like weakness in one of them.
programmes.countryNote: Tutoring here is the cheapest in the whole arc and the most often skipped. The useful work is literacy in the weaker language and the ability to explain an answer in writing, because inquiry-based assessment rewards justification in prose. A gap left here reappears in the Middle Years criteria on communication and later in a Diploma language A course.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, bilingual
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with a Personal Project in the final year marked out of 24. Language acquisition is assessed by phase rather than by year group, across listening, reading, speaking and writing.
programmes.countryNote: Phase placement is the single most common fixable problem in a bilingual Middle Years programme. A student placed below their fluency coasts and learns little; one placed above it loses marks that have nothing to do with ability. Ask the school which phase your child is in and why, before concluding that anything needs tutoring at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, with the bilingual option
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum. A Bilingual Diploma is available on specific bases involving either two languages at A level of the programme or a subject completed in another language.
programmes.countryNote: The decision that produces or forecloses the bilingual award is made on the subject form at the end of Year 11, and families frequently sign it without knowing the requirement. Ask the coordinator to confirm the current basis in writing before the form goes back, because reversing a subject choice after the first term is disruptive and sometimes not possible.

programmes.name: IGCSE, for students crossing in or out
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with tiering, and a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. Nothing in it resembles criterion-based marking or phase-based language assessment, so a crossing in either direction is a genuine adjustment rather than a change of timetable.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's sector is large enough that families move between systems regularly: 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25. A bilingual continuum student moving into IGCSE needs timed paper technique urgently and may also need to choose between a first-language and a foreign-language entry in their second language, which are separate qualifications.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-swiss-internati.subjectsIntro: Below, the subjects a bilingual household most often asks about, each with the structural note that determines what tutoring should do and how easily it can be staffed.

subjects.name: Language A: Literature
subjects.levels: HL and SL, in English, French or German
subjects.description: Studied as a first language, assessed through written papers and an oral component. A student taking two language A courses carries two sets of set texts and two oral components, which is a workload fact that families underestimate when the bilingual award is the goal.

subjects.name: Language A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level runs Paper 1 at thirty-five per cent, Paper 2 at thirty-five and the Individual Oral at thirty; Higher Level adds the HL Essay at twenty. The dominant Paper 1 loss is identifying a technique rather than analysing its effect, which is a sentence-level fix.

subjects.name: Language acquisition: French B, German B, Arabic B
subjects.description: Assessed across receptive, productive and interactive skills. Placement is the first thing to check: ab initio, B at Standard and B at Higher are different courses, and being in the wrong one is a common and fixable cause of apparent underperformance.

subjects.name: Sciences taught in a second language
subjects.description: The content is the standard Diploma science — Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, the investigation at twenty with a 3,000-word cap. The difficulty is usually vocabulary and command terms in the second language rather than the science, and that distinction changes the tutor you need.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level two papers at forty per cent each plus the Exploration at twenty; Higher Level three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty plus the Exploration at twenty. Paper 3 at Higher Level is the least practised component in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure, with modelling and statistics in place of the heavier pure content. Modelling answers require a written interpretation in context, which is harder in a second language and is where bilingual students lose avoidable marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Energetics, organic mechanisms and sign conventions carry the Higher Level losses. Where these are taught in a second language the first diagnostic should separate vocabulary failures from conceptual ones, because the two have completely different remedies.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The heaviest content load in the group, so most of the gain comes from systematic retrieval rather than explanation. Command-term compliance is the largest single avoidable loss, and it is harder for a student working in their second language.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Economics portfolios are three commentaries of no more than 800 words each on real published articles; Business Management adds a pre-released case at Higher Level. Both reward precise technical vocabulary, which makes them demanding second-language subjects.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition by phase
subjects.description: Assessed in four skills, each out of eight, with phase rather than year group setting expectations. A student can look broadly competent while one skill carrying a quarter of the grade sits well below the others, and speaking is usually that skill.

sections.heading: What a Bilingual Diploma actually requires, and when the decision is made
paragraphs: The Bilingual Diploma is a real distinction and families at bilingual schools frequently pursue it without knowing the requirement, which means the decision gets made by accident on a subject form. The award can be obtained on more than one basis. One route involves completing two languages studied at A level of the programme. Another involves completing a group three or group four subject — an individuals and societies subject, or a science — in a language other than the student's nominated language A. There is also a route through the Extended Essay in a second language A.

Those are not interchangeable in workload. Two languages A means two sets of set texts, two written paper sets and two oral components, carried alongside four other subjects and the core. Completing a science in a second language means one extra layer of difficulty on an existing subject rather than an extra subject. For some students the first is natural and the second would be punishing; for others it is the reverse. Nothing about this is obvious from the outside, which is why it should be discussed before the form rather than after.

The practical instruction is narrow and important: ask the coordinator to confirm the current basis for the award in writing, and to say which of your child's provisional subject choices would satisfy it. Requirements are specific and they are periodically revised, so a figure or a rule read on a third-party page — including this one — is not a safe planning basis. The school holds the version that governs the cohort.

Where tutoring fits is in making the chosen route survivable. If the route is two languages A, the workload needs managing and the oral components need rehearsing, because they are rehearsable and students rarely do it. If the route is a subject in a second language, the early work is technical vocabulary and command terms in that language, which is a four to six session job rather than a two-year commitment. Both are cheap compared with abandoning the route in Year 13.

sections.heading: Why language work is priced and staffed differently from subject work
paragraphs: Dubai's subject tutoring market is deep, and depth means competitive pricing. The emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, and a sector that size employs many subject teachers. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on published rates read in October 2026, with named IB specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more and a single provider publishing AED 650.

Language work inside a Diploma programme is a different market, and the reason is not prestige. The relevant pool is not people who speak French or German. It is people who have taught a Diploma language A course, or a Diploma science in that language, and who know the assessment: the oral components, the set-text requirements, the criteria. That is a much smaller group than the set of fluent speakers, and it is smaller again for German than for French in this region. Scarcity in a deep market usually shows up as a waiting period rather than a premium, which is a better outcome for a family and a worse one for a deadline.

The implication is that language requests should be made earlier and specified more precisely than subject requests. Say which language, which course and level, and whether the need is the language itself or a subject taught in it. Those three facts determine whether a match exists at all. A vague request for a French tutor produces a fluent speaker; a precise request for somebody who has taught French A: Language and Literature at Standard Level produces either the right person or an honest no.

There is also a cheaper possibility that gets missed. A substantial share of what looks like a language problem in a bilingual science or mathematics class is technical vocabulary and command terms, not fluency. That is a four to six session block with a subject specialist who works in the language, rather than a two-year engagement with a language teacher. The first diagnostic should distinguish the two, and asking for that distinction explicitly is worth doing before any package is bought.

sections.heading: Separating a language problem from a subject problem
paragraphs: This is the diagnostic that matters most in a bilingual household and it is rarely done. A student losing marks in a science taught in their second language has one of three problems, and they need completely different responses. Either they do not understand the science. Or they understand it and lack the technical vocabulary to express it in the language of assessment. Or they understand it, have the vocabulary, and are misreading command terms in that language, which is a specific and narrow failure.

Distinguishing them takes one session and a marked script. Give the student the same question in both languages. If the answer is correct in the stronger language and wrong in the weaker one, the science is intact and the problem is linguistic. If it is wrong in both, the science is the problem and language is a secondary issue. If the answer is correct in substance but addresses the wrong command — describing where the paper asked for an explanation — then the fault is command-term recognition in that language, which is the cheapest of the three to fix.

That third case is more common than families expect, because command terms are a small closed vocabulary that carries disproportionate weight. Explain, evaluate, analyse, discuss, justify, compare and outline each specify what an answer must do, and the mark scheme is built around that specification. A student who knows the science and misreads the command writes something true and scores a fraction. In a second language that misreading is more likely and equally fixable: an hour sorting past questions by command term in the language of assessment moves marks quickly.

The reason to insist on this diagnostic before buying a package is financial as well as pedagogical. The linguistic and command-term cases are four to six session blocks. The conceptual case is a term of weekly subject teaching. Buying the second when you needed the first is one of the more expensive mistakes available in a bilingual programme, and nobody will stop you making it.
bullets: Same question in both languages: the fastest diagnostic available
Correct in the stronger language only means the science is intact
Wrong command in a correct answer means command-term recognition

sections.heading: Boarding and weekly commuting: what changes and what does not
paragraphs: A boarding student is in a different logistical position from a day student, and in some respects a better one. The hours are structured: boarding houses have study periods, and a fixed online session inside one of them is usually straightforward to arrange with house staff, though it needs asking rather than assuming. Once arranged, that slot is more reliable than any day student's, because nothing depends on an afternoon commute across Dubai.

What boarding changes is the parent's visibility. A day student's parent hears about a bad week; a boarding parent often does not until a report. That makes the written evidence trail more important rather than less: a risk list from the first diagnostic, updated monthly, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work attached. Ask for it monthly and read it, because it replaces the informal signal that a day family gets for free.

Weekly commuting, for families based outside Dubai or travelling between the UAE and elsewhere, changes which days are usable rather than removing them. A student travelling at the start and end of the week has three reliable evenings rather than five, and the slot should sit in the middle of that window rather than at either edge. Travel abroad is handled as a one-off time adjustment rather than a cancelled term, which is the practical advantage of an online arrangement over a travelling tutor.

What does not change in either case is the internal deadline calendar. Internal assessment and core deadlines are set by the school, arrive in clusters, and land hardest in the autumn of the final Diploma year alongside mocks. They do not pause for a travel week or a boarding routine. Ask the coordinator for the whole calendar at the start of the first Diploma year, and agree in advance what sessions will contain during a cluster: process coaching on the piece that is due rather than subject teaching that competes with it.

sections.heading: Where a continuum student's language weakness hides
paragraphs: In a bilingual continuum there is no terminal examination until the final two years, which means a language asymmetry can persist for a long time without producing a visible result. It still produces marks, though, and they are visible in the Middle Years criterion breakdown if anybody looks. That document is the early-warning system, and most families never ask for it.

In language acquisition the assessment divides across listening, reading, speaking and writing, each marked out of eight, with phase rather than year group setting expectations. A student can look broadly competent while one skill carrying a quarter of the grade sits well below the others. Speaking is usually that skill, because it is least practised in a classroom and most uncomfortable to practise alone. It is also the most improvable in a short run of focused sessions, which makes it a good first target.

In subject groups taught in a second language the hiding place is criterion communicating, where it exists, or the equivalent descriptor about using appropriate terminology. A student who understands the material and cannot express it in the language of instruction scores well on knowing and understanding and poorly on communicating, which averages to an unremarkable grade and conceals a specific, fixable problem. The remedy is terminology and written structure, not more content.

The first thing to check before any of this, however, is placement. Being in the wrong phase or the wrong course — ab initio rather than B, or B at Standard rather than Higher — is a common and entirely fixable cause of apparent underperformance, and it costs nothing to establish. Ask the school which phase or course your child is in and on what basis, and ask whether a change is possible. That question has resolved more apparent language problems than any amount of tutoring.

sections.heading: Market bands, and the five questions that settle a price
paragraphs: For completeness, the published bands read in October 2026. Budget online platforms and university-student tutors between roughly AED 45 and 150 an hour, some entry rates quoted from AED 33. A qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, with one agency publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel at roughly AED 180 to 500. One provider publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages advertised include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those belong to the providers that published them. Three of the six pages competing for searches like this one publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no Dubai family budgets in. They are reproduced here so that a parent has a reference range, not as an endorsement of anybody. IB Gram's own figure follows the free trial lesson and depends on subject, level, language and frequency, which is why a single number would mislead.

Five questions settle almost any price conversation and should be answered in writing. Does the figure include VAT. Is the rate per hour or per session, and how long is a session. What happens if we stop after one month. Who marks work between sessions, in which language, and is that time inside the rate. And what happens if the matched tutor becomes unavailable, including whether the written risk list hands over.

For a bilingual household add a sixth: in which language will work be marked and feedback given. A tutor marking a French A essay in English is giving feedback the student then has to translate, which loses most of its value. It sounds like a small point and it is the difference between useful marking and decorative marking.

sections.heading: What this page will not claim
paragraphs: No statement about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because making one responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none here. No fine amount for unpermitted tutoring, because the ministry published no schedule and the figure circulating online could not be verified. No IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency, because no official source for one could be read; the British-track figures are published and the IB one is not. No IB examination or results date, because the organisation's own site could not be checked. No star rating, satisfaction percentage or student count, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method.

On permits, the relevant fact is that the cost is zero. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

On assessed work the line is authorship and it is not negotiable. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so the words become theirs. The caps are 4,000 words on the Extended Essay, 1,600 on the Theory of Knowledge essay, 950 on the exhibition commentary, 3,000 on the sciences investigation and 800 per Economics commentary.

And position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, and has no arrangement with any school named on this page.

sections.heading: Getting started in a bilingual household
paragraphs: Three pieces of information, all free, make a sensible start possible. The phase or course your child is placed in for each language, and on what basis. The criterion breakdown behind the most recent reported grade in the subject that worries you, not the grade itself. And for a Diploma student, the coordinator's internal deadline calendar plus written confirmation of the current basis for a Bilingual Diploma if that award is the goal.

Then specify the request precisely, because in language work precision is what determines whether a match exists. Which language, which course and level, and whether the need is the language itself or a subject taught in it. A vague request produces a fluent speaker; a precise one produces either the right specialist or an honest statement that nobody is available in the slot you want, which is more useful than a substitution.

Then run the diagnostic that separates the three cases: conceptual, vocabulary, or command-term recognition. Same question in both languages, plus a marked script. Two of the three are a four to six session block rather than a term of weekly teaching, and buying the wrong one is the main way money disappears in a bilingual programme.

The limit, stated once more. No tutor is sent to an Al Jaddaf address or anywhere else in the UAE; lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a boarding student that is the only practical arrangement anyway, and for a day student in a city with heavy afternoon traffic it means the slot is a start time rather than an arrival window. The reason to choose it here is narrower than convenience: a bilingual Diploma request needs somebody who has taught that course in that language, and that pool is defined by competence rather than by distance.

process.title: Check placement before assuming anything needs tutoring
process.description: Which phase or course your child sits in for each language, and on what basis. Ab initio, B at Standard and B at Higher are different courses, and a Middle Years phase is set by capability rather than year group. Wrong placement is common, free to establish and often the whole problem.

process.title: Confirm the Bilingual Diploma basis in writing
process.description: Ask the coordinator which of your child's provisional subject choices would satisfy the current requirement, before the Year 11 subject form goes back. Requirements are specific and periodically revised, so the school holds the version that governs the cohort rather than any third-party page.

process.title: Specify the language request precisely
process.description: Which language, which course, which level, and whether the need is the language itself or a subject taught in it. A vague request produces a fluent speaker. A precise one produces the right specialist or an honest no, and in a narrow pool an honest no is more useful than a substitution.

process.title: Run the three-way diagnostic first
process.description: The same question in both languages plus a marked script, to separate a conceptual gap from a vocabulary gap from a command-term misreading. Two of those three are a four to six session block rather than a term of teaching, and buying the wrong one is the expensive mistake here.

process.title: Ask in which language work will be marked
process.description: A French A essay marked in English gives feedback the student has to translate, which loses most of its value. It sounds minor and it is the difference between useful marking and decorative marking. Add it to the five standard price questions before agreeing anything.

process.title: For boarders, insist on the monthly written trail
process.description: A boarding parent does not get the informal weekly signal a day parent gets for free, so the risk list from the diagnostic, updated monthly with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work attached, is the replacement. Ask for it and read it.

whyPoints.title: Bilingual problems treated as structural, not as weakness
whyPoints.description: Wrong phase placement, a subject taught in a second language, two language A courses carried at once. None of those is a difficulty with the subject, all are diagnosable, and the first one is free to check and frequently the entire explanation.

whyPoints.title: The Bilingual Diploma decision flagged before the form
whyPoints.description: The routes differ enormously in workload: two languages A is the heaviest, a science in a second language is one extra layer. The decision is made on the Year 11 subject form and reversing it later is disruptive, so it deserves a session rather than an assumption.

whyPoints.title: Language supply described honestly
whyPoints.description: The pool is people who have taught the course in that language, not fluent speakers, and it is narrower again for German than for French in this region. In a deep market scarcity shows up as a waiting period, which is why language requests need making earlier and specifying better.

whyPoints.title: The three-way diagnostic before any package
whyPoints.description: Conceptual, vocabulary, or command-term recognition. Two of the three are short blocks and one is a term of teaching, so the diagnostic determines whether you are spending four sessions or forty. Nobody will stop you buying the wrong one.

whyPoints.title: Boarding handled as its own logistical case
whyPoints.description: A session inside a study period is more reliable than any day student's slot once house staff have agreed it, but the parent loses the informal weekly signal. The written monthly trail replaces it, and asking for it matters more for a boarder than for anybody else.

whyPoints.title: Sourced figures only, and the absences stated
whyPoints.description: No VAT assertion, no fine amount, no IB equivalency threshold, no IB examination date, no star rating. Each is absent because it could not be sourced, and on a page that quotes money the absences are the most informative part.

faqs.question: What does a Bilingual Diploma require at a school like SISD?
faqs.answer: The award can be obtained on more than one basis: completing two languages studied at A level of the programme, completing a group three or group four subject in a language other than the nominated language A, or in some cases through an Extended Essay in a second language A. The routes differ enormously in workload. Ask the coordinator to confirm the current basis in writing and to say which of your child's provisional subject choices would satisfy it, before the Year 11 form goes back.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a tutor for a Diploma subject taught in French or German?
faqs.answer: Yes, and not because of prestige. The relevant pool is not fluent speakers but people who have taught that Diploma course in that language and know its assessment, which is a much smaller group, and smaller again for German than for French in this region. In a market as deep as Dubai's, that scarcity usually appears as a waiting period rather than a premium. Specify the language, course and level precisely, and expect either the right person or an honest no.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to homes in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For a boarding student the comparison barely applies, and for a day student the online slot is a start time rather than an arrival window.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's problem is the science or the language?
faqs.answer: Give them the same question in both languages and look at a marked script. Correct in the stronger language and wrong in the weaker one means the science is intact and the problem is linguistic. Wrong in both means the science is the issue. Correct in substance but answering the wrong command — describing where the paper asked for an explanation — means command-term recognition in that language, which is the cheapest of the three to fix.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest fix for a bilingual student losing marks in a science?
faqs.answer: Usually a four to six session block on technical vocabulary and command terms in the language of assessment, delivered by a subject specialist who works in that language. Command terms are a small closed vocabulary carrying disproportionate weight: explain, evaluate, analyse, discuss, justify, compare and outline each specify what an answer must do, and the mark scheme is built around that. Sorting past questions by command term in that language moves marks quickly and cheaply.

faqs.question: Why should I check my child's language phase first?
faqs.answer: Because wrong placement is common, free to establish and frequently the entire explanation for apparent underperformance. Middle Years language acquisition is assessed by phase rather than by year group, and in the Diploma ab initio, B at Standard and B at Higher are different courses. A student placed below their fluency coasts and learns little; one placed above it loses marks that have nothing to do with ability. Ask the school which placement applies and on what basis.

faqs.question: Which language skill is usually weakest in a bilingual programme?
faqs.answer: Speaking, in most cases. Language acquisition divides across listening, reading, speaking and writing, each marked out of eight, so a student can look broadly competent while one skill carrying a quarter of the grade sits well below the others. Speaking is least practised in a classroom and most uncomfortable to practise alone, which is exactly why it is also the most improvable in a short run of focused sessions against the published criteria.

faqs.question: How does tutoring work for a boarding student at SISD?
faqs.answer: Sessions sit inside study periods, which needs arranging with house staff rather than assuming, and once agreed the slot is more reliable than any day student's because nothing depends on an afternoon commute. What changes is the parent's visibility: a boarding parent does not get the informal weekly signal. The replacement is the written trail — a risk list from the first diagnostic, updated monthly with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work attached.

faqs.question: In which language should work between sessions be marked?
faqs.answer: The language of assessment, and it is worth making explicit before agreeing anything. A French A essay marked in English gives feedback the student then has to translate, which loses most of its value, and the same applies to a science taught in German. It sounds like a small administrative point and it is the difference between marking that changes a script and marking that decorates it. Add the question to the standard five about price.

faqs.question: Is carrying two languages A as well as four other subjects realistic?
faqs.answer: For some students yes, and for others it is punishing, and the difference is not simply ability. Two languages A means two sets of set texts, two written paper sets and two oral components alongside four other subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. A student who manages deadlines well may find it stimulating; one who does not will find the combination unmanageable in the final year. It is worth one session of honest comparison before the subject form.

faqs.question: What does subject tutoring cost for a Dubai bilingual household?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, named IB specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 500, and budget platforms between AED 45 and 150, with one provider publishing AED 650. Those belong to the providers that published them. Language work inside a Diploma sits in the specialist band, where availability rather than price is usually the constraint.

faqs.question: Do internal deadlines change for a travelling or boarding family?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the point worth planning around. Internal assessment and core deadlines are set by the school, arrive in clusters, and land hardest in the autumn of the final Diploma year alongside mock examinations. They do not pause for a travel week or a boarding routine. Ask the coordinator for the whole internal calendar at the start of the first Diploma year, and agree in advance that sessions during a cluster will coach the piece that is due rather than teach competing content.

faqs.question: Can a bilingual student's Extended Essay be written in their second language?
faqs.answer: In some circumstances it can, and it is one of the routes associated with bilingual recognition, but the current requirement should be confirmed with the coordinator rather than assumed from any third-party page. What tutoring can legitimately do either way is narrow: explain the criteria in the board's published wording, help turn a broad question into one the available sources support, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses. The 4,000-word cap applies regardless of language.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after a month of bilingual support?
faqs.answer: Which of the three problems was being worked on — concept, vocabulary or command-term recognition — what the baseline was, and two marked pieces from different weeks in the language of assessment so the change is visible in the text. If the target was a command-term misreading or vocabulary, something should have moved inside two to three weeks. A conceptual gap moves at roughly two to four weeks per topic, so expect less and ask which topics closed.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-swiss-internati.closingHeading: Check the placement, confirm the route, then run the diagnostic
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-swiss-internati.closingBody: For a bilingual household the order saves money. Establish which phase or course your child sits in for each language and on what basis, because wrong placement is common and free to check. Then run the three-way diagnostic that separates a conceptual gap from a vocabulary gap from a command-term misreading, because two of those three are a short block rather than a term. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to an Al Jaddaf address.
