sections.heading: Drafts as evidence, without crossing the line
paragraphs: Internal assessment is worth about a fifth of most diploma subject grades and it is produced over weeks, which makes it the most evidence-rich part of the whole system and the part where the academic-honesty boundary matters most. The evidence you want is a trail of the student's own decisions: a planning note, an early draft, feedback given as questions and criterion references, and a later draft where the student has acted on some of it and ignored the rest.

That last detail is the tell. A genuine trail shows a student exercising judgement, including judgement a tutor disagreed with. A manufactured one shows each piece of feedback implemented perfectly, in a register that does not match the student's other writing. Schools notice the second kind, and the consequence of a malpractice finding lands on the student rather than on whoever supplied the text.

So the rules here are firm and they also happen to produce better evidence. A tutor reads the criteria with the student and explains what each letter rewards. A tutor models technique on different material, never on the student's own task. A tutor responds to a draft the student wrote in their own words. A tutor helps build a timeline against the school's internal deadlines. Nobody writes, restructures to completion or submits anything, and one provider in this search result sells completed internal assessments outright, which is the clearest available signal to go elsewhere.

For middle-years students the equivalent is the personal project journal, where the reflecting criterion carries eight marks and cannot be awarded from a thin record. Coaching a student to log as they go is legitimate, useful and entirely their own work, and it is the single cheapest set of marks on this page to protect.

A real trail shows the student accepting some feedback and rejecting some
Feedback belongs in questions and criterion references, not in sentences to paste

sections.heading: What a weekly note should actually contain
paragraphs: A session note is four sentences and takes two minutes to write, which is why its absence is informative. It should say what was worked on, what the student got wrong and why, what was set for next time, and whether the three named errors are moving. That is it. Anything longer is usually padding and anything shorter is usually a receipt.

What a note should not contain: adjectives about attitude without evidence, a grade prediction, a request for more hours in place of a diagnosis, or a summary of what the tutor explained rather than what the student produced. The last of those is the commonest and the most misleading, because a note describing excellent explanations of trigonometry tells you nothing about whether your child can now do trigonometry under a clock.

Over a term these notes do work that nothing else does. They let you answer the four-week and twelve-week tests honestly. They hand a replacement tutor a diagnosis on day one, which in a market where mid-year changes are routine is worth more than loyalty to any individual. And they let you walk into a Dubai consultation evening with dates, scripts and a sentence that names a specific loss, which is a different conversation from a worried parent describing a feeling.

Ask for the notes in writing, in a form you can keep, and read them. A provider who sends them and a parent who never opens them end up in the same place as a provider who sends nothing, and the four-week test cannot be run from memory.

sections.heading: Six questions that expose a tutor with no evidence
paragraphs: Ask these before the first paid hour, to every provider you are considering, including us. They take a tutor thirty seconds each to answer if the answers exist, and they are unanswerable if they do not. That asymmetry is the whole value: you are not testing charm, you are testing whether a working method is in place.

Watch for the shape of the deflection rather than the content. Pointing at a testimonial instead of a script, offering a free consultation instead of answering, listing qualifications instead of describing the method, or quoting an unverifiable success statistic are all the same move. A statistic without a number of students, a date and a method behind it is not evidence, and in a market where competitors publish satisfaction percentages nobody can reproduce, treating those claims as noise is simply accurate.

The flip side is worth saying. A tutor who answers all six plainly, admits the limits of what they can promise, and offers one anonymised marked script is demonstrating the thing you are actually buying. We hold no regulator or examination-board accreditation, we do not describe tutors as examiners, and nobody here will predict a grade before teaching your child. What we will do is produce the week-four list and the twelve-week tally.

If you are hiring a visiting tutor locally instead, the same six questions apply unchanged, plus two more: ask for identification and for confirmation of the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is issued free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those two are about compliance rather than teaching, and they are reasonable to ask of anyone.

sections.heading: Using the file at a Dubai parents' evening
paragraphs: The evidence file has a second job that families rarely plan for: it changes what the school can do for you. Dubai Year 11 and Year 12 classes are large and teachers are triaging. A parent describing a worry is one of twenty-five such conversations in an evening. A parent arriving with four dated scripts and one specific sentence is giving a head of department something they can act on inside the school's own processes.

Three things it can open up. A tier or set review, where entries for Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, close months before the exam and are moved on evidence rather than on confidence. A second look at a predicted grade, which is a professional judgement a teacher is entitled to revisit when new marked work exists. And clarity on a coursework or internal assessment deadline, where seeing the draft trail tells a teacher the student is working rather than drifting.

How to do it well: bring no more than four scripts, have the sentence ready, and ask a question rather than making a case. Our daughter is losing method marks on structured algebra; here are four papers; what would you want to see before reviewing her tier? That phrasing puts the school in charge of its own decision, which is both appropriate and far more effective than arriving with a demand or a tutor's opinion attached.

What not to do: never present a tutor's prediction as a forecast the school should adopt, never imply any provider can influence an entry, a boundary or an equivalency decision, and never let a tutoring arrangement become a reason to disengage from the school. The teacher who sets the work and knows the cohort remains the most important adult in this picture, and the file exists to inform them, not to argue with them.

process.title: Send a recent marked paper
process.description: A photograph of the last marked script or piece of work, with the specification code and level, is worth more than any description of the problem. It lets the tutor arrive at the free lesson already knowing where to look, and it is the first item in your evidence folder.

process.title: A free first lesson, no card details
process.description: One full lesson at no charge with no payment method taken. Judge it on one question: did your child's own work appear on the screen and did they spend most of the hour producing something. The note that follows should describe their work, not the tutor's plan.

process.title: Week four: the ranked list
process.description: Three named causes of mark loss from your child's own work, in priority order, each labelled content, method or timing, with a realistic estimate of how long each takes to close. This is the deliverable to judge the arrangement on, and it is why the first month is worth paying for even if nothing follows it.

process.title: A marked cycle and a timed paper
process.description: An hour taught, about thirty minutes of marked work between sessions, and a full timed paper every two or three weeks with minutes recorded per question. That cadence is what fills the twelve-week ledger, and the ledger is what tells you whether to continue.

process.title: Week twelve: closure, not activity
process.description: We review the error tally across every dated script and say plainly whether the three named errors are cheaper than they were. If they are not, we change the diagnosis or the tutor rather than adding hours, and we tell you which we think it is.

whyPoints.title: Evidence, in writing, by default
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts keyed to mark-scheme wording, timing data per question, a four-sentence note after every session, and a ranked diagnosis by week four. All of it dated, all of it yours to keep and to show the school.

whyPoints.title: Progress reported in marks and errors
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries move between series, so nobody here converts a mark into a confident grade or issues a prediction. What we report is the cost of named errors across comparable papers, which is the only measure that holds up.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops being a filter
whyPoints.description: Over video, the near-me question collapses to a question about the hour of the evening. That leaves specification match, marking quality and written output as the things you are choosing between, which is where the grade actually lives.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what evidence cannot do
whyPoints.description: A file does not change a boundary, an entry, a prediction or an equivalency decision, and no provider can. What it can do is give a head of department something concrete to act on inside the school's own processes.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. We hold no regulator or board accreditation, and we publish no success statistics we cannot evidence.

whyPoints.title: The work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: On internal assessment and coursework, feedback comes as questions and criterion references on a draft they wrote. A trail showing their own judgement is both the only legitimate kind and the better evidence.

faqs.question: Does it genuinely matter whether a tutor lives near us in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It matters for exactly one thing: whether an in-home session reliably happens on a school night, given what the roads do between five and seven. It does not affect whether the tutor has taught your child's specification, whether they mark to the board's scheme, or whether anything useful arrives in writing between sessions. Those three decide the grade. For mainstream subjects a nearby tutor costs you nothing; for scarce codes and Higher Level sciences, insisting on proximity means selecting from a very short list, which is how families end up with a generalist.

faqs.question: What should I have in my hands after four weeks of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three named causes of mark loss from your child's own work, ranked in priority order, each labelled content, method or timing, with a rough estimate of how long each takes to close. Plus at least one annotated script showing marks awarded and withheld at specific points, and a short note after each session. If what you have instead is a general sense that things are going well, the arrangement has not produced anything yet, and adding hours will not fix that.

faqs.question: How do I read the annotations on a marked script if I do not know the subject?
faqs.answer: Four checks need no subject knowledge. Count blanks and unfinished final questions, which indicate timing rather than knowledge. Look for correct answers with no working in subjects where method is credited, because those are the cheapest marks to recover. Read the long answers and see whether sentences connect or merely sit beside each other. Then check whether the same topic appears in the lost column across several papers. Finally, judge the marking itself: credible annotation quotes the scheme and names the mark that was missed.

faqs.question: My child jumped two grades in a mock. Should I believe it?
faqs.answer: Probably not as a sustainable change. Two grades in three weeks is usually a paper-difficulty effect or luck with topics, and the honest response is to re-test on a comparable paper before treating it as real. That is not cynicism: the same caution applies to a sudden drop, which causes a great deal of unnecessary panic in Dubai mock seasons. Durable progress looks slower and duller: the cost of a named error falling across dated scripts, fewer blanks at the end, better minutes per question.

faqs.question: How often should I receive a written update?
faqs.answer: After every session, and it should be four sentences: what was worked on, what the student got wrong and why, what was set for next time, and whether the three named errors are moving. Longer than that is usually padding. What a note should never contain is a grade prediction, adjectives about attitude with no evidence behind them, or a summary of what the tutor explained rather than what your child produced. That last one is the commonest and the most misleading.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give me a predicted grade for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of one who offers. Predicted grades are issued by the school as a professional judgement for university applications, and no tutor has the standing or the cohort data to produce one. What a tutor can legitimately do is report marks on comparable papers, the cost of named errors over time, and timing data, and note that grade boundaries move between series so a mark does not convert cleanly. If the school is reconsidering a prediction, that file is exactly what a teacher reviews.

faqs.question: What evidence does a Dubai school actually accept for a tier review?
faqs.answer: Marked work at the tier you are asking for, dated, and ideally four pieces rather than one. A head of department deciding between Foundation and Higher, or Core and Extended, is weighing whether a student can access the harder paper without collapsing, and the only persuasive answer is scripts from the harder paper. Bring no more than four, have one specific sentence ready, and ask what else they would want to see rather than making a case. Entries close months before the exam, so raise it in the autumn term.

faqs.question: How do I know the improvement is not just easier papers?
faqs.answer: Insist on comparability and on error tracking. Two papers from the same board, same tier and similar vintage give a usable comparison; a mark from an unspecified source does not. More reliably, track the cost of the three named errors across every dated script: if marks lost to missing working fell from eleven to four across four papers, that is real regardless of paper difficulty. Score alone is the weakest measure available, which is why progress should be reported in errors and marks rather than in a single number.

faqs.question: What does progress look like week by week in an essay subject?
faqs.answer: Structural rather than numerical, and visible to a parent who has not read the text. Count the paragraphs that begin with a method or technique rather than with a plot event. Watch for short embedded quotations replacing long retold extracts. Look for the register matching the audience the task names. Those changes take four to six weeks and they persist, whereas an essay mark out of thirty bounces around with the question. Keep two essays six weeks apart and compare them side by side; the difference is usually obvious.

faqs.question: Should I ask a tutor for their previous students' results?
faqs.answer: Ask for one anonymised marked script with the mark scheme beside it instead. Results claims are unverifiable, and a provider quoting a satisfaction percentage or an average improvement without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is quoting noise. A marked script shows you how they mark, which is the thing you are actually buying. Competitors in this market publish review counts and ratings that contradict each other on the same page, which is a reasonable argument for ignoring that entire category of claim.

faqs.question: How can I be sure a coursework draft is my child's own work?
faqs.answer: Look at the trail rather than the final text. A genuine one shows planning notes, an early draft, feedback given as questions and criterion references, and a later draft where your child acted on some of it and ignored some. That pattern of judgement, including judgement the tutor disagreed with, is what an honest process looks like. A draft where every suggestion is implemented perfectly in a register unlike your child's other writing is the pattern schools notice, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs in a tutor's progress report?
faqs.answer: A percentage with no annotation. A recommendation for more hours offered in place of a sharper diagnosis. A description of what the tutor explained rather than what the student produced. A grade prediction. Attitude adjectives with nothing behind them. And any statistic about past students without a number, a date and a method attached. Each of those is a substitute for evidence, and the substitution is usually unconscious rather than dishonest, which does not make it less expensive over a term.

faqs.question: How many marked papers before a pattern is trustworthy?
faqs.answer: Three to four scripts across a few weeks is usually enough to see clustering, and one is almost never enough. What you are looking for is repetition: the same topic in the lost column, the same marks given away for missing working, the same time overspend on low-value questions. A single bad paper can be illness, a hard question or a bad morning. Four papers showing the same three errors is a diagnosis, and that is the point at which spending money on fixing them is a sound decision.

faqs.question: If we want someone physically nearby, can you arrange that?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we offer only in India, and tutoring for families here runs one to one over live video. If what your child needs is an adult in the room, the useful part of this page for you is the six-question list and the two compliance checks: identification and the MoHRE private tuition work permit, issued free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those questions work on any tutor, in any format.

faqs.question: How do we hand over to a new tutor without losing the diagnosis?
faqs.answer: By keeping the file. Dated annotated scripts, the session notes and the ranked list of named errors hand a replacement tutor a working diagnosis on day one instead of costing you a fortnight of rediscovery. In a market where mid-year changes are routine, that folder is worth more than loyalty to any individual, and it is also the reason a tutor change in February need not be a disaster. Ask for everything in a form you can keep rather than inside a platform you might lose access to.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask for the evidence before you ask for the postcode
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Reorder the questions and this search gets easier. Specification and level first. Then evidence: one anonymised marked script, and what will exist in writing after four weeks. Then the hour of the evening that genuinely works in your household. Geography comes last, and over video it does not come up at all. Send a photograph of a recent marked paper with the code and the level, and we will propose a tutor who teaches that paper. The first lesson is free and takes no card details, and by week four you will have three named causes of mark loss in writing or a clear reason to change.

intro.heading: Internal assessment is where a Dubai Diploma grade is quietly decided
paragraphs: A Diploma student sits examinations for a few weeks and works on internal assessment for roughly two years. In most DP subjects the IA is worth between 20% and 25% of the final grade, and in a handful of courses it is worth more. That share is banked before any examination paper is opened, which is why a student who drifts through the IA has to find those marks back under timed conditions, against papers that are harder to recover marks in.

Dubai schools are not careless about this. The constraint is timetable. A DP teacher carrying two SL classes and an HL class has to teach a syllabus to a fixed deadline, and the IA is an individual project with as many directions as there are students in the room. Teachers are permitted one formally marked draft per student under IB rules on supervision, and that single round of feedback has to carry the whole project. A student who has not understood what criterion C is asking for by the time the draft comes back has used up the only structured intervention the course offers.

What a tutor adds is time on the criteria themselves. Most lost IA marks are not subject errors. They are a method section that omits the controlled variables, a conclusion that restates the result instead of comparing it to a published value, a reflection that is personal rather than mathematical, or an evaluation that lists limitations without saying what each one did to the data. Those are diagnosable in one reading of a draft and fixable in two or three sessions, and none of them require anyone to write a single sentence of the student's work.

That boundary matters more in the IB than in most systems. Every submitted IA is accompanied by an academic honesty declaration from both student and supervisor, and work found to be other than the student's own is a malpractice case that can cost the whole Diploma. There are operators in this market that sell finished Internal Assessments outright. IB Gram does not and will not. A tutor here explains what a criterion wants, reads what the student has produced, asks the questions a moderator would ask, and sends the student back to their own keyboard.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen, which suits IA work better than it suits ordinary teaching. An IA session is two people looking at the same document, the same spreadsheet or the same graph. Nothing about that improves by having a second person physically in the room in Al Barsha or Dubai Hills, and a great deal improves by being able to book a Chemistry HL specialist for Tuesday at eight rather than whoever is free to drive across town.

This page sets out what each DP internal assessment actually is, what it is worth, what the criterion letters reward, where Dubai students most often lose marks, how a two-year IA calendar should be counted backwards, and what this kind of support costs in the Dubai market. If you only read one section, read the one on the honesty line.

dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.programmesIntro: Internal assessment is not only a Diploma problem. It runs through the IB continuum in different forms, and a Dubai family moving between IB schools will meet all three versions. Here is what internally assessed work means at each stage, and what it means for a child in a Dubai school specifically.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the core. Each subject carries its own internally assessed component: a mathematical exploration, a scientific investigation, three Economics commentaries, a Psychology experimental study, a Business Management research project, an oral in each language. Marks are awarded by the school teacher against published criteria and then externally moderated, which can move a whole cohort's marks up or down.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are small by UK or Indian standards, often one or two teaching groups per subject, so a single teacher usually supervises every IA in that subject. That makes the marked draft a scarce resource and makes outside criterion coaching more useful here than in a school with four parallel classes and a department moderating internally.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, marked out of eight and reported on a 1-7 scale. In the final year the Personal Project is the flagship internally assessed piece, moderated externally. MYP students are therefore already fluent in criterion language before they reach the Diploma, which is an advantage that frequently goes unused.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run a full IB continuum from PYP through MYP to DP, so a child may meet criterion-referenced marking at eight years old. Others take students in at Year 12 from British IGCSE streams, and those students arrive having never been marked against a criterion in their lives. The gap between those two intakes is the single most common reason a DP1 student struggles with their first IA.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study and a core that includes a reflective project. The reflective project is internally assessed and externally moderated, and it asks for an ethical dilemma connected to the career-related study, with a research question and a reasoned argument.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is still rare in Dubai compared with the Diploma, offered by a small number of schools rather than being a mainstream route. Families considering it should confirm the exact course combination with the school before planning any support, because the reflective project differs enough from an EE that experience with one does not transfer cleanly to the other.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external assessment at all. The PYP Exhibition in the final year is an extended collaborative inquiry presented to the school community, assessed internally against school-set expectations rather than IB criteria. It is a rehearsal for everything internally assessed that follows.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a deep PYP layer because so many families arrive mid-primary. For a parent, the Exhibition is the first visible sign of how an IB school judges independent work, and it is worth attending for that reason alone rather than for the mark, since no mark is reported.

dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.subjectsIntro: Each DP subject has its own internally assessed task with its own criteria, its own length limit and its own failure modes. The eight below are the ones Dubai families most often ask about, with the specific thing that costs marks in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematical exploration, 12 to 20 pages, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The commonest loss is use of mathematics: a student picks a topic whose maths sits below their course level, caps the top band and cannot recover it by writing more.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same criteria, different mathematical register. AI explorations lean on modelling and statistics, which makes data provenance the risk. An exploration built on a dataset the student cannot source or justify loses reflection marks because there is nothing honest to reflect on.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation, around 3,000 words, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Physics drafts most often fail on uncertainty: raw uncertainties recorded but never propagated into the gradient, so the conclusion claims a precision the data cannot support.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same assessment model as Physics. Chemistry investigations lose marks on control of variables that are chemically significant rather than obvious, and on conclusions that quote a literature value without comparing percentage error or explaining the direction of the discrepancy.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Scientific investigation with the same four criteria. Biology is where statistical treatment decides the grade: a student who runs five replicates and then applies a test that needs more, or who reports a mean without a measure of spread, is capped on data analysis regardless of how careful the practical work was.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries of up to 800 words each, one per unit of the syllabus, each built on a news article published within a set recency window. The commonest fault is a commentary that explains theory and diagrams but never applies them to the article's own specifics.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: An experimental study replicating a published study, reported in around 2,200 words. Marks are lost on the link between the chosen study and the hypothesis, and on inferential statistics applied without stating assumptions or justifying the significance level.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project at HL and a written commentary at SL, both built on primary or secondary evidence about a real organisation. Weak projects ask a research question the available evidence cannot answer, which is a planning failure visible on page one.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: A fieldwork write-up of around 2,500 words based on data the student collected. Dubai students often have excellent urban fieldwork available to them and then write it up as a report rather than as an argument answering a fieldwork question.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation of around 2,200 words in three sections, including an evaluation of sources. The source evaluation section is where marks concentrate and where students most often summarise sources instead of weighing their value and limitations.

dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.regionsIntro: IA support is booked from every part of Dubai, and the pattern of requests changes by community because the schools differ. These are the areas we hear from most, with what the local school mix means for internal assessment specifically.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Al Sheif
regions.note: The densest IB cluster in Dubai, with full-continuum schools inside a few kilometres of each other. Requests here are heavily Maths AA and the sciences, and often come from MYP-trained students who understand criteria but underestimate DP length limits.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Long-established IB and British schools side by side. A recurring pattern is a student who moved from an IGCSE stream into DP1 and is writing their first criterion-marked piece of work with no prior experience of it.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Continuum schools with large Indian and British expatriate intakes. Economics and Business Management commentaries dominate the requests, usually two weeks before an internal deadline.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A strong IB continuum presence serving families who stay in the same school from primary. Students here tend to arrive at the DP comfortable with reflection criteria and weaker on formal data analysis.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Diploma provision serving the Deira and Creek side of the city. Evening session slots fill early here because the commute home compresses the usable study window after school.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: A newer school belt with rapidly growing DP cohorts. First-year IB departments mean small subject groups, so a student taking Physics HL may be one of four, with correspondingly little peer benchmarking.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A mix of British and IB provision along the coast. We see a lot of dual-track families here, with one child writing an IGCSE coursework piece while an older sibling writes a DP exploration.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's thickest concentration of IB World Schools, with several running the full continuum. Students from these schools arrive at IA support already fluent in criterion language, so sessions move quickly to the specifics of data treatment and length discipline.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Continuum and Diploma schools serving the eastern and southern communities. Economics commentaries and Maths explorations are the two most requested components from this cluster, and internal draft deadlines here often cluster in the same fortnight.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Ranches and Dubai Hills
schoolClusters.note: Established Diploma provision alongside British schools, which produces the IGCSE-to-DP transition cases that make up a large share of first-IA enquiries. Small HL groups are normal in this cluster.

dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.modesIntro: Internal assessment support is not open-ended tutoring. It works best in defined blocks tied to a point in the project, because a student who gets criterion feedback before they have written anything has nothing to apply it to.

modes.title: Topic and research-question block
modes.description: Two or three sessions at the start, before any writing. The work is narrowing a topic until the criteria can actually be met: checking that the mathematics reaches the course level, that the variables can be controlled with available equipment, or that the chosen article carries enough specifics to analyse. Most salvageable IA disasters are caused here and visible nowhere else until the draft.

The tutor reads it against each criterion letter and reports where it currently sits and what the next band asks for, in the criterion's own language. The student then revises. No sentences are supplied, no passages are rewritten, and the file the student submits to school is the file the student typed.

sections.heading: What IB internal assessment help actually means
paragraphs: Internal assessment is any component of an IB course marked by the student's own teacher against IB criteria and then externally moderated. It is not coursework in the old British sense, where a task was set and everyone answered the same question. In most DP subjects the student chooses the topic, designs the task, carries it out and writes it up, and the criteria reward the quality of those choices as much as the quality of the final answer.

So IB internal assessment help in Dubai means something narrower than general tutoring. It is not teaching the syllabus, although syllabus gaps often surface during it. It is coaching a student through a project they own, against a published mark scheme, inside a deadline set by their school rather than by the IB. The deliverable is a student who understands what each criterion letter rewards and can see their own draft the way a moderator will see it.

There are three distinct moments where outside help earns its cost. The first is topic choice, because a topic that cannot reach the top band of the hardest criterion sets a ceiling nothing else can lift. The second is the student's own first full draft, because that is the only point where structural change is still cheap. The third is the last fortnight, where the useful work is narrow and specific: the reflection, the evaluation, the citations and the length.

Everything outside those three moments is usually better spent on the subject itself. A student who cannot yet explain standard deviation will not write a strong data analysis section no matter how much criterion coaching they receive, and the honest advice in that case is to fix the statistics first and come back to the IA afterwards.

sections.heading: Every DP internal assessment, its length limit and what it is worth
paragraphs: Parents are rarely told the numbers plainly, and the numbers are the reason the IA deserves attention. The table below sets out the internally assessed component for the DP subjects Dubai students take most, with its approximate length limit and the share of the subject grade it carries. Weightings differ between standard and higher level in several subjects because the external papers differ, and length limits are set by the subject guide rather than by the school.

Two patterns are worth noticing. First, the share is higher at standard level in most subjects, because SL students sit fewer or shorter papers, so the IA is a larger slice of a smaller pie. A parent who assumes the IA matters more to the HL student has it backwards. Second, the length limits are short. A 2,200-word historical investigation or an 800-word Economics commentary leaves no room for a leisurely introduction, and students who write to the limit rather than to the criteria routinely lose marks for material that should have been cut.

Always confirm the exact current figure against your child's subject guide or with the school's DP coordinator before planning around it. Subject guides are revised on a rolling cycle, the IB publishes the authoritative version, and a page like this one is a map rather than the territory. Where a figure here differs from the guide your child's teacher is working to, the guide wins.

One further use for the table: it tells a family where to spend money if they can only spend it once. A student taking Economics SL, Psychology SL and Biology HL has three internally assessed components carrying very different weight, and the Economics commentaries are the ones that move the most grade per hour of effort. Ranking the components by weighting before booking any support is a five-minute exercise that changes what the support should be.

sections.heading: The criterion letters, and what each one is really marking
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single IA criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are the whole game. An IA is not marked as an essay and then adjusted. It is marked letter by letter, each letter against a band descriptor, and the total is the sum. A student who knows that will spend their last week on the weakest letter instead of polishing the strongest one.

The sciences share one set of criteria across Physics, Chemistry and Biology, which is useful for a family with two children in different sciences. Mathematics has its own set, and the mathematics criterion that decides most grades is the one about the level of mathematics used. The table shows both sets side by side with the thing each letter actually rewards and the thing that most often costs the band.

The practical use of this table is diagnostic. Read a draft once per letter, not once overall. A science draft that reads well often turns out to be strong on research design and weak on evaluation, and the weak letter is where the marks are. A maths exploration that looks impressive often turns out to be strong on presentation and personal engagement and capped on use of mathematics, which is the letter nothing else compensates for.

Students can do this reading themselves, and the better ones do. Print the band descriptors, print the draft, and mark the draft once per criterion with a different colour each time. The exercise takes an hour and usually produces a shorter and more accurate list of jobs than a teacher's comments do, because it forces the student to look for evidence of a band rather than for things that read awkwardly. A tutor's value then shifts from finding the problems to confirming the diagnosis and teaching whatever the weak letter turns out to need.

sections.heading: Where Dubai IB students lose IA marks most often
paragraphs: Across IA drafts from Dubai schools the same handful of faults recur, and almost none of them are about intelligence or effort. They are about not having read the band descriptors. The most expensive single error is topic choice at the wrong level: a Maths AA HL student who explores a problem that resolves with standard-level trigonometry has capped use of mathematics before writing anything, and no amount of late work lifts that ceiling.

The second is uncertainty treatment in the sciences. Dubai school laboratories are generally well equipped, so students collect good raw data, record instrument uncertainties correctly in the table, and then compute a mean and a gradient as if those uncertainties had vanished. A conclusion that states a result to four significant figures from data that supports two is a conclusion the evaluation criterion has to punish.

The third is the reflection and evaluation pair, which students treat as a conclusion to the writing rather than as analysis. Reflection in a mathematical exploration means thinking about the mathematics: why this method rather than that one, what the result implies, what breaks if an assumption is relaxed. Evaluation in a science investigation means saying what each weakness did to the numbers and in which direction. Both are marked on specificity, and both are usually written in generalities.

A fourth, smaller, but entirely avoidable loss is administrative: missing citations for a dataset, an appendix that is referred to and not attached, a word count that includes material it should exclude, or a graph exported at a resolution nobody can read. These cost real marks and take an evening to fix.

sections.heading: The honesty line: what a tutor may and may not do with an IA
paragraphs: This is the section that should decide who you hire. The IB requires every student to submit work that is their own, and both student and supervisor sign a declaration to that effect. Work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence is not a lower mark but the potential loss of the Diploma. That penalty falls on the student, not on whoever was paid.

Within that rule, legitimate support is broad and genuinely useful. A tutor may explain what a criterion means, teach the statistics a student needs, discuss whether a research question is viable, ask the questions a moderator would ask, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, flag that an appendix is missing, and teach referencing conventions. A tutor may read a draft and report where it sits against each band. None of that is prohibited, and all of it is what the better IB departments in Dubai do with their own students when they have the hours.

What a tutor may never do is produce the work. That means no supplying sentences for the student to paste, no rewriting a paragraph into better English, no generating a dataset, no building the spreadsheet model and handing it over, no choosing the topic on the student's behalf, and emphatically no finished documents. Operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments for a few thousand dirhams. Buying one puts a child's entire Diploma at risk, and we decline that work rather than pricing it.

Artificial-intelligence tools sit in the same frame. A student may use them where their school's policy permits and must disclose and cite that use the way they would cite any other source. What they may not do is submit generated text as their own writing. If you are unsure where your child's school draws that line, ask the DP coordinator in writing and keep the reply, because school policies on this differ across Dubai and the school's policy is the one that will be applied.
bullets: Permitted: explaining criteria, teaching method, questioning a draft
Permitted: reporting where each criterion currently sits
Not permitted: supplying text, rewriting prose, producing data
Not permitted: any finished or part-finished assessed document

sections.heading: The two-year IA calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this, so students discover it by missing it. Internal assessment deadlines are set by the school, not by the IB, and they sit much earlier than families expect, because the school needs time to mark, to moderate internally, and to upload samples before the IB's own submission window. By the time examination revision begins in earnest, every IA should already be finished and submitted.

The practical consequence is that the heaviest IA work in a Diploma falls in the second and third terms of the first year and the first term of the second year, which in Dubai means it collides with Ramadan in some years and with the long summer break in all of them. A student who plans to write their exploration over the summer between DP1 and DP2 is planning to write it without access to their teacher, which is a choice rather than a plan.

The table counts a typical IA backwards in relative terms rather than fixed dates, because every Dubai school sets its own internal calendar and the IB's own dates should be read from the official source rather than from a tutoring page. Ask your child's coordinator for the school's internal deadline list at the start of DP1 and put it on a wall. Families who do that rarely have an IA emergency; families who do not, do.

Two Dubai-specific wrinkles are worth planning around. Laboratory access over the long summer break is usually unavailable, so any science investigation needing repeat data collection has to finish its practical work before term ends. And in years when Ramadan falls across the spring term, the working rhythm of the household and the school day both change for a month, which is a month that cannot be assumed to be productive drafting time. Both are foreseeable, and both are regularly not foreseen.

sections.heading: What IA support costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked pages for this kind of query publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family pays in. So here are the market bands in dirhams, attributed, with the caveat that these are what the market charges rather than a price list of ours.

Start from the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is how an IA block is actually bought. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost tables put a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. An IA block is usually four to eight sessions in total rather than an open-ended weekly booking, so the sensible way to budget for it is as a project cost of a few hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams, not as a recurring subscription.

On an hourly basis, published rates in this market run from around AED 45-65 at the budget online end, where EdFlik advertises, up to AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, and AED 650 at the premium examiner-branded end where BartyED sits. Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Specialist IB and IGCSE support clusters at AED 200-450 and above.

What moves the number for IA work specifically is subject scarcity rather than level. A Maths AA exploration or an Economics commentary can be supported by a wide pool of tutors. A Physics HL investigation involving uncertainty propagation, or a Psychology study needing a defensible inferential test, draws on a much smaller pool, and small pools price higher everywhere. Ask what the hour includes: whether written criterion feedback between sessions is part of it or billed separately is the single biggest hidden variable in this market.

sections.heading: Why IA support online beats a tutor in your living room
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. That is worth stating plainly rather than burying, because the phrase parents search is a home tutor and the honest answer is that for internal assessment the online format is not a compromise.

An IA session is a document session. The student has a draft, a spreadsheet and a graph, and the tutor needs to see all three, annotate them and hand them back. A shared screen does that better than two people leaning over one laptop, and it leaves a written record of the session the student can reread at eleven at night. Nothing in that workflow improves by adding a car journey across Sheikh Zayed Road.

The pool argument matters even more. The Dubai in-home market prices travel into every hour, which means the tutor you can book is the tutor who lives within a reasonable drive of your community at the hour your child is free. For a Chemistry HL investigation that is a severe constraint. Online, the constraint disappears, and the relevant question becomes whether the tutor has supervised this kind of investigation before, which is the question that should have been asked first.

Scheduling is the last practical point. Dubai school runs, after-school activities and the evening traffic pattern mean the realistic window for serious IA work is after seven in the evening on a weekday, or a long weekend morning. Online slots exist at those hours. In-home slots at those hours cost a premium precisely because someone has to drive to them.

process.title: Tell us the component and the deadline
process.description: Which subject, which level, which internally assessed component and the school's internal deadline. If the student already has a draft or a marked set of teacher comments, send those too. Those three facts decide whether this is a topic problem, a draft problem or a final-fortnight problem, and they determine who should take it.

process.title: We match a tutor who has supervised that component
process.description: Not a generalist in the subject. For a Physics investigation that means someone who has worked through uncertainty propagation and evaluation bands before; for an Economics commentary, someone who has marked against the key-concept requirement. Where no specialist is free at your preferred hour we say so and offer the next available slot rather than substituting.

process.title: A free trial session on the real work
process.description: The first session uses the student's actual draft or actual topic shortlist, not a sample task. By the end of it you should know where each criterion currently sits and what the realistic ceiling is given the time left. If that session does not tell you something you did not already know, there is no reason to book a second.

process.title: A short defined block, not an open subscription
process.description: Most IA work resolves in four to eight sessions clustered around the three moments that matter. We will say when a block is finished rather than extending it. If the underlying issue turns out to be a subject gap rather than an IA gap, we will say that too, because criterion coaching cannot substitute for not knowing the statistics.

process.title: Written criterion feedback the student acts on
process.description: After a draft review the student receives written notes organised by criterion letter, with the question a moderator would ask at each one. The revision is theirs to make. Nothing is rewritten for them, and the file submitted to school is the file they typed.

whyPoints.title: We work criterion by criterion
whyPoints.description: Feedback is organised by the letters the mark scheme uses, so a student can see the weakest letter and spend their last week there. General impressions about an IA being well written are what schools already give and are not what moves a mark.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA is written out on this page so you can hold us to it. Operators selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market; we decline that work and explain why to any family that asks for it.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the company that published it, read in October 2026, and labelled as the market rather than as our price. We would rather be checkable than cheap-looking.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not the nearest available body
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the tutor is chosen for having supervised that exact component, not for living near your community. That is the single clearest advantage the format has over the in-home market in Dubai.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what late help can do
whyPoints.description: Three weeks before a deadline the realistic gains are in reflection, evaluation, citations and length. A tutor who promises structural transformation at that point is selling hope. We say what is recoverable and what is not.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around Dubai evenings
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time in the slots that actually exist after school runs, activities and traffic, including late weekday evenings and weekend mornings, with Ramadan timings shifted to suit the family.

faqs.question: How much of my child's IB grade actually comes from internal assessment?
faqs.answer: In most Diploma subjects the internally assessed component is worth around 20% of the subject grade, and in several standard level courses it is worth 25% or 30% because SL students sit fewer external papers. Economics SL is at the higher end with three commentaries. Across six subjects that means roughly a fifth to a quarter of the whole academic grade is decided by work done at home over two years rather than in the examination hall. Confirm the exact figure for each of your child's subjects against the current subject guide, because weightings are revised on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: Is it against IB rules for a tutor to help with an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: No, provided the help stays on the right side of a clear line. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, teach the method or statistics the student needs, discuss whether a research question is viable, question a draft, and report where it sits against each band. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite prose, generate data or hand over any finished part of the document. Both the student and the school supervisor sign a declaration that the work is the student's own, and work that is not is treated as malpractice with consequences for the student.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student in Dubai start thinking about their first IA?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect. School internal deadlines usually sit three to four months before anything needs to reach the IB, and the project itself needs data collection time before that. In practice a student should be testing candidate topics nine to twelve months ahead of their school's submission date, which for a first IA often means during the second term of DP1. Ask the DP coordinator for the school's internal deadline list at the start of the year and work backwards from it rather than forwards from today.

faqs.question: How many internal assessments does a full Diploma student have to produce?
faqs.answer: One in each of the six subjects, plus the core. That is six internally assessed components, although some of them are multi-part: Economics is three separate commentaries, and language courses include oral components assessed internally. Add the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and a Diploma student is managing nine or ten separate pieces of independent assessed work across two years. Mapping all of them on one calendar in DP1 is the most useful hour a family can spend on the Diploma.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses the school's internal IA deadline?
faqs.answer: That is a school matter rather than an IB one, and schools in Dubai handle it differently. The common consequence is losing the right to the formally marked draft, because the teacher's marking window has closed, which means the student submits without the one round of structured feedback the course provides. In more serious cases a school may submit the work as it stands. The practical answer is to treat the internal deadline as immovable and the two weeks before it as already spoken for.

faqs.question: Does the mark my child's teacher gives for an IA always stand?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Internal assessment is marked by the teacher and then externally moderated, which means the IB samples a school's marked work and checks it against the criteria. If the sample suggests a school has marked generously or harshly, the whole cohort's marks for that component can be adjusted up or down. This is why criterion language matters so much: a mark that is defensible against the band descriptors survives moderation, and a mark based on a teacher's impression of a hard-working student may not.

faqs.question: Which IB subject has the heaviest internal assessment load?
faqs.answer: By weighting, Economics at standard level is usually the heaviest because three separate commentaries together carry about 30% of the grade. By workload rather than weighting, the experimental sciences are the hardest, because a 3,000-word scientific investigation requires laboratory access, repeated data collection and a genuine analysis of uncertainty, none of which can be compressed into a weekend. Mathematics sits in between: shorter in pages but demanding in the one criterion that rewards mathematics at the level of the course.

faqs.question: How long should an IB internal assessment be?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the limits are tighter than students assume. A mathematical exploration is typically 12 to 20 pages, a scientific investigation around 3,000 words, a historical investigation around 2,200, a Geography fieldwork write-up around 2,500 and each Economics commentary up to 800. Those limits are set in the subject guide, and examiners stop reading at the limit in several components. Writing to the criteria and then cutting to the limit produces a better mark than writing to the limit and hoping the criteria are covered.

faqs.question: What is the academic honesty declaration my child has to sign?
faqs.answer: It is a statement submitted with assessed work confirming that the work is the student's own and that all sources and assistance have been acknowledged. The school supervisor signs a corresponding declaration confirming that, to the best of their knowledge, the work is the student's. It is not a formality. It is the document that makes a malpractice finding possible, and it is the reason any service offering to produce an IA is asking a child to make a false declaration about their own work.

faqs.question: Can my child use ChatGPT or similar tools while working on an IA?
faqs.answer: Only within the school's own policy, and only with disclosure. The governing principle is that submitted work must be the student's own and any assistance or source must be acknowledged, which means generated text presented as the student's writing is not acceptable. Schools in Dubai are setting different detailed rules on this, from outright prohibition in assessed drafting to permitted use with citation for brainstorming. Ask the DP coordinator in writing where your child's school draws the line, and keep the reply.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions does IA support usually take?
faqs.answer: Four to eight for a single component, clustered rather than spread. A typical pattern is two sessions on topic and research question before any writing, one or two on data and analysis, one criterion review of the student's own draft with written notes, and one short block in the final fortnight on reflection, evaluation and citations. Spreading the same hours weekly across a year tends to work worse, because criterion feedback only means something when there is a draft to apply it to.

faqs.question: What do families in Dubai pay per hour for IA support?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, run from about AED 45-65 at the budget online end up to AED 650 for premium examiner-branded providers. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate puts specialist IB and IGCSE support at AED 200-450 and above, and in-home visits at AED 180-350 before independent tutors quoting up to AED 500. Those are the market's figures, not ours. Ask whether written feedback between sessions is included, because that varies more than the headline rate.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support internal assessments in two different subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The three experimental sciences share one set of IA criteria, so a tutor who has supervised Chemistry investigations transfers reasonably to Biology on the criteria even if the subject content differs. Mathematics has a separate criterion set and Economics another again, so combining a maths exploration and an Economics commentary with one person is usually a compromise. For two components in the same assessment family, one tutor is efficient; across families, two specialists are better.

faqs.question: My child's IA draft came back covered in teacher comments. Is that a bad sign?
faqs.answer: Usually the opposite. A heavily annotated draft means the supervisor engaged with it properly and used the one formally marked round of feedback the course allows. The bad sign is a draft returned with a grade and three general remarks, because that leaves the student nothing actionable. Work through the comments criterion by criterion, group them by letter, and deal with the weakest letter first. Most sets of teacher comments contain two or three structural points worth real marks buried among a dozen presentational ones.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities care about internal assessment marks specifically?
faqs.answer: They see the subject grades, not the component breakdown, so the IA matters because it moves the grade rather than because anyone reads it. Where internal assessment does matter separately is in Ministry of Education equivalency for the UAE certificate, which assesses the qualification as a whole against published requirements. The British track requirements are published, including five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count; for the IB, check the current requirement directly on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any tutoring site.

dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.closingHeading: Start with the draft you already have
dubai/ib-internal-assessment-help.closingBody: The most useful first step is not a decision about tutoring. It is to put every internally assessed component your child owes on one calendar, with the school's internal deadline next to each, and then read the band descriptors for whichever one is closest. If after that you want a second reader on a draft, the trial session is free and uses the student's own file rather than a sample task. You will come out of it knowing where each criterion sits and what is realistically recoverable in the time left. If the answer is that your child is in better shape than they thought, that is a useful hour too, and we will say so.

dubai/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.heroSubtitle: IB math AA vs AI guidance in Dubai is usually asked as which is easier, and that is the wrong question. The two courses assess different things: AA rewards algebraic method and proof, AI rewards modelling, statistics and commentary on real data. This page sets out the content, the calculator policy, the exploration criteria by letter, what each course costs to support in AED, and which university routes expect which. Sessions run online.

dubai/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.tutorsIntro: The tutors below state which of the two courses they teach and at which level, because the two are not interchangeable. Each profile names whether the tutor covers the non-calculator paper, the Higher Level third paper, and exploration coaching, so you can match on the component rather than on the word mathematics.

intro.heading: Two courses, not one course at two difficulties
paragraphs: The IB offers two mathematics courses, each available at Higher and Standard Level. Analysis and Approaches builds from algebraic technique, functions and calculus, with an emphasis on proof and on working without technology in one paper. Applications and Interpretation builds from modelling, statistics and the interpretation of real data, with technology permitted across the papers. They share a common core of content and then diverge, and a student can be genuinely strong in one and uncomfortable in the other.

Dubai families almost always arrive at this question asking which is easier, usually because somebody at the school gates said one of them was. That framing produces bad decisions, because the courses fail students in different ways. A capable arithmetician with no patience for proof will be miserable in Analysis and Approaches and may do very well in Applications and Interpretation. A student who enjoys algebraic manipulation and dislikes writing commentary on data will have the opposite experience.

There is a second question underneath, and it is the one with money attached. Support for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the scarcest mathematics specialism in this market, which pushes it towards the upper end of the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour and above. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level sits in the general band. So the course choice carries a two-year cost consequence as well as an academic one, and almost nobody mentions it at option time.

Both courses carry the same internally assessed component: the mathematical exploration, marked against five criteria lettered A to E for a total of twenty marks. Nobody in the competitor set names a single one of those criteria, which is remarkable given that the exploration is the one part of the grade a student can work on calmly, outside examination conditions, with time to improve it. This page names all five with their mark allocations, because that is the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject.

The third element is the university question, and it is where the expensive mistakes happen. Mathematics-heavy routes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, and some specify it at Higher Level. A student who chooses Applications and Interpretation and later applies for engineering may find the route closed, and the discovery usually comes after the switching window has shut. No institution's requirement is reproduced here, because requirements change between cycles and a stale figure on a tutoring page is worse than none.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video with the working on a shared screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service, and for mathematics the online format is practically better: the student's own working is visible and annotated live, and the annotations stay in the file, which matters for a subject where the marks are in the method.

dubai/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.programmesIntro: The course choice is made before any Diploma mathematics has been taught, which is the structural problem. These three stages are where the decision is made, tested, and occasionally reversed.

programmes.name: The option year
programmes.description: The choice is made on IGCSE or MYP evidence, neither of which separates algebraic appetite from data-handling appetite. The cheapest useful intervention is a short diagnostic task containing both an algebraic proof question and a modelling question, because a student's reaction to those two items predicts the fit better than a grade does.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run option processes on their own timetables, frequently before IGCSE results arrive. Asking the coordinator what evidence informs the mathematics placement, and whether the choice can be revised in the first term, is worth doing before the form is signed.

programmes.name: First Diploma year
programmes.description: The year the choice is tested and the year a change is still realistically possible. Internal examinations towards the end of it are the first honest measurement. This is also the cheapest year to fund mathematics properly, because the non-calculator discipline in Analysis and Approaches and the commentary discipline in Applications and Interpretation are both habits best built early.
programmes.countryNote: Schools set their own deadlines for course and level changes, usually inside this year. A student struggling in the first term who waits for mock results has often waited past the point where the school can still move them.

programmes.name: Final Diploma year
programmes.description: The course is fixed, so the question becomes which component gets the funded hours. In practice the answers are the exploration if it is not yet submitted, the Higher Level third paper if the student sits one, and the non-calculator paper in Analysis and Approaches, which is where that course's marks most reliably leak.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates holding offers that name mathematics should check whether the named course is specified, because that determines whether the final year's spending is about a grade or about a prerequisite. Those two aims point at different components.

dubai/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.subjectsIntro: The grid below breaks both courses into the components a family is actually choosing between and funding, with what each one rewards and where it is usually weak.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1
subjects.description: Sat without technology, which is the single defining feature of the course. Students who revise with a calculator always to hand are systematically under-prepared for it, and the fix is mechanical: untimed non-calculator practice first, then timed, with the working written in full.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Paper 2
subjects.description: Technology permitted, which tempts students into treating questions as button sequences. Marks still go on method and on stating what has been found, so the habit of writing the route to the answer transfers directly from Paper 1 practice.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Papers 1 and 2
subjects.description: Technology permitted throughout. The recurring loss is interpretation: a result obtained and never explained, a model fitted and never evaluated, an assumption never stated. These are writing failures in a mathematics paper and they respond quickly to marked practice.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3, Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Short, investigative, and built from extended questions that award marks for setting out and justifying an approach. Fewer past versions exist than for the other papers, which is why it is under-practised and why two marked attempts have an unusually high return.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3, Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A long data-led investigation requiring structured commentary alongside the calculation. Students who are fluent with technology and reticent in writing lose most of their marks here, and the fix is a template for stating method, result, meaning and limitation.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Shared in the core and then diverging sharply. Analysis and Approaches extends into proof, including proof by induction at Higher Level; Applications and Interpretation stays closer to applied computation. A student's appetite for proof is the clearest single signal of course fit.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Where Applications and Interpretation is deepest and where Analysis and Approaches is comparatively light. Students arriving from a curriculum with little statistics find this the steepest part of Applications and Interpretation, and it is also where its exploration topics usually come from.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Substantially heavier in Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level. This is the content that makes Analysis and Approaches Higher Level the scarcest specialism in the Dubai market and therefore the most expensive component to support well.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: The internally assessed component, marked against five criteria from A to E out of twenty in total. It is the part of the grade a student can improve calmly outside examination conditions, and it is also the part most often left until the deadline week.

dubai/ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.regionsIntro: What location changes in mathematics is access to the scarce specialisms, because an in-home pool is limited to whoever will drive. These notes cover the pattern across the city.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Large Diploma cohorts with heavy Analysis and Approaches Higher Level uptake, which means local demand for the scarcest specialism peaks in the same weeks every year. In-home quotes sit at the top of the published band because of distance between gates.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short commutes make a weekday 16:30 session realistic, which suits non-calculator practice. That work benefits from short frequent sessions rather than a single long block, so an early slot is genuinely more useful here.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Households often running a Diploma candidate and an IGCSE sibling in mathematics at once. One tutor covering both is sometimes possible, but the Diploma course and level should be confirmed first, since Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is a separate specialism.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long eastern commutes mean few Higher Level mathematics specialists will travel on a weekday evening, so the local in-home pool is thin as well as expensive. This is where online delivery changes what is available rather than only what it costs.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Central apartments with limited quiet space during the mock period. Exploration work splits well into two shorter sessions, and Paper 3 practice needs only an hour, both of which suit this constraint.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University-belt families with strong mathematics uptake and a high share of students heading for engineering and computing. Demand here concentrates on Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and on the third paper specifically.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Large cohorts with substantial Analysis and Approaches Higher Level entry, which concentrates demand for the market's scarcest mathematics specialism into a short annual window. Booking in the first Diploma year secures a better match at the same hourly figure.

schoolClusters.city: Central and eastern Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: A mix of continuum IB schools and schools where the Diploma sits alongside other curricula. Students arriving from IGCSE frequently choose the mathematics course on an IGCSE grade, which does not separate algebraic appetite from data-handling appetite.

sections.heading: What each course contains, and what the calculator rule really does
paragraphs: Both courses are organised around the same five content areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. They share a common core and then diverge in depth. Analysis and Approaches goes substantially further in algebra and calculus, with proof as a running theme and proof by induction at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation goes substantially further in statistics and in modelling, and treats mathematics as a tool applied to data and context.

The calculator policy is the difference students feel first. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without technology and Paper 2 with it. In Applications and Interpretation, technology is permitted across the papers. That one rule reshapes how a student has to revise. An Analysis and Approaches candidate who always works with a calculator in reach will discover the gap only under examination conditions, by which point the arithmetic and algebraic fluency that Paper 1 assumes has not been built.

The reverse problem is less obvious and just as costly. An Applications and Interpretation candidate with technology always available can reach correct results without ever explaining them, and the papers award marks for interpretation, assumptions and limitations. Fluency with the device masks a writing weakness until a marked script exposes it, usually in the final year.

sections.heading: How each course actually loses marks
paragraphs: In Analysis and Approaches the dominant loss is unwritten method. The mark scheme pays for a recognisable route to the answer, so a capable student who does three steps mentally and writes the fourth is discarding marks already earned. This is the most recoverable loss in the whole subject and it changes inside three marked papers, because the student sees their own correct answer scoring below a classmate's messier one.

The second Analysis and Approaches loss is the non-calculator paper specifically. Surds, exact trigonometric values, logarithm manipulation and algebraic fractions all behave differently without a device, and a student who has never practised them that way loses time as well as accuracy. The remedy is unglamorous: a sheet of non-calculator work weekly from the first year, marked, with the working written in full.

In Applications and Interpretation the dominant loss is commentary. A modelling question asks what the model implies, what it assumes and where it stops being valid, and a student who answers only the computation leaves the interpretation marks on the table. The fix is a four-line template applied repeatedly: state the method, state the result, state what it means in context, state one limitation.

The second Applications and Interpretation loss is statistical precision: a test selected without justification, a correlation described as a cause, a conclusion stated more strongly than the data supports. These are marked explicitly and they are teachable quickly, which is why four sessions on statistical writing frequently outperforms a term of general support in this course.
