sections.heading: Dubai's Diploma maths context: schools, regulator and the timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 different curricula, and seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. A growing Diploma population in the emirate is competing for a maths specialist supply that grows more slowly.

School-level provision is the practical constraint families meet. Not every Dubai school runs all four maths courses. A smaller Diploma cohort may offer Analysis at both levels and Applications at Standard only, or share one teacher across routes. Where the audit concludes that the right course for a student is not on the school's timetable, the conversation becomes a different one, and it is better to have it in September of Diploma Year 1 than in the spring.

The mandatory-subject requirement adds to the week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising no such lesson falls below 25 minutes. A Diploma maths plan has to fit the hours a student actually has.

Two closing points of record. For the mandatory subjects, the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold the relevant approval from KHDA. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, operates no UAE office or centre, and does not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are referenced and linked at ibo.org instead.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the component
process.description: The useful opening message says Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher Level, and which paper is the problem. Those three facts determine the tutor, the calculator rule and the session plan. An enquiry that says only 'IB maths' has to be unpacked before anything can start.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. For maths it is spent on one question worked aloud under the correct calculator rule, so both the student and the parent see where the reasoning breaks and how it is marked rather than hearing a description of the approach.

process.title: A Paper 1 under the correct rule
process.description: One timed Paper 1, sat without a calculator for Analysis and with one for Applications, marked to the published scheme. The output is the Paper 1 against Paper 2 comparison, which is the single most diagnostic number available in a maths file, plus a topic-level map of where the chain broke.

process.title: Exploration topic tested before writing
process.description: Where the Exploration is in scope, the first session tests whether the chosen topic permits mathematics at the course level, because criterion E carries six of the twenty marks and a topic that cannot carry the mathematics caps the piece. Changing a topic early is cheap; discovering the limit at draft stage is not.

process.title: Weekly component work with marking between
process.description: Sessions on Gulf Standard Time aimed at one component, with a timed question set between sessions and marked before the next. Reports go to the parent the same evening and name the topic, the paper and the marks lost, so progress is readable without a meeting.

process.title: Course review at the halfway point
process.description: Mid-plan the evidence is re-read. Where the Paper 1 gap has closed the frequency drops; where the losses were spread rather than concentrated, the course-level conversation is revisited with the school while there is still time to act on it.

whyPoints.title: Four courses, four plans
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Applications at Standard and Higher Level are treated as four distinct courses with different calculator rules, different content weight and different university consequences. A tutor is matched to one of them rather than to 'maths', which is the most common mismatch in this market.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 practised the way it is sat
whyPoints.description: In Analysis and Approaches the calculator is put away for Paper 1 work, because that is the paper's design. The gap between a student's Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks is the clearest diagnostic in a maths file, and it only exists if someone measures it honestly.

whyPoints.title: Exploration criteria named by letter
whyPoints.description: Feedback refers to criteria A to E and their allocations, including the six marks on use of mathematics and the six across personal engagement and reflection. Almost no competing page in this market names a single criterion, which is odd given they are the basis of the mark.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own component
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level third paper rewards persistence through an unfamiliar stem rather than additional content knowledge, and that is a taught behaviour. Treating it as more Paper 2 practice is why students meet it properly for the first time in a Year 13 mock.

whyPoints.title: The route decision checked against real requirements
whyPoints.description: Analysis against Applications is settled by reading the stated maths requirement of the universities on the student's own list, then the marked evidence. A route chosen for prestige is the common error, and it is expensive because it is hard to reverse later.

whyPoints.title: The student does the mathematics
whyPoints.description: Exploration support is questioning, criteria-referenced marking and feedback on the student's own draft. Nothing is written or calculated for them. That is the IB rule and it is also what makes the work defensible if anyone asks how it was produced.

faqs.question: Which of the four IB maths courses should a Dubai Diploma student be in?
faqs.answer: They are separate courses sharing five topic headings. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented and sits Paper 1 without a graphic display calculator at both levels. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-oriented and permits a calculator in every paper. Higher Level Analysis adds calculus depth, proof, complex numbers and vectors; Higher Level Applications adds statistical inference, matrices and graph theory. Neither is the easy route. The decisive practical question is which one the universities on the student's list accept for the course they intend to apply for, because that requirement cannot be adjusted afterwards.

faqs.question: How are the IB maths papers weighted at Higher and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40 per cent each and the Exploration carries 20 per cent. At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 30 per cent each, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and the Exploration carries 20 per cent. Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, runs for an hour and consists of two extended problem-solving questions. The figure families most often underestimate is the Exploration: a fifth of the maths grade awarded for a written investigation produced without time pressure, which makes it the most recoverable portion of the course.

faqs.question: What does a wide gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks mean in IB maths?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches that gap is usually calculator dependence, and it is the most diagnostic number in a maths file. Paper 1 is designed around exact values, algebraic simplification and recognised identities doing the work a calculator would otherwise do. A student who met every topic with technology available cannot sketch a function from its equation or give a trigonometric ratio as a surd, so they score below their actual understanding. The fix is weeks of practice with the calculator physically out of reach, which students resist and which produces measurable movement faster than any content revision.

faqs.question: What makes a good Exploration topic for IB maths?
faqs.answer: One that permits mathematics at the level of the course. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty available marks, and a topic that can only support arithmetic and a graph caps the piece however well it is written. The test to apply before any writing starts is simple: name the specific mathematics the topic will require, and check it against the syllabus content for the student's course and level. Genuine interest matters too, because personal engagement carries three marks and is assessed through the choices visible across the work rather than through a statement of enthusiasm.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the IB maths Exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating before the first session. A tutor may teach the mathematics a topic requires, question whether the topic can carry that mathematics, name criteria A to E and their mark allocations, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not choose the topic, perform the calculations, or rewrite a draft into its final form. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against the student, not the provider. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is the thing to refuse at any price.

faqs.question: What is IB Maths Paper 3 and why do Higher Level students struggle with it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, runs for one hour, carries 20 per cent of the grade and consists of two extended problem-solving questions. Each builds from a single scenario through many parts, and the stem often introduces an unfamiliar definition the student is expected to work with. Students struggle because they read the unfamiliar stem as evidence of something untaught and stop, losing every subsequent part of a long question. The paper rewards persistence and the willingness to continue past an unresolved part, which is a taught examination behaviour rather than extra content knowledge.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths necessary for engineering at the universities Dubai students apply to?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and sometimes a specific route is named as well as the level. Some engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, others accept either route at Higher Level, and a few accept Standard Level with conditions. The requirement is published by each university on its own pages and varies by institution and by course within an institution. Read the actual requirement for the actual courses on the student's list before making the Diploma route decision, because it is the one input to that decision that cannot be revised afterwards.

faqs.question: How many maths tutoring sessions does a Dubai Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on which component is failing, and the useful answer is smaller than most plans assume. A wide Paper 1 against Paper 2 gap in Analysis is typically eight to ten focused hours of calculator-free practice and marking. An Exploration topic that will not carry the level needs three or four sessions, placed before any writing. Paper 3 work is six to eight hours of component-specific practice. Slow algebraic manipulation needs ten to twelve short high-frequency sessions. Those are specific purchases; a year of undifferentiated weekly content review is how students have tutoring and no measurable movement.

faqs.question: Can my child change IB maths course after starting Diploma Year 1?
faqs.answer: Often yes, for a limited period, and the window is usually earlier than families expect. Most Dubai Diploma programmes allow changes in the first term, after which the timetable, the teaching set and completed work make it impractical. Ask the IB coordinator for the actual date in September, then arrange for marked evidence to exist before it. A Paper 1 sat under the correct calculator rule, with the loss pattern reported as concentrated by topic or spread across the paper, is what turns the conversation from a preference into a decision the school can act on.

faqs.question: Does a graphic display calculator need to be taught, or do students pick it up?
faqs.answer: It needs teaching, and treating it as intuition costs marks in both courses. In Applications and Interpretation the calculator is permitted throughout, so command fluency across statistical tests, regression and solvers is part of the subject. In Analysis and Approaches it is permitted in Papers 2 and 3 only, which means a student has to hold two habits at once. Marks are lost to half-remembered sequences, to answers reported without the accuracy the question specified, and to accepting a value the machine returned without checking that it makes sense in context.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, place IB tuition from AED 200 an hour at Unitors and specialist work at AED 270 at TutorChase, with the Bestimate survey putting IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above. Budget online provision starts at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik. Premium named listings reach AED 650 at BartyED. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is among the scarcest subjects in the emirate, so it tends to price at the upper end. Each figure belongs to the provider that published it.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition as good as having a tutor in the room in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For mathematics specifically it has a real advantage. A long Paper 3 solution stays visible in full on a shared screen, annotations are saved and re-readable, and a graph or spreadsheet can be manipulated live. A worked solution on paper at a kitchen table is gone by the following week. The published cost difference also runs one way: AED 180-350 for qualified in-home work in this market against AED 150-300 online. What presence in the room genuinely buys is attention management for a distractible student. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: My child moved from MYP maths into Diploma maths and is struggling. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually algebraic speed and timed-paper technique rather than understanding. MYP mathematics is assessed against criteria covering knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating and applying mathematics in context, and it does not run on external timed papers. Students arrive comfortable with investigation, which maps well onto the Exploration, and unpractised at producing accurate manipulation at pace. In Analysis and Approaches the additional shock is Paper 1 without a calculator, a rule MYP assessment never imposed. A timed Paper 1 in the first term identifies both problems immediately rather than in a Year 13 mock.

faqs.question: Do maths tutors working with Dubai students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with a stated two-working-day completion time via the smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level Analysis specialist is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the alternatives named. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is among the most requested and least supplied subjects in this emirate, and demand concentrates in the same weeks every year. The honest options are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. All three are better than a general maths tutor placed into a course whose Paper 1 rules and Paper 3 structure they have not taught. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one Paper 1 and the correct calculator rule
dubai/ib-maths-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful step in Diploma maths is a single timed Paper 1, sat under the rule that applies to the student's own course, and marked to the published scheme. Compared against their Paper 2 performance it tells you whether the problem is understanding, algebraic fluency or calculator dependence, and those three have different fixes and different costs. Send the course, the level and the component that is failing, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and read the comparison before committing to anything. If the Exploration is in scope, test the topic before a word of it is written.

intro.heading: Which maths course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: There are four IB mathematics courses, not one. Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. They share a small common core and then diverge sharply in content, in paper structure and in what a good answer looks like. A tutor advertised for 'IB maths' who cannot immediately name which of the four they teach is advertising for all of them and specialising in none.

This matters in Al Barari for a specific reason. There is no school inside the community, so pupils commute out to the Dubailand and Nad Al Sheba belt, west to Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, or towards Al Barsha South. Those schools make placement decisions differently. Some stream on IGCSE grade, some on a school test, some on the student's stated university plans, and some simply on which course they can timetable. The result is that two neighbouring Al Barari households can have Year 12 students in different courses at different levels, with different problems.

The second thing families discover late is that the choice has consequences beyond difficulty. Many university courses in engineering, physics, economics and mathematics itself expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a student who took Applications because it was described as the easier route can find a door closed in Year 13. The reverse mistake also happens: a student placed in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level who did not need it spends two years fighting a course that was never a prerequisite for anything they want.

So this page starts with the course decision, sets out the paper weightings and durations, breaks the exploration down criterion by criterion with its mark allocations, and only then compares what maths tutoring costs in this market. It also compares Al Barari with the communities around it, because a proximity search is how most families start and it is worth knowing what it can and cannot deliver.

There is one further reason to establish the course before anything else, and it is about diagnosis rather than selection. A school report saying a Diploma student is struggling in mathematics does not distinguish between a topic the student has not met and an algebraic fluency that was never secure. Those look identical on paper and need completely different responses: a topic takes a few weeks of weekly sessions, while fluency takes a holiday block of four or five sessions a week, because fluency comes from volume rather than from explanation. Separating the two in the first session is the most useful hour a maths tutor spends.

One statement of fact before the detail. IB Gram delivers mathematics tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject where a session consists of worked problems on a shared screen and a marked past paper, that format is not a compromise, and it widens the shortlist to every tutor who teaches your child's exact course.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barari.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through every IB programme and the tutoring job changes completely at each stage. These are the three that matter to Al Barari families, plus the route into the Diploma.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Mathematics within units of inquiry rather than as a separate subject, with no external assessment. The target worth working to is fluency: place value, fractions, operations and the beginnings of algebraic thinking, all of which the Middle Years Programme assumes from the first week.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Barari families this is the one stage where having an adult in the room genuinely matters more than specialist knowledge. Since we make no home visits in the UAE, we will say so where that is what a child needs rather than selling a screen to a seven-year-old.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the criterion most pupils score worst on, because it rewards generalising and justifying rather than calculating, and no amount of arithmetic practice improves it.
programmes.countryNote: MYP5 mathematics is also where the Diploma course decision is effectively made in most Dubai schools, often on the basis of criterion grades the family never read closely. If your child is heading for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, the criterion to watch is investigating patterns rather than knowing and understanding.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four courses across two subjects and two levels. All four carry an exploration worth 20% of the final grade, internally assessed and externally moderated. Higher Level adds a third paper. The commonest tutoring request in Dubai is Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and the commonest unspoken problem is that the student was placed in it without the algebraic fluency it assumes.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session. No IB exam or results dates appear on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a parent acts on is worse than none; confirm every one with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: The route in from IGCSE
programmes.description: Most Al Barari Diploma students came through IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are the best preparation for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, because they introduce calculus and logarithms before the Diploma does. Without them the first Diploma term is steep.
programmes.countryNote: The practical point for a Dubai family is that the Extended or Higher tier is effectively a prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at either level. A pupil entered for Core or Foundation who intends to take the Diploma mathematics route has a content gap rather than a confidence problem, and it should be addressed before Year 12 rather than during it.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: Within IB mathematics these are the topic areas Al Barari families ask about, with where the marks actually go. The split by topic is more useful than a split by course, because the weak areas repeat across all four.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and functions
subjects.description: The single strongest predictor of a Diploma mathematics grade. Students who cannot rearrange confidently lose marks in every later topic, because algebra is the carrier for all of it. Partial fractions, logarithmic manipulation and function transformations are the recurring weak points.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, then optimisation and related rates in context. Students who learn the rules without the reasoning fail on the applied questions, where the difficulty is setting up the expression rather than differentiating it. Implicit differentiation at Higher Level is a common collapse point.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Techniques of integration, areas, volumes of revolution and, at Higher Level, substitution and integration by parts. The error pattern is mechanical: limits substituted in the wrong order, constants dropped, or a definite integral treated as an indefinite one with a constant left attached.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction and proof by induction. This is the content least like anything in IGCSE, so students arrive with no technique at all. Induction in particular is a format that can be taught in two sessions and is then reliable marks for the rest of the course.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity. Marks are lost on argument conventions and on failing to sketch the Argand diagram, which usually makes the question obvious. A self-contained topic, which means it rewards focused tutoring unusually well.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: All four, heavily weighted in AI
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. In Applications and Interpretation the difficulty is interpretation rather than calculation: correct output from the calculator with no statement of what it means in context earns very little. Conditional probability is the standard trap in both courses.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: All four, extended in AA HL
subjects.description: Identities, equations, the unit circle and, at Higher Level, compound angle formulae. The dominant error is solving an equation and reporting only the principal value, losing the other solutions in the interval. Exact values without a calculator are examinable in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes, intersections and distances. Students handle the algebra and lose marks on interpretation: whether two lines are skew, what the angle between a line and a plane actually means geometrically. Diagrams are not required but reliably raise marks.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and the binomial theorem
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to infinity and binomial expansion, with extension at Higher Level. A reliable source of early-paper marks and a reliable source of lost ones, usually through off-by-one errors in the index or forgetting the condition for convergence.

subjects.name: Mathematical modelling
subjects.description: Choosing and fitting a model, then evaluating its fit and limitations. The Applications course rewards the evaluation step, and students routinely stop after fitting. The habit worth building is writing one sentence on what the model cannot capture, which is where the available marks sit.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page individual piece of mathematics on a topic of the student's choice, marked out of 20 across five criteria. Topic choice decides most of the outcome: a question that is too large produces description instead of mathematics, and one that is too small cannot reach the higher bands for use of mathematics.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.levels: All four, examined in Papers 2 and 3
subjects.description: A genuinely teachable set of marks. Solving numerically, finding intersections, using statistical functions and knowing when a calculator answer needs supporting working. Students lose marks both by not using the calculator where it is allowed and by using it without showing the method that earns credit.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that shapes two years, and families in the Dubailand belt often make it on hearsay. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route: it emphasises algebraic manipulation, calculus, proof and, at Higher Level, complex numbers. Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route: it emphasises data, distributions, hypothesis testing, modelling and technology-led method. Both are rigorous courses and both carry a 20% exploration.

The reputation that Applications is the easier course is unreliable. At Standard Level it is genuinely more accessible for a student without strong algebra. At Higher Level it includes a third paper of extended problem solving that many students find harder than the Analysis and Approaches equivalent, because it requires sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar context rather than execution of known techniques. A student choosing Applications Higher Level to avoid difficulty has usually chosen a different difficulty.

The decision that actually matters is the university one, and it has to be made before Year 12 rather than during Year 13. Many engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics courses specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Entry requirements vary by institution and by year, and they are published by the universities themselves. Check the specific course pages of the universities your child is considering, in the UAE and abroad, and take the written requirement rather than a school's general impression.

The practical tutoring consequence is that a mismatch should be identified in the first term, not the fourth. If your child is in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level without the algebraic fluency it assumes, the honest options are a holiday intensive block to build that fluency or a conversation with the school about moving level while the change is still administratively possible. A tutor's useful contribution to that conversation is a marked diagnostic paper, which is evidence rather than opinion.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and the clock
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject where structure is most worth knowing precisely, because the weightings tell you where tutoring time should go. At Standard Level in both courses there are two papers, each carrying 40% of the grade, with the exploration carrying the remaining 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers, with Papers 1 and 2 carrying 30% each, Paper 3 carrying 20%, and the exploration again 20%.

Read that carefully, because it has a direct consequence. At Higher Level, Paper 3 and the exploration together carry 40% of the grade, and both are the components students prepare least. Paper 3 is a small number of extended questions requiring sustained reasoning, and it cannot be prepared by doing short questions well. The exploration is a piece of coursework that many students begin far too late. Together they are the most neglected 40% in the Diploma.

The time pressure differs too. Standard Level papers run an hour and a half each. Higher Level Papers 1 and 2 run two hours each, with Paper 3 at an hour. A two-hour mathematics paper is an endurance problem as much as a knowledge one, and students who have only ever practised individual questions discover in the mock that their accuracy falls in the final half hour. That is a fixable, practisable problem, and it only becomes visible under full-length timed conditions.

Confirm the current weightings for your child's specific course with their teacher or Diploma coordinator before planning around them, because the IB revises subject guides periodically and the current guide is the authority. The structural point, though, is stable: Higher Level carries an extra paper and the exploration is a fifth of the grade in every version of the course.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single exploration criterion, let alone its mark allocation, and that omission is why so many Dubai students lose marks in a component they had months to prepare. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and knowing the split changes how a student spends their time.

Criterion A, presentation, carries 4 marks and rewards a coherent, organised, focused piece. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries 4 and rewards correct notation, defined terms and appropriate use of symbols and graphs. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries 3 and rewards genuine independent thinking rather than enthusiasm in the introduction. Criterion D, reflection, carries 3 and rewards critical discussion of what the mathematics showed and what it did not. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6 and is the largest single block.

Two conclusions follow immediately. First, criterion E is worth more than any other, and it rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and at a level commensurate with the course. A beautifully presented exploration using mathematics below the level of the course cannot score well, which is the commonest failure among capable students who chose a safe topic. Second, criteria C and D together carry 6 marks and are the easiest to secure, because they reward thinking that the student can actually do if they know it is being marked. Most students who lose them lose them by not knowing they exist.

Topic choice is where a tutor earns their fee on this component. A question too large produces description instead of mathematics; one too small cannot reach the upper bands of criterion E. The right scale is a question the student can genuinely investigate using mathematics at or slightly beyond their course level, with a real reason for choosing it. That conversation takes an hour and saves a term. Confirm the current criteria and mark allocations with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its subject guides.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Ask a student what they are weak at and they will name a topic. Mark a paper and a different picture emerges. Across Diploma mathematics, a large share of lost marks comes from four repeated behaviours rather than from absent content, and all four are fixable inside a term.

The first is unshown method. IB mark schemes award method marks for the steps, so a correct final answer with no visible working scores below a wrong answer with sound method. The students most affected are the quick ones, who have been rewarded for mental calculation since primary school. The second is non-calculator execution in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1. A student who can find a root on a graphing display and cannot complete the square by hand will lose marks across the whole paper, and this only becomes visible when practice is actually done without the device.

The third is incomplete solutions in trigonometry and in equations with multiple roots. A student solves, reports the principal value, and loses the other solutions in the given interval. It is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, and it responds to a fortnight of deliberate practice. The fourth is interpretation, which dominates in Applications and Interpretation: correct statistical output with no sentence saying what it means in the context of the question earns very little, because the marks are attached to the interpretation rather than the number.

Genuine content gaps exist too, and when they do they are usually narrow: implicit differentiation, integration by parts, conditional probability, induction, argument conventions in complex numbers. Those are weeks of work. What takes a year is rebuilding algebraic fluency that was never secure, which is why identifying a course mismatch in the first Diploma term matters so much more than identifying it in the third.

sections.heading: Maths tutor supply in Al Barari against its neighbours
paragraphs: A proximity search is how most families start, so here is what it can deliver in this part of Dubai. For Middle Years mathematics and Standard Level Diploma work, local supply across the Dubailand communities is reasonable: there are plenty of competent mathematics teachers in Dubai and a number of them will travel. For Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and particularly for exploration coaching and Paper 3 preparation, the pool narrows to a point where distance filtering stops being viable.

The reason is specificity. A tutor who can teach mathematics well is common. A tutor who knows which Paper 1 questions are examinable without a calculator, which exploration topics reach the upper band of criterion E, and how Paper 3 differs in kind from Papers 1 and 2 is not. Add the requirement that this person lives within driving distance of a villa community off Al Ain Road and has a free slot in a narrow evening window, and the number falls close to zero in every community in this belt, Al Barari and Nad Al Sheba alike.

The communities do differ, but in scheduling rather than supply. A Nad Al Sheba pupil can start at half past four; an Al Barari or Arabian Ranches 3 pupil realistically starts at five or later. For a demanding Higher Level course that difference is material, because a two-hour paper practised at seven in the evening after a commute and other homework is not a fair test of anything. This is the strongest argument for weekend mornings in mathematics specifically: full-length timed papers need a rested student and a clear two hours.

In-home rates also rise with distance from the centre, so the further out the community the worse the value of a proximity search becomes. Market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. The money buys presence, not specialism. For a subject taught through worked problems on a shared screen, with the student's own working visible and a paper marked in front of them, presence is the thing least needed.

sections.heading: The exploration and academic honesty
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is the component where the honesty question is sharpest, because it is individual, unsupervised and worth a fifth of the grade. There are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at a published price, and a mathematics exploration is among the easiest things to buy. Submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student.

The boundary we work to is explicit and we state it to the student rather than only to the parent. A tutor may teach any mathematics the exploration requires, including content beyond the course if the student's chosen question needs it. A tutor may test whether a topic is viable, which is the most valuable hour available on this component. A tutor may explain each criterion and what its descriptors mean. A tutor may read the student's own draft and say what is not working: where notation is wrong, where reflection is missing, where the mathematics sits below course level.

A tutor may not write any part of it, supply the mathematics as a finished worked solution to be transcribed, choose the topic on the student's behalf, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student makes the change. That is slower and it is the only version that is both lawful and effective.

Effective, because of how the criteria work. Personal engagement and reflection carry 6 of the 20 marks between them and both reward thinking the student actually did. An exploration written by someone else reads as competent and disengaged, which is exactly the profile that loses those 6 marks and then struggles on criterion E too, because the mathematics was not chosen for this student's level. The students who score well chose a question they could genuinely investigate, early, and worked at it over weeks.

process.title: A diagnostic that separates algebra from topics
process.description: The first session works through questions designed to distinguish a topic gap from an algebraic fluency gap, because the two look identical in a school report and need completely different responses. Topics take weeks; fluency takes a holiday block. Knowing which you are dealing with is the whole value of the diagnostic.

From Al Barari, weekday sessions start at five at the earliest, so we often recommend a weekend morning for the paper work and a shorter weekday slot for topic teaching.

process.title: Problem sets between sessions, marked in the next one
process.description: Mathematics improves through volume, not explanation. Each session ends with a set of questions, and the next session starts by marking them. That loop is where the gain happens, and a session plan that does not include it is a lecture rather than tuition. The written note tells you what was set and whether it came back.

If the evidence says the course level is wrong, we will say so and give you a marked paper to take to the school. If it says the subject is secure, we will say that too, even though it ends the booking.

whyPoints.description: A topic gap and an algebraic fluency gap look the same in a school report and need entirely different responses. We separate them in the first session, because telling a family that their child needs a holiday block of fluency work rather than four weeks on calculus is more useful than selling them the four weeks.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should an Al Barari student take, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, not on perceived difficulty. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebra, calculus and proof; Applications and Interpretation emphasises statistics, modelling and data. Many engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics courses specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, so check the published entry requirements of the specific universities your child is considering rather than relying on a general impression. Applications at Higher Level is not an easy option either: its third paper demands sustained reasoning in unfamiliar contexts, which many students find harder than executing known techniques.

faqs.question: How are the exploration's 20 marks divided between the criteria?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four courses at both levels. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation worth 4, mathematical communication worth 4, personal engagement worth 3, reflection worth 3, and use of mathematics worth 6. Confirm the current allocations with your child's teacher, since the IB revises subject guides. The practical point is that use of mathematics is the largest single block and rewards mathematics at or slightly above course level, which is why a safe topic using simple mathematics cannot reach the top bands however neatly it is presented.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1 really sat without a calculator?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches, yes, and it is the fact students most often fail to internalise until a mock. A candidate who can find a root on a graphing display but cannot complete the square, use exact trigonometric values or manipulate logarithms by hand will lose marks across the entire paper rather than on one question. The fix is uncomfortable and quick: practise with the device removed from the desk. In Applications and Interpretation technology is assumed throughout, which shifts the problem from execution to interpretation.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 at Higher Level and how do you prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level, runs for an hour and carries 20% of the grade. It consists of a small number of extended questions requiring sustained reasoning across several connected parts, usually in a context the student has not seen. It cannot be prepared by answering short questions well, because the difficulty is holding a long argument together rather than executing a technique. Whole papers under timing are the only preparation that works, which is one reason a weekend morning slot suits Higher Level mathematics better than a weekday evening.

faqs.question: My child was placed in Analysis and Approaches HL and is struggling. What now?
faqs.answer: Establish first whether the problem is a topic gap or algebraic fluency, because they look identical in a report and need different responses. A topic gap is weeks of work. Fluency that was never secure is a holiday intensive block at four or five sessions a week, because fluency comes from volume. If the evidence says the level is wrong, the honest options are that block or a conversation with the school about moving level while it is still administratively possible, and a marked diagnostic paper is the most persuasive thing to bring to it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an Al Barari villa?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For mathematics specifically this costs very little: a session is worked problems on a shared screen with the student's own working visible, plus a paper marked in front of them. What it gains is a shortlist of tutors who teach your child's exact course rather than those willing to drive to a villa community at five on a weekday.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Higher Level maths need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the first Diploma year is usually enough if it starts early, rising to two in the term before mocks or the exam session. Higher Level consumes roughly half again the time of the Standard Level version of the same course, because there is more content, an extra paper and the same exploration. Beyond two sessions a week in term time the limiting factor becomes the student's capacity to do the problem sets, and the problem sets are where the improvement actually happens rather than in the session.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and university-student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for IB specialists, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Monthly, at one session a week, that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above respectively. Those are the market's published numbers, not IB Gram prices; our first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose my child's exploration topic?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test whether a proposed topic is viable, which is the single most valuable hour available on this component, and can explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor cannot do is choose the topic on the student's behalf or hand over a question to be adopted wholesale, because personal engagement carries 3 marks and rewards thinking the student actually did. The right scale is a question the student can genuinely investigate using mathematics at or slightly beyond their course level, with a real reason for having chosen it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths preparation suits Analysis and Approaches best?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, taken alongside the main course in Years 10 and 11. Both introduce calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities before the Diploma does, so the first Analysis and Approaches term is consolidation rather than first contact. The Extended or Higher tier in the main maths course is effectively a prerequisite in any case. A pupil entered for Core or Foundation who intends to take Diploma mathematics has a genuine content gap that should be addressed before Year 12.

faqs.question: Why do students lose marks when their answers are right?
faqs.answer: Because IB mark schemes award method marks for the steps, so a correct answer with no visible working scores below a wrong answer with sound method. The students most affected are the quick ones who have been rewarded for mental calculation since primary school. The second common loss is incomplete solution sets in trigonometry and multi-root equations, where a candidate reports the principal value and loses the rest of the interval. Both are habits rather than knowledge gaps, and both respond to a fortnight of deliberate practice with a tutor watching.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning better than a weekday evening for maths?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level, usually yes. Full-length timed papers need a rested student and a clear two hours, and from Al Barari a weekday session realistically starts at five after a commute and before other homework. A paper practised at seven in the evening is not a fair test of anything and tends to produce a misleadingly poor result that knocks confidence. The arrangement that works for many families here is a weekend morning for paper work and a shorter weekday slot for topic teaching.

faqs.question: How does the Middle Years Programme prepare a student for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Unevenly. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria including investigating patterns, which rewards generalising and justifying, so pupils from that route often arrive stronger at investigation and weaker at algebraic fluency than their IGCSE counterparts. That reverses the usual diagnosis: where an IGCSE entrant typically needs help with the exploration's open-ended demands, a Middle Years entrant more often needs drilling on manipulation. Knowing which route your child came through tells a tutor where to look first.

faqs.question: Should the same Al Barari tutor take both maths and physics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and in the Diploma it can be genuinely useful because a physics difficulty is frequently a mathematics difficulty wearing a different label. A tutor seeing both will spot that the problem in a fields question is rearranging rather than physics. The limit is level: at Higher Level in both subjects the right answer is usually two specialists, because Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Physics Higher Level are each narrow specialisms. Sessions remain separate one-to-one lessons in consecutive slots in either case.

faqs.question: Do maths tutors in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with suspicion. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask the same of any agency placing a tutor.

intro.heading: Where an Al Barsha Diploma student actually is in the maths course this November
paragraphs: It is early November. A DP2 student at a school around Al Barsha has roughly seven months of course left and about eight weeks of usable term before the winter break closes the door on quiet work. The syllabus is not the problem by this point. The problem is that three things have landed on the same desk: an exploration that needs a question and a data set, a set of January mocks that will be reported home, and the topics from DP1 that were understood once and have not been touched since. An IB maths tutor in Al Barsha is hired now because this is the fortnight when all three become visible at the same time.

For DP1 students the November pressure is different and just as real. Most schools in the Al Barsha cluster ask students to confirm Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and Higher or Standard Level, somewhere between late November and the February review. That decision is usually made on how the first term felt, which is the worst available evidence. A student who found the AA algebra chapter unpleasant may simply have missed two weeks of index laws in Year 11. A student who is cruising through AI Standard Level may be closing a door on an engineering degree they have not thought about yet.

The exploration is where the term either banks marks or loses them. It carries twenty of the available marks and is assessed against five criteria lettered A to E. Schools in Dubai typically run an internal timeline with a topic proposal in Term 1, a full draft in Term 2 and one round of written feedback, because the IB permits a single formal round of comment on a draft. A student who arrives at the Term 2 draft deadline with a borrowed topic and no personal data has already capped two criteria before a tutor can help. Getting the question right in November is worth more than any amount of polishing in March.

Then there is the mock. January mocks at most Al Barsha-area schools are sat under exam conditions on past papers, and they are the first time a student experiences two ninety-minute papers back to back at Standard Level, or two two-hour papers plus a one-hour Paper 3 at Higher Level. Nearly every mark lost in a first mock is lost to timing, calculator policy and notation rather than to not knowing the content. That is a coachable set of problems, but only if the coaching happens before the mock rather than in response to the report that follows it.

IB Gram works to that calendar. Lessons are delivered live online over video, one to one, scheduled around an Al Barsha school run rather than around a tutor's driving radius. A family in Al Barsha 2 gets a tutor who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level every week, not whichever maths graduate is free to drive from Al Quoz at five o'clock. The free trial lesson exists so the match can be tested on a real topic from the student's own current unit before any money changes hands.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: Al Barsha holds one of the denser concentrations of IB and British curriculum schools in Dubai, so a maths tutor working this neighbourhood meets students at four distinct points. The notes below say what each stage demands in maths specifically, and what the November position looks like at each one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes a maths course: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Assessment is two or three written papers plus the exploration. AA Standard Level sits Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each ninety minutes and each worth forty per cent. Higher Level in either route sits two two-hour papers at thirty per cent each and a one-hour Paper 3 worth twenty, with the exploration taking the last twenty.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, and KHDA inspects the schools that deliver it annually. For an Al Barsha DP2 student in November the live tasks are the exploration draft and the January mock. For DP1, it is the AA-against-AI confirmation. Neither is an exam-hall problem yet, which is precisely why the work is easy to postpone.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP maths is assessed against four criteria rather than by percentage: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Standard and Extended pathways diverge from MYP 4. The criterion that catches students out is investigating patterns, because it asks for generalisation and proof of a rule rather than a correct answer, and nothing in a primary maths background rehearses that.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai International Academy Al Barsha runs the full IB continuum, so a student there meets criterion-based maths marking years before the Diploma. In November, MYP 5 students are typically mid-way through the eAssessment preparation year, and the gap that matters is algebraic fluency: a student who cannot manipulate an expression quickly will spend the Diploma translating instead of thinking.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Most British curriculum schools around Al Barsha run IGCSE Mathematics at 16 before students split towards A Level or the Diploma. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher are the two common entries. Both reward algebraic manipulation far more heavily than the earlier years do, and both assume a calculator throughout, which leaves an exposed gap for any student heading towards AA Standard Level and its non-calculator Paper 1.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May-June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres. A Year 11 student in Al Barsha sitting a November entry is in the exam window as this page is read.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP maths is taught inside units of inquiry rather than as a separate subject block, which suits conceptual understanding and can leave number fluency uneven. The practical consequence shows up four years later: a student who never drilled times tables and fraction arithmetic spends MYP and then Diploma maths doing arithmetic in working memory that should be automatic, and runs out of time on papers for reasons that have nothing to do with the topic.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Barsha families move between a PYP primary and a British secondary, or the reverse, inside the same postcode. The transition gaps are specific and short: formal written methods, negative number work and early algebraic notation. Half a term of weekly online work closes them, and doing it in Year 6 is cheaper than doing it in Year 12.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: An IB maths tutor in Al Barsha is asked for one of a small number of things. Each line below names the course or component, the level it runs at, and what the November work on it looks like for a student in this cluster.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, and the one UAE and overseas engineering, physics and economics degrees usually expect. Standard Level loses most marks on the non-calculator Paper 1, where index and log manipulation, trigonometric identities and differentiation from first principles have to be clean without a screen to check them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, calculator-permitted throughout. Standard Level students lose marks not on calculation but on interpretation: writing what a regression gradient means in the context given, choosing the correct statistical test, and stating a conclusion the data actually supports.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks, five criteria lettered A to E. Criterion C, personal engagement, and criterion D, reflection, are the two most commonly under-marked, because they require the student to have made choices and then interrogated them rather than to have performed a procedure correctly.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, AA
subjects.description: A non-calculator paper is a separate skill from the syllabus it tests. Exact-value trigonometry, surd arithmetic, log laws and algebraic fraction work all have to run without a device. Students who prepared with a graphical calculator in hand for two years meet this properly for the first time in a January mock.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level
subjects.description: One hour, twenty per cent of the grade, two extended problem-solving questions that build a result in stages. It rewards reading the whole question before starting and carrying notation forward consistently. It is the component most often left unpractised because it looks unlike anything else in the course.

subjects.name: Calculus for AA
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration carry a large share of both papers. The HL extension into implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and by parts is where a student who coped with Standard Level content starts to feel the level difference properly, usually in Term 2 of DP1.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability for AI
subjects.description: Regression, correlation, the normal distribution, hypothesis testing and chi-squared. Marks are lost in the wording of conclusions rather than in the arithmetic. A chi-squared test performed correctly and then concluded without reference to the significance level earns part marks only.

subjects.name: Vectors and complex numbers
subjects.description: Two Higher Level topics that reward visualisation. Vector geometry questions on lines and planes, and complex number work in modulus-argument form including de Moivre's theorem, are standard Paper 2 and Paper 3 territory and are usually taught late in DP1.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator fluency
subjects.description: The permitted calculator is examinable in effect. Finding intersections, solving numerically, running a regression and reading a distribution all have to be fast and correct under time. Students who learned the device by trial and error carry a two-to-three minute penalty on every question that needs it.

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, week by week
paragraphs: Between early November and the winter break there are about eight teachable weeks. That is enough to fix one structural problem properly or to patch four superficially, and families who decide which in week one get more out of the term than families who start by asking for general maths help.

For a DP2 student the sequence is fixed by the school's own exploration timeline and its mock dates. Weeks one and two belong to the exploration question, because every later criterion depends on it. Weeks three to five are the first real timed paper work on DP1 content, which is also where a student discovers that the topics from last year have decayed. Weeks six to eight are mock rehearsal: full papers, to time, marked properly.

For a DP1 student the same eight weeks carry the route decision. If AA against AI is still open, the useful thing is not a conversation about which is harder but a diagnostic: give the student a non-calculator algebra set and an interpretation-heavy statistics set, and see which one produces work rather than silence. That evidence is worth more than a preference formed in week three of term.
The table below is the shape most Al Barsha Diploma families end up with. It is not a syllabus; it is an allocation of eight weeks that assumes one session a week and homework between them.

One practical note on scheduling it in Al Barsha. School finish times, the drive back from campuses along Sheikh Zayed Road and the fact that most Diploma students are also running Internal Assessment deadlines in two or three other subjects mean the realistic slot is a single fixed weekday evening, held every week, rather than a flexible arrangement that quietly becomes fortnightly. Eight weeks only works as eight weeks if the eighth one actually happens.

sections.heading: The exploration, read criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is twenty of the marks in every IB maths course, at both levels and on both routes. It is assessed against five criteria, lettered A to E, and the mark totals differ between them. That asymmetry is the single most useful piece of information a DP2 student can have in November, because it tells them where to spend the next six weeks.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries the largest allocation, and it is the criterion a topic choice either enables or forecloses. A question that can be answered with a few lines of routine Standard Level work cannot reach the top band however well it is written. A question that requires genuine selection and application of technique at the level studied can. This is why the topic has to be settled first and polished later, not the reverse.

Criteria C and D, personal engagement and reflection, are where UAE students lose the most avoidable marks. Both require evidence of thinking, not of effort. Personal engagement means the student made choices that were theirs: a data set they collected, a context they know, a question they wanted answered. Reflection means they interrogated what they did: why that technique, what the limitation was, what the result does and does not show. A paragraph at the end saying the investigation was interesting earns nothing.

A tutor's role here has a hard boundary, and this page states it plainly. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what a criterion means, question a student's reasoning and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or complete any part of an exploration. The IB treats that as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

sections.heading: What AA and AI papers are actually worth, and what that means for revision
paragraphs: A surprising number of students revise without knowing the weighting of the component they are revising for. Standard Level in both routes sits two papers at forty per cent each, with the exploration taking the remaining twenty. Higher Level in both routes sits three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty per cent, again with twenty for the exploration. The Higher Level Paper 3 is therefore worth as much as the entire exploration, and it is routinely the least practised thing in the course.

The calculator rules split the routes. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator; AA Paper 2 permits one. Applications and Interpretation permits a calculator on every paper. This is not a detail. It means an AA student needs two separate kinds of preparation, and it means the single most common January mock shock, a collapsed Paper 1 mark, is predictable and preventable in November.

For an AI student the equivalent trap is verbal rather than technical. The arithmetic is done by the device; the marks sit in interpretation. Writing what a gradient means in context, stating a hypothesis test conclusion with reference to the significance level, and saying what a model does not capture are all mark-bearing sentences that students who are good at calculation often skip.
Revision time should follow the weighting and the failure mode, not the comfort. The table sets out what each component is worth and what to do about it.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the decision an Al Barsha DP1 student makes this term
paragraphs: The route decision is made on bad evidence more often than any other choice in the Diploma. A student picks the course that felt easier in the first six weeks, or the one a friend chose, or the one a parent heard was better for university. Term 1 of DP1 is when the decision is still cheap to change and when the evidence is finally available.

The honest framing is that neither route is the easy one. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy, proof-aware and non-calculator in part. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-heavy, statistics-dense and demands written interpretation at a level many strong calculators find uncomfortable. A student who writes poorly about numbers will struggle in AI exactly as a student with weak algebra struggles in AA.

Where it does matter is at the other end. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and many economics degrees commonly ask for Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, and UAE universities set their own prerequisites that have to be read on their own admissions pages rather than assumed. A student in Al Barsha heading towards a technical degree should confirm the requirement with the named university before confirming the route, because reversing this choice in DP2 is close to impossible.
Tutoring helps here by replacing opinion with a diagnostic. Two short timed sets, one algebraic and one interpretive, generate more useful evidence in ninety minutes than a term of impressions.

The timing matters as much as the diagnostic. A route change requested in Term 1 of DP1 is usually a form and a conversation with the coordinator; the same request in Term 3 means catching up a year of the other course alongside everything else, and by DP2 it is effectively closed. Treat this term as the window it is.

sections.heading: What IB maths tutoring costs around Al Barsha, as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Most published comparisons quote an hourly rate, which is not the number a family budgets against. A household plans by the month, so start there. A single weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor working online comes to roughly four to five hours a month, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at around AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Translating that back to the hour: the budget online tier, typically university students, runs about AED 45-150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate putting the specialist band at AED 200-450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour by the same sources.

Packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of these are market figures published by other providers and carry their dates and sources; none of them is an IB Gram price list. What IB Gram quotes depends on level, subject and frequency, and the way to find out what a specific plan costs is the consultation after the free trial lesson.

One piece of context worth having while budgeting: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A family whose school bill is flat this year has a clearer view of what a tutoring line can absorb than one absorbing a fee increase at the same time.

sections.heading: Online against an in-home tutor on an Al Barsha school run
paragraphs: The in-home question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. Hiring a tutor who drives to an Al Barsha villa is a real option in this market, it costs more per hour because travel is priced in, and the pool of people willing to make the drive at five o'clock on a Tuesday is the pool you choose from. That last point is the one that matters for a subject as specialised as Higher Level Analysis and Approaches.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and that service exists only in India. Teaching here is live online, one to one, over video, with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. The argument for it is not that it is cheaper, although at AED 150-300 against AED 180-500 it usually is. The argument is selection: an Al Barsha family gets a tutor who teaches AA Higher Level every week of the year, rather than whoever is free and within a twenty-minute radius.

There is an Al Barsha-specific operational point too. Bus loops out of Al Barsha South and the Al Khail school corridor are long, and a student who leaves school at 15:00 may not be home until 16:45. An in-home session booked for 16:00 either starts late or starts with a tutor waiting in the lobby on the clock. An online session booked for 17:00 starts at 17:00, and the ten minutes a child needs to put a bag down are not billable travel.

Group classes at a tuition centre are the third option and the cheapest per student. They work for a shared syllabus push and not for an exploration or a specific Paper 3 weakness, because a group cannot pursue one student's error pattern.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Exam calendars are published forwards and lived backwards. A Diploma candidate in Al Barsha does not need to memorise a date; they need to know what should already be finished by the time each milestone arrives. Dubai candidates sit the May session, and the school's own internal deadlines for the exploration and for mocks arrive long before it.

The IB's session and results dates are published by the IB itself and by each school's Diploma coordinator, and they are the only sources worth acting on. This page deliberately publishes no IB exam or results date, because a wrong date a parent acts on is worse than no date at all. Confirm every one with the school coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages.

For the Cambridge and Pearson qualifications that sit alongside the Diploma in this neighbourhood, the published position is firmer. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May-June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026.
