sections.heading: The Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies load nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A maths plan built for an Al Barsha student has to fit around subjects that are not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's published requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any tutoring in those subjects can be described. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

Why this belongs on a maths page: a Diploma student carrying six subjects plus the core plus mandatory UAE subjects has a fixed number of evening hours. A maths plan that ignores the Arabic timetable gets abandoned in week three. Scheduling around it from the start is the difference between a plan and an intention.

sections.heading: KHDA, the schools around Al Barsha, and what an inspection band means
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. An Al Barsha family is in KHDA territory, and KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak.

The scale of the market around this neighbourhood is worth stating. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools taking the largest share of enrolment, Indian curriculum next, then US curriculum, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for about a fourteenth of enrolment. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent.

What an inspection band does not tell a parent is anything about their own child's maths set. A school rated Outstanding can still have a DP2 cohort where half the students have never sat a timed non-calculator paper, and a school in a lower band can have a maths department that drills technique relentlessly. The band describes the institution; the mark scheme describes the student.

IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or accreditation, and this page claims none. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram has no UAE premises and does not hold that permit. Individual private tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through MoHRE's own smart app, website and e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

process.title: Tell us the route, the level and the deadline
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard Level, the school, and what the nearest deadline is: an exploration sign-off, a January mock, the May session. Those four facts determine the match, and a route named wrongly wastes the first two sessions.

process.title: A free trial lesson on live work
process.description: The trial runs on the topic the student is in this week, not on a diagnostic quiz. A parent can see whether the tutor explains in a way their child follows, and the tutor can see where the gaps actually are. No payment is taken before the trial happens.

process.title: An eight-week plan with a named outcome
process.description: After the trial, a written plan for the rest of the term: which weeks go on the exploration, which on timed paper work, and what should exist by the winter break. A plan with a stated end state is reviewable; a plan to have lessons is not.

process.title: Weekly sessions with work in between
process.description: A fixed slot after the Al Barsha school run, work set between sessions and marked at the start of the next, and short notes home that say what was done rather than that progress was good. The slot moves for Ramadan or for mock weeks by arrangement.

process.title: Review at the mock, change if needed
process.description: The January mock is the first honest measurement of the plan. The error log, sorted by cause, drives what changes. If the match is not working the tutor changes without a penalty, because a term spent with the wrong teacher is the expensive outcome here.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one route and one level
whyPoints.description: A tutor who teaches AA Higher Level weekly brings a different instinct from a general maths graduate covering everything. The match is made on route and level first, which is only possible because the pool is not limited to people who can drive to Al Barsha by five.

whyPoints.title: The exploration taught, not written
whyPoints.description: Criterion coaching, technique selection and feedback on the student's own draft, with an explicit statement of the boundary. A tutor who offers to write any part of an exploration is exposing the student to an IB malpractice finding, and that is the student's problem, not the tutor's.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Three of six ranking competitors in this market publish no price at all. The AED bands on this page are market figures with their sources named and dated, so a family can see where any quote sits before they ask for one.

whyPoints.title: Sessions timed to the Al Barsha school run
whyPoints.description: Bus loops out of Al Barsha South and the Al Khail corridor run long. A session set for 17:00 and held online starts at 17:00, rather than absorbing a tutor's drive through Hessa Street traffic into the billed hour.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no school partnership, no grade guarantee, no statistic without a source. Every regulatory fact on this page is attributable to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and the IB dates a family needs come from the school's coordinator.

faqs.question: It is November and my child is in DP2 — is it too late to start IB maths tutoring in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: No, but what you buy changes. Starting in November, there are about eight teachable weeks before the winter break, and they are best spent on two things: getting the exploration question right, because every criterion depends on it, and establishing a real timed-paper baseline before January mocks. What is no longer realistic is re-teaching DP1 from the start. A tutor working from an error log sorted by cause rather than by chapter can usually lift a predicted grade meaningfully across one term. Starting in March is a different and much narrower conversation.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Barsha family expect to pay a month for weekly IB maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Budget by the month rather than the hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures with their dates, not IB Gram's price list. What a specific plan costs here depends on level, route and frequency, and the consultation after the free trial is where that number is set.

faqs.question: My child is choosing between Maths AA and AI this term — how do we decide?
faqs.answer: Replace the preference with a diagnostic. Give the student one short timed non-calculator algebra set and one interpretation-heavy statistics set, and see which produces work rather than silence. Then check the destination: engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and many economics degrees commonly ask for Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and each university publishes its own requirement, which has to be read rather than assumed. Neither route is the easy one. AA punishes weak algebra and AI punishes weak writing about numbers, and the choice is close to irreversible once DP2 starts.

faqs.question: How much exploration help can a tutor give before it counts as malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the mathematics a topic needs, explain what each criterion means and how it is marked, question the student's reasoning, and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or complete any part of the exploration, and nobody here will. The IB treats produced coursework as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student. Anyone offering a finished exploration is selling an expulsion risk. The school also permits only one formal round of feedback on a draft, which is why the draft has to be the student's own.

faqs.question: Which parts of Maths AA Paper 1 cost Al Barsha students the most marks in a January mock?
faqs.answer: The non-calculator ones, and predictably so. Exact-value trigonometry, surd and index manipulation, log laws and differentiation from first principles all have to run clean without a screen. Students who prepared for two years with a graphical calculator in hand meet that properly for the first time under mock conditions, and the mark collapse reads as a content problem when it is a fluency problem. The fix is unglamorous: short, frequent, timed non-calculator sets from November, so that by January the hand does the algebra while the head does the question.

faqs.question: What is Higher Level Paper 3 and why do students arrive at it unprepared?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a one-hour paper sat only by Higher Level candidates in both routes, worth twenty per cent of the grade, and built from two extended problem-solving questions that develop a result across several parts. It is worth as much as the entire exploration. Students arrive unprepared because it resembles nothing else in the course and is therefore easy for a scheme of work to postpone. Practising it means sitting whole questions to time and learning to carry notation and results forward between parts, rather than drilling topics in isolation.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session realistically begin for a child at an Al Barsha South school?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first assume. The bus loops serving Al Barsha South and the Al Khail school corridor are long, and a student who leaves at 15:00 can reach home nearer 16:45 than 16:00. A 17:00 start holds up across a whole term where a 16:15 start quietly becomes a weekly argument. Because teaching is online, the ten minutes a child needs to put a bag down and eat something are not being paid for as a tutor's waiting time, and a slot that starts on time every week is worth more than a slot that starts early on paper.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our villa in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor travels to a UAE address; that service exists only in India. UAE teaching is live online, one to one, over video with a shared whiteboard. In-home tutoring is a real option in this market from other providers, quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, and the trade-off is honest: you gain a person in the room and you choose from whoever will drive to Al Barsha at five o'clock. For Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, that pool is small.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP2 maths student in this neighbourhood usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour is the common starting point and is enough if the student is broadly on track and the aim is to stop gaps opening. Two becomes sensible in two situations: an exploration that is behind schedule, where one session goes on the report and one on course content, and a Higher Level student who needs separate Paper 1 and Paper 3 practice. More than two a week rarely helps during term, because the limiting factor is the work done between sessions rather than the contact hours themselves.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how can a parent check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Which Al Barsha schools do you most often support IB maths students from?
faqs.answer: Requests from this neighbourhood come largely from the IB continuum and British curriculum schools inside a few kilometres: Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, GEMS Dubai American Academy, GEMS Founders School Al Barsha South, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Repton Al Barsha and the American School of Dubai, plus the Al Khail corridor campuses a short drive away. Students are supported from these schools; no school named is a partner, client or endorser of IB Gram, and none has any affiliation with it. Named schools here are context for the curriculum mix, nothing more.

faqs.question: Will tutoring follow my child's own school scheme of work or run a separate syllabus?
faqs.answer: It follows the school. A tutor working to a different sequence than the class creates two sets of homework and one confused student. In practice that means asking for the unit plan or the current topic each week, aligning timed practice to what the department has actually taught, and holding back topics the class has not reached unless the student needs them for the exploration. The exception is technique work, such as non-calculator fluency, which has to run alongside the scheme from November rather than waiting for a slot in it.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a normal adjustment rather than a favour. Dubai school timetables shorten during Ramadan and household rhythms change, so a mid-afternoon slot that worked in January is often unusable. The practical options are a later evening session after Iftar, a weekend morning slot, or a short pause with the hours carried forward. Because teaching is online, moving a session costs nothing in travel and does not depend on a tutor's willingness to drive across Dubai late at night. Agreeing the Ramadan pattern in advance avoids losing three weeks to rescheduling.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the exact route and level we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than matched to an approximation. If no Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist has a slot at the time you need, the honest options are a different time with the right tutor, a wait of a week or two, or a Standard Level-strong tutor for consolidation work while the specialist slot opens. What does not happen is a general maths tutor being presented as a route specialist. Coverage limits are disclosed because the alternative is a family discovering the mismatch in session four, having paid for three.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE results from last year tell us anything useful about Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Something, but less than parents expect. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher both permit a calculator throughout and both reward procedural accuracy, so a strong grade confirms the student can execute. It does not test non-calculator fluency, radian measure, function notation at Diploma level, or the expectation that a method is justified rather than merely correct. A student with a grade 8 who has never worked without a calculator is still exposed on AA Paper 1. The useful diagnostic is a short Diploma-style set, not last summer's certificate.

intro.heading: What actually differs between Al Barsha South and the next community over
paragraphs: A family in Al Barsha South searching for an IB maths tutor is usually weighing one local question against another: would there be more choice in Al Barsha 1, in Dubai Hills Estate, in Jumeirah Village Circle? It is a reasonable question with an unhelpful answer, because the thing that varies across those four communities is not the supply of mathematicians. It is which Diploma school the children attend, and therefore which of the two IB mathematics routes they are enrolled on.

That matters more than any amount of local supply. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with separate papers, separate calculator expectations and separate university consequences. A student on Applications and Interpretation Higher Level has a statistics-heavy course with a Paper 3 investigation; a student on Analysis and Approaches Higher Level has a proof-and-calculus course with a non-calculator Paper 1 worth 30% of the grade. Put a strong Analysis teacher in front of an Applications student and the lesson is pleasant and nearly useless.

Dubai's school market is the densest in the UAE: KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for roughly 7% of total private enrolment. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places. That growth is why the IB cohort in New Dubai is spread thinly across many schools rather than concentrated in a few, and why no single residential community contains a deep bench of Diploma mathematics specialists.

There is a second reason the local-supply question misleads. A Diploma mathematics teacher working in a Dubai school is covered by rules about who they may tutor privately. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So the teachers physically nearest a child in Al Barsha South are frequently the very people who should not be tutoring that child, which shrinks a local pool that was never large.

The comparison this page makes, then, is not Al Barsha South against Dubai Hills on convenience. It is a comparison of what a student actually needs against what proximity can supply. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school or examination board, and lessons for Al Barsha South families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. Said plainly, because a page that implies otherwise is selling something it does not have.

The rest of this page sets out the route decision, the paper weightings, the four places marks disappear, the twenty marks of the Exploration, and what the Dubai market charges for a specialist. It ends with the comparison stated bluntly: from Al Barsha South, Arjan or Dubai Hills, the correct answer is the same, and it is not the nearest tutor.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.programmesIntro: Al Barsha South sits within reach of IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools alike, so the mathematics question arrives at different ages in different households. These are the three programme stages where a maths tutor is actually bought in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes mathematics, choosing Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level sits two papers weighted 40% each plus the Exploration at 20%. Higher Level sits three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% plus the Exploration at 20%. The route is normally fixed in the first term of DP1 and is difficult to change after the second.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary in which combinations they timetable. A smaller IB cohort may offer Analysis at Higher Level and Applications only at Standard, which quietly removes a route a child in Al Barsha South might have been better suited to. That is a question to ask the school before option forms are signed, not after.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, each out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Criterion A rewards knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating and D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no terminal paper in most schools, which is precisely why the move into Diploma mathematics catches students out.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the single most common reason an Al Barsha South family books maths tutoring. An MYP 5 student used to criterion-marked investigations meets timed papers, a formula booklet and a graphic display calculator in DP1, and the drop in reported grade is usually about assessment format rather than ability.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics, as the other route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Many Al Barsha South children sit Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 before moving to a Diploma school at 16. The three leave students in different places: 0607 students arrive used to a graphics calculator, while 0580 students arrive with stronger hand algebra and no calculator fluency.
programmes.countryNote: A student entering DP1 from 0580 Extended is usually well placed for Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 and underprepared for calculator work. A student entering from 0607 is the reverse. Naming which of the three your child sat is the fastest way to get the first Diploma maths lesson aimed correctly.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.subjectsIntro: Maths is the page subject, but the comparison families make across New Dubai communities usually involves a second or third subject too. These are the Diploma courses most frequently requested alongside mathematics by Al Barsha South households.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and is worth 40% at Standard Level and 30% at Higher. Marks are lost in proof structure, in integration by substitution and in trigonometric identities rushed under time pressure rather than in the harder-looking topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use throughout, with a calculator permitted on every paper. The commonest mark loss is interpretation: a correct regression or hypothesis test followed by a sentence that does not answer the question in context. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Assessed as Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the Scientific Investigation at 20%. Students with weak Analysis and Approaches algebra usually present as weak at physics, because rearranging before substituting is where the working falls apart rather than the physics itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised as Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3 under the current guide, with the same 36/44/20 assessment split as physics. Moles, equilibrium and energetics carry the calculation marks, which is why a chemistry request from a Diploma student often turns out to be a mathematics request.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the Internal Assessment commentaries decide most grades. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that reward the same arithmetic discipline as Applications and Interpretation, and students comfortable in one are usually comfortable in the other.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper-based theory alongside the solution development work. Students on Applications and Interpretation often pair this well, since both reward algorithmic thinking and precise definitions over elegant proof.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The data-based questions and the statistics in the Scientific Investigation are where mathematical weakness shows. A biology student who cannot handle standard deviation and error bars loses marks in a subject they otherwise know well.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Toolkit application and the Higher Level quantitative content, including ratio and investment appraisal. Frequently chosen alongside Applications and Interpretation by Al Barsha South students aiming at business degrees.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay and the Individual Oral. Requested alongside maths by students whose difficulty is written structure rather than content, which is a different tutoring problem with a different cadence.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition of three objects with a commentary, the TOK essay on a prescribed title, and a 4,000-word Extended Essay. Supported as process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafting, never as writing or redrafting on their behalf.

sections.heading: Al Barsha South against Al Barsha 1, Dubai Hills and JVC, judged on maths routes
paragraphs: Set the four communities side by side and the differences are real but not the ones families expect. Al Barsha South has no Metro station and a bus-dependent school run. Al Barsha 1 is denser and closer to several large schools. Dubai Hills Estate has newer provision and shorter journeys. Jumeirah Village Circle has schools inside the district itself. All four draw from an overlapping set of Diploma schools, and none of them contains a concentrated supply of Diploma mathematics teaching.

What does change is the probability of a particular route. A community feeding mainly British-curriculum schools produces students who arrive at Diploma maths from IGCSE, usually onto Analysis and Approaches. A community feeding an IB continuum school produces students arriving from MYP, with a higher share on Applications and Interpretation because the school timetables it. The tutoring need follows the route, so two households three kilometres apart can need genuinely different people.

The table sets this out as a comparison a parent can check. It deliberately does not rank the communities, because ranking them would be dishonest: the quality of a Diploma maths lesson in 2026 has almost nothing to do with the driving distance between two addresses in New Dubai. What it has to do with is whether the person teaching has taught that route at that level and marked its papers.

One practical difference does survive the comparison, and it is scheduling. Al Barsha South and Arjan return later from the school run than Al Barsha 1 or JVC, so the first workable weekday slot is later. For non-calculator Paper 1 work, which is cognitively demanding and unforgiving, a later and calmer slot is usually better anyway.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and what each closes off
paragraphs: The route decision is normally made in the first term of DP1, often on a form, and is hard to reverse by the second. It is a bigger decision than it looks, because it is partly a mathematics decision and partly a university decision.

Analysis and Approaches is the proof and calculus course. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, worth 40% at Standard Level and 30% at Higher. The content rewards algebraic fluency, and the students who do well in it are usually the ones who were comfortable manipulating expressions at IGCSE. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics and modelling course, with a calculator permitted on every paper, and Higher Level content including matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams. Both are respectable courses; they are not interchangeable.

The admissions side is where families most need accurate information and most often get vague reassurance. Many engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees ask specifically for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, while a wide range of business, social science, life science and design programmes accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. The only reliable method is to read the stated entry requirements on the university's own admissions page for the specific course and year of entry, because requirements differ between institutions and change between cycles. Any provider telling you one route is universally accepted is guessing on your behalf.

For tutoring, the honest position is that the earlier a mismatch is caught, the cheaper it is. A student on Analysis and Approaches Higher Level who cannot do Paper 1 algebra reliably by the end of DP1 is in a two-year problem; the same student moved to Standard Level, or to Applications, in term two is in a manageable one. We will say which it looks like after a diagnostic lesson rather than selling two years of support into the wrong course.

sections.heading: Paper by paper, Higher Level against Standard Level
paragraphs: The weightings are published and worth knowing precisely, because they tell a family where to spend money. At Standard Level in either route, there are two papers at 40% each plus the Exploration at 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers at 30%, 30% and 20%, plus the Exploration at 20%.

Read that arithmetic properly and a pattern appears. At Standard Level, a single paper is worth twice the Exploration. At Higher Level, Paper 3 and the Exploration are worth the same 20% each, and Paper 3 is the component students have practised least because schools reach it last. A Higher Level student who has sat two full Paper 3s before the mock is unusual, and it shows.

This is also why the Standard versus Higher conversation is a resource conversation rather than a pride one. Higher Level mathematics in either route is a substantially larger commitment of hours, and it only pays if the student needs it for a stated degree requirement or genuinely enjoys the subject. A student taking Higher Level maths because the school expects it, while two other Higher Level subjects suffer, has made an expensive choice that no tutor can repair.

For an Al Barsha South family deciding how much to buy, the practical plan is usually weekly support on content through DP1, then a technique block on the lowest-practised paper in DP2, with the Exploration supervised separately. That ordering treats the weightings as the budget rather than treating every topic as equal.

sections.heading: The four places IB maths marks go, identically in every community
paragraphs: Across every New Dubai community we see the same four leaks, in roughly the same proportions. They are worth naming because they are diagnosable in one lesson, and because none of them is fixed by finding somebody who lives closer.

The first is working shown too briefly. IB mark schemes award method marks, and a student who writes a line of reasoning in their head and an answer on the page loses marks on correct mathematics. The second is calculator dependence in the wrong direction: Analysis and Approaches students reaching for the graphic display calculator on Paper 1 questions they must do by hand, and Applications students accepting a displayed value without an estimate to sanity-check it against.

The third is command and context. A regression line correctly calculated and then interpreted in a sentence that does not answer the question asked scores the calculation and nothing else. This is the dominant loss in Applications and Interpretation, and it responds very quickly to being shown a mark scheme.

The fourth is Paper 3 at Higher Level, and it is less a weakness than an absence. Schools reach Paper 3 style questions late, so students meet a 20% component with two or three attempts behind them. Four or five full Paper 3s under timing, marked properly, is one of the highest-value blocks of work available to a DP2 student in either route.

None of the four is a local phenomenon. We see the same proportions in Al Barsha South, in Arjan, in Dubai Hills Estate and in Jumeirah Village Circle, because they are products of how the course is assessed rather than of how any particular school teaches it. That is the practical case against choosing a tutor by driving distance: the problem in front of your child is a mark-scheme problem, and the person best placed to solve it is whoever has marked the most of those papers, wherever they happen to sit.

sections.heading: The Exploration: twenty marks, five criteria letters
paragraphs: The mathematical Exploration is 20% of the grade in all four route-and-level combinations, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria. Criterion A covers presentation and is worth 4. Criterion B is mathematical communication, worth 4. Criterion C is personal engagement, worth 3. Criterion D is reflection, worth 3. Criterion E is use of mathematics, worth 6 and the largest single allocation.

Knowing those letters changes how a student chooses a topic. Criterion E rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and at a level commensurate with the course, which means a beautifully written investigation built on arithmetic the student met two years ago cannot score well however polished it is. The commonest failure in Dubai cohorts is a topic with genuine personal interest and insufficient mathematics in it, and it is a failure that can be caught in the first conversation rather than three weeks before the school deadline.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and we state it precisely. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposed topic has enough mathematics to reach Criterion E, teach any technique the student needs, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft to completion or produce any part of the Exploration. IB academic-honesty rules put the consequence on the student, and a provider offering to supply a finished Exploration is offering to put your child at risk of a malpractice finding.

Deadlines are the school's. Diploma coordinators set internal dates for proposal, first draft and final submission that sit well before any external deadline, and those internal dates are what a tutoring plan has to respect. We take them from your child's coordinator rather than publishing a date here, and IB session and results dates are not stated anywhere on this page because they could not be confirmed from the IB's own site.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges a Diploma maths family
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most Al Barsha South families start. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which puts a budget online tier at roughly AED 45 to 150. For drilling non-calculator arithmetic with a DP1 student, that tier can genuinely be the right purchase, and saying otherwise would be dishonest.

It stops being the right purchase the moment the work requires knowing the course. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, which sets a qualified-tutor band around AED 150 to 300 online. Dedicated IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing 200 to 450 plus. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor at the top of the market.

In-home visits are priced on a different basis again. Bestimate lists in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with travel inside the hourly figure. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Those are other providers' published rates with their sources and dates, not an IB Gram price list. The comparison that matters for this page is simple: the premium between a general tutor and a route-matched Diploma specialist is one band, and it buys somebody who knows that Paper 1 forbids a calculator and that Criterion E is worth 6. The premium for travel buys travel, in a city where the Al Barsha interchange at 17:00 decides how much of it you are paying for. KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, is useful context: the fee line is flat, so the tutoring line is the one a family can still control.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education.

Private tutoring itself is regulated by permit. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so no figure can be quoted honestly.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a separate matter requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office, centre or branch, and claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

Two checks a parent can run without help. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE permit, since it costs them nothing and there is no reasonable excuse for not having it. And read your school's most recent KHDA inspection report, looking past the headline band at what the narrative says about teaching in mathematics specifically; a school rated Very Good overall can have a weaker maths department, and that is the paragraph worth finding.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same from Al Barsha South, Arjan or Dubai Hills
paragraphs: Put the comparison back together and it resolves. The four communities differ on school run timing, on which Diploma schools their children attend, and therefore on the mix of mathematics routes. They do not differ on the existence of a local Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist, because in a residential district of this size there is no such thing.

This is why the delivery answer does not change with the postcode. Lessons to Al Barsha South, Al Barsha 1, Arjan, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Dubai address; that service exists only in India. A family choosing by distance is selecting from everyone who can drive to them, which in practice means a general maths tutor. A family choosing by route is selecting from everyone who teaches their child's actual course.

The honest limits, stated before you enquire rather than after. A common combination such as Analysis and Approaches Standard Level is usually matched in a few days. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, with its matrices and graph theory content, is a narrower pool and can take longer, and occasionally we cannot cover a combination at all. We say so at the point of enquiry rather than matching you to whoever is free and hoping the fit holds.

What you get first is a free diagnostic lesson with a written outcome: the route, the level, which syllabus content is insecure, which of the four mark leaks is actually happening, and whether the Exploration topic has enough mathematics in it. If the conclusion is that your child needs a change of level rather than a tutor, we will write that down. It is a worse sale and a better answer.

process.title: Name the route and the level
process.description: Tell us whether it is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher, and which year of the Diploma. Those four facts decide the match. Without them the first lesson is spent establishing what a single line in your enquiry could have said.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson at no cost. The tutor tests a sample of syllabus content, looks at recent script evidence, and identifies which of the four common mark leaks is operating. You receive a written summary whether or not you go further.

process.title: Set a block against the weightings
process.description: We plan hours against what the components are worth rather than against the textbook order. For a Higher Level student late in DP1 that usually means Paper 3 practice and Exploration supervision before any further content teaching.

process.title: Work from official material
process.description: Homework comes from official past papers at the correct route and level, marked against published schemes. We cite and link the official source rather than reproducing or distributing it, so your child is working from the current version.

process.title: Review on a timed paper, then decide
process.description: Progress is measured on a full timed paper marked against the scheme, not on a sense that lessons are going well. If the gap has closed we stop. If it has not, we change the tutor or the approach rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the route, not the map
whyPoints.description: A student on Applications and Interpretation Higher Level is matched to someone who has taught matrices and Voronoi diagrams, not to the nearest available mathematician. Online delivery is what makes the pool large enough for that to be possible from Al Barsha South.

whyPoints.title: The weightings drive the plan
whyPoints.description: Hours are spent where marks are: Paper 3 and the Exploration are 20% each at Higher Level, and Paper 3 is the component schools reach last. Treating every topic as equally urgent is how a term of tutoring produces no grade change.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the Exploration
whyPoints.description: We teach technique, explain the five criteria and give feedback on the student's own draft. No tutor will write, redraft or produce any part of an Exploration. The malpractice consequence lands on the student, which is reason enough never to cross it.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, claims absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here belongs to the provider that published it, with the source named. We publish no success rate, no star rating and no grade guarantee, because we cannot evidence them and a page that cannot evidence a number should not print it.

whyPoints.title: University requirements checked, not asserted
whyPoints.description: We will tell you that many engineering and mathematics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and then tell you to read the course page for your child's year of entry. Nobody should take a route decision on a tutoring provider's summary.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated up front
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a narrow combination we say so at enquiry. A short wait for a route-matched Higher Level tutor is a better outcome than an immediate start with a generalist who has never seen a Paper 3.

faqs.question: Would my child get a better IB maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate than in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural rather than diplomatic. Neither community contains a concentrated supply of Diploma mathematics specialists, because Dubai's International Baccalaureate cohort is spread thinly across many schools rather than clustered in a few neighbourhoods. What genuinely differs between Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South is the school run and therefore the earliest workable session time. Since lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, the tutor pool is identical from both addresses, and the decision moves to which mathematics route your child is actually enrolled on.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Look at the Diploma option form or the subject list on the most recent report, which names the course in full. If it only says Mathematics, ask the Diploma coordinator directly; they answer this question constantly. The practical test is the calculator: an Analysis and Approaches student sits a Paper 1 with no calculator permitted, while an Applications and Interpretation student uses one on every paper. Getting this right before the first lesson matters more than anything else in your enquiry, because the two courses need different teaching.

faqs.question: Can my child change IB maths route or level after DP1 has started?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it gets harder every term. Schools usually allow a route or level change in the first term of DP1 and are reluctant after the second, because the content diverges quickly and the timetable blocks may not permit it. The honest signal to watch is whether a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student can do Paper 1 algebra reliably without a calculator by the end of DP1. If not, raise it with the coordinator immediately rather than buying two years of tutoring into a mismatch.

faqs.question: What exactly is Paper 3 and why do Higher Level students struggle with it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level and is worth 20% of the final grade. In Analysis and Approaches it is extended problem solving; in Applications and Interpretation it is an extended modelling investigation. Students struggle with it mainly because schools reach it last, so a cohort can meet a fifth of the assessment with two or three attempts behind them. It rewards reading a long stem carefully and following a structured argument rather than knowing additional content. Four or five full timed attempts, properly marked, is the fix.

faqs.question: How are the twenty Exploration marks actually distributed?
faqs.answer: Across five criteria. Criterion A, presentation, carries 4 marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries 4. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries 3. Criterion D, reflection, carries 3. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6 and is the largest single allocation. That distribution is why topic choice decides the grade: an investigation written with real personal interest but built on mathematics below the level of the course cannot reach the Criterion E marks, however well presented it is. Test the topic against Criterion E first.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths worth taking if my child finds it hard?
faqs.answer: Only if a stated degree requirement needs it or the student genuinely enjoys the subject. Higher Level mathematics in either route is a much larger commitment of hours, and those hours come out of two other Higher Level subjects. A student carrying Higher Level maths for status while their other grades slip has made an expensive choice no amount of tutoring repairs. Read the entry requirements on the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses your child is considering, for their year of entry, before treating the decision as settled.

faqs.question: My child came from MYP maths and the Diploma grades have dropped. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the assessment changed more than the mathematics did. MYP maths is marked against four criteria, each out of 8, in extended investigative tasks. Diploma maths is marked on timed papers against a mark scheme, with a formula booklet and a graphic display calculator. A student fluent in criterion-marked investigation can look weak in their first DP1 paper simply through unfamiliarity with the format. The fix is usually technique and timing work rather than content reteaching, and it tends to resolve within a term of weekly sessions.

faqs.question: Does coming from Cambridge 0580 or 0607 change what the first Diploma lesson covers?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. A student from Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended arrives with stronger hand algebra and limited graphics-calculator fluency, which suits Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 and leaves a gap on calculator papers. A student from Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 arrives comfortable with a graphics calculator and often weaker on manipulation by hand. Telling us which of the two your child sat lets the tutor open the right gap in the first lesson rather than discovering it in the third.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths specialist cost around Al Barsha South compared with a general tutor?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates fall into bands. Budget online tuition starts low, with Tutopiya listing from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Dedicated specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 200 to 450 plus. Those are other providers' figures with their sources. The step from generalist to route-matched specialist is one band, not several.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a villa in Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for families in Al Barsha South, Al Barsha 1, Arjan, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market is real and other providers publish it at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. What that premium buys is the travel, and in New Dubai at 17:00 the travel is considerable.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma maths session realistically start on a weekday in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Buses serving Al Barsha South generally return between about 15:20 and 16:10 depending on route, so 16:45 is the first slot that works without rushing a student straight from a bus into non-calculator algebra. Many families in Al Barsha South, Arjan and Dubai Science Park choose 19:00 or 19:30 instead, after parents are home. For Paper 1 work that later slot is usually better: it is the most cognitively demanding component and a tired student practising it badly reinforces the wrong habits.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Diploma student here usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session is the normal starting point and is enough for a content problem through DP1. A DP2 student with a specific paper weakness often does better with one weekly lesson plus a full timed paper sat alone between lessons, since the marking conversation is where the gain happens. Two sessions a week is worth buying only for a short defined block, usually before mocks or when a Higher Level student is making up lost ground on Paper 3. Open-ended twice-weekly arrangements tend to produce dependence rather than grades.

faqs.question: Where is the line between Exploration feedback and doing my child's work?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may explain what each of the five criteria rewards, discuss whether a proposed topic contains enough mathematics to reach Criterion E, teach any technique the student needs, and comment on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor must never write, redraft to completion or produce any part of the Exploration. IB academic-honesty rules place the consequence on the candidate, so a provider offering a finished Exploration is offering to put your child at risk of a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB session or results dates printed anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: Because we could not confirm them from the IB itself. The IB's own site returns an automated-access error, so no IB session or results date in this project has been verified at source. Publishing an unverified date on a page a parent plans around is worse than publishing none. UAE Diploma students sit the May session, with November available as a second session, and the dates that actually govern your child's year are the internal deadlines set by their Diploma coordinator. Ask the coordinator, and check ibo.org directly for session dates.

faqs.question: What if nobody teaches Applications and Interpretation Higher Level when we ask?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the enquiry rather than matching you to someone unsuitable. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is usually covered within a few days. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a narrower pool because of the matrices and graph theory content, so it can take longer, and occasionally a combination cannot be covered at all. In that case we say so and you are free to look elsewhere. A short wait for a route-matched tutor beats an immediate start with somebody who has never seen a Paper 3.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.closingHeading: The route decides the tutor, not the distance
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.closingBody: Everything on this page points one way. Between Al Barsha South, Al Barsha 1, Arjan, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle, what changes is the school run and the mix of mathematics routes. What does not change is that a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist is found by searching for the course, not the postcode. Send us the route, the level, the Diploma year and the component going wrong, and the first lesson is free. You will finish it with a written account of which syllabus content is insecure, which mark types are being dropped, and whether the Exploration topic has enough mathematics in it to reach the Criterion E marks.

intro.heading: Two courses with the same word on the timetable
paragraphs: The question behind most searches for an IB maths tutor in Al Furjan is whether anyone nearby actually knows this syllabus. The honest answer starts with a different question: which syllabus? Since the current structure, IB mathematics has been two separate courses. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches builds algebra, calculus and proof. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation builds statistics, modelling and technology-led methods. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct courses sharing one word on a school timetable.

A tutor who teaches maths in general will be competent in both and specialist in neither, and at Higher Level that gap is wide. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level examines proof by induction, complex numbers and calculus techniques that an Applications specialist may not have taught in years. Applications Higher Level examines statistical tests, matrices and graph theory that an Analysis specialist can do but has not taught to a mark scheme. The difference shows up on Paper 3.

Al Furjan makes this harder than it needs to be. The community sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, residential rather than academic, and the Diploma specialists in Dubai cluster near the schools that run the programme, which in this corridor are fewer than further north. The pool of people who will drive into the villa districts for a 17:00 lesson is small, and a small pool means taking the available tutor rather than the right course specialist.

IB Gram answers that by removing the drive. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and no tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. What that buys an Al Furjan family is a tutor matched to Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specifically, rather than to the subject called maths.

This page is written to be checkable. It sets out the two courses side by side with the university consequences, the paper structure and weightings at each level, where marks are actually lost rather than which topics feel hard, the exploration criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, and what the calculator is examined on. If a tutor cannot discuss those things, they are not teaching this syllabus.

One note on exam dates. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and we do not publish specific IB exam or results dates on these pages because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we will not put an unverified date in front of a parent who might act on it. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the real internal calendar, and that document is the one worth asking for in September. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which matter to the IGCSE families in this corridor, are published and are used elsewhere on this site with their sources attached.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Mathematics support looks different at each IB stage, and the handover points are where most damage happens. These are the stages an Al Furjan family will pass through.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Number sense, fact recall and the ability to explain a method aloud. PYP mathematics is embedded in transdisciplinary units rather than taught as a separate timetabled subject in the way parents often expect, so a gap in multiplication fluency or place value can persist without any assessment flagging it. Explaining a method is the skill that later becomes showing working for method marks.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Furjan primary children are home earliest, often by 15:30 on Dubai Investments Park routes, which makes short afternoon sessions practical. Forty minutes twice a week beats ninety minutes once, because fact fluency responds to frequency. This is also the cheapest point to fix a number gap that would otherwise resurface as an algebra problem in MYP 4.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D on an eight-point scale: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where capable students stall, because it asks for generalisation and justification rather than correct answers. Many schools also split MYP mathematics into standard and extended routes from MYP 4.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage that decides whether Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is realistic. Algebraic fluency built in MYP 4 and 5 is what makes the first Diploma term survivable, and it cannot be built in that term. Middle Years students in Al Furjan are home between 15:40 and 16:30, so a 17:00 slot is the usual fit for a weekly session through the year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one of the four mathematics courses. All four include an internally assessed exploration worth 20 marks against criteria A to E. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three, with Paper 3 carrying 20 per cent and consisting of extended problem-solving questions that reward sustained reasoning rather than question recognition.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Furjan generally travel to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor for school, so they are home closer to 17:00 and book 18:00 or 19:00 sessions. The course choice is made in Diploma 1 and has consequences well beyond school: some engineering programmes will not accept Applications and Interpretation, so the decision deserves checking against actual admissions pages rather than assumption.

programmes.name: The bridge into Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: A short block closing the gap between MYP 5 or Extended IGCSE and the first term of Diploma mathematics. In Analysis and Approaches that means function notation, algebraic manipulation without a calculator, and the beginnings of proof structure. In Applications it means confident use of the graphic display calculator and the vocabulary of statistical testing.
programmes.countryNote: This is the highest-value and least-bought intervention in the whole set. Four to six sessions over the summer cost a fraction of catching up during the first Diploma term, and they decide whether a student entering Higher Level stays there. Al Furjan families moving school for the Diploma also carry a settling period, which makes arriving with the algebra already fluent more valuable still.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Mathematics appears in more of the Diploma than its own timetable slot. These are the courses and components an Al Furjan family may need covered, and what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus, proof, complex numbers and statistics, examined across three papers with Paper 3 worth 20 per cent. The demand is sustained reasoning: a Paper 3 question runs for many parts and a student who loses the thread early cannot recover it. Non-calculator fluency is examined directly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same spine with reduced depth and no Paper 3. Two papers, one with and one without calculator access. The commonest failure is treating it as the safe option after Extended IGCSE: the calculus and the function work still move considerably faster than Year 11 pace, particularly in the first term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics, probability distributions, hypothesis testing, matrices, graph theory and modelling, with the graphic display calculator central throughout. Higher Level statistics goes well beyond what most students expect from the course's reputation, and Paper 3 presents extended modelling scenarios with real data.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and financial mathematics with heavy technology use across two papers. It suits students heading for social sciences, business or design. It is not a lighter version of Analysis and Approaches; it is a different selection of content with its own demands in interpretation and communication.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing marked out of 20 against criteria A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. The mark is decided far more by the choice of topic and the depth of reflection than by the difficulty of the mathematics attempted.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended problem solving
subjects.description: Two extended-response questions worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade in both courses. Scaffolded across many parts, so an early error propagates. The skill is reading the question's structure and recognising what each part is setting up, and it is trainable only by doing whole Paper 3 questions under timing with marked feedback.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: An examined skill, not a convenience. Students lose marks by solving graphically when working is required, by not knowing the statistical functions on their model, and by failing to state what was found with technology. The specific model matters, and a tutor should know the one your child's school uses.

subjects.name: MYP mathematics, standard and extended
subjects.description: Criteria A to D on an eight-point scale, with criterion B on investigating patterns being the most consistently under-scored. Many Dubai schools split standard and extended routes from MYP 4, and that split is the first decision point on the road to Analysis and Approaches Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics HL
subjects.description: A substantial share of Physics Higher Level marks depend on mathematical handling: rearranging relationships, gradient and area interpretation, logarithms and small-angle work. Students who are solid in Physics concepts but weak in algebra often need mathematics support rather than more Physics.

subjects.name: Quantitative work in Economics and Business
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics involves calculation and diagram interpretation that catches students who chose the subject expecting essays. Business Management brings break-even, investment appraisal and ratio work. In both cases the barrier is arithmetic confidence rather than economic understanding.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in mathematics
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised mathematical research. Essays fail when the research question has no mathematics in it or far too much, and that is diagnosable in one early session. Support is feedback on the student's own drafts and questioning of the question, never drafting.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge on mathematical knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge in Theory of Knowledge, and students taking Higher Level mathematics are often asked to write about it. The useful contribution a maths tutor makes is supplying real mathematical examples, since generic claims about certainty and proof score poorly.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: The choice is made in Diploma 1 and it follows a student into university applications, so it deserves more than a conversation about which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof course. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics, modelling and technology course. Both are rigorous, both run at two levels, and both carry the same exploration. They are not a hard version and an easy version of one subject.

The consequence that catches families is admissions. A number of engineering and mathematics degree programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and will not accept Applications and Interpretation in its place. Others accept either. The only reliable method is to read the admissions page of the specific universities and courses your child is considering, in Diploma 1, while the choice is still open rather than after it has closed.

The second consequence is fit. A student who is fluent algebraically and enjoys structure belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who is strong with data, context and technology but finds abstract manipulation a grind often performs considerably better in Applications and Interpretation, and a better grade in the right course beats a poor grade in the prestigious one for most purposes. The error to avoid is choosing on reputation.

Higher or Standard is a separate decision from which course. Higher Level in either course adds Paper 3 and twenty per cent of the grade with it, plus a substantial increase in content. The evidence for a Higher Level entry is consistent accuracy across MYP 5 or Extended IGCSE, not a single strong result, and a tutor reading three marked papers can give you a more honest view of that than a predicted grade will.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Planning revision without knowing the component structure is guesswork, and it is the first thing to establish with any tutor. Standard Level in both courses sits two papers. Higher Level sits three, with Paper 3 carrying twenty per cent of the grade. The exploration is marked internally out of twenty against criteria A to E and moderated. A student losing most marks on one component needs that component weighted in the plan, which cannot be done without knowing what it is worth.

Paper 1 and Paper 2 differ in calculator access, and for Analysis and Approaches students that difference is the single most practically useful fact about the exam. The non-calculator paper examines manual fluency: exact values, algebraic manipulation, differentiation and integration by hand. Students who have done two years of homework with a calculator beside them meet that paper unprepared, and the fix is months of maintenance rather than a week of revision.

Paper 3 at Higher Level is a different kind of assessment altogether. It consists of extended problem-solving questions, scaffolded across many parts, where each part builds on the last. The skill is reading what the question is constructing and holding the thread for twenty minutes or more. Topic revision does not develop it. Whole questions under timing, marked, with the discussion focused on where the thread was lost, is the only method that does.

The exploration deserves planning time out of proportion to its twenty marks, because those marks are available to every student regardless of mathematical strength. A well-chosen topic with genuine personal engagement and real reflection scores highly with modest mathematics, while an ambitious topic handled superficially does not. That is a planning decision made months before the deadline.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go
paragraphs: Ask a tutor which topics are hardest and you learn nothing, because the answer is the same for every cohort. Ask where marks are lost and a specialist names behaviours rather than topics. The largest single category is method not shown. In a multi-step question, working earns marks independently of the final answer, so a student who produces a correct result from a calculator with nothing written down forfeits marks they have genuinely earned.

The second category is notation. Mathematics at Diploma level is marked as written communication as well as calculation. Equals signs used as connectives, missing differentials, limits omitted from definite integrals, and set or interval notation written loosely all cost marks that the student would call unfair. They are also among the fastest things in the entire syllabus to correct, which makes them unusually good value for early sessions.

The third is context loss. Applications and Interpretation in particular asks for interpretation of a result in the situation described, and students answer with a number. A gradient is not an answer; a gradient expressed as a rate of change in the units of the problem is. The same failure appears in Analysis and Approaches modelling questions and in the exploration's reflection criterion.

The fourth is the Higher Level thread problem on Paper 3, and it is structural rather than careless. When a long question has eight parts and part three is wrong, parts four onwards often collapse. Training for that involves practising the recovery, which means reading the question's design, checking intermediate results for plausibility, and knowing when to state an assumption and carry on rather than stopping.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is twenty marks, internally assessed and externally moderated, and it is the most predictable part of the Diploma mathematics grade because the criteria are published and stable. Yet it is where students most often lose marks they could have kept, almost always for the same two reasons: a topic chosen for its mathematical ambition rather than for the student's genuine interest, and reflection that summarises instead of evaluating.

What the criteria reward is worth stating plainly. Presentation asks for a coherent, organised, concise piece of work. Mathematical communication asks for correct notation, defined terminology and appropriate representation. Personal engagement asks for evidence of the student's own thinking, which cannot be manufactured in the final draft. Reflection asks for critical evaluation of the mathematics and its limitations. Use of mathematics asks for work that is relevant, correct and commensurate with the course level.

The practical implication is that the highest-scoring explorations are often mathematically modest. A student who investigates something they actually care about, uses mathematics at the right level correctly, and reflects honestly on what the model does not capture will outscore a student who attempts something impressive and handles it superficially. Choosing the topic is therefore the highest-value session in the whole block, and it belongs months before the deadline.

The boundary here is absolute and we state it at the first session. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question the topic, teach the mathematical technique the investigation needs, show how published work structures an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own draft against each criterion. A tutor may not write, rewrite, supply the mathematics, or outline the exploration for the student to fill in. At least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student as malpractice.

sections.heading: The calculator is an examined skill, not an accessory
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics student needs a graphic display calculator, and in Applications and Interpretation it is central to the course rather than incidental to it. What parents rarely realise is that calculator competence is itself examined. Marks are available for using technology appropriately and for stating what was obtained from it, and marks are lost by solving graphically where analytic working was required or by not naming the function used.

The model matters. Schools in Dubai standardise on particular models, and the statistical and graphing menus differ between them in ways that cost time under exam pressure. A tutor should know which model your child's school uses and work on that one. A student who has learned the menus of a different model is slower in the exam and more likely to misread an output, which is a wholly avoidable loss.

For Analysis and Approaches students the opposite risk applies. Because one paper is sat without a calculator, two years of calculator-assisted homework quietly erodes manual fluency: exact trigonometric values, surd manipulation, differentiation and integration by hand. The remedy is maintenance across the two years rather than revision at the end, and it is why a weekly session that includes non-calculator work beats an intensive block in the spring.

There is a related exam-room discipline worth teaching early: write down what you asked the technology for and what it gave you. A student who records the equation solved and the value returned has shown method; a student with a bare number has not. That single habit recovers marks across every calculator paper and takes one session to establish.
