sections.heading: The gap between IGCSE or MYP maths and the Diploma
paragraphs: Most families in the Al Furjan corridor arrive at Diploma mathematics from Extended IGCSE or from MYP 5, and in both cases the first term is where confidence breaks. Extended IGCSE builds procedural competence: recognise the question type, apply the method, get the answer. Diploma mathematics, particularly Analysis and Approaches, asks for reasoning about unfamiliar situations and for proof, which is a different activity using the same arithmetic.

The specific gaps are consistent enough to name. Function notation used fluently rather than decoded each time. Algebraic manipulation without a calculator, including surds and exact values. Early proof structure, including what it means for a statement to be shown rather than illustrated by examples. Interpreting a result in the context given. None of those is conceptually difficult, and all of them take time that the first Diploma term does not have spare.

For students coming from MYP 5 the picture differs. MYP criterion B work in investigating patterns builds exactly the generalisation habit the Diploma wants, so those students often reason well and are weaker on procedural speed. The bridging work for them is fluency and exam technique rather than conceptual preparation, which is the opposite of what IGCSE students need. A tutor should know which gap they are treating.

Four to six sessions over the summer is the normal size of this block, and it is the single best-value purchase in Diploma mathematics support. Al Furjan families often change schools for the Diploma, which adds a settling period in the same term, so arriving with the algebra already fluent matters more here than it would elsewhere in the city.

sections.heading: Is there an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutor near Al Furjan?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that there may be, and you should not rely on it. Al Furjan is residential, and the Diploma mathematics teachers in Dubai work near the schools that run the programme, which in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor are fewer than in Al Barsha, Al Khail or Jumeirah. Requiring Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specifically, in a fixed evening slot, reachable by car, reduces that pool to a handful of people who are mostly already committed.

What families do in that situation is take the nearest competent mathematics tutor and hope the difference does not matter. At Standard Level it sometimes does not. At Higher Level it becomes visible within two sessions, usually on Paper 3 work, because teaching an extended scaffolded question requires having taught it before. A tutor meeting Paper 3 for the first time alongside the student is not a specialist in that component.

Online delivery replaces the map with a calendar, and that is the whole argument. IB Gram matches on course and level and delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, since home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a subject where the required specialism is this narrow, the trade favours the wider pool by a large margin.

Where we cannot cover a request, we say so. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels are among the better-covered subjects in the UAE set, usually matched within a few days. Availability tightens in January and February when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai wants an evening slot. The free trial is the check: bring a marked paper and ask what pattern connects the lost marks.

sections.heading: What a mathematics tutor will not do, and why it protects your child
paragraphs: In a market where completed internal assessments are advertised at fixed prices, a clear statement of limits is worth more than a list of promises. An IB Gram mathematics tutor teaches technique, questions a research question or an exploration topic, demonstrates method, marks the student's own work against the published criteria, and writes down the feedback given. That is the whole of the legitimate territory, and most of the available marks sit inside it.

What a tutor will not do is write or rewrite an exploration, supply the mathematics for one, outline it for the student to fill in, or produce an Extended Essay. If a student submits work that is not their own, the IB treats it as malpractice and the Diploma is what is at risk. The seller's revenue is not. Stating that plainly is uncomfortable marketing and accurate advice.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked, and sessions work from material the school has issued to the student. That is a copyright matter for published documents and a malpractice exposure for anything unreleased, and neither risk is worth taking to save a download.

Two further things we will not do. We will not predict or guarantee a grade, for this or any subject; nobody can, and a provider who does is selling confidence rather than teaching. And we will not describe a tutor as an IB examiner without evidence of current status, because examiner status is frequently claimed in this market and gives nobody access to marking, boundaries or paper content in any case.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course does my child in Al Furjan actually sit, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator, because the two are separate courses and a tutor needs to know which before the first lesson. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof course; Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the statistics, modelling and technology course. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, so there are four distinct syllabuses sharing one word on the timetable. A tutor who says the two are broadly similar is telling you they work from generic material rather than from either syllabus.

faqs.question: Will choosing Applications and Interpretation close off engineering at university?
faqs.answer: It can, and that is the reason the choice deserves attention in Diploma 1. A number of engineering and mathematics degree programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and will not accept Applications and Interpretation instead; others accept either. There is no general rule, so the only reliable method is reading the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses your child is considering while the choice is still open. Doing that in Diploma 2 is too late to act on what you find.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does it need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level, in both mathematics courses, and carries twenty per cent of the grade. It consists of extended problem-solving questions scaffolded across many parts, where each part builds on the one before. The skill it tests is holding a long argument together for twenty minutes or more, and an error in part three often collapses everything after it. Topic revision does not develop that. Whole questions under timing, marked, with discussion of where the thread was lost, is the method that does.

faqs.question: How many marks is the maths exploration worth and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks, internally assessed and externally moderated, against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Those marks are available to every student regardless of mathematical strength, which makes the exploration the most recoverable part of the grade. The highest scorers are often mathematically modest pieces on topics the student genuinely cares about, handled correctly and reflected on honestly. Ambitious topics handled superficially score poorly, and the topic cannot be changed late.

faqs.question: On the exploration, what may an Al Furjan student's tutor legitimately touch?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary that we state at the first session. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question the topic until it carries real mathematics, teach the technique the investigation needs, show how published work structures an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own draft against each criterion. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it, supply the mathematics or outline it for the student to complete. Feedback is given in writing so the school can see the nature of the support.

faqs.question: My child uses a calculator for everything. Is that a problem in AA?
faqs.answer: Yes, because Analysis and Approaches examines one paper without a calculator. Two years of calculator-assisted homework erodes exact trigonometric values, surd manipulation, and differentiation and integration by hand, and that erosion is invisible until the non-calculator paper. The remedy is maintenance across both years rather than revision at the end: a weekly session that always includes some manual work keeps the fluency alive. Rebuilding it in the final term is possible but costs far more hours than keeping it would have.

faqs.question: Does the specific calculator model matter for IB maths?
faqs.answer: It does, more than parents expect. Schools in Dubai standardise on particular graphic display calculator models, and the statistical and graphing menus differ between them in ways that cost time under exam pressure and invite misread outputs. A tutor should know which model your child's school uses and teach on that one. Calculator competence is also itself worth marks: students lose them by solving graphically where analytic working was required, and by not recording what they asked the technology for and what it returned.

faqs.question: What is the real gap between Extended IGCSE maths and Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Extended IGCSE builds procedure: recognise the question type, apply the method, produce the answer. Diploma mathematics, especially Analysis and Approaches, asks for reasoning about unfamiliar situations and for proof. The named gaps are fluent function notation, algebraic manipulation without a calculator including surds and exact values, early proof structure, and interpreting a result in context. None is conceptually hard and all take time the first Diploma term does not have. Four to six summer sessions close most of it.

faqs.question: The answers are correct but the mark is low. What is the marker penalising?
faqs.answer: Because method earns marks independently of the answer. In a multi-step question, working is credited, so a correct result lifted from a calculator with nothing written down forfeits marks the student genuinely earned. Notation is the other reliable loss: equals signs used as connectives, missing differentials, limits omitted from definite integrals, loose interval notation. Students call these unfair, which is a sign nobody has taught them that the paper marks written mathematical communication alongside calculation. Both are among the fastest things in the syllabus to fix.

faqs.question: Is a general maths tutor enough for Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and rarely for Higher Level. At Standard Level a strong general mathematics teacher can cover most of the content competently, provided they learn the exploration criteria and the calculator conventions. At Higher Level the gap shows within about two sessions, usually on Paper 3, because teaching an extended scaffolded question well requires having taught it before. A tutor meeting Paper 3 for the first time alongside your child is learning the component, not teaching it, and that is an expensive way to learn.

faqs.question: When should an Al Furjan family start maths tutoring for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The useful year starts in September of Diploma 1, not in the spring of Diploma 2. Mathematics compounds: a misunderstanding caught in the week it is taught costs one session, and the same misunderstanding caught in the mock costs five. Starting early also protects the exploration marks, since the topic session belongs months before the deadline. January and February are the tightest weeks in the Dubai Diploma year for evening slots, because every Diploma 2 family is looking at the same time.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5. What decides whether Higher Level maths is realistic?
faqs.answer: Consistent algebraic accuracy across a year of marked work, not one strong assessment. MYP mathematics is marked against criteria A to D on an eight-point scale, and criterion B on investigating patterns is the one that signals Diploma readiness, because it asks for generalisation and justification rather than correct answers. Many Dubai schools also split standard and extended routes from MYP 4, and that split is the first real decision point. A tutor reading three marked tasks will give you a more honest view than a predicted grade.

faqs.question: Are IB maths exam dates published on this page?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and we write about that session, but we do not publish specific IB exam or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we will not put an unverified date in front of a parent who may act on it. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the real internal calendar, including the school's own deadlines for the exploration, and that is the document worth asking for in September rather than in February.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics for a Higher Level student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. A substantial share of Physics Higher Level marks depend on mathematical handling: rearranging relationships, gradient and area interpretation, logarithms, small-angle work. A student solid on physics concepts but shaky on algebra may need mathematics support rather than more physics. Where one tutor genuinely covers both to Higher Level standard, that is efficient. Where they do not, two specialists beat one generalist, and we will tell you which situation you are in.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the first maths session to make it useful?
faqs.answer: A marked paper, ideally the most recent one, plus the exploration draft if there is one and the name of the calculator model the school uses. Within twenty minutes a specialist should be naming a pattern in the lost marks: method not shown, notation errors, interpretation missing from context answers, or the Paper 3 thread problem. A first session spent on introductions and a general plan has told you nothing you could not read on a website, and it has used an hour you paid for.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee my child will get a 7 in IB maths?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. We do not predict or guarantee grades in any subject, and a provider who does is selling confidence rather than teaching. What can be stated is where marks are available and how they are usually lost: method not shown, notation, interpretation in context, the Paper 3 thread, and twenty exploration marks decided largely by topic choice and reflection. Working on those is what moves a grade. Any page promising a specific score should be read with that in mind.

intro.heading: What an hour of IB Maths help is worth, and what it costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Start with the number, because every other decision follows from it. Published hourly rates for maths support in Dubai begin at about AED 45 with EdFlik's budget tier and reach AED 650 at BartyED's named end, while Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts qualified subject specialists between AED 200 and AED 450 an hour. That is a fourteen-fold spread for a service described in almost identical words on every site selling it. A parent in Al Garhoud holding three quotes is not comparing three prices. They are comparing three different products, and none of the three sellers explains which product is in front of them.

The second number is the hour count, and it is the one that decides the bill. A Diploma Programme maths course runs across two academic years. A family that books weekly through both years is buying something close to seventy sessions; a family that waits until the final two terms is buying twenty-five and paying a higher effective rate because scarce specialist time in the run-up to the May session is priced accordingly. Multiply either count by the band you chose and you have the real figure. At AED 250 an hour, seventy sessions is AED 17,500 over two years, which sits in the same conversation as a term of school fees rather than in the same conversation as a textbook.

The third number is the one nobody puts on a website: how much of the hour is teaching. An in-home visit priced at AED 300 is a 60-minute lesson plus 40 to 80 minutes of someone's driving, and the driving is inside the price whether or not it appears on the invoice. From Al Garhoud, a tutor coming off Sheikh Rashid Road at 4pm against airport traffic is absorbing a genuine cost, and a rational tutor prices for it. Online delivery removes that line item completely, which is why the same quality of teaching sits a band lower in the table further down this page.

What the money should be buying is diagnosis. Most Al Garhoud students who arrive at IB Maths tutoring are not short of content; they have sat in the same lessons as everyone else. They are losing marks to method presentation, to unlabelled calculator output, to abandoning the second half of a structured question, and to treating the command term as decoration. Those are cheap problems to fix and expensive problems to ignore, and they are invisible to an hour spent re-explaining the chapter the student has already heard twice.

So this page is written as a budget rather than a brochure. It prices the market with attribution, sets out the Analysis and Approaches versus Applications and Interpretation decision as the two-year spending decision it actually is, breaks the grade down by paper so you can see which component is worth protecting, and names the three ways Garhoud households routinely waste money on maths. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and the comparison table below makes the case on cost rather than on convenience.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers maths across the three IB school programmes plus the Career-related Programme, and the cost profile of each is different. Primary Years work is short and frequent, Middle Years work is about closing the gap before DP1, and Diploma work is where the hours and the money concentrate.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP maths is organised around number, pattern and function, measurement, shape and space, and data handling, taught through units of inquiry rather than as a separate textbook subject. Support at this stage is usually short and frequent: 30 to 45 minutes, twice weekly, working on number fluency and the ability to explain a method out loud. The cost profile is the lowest of any IB stage because the sessions are shorter and a generalist teacher can carry them competently, which is one of the few places where the budget band genuinely is the right band.
programmes.countryNote: Al Garhoud and Al Rashidiya households often have a PYP child and a DP child in the same week, in two different schools with two different holiday calendars. Scheduling the younger child immediately after the school run, while the older sibling is still travelling home, uses the one quiet half-hour in a Garhoud evening and keeps the two bills from colliding.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics splits into standard and extended from around MYP 4, and the choice between them shapes which DP route is realistically open two years later. Assessment runs on four criteria rather than on papers, so a student can hold solid knowledge and still score poorly on communication or on applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Tutoring here is cheaper per hour than DP work and considerably cheaper than the DP catch-up it prevents, which makes MYP 4 and MYP 5 the highest-return spending window on the whole eleven-year path.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Al Garhoud run the full IB continuum, so a Garhoud student may move from MYP into DP without changing building. That continuity is useful and it hides a problem: the extended maths cohort is small, and a student who drifts into standard in MYP 5 can find the Analysis and Approaches door quietly closed before anyone discusses it with the family.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: DP Mathematics is taken as Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level. Standard Level sits two papers at 40% each plus the exploration at 20%. Higher Level sits three papers, weighted 30%, 30% and 20%, with the exploration again at 20%. The subject is compulsory, so every Diploma candidate in Dubai is in one of four maths courses, and the volume of tutoring demand in this city sits almost entirely here. Two years of weekly support is the largest single tutoring commitment most families make.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the May session, which is also the session most Al Garhoud schools build their internal deadlines around. The practical effect on spending is that demand for specialist maths hours peaks between January and April each year, and a family that books in February is competing for the same scarce slots as every other DP2 household in the emirate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills component. Where a CP student carries a DP maths course, the assessment is identical to any other DP candidate's, so the tutoring is identical too. Where the maths requirement sits inside the career-related study instead, the work is usually applied numeracy for a vocational qualification and the hour count needed is far smaller. Establishing which of the two situations applies before booking anything is the difference between a short block and a two-year commitment.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across Dubai is thinner than DP provision, so a Garhoud family exploring it is often choosing between schools in different parts of the city rather than between two options nearby. Online delivery matters more than usual here, because the subject specialist for a narrow career-related combination may not be anywhere in the emirate.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Maths does not sit alone in a DP timetable, and the subjects that fail alongside it are predictable. The list below covers the maths courses themselves and the quantitative subjects whose marks move when a student's algebra and graph reading improve.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route: proof, calculus developed from first principles, trigonometric manipulation and a technology-free Paper 1 at both levels. Marks are lost in multi-step algebra where method is not shown, and in differentiation and integration questions where the student reaches for the calculator the paper does not allow. This is the course most Al Garhoud students take when a science or engineering degree is the target.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, graph theory at Higher Level, and a calculator permitted in every paper. The common failure is not arithmetic but writing: a correct model described in language that earns no interpretation marks. Students arriving from a strong but applied IGCSE background usually fit this course better than they fit Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: The Mathematics Exploration
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page piece of the student's own mathematics, marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. It is the most predictable mark on the course because the criteria are published and the deadline is internal. A tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student has written; the mathematics and the writing must be the student's own.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Assessed on four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students who score well on the first criterion and badly on the third are not weak at maths; they are weak at explaining it, which is a different and faster fix. Extended maths from MYP 4 is the practical prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics marks move with maths marks more tightly than any other pairing. Rearranging an equation with three subjects, reading a gradient off a non-linear graph, handling uncertainties and significant figures: these are maths skills assessed on a Physics paper. A student losing marks in both subjects often has one problem, not two, and paying two tutors to fix it is the most common duplication we see.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The calculation strand, from moles and limiting reagents to equilibrium constants and pH, punishes the same weaknesses as Paper 2 in maths: unit handling, significant figures, and confidence with logarithms. Where a Garhoud family is already paying for Chemistry support, aligning it with the maths work rather than running the two in parallel usually reduces the total hour count.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics carries quantitative work across all three papers, and Paper 3 is explicitly calculation-heavy: elasticity, national income accounting, exchange rate arithmetic. Students who dislike maths often choose Economics expecting relief and find the same algebra wearing different clothes. Diagram accuracy and the ability to read a numerical answer back into a sentence are the two marginal marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic, number bases, Boolean algebra and complexity all draw on the discrete maths that Analysis and Approaches students meet and Applications and Interpretation students sometimes do not. The internal assessment is a developed solution rather than a maths exploration, so the supervision pattern differs, but the habit of documenting a method properly transfers directly from one to the other.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Break-even analysis, investment appraisal, ratio analysis and cash-flow forecasting are the quantitative tools examined here, and they are the parts of the course where marks are won cleanly because they are either right or wrong. A student comfortable with the financial mathematics in Applications and Interpretation has a measurable advantage, and the two can be supported by one tutor.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge examined in Theory of Knowledge, and a maths student who can articulate why a proof is not the same kind of claim as an experimental result has material most of the cohort lacks. Support here is about argument and example selection, not about calculation, and it is usually a short block of sessions rather than a continuing commitment.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.regionsIntro: Al Garhoud sits beside the airport and the golf club, which shapes both the school options and the household rhythm. The notes below describe what each nearby area means for the cost and the timing of a maths session, not for its property market.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Low-rise villas and older apartment stock beside Dubai International. A heavily aviation-employed population means rostered shifts and parents frequently away, so a student who can work unsupervised between sessions gets far more out of each paid hour than one who cannot.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Immediately east towards Mirdif, mostly villas with established school provision and shared bus routes with Garhoud. Journeys home are short enough that a 4pm start is realistic, which is the earliest viable slot anywhere in this cluster and the cheapest to book.

regions.name: Port Saeed
regions.note: Denser apartment living north towards Deira. Study space is the constraint rather than travel: a shared room with a television in it costs more in lost attention over a term than the difference between two tutoring bands costs in money.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Across the Ras Al Khor corridor, with established schooling drawing directly from Garhoud. Short run outside pick-up, slow inside it, which is exactly the window an in-home tutor would have to drive through and price for.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Over the creek side, home to several of the cluster's long-established schools. For most Garhoud families this is a destination rather than a residential alternative, and the morning run there sets how early the evening can start.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Inland towards Mirdif, lower density and newer villa stock. The Nad Al Hamar road carries school traffic in both directions at the same hour, so a 4.30pm session is a safer booking here than a 4pm one.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: North across the creek, dense and school-rich with a broad curriculum mix. Households here commonly run two assessment systems across two children, which doubles the scheduling problem without doubling the budget available.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: North-east along the Dubai-Sharjah corridor with substantial Indian and British curriculum provision. The practical point for maths is that a student here may be sitting IGCSE while a Garhoud cousin sits MYP, and the two need different tutors.

schoolClusters.city: Al Garhoud and the creek side
schoolClusters.note: An unusually wide curriculum mix inside a small radius, including full IB continuum provision, American curriculum and British curriculum within minutes of each other. For a maths conversation that matters because the same Year 11 student could be heading for Analysis and Approaches, for A Level Mathematics, or for AP Calculus depending only on which gate the family drove through.

schoolClusters.city: Within a short run across the creek
schoolClusters.note: The wider old-Dubai set that Garhoud buses also serve. Every one of these is inspected annually by KHDA and given a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the inspection report names the subjects where attainment in mathematics sits below expectation. Reading that section before buying tutoring is free and tells you more than any tutor's own marketing.

modes.description: One 60 or 90 minute session a week, following the school's own scheme of work rather than a parallel syllabus. This is the cadence that makes the two-year arithmetic work in the family's favour: the hour count is high but the rate is stable, no crisis premium applies, and the tutor sees the student's work often enough to diagnose rather than guess.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor costs in Dubai, and what sits inside the rate
paragraphs: Market rates for maths tutoring in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour depending on the tier, and the figures below are the ones providers publish themselves rather than estimates. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors quotes IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. None of these are IB Gram's prices; they are what the market charges, and a parent who knows the bands cannot be sold the wrong one.

The single most useful thing in the table is the fourth column, because it is the one no provider fills in. Two tutors can both honestly describe themselves as teaching IB Mathematics and mean completely different work. At the budget end the hour is usually homework supervision: the student brings a question, the tutor works it, the student watches. That has value for a MYP child consolidating number work and almost none for a DP2 candidate three months from Paper 3, where the problem is rarely the content and almost always the technique under timed conditions.

At the top end the premium is for scarcity and reputation rather than for a different syllabus. The syllabus is the same document for everyone. What AED 650 buys is a person whose diary is full, which has real value when you need a specific slot at a specific point in the year, and no value at all in September of DP1 when supply is loose. A Garhoud family that pays the April rate in September has spent the premium on nothing. Read the table from the bottom row upwards and ask what the extra AED 200 is buying in your particular week.

sections.heading: The three places Al Garhoud families lose money on maths tuition
paragraphs: The first loss is buying content hours for a technique problem. A student who scores 4 in Paper 2 while understanding the chapter is not short of teaching about the chapter. They are losing marks to unlabelled calculator output, to answers not given to three significant figures, to method that exists in their head and not on the page, and to abandoning part (c) of a structured question because part (b) came out wrong. Re-teaching the topic costs ten hours and moves nothing. Marking one of the student's own scripts line by line costs one hour and names the problem. Any provider who will not open with a marked script is selling hours rather than diagnosis.

The second loss is the crisis premium. Specialist maths availability in Dubai tightens sharply between January and April because every DP2 household in the emirate reaches the same conclusion in the same fortnight. A family that starts in February is buying from a thin market at the thin market's price, and is also buying from the subset of tutors still free at that point, which is not a random subset. Starting in DP1, even at a lower cadence, costs less per hour and gets a better choice of teacher. The cheapest hour on the whole course is an early one.

The third loss is paying twice for one problem. A Garhoud student struggling in Physics and in Maths usually has a single underlying weakness: rearranging relationships with three or more variables, and reading information off a graph that is not a straight line. Two tutors, two invoices, two sets of homework, one problem. Where the marks in both subjects are falling in the same way, one tutor who can hold both syllabi is cheaper and more effective than two specialists who never speak to each other. This is worth checking before the second engagement starts rather than after.
bullets: Ask for a marked past paper before the first full term is booked
Book in DP1 at a lower cadence rather than in DP2 at a higher one
Check whether the Maths and Physics problems are the same problem
Decline any package that cannot be paused at the end of a term
Treat a quote with no stated session length as incomplete rather than competitive

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets two years of spending
paragraphs: The route decision is made once, usually in Year 11, and it determines the shape of every tutoring hour afterwards. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic course: proof, calculus built from first principles, trigonometric manipulation, and a Paper 1 at both levels where no calculator is allowed. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling course: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, graph theory at Higher Level, with technology permitted in every paper. They are not easier and harder versions of one subject. They reward different habits and they fail for different reasons.

That difference lands directly on the invoice. An Analysis and Approaches student pays for technique: by-hand accuracy protected under time pressure, method written out so the marks can be awarded, and the discipline of not reaching for a calculator in a paper that forbids it. An Applications and Interpretation student pays for interpretation and for writing: a correct regression described in language that earns the marks, a model whose limitations are stated, a calculator used fluently rather than hopefully. Hours bought against the wrong profile do very little, which is why a tutor who treats the two courses as one course is poor value at any rate.

Getting the route wrong is the single most expensive mistake available here. A student moved from Applications and Interpretation into Analysis and Approaches in the second term of DP1 is carrying a term of unseen algebra into a course that assumes it, and closing that gap is intensive work at full rate during the busiest part of the year. The signal to watch is not the student's preference but their IGCSE or MYP record: strength in extended or higher-tier algebra points one way, solid applied competence points the other. Where university entry requirements are relevant, read them on the university's own programme page before committing, because the pattern varies by institution and by course.

sections.heading: What the grade is made of, paper by paper, and which component is worth protecting
paragraphs: A Standard Level maths grade is two papers at 40% each plus the exploration at 20%. A Higher Level grade is three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% plus the exploration at 20%. Those percentages are the whole of the argument about where to spend hours, and almost no family sees them laid out before they start buying. A student who is four marks off a grade boundary and has spent every session on Paper 1 content has been working on 30% of the grade while a fifth of it sat untouched on a hard drive.

The exploration is the component to protect first, for three reasons that have nothing to do with how interesting it is. It is worth 20% at both levels. Its criteria are published, so the target is visible. And its deadline is internal, which means it is the one part of the course where the student controls the timetable rather than the examination schedule controlling it. Marks lost here are lost by omission: a reflection section written in the last hour, a personal engagement criterion treated as a sentence of decoration. These are the cheapest marks on the course to secure and the most commonly left on the table.

Paper 3 at Higher Level deserves separate attention because it is not a longer version of the other papers. It is two extended tasks that build, where part (d) depends on part (a) and a student who stalls early can lose the whole structure. The specific skill is continuing after a wrong answer: stating an assumption, carrying it forward, and collecting the method marks that remain available. That is coachable in a handful of sessions and it is invisible in any amount of topic revision. The table below sets out where each component leaks marks so you can see which column your child's script is in.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion, and where a tutor's job stops
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is marked against five criteria. Presentation covers coherence and organisation. Mathematical communication covers notation, terminology and the consistent use of symbols. Personal engagement covers evidence that the student made the work their own. Reflection covers critical discussion of results and limitations. Use of mathematics carries the largest share and asks whether the mathematics is correct, relevant and at a level commensurate with the course. A student who knows the five criteria by name and marks their own draft against them is in a different position from one who writes a report and hopes.

The two criteria that routinely cost Al Garhoud students marks are reflection and personal engagement, and both fail for the same reason: they are written last, at speed, after the mathematics is finished. Reflection is not a summary. It asks what the result means, where the model breaks, what a different assumption would have produced. Personal engagement is not a sentence about why the topic is interesting; it is visible in the choices the student made about data, method and direction. Both are teachable, and both need to be designed into the work at the start rather than appended at the end.

The boundary matters as much as the criteria. A tutor teaches the criteria, explains the mathematics the student has chosen to use, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor does not write the exploration, does not supply the mathematics, and does not edit the work into its final form. IB academic honesty rules make producing a student's assessed work a malpractice matter for the student as well as a liability for anyone selling it, and at least one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. We will not, and any family offered that should treat it as a warning about everything else on the invoice.

sections.heading: Buying hours against the calendar, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Dubai IB candidates sit the May session, and every internal deadline in a Garhoud school's DP calendar is set backwards from it. Exact IB session and results dates should be taken from ibo.org or from the school's own IB coordinator rather than from any tutoring website, this one included, because they are revised and because a date a parent acts on has to be right. What can be said with confidence is the shape of the year, and the shape is what determines when hours are cheap and when they are scarce.

Counted backwards, the sequence is consistent. The exploration's school deadline lands in DP2 term one for most schools, which puts topic selection in DP1 term three. Mock examinations sit in the winter of DP2. Predicted grades follow the mocks, and they are the grades universities see first. Final internal submissions close before the examination window opens. Each of those is a point where a specific kind of help is worth money and a general kind is not, and a family that maps them in DP1 buys half as many hours as one that reacts to each in turn.

The practical scheduling consequence in Al Garhoud is about supply rather than about the student. Demand for specialist maths hours rises steeply from January, and the families who book in that window pay more for a narrower choice of teacher. Ramadan also shifts the viable evening: sessions move to post-Iftar timing for many households, and the schools adjust their own days. Agreeing both of those in advance, rather than renegotiating them in the week they arrive, is the difference between a timetable that survives the spring and one that quietly stops.

sections.heading: The schools around Al Garhoud, and what a KHDA report tells a paying parent
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak, together with subject-level commentary. In 2024-25 the emirate held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with British provision the largest by enrolment and IB programmes accounting for seven per cent of it. Al Garhoud's own cluster is unusually mixed for its size, which is why two neighbours' children can be in entirely different maths systems.

The part of the inspection report worth a paying parent's time is not the headline band. It is the subject paragraphs, where inspectors state whether attainment and progress in mathematics are above, in line with, or below curriculum expectations, and at which phase. A school rated Good overall can have a weak mathematics phase, and a school rated Very Good can be carrying a cohort whose Higher Level results are thin. That paragraph tells you whether the gap you are buying tutoring to close is your child's gap or the year group's, and those two situations need different amounts of help.

KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting two years of maths support alongside fees, that is a genuinely useful fixed point: the larger number in the household education budget is not moving this year, which makes the tutoring number easier to plan around. Seven new private schools are also opening for the 2026-27 intake, four British curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places across the emirate.
bullets: Read the mathematics paragraphs in the inspection report, not only the overall band
Reports are published on the KHDA site and cost nothing to read
A weak year group and a weak student need different quantities of help
Dubai private school fees are held flat for 2026-27 under the KHDA announcement of May 2026

sections.heading: Permits, receipts and what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone.

Two things follow for a Garhoud family writing a cheque. A tutor can hold the permit, so asking is reasonable and cheap. And in Abu Dhabi, where ADEK's professional-ethics rules apply to private and charter school staff, teachers are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. Anyone marketing your child's own class teacher as a private tutor is selling something with a problem attached, whatever it costs. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or any examination board, and no tutoring provider in this market should tell you otherwise.

On the receipt itself, three questions settle most disputes before they start. Is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session? Does it include any written feedback between lessons, or is that extra? And what happens if you stop after one lesson? Our answer to the third is that a trial lesson comes before any payment and no card details are held, so the decision after it costs nothing. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

process.title: Send the last marked paper
process.description: Before any price is discussed, send the most recent marked maths paper or report. A script shows where marks are leaking in a way a conversation cannot, and it often shows that the problem is narrower and cheaper to fix than the family assumed. This step costs nothing and changes what we recommend in roughly half of cases.

process.title: Confirm the course, not the subject
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard Level, and which school's scheme of work is being followed. Those four facts decide which tutor is the right one. A provider who books you without asking them is matching on availability rather than on fit, and the difference shows up in the third session.

process.title: Meet the tutor in a trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the tutor who would actually teach, before any payment and with no card details held. The student should finish it able to name one thing they will do differently in the next paper. If they cannot, the match is wrong and we would rather find that out in the trial than in week six.

process.title: Agree the cadence and the ceiling
process.description: Weekly across the course, a bounded exploration block, or a short diagnostic intensive, with the number of sessions and the stop point written down. Garhoud households with rostered shifts also set which evenings are realistic and what happens in Ramadan, when sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing.

process.title: Read the notes and check against the school
process.description: Session notes go out after each lesson, so a parent who is away on a roster can read what was covered and what was set. Every few weeks, compare that against the school's own feedback. Where they disagree, the school's assessment is the one that counts and the tutoring plan changes to match it.

process.title: Review at the end of each term
process.description: Three questions at each review: has the named leak closed, is the cadence still right, and is the spend still proportionate to what is left on the course. Hours that are no longer earning their keep get cut. A plan that only ever grows is a plan nobody is reading.

whyPoints.title: Prices with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. A family that can see the bands cannot be sold the wrong one, which is worth more than any claim we could make about value.

whyPoints.title: Route-specific teaching, not generic maths
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are taught as the separate courses they are, by tutors who teach one of them rather than both indifferently. The failure patterns differ, the papers differ, and the technology rules differ. Hours bought against the wrong profile are the quietest waste in this market.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: The first session reads the student's own marked script and produces a short list of where marks are actually going. Most students who arrive for maths support are not short of content, and ten hours of re-teaching a chapter they have already heard twice moves nothing. Naming the leak is the work; closing it is the easy part.

It also removes the travel that an in-home rate silently includes, which is why the same standard of teaching sits a band lower in the rate table above.

whyPoints.description: We teach the exploration criteria, explain the mathematics a student has chosen, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. We do not produce assessed work. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice risk carried by the student, and declining it is not a marketing position but a condition of doing this properly.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor in Al Garhoud actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from about AED 45 an hour at EdFlik's budget tier to AED 650 at BartyED's named end. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts qualified IB and IGCSE specialists between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, and in-home visits between AED 180 and AED 350. Unitors quotes IB support from AED 200 and TutorChase lists AED 270. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's price list. What we would rather do is look at your child's last marked paper first, because the number of hours you need varies far more than the hourly rate does, and the hour count is what decides the bill.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition genuinely cheaper than a home tutor in Garhoud?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is mechanical rather than promotional. An in-home rate has to cover the tutor's travel, and from most of Dubai to Al Garhoud at 4pm that is 40 to 80 minutes of driving against airport traffic. Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 against qualified online teaching at AED 150 to 300 for comparable experience. The teaching is the same; the difference is the car. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the travel line never appears on your invoice in the first place.

faqs.question: Which IB Maths course needs more tutoring hours, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Neither reliably needs more hours, but they need different ones, and that is what families get wrong. Analysis and Approaches students buy technique: by-hand accuracy for the technology-free Paper 1, method written out so marks can be awarded, calculus from first principles. Applications and Interpretation students buy interpretation and writing: a regression described in language that scores, a model whose limitations are stated, calculator fluency. Higher Level on either route adds Paper 3 at 20% of the grade, which is where the final two terms concentrate. Hours bought against the wrong profile do very little work, whatever the rate on them.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions should a Garhoud family budget for across the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Weekly support across both DP years is roughly sixty to seventy sessions. A bounded exploration block is six to ten. A diagnostic intensive before mocks or finals is eight to eighteen across four to six weeks. Most families who plan from DP1 end up somewhere between the second and third of those rather than at the first, because early diagnosis narrows what actually needs teaching. Families who start in February of DP2 usually buy more hours at a worse rate from a thinner choice of tutors, which is the single most common avoidable cost on this page.

faqs.question: Is a premium tutor at AED 500 an hour worth it for IB Maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and for a reason that has nothing to do with the syllabus. The syllabus is one published document and every tutor works from it. What the premium buys is scarcity: a person whose diary is full, at a specific hour, at the time of year when specialist maths availability in Dubai is tightest. In January to April of DP2 that can be worth paying for. In September of DP1 supply is loose and the same money buys nothing extra. Ask what the premium is purchasing in your particular week, and be suspicious of any answer framed as a predicted result.

faqs.question: Where do parents most often waste money on maths tutoring here?
faqs.answer: Three places. Buying content hours when the problem is technique, which means paying to re-teach a chapter the student has already heard twice while the marks leak from calculator presentation and abandoned part (c) answers. Paying the crisis premium by starting in February of DP2 rather than in DP1. And paying twice for one problem, when a student weak in both Maths and Physics has a single weakness in rearranging relationships and reading non-linear graphs. The first can be found by marking one script, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Does a quoted maths tutoring rate in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: You have to ask, because providers in this market quote inconsistently and some publish a figure without stating either way. We would not tell you what UAE VAT treatment applies to tuition generally, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring website, and several competitor pages state it wrongly. What we will do is tell you plainly whether a figure we quote you is inclusive before you agree to it. When comparing two quotes, confirm three things: inclusive or exclusive, per hour or per session, and how long a session runs.

faqs.question: How realistic is a 7 in Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It is achievable and nobody can promise it, and any provider who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What can be said usefully is where the grade is decided: Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 30% each, Paper 3 at 20%, and the exploration at 20%. Students who reach the top band almost always have the exploration secured early and a reliable process for continuing through Paper 3 after a wrong answer. Those two are coachable. Raw content knowledge is rarely the constraint at that level, and it is where most hours get spent anyway.

faqs.question: How is the IB Maths grade weighted at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Standard Level is Paper 1 at 40%, Paper 2 at 40% and the exploration at 20%. Higher Level is Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 30%, Paper 3 at 20% and the exploration at 20%. On the Analysis and Approaches route, Paper 1 is sat without technology. Those percentages are the whole argument about where to spend hours, and most families never see them before they start buying. A student four marks off a boundary who has spent every session on Paper 1 content has been working on 30% of the grade.

faqs.question: What exploration support is a tutor allowed to give under IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor teaches the five published criteria, explains the mathematics the student has chosen to use, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written themselves. A tutor does not produce the work, supply the mathematics, or edit it into its final state. The distinction matters because IB academic honesty rules make producing a student's assessed work a malpractice matter for the student. At least one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; a family offered that should treat it as a warning about everything else being sold.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks before the maths exam. Is tutoring still worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only if it is bought as diagnosis rather than as coverage. Eight weeks is not enough to re-teach two years and is more than enough to close three specific leaks. The first session should be a full timed paper marked against the published markscheme, and everything after it should target what that script shows. Expect exam-room process to feature heavily: time per mark, what to do when part (b) collapses, how to present method so it can be credited. Buying a general revision course at this point is the most expensive way to feel busy.

faqs.question: Is a calculator problem something a tutor should be paid to fix?
faqs.answer: Often yes, because it is rarely only about the calculator. Students lose marks on Paper 2 for unlabelled output, for not stating what was entered, for answers given to the wrong number of significant figures, and for trusting a graph they have not checked. On the Applications and Interpretation route, where technology is permitted throughout, fluency is a scored skill rather than a convenience. It is also fast to fix: two or three sessions with the student's own device and their own marked script, rather than a term of general work.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Should my child take AA if they want to study engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Read the specific programme's entry page before deciding, because requirements vary by institution and by course and a tutoring website is the wrong source for them. The general pattern is that mathematically intensive degrees expect the algebraic route and often expect it at Higher Level, while business, design and many social science routes accept either. What we can say about the cost of the decision is that reversing it mid-DP1 is expensive: a term of unseen algebra has to be closed at peak rate during the busiest part of the year.

faqs.question: Should the same tutor take on both Maths and Physics for one student?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it is usually cheaper and better. A Garhoud student losing marks in both subjects often has one weakness rather than two: rearranging relationships with several variables, reading gradients from curves, handling units and significant figures. Two tutors means two invoices, two sets of homework and no coordination between them. Where the marks in both subjects are falling the same way, one tutor holding both syllabi reduces the total hour count. Where they are failing for genuinely different reasons, we say so and recommend two, because pretending otherwise saves money once and costs it twice.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the price list
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: If you are weighing maths quotes for a student at a school around Al Garhoud, the cheapest useful step is also the free one: send the last marked paper. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and the rate table above explains why that works in your favour rather than against it.

intro.heading: Four dates decide a Diploma mathematics grade, and three of them are not the exam
paragraphs: Parents in Al Habtoor City usually start looking for mathematics help after a disappointing DP1 report or a weak mock, which means they are reacting to the third or fourth of four decisions rather than the first. The four are these: which course, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. Which level, Higher or Standard. When the exploration is started and on what topic. And how the final months are spent across three papers at Higher Level or two at Standard. Only the last of those is about the exam, and by the time most families call, the first two are already locked.

Running the year backwards makes the sequence visible. The written papers sit in the May session for almost every Dubai school. Before them come study leave and the school's own revision programme, which fills afternoons for two to three weeks. Before that come mocks, usually in the new year of DP2, and mock results are the last point at which new content can still be taught usefully. Before that sits the exploration deadline, set by the school and landing in DP2 term one, right in the middle of teaching. Before that, in DP1, the course and level confirmation. Each step forward in the year removes options, and the cost of help rises as the options shrink.

Al Habtoor City's own situation adds a wrinkle. The three towers sit on the Dubai Water Canal with no school inside the development, so children here attend campuses in Al Safa, Jumeirah, Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Al Barsha. That means four different exploration deadline calendars and four different mock timetables among neighbours in the same lift. A tutor working to a generic syllabus order will be out of step with at least three of them. A tutor working from your school's own dated list will not.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are not sold anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. For mathematics specifically this is less of a compromise than it sounds, because the work is a shared screen with annotation: a problem written out, worked through, corrected in real time, and left behind as a record the student can rewatch. What it buys is a tutor chosen for having taught Analysis and Approaches Higher Level through several sessions, rather than whoever could reach the canal by half past four.

A note on dates. IB session and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate and confirmed by your school's Diploma coordinator, and they are not reprinted here, because a specific date typed onto a page becomes wrong on its own. Series are named by month instead. Where Cambridge or Pearson dates appear elsewhere on this site they are quoted from the boards' own timetable pages with the source given.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.programmesIntro: Mathematics in the IB continuum builds in stages, and a Diploma problem is often a stage-two problem that nobody caught. The programmes below are listed with what the mathematics looks like inside each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one mathematics course, either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Assessment is two written papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, plus the mathematical exploration, an independent piece worth roughly a fifth of the grade and marked against criteria the student should read in full before starting.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally offer both courses but not always both levels of both, so the real choice at a given school may be narrower than the IB's catalogue suggests. Al Habtoor City families attending four or five different campuses therefore face four or five different sets of actual options, and that is worth checking in Year 11 rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Levels are reported out of 8 per criterion rather than as percentages. Standard and extended mathematics routes diverge in the final years and the route taken shapes which Diploma course is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: The extended mathematics route in MYP 5 is the usual preparation for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. A student arriving at the Diploma from standard MYP mathematics and choosing Analysis and Approaches Higher Level has a gap to close in algebraic fluency, and that gap is best addressed in the summer before DP1 rather than discovered in October.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Number, pattern and function, measurement, shape and space, and data handling, taught inside transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than as a separate timetabled subject. Assessment is descriptive, so there is no grade to lift. Support at this stage is about number sense and fluency with operations.
programmes.countryNote: The transition into MYP mathematics at Year 7 is where primary gaps become visible, because the assessment language changes to criteria and levels at the same moment the content steps up. Families on the Jumeirah coast most often ask for help at exactly this point.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where mathematics is one of the chosen Diploma courses, the assessment is identical to a full Diploma candidate's, so tutoring works the same way, exploration included.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools near Al Habtoor City run the Career-related Programme, so most families meeting it have moved into it from abroad. Where mathematics is taken, the exploration criteria and deadlines are the same as a Diploma candidate's and should be planned the same way.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-habtoor-city.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on paper and several in practice. The entries below break the Diploma courses into the components a tutor actually works on, with the place marks tend to disappear in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, complex numbers, vectors, calculus to second-order techniques, and statistics. Marks go in the proof questions, where a student who can execute a method cannot build an argument, and in Paper 3's extended investigation, which rewards structured reasoning over speed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same spine at lower depth across two papers, one with a calculator and one without. The non-calculator paper is where Standard Level grades are decided, because exact-value work in trigonometry and logarithms exposes any reliance on the graphing calculator.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics, probability distributions, modelling, matrices, graph theory and applied calculus, with a graphing calculator permitted throughout. The reliable loss is unexplained working: students produce a correct number from the calculator and lose method marks because nothing on the page shows how.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, calculator-permitted on both papers. Students underestimate the written demands: interpreting a regression result in context, justifying a model choice, and commenting on validity all carry marks that pure computation does not reach.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An independent piece of roughly twelve to twenty pages worth approximately a fifth of the grade, assessed against lettered criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Most of the final mark is decided by the topic choice, long before any writing happens.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level only
subjects.description: An extended problem-solving paper on both courses, built from scaffolded parts that lead somewhere. It rewards students who have practised sustained reasoning and punishes those who have only practised single-step questions. It is also the component most often left unpractised until the final weeks.

subjects.name: Graphing calculator technique
subjects.description: On Applications and Interpretation the calculator is required on every paper; on Analysis and Approaches it is permitted on one. Knowing which functions to use, how to show evidence of their use, and when the calculator is the wrong tool is worth a measurable number of marks and is almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency
subjects.description: Rearranging, factorising, handling indices and surds, and manipulating fractions without error. Nearly every mathematics problem presenting as a topic weakness turns out on inspection to be an algebra weakness, and it is the one thing worth fixing before anything else in DP1.

subjects.name: Command terms and mark-scheme literacy
subjects.description: Show that, hence, verify, justify and state each demand a different response and carry different credit. Students who answer every question the same way lose marks they could have kept, and the fix is reading real mark schemes rather than being told to show working.

subjects.name: Physics and economics mathematics
subjects.description: The algebra and calculus that Diploma physics and the quantitative parts of economics assume. Where a student is struggling in both mathematics and physics, the shared cause is usually algebraic rather than conceptual, and fixing it once improves two grades.

sections.heading: The mathematics year in reverse, from the May session back to the course choice
paragraphs: Work the calendar backwards and the spending decision makes itself. The written papers sit in the May session for Dubai candidates. Immediately before them is study leave and the school's own revision programme. Before that, mocks in the new year of DP2, and mock results mark the boundary after which teaching new content stops being a good use of money. Before that, the exploration deadline, set by the school and landing in DP2 term one. Before that, in DP1, the course and level confirmation that constrains everything else.

What this ordering shows is that the two most expensive mistakes are both made early. The first is choosing Analysis and Approaches Higher Level on ambition rather than on evidence, which produces a student who spends two years at the bottom of a class and a parent who buys tutoring to fix a fit problem. The second is starting the exploration late, which converts a piece of work worth roughly a fifth of the grade into a rushed submission completed alongside mock revision. Neither is a teaching problem and neither is fixed by more hours in April.

The table below is a planning skeleton rather than a date list, because specific IB session and results dates belong to the International Baccalaureate and to your school's Diploma coordinator, and a date printed on a page and left alone goes stale on its own. What the table gives instead is the order of events, who controls each one, and the mathematics-specific thing that should already be finished by then.

Use it with your own school's dated list in hand. Al Habtoor City families attend four or five campuses, each with its own exploration deadline and mock window, and the difference between schools can be six weeks. Six weeks is the entire difference between an exploration written properly and an exploration written in the gaps of a revision timetable.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, decided on evidence
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a Diploma mathematics grade and it is routinely made on reputation. Analysis and Approaches is widely believed to be the serious one and Applications and Interpretation the easier one, and neither belief survives contact with the papers. They are different courses for different destinations, and the Higher Level version of either is demanding.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented course: functions, trigonometry, calculus, and at Higher Level complex numbers, vectors and more advanced calculus techniques. One of its papers is sat without a calculator, which means exact values in trigonometry and logarithms have to be handled by hand. Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling, matrices and graph theory, with a graphing calculator permitted on every paper. Its difficulty is not computation but interpretation: justifying a model, commenting on validity, explaining what a regression coefficient means in the context given.

The destination test is the one worth applying. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and some will specify it. Business, design, social sciences and life sciences routes frequently accept either, and in several cases Applications and Interpretation is the better preparation for what the degree actually uses. Check the specific universities and courses your child is considering rather than relying on a general impression, and do it before the choice is confirmed in DP1 rather than after.

The fit test is the second one. A student who enjoys exact answers, manipulates algebra comfortably and finds proof interesting belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who is strong at reading data, writing about it and building models, but who loses accuracy in multi-step algebra, will produce better work in Applications and Interpretation and will not spend two years behind. The honest way to settle it is a timed paper from each course, marked properly. Two hours of evidence beats a term of opinion, and that is a reasonable thing to ask a tutor to arrange in a trial lesson.

sections.heading: The exploration: where a fifth of the grade is won or thrown away
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is worth roughly a fifth of the final mathematics grade and it is the only part a student controls completely. It is also the part most often left until the deadline is visible, which is why so many Dubai Diploma students hand in something competent rather than something good. The difference between those two is usually decided in the first week, by the topic.

A workable topic has three properties. It admits mathematics at the level of the course, which rules out topics where the mathematics stops at a graph and a percentage. It belongs to the student, which is what the personal engagement criterion is reaching for and which cannot be manufactured in a final draft. And it is small enough to finish, because an exploration that tries to model an entire system runs out of pages before it reaches any conclusion. A tutor's most valuable hour in the whole cycle is the one spent rejecting three topics before any time is wasted on them.

The criteria are published and lettered, each with a stated maximum, and the student should read them before writing anything. That turns feedback into arithmetic rather than opinion: this criterion is capped at a stated maximum, your draft supports a lower level, and here is what the next descriptor actually asks for. Students are frequently surprised that reflection and mathematical communication carry real marks, and that presenting results without discussing their limitations leaves credit on the table.

The boundary has to be explicit. A tutor must not write the exploration, draft the analysis or produce the mathematical argument on the student's behalf. Under IB academic honesty rules that is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. One provider ranking for Dubai searches sells completed internal assessments outright, which is a different transaction entirely. What is permitted is substantial: teaching the mathematics the topic needs, checking a technique is being used correctly, explaining a criterion, marking the student's own draft against it, and asking the questions that make the weakness visible to the student rather than describing it to them.
