sections.heading: What a parent can verify before paying anything
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions are made on reassurance, which is the weakest available evidence. There are four things a parent can actually verify about a mathematics tutor before any money changes hands, and all of them can be established in a message or in a trial session.

First, whether they know which of the four courses the student sits and what is not examinable in it. A tutor who asks whether it is Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, before discussing anything else has demonstrated something a reference cannot. Second, whether they will produce a categorised list of lost marks from the student's script. That output is checkable: it either arrives or it does not. Third, whether they will do non-calculator work without a calculator, which sounds trivial and is the commonest quiet shortcut in Analysis tutoring.

Fourth, what they will refuse to do with the exploration. The honest answer is that they will teach the mathematics, question whether the topic can support the work, read the five criteria with the student and give feedback on the student's own drafts, and will not write it, do the mathematics for it, edit it to completion or supply a model. Operations selling completed Internal Assessments exist in the Gulf market at fixed prices, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

On price, the published Dubai bands give a benchmark. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is published at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Those are the providers' own figures. A rate inside those bands is normal; a rate far above them should come with something specific attached.

sections.heading: Online delivery, handwritten mathematics and the Al Khail Gate week
paragraphs: Mathematics tutoring over video raises a reasonable objection: the work is handwritten, so how does the tutor see it. In practice through a shared writing surface, a document camera or a phone propped over the page, with the student writing while the tutor watches the working appear. That is better than reviewing a finished answer, because the error in a mathematics solution is almost always earlier than the last line, and a tutor watching can intervene where it happened.

The format also makes non-calculator work honest in a way that is harder to police otherwise. A tutor can see whether the calculator is genuinely off the desk during Paper 1 practice, which matters because the quiet shortcut of allowing it is the commonest way Analysis tutoring fails to prepare a student for the paper that actually counts.

For this community the selection argument is strong because Diploma mathematics cohorts are small. There may be nobody within a short drive of Al Khail Gate teaching Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, a course with a small national cohort, while several tutors teach it weekly online. For a student whose problem is graph theory or matrix applications specifically, that is the difference between help and sympathy.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. One practical consequence worth stating: long sessions, for Paper 3 or a full timed paper, are booked at weekends, because students travelling back along the Al Khail corridor rarely have an uninterrupted ninety minutes on a weekday evening.

process.title: Send the course, the level and a marked script
process.description: Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, plus a photograph of the most recent marked paper. Those two things are enough to begin a topic-level diagnosis, and without them the first session is spent on questions the family could have answered in a message.

process.title: Free trial that produces a categorised list
process.description: The trial reads the script question by question and labels every lost mark as conceptual, procedural, presentational or temporal. That list is the output, and a family can hold it. No payment is taken before the session happens.

process.title: Fix the fast three categories first
process.description: Presentational, temporal and procedural losses move within days or a single session. Doing those before tackling a conceptual gap raises the mark quickly and makes the slower teaching work more measurable, which keeps a student engaged with it.

process.title: Audit the assumed algebra if Year 12
process.description: Nine specific skills, two or three minutes each. Where gaps exist, a short intensive block while the course content is still introductory prevents the gap compounding through functions and calculus across two years.

process.title: Book long sessions at weekends
process.description: Paper 3 practice and full timed papers need an uninterrupted block that a weekday evening in this belt rarely provides. A Saturday or Sunday morning sat properly to time is worth more than two interrupted weekday hours.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is conceptual, procedural, presentational or temporal, and three of those four move in days. A report that says work harder sends a student to revise content, which is the one response that does nothing for three of them.

whyPoints.title: Proof taught as a structure
whyPoints.description: Students who say they cannot do proof usually do not know what the answer should look like. Four worked examples and four attempts changes that, and it is among the highest-return hours in the Higher Level syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Calculus fixed at the failing technique
whyPoints.description: A missing constant or an unstated substitution destroys chains of later marks. Ten examples of the one failing technique beats a general calculus revision programme that spends its time on the differentiation already secure.

whyPoints.title: The context mark in statistics
whyPoints.description: A hypothesis test concluded without reference to the context and the significance level loses the final mark. It is a one-line habit worth marks in several questions a paper and the cheapest improvement on the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: The algebra audit done early
whyPoints.description: The Diploma assumes nine or so algebraic skills rather than teaching them. Testing for them in September of Year 12 either saves a family a term of unnecessary support or catches a gap before it compounds.

whyPoints.title: Online only in the UAE, with the working visible
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live over video on Gulf Standard Time with the working appearing line by line, which also keeps non-calculator practice honest. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring runs only in India.

faqs.question: My daughter has a 4 in IB maths. What does that actually tell us?
faqs.answer: Very little on its own, because the same 4 is produced in several different ways. One student has secure algebra and loses the whole calculus topic. Another understands broadly and never writes the working the mark scheme pays for. A third knows the content and runs out of time on the long questions carrying most marks. Those need completely different work. The script tells you which, and reading it question by question takes about forty minutes. Ask any tutor to produce a categorised list of lost marks rather than an impression.

faqs.question: What are the four reasons a student loses marks in IB maths?
faqs.answer: Conceptual, where the mathematics was not understood; procedural, where it was understood and executed wrongly; presentational, where the answer is right and the working that earns credit was never written; and temporal, where marks were lost at the end because time ran out. Conceptual losses take weeks to fix. Procedural losses take days. Presentational losses can change in one session with a mechanical habit. Temporal losses need minutes budgeted against marks. Most students at a 4 or 5 are weighted towards the last three, which is good news.

faqs.question: Can proof by induction really be taught in a couple of sessions?
faqs.answer: The structure can, and the structure is what carries the marks. An induction proof has a fixed shape: state the proposition, verify the base case explicitly, assume it for an arbitrary case, use that assumption to establish the next case while showing where it was used, and conclude by naming the principle. A student who writes that shape with an algebraic slip in the middle collects most of the credit; one with perfect algebra and no structure does not. Four worked examples and four attempts usually changes it.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose whole questions in integration?
faqs.answer: Because integration errors chain. A missing constant of integration means a boundary condition cannot be applied and every later step is wrong. An unstated substitution loses the method mark and often confuses the student two lines on. Limits not converted after a substitution produce a sign error that looks like carelessness and is a procedural gap. The fix is narrow: identify the one failing technique, do eight or ten examples of exactly that, then re-test inside a full paper question that uses it.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest mark to recover in IB maths?
faqs.answer: The statistical conclusion stated in context. A hypothesis test worked perfectly and concluded with reject the null hypothesis loses the final mark; the same test concluded with a sentence naming what that means for the situation described, at the stated significance level, collects it. It appears in several questions a paper on both courses. Students find this hard to believe until it is shown on their own script, which is why the first session works from their paper rather than from a worksheet.

faqs.question: My son was fine in Year 12 maths and is struggling now. Why?
faqs.answer: Most likely a gap in the Higher Level extension content, which arrives later in the two years and is taught faster because the shared material came first. In Analysis that means proof, complex numbers, vectors and the harder calculus techniques; in Applications, matrices, graph theory and advanced modelling. The diagnosis takes one session: list the extension topics from the syllabus and have him attempt one question on each. The gaps are usually one or two topics rather than five, and a targeted block beats general revision.

faqs.question: What algebra does the IB assume a Year 12 student already has?
faqs.answer: A specific list, each testable in two or three minutes: rearranging where the subject is on the denominator, negative and fractional indices, factorising with a leading coefficient, non-linear simultaneous equations, exact form and surds, function notation and composition, reading gradients and intercepts, and converting between radians and degrees. Cambridge IGCSE Extended and Pearson Higher tier teach these. Core and Foundation do not teach several. Running the audit in September of Year 12 takes half an hour and either saves a term or catches a gap early.

faqs.question: How does a tutor see handwritten working in an online maths lesson?
faqs.answer: Through a shared writing surface, a document camera or a phone propped over the page, with the student writing while the tutor watches the working appear line by line. That is better than reviewing a finished answer, because a mathematics error is almost always earlier than the last line. It also keeps non-calculator practice honest, since the tutor can see whether the calculator is genuinely off the desk, which is the commonest quiet shortcut in Analysis Paper 1 preparation.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come to our apartment in Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address anywhere in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma mathematics the online pool matters more than usual because cohorts are small: there may be nobody within a short drive teaching Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, while several teach it weekly online.

faqs.question: What should I ask a maths tutor before paying?
faqs.answer: Four things, all checkable. Which of the four courses is my child in, and what is not examinable in it? What will the first session produce, and will it include a categorised list of lost marks from the script? How do you run non-calculator practice? And what will you refuse to do with the exploration? Good answers are specific: they ask which course before discussing topics, they commit to a written diagnostic output, they keep the calculator off the desk, and they will teach and feed back but never write or calculate.

faqs.question: Does the choice between Analysis and Applications affect university options?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, sometimes at Higher Level, so a student who chose Applications for comfort can find a course closed in Year 13. Equally, a student heading for design, business, social sciences or medicine may be better served by Applications, where the statistical content is more useful and the grade more attainable. Read the actual entry requirements of several plausible universities in term one of Year 12.

faqs.question: How much should we pay for IB maths tutoring in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published bands give the benchmark. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 500 with travel included. A rate inside those bands is normal for the work; a rate well above them should come with something specific attached.

faqs.question: How often should a Diploma maths student practise?
faqs.answer: Frequently and briefly rather than occasionally and at length, because algebraic fluency decays without use. Twenty focused minutes four times a week beats two hours on a Sunday for maintaining manipulation speed, which is exactly what a non-calculator Paper 1 tests. Long sessions are reserved for full timed papers and Higher Level Paper 3, which need an uninterrupted block and in this belt realistically mean a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening after the school run.

faqs.question: Does the calculator model make a difference to the marks?
faqs.answer: It does on the papers where technology is permitted. The IB specifies permitted graphical display calculator models and prohibits others, and a student who learned a different model's menus loses minutes per question on papers designed around fast tool use. In statistics especially, the paper assumes regressions and tests are run with technology rather than by hand. An hour of model-specific practice, finding intersections, solving numerically, running a test, is among the best-value preparation available and almost nobody schedules it.

faqs.question: What if no tutor teaches our exact maths course at the time we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level in particular has a small cohort, so a specific course at a specific hour does occasionally come up empty, especially in the weeks before the session when demand peaks across the city. The honest options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the diagnostic list, or a wait with a date attached. A tutor teaching the wrong one of the four courses covers content the student will not be examined on.

intro.heading: Why maths is the most expensive hour a family here buys, and usually the right one
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject Al Khawaneej families ask about most, and it is also the one where the money question is sharpest. Two things make it so. The first is supply: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is taught by a small number of people in any Dubai school, the content genuinely requires them, and a tutor who is comfortable with calculus, proof and complex algebra is a scarcer commodity than one comfortable with Standard Level statistics. Scarcity sets the price, not difficulty.

The second is leverage, which works in the family's favour. Maths weakness does not stay inside maths. A student who cannot reliably make a chosen quantity the subject of a relationship loses marks in physics for mathematical reasons, loses chemistry marks in mole arithmetic and pH logarithms, and loses economics marks on quantitative questions they understood conceptually. An hour that fixes rearrangement buys marks in three or four subjects at once, which is a return no other single subject offers.

Put those together and the sensible conclusion is uncomfortable but clear. If a family in this catchment can afford exactly one tutored hour a week, maths is usually where it should go, even though it is the priciest option on the published rate card. The arithmetic favours it. What does not favour it is buying the wrong thing: the wrong route, the wrong level, or the wrong kind of session, each of which turns a good decision into an expensive one. Spend it badly and maths becomes the most expensive line in the household's education budget with the least to show for it, which is a common outcome in this catchment.

There is a route decision sitting underneath all of this that most families treat as a timetable formality. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different content, different assessment emphases and different university consequences, and the choice is normally made in a week of option forms on the basis of what a student enjoyed in Year 11. It is the single largest cost determinant in the two years, because the wrong route produces two years of remedial tutoring and sometimes a closed door at application time.

What follows prices the subject honestly. The two routes compared on the things that actually matter. Why the Higher Level band is what it is. What the hours have to do, which in maths is unusual. Where the money leaks. How the exploration is marked, criterion by criterion with the marks named, because nobody else publishes that. And the technology marks, which are quietly given away. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since in-home visiting is offered only in India.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics assessed against four criteria: knowledge and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-khawaneej.subjectsIntro: Maths is bought for its effect on other subjects as much as for itself. These are the subjects Al Khawaneej families most often find improving once the maths is fixed, and the ones that reveal maths weakness first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebra, functions, trigonometry and proof, with Higher Level going considerably further in each. The route most often required for engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees. The scarcest teaching commodity in this catchment at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, probability, modelling and technology-assisted work, with less emphasis on formal algebraic manipulation. Suited to students heading for social sciences, business, design and many life-science routes. Better supplied and priced nearer the qualified band.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where maths weakness is most visible. A student losing marks on kinematics or fields questions is frequently losing the algebra inside them, not the physics, which is why a maths hour often shows up in a physics grade first.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, proportional reasoning and logarithms for pH all sit on maths foundations. Calculation losses in chemistry are regularly mathematical rather than chemical, and respond to maths work faster than to chemistry revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Quantitative questions and diagram interpretation reward confident handling of gradients, rates and proportions. Students who understand the economics and fumble the numbers lose marks that maths tutoring recovers more cheaply than economics tutoring does.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, complexity and logic draw on the same habits as mathematical proof. Students strong in Analysis and Approaches usually find the theoretical sections straightforward and need help only with the developed solution.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Financial calculations, ratios and forecasting carry real marks and are frequently the weakest part of an otherwise capable student's paper. A short block of applied numeracy fixes more here than further content coverage.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Statistical treatment of data and the quantitative sections of the internal assessment both depend on maths confidence. Students on the Applications and Interpretation route often have an advantage here that they do not realise they have.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Materials, forces and tolerances all require numerical reasoning, and the written components reward justification supported by figures. Maths work tends to improve the quality of the justification rather than the arithmetic alone.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the richest areas of knowledge to write about, particularly on what counts as proof and whether mathematical knowledge is discovered or invented. Support is on structuring the argument; the essay remains the student's own work.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets the budget
paragraphs: This is the decision that determines what the next two years cost, and it is usually made in a hurry. The two routes are not harder and easier versions of the same course. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic manipulation, calculus, functions and proof. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics, probability, modelling and technology-assisted work. A student can be strong at one and genuinely weak at the other, and matching the route to the student is worth more than any amount of tutoring applied afterwards.

The university consequence is the part families most need to check and most often assume. Several degree routes name Analysis and Approaches specifically, particularly engineering, mathematics, physics and some economics programmes, while many social science, business, design and life science routes accept either. The reliable method is to read the admissions page for the exact degree at the exact institution, note what it names, and choose the route from that rather than from a general impression about which looks more impressive.

The test for readiness is not a conversation. Give the student an unfamiliar Higher Level Analysis and Approaches question and watch whether they can set it up without being told what to find. If they can, the route is a reasonable fit and tutoring is about depth. If they cannot, that is fixable, but it needs a term of deliberate work before the course accelerates rather than two years of remedial sessions chasing it. Buying one or two sessions of route advice before option forms close is the cheapest significant decision in this subject.

sections.heading: Why the Higher Level maths hour costs what it does
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures put specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above in Bestimate's rate table, Unitors publishes from AED 200 an hour for IB tuition, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named teaching. At the other end, Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from around AED 45 to 65. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches sits firmly in the upper bands, and the reason is supply rather than any claim about the subject's difficulty.

Count the people. A Dubai secondary school with a Diploma cohort will usually have one or two staff who teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level confidently, because the group is small and the content demands it. Those people are employed full time. The subset of them free on a given weekday evening is smaller again, and the subset willing to drive to the eastern edge of the city is smaller still. Price follows that chain, and so does availability, which in some weeks is the real constraint rather than cost.

The honest implication is worth stating. At Standard Level, particularly on the Applications and Interpretation route, the qualified band around AED 150 to 300 an hour buys genuinely good teaching and the specialist premium is not always necessary. At Higher Level Analysis and Approaches it generally is, because the difference between a tutor who can explain a solution and one who can see why this particular student cannot start the question is the whole value of the hour. All figures here are provider-published and were read in October 2026; none is an IB Gram price, and our own starting point is a consultation and a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Where maths tutoring money actually leaks
paragraphs: Maths has its own specific failure modes, different from the general tutoring wastes, and each of them feels productive while it is happening. That is what makes them expensive: nobody stops an arrangement that feels like it is working.

The first is buying demonstration instead of practice. An hour in which a tutor solves problems while a student watches produces a student who recognises solutions and cannot generate them, which is precisely the gap that shows up in a timed paper. The second is tutoring the wrong level: a student struggling with Higher Level content whose actual problem is Standard Level algebraic fluency will not be helped by more Higher Level content, however well explained. The third is neglecting the technology marks, which are available, learnable and routinely given away because they feel like administration rather than mathematics. The fourth is leaving the exploration until the term it is due, which converts a coachable twenty-mark component into a panic.

The table sets these out with what each costs and what plugs it. None requires paying more; all require spending differently. The single most valuable change for most families in this catchment is restructuring the hour so the student works and the tutor intervenes, rather than the reverse. It is less comfortable to sit through and it is the difference between an hour that moves marks and an hour that produces a feeling of progress. Ask a prospective tutor directly how the hour will be divided, and treat a vague answer as a description of the first leak.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion with the marks named
paragraphs: Every Diploma maths candidate produces a mathematical exploration, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria labelled A to E. Research across competing pages for this project found that not one of them names a single criterion, let alone its mark allocation, which is remarkable given that the exploration is a fifth of what a student is judged on. Confirm the current allocations against your child's subject guide, since guides are revised, but the shape below is what students are working to.

Criterion A covers presentation: the exploration has to be coherent, organised and concise, and this is where a rambling piece loses marks that have nothing to do with its mathematics. Criterion B covers mathematical communication: correct notation, defined terms, consistent symbols. Criterion C covers personal engagement, which is the one students fake and examiners notice. Criterion D covers reflection, meaning genuine critical consideration of what the mathematics showed and what its limits were. Criterion E, worth the most, covers the use of mathematics: whether it is at the level of the course, correct, and thorough.

Two practical consequences follow. First, a technically strong exploration with no genuine personal engagement and thin reflection loses more marks than most students expect, because those criteria are not decoration. Second, topic choice decides criterion E before a word is written: a topic whose mathematics sits below the level of the course cannot score well there however neatly it is executed. Coaching that happens at topic-choice stage is therefore worth several times coaching that happens at drafting stage, which is the opposite of when most families seek it.

sections.heading: The technology marks nobody practises
paragraphs: Diploma maths assessment assumes competent use of technology, and on the Applications and Interpretation route it assumes a great deal of it. Those marks are available, specific and learnable, and they are among the most reliably discarded marks in the subject because they feel like administration rather than mathematics. A student who can find a regression line, read a distribution, solve numerically and graph a function confidently on their own device under time pressure is picking up marks that a mathematically stronger but slower classmate loses.

The failure is nearly always practice rather than ability. Students learn the mathematics in one place and the device in another, usually by watching somebody demonstrate it once. Under exam conditions they then spend two minutes navigating menus, which costs them the question after it as well. The fix is deliberate: timed drills on the specific operations the course expects, on the actual device the student will take into the examination, repeated until the sequence is automatic.

There is a second-order benefit worth noting. A student fluent with the technology can check their own algebraic work quickly, which changes their behaviour in the non-calculator sections too, because they know what a sensible answer looks like. This is one of the cheapest improvements available in Diploma maths and it almost never appears in a tutoring plan, because it is unglamorous and it does not feel like teaching mathematics. It is, however, exactly the sort of thing a specialist tutor notices in a marked script and a generalist does not.

sections.heading: What the monthly figure has to buy
paragraphs: Converting hourly rates into a monthly figure makes the decision easier to live with. One weekly session at the qualified band published by Unitors from AED 200 an hour for IB works out near AED 800 a month. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Published packages circulate around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

The question then becomes what that monthly figure has to achieve, and in maths it should be specific. By the end of a month there should be evidence of one of three things: the student can now start unfamiliar questions of a type they previously could not, the technology operations have become automatic, or the exploration has moved from no topic to a feasible topic with criterion E satisfied in principle. Those are checkable. A general sense that maths is going better is not, and it is what most arrangements deliver.

One piece of context makes the budgeting easier this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A household that had planned for a fee increase and did not receive one has room in the education line it did not have previously, and maths is the subject where that room produces the widest return because of the leverage into the sciences and economics.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will say about availability before you pay
paragraphs: Send three things. The most recent marked maths paper with the teacher's comments intact. The route and level your child is on, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. And the realistic weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, which for a student travelling home across eastern Dubai is later than families expect and shorter than they hope.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video, used as a diagnostic. Ask the tutor to set an unfamiliar question at your child's level and watch what happens. What you are listening for afterwards is where the student stopped and why: a missing technique, an algebraic fluency gap, or a failure to identify what the question was asking for. A tutor who names that precisely has done the work. A tutor who spends the hour demonstrating solutions has shown you the first money leak on this page in action.

The disclosure, before any payment. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists are the scarcest commodity in this market, and there are weeks when no UAE-based specialist holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that is the case you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same route and level over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What will not happen is a Standard Level tutor being presented as a Higher Level specialist because a slot needed filling, since that is the most expensive mismatch available in this subject.

faqs.question: Why is an IB Higher Level maths tutor more expensive than other subjects?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. A Dubai secondary school with a Diploma cohort usually has one or two staff who teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level confidently, because the group is small and the content requires it, and those people are employed full time. The subset free on a weekday evening is smaller, and the subset willing to drive to the eastern suburbs smaller still. Published specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above reflect that chain. In some weeks availability, rather than price, is the binding constraint.

faqs.question: How do we choose between the two IB maths routes before option forms close?
faqs.answer: Decide on two things: the degree routes being considered and a cold test of readiness. Engineering, mathematics, physics and some economics programmes commonly name Analysis and Approaches specifically, while many business, social science and design routes accept either, so read the admissions page for the exact degree rather than guessing. Then give the student an unfamiliar Higher Level Analysis question and watch whether they can set it up without being told what to find. That attempt tells you more than any conversation about which subject they enjoy.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one tutored subject, should it be maths?
faqs.answer: In most Al Khawaneej households, yes, despite maths being the priciest option on the published rate card. The reason is leverage. A student who cannot reliably rearrange a relationship loses physics marks for mathematical reasons, loses chemistry marks in mole arithmetic and logarithms, and loses economics marks on quantitative questions they understood conceptually. An hour that fixes algebraic fluency buys marks in three or four subjects at once, which no other single subject offers. The exception is a subject that has collapsed entirely and needs rescuing.

faqs.question: What is the mathematical exploration marked on?
faqs.answer: Five criteria labelled A to E, totalling twenty marks. A covers presentation, meaning coherence and organisation. B covers mathematical communication, meaning notation and defined terms. C covers personal engagement. D covers reflection, meaning genuine critical consideration of what the mathematics showed. E, worth the most, covers the use of mathematics, including whether it sits at the level of the course. Confirm current allocations with your child's subject guide. Topic choice largely decides criterion E before a word is written, which is why coaching belongs at that stage.

faqs.question: Where does coaching stop on the mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is worth saying in both directions. A coach may help narrow a topic until the mathematics genuinely sits at the level of the course, read the criteria with the student letter by letter, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A coach may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's sentences, supply the mathematics or produce the analysis. The exploration is submitted as the student's own work, and operators selling completed assessments put the whole Diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the lesson and freeze on a maths paper?
faqs.answer: Usually because the sessions have been demonstrations rather than practice. Watching somebody else solve problems builds recognition; a timed paper requires generation from a cold start, which is a different skill. The restructure is simple and uncomfortable: the student attempts, the tutor intervenes only at the point where the student stops. Ten openings in twenty minutes, where the student identifies what applies without completing the question, trains the missing skill far faster than three fully worked solutions.

faqs.question: Are the calculator and technology marks really worth tutoring?
faqs.answer: They are among the most reliably discarded marks in the subject, which makes them excellent value. The assessment assumes competent technology use, particularly on the Applications and Interpretation route, and students who learned the mathematics in one place and the device in another spend exam minutes navigating menus. The fix is timed drills on the specific operations the course expects, on the actual device going into the examination, until the sequences are automatic. Fluency here also improves work in the non-calculator sections, because the student knows what a sensible answer looks like.

faqs.question: What should a month of maths tutoring have produced?
faqs.answer: One of three checkable things. The student can now start unfamiliar questions of a type they previously could not. The technology operations the course expects have become automatic. Or the exploration has moved from no topic to a feasible topic whose mathematics sits at the level of the course. A general sense that maths is going better is not evidence and is what most arrangements deliver. Agree which of the three is the target at the first session so the check is possible at the fourth.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class a reasonable alternative at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is structural rather than about teaching quality. The usual Higher Level problem is that one particular student cannot start one particular kind of question, and the cause differs between students who produce the same wrong answer. A group covers content efficiently and cannot stop to find out which cause applies to your child. Group teaching has an honest use before a content test. Ask for the student-to-tutor ratio in writing, because attractive per-head rates are sometimes advertised in language that sounds individual.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Higher Level student here need?
faqs.answer: One, placed well, plus practice between sessions that the student actually does. A second session is worth adding for a specific reason, such as a deadline cluster or a mock window, and then stopping. For a student travelling home to Al Khawaneej from Al Warqa or Al Qusais, the binding constraint is attention rather than hours, so a weekend morning with a rested student generally outperforms a second tired weekday evening by a wide margin.

faqs.question: What if my child is on the wrong maths route already?
faqs.answer: It is worth raising with the school quickly rather than waiting, because a route change becomes progressively harder as the course advances and at some point stops being possible. In the meantime the tutoring question changes: the work is closing the specific fluency gap that makes the current route hard, not covering more of the course's content. Where a change is not available, be realistic about the target grade and check whether the degree routes being considered actually require what the family assumed they require.

faqs.question: Does an undergraduate maths tutor make sense at the budget rate?
faqs.answer: For a Middle Years student or for Standard Level content, often yes, and the published budget rates of roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour are honest for what they are. Many capable engineering undergraduates study out at Academic City. The gap appears in two places: diagnosing why a particular student cannot start a question, and knowing how the exploration is marked criterion by criterion. Both are specialist knowledge rather than recent experience of passing the course, and at Higher Level they are what the premium buys.

faqs.question: When should exploration coaching start?
faqs.answer: A term before most families think of it, because topic choice is where the marks are won and it is the cheapest stage to coach. A topic whose mathematics sits below the level of the course cannot score well on the criterion worth the most, however neatly it is executed, and discovering that during drafting wastes weeks. Starting early also allows personal engagement and reflection to be genuine rather than retrofitted, which examiners distinguish more reliably than students expect.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before a first maths session?
faqs.answer: Three things. The most recent marked maths paper with the teacher's comments intact, which is where the diagnosis comes from. The route and level, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, because a tutor match on the wrong route is the most expensive mismatch in this subject. And the measured weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, taken from a week of noting when the first page was actually open rather than estimated.

Then insist the hour is spent with the student working rather than watching. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and when no Higher Level specialist can fit your week we will say so.

intro.heading: Al Mamzar's maths problem is a supply problem before it is a teaching one
paragraphs: Al Mamzar sits at the top of the Deira peninsula, with the Corniche on one side and the Sharjah border a few minutes up Al Ittihad Road. It is a residential pocket of mid-rise towers and older villas, and the families in it send children to schools spread across Al Garhoud, Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Mirdif. Very few of those schools run the full IB Diploma, which means a Diploma student living in Al Mamzar is usually travelling to reach their course in the first place. The tutoring question inherits that geography.

IB Mathematics narrows the pool again. There are two separate courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each sat at Standard or Higher Level, so a school year group splits four ways before anyone talks about tuition. A tutor who is strong on Applications statistics may have never taught the Maclaurin series work that sits only in Analysis Higher Level. A parent who books on proximity alone is choosing from whoever lives nearby rather than from whoever teaches the course their child is actually entered for.

That is the reason this page answers the supply question first and the teaching question second. Searching for a maths tutor near Al Mamzar returns listings, not availability, and almost none of them say which of the four IB Mathematics routes they can take to Higher Level. The single most useful thing a parent can do before paying anybody is to find out from the school which course code their child is entered for, then insist the tutor names the same one back.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Al Mamzar or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Lessons here run live, one-to-one, over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own graphic display calculator on screen. That is not a compromise forced by logistics. It is what lets an Al Mamzar family book the person who marks Analysis HL explorations rather than the person who happens to live two streets away.

The rest of this page is the detail a parent needs to judge a maths tutor rather than hire one on faith: how the two courses differ, what each paper is worth, the topics where Deira students reliably drop marks, the five criteria an exploration is marked against, the shape of the assessment year counted backwards, and what the Dubai market charges per hour in AED. None of it is a sales argument. All of it is checkable against the school, the course outline or a published source, and a parent who reads only the two tables will still know more about IB Mathematics than most tutoring enquiries begin with.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mamzar.programmesIntro: An Al Mamzar enquiry about maths arrives at one of three points: a Middle Years student whose numeracy is slipping, a Diploma student in the middle of a course they may have mis-chosen, or a Year 11 student deciding between the two Diploma routes. Each needs a different tutor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria, each on a 0-8 scale: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no single final exam driving the grade, so a student can hold a solid 5 while carrying gaps in algebraic fluency that only surface in Diploma year one. The fix at this stage is almost always procedural: index laws, fraction arithmetic, rearranging, and reading a question for the command term before starting.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mamzar families often use MYP 4 and 5 as the window to repair numeracy before a Diploma choice has to be made. Several schools in the Al Qusais and Al Nahda belt run MYP alongside an IGCSE pathway, so a student may sit criterion-marked tasks and externally marked papers in the same year. A tutor needs to know which of the two is driving the report grade before planning anything.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and calculus-heavy route. At Higher Level it adds complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions, proof by induction, Maclaurin series and differential equations solved by separation of variables or an integrating factor. Standard Level keeps the same five topic areas but stops well short of that depth. This is the course most engineering, physics, computer science and mathematics degrees expect, and it is the one where a weak algebraic base shows up fastest.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Mamzar sitting AA HL are typically at schools in Al Garhoud or Mirdif, and are competing for the same places as the rest of the Dubai cohort. Admissions pages at the UAE's own universities and at the UK and North American destinations Dubai families apply to generally name Analysis and Approaches where a maths prerequisite exists. Confirm the exact wording on the department's page rather than relying on a school's summary.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and technology. The graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, including in Paper 1, which is the clearest structural difference from Analysis. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory, Markov chains and a far heavier statistical inference load. Students who are competent but not instinctive with algebra often perform better here, and the course suits business, economics, psychology, design and geography routes.
programmes.countryNote: Applications is the quieter of the two courses in Deira school timetables, which makes it harder to find local help for: a neighbourhood tutor is statistically more likely to have taught Analysis. Al Mamzar families on the Applications route are the ones for whom a wider, non-local specialist pool matters most, because the course's graph-theory and Markov-chain content at Higher Level is genuinely specialist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

Marks are lost most often in calculus technique at HL and in trigonometric identities at SL. subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with calculator use assumed in both papers. HL adds matrices, eigenvalues, graph theory and Markov chains. The common failure is interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression output described in a sentence that does not answer the question asked.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria at 0-8 each. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where most marks are quietly dropped, because students describe a pattern instead of generalising and then verifying it. Extended mathematics in MYP 4-5 is the usual on-ramp to Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics and AA HL are taken together constantly, and the maths failure usually arrives first. Students who cannot rearrange a formula under time pressure lose Physics marks that have nothing to do with physics. Shared tuition planning across the two subjects is worth more than extra hours in either.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The quantitative sections - energetics, equilibrium constants, pH and buffer calculations - sit directly on the algebra an AA or AI student is already practising. Logarithms in pH work are the single most common crossover gap for Diploma students in Deira schools.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics carries quantitative questions on elasticity, market structures and national accounts arithmetic. Applications and Interpretation students pair with it naturally; Analysis students sometimes find the diagram-plus-explanation format harder than the calculation itself.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Finance and accounts, with ratio work, break-even analysis and investment appraisal. The arithmetic is light but the interpretation is marked hard, and the HL toolkit carries techniques that reward a student comfortable with the statistics side of Applications.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic, algorithmic thinking and the internal assessment solution. Students strong in Analysis HL often take it, and the paper-based pseudocode questions reward exactly the stepwise discipline that calculus technique builds.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge and turns up in essay prompts about certainty and proof. A maths tutor can supply worked examples a student can legitimately use, while the essay itself stays entirely the student's own writing.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mamzar.modesIntro: Maths tuition fails more often from the wrong shape than the wrong tutor. These are the three patterns that work for a Diploma or MYP maths student in this part of Dubai, and the signals that tell you which one you need.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: A single fixed hour a week, same tutor, running alongside the school's scheme of work. This is the shape for a student who is coping but not secure, and it is the only one that reliably closes algebraic gaps, because fluency is built by repetition over months rather than by intensity over a fortnight.
bullets: One hour weekly, same slot, same tutor through both Diploma years
Topic order follows the school's sequence, not a generic syllabus march
Non-calculator Paper 1 technique practised deliberately, every few weeks
A short written note to the parent after each session

modes.title: Exploration coaching, bounded
modes.description: A short block of sessions around the mathematical exploration, built around the five published criteria. The tutor teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, questions whether the aim is answerable, and gives feedback on drafts in the way the IB permits. The student does every piece of the writing and every calculation themselves.
bullets: Four to six sessions, usually across DP1 term three and DP2 term one
Criterion-by-criterion feedback, with the criterion letter named each time
Help choosing mathematics at the right level for the course entered
No drafting, no editing to completion, no supplied calculations

modes.title: Paper-technique intensive before the May session
modes.description: A concentrated run of sessions in the final term aimed at marks rather than content. Full papers under time, marked against the published command terms, with the error log driving the next session. It works only for a student whose content base is already there; it cannot substitute for the year.
bullets: Timed Paper 1 and Paper 2 sets, plus Paper 3 at Higher Level
Marking that separates method marks from answer marks explicitly
An error log kept across sessions, grouped by cause not by topic
Calculator-efficiency drilling for the papers that permit one

sections.heading: What a search for an IB maths tutor in Al Mamzar is actually asking
paragraphs: The literal answer: there is no large pool of IB Mathematics specialists living in Al Mamzar, and a parent who restricts the search to a fifteen-minute radius is choosing from a handful of people, most of whom teach a different curriculum. An IB maths tutor in Al Mamzar is best found by course rather than by location, and taught live over video, which is how IB Gram delivers every UAE booking.

The arithmetic is simple enough to do on paper. Dubai has 227 private schools across seventeen curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7% of private-school enrolment in the emirate. Of the schools near Al Mamzar, only a small number run the Diploma. Now split Diploma mathematics into four separate entries - Analysis SL, Analysis HL, Applications SL, Applications HL - and the number of people within a short drive who have actually taught your child's specific entry to its ceiling drops close to zero.

That is not a reason to give up on quality; it is a reason to stop using distance as the filter. The thing that changes a maths grade is a tutor who has marked the paper your child will sit, knows which command terms carry method marks, and can tell within two sessions whether the problem is content, technique or arithmetic confidence. None of those properties correlate with where the tutor parks.

So the honest framing for an Al Mamzar family is this: you are not looking for a neighbour. You are looking for a Mathematics specialist who is free at the hour your child is home and awake, which in this neighbourhood usually means after 4.30pm on a school day and sometimes after 7pm when a parent is driving back from Sharjah. Online delivery makes that hour the constraint instead of the traffic.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that decides the tutor
paragraphs: Before a single hour is booked, establish which of the two IB Mathematics courses your child is entered for and at which level. The two are not harder and easier versions of one subject; they are different subjects with a shared name. A tutor matched to the wrong one will be confident, pleasant and of limited use.

Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and sustained calculus technique. Its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so a student who has learned every method by typing it into a screen is exposed immediately. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, vector equations of lines and planes, Maclaurin series and differential equations. Those topics are where the HL grade is won and lost, and they are the topics a general maths tutor is least likely to have taught recently.

Applications and Interpretation assumes technology throughout and leans on modelling and statistics. At Higher Level it carries matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, and Markov chains, plus a much heavier inferential statistics load including chi-squared and t-tests. Students lose marks here less often on the calculation than on the sentence afterwards: a regression line correctly found and then described in words that do not answer the question posed.

For a student in DP1 who suspects they chose wrong, the window to move is narrow and controlled by the school's coordinator, not by the IB directly. Raise it early in the first year rather than late in the second, and bring evidence: marked work, not a feeling. A tutor's job at that point is to tell you honestly whether the student is struggling with the course or with mathematics, which are different diagnoses with different answers.

sections.heading: How IB Mathematics is assessed, paper by paper
paragraphs: Every IB Mathematics grade is built from external papers plus one internally assessed exploration worth a fifth of the total. Knowing the split matters because it tells you where an hour of tuition buys the most. A student two marks off a boundary in May did not lose those marks evenly across the course.

At Standard Level there are two papers. Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 40% of the grade, and the exploration carries the remaining 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers: Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 30%, Paper 3 carries 20%, and the exploration again carries 20%. Paper 3 is the component that does not exist at Standard Level at all, and it is the one students meet least often in practice, because it is built from two long extended-response problems rather than a spread of shorter questions.

That structure has a direct tuition consequence. A Higher Level student who has done thirty short questions a week all year may still be unprepared for Paper 3, because the skill it tests is sustaining a single argument across twenty-plus marks, carrying a result forward, and recognising when the question is scaffolding a method it expects you to have noticed. Practising it requires whole problems under time, not question banks.

The exploration sits outside all of that and is marked by the school against IB criteria, then moderated. It is the one component where a student has months rather than two hours, and the one most often left until the deadline forces a rushed choice of topic. On a mark-per-hour basis, it is the best-value component on the course, and the easiest to damage by getting help of the wrong kind.

sections.heading: Where Deira-schooled students lose IB maths marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Patterns repeat across a cohort, and in the Deira and Al Qusais schools the pattern is usually a procedural one carried up from the middle years rather than a conceptual failure in the Diploma itself. A student can understand differentiation perfectly and still lose four marks because they cannot handle a negative fractional index cleanly at speed.

The first cluster is algebraic manipulation: index laws, surds, partial fractions, and rearranging a formula with the unknown appearing twice. These are MYP and IGCSE skills, and when they are shaky every later topic costs more time than it should. The second cluster is trigonometry, specifically identities and solving equations over a given interval, where students find one solution and lose the marks attached to the rest.

The third is calculus technique at Higher Level, especially integration by substitution and by parts, and recognising which is called for. The fourth is statistics in Applications: students run the right test on the calculator and then write a conclusion that states the arithmetic rather than answering the question about the context. The fifth is the non-calculator paper itself for Analysis students, where a year of screen-based practice shows up as slowness rather than error.

A first diagnostic session should separate those causes rather than reteach a topic. The useful output is a short list: this student loses marks to indices, to interval solutions in trigonometry, and to interpretation sentences. That list then drives every subsequent hour, and it is the difference between tuition that moves a grade and tuition that pleasantly revisits the week's lesson.
bullets: Indices and surds: the most common single source of avoidable mark loss
Trigonometric equations: finding one root and stopping
Integration: choosing the wrong technique and committing to it
Applications statistics: a correct test with a conclusion that answers nothing
Non-calculator fluency in Analysis Paper 1, eroded by screen-based practice

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration: five criteria and the line a tutor may not cross
paragraphs: The exploration is marked against five criteria, and most students can name none of them. Criterion A covers presentation and coherence. Criterion B covers mathematical communication, including correct notation and consistent definitions. Criterion C covers personal engagement. Criterion D covers reflection. Criterion E, worth the largest share, covers the use of mathematics, judged against the level of the course the student is entered for.

Criterion E is where the grade is usually decided, and it is where a sensible-looking project fails. An Analysis Higher Level student who builds a careful piece of work around fitting a straight line to some data has not used mathematics commensurate with the course. An Applications Standard Level student who attempts something at degree level and does not understand it loses marks for a different reason. Choosing mathematics at the right altitude is the single most consequential decision in the whole component, and it is made in the first fortnight.

The boundary on help is firm and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach any mathematics the student wants to use, discuss whether an aim is answerable, ask whether a definition is being used consistently, point at a criterion by letter, and give feedback on a draft. A tutor never writes the exploration, does not produce the calculations, does not edit the prose to completion, and does not supply a topic the student then adopts wholesale. IB academic-honesty rules make the first of those a malpractice question for the student, which is a far larger problem than a disappointing mark.

The practical sequence that works: pick a question narrow enough to answer in twelve to twenty pages, check the mathematics needed is at course level, do the mathematics, then write. Students who write first and insert mathematics afterwards tend to score well on presentation and badly on criterion E, which is the wrong trade.

sections.heading: The IB maths year, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May examination session, and the school's internal calendar is what actually governs a student's year. Working backwards from May rather than forwards from September changes what a parent books and when. The IB's own exam and results dates should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before anybody plans around them; the dates that matter most to a maths student are set inside the school anyway.

Roughly eighteen months out, in DP1, the exploration topic should be settled. Twelve months out the exploration should be substantially done, because the final year's teaching load does not leave room for it. Six to eight months out, mock examinations arrive, and they are the first honest read on paper technique under time. Three months out is the last point at which a content gap can be closed without cannibalising revision. Four weeks out, the only sensible work is timed papers and the error log.

The most common planning mistake made in Deira households is booking tuition in the final term for a problem that was visible in DP1. A student who was dropping indices marks in the first mock is still dropping them in April unless somebody addressed it specifically, and April has no spare hours. The second most common is pausing tuition over the summer between the two Diploma years, which is exactly when the exploration can be finished calmly.

Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sitting alongside the Diploma run on different calendars worth knowing if a younger sibling is involved: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting in Dubai.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around Al Mamzar, in AED
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually meets. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate research puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A two-year Diploma maths commitment at one hour a week therefore sits in a range most families can plan for, and the exam-year spike is predictable rather than a surprise.

Converted to hours, the Dubai market bands are reasonably consistent across published sources. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from around AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work, and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200-450 and upwards. At the top, BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The gap between those two package figures is the travel premium, and it is worth naming for what it buys: a person in the room, and a tutor pool limited to whoever can reach your building. For a specialist Analysis Higher Level entry in Al Mamzar, that is a poor trade, which is why IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE and puts the whole budget into the match instead. Home visiting is a service offered only in India.

These figures are the market, cited from the sources named and read in October 2026, not a price list for IB Gram. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the diagnosis actually justifies, which is often fewer than a parent expects at the start of DP1 and more than they expect in DP2.

sections.heading: Verifying a maths tutor from Al Mamzar: permits, claims and three questions
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you as fact. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service.

Regulators matter in the other direction too. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram does not hold one and makes no claim of approval, accreditation or partnership with KHDA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any tutoring service that implies otherwise is worth questioning.

Three questions settle most of it. First: which IB Mathematics course and level have you taught to final examinations, named exactly? Second: how will you mark a Paper 1 answer, and will you show me the method marks separately from the answer mark? Third: what will you not do with the exploration? A tutor who answers the third one crisply and unprompted is usually the one worth booking.

Add one practical check for an Al Mamzar household. Ask for the hour in Gulf Standard Time, in writing, and ask what happens when it is missed. A specialist booked at a time that collides with the drive back from Sharjah is a specialist you will cancel on, and a cancelled hour teaches nobody anything.
bullets: Ask for the course and level by name: "Analysis and Approaches HL", not "IB maths"
Ask how method marks and answer marks are reported back to you
Ask what the tutor will refuse to do with the exploration
Confirm the permit position rather than accepting a claim of accreditation
Fix the hour in Gulf Standard Time and agree a rescheduling rule in advance

process.title: Tell us the entry, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps names the course and level - Analysis HL, Applications SL - plus the school, the year group and the hour that genuinely works on a school day in Al Mamzar. A subject name alone sends the request to the wrong half of the maths pool.

process.title: A diagnostic hour, free
process.description: The trial lesson is a diagnosis rather than a sample lesson. The tutor sets work that separates content gaps from technique gaps from arithmetic confidence, and writes back with the short list. If the diagnosis says fewer hours than you expected, that is what you are told.

process.title: Agree the plan against the school's calendar
process.description: Mock dates, exploration deadlines and the school's teaching order decide the plan, not a generic syllabus march. For a DP1 student that usually means exploration work in term three; for a DP2 student it means paper technique from the first mock onwards.

process.title: Fix the hour and keep it
process.description: One slot, same tutor, in Gulf Standard Time, chosen to survive a normal Al Mamzar weekday rather than an ideal one. Later starts are standard here. Sessions run live over video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own calculator visible on screen.

process.title: Review against marks, not impressions
process.description: Every few weeks the error log and the last marked paper decide whether the plan holds. If a tutor is not the right match for the course, we say so and change the tutor rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.description: An Analysis Higher Level request goes to someone who has taught Analysis Higher Level to examinations. In a neighbourhood where the local specialist pool for a specific IB Mathematics entry is close to empty, that is the whole of the argument for teaching online.

whyPoints.title: Paper technique marked, not described
whyPoints.description: Answers come back with method marks and answer marks separated, so a student can see that a correct final value scored two of five. That distinction is invisible in most homework help and it is where Diploma maths grades actually move.

whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches mathematics, questions an aim, and gives feedback against a named criterion. A tutor never writes an exploration or produces a student's calculations. The boundary is published here because the alternative puts a student's diploma at risk.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the name of whoever published it and the month it was read. No invented statistics, no satisfaction percentages, no self-awarded ratings - if a number cannot be sourced, it is not on the page.
