whyPoints.description: Sessions are booked to the half hour after school transport actually arrives, with later slots available for families crossing the Sharjah boundary. A plan that assumes a 4pm start in Al Mamzar is a plan that gets cancelled.

faqs.question: Is there an IB maths tutor actually based near Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: Very few, and that is the honest answer. Al Mamzar is largely residential, the nearest Diploma schools are in the Al Garhoud cluster, and IB Mathematics splits into four separate entries across two courses and two levels. The number of people within a short drive who have taught your child's exact entry to final examinations is close to zero. IB Gram does not place tutors at UAE addresses at all; lessons run live one-to-one over video, which means the match is made on course expertise and availability at your hour rather than on driving distance.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics AA or AI if they want to study engineering?
faqs.answer: Engineering departments generally name Analysis and Approaches where a mathematics prerequisite is listed, because the course carries the calculus and algebraic technique the first year of a degree assumes. Check the exact wording on the department's own admissions page rather than a school summary, since requirements differ between institutions and between countries. If your child is competent but not fluent algebraically, the harder question is Analysis at Standard or Higher Level, and that is a conversation to have with marked work in front of you rather than on instinct.

faqs.question: How many marks is Paper 3 worth in IB Mathematics HL?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 carries 20% of the Higher Level grade and does not exist at Standard Level. It is built from two long extended-response problems rather than a spread of shorter questions, which makes it the component students practise least and find most unfamiliar. The skill it tests is sustaining one argument across twenty or more marks, carrying results forward, and spotting that an early part was scaffolding for a later one. Preparing for it needs whole problems under timed conditions; question banks of short items do not develop the same stamina.

faqs.question: My son is getting 4s in Mathematics AA SL at a Deira school. What usually moves that?
faqs.answer: In that band the cause is normally procedural rather than conceptual. The repeat offenders are index laws, surds, rearranging a formula where the unknown appears twice, and trigonometric equations where one solution is found and the rest are left. A first session should separate those causes rather than reteach the week's topic, and produce a short written list of what this specific student loses marks to. That list then drives every later hour. Expect movement over a term of consistent weekly work, not over a fortnight of intensive sessions.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on help with the IB mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is worth stating. A tutor may teach any mathematics the student wants to use, discuss whether the aim is answerable, check that notation and definitions are consistent, point at a criterion by its letter, and give feedback on a draft. A tutor never writes the exploration, never produces the calculations, and never edits the prose to completion. IB academic-honesty rules treat supplied work as a malpractice matter for the student, so the risk of getting this wrong falls on your child rather than on the tutor.

faqs.question: Which graphic display calculator does my child need for IB Mathematics?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and it matters more than parents expect, because fluency is model-specific. Ask the department which models they teach and permit, then make sure the tutor works on the same one; a student who learns a menu path on one calculator loses time hunting for it on another under examination pressure. Applications and Interpretation assumes calculator use in both papers, so the fluency requirement is higher there. Analysis students need the opposite discipline too: deliberate non-calculator practice, because Paper 1 permits no technology at all.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of IB maths tuition is sensible in DP1?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the usual starting point in the first Diploma year, and for most students it is enough. The first year's job is closing procedural gaps and getting the exploration topic settled, both of which respond to consistency rather than volume. Two hours is justified where a student has moved curriculum recently, is taking Higher Level with a weak algebraic base, or is carrying Physics and Mathematics Higher Level together. Adding hours before a diagnosis has identified a specific cause usually buys pleasant revision rather than movement in a grade.

faqs.question: Is Mathematics AI HL accepted by UAE universities for an economics degree?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is designed with exactly those routes in mind - economics, business, psychology, geography and design - and its statistical content maps well onto a first-year quantitative methods course. Individual departments, however, set their own prerequisites and some economics programmes still name Analysis. Read the department's published entry requirements directly and confirm them with the admissions office rather than relying on a general statement, because the answer varies by institution and can change between intakes.

faqs.question: What does an online IB maths lesson for an Al Mamzar student actually look like?
faqs.answer: A fixed hour in Gulf Standard Time, live, one tutor and one student, on a shared whiteboard both can write on. The student's graphic display calculator is visible on screen so key sequences can be corrected in real time, and work is photographed or shared beforehand so the tutor arrives knowing what went wrong. Sessions end with a short note to the parent naming what was covered and what was set. Nothing is pre-recorded, and no tutor travels to an Al Mamzar address; home visits are a service offered only in India.

faqs.question: My daughter moved from MYP into Mathematics AA HL and is drowning. Can she change level?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the window is narrow. Level changes are controlled by the school's Diploma coordinator and are far easier early in DP1 than late in DP2, so raise it in the first term rather than after the first mock. Bring marked work rather than a description of how it feels. The underlying issue after an MYP course is often algebraic fluency rather than ability, because criterion-marked tasks can mask procedural gaps that an Analysis Higher Level paper exposes immediately. A diagnostic session should tell you which of the two you are dealing with.

faqs.question: Do maths tutors working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with caution. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: What do maths tutors charge per hour around Deira and Al Mamzar?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 split into bands. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes about AED 270, Bestimate puts specialist work at AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180-500. Those are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram's own prices.

faqs.question: When should an IB maths exploration be started?
faqs.answer: Topic settled by roughly eighteen months before the May session, mathematics done and a full draft existing by around twelve months out. That timing exists because the second Diploma year has no spare capacity: a student finishing an exploration in DP2 is doing it instead of paper practice. The summer between the two years is the most underused window families have, and it is when a calm, well-chosen exploration gets finished. Students who leave the topic choice until the school's deadline forces it almost always pick something too broad.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if they are on different IB maths courses?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and it is worth resisting. If one child is on Analysis Higher Level and the other on Applications Standard Level, those are different subjects sharing a name, and the depth that makes a tutor useful on one does not transfer. Separate matches cost the same per hour and work considerably better. Where both children are on the same course and level, a shared tutor is sensible and keeps the scheduling simple, but the sessions should still run separately rather than as a pair taught together.

intro.heading: Why the same maths hour costs AED 50 or AED 650
paragraphs: There is no other school subject where the price range is this wide or the difference in what you receive this large. Across the Dubai market, Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table shows named IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200-450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate, up to AED 500 independently. Every one of those figures is real and published by the provider named.

What separates them is not enthusiasm. At the bottom of the range you are buying somebody who was good at maths recently, which genuinely helps a student stuck on content. At the top you are buying somebody who has marked the course, knows what the exploration criteria reward, and can tell you in one session whether a Higher Level grade is arithmetically reachable before the May session. In the middle you are buying a trained teacher who knows the syllabus and may or may not know the assessment design, and that distinction is where most Al Manara money is lost.

The geography matters too, because Al Manara sits inland between two school clusters - the coastal Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah campuses seaward, the Al Barsha and Al Quoz cluster inland - and the nearby tutor pool is weighted towards the UK curriculum, which accounted for 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25 against 7% for the IB. So an in-home maths quote to an Al Manara villa is usually a British-curriculum maths teacher pricing in a drive, not an IB specialist pricing in expertise. Both are reasonable products. They are not the same product.

The costliest decision of all is not the hourly rate; it is the course. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are different courses, not tiers of one. Analysis is algebra, calculus and proof, with an HL Paper 3 extended investigation. Applications is modelling and statistics with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout, and HL content including matrices and graph theory. Competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes generally expect Analysis, often at Higher Level, and a student on the wrong route may find courses closed that nobody mentioned in Year 11.

So this page is a budget document. It prices the market with sources attached, sets the two courses side by side, maps the paper weightings at HL and SL, names the exploration criteria so you can test a tutor in thirty seconds, and lists the five specific places IB maths money is wasted in Dubai. It gives no IB Gram price list: what a block costs depends on the level, the component and the weeks remaining, and a figure typed into a landing page goes stale while a parent relies on it.

On delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is what makes it possible to pay for IB specialism rather than for a drive along Al Wasl Road.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara maths enquiry needs locating in the IB continuum first, because what an hour buys changes completely between stages - and so does what it costs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one mathematics course, choosing between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at Higher and Standard Level. All four combinations include the exploration, an independent piece of mathematics typically running 12 to 20 pages, assessed against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Higher Level candidates also sit Paper 3.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all Al Manara maths spending goes and where the rates are highest. The usual trigger is a Year 12 report after the first proper assessment, when a student who reached a strong IGCSE grade meets Higher Level and discovers that pattern recognition no longer earns marks.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Standard and Extended pathways assessed against four criteria scored 0-8: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the criterion that matters most for later, because generalising and justifying a rule is precisely the skill the Diploma exploration will assess under a different name.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest point in the whole pathway to buy mathematics support, at mid-market rather than specialist rates, and the point at which Dubai families are least inclined to. Technique built here at AED 150-300 an hour is technique that does not have to be retrofitted at AED 200-450 in Year 12.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: No external assessment and no marks, with reporting against conceptual understanding. What it builds is number sense and the habit of explaining why an answer works, which is the foundation every later criterion rests on. Fluency problems that look small here become the rearrangement failures that cost Higher Level marks.
programmes.countryNote: Primary maths support in Dubai sits at the bottom of the rate card and does more per dirham than anything bought later. For an Al Manara family moving into the IB from another system, the adjustment is usually about justification rather than content level.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme mathematics
programmes.description: CP students take at least two Diploma courses, which may include a mathematics course, assessed exactly as a Diploma student's would be with the same papers and the same exploration. The programme is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is often confused with the Diploma when families compare post-16 costs and workload.
programmes.countryNote: If a UAE federal university is in view, the Ministry of Education equivalency position should be checked directly with the authority before building a pathway, since a CP certificate is not the Diploma and no IB points threshold for equivalency appears in the sourced guidance.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: IB mathematics is four courses rather than one, and the money goes to different places in each. Below, what each component assesses and where candidates lose marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof at depth, with three papers including Paper 3, a sustained pair of investigative questions. The most expensive hour in Dubai school tuition and the one where specialism matters most: marks go on unjustified steps, missing domains and induction attempted without the inductive step written out.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same character of mathematics with reduced depth and two papers rather than three. Students lose marks on calculus technique and on reading questions that look familiar and are not. A common and costly error is assuming SL is HL with fewer topics; the assessment emphasis differs as well as the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, matrices and graph theory with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout, plus Paper 3. Frequently chosen as the easier route and frequently a surprise: the HL statistics content is demanding and the modelling questions punish answers that produce a number without interpreting it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route at reduced depth, two papers. Marks are lost reporting a regression coefficient without interpreting it in context, choosing a statistical test the data does not support, and trusting the calculator output without checking whether it is plausible.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: The internally assessed component, typically 12 to 20 pages, marked against presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Personal engagement and reflection are where students and generalist tutors both under-invest, because they reward something that is not mathematical skill.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: A pair of extended, structured investigations that build across many parts, where an early error propagates. It cannot be topic-spotted and it rewards mathematical stamina rather than recall. This is the single component where a specialist is hardest to substitute, in either course.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, investigating patterns
subjects.description: The criterion that asks a student to find a pattern, generalise it and justify the generalisation. Most lost marks are in the justification, which students treat as optional. It is the same skill the Diploma exploration assesses, two to four years earlier and at a lower hourly rate.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics as the foundation
subjects.description: The algebraic fluency the Diploma assumes. A student who reached a strong IGCSE grade through recall rather than understanding usually meets a wall in the first Diploma term, and the fix is foundation work nobody wants to pay specialist rates for.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Pre-Diploma preparation taken by stronger IGCSE candidates and genuinely useful for Analysis and Approaches. The jump in algebraic demand is steep, which makes it a useful early signal of whether HL Analysis is realistic for a given student.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator skills
subjects.description: Assumed rather than taught in most classrooms, and more consequential in Applications and Interpretation where the calculator is integral. Worth a session or two, not a term - which makes it one of the easier places to overspend if a tutor builds a block around it.

subjects.name: Statistics for the exploration
subjects.description: Many explorations and internal assessments in other subjects rest on a statistical test, and students frequently choose one their data cannot support. Teaching the choice of test, and its assumptions, is high-value work that transfers beyond mathematics.

subjects.name: Proof and mathematical argument
subjects.description: Induction, contradiction and direct proof, where marks are awarded for the structure of the argument rather than for arriving at the result. Students lose whole questions by asserting what they were asked to show, and this is almost never addressed by content revision.

sections.heading: The Dubai rate card for IB maths, with every source named
paragraphs: Three of six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all - one page's own FAQ asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer - and the two that do quote in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. So here is the AED market with a name attached to every figure, which is the part a parent can verify independently.

Budget online tuition: Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online: around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. A named IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist: AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table showing 200-450+. Premium or examiner-led: AED 500-650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one, travel included: Bestimate 180-350, independent home tutors 200-500.

Monthly, which is the more useful frame for a two-year Diploma: published packages run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. For Higher Level mathematics in an exam year, plan on that top band if a specialist is involved.

One caution on the top of the range. Examiner-led pricing assumes examiner status, and Caution 17 of this project's research is explicit: tutors should not be described as IB or Cambridge examiners where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content. If somebody charges AED 650 on that basis, ask what the evidence is. Fee context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: The decision that costs more than any tutoring: AA or AI
paragraphs: Before any money is spent on hours, the course choice should be examined, because getting it wrong costs more than two years of tuition. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, functions, calculus and proof route. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout and Higher Level content that includes matrices and graph theory. They are separate courses with separate papers and separate university consequences.

The widespread belief that Applications is the easy option is the source of most of the damage. It is a different mathematics, not a lighter one, and its Higher Level statistics content defeats plenty of students who chose it to avoid calculus. Meanwhile competitive engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics programmes expect Analysis, typically at Higher Level, which means a student who took Applications to protect their grade may have closed the degree they wanted.

The reverse error is just as expensive. A student heading for design, business, some medical systems or the social sciences, who takes Analysis Higher Level to look strong, may spend two years fighting a course whose content they will never use while their other five subjects suffer. The right question is not which is harder but which is correct for the intended destination, checked against those universities' own published requirements rather than against general guidance, including this page's.

Where a tutor adds genuine value here is diagnosis rather than opinion: looking at a marked piece of algebra done under time pressure and saying whether Analysis Higher Level is a realistic proposition for this student within the hours their full Diploma allows. That is evidence. Get it in Year 11, because changing route in Year 12 is permitted at some schools and painful everywhere.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit: weightings at HL and SL
paragraphs: Spending decisions should follow the mark allocation, and most families have never seen it laid out. Every one of the four IB maths courses carries an internally assessed exploration alongside externally marked papers, and Higher Level candidates sit three papers where Standard Level candidates sit two. The exploration is worth roughly a fifth of the grade in each course, and it is completed and marked months before the written session.

That timing is the key financial fact about IB maths. Exploration marks are banked. A student who lands a weak exploration carries that into the session and cannot retrieve it with strong paper performance, which means the cheapest point to spend money is while the exploration is still being planned - not in the revision term, when the hourly rates are at their highest and the recoverable marks are at their lowest.

On the papers themselves, the Higher Level Paper 3 deserves separate budgeting. It is a pair of extended investigative questions that build across many parts, so an early error propagates through everything that follows, and it cannot be prepared by topic-spotting. It rewards stamina and structure, which are trained by working full investigations under time and then dissecting them. That is specialist work and it takes several sessions rather than one.

Confirm the exact weightings for your child's course and level with the school or the subject guide rather than with any summary, including this one, because the IB revises assessment structures between cycles and the school holds the current version. The table sets out the shape so you can see where the money should go.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Ask any prospective maths tutor to name the exploration criteria and say what each is worth. It takes thirty seconds and it is the most reliable test available, because across the entire competitor corpus researched for this market not one page names a single IB assessment criterion. A teacher who has marked explorations answers immediately. One who has not will talk about quality, originality and presentation in general terms.

The criteria cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The last of those is where strong mathematicians already score, and the first four are where marks are routinely left on the table - particularly personal engagement and reflection, which reward something that is not mathematical skill at all. A technically impressive exploration with no genuine engagement and no reflection on what the mathematics showed loses bands that a weaker piece of mathematics would have kept.

The single most expensive mistake is the question. An exploration built on a question that is too broad, or that has no real mathematics in it, or whose data cannot support the analysis, cannot be rescued by work later - it has to be restarted, usually at the point when there is no time to restart. That is why a short block at the question-choosing stage returns more than any amount of work on a draft that is already structurally wrong.

The boundary here is absolute and it protects your child rather than the provider. A tutor may explain each criterion, interrogate the question until the student can defend it, teach the mathematics or the statistical test required, mark practice work, and give written questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to show the right register, supply data or a question, or edit to completion. In this market one provider sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Five places Al Manara families waste IB maths money
paragraphs: First, hiring at specialist rates for foundation work. A Year 12 student who cannot rearrange reliably needs algebraic fluency rebuilt, and that is mid-market teaching at AED 150-300 rather than specialist teaching at AED 200-450 and above. Paying the top rate for work that does not need the top skill is the most common overspend in Dubai maths tuition, and it is often the tutor who should say so.

Second, buying the exploration block too late. The mark is banked before the papers, so an exploration that is structurally wrong in March cannot be fixed by hours in April. Money spent while the question is still being chosen buys a different outcome from the same money spent on a finished draft, and the second purchase is frequently the larger one.

Third, paying a travel premium for a screen-based subject. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180-500 against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. For maths, where the work is annotated calculation that both parties need to see, a shared screen is at least as good as a shared table - and the premium buys a drive from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim through late-afternoon traffic, not better mathematics. Where supervision is the real need, in-home is worth paying for, and plenty of Dubai providers deliver it.

Fourth, group classes for a 1-7 subject with four courses. A tuition centre group cannot be taught to one student's course and level, and a room containing AA HL, AI SL and IGCSE students receives generic mathematics. It is cheaper per hour and often worth nothing per hour for a Diploma candidate. Fifth, a block built around graphical display calculator training: it is a genuine need, more so in Applications and Interpretation, and it is one or two sessions rather than a term.

sections.heading: The algebra nobody wants to pay for
paragraphs: The most common real problem in Diploma mathematics is not the Diploma content. It is that the student arrived without the algebraic fluency the course assumes. They reached a good IGCSE grade by recognising question types and reproducing methods, which the IGCSE rewards sufficiently, and then met a course where every question requires rearrangement, substitution and manipulation under time pressure as a precondition rather than as the task.

It shows in a specific way on a marked script. The method is right. The physics or the calculus is understood. The question is abandoned two lines in, or finished with a value that is wrong because a sign flipped in the third step. That is not a Diploma content gap and no amount of Higher Level teaching fixes it - which is why a family can spend a term at specialist rates and see the same marks.

The honest prescription is unglamorous: a defined block of foundation work, diagnosed from marked papers, targeting rearrangement, indices, surds, fractions and function manipulation under time. It is mid-market teaching rather than specialist teaching, it usually takes weeks rather than terms, and it unblocks everything bought afterwards. A tutor who identifies this and says so is saving you money rather than losing a sale.

There is a prevention version of the same argument. The same work done in Year 11 - or earlier, as MYP Criterion B generalisation and justification practice - costs mid-market rates and removes the Year 12 crisis entirely. For an Al Manara family with a child in Year 10 or 11 who is coping but not comfortable, that is the single best-value maths purchase available in this market.

sections.heading: Budgeting a Diploma maths year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Treat two years of Diploma mathematics as a budget with phases rather than as an open monthly commitment, because the phases need different things and cost different amounts. Most UAE candidates sit the May session, and IB session dates are not published on this page: ibo.org blocks automated fetching, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been verified from the IB itself. Confirm every date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly.

Counting backwards, the final phase before the papers is timed-paper work with marked scripts and a logged error list, plus Paper 3 stamina practice for Higher Level candidates. The phase before it belongs to the mock round, which is the last honest diagnostic the school will provide and the best evidence available for whether a Higher Level grade is reachable. Before that, the exploration is finished and away. Before that, the exploration question is chosen - and that is the cheapest high-value moment in the whole two years.

Earlier still, in the first Diploma term, is the foundation window: the point at which an algebra problem can be fixed at mid-market rates before it compounds. And before the Diploma begins at all, in Year 11, is the course decision between Analysis and Applications, which costs nothing to make well and a great deal to make badly.

Mapped that way, a sensible Al Manara budget is not a flat monthly fee for two years. It is a foundation block early, a short exploration block at question stage, weekly support through the second year where the subject genuinely needs it, and a Paper 3 and timed-paper block before the session. That shape costs less than continuous specialist hours and does more.

sections.heading: Verifying the tutor, and what no provider can claim
paragraphs: Two free checks before the first paid hour. The permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you.

On a page that prices everything else, this is the one line item at zero. MoHRE's own service page is titled "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", it lists no fees at all, it states a two-working-day completion time, and the whole process runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Nothing in the AED 33 to AED 650 spread set out above is paying for it. Eligibility is wide enough that almost any credible Al Manara maths tutor already qualifies: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Free, two days, and open to that many categories together mean a working tutor without one has chosen not to have one, which is a fact about the tutor rather than about the paperwork.

A related rule, because it comes up constantly in Dubai: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat it as press-reported and verify against current policy, but decline the arrangement where your child's own maths teacher is paid privately.

And the claims to refuse, because the top of the maths rate card is where they appear. No individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals - KHDA regulates schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. Nobody should claim IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership. Nobody should be described as an IB examiner without evidence of current status, and examiner status must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and operates no premises in the UAE.

sections.heading: Availability at Higher Level, stated honestly
paragraphs: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people in any city, and Paper 3 specialism narrows the pool further. In the weeks before the May session, the right specialist may not have a slot at the hour an Al Manara family needs. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking phone number. This page would rather say it.

What that means in practice is a disclosure and a choice. Where the exact match is unavailable at your preferred time, the options are stated: a different hour with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date, or an adjacent specialist - an Applications Higher Level teacher covering a statistics-heavy exploration, say - who can address the component you need now, with the limits named so you can judge.

Delivery being online also means the specialist may sit outside the UAE. That is stated rather than disguised, and sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the Al Manara school run, which varies by whether your child travels seaward to Umm Suqeim or inland to Al Barsha. A family paying specialist rates is entitled to know exactly what they are buying and from where.

The free trial lesson is what converts all of this from a promise into a check. One lesson, no cost, with the marked paper or the exploration draft on screen, and the tutor naming the course, the level and the criteria. If the fit is wrong, nothing is owed and no block has been bought - which is the only honest way to sell the most expensive hour in Dubai school tuition.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the component
process.description: "Analysis and Approaches HL, Year 12, exploration question not yet agreed" is actionable in one message and tells a specialist exactly where the money should go. "IB maths help" is three exchanges away from a plan, and the exchanges are the expensive part.

process.title: Send the marked paper or the exploration draft
process.description: A marked script shows whether marks are going on content, on algebraic fluency or on notation and command terms - three problems with three different prices. An exploration draft shows whether the question itself is the problem, which is the one that cannot be fixed later.

process.title: Apply the criteria test yourself
process.description: You get a named tutor with the IB maths courses and levels they have taught. The check you can run without any IB knowledge is to ask them to name the exploration criteria and what each is worth. A specialist answers in seconds; a generalist talks about quality.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson at no cost with the marked work on screen. It should end with the component named, the type of problem named, and an honest number of hours - including the answer that foundation work at a lower rate is what is actually needed. Nothing is owed if the answer is no.

process.title: Buy the phase, not a subscription
process.description: A foundation block, a short exploration block at question stage, weekly support where the subject needs it, then a timed-paper and Paper 3 block before the session. That shape costs less than continuous specialist hours across two years and delivers more.

process.title: Review against the school's marks
process.description: Progress is judged on the school's next assessed piece, the mock, and the exploration band where one is given - never on a tutor's internal tests, which no university sees. If the mark moved, the spend worked. If not, the diagnosis is revised rather than repeated.

whyPoints.title: Every rate carries its publisher
whyPoints.description: Tutopiya, EdFlik, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED each published a figure quoted on this page, and you can go and check them. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The criteria get named
whyPoints.description: Not one page in the researched competitor corpus names a single IB assessment criterion. The exploration criteria - presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, use of mathematics - are named here and are the test a parent can apply to any tutor in thirty seconds.

whyPoints.title: You are told when a cheaper tier is correct
whyPoints.description: Foundation algebra does not need a specialist rate. Calculator fluency is one or two sessions. A tutor who says so is reducing your bill, and it is the clearest signal that the diagnosis came from marked work rather than from a sales conversation.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home maths tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180-500 because a drive from Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim is priced into the hour. For annotated calculation on a shared screen that premium buys logistics, not mathematics - and the same monthly spend buys roughly eight online sessions against four in-home visits.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost per hour around Al Manara?
faqs.answer: Market figures with their publishers, not ours. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, named IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently. IB Gram's own figure comes from the consultation after the free trial, because it depends on level, component and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level maths the most expensive hour in Dubai school tuition?
faqs.answer: Because the pool of people who can teach it well is small and the components are unforgiving. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level demands algebra, calculus and proof at depth, and Higher Level candidates also sit Paper 3, a pair of extended investigations that build across many parts so that an early error propagates through everything after it. A teacher who has not marked the course can teach the mathematics correctly and still miss the technique, which is the part being bought. Scarcity plus consequence is what produces the AED 200-450 and above band.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the cheaper course to tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and choosing it to save money is usually a false economy. Applications is a different mathematics rather than a lighter one: modelling and statistics with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout, and Higher Level content including matrices and graph theory. Its statistics load defeats plenty of students who picked it to avoid calculus. The larger cost is admissions: competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes generally expect Analysis, often at Higher Level, so a route chosen to protect a grade can close the degree it was protecting it for.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest moment to spend money on IB maths?
faqs.answer: Two moments, both early. First, the course decision in Year 11 between Analysis and Applications, diagnosed from marked algebra done under time pressure rather than from a report - that costs a session or two and prevents two years on the wrong course. Second, the exploration question stage, before any mathematics is done, because an exploration built on a question with no real mathematics in it cannot be rescued and has to be restarted. Spending in the revision term is the most expensive and least recoverable option of all.

faqs.question: Can a weak exploration be made up for in the written papers?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the arithmetic that should drive the budget. The exploration is internally assessed, worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and completed and marked months before the written session. Whatever band it lands in travels with the student into the exams, and strong paper performance does not retrieve the marks lost there. That is why a short block while the question is still being chosen returns more than a larger block spent on a finished draft, and why late exploration help is the most frequently wasted purchase in IB maths.

faqs.question: What are the exploration criteria, and why should I ask a tutor to name them?
faqs.answer: They cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Ask because it is the fastest test of real IB experience available: across the sixty-odd competitor pages researched for this market, not one names a single IB assessment criterion. A teacher who has marked explorations answers in seconds. Personal engagement and reflection are where marks are most often left on the table, because they reward something that is not mathematical skill - a technically strong piece with no genuine engagement loses bands a weaker one keeps.

faqs.question: My child understands the maths but keeps losing marks. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost always algebraic fluency rather than Diploma content. It shows in a specific way on a marked script: the method is right, the concept is understood, and the question is abandoned two lines in or finished with a wrong value because a sign flipped in the third step. No amount of Higher Level teaching fixes it, which is why families can spend a term at specialist rates and see the same marks. The fix is a defined foundation block on rearrangement, indices, surds and function manipulation under time - mid-market work, not specialist work.

faqs.question: Is a maths group class at a Dubai tuition centre worth considering?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE topic revision, often yes, since the content is common. For the Diploma it is usually poor value, because there are four distinct maths courses and a room containing Analysis HL, Applications SL and IGCSE students can only receive generic mathematics. Nobody can teach to one student's exploration criteria in a group. It is cheaper per hour and can be worth nothing per hour for a Diploma candidate. Note also that a centre with premises operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different licence from an individual tutor's MoHRE permit.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an Al Manara home?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For an Al Manara family lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the exploration draft and the mark scheme are visible to both sides and the annotated work stays with the student. For mathematics specifically that is no compromise: the work is annotated calculation both parties need to see, and a shared screen does that at least as well as a shared table.

faqs.question: How much of my budget should go on Paper 3 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: A dedicated block rather than a few minutes inside general revision. Paper 3 is a pair of extended, structured investigations that build across many parts, so an early error propagates and a familiar-looking topic gives no advantage. It cannot be topic-spotted and it rewards stamina and structure, which are trained by working full investigations under time and then dissecting where the chain broke. Several sessions, placed before the mock round rather than after it, and with a specialist - this is the component where a non-specialist can least substitute at any price.

faqs.question: Can an A Level maths teacher near Al Manara tutor the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For content gaps in the first Diploma year, often yes - the calculus is the same calculus. For the assessment design, be careful. Grades run 1-7, there is an internally assessed exploration in every course with criteria published by letter, Higher Level candidates sit a Paper 3 with no A Level equivalent, and command terms carry mark-scheme consequences. The local pool near Al Manara is weighted that way: the UK curriculum took 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25 against 7% for the IB, and tutor supply follows enrolment.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Diploma maths realistically need?
faqs.answer: Usually one protected weekly hour, rising to two in a specific phase such as a Paper 3 block or the weeks after a disappointing mock. More than that competes with the other five Diploma subjects, the core, and the practice a tutor sets between lessons, which also has to fit. A student doing four hours of maths tuition a week is usually a student whose other subjects are about to slip. Buy the phase that the diagnosis points to rather than a standing weekly commitment across two years.

faqs.question: Should I pay extra for a tutor described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and never for what the title is implying. Premium rates in this market reach AED 650, with BartyED publishing that figure, and examiner framing is often what justifies it. Current examiner status should be evidenced before it is charged for, and it must never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it is not. Ask what the evidence is and what concretely changes in the lesson. A specialist who has taught and marked the course at your child's level is the thing you actually need.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list IB exam dates for planning?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated fetching, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified exam date to a parent who will plan a revision budget around it does real harm. UAE candidates sit the May session, which is a pattern rather than a date. Confirm every specific date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are sourced from the boards and used elsewhere on this site with their framing intact.

faqs.question: What if no Analysis Higher Level specialist is free at our time?
faqs.answer: You are told, with options rather than a quiet substitution. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people and Paper 3 specialism narrows the pool further, so before the May session the right person may not have your preferred hour. The honest alternatives are a different time with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date, or an adjacent specialist who can cover the component you need now with the limits of the match stated. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.closingHeading: Spend on the phase, not on the month
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-manara.closingBody: If you are pricing an IB maths tutor in Al Manara, the question that saves the most is not what an hour costs but which phase you are in. Send the course and level, the component, and the marked paper or exploration draft, and you will get a named tutor who has taught that course, an honest view of whether specialist or mid-market work is what you actually need, and a free trial lesson before any block is agreed. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed to the real return from Umm Suqeim or Al Barsha. If foundation algebra at a lower rate is the right answer, you will be told that instead of sold an upgrade.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Mathematics at Higher and Standard Level, both routes, for students at the Diploma schools reachable from Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai. Work is scoped from where the student actually is in the two-year course and from the school's own deadlines rather than from a standard syllabus order.

intro.heading: What can eight weeks of maths actually do?
paragraphs: Almost every family that contacts a tutor about Diploma Mathematics arrives with the same underlying question, usually unasked: is it too late, and if not, what will this actually change? It is a fair question and it deserves a numerate answer rather than reassurance. Eight weekly sessions is about eight hours of teaching and perhaps sixteen hours of work if the student does what is set. That is a real quantity and it is also a finite one.

What those eight hours can achieve depends almost entirely on one thing: where the student is in the course and what the next fixed date is. In the first term of Diploma year one, eight hours spent on algebraic fluency and the habit of writing method compounds across two years and is the best value in the whole programme. Eight hours three weeks before an Exploration deadline can only be process coaching on work the student has already done. Eight hours six weeks before the written papers cannot teach a year of calculus, but it can convert a student who knows the mathematics into one who finishes the paper, which is frequently worth a grade.

Families in Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai face an extra complication in reading their own position. Because the schools in this district largely run to sixteen, most Diploma students here have moved campus, often recently. Nobody at home has a long history with how that school sequences its topics, when its internal deadlines fall, or how hard its mocks are marked. A parent can genuinely not know whether their child is behind, on track, or being taught in an unusual order.

The first job, then, is to locate the student on the calendar before buying anything. That means three dates from the school, all of which it publishes or will give you on request: the internal deadline for the Mathematical Exploration, the mock examination window, and the term calendar showing which weekdays carry school commitments. Those three govern the work. The written papers matter, obviously, but they are months away and the school-set dates arrive first.

It is also worth being blunt about the arithmetic of a term. Between term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan and the school's own mock windows and trips, a notional eight-week block in the UAE academic year routinely delivers six. A plan agreed in vague terms loses those two weeks silently and then disappoints at the end. Counting the genuinely available weeks on a calendar before anything is agreed takes five minutes and changes what should be promised, which is why it is the first thing we do rather than the last.

One thing this page will not do is state an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a date a family reorganises a year around should not rest on a secondary guess. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. Everything below is planned from the dates your school controls, which are in any case the ones that bind first.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: Where a student sits on the IB continuum determines what the next eight weeks can be used for, because the assessment model and the fixed dates differ at each stage rather than merely getting harder.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Mathematics is compulsory, taken as Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Higher or Standard Level, assessed through written papers plus an internally assessed Exploration. The Exploration's deadline is set by the school, not by the IB, and it is almost always the first hard date a Diploma Mathematics student meets.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Al Mankhool sits outward from the district, in Al Jaddaf, across the creek and toward Nad Al Sheba, so a student from here has usually changed campus for the Diploma. That means an unfamiliar topic sequence and unfamiliar internal deadlines, which is precisely why locating the student on the calendar comes before buying hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria on a 1-8 scale with no terminal papers in most schools, and split into Standard and Extended routes in the final years. The Extended route carries the algebraic depth that Analysis and Approaches Higher Level assumes later, so the route decision has a two-year shadow.
programmes.countryNote: For a Year 10 or Year 11 student here, an eight-week block has a different purpose entirely: it is pre-emptive. Closing an algebra gap now costs eight hours; discovering it in the October of Diploma year one costs a term, because the Diploma's own timetable leaves no room for remedial work in its first term.

programmes.name: The IGCSE route into Diploma Mathematics
programmes.description: The majority route in this part of Dubai. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher; Additional Mathematics 0606 is the optional course that introduces calculus before Year 12. Which of these a student took predicts most of their first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the single most useful eight-week window available to a family in this district, because it is the only block in the whole programme with no competing deadline. A student who closes the gap between 0580 Extended and Analysis and Approaches in those weeks starts the Diploma level rather than behind.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics, the local alternative
programmes.description: The other post-sixteen route from these schools, with Mathematics and Further Mathematics as separate qualifications and modular assessment points rather than one compulsory subject at two routes and two levels. The content maps more closely onto Analysis and Approaches than onto Applications and Interpretation.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to an eight-week conversation because some families who arrive asking for Diploma Mathematics help are really asking whether the Diploma is the right programme. If the mathematics is sound and the breadth is the problem, more mathematics hours make the week worse. That is a conversation with the school, and it has its own deadline.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Diploma Mathematics is taught as a sequence of topics across two years, and an eight-week block is always landing somewhere in that sequence. Below are the topics students in this district most often need help with, and what a short block can realistically do with each.

subjects.name: Algebra, sequences and functions
subjects.description: The foundation and the usual site of an undiagnosed gap. Eight weeks here early in year one is the highest-return block in the programme; eight weeks here in the final term means abandoning other revision to repair it, which is sometimes still the right call.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and the unit circle
subjects.levels: HL and SL, Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Identities, equations and radian measure. A short block works well because the content is bounded and the techniques are drillable, and insecurity here quietly limits later calculus questions involving trigonometric functions.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Arrives early in year one and everything after depends on it. A student who can differentiate but cannot tell from a worded question that differentiation is wanted has an interpretation problem rather than a technique one, and the two need different weeks.

subjects.name: Integration and its applications
subjects.description: Harder to repair in a short block because it assumes secure differentiation underneath it. Where an eight-week request arrives about integration, the first session usually establishes whether the real gap is one layer down.

subjects.name: Statistics, probability and distributions
subjects.description: Bounded, teachable and frequently neglected until late, which makes it one of the better late-block choices. Marks are lost on interpreting what a result means rather than on computing it, especially in Applications and Interpretation.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometry
subjects.description: Demands holding a geometric picture and an algebraic relationship together. Sessions benefit from drawing before calculating, every time, and students who skip the diagram lose marks they could not have lost otherwise.

subjects.name: Proof, complex numbers and series
subjects.description: Second-year content that separates a comfortable Higher Level student from a struggling one. Short blocks here are viable only if the algebra underneath is solid; otherwise the block becomes algebra work with a different name.

subjects.name: Modelling with functions
subjects.levels: HL and SL, Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The spine of the Applications route. Marks sit in choosing a model, justifying the choice and stating the limitations in writing, which is a communication skill. Students who compute well often say nothing about what the model cannot do.

subjects.name: Matrices, graph theory and networks
subjects.description: Self-contained topics that respond well to a focused block, which makes them a sensible target when time is short and other ground is already lost. Technology use is assumed and calculator technique has to be taught explicitly.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: The component with a school-set deadline, which makes it the thing that most often determines what an eight-week block is for. Personal engagement and reflection carry the marks students miss, and both depend on a topic chosen early enough to change.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.regionsTitle: Where the calendar differs around Al Mankhool
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mankhool.regionsIntro: Students from this district attend Diploma schools in several directions, and those schools do not share a term calendar, a mock window or an Exploration deadline. The notes below are about that variation rather than about distance.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: A mixed intake across British, Indian and IB provision, which means neighbouring families are working to different school calendars. Comparing deadlines with a friend down the corridor is a common source of a nasty surprise two weeks before one of them is due.

regions.name: Bur Dubai and Al Fahidi
regions.note: Long-established schools mostly running to sixteen, so Diploma students have moved campus. Their new school's internal deadlines are unfamiliar to the household, and the first term of year one is usually when that becomes apparent.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense and close, with a strong informal tuition market. The risk at short notice is buying whoever is available rather than whoever matches the route and level, and in the final term a mismatch cannot be recovered from.

regions.name: Al Satwa and Al Hamriya
regions.note: Students travelling in several directions for school, so a family here may have two children on two calendars. Planning an eight-week block for each separately is more effective than one household schedule that suits neither.

regions.name: Al Jafiliya and Za'abeel
regions.note: Working-parent households where sessions drift into the evening. For a late block on timed-paper practice that is a real cost, because accuracy under time is the first thing fatigue removes. A weekend morning slot is usually stronger in the final weeks.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The adjacent school belt, where several large schools run to sixteen. Families here and in Al Mankhool often share tutors, which works well where the route and level match and badly where only the subject does.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Dubai Healthcare City
regions.note: The nearest IB continuum option, so some students here have been on the same school's calendar since primary. Those families usually know the Exploration deadline well in advance, which is a genuine planning advantage.

sections.heading: Locate the student on the calendar first
paragraphs: Before anything is bought, establish where in the two-year course the student actually is and what the next fixed date is. That sounds obvious and it is routinely skipped, because the conversation families have is about the grade rather than about the calendar. A grade tells you there is a problem. The calendar tells you what can be done about it.

Diploma Mathematics has a reasonably predictable shape across two years. Year one establishes the algebraic and functional base and, in Analysis and Approaches, introduces differentiation; year two builds on that base and adds the harder material, with the Exploration landing somewhere in between according to the school's own scheduling. A student who is struggling in year two is almost always struggling with something that was supposed to have been secured in year one, which is why an audit at the end of year one is worth more than a term of help in year two.

In this district there is a specific reason families cannot read their own position confidently. Most Diploma students here moved campus at sixteen, so the household has no history with how that school sequences topics or how demanding its internal assessments are. A student can be behind their class and on top of the syllabus, or the reverse, and a report comment will not distinguish the two.

The table below gives the shape of the two years and what to do if a term's prerequisite is not secure. Take the actual dates from your school's term calendar; this is the structure, not your child's schedule.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can and cannot change, honestly
paragraphs: Eight weekly sessions is roughly eight hours of teaching. It is enough to make one bounded topic reliable, to install the method-writing habit, to fix an interpretation failure, or to rebuild paper timing. It is not enough to teach a year of calculus, and anybody who implies otherwise is selling comfort.

The most common late request in this district is a block six to eight weeks before the written papers for a student whose content coverage is patchy. The honest answer is that the eight hours should not attempt coverage. They should be spent on the highest-mark-density things the student can still change: finishing the paper, writing method so partial credit is earned, answering the question that was asked rather than the one that was recognised, and securing one or two bounded topics such as statistics or matrices where a short block genuinely delivers. That plan frequently moves a grade. A plan that tries to cover the syllabus in eight hours moves nothing.

A second common request is help three weeks before an Exploration deadline. Eight weeks of work is not available, so the block becomes process coaching on what the student has already produced: whether each criterion is addressed, whether the reflection does real work, whether the mathematics used is sufficient for the level. That is useful and it is bounded, and it is a smaller purchase than families expect.

The table sets out starting positions against what a block of around eight sessions can realistically deliver. It is worth reading before agreeing a plan, because the most valuable thing a tutor can tell you is which of these rows you are in.

sections.heading: The Exploration deadline, not the exam, is the live clock
paragraphs: Families plan around the written papers because that is what an examination feels like. For most Diploma Mathematics students the binding date arrives much earlier and is set much closer to home: the school's internal deadline for the Mathematical Exploration. It is not an IB date. Each school sets its own, and in this district, where students have often recently changed campus, parents frequently do not know it until a fortnight before.

Counting backwards from that deadline gives a plan that actually works. The writing comes before the deadline. The mathematics has to be done before the writing. The topic has to be chosen before the mathematics, and crucially it has to be chosen early enough that it can be abandoned if it turns out not to support the required level of work. A topic chosen late is a topic the student is stuck with, and being stuck with the wrong one caps the mark regardless of effort.

What the marks reward is worth being precise about, because students lose them in the same two places repeatedly. Personal engagement suffers when the topic is borrowed rather than owned, and it reads as borrowed to an experienced marker. Reflection suffers when the student describes what they did instead of evaluating what it showed and what its limits were. Neither of those is a mathematics problem, which is why a strong mathematician can submit a weak Exploration.

The boundary for any tutor is firm. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, test whether a topic can sustain the mathematics required at that level, model an approach on an entirely different example, read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold, and point out a section that fails to address its criterion. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and we do not supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.
bullets: Ask the school for the Exploration deadline at the start of the year, not the term it falls
Choose the topic early enough that it can still be abandoned
Personal engagement and reflection are where the marks are lost, not the mathematics
Reflection means evaluating what the work showed, not describing what was done
A tutor may question a draft; a tutor may not write any part of one
The school's supervisor holds the authority; a tutor's role sits inside it

sections.heading: Mock season: three weeks that reset the plan
paragraphs: Mocks are the only point before the real papers where a Diploma Mathematics student produces a marked script under genuine time pressure, and they are consistently underused. The grade is discussed at home, the script is filed, and sessions carry on in syllabus order. The most informative document of the two years has just been put in a drawer.

Use the three weeks properly. The week before should contain one full paper under time and no new content, so that the mock is not the first encounter with the clock. The week of the mock should contain almost nothing, because a tired student mocks badly and a mock's value lies in being a fair reading of where they are. The fortnight afterwards is where the work is.

The audit is mechanical. Take the marked script and assign every lost mark to one of four causes: the content was not known, the method was not shown, the question was misread, or the time ran out. Then count them. In most scripts from this cohort the content category is not the largest, which is uncomfortable because it is the category families have been paying to address. The other three are faster to fix and the repairs are specific rather than general.

Then rebuild the eight weeks from the count rather than from the syllabus. If method marks are the biggest loss, the next sessions are about writing, not about topics. If the clock is the biggest loss, the next sessions are timed papers with a pacing rule. This is the single highest-leverage use of a marked script, and it costs one session to do.

sections.heading: Revising in syllabus order is why late plans fail
paragraphs: When time is short, students revise in the order the syllabus lists topics. It feels organised and it is close to the worst available strategy, because the syllabus order has nothing to do with where this particular student's marks are available. A student with secure algebra and weak statistics who revises from the beginning spends the first three weeks on material they already know.

The alternative is mark-density triage, and it requires the marked script. Rank the remaining weeks by where the recoverable marks are: topics the student nearly knows and could make reliable, question types where partial credit is being forfeited, and the paper-level habits that cost marks across every topic. Work down that list. Topics the student has no grasp of at all, with a short time remaining, are often best left - which is a hard thing to say to a family and usually the right call.

There is a specific trap in Diploma Mathematics worth naming. The technology-free paper and the paper with technology fail differently, and students practise them together. Accuracy and speed in written arithmetic is its own skill, and a student who has done all their practice with a calculator to hand will know the mathematics and still lose marks under time. In a final-term block this deserves its own slot in the week.

Finally, protect the habit work. Writing out method, checking what the question actually asked, and a pacing rule for how long a question gets before moving on are worth marks in every topic simultaneously. In a short block they outperform any single topic, and students neglect them because they feel like admin rather than mathematics.

sections.heading: Route and level changes have a deadline too
paragraphs: Some of the families who arrive asking for eight weeks of mathematics help are actually in a different conversation: the student is on the wrong route or the wrong level, and no amount of tuition fixes a structural mismatch. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is a demanding course with front-loaded calculus, and a student who was placed in it on the strength of an IGCSE grade rather than on demonstrated algebraic fluency can be working hard and still falling behind.

Whether a change is possible, and when, is set entirely by the school. Some allow a move between routes or down a level in the first term of year one and not afterwards; some have an earlier cut-off. The date is rarely advertised and is almost always earlier than a struggling family would like. Asking about it is free, carries no obligation, and is better done in October than in March.

What a short diagnostic block does well here is produce evidence for that conversation. Two or three sessions with a specialist, working through questions at the current level, will establish whether the student is behind on a fixable gap or genuinely mismatched to the course. That evidence is more useful in a meeting with the school than a parent's impression, and it is a small purchase.

If a change is not available, the plan shifts to damage limitation and it should be honest about that. A mismatched Higher Level student can still improve a grade substantially through method marks, question interpretation and paper timing, without ever becoming comfortable with the hardest content. That is a legitimate goal and it should be stated as the goal rather than dressed up as something else.
