sections.heading: The UAE year: Ramadan, holidays and where the weeks actually are
paragraphs: An eight-week plan assumes eight weeks exist, and in the UAE academic year they frequently do not. Term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan and family travel all remove sessions, and a plan agreed in general terms loses two or three of its eight before anyone notices. Counting the actual available weeks on a calendar at the start is a five-minute job that changes what should be promised.

Ramadan needs deciding in advance rather than improvising. School hours shorten, the shape of the day changes and productive working energy moves to after Iftar. A session slot that works in a normal term will not survive unchanged, and the families who keep continuity are the ones who agree beforehand that the hour moves to a post-Iftar time for that period and returns afterwards. The ones who do not agree it typically lose the month and the momentum with it.

The school's own calendar removes more weeks than parents expect. Mock windows, internal assessment deadlines across six subjects, Creativity Activity Service commitments, Extended Essay supervision meetings and school trips all land on specific dates. Asking for the term calendar at the start of term and marking the genuinely free weeks turns a notional eight-week plan into a real one, which may be six weeks and should then be scoped as six.

Where a final-term block needs more volume than one session a week, the sensible place to find it is a protected weekend morning rather than a second weekday evening. Timed-paper practice in particular needs a rested student and an uninterrupted two hours, and neither is available at eight o'clock on a school night after a full day and three hours of homework.

sections.heading: What late costs, and what the market charges
paragraphs: Lateness is expensive twice over in this market. The first cost is the obvious one: fewer weeks, so less can change. The second is that rates across Dubai tend to firm up as a series approaches, and availability of genuine specialists narrows at exactly the point when the most families are looking. A block booked in the first term of year one is bought in a buyer's market; the same block booked eight weeks before the papers is not.

The published bands, for context, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. None of those is an IB Gram price.

The planning figure most families find more useful is the monthly one, because a block is a monthly commitment rather than an hourly purchase. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, near AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support - and the exam-year band is the relevant one for a final-term block.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video. In a final-term block the format matters practically as well as financially, because session volume has to rise and a slot that can move inside the week is worth more than one tied to somebody's driving route.

sections.heading: Regulators, the permit and the mandatory block
paragraphs: Two things a parent can verify before paying anyone, both quick. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no part of any quoted rate is a permit fee. Operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The second is the school's inspection report. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Elsewhere, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates there, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Finally, the block that competes with mathematics for timetable space. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited.

process.title: Send three dates and the route
process.description: The school's Exploration internal deadline, the mock window, and the term calendar, plus the Mathematics route and level from the option form. Those four facts determine what a block can be, and all four are available from the school for the asking.

process.title: Count the weeks that actually exist
process.description: Term breaks, holidays, Ramadan and travel remove sessions from every notional eight-week plan. We count the genuinely available weeks on a calendar before agreeing anything, so a six-week block is scoped as six rather than promised as eight.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a marked script
process.description: A full session at no charge with a specialist on the right route and level, built around the most recent marked paper. The script shows whether marks are going to content, method, misreading or the clock, which is four different plans for the same eight weeks.

process.title: Agree what the block will not do
process.description: Stated plainly before it starts. Eight hours can make a bounded topic reliable, install method writing, or rebuild paper timing. It cannot teach a year of calculus or change an Exploration topic three weeks from the deadline, and saying so is part of the service.

process.title: Re-audit at the halfway point
process.description: Four sessions in, a second timed paper and a second audit. If the four-way split has not shifted, the plan changes or the tutor does. A block that is not working is better stopped at week four than discovered at week eight.

whyPoints.title: Scoped to the term, not to a programme
whyPoints.description: The same eight hours do different work in the first term of year one, three weeks from an Exploration deadline, and six weeks from the papers. We establish which of those you are in before quoting a plan, because it changes the plan completely.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the ceiling
whyPoints.description: Eight hours can fix finishing the paper, earn partial credit through written method, or make one bounded topic reliable. It cannot teach a year of untaught content. We say which row you are in rather than selling the comfortable version.

whyPoints.title: The school's dates drive the plan
whyPoints.description: The Exploration deadline, the mock window and the route-change cut-off are all set by the school and all arrive before the written papers. We build from those, and we do not publish IB dates we have not been able to verify at source.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts audited, not filed
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock, then counted. In most scripts content is not the largest category, which redirects the remaining weeks away from where families assumed they should go.

whyPoints.title: Triage instead of syllabus order
whyPoints.description: With weeks remaining, revising from the start of the syllabus wastes the first third of them. We rank by recoverable marks, protect the habits that pay across every topic, and sometimes recommend abandoning a topic outright.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims limited
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band here belongs to the provider that published it with the month it was read. No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no board documents supplied, and no statistic without a source.

faqs.question: My child's exams are weeks away. Is it worth starting IB maths tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the hours are spent on the right things. Eight sessions cannot teach a year of calculus, and a plan that attempts syllabus coverage in that time achieves nothing. What it can do is convert a student who knows the mathematics into one who finishes the paper: pacing rules, written method so partial credit is earned, answering the question that was asked, and securing one or two bounded topics such as statistics or matrices. That combination frequently moves a grade. The first session should tell you honestly which outcome is available.

faqs.question: How do we work out where our child actually stands in the course?
faqs.answer: From three documents the school will provide on request: the internal deadline for the Mathematical Exploration, the mock examination window, and the term calendar. Those govern the work and they all arrive before the written papers. Then add one marked script. In this district most Diploma students changed campus at sixteen, so the household has no history with how that school sequences topics or marks its mocks, and a report comment cannot distinguish a student who is behind their class from one who is behind the syllabus.

faqs.question: Which date should we be planning the term around?
faqs.answer: Almost always the school's internal Exploration deadline rather than the written papers. It is set by your child's school, not by the IB, it varies widely between schools in this area, and parents here routinely discover it a fortnight before it falls. Counting backwards from it gives a workable plan: writing before the deadline, mathematics before the writing, topic choice before the mathematics, and the topic chosen early enough that it can still be abandoned if it will not support the level required.

faqs.question: What should we do with the marked mock script?
faqs.answer: Audit it before anything else. Assign every lost mark to one of four causes - content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out - and count them. In most scripts the content category is not the largest, which is awkward because it is the one tuition is usually bought to address. Then rebuild the remaining weeks from the count rather than from the syllabus order. The week before a mock should hold one timed paper and no new content; the week of it should hold almost nothing.

faqs.question: Is revising from the start of the syllabus a sensible plan when time is short?
faqs.answer: It is close to the worst available plan, because the syllabus order has no relationship to where this student's marks are recoverable. A student with secure algebra and weak statistics who starts at the beginning spends three weeks on known material. Rank instead by recoverable marks: topics nearly known, question types where partial credit is being forfeited, and paper-level habits that pay across every topic at once. With weeks remaining, deliberately leaving a topic untouched is sometimes the correct decision.

faqs.question: Should the non-calculator paper be practised separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a final-term block it deserves its own slot in the week. Accuracy and speed in written arithmetic is a distinct skill, and a student who has done all their practice with technology to hand will know the mathematics and still lose marks under time. Twenty minutes a week of timed written work changes more than another hour of topic teaching. No student does this unsupervised because it is uncomfortable and shows no progress until it suddenly does, so it has to be built into the session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor still help if the Exploration is due in three weeks?
faqs.answer: Within limits that should be stated upfront. There is no time to change topic or collect new data, so the block becomes process coaching on what already exists: whether each criterion is addressed, whether the reflection evaluates rather than describes, whether the mathematics used is sufficient for the level. That is genuinely useful and it is a smaller purchase than families expect. What a tutor cannot do is write, draft or rewrite any part of it - IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and the malpractice finding would land on your child.

faqs.question: Where do students lose Exploration marks if their maths is strong?
faqs.answer: On personal engagement and reflection, almost every time. Personal engagement suffers when the topic was borrowed rather than owned, and it reads as borrowed to an experienced marker. Reflection suffers when the student recounts what they did instead of evaluating what it showed and where its limits were. Neither is a mathematics problem, which is why a capable mathematician can submit a weak Exploration. Both are fixed by choosing a topic the student actually cares about, early enough that it can still be changed.

faqs.question: Could my child be on the wrong maths route or level entirely?
faqs.answer: It happens, usually when a placement was made on an overall IGCSE grade rather than on demonstrated algebraic fluency. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is front-loaded with calculus, so a mismatched student works hard and falls behind anyway. Whether a change is possible is set by the school, often only in the first term of year one, and the date is rarely advertised. Two or three diagnostic sessions produce evidence for that conversation, which is more useful in a meeting than a parent's impression and is a small purchase.

faqs.question: How many weeks does an eight-week plan actually have in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Usually fewer than eight. Term breaks, public holidays, Ramadan, family travel and the school's own mock windows, internal deadlines and trips all remove sessions, and a plan agreed in general terms loses two or three before anyone notices. Counting the genuinely available weeks on a calendar at the outset takes five minutes and changes what should be promised. If the answer is six weeks, the block should be scoped as six weeks rather than sold as eight and quietly delivered as six.

faqs.question: What happens to the sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They should move deliberately rather than lapse. School hours shorten, the day changes shape and productive energy moves to after Iftar, so a slot that works in a normal term will not survive unchanged. Agree before Ramadan begins that the hour shifts to a post-Iftar time for that period and returns afterwards. Families who settle this in advance keep continuity through a month that otherwise costs four sessions and the momentum with them. Online delivery makes the shift straightforward; a fixed arrival time is the hardest thing in the week to move.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start maths support early rather than in the final term?
faqs.answer: Cheaper and more effective, for two separate reasons. Eight hours early in year one go into algebraic fluency and method habit, and everything in the following eighteen months compounds on them. Eight hours in the final term can only work on what is still changeable. Separately, rates across this market tend to firm up as a series approaches and genuine specialists become scarcer at exactly the moment most families are looking. A block bought in the first term is bought in a buyer's market.

faqs.question: What does a final-term maths block cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 table, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, specialist IB provision at AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Budget provision runs AED 33 to 65 from Tutopiya and EdFlik. In-home including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist exam-year support is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. All read October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an Al Mankhool address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a final-term block that is a practical advantage rather than a compromise, because session volume has to rise and an hour that can move inside the week is worth more than one tied to a tutor's driving route - and the pool becomes every specialist on your child's route and level rather than the few willing to travel here.

faqs.question: How will we know within a few weeks whether the block is working?
faqs.answer: Because there is a measurement built into it. Four sessions in, the student sits a second timed paper and it is audited the same way as the first: every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock, then counted. If the split has not shifted, something is wrong with the plan or the match, and that is the point to change it rather than at week eight. A block that is not working is better stopped halfway than completed out of politeness.

intro.heading: Diploma maths is a four-term job, and each term has a different task
paragraphs: Most families buy IB maths tutoring as a single product: an hour a week, for as long as it seems necessary. That is not wrong, but it hides the thing that actually determines whether the money works, which is that Diploma mathematics runs on a four-term timeline and each of those terms has a different job. Buying DP2 work in DP1, or DP1 work in DP2, is the commonest way a reasonable spend produces no visible movement.

The first term of DP1 is for two decisions and one habit. The decisions are whether the student is on the right course, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at the right level, and whether the exploration topic is going to have enough mathematics in it. The habit is writing the method down before reaching for the calculator, which is where method marks live and which takes a term of weekly correction to become automatic.

The second and third terms are for content and for the exploration being actually written, by the student, on the school's internal timeline. The fourth term is for papers: Paper 1 technique without a calculator, Paper 2 discipline with one, and at Higher Level the Paper 3 format, which is where students who know the mathematics lose marks to an investigation structure they have never met.

There is one thing this page will not do, and it is worth stating because other pages do it. It will not publish an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be right. UAE Diploma schools sit the May session; for the actual dates, ask your school's IB coordinator or check ibo.org directly, and treat any third-party date, including a tutoring page's, as unverified.

The cost argument follows from the same timeline, and it is arithmetic rather than persuasion. A weekly hour held from the first term of DP1 buys seventy or more sessions and sits in the middle of the published monthly bands for most of its life. The same total outlay started in the spring of DP2 buys a third of that, at the top of the bands, at the one point where nothing structural can still be changed. Families are not usually shown that comparison, and it is the most useful number on this page.

Al Mizhar's own contribution to the timeline is the school run. These villa communities sit beyond Mirdif, and collecting bus routes from Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais can run the better part of an hour, which puts students home late and sets the earliest workable slot at around 5.30pm and often later. IB Gram teaches one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, so nobody is driving out here; home visits are a service offered only in India. That removes the half of the scheduling problem a family cannot control and leaves the half they can measure.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: Maths tutoring is bought by course and spent on topics, and the topics that matter change with the term. These are the areas Al Mizhar families ask about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and proof-heavy route expected by most engineering and physical science degrees. Standard Level is already demanding; Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and a substantially harder calculus load, plus a third paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and data, technology assumed throughout, with a heavier statistics weighting. Accepted widely for business, social science and design routes and by fewer engineering ones. The Higher Level course is demanding and the statistics is not a soft option.

subjects.name: Number, algebra and the DP1 fluency base
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponentials and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at AA Higher Level proof by induction and complex numbers. This is first-term work and the place where an incoming IGCSE or MYP gap shows itself before anything else does.

subjects.name: Functions and graphing
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational functions and sketching without a calculator. Marks go missing on domain and range and on reading a transformation in the wrong order, both of which are early-term work rather than revision work.

subjects.name: Geometry, trigonometry and radians
subjects.description: Radian measure, identities and equations, and at AA Higher Level three-dimensional vectors. Students arriving from IGCSE worked in degrees, and the switch to radians costs marks for a whole term unless it is drilled deliberately in the first one.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and regression, weighted far more heavily in Applications and Interpretation. The recurring loss is interpretation: the calculation is right and the sentence explaining it in context is missing, which is a habit built over months.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration and applications, reaching considerably further at AA Higher Level with integration techniques and differential equations. Mostly second and third-term content, and the part the non-calculator paper exposes most ruthlessly.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Independent written mathematics carrying twenty per cent of the grade, assessed on criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Topic choice is first-term work; writing is second and third-term work. A tutor coaches and writes none of it.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, no calculator
subjects.description: Exact values, surds, algebraic manipulation under time pressure, and showing method so partial credit survives a wrong answer. Fourth-term work and the single highest return per hour available anywhere in the subject.

subjects.name: Paper 2 discipline, with a calculator
subjects.description: The trap is using the calculator instead of thinking and losing method marks as a result. The fix is a rule practised until automatic: write the substitution or rearrangement down even when the answer is already on the screen.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: An extended scaffolded investigation sat only by Higher Level students. The mathematics is familiar and the format is not, so students who have never attempted one lose marks to the structure. Two or three past investigations in the fourth term solves it.

subjects.name: Bridging work either side of the course
subjects.description: Before DP1, closing the IGCSE or MYP gap in proof, radians and symbolic manipulation. After the final paper, reducing the first-year step into a mathematics-heavy degree. Both are defined summer blocks with a visible finish rather than ongoing arrangements.

sections.heading: The four terms, and the job each one has
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is usually described by content and is better understood by timeline. Four terms separate the start of DP1 from the final papers, and the work that pays is different in each. A family who knows which term they are in can judge a tutor's plan in about a minute.

The first term carries the decisions. Course and level can still be changed, the exploration topic is still open, and the method-writing habit can still be built from scratch rather than retrofitted. It is also the term in which an incoming gap from IGCSE or MYP shows itself, usually as an algebra problem wearing a Diploma costume.

The second and third terms carry the content and the exploration. Calculus arrives, statistics deepens, and the exploration has to be actually written by the student against the school's internal deadlines. This is the stretch where continuity matters most and where a travelling household most often loses a fortnight it cannot see the cost of until later.

The fourth term carries the papers and nothing else. New content at this stage is almost always the wrong purchase; the right one is timed past-paper work with the criteria open and the recurring errors named. The table sets out the whole shape, and the useful way to read it is to find your term and then check whether what you are being sold matches the row.

Running underneath all four terms is one thing that is never finished, which is interpretation. A correct calculation with no sentence saying what it means in the context the question set up loses marks in every term and in every one of the four courses, and it is the loss families notice last because the mathematics looks right. Ten minutes a lesson, every lesson, for two years is what fixes it. That is not a topic to be covered and ticked off; it is the one piece of work that belongs in every row of the table.

sections.heading: The exploration, dated backwards from the school's deadline
paragraphs: The exploration carries twenty per cent of the maths grade and is the component most often mistimed. The school sets its own internal deadlines, which is where a family should start, and the useful exercise is to write those dates down and work backwards from them rather than forwards from today.

Topic choice is the decisive step and it belongs in DP1 term one or two. A topic with too little mathematics in it has no route to the higher bands, whatever happens afterwards, and that is not something a tutor can repair in the final fortnight. The conversation a parent can usefully have costs nothing: ask your child what the mathematics in their topic actually is, and listen for whether the answer names techniques or only names an interest.

Writing belongs in terms two and three, in drafts, with the tutor responding to each one through questions. The criteria include presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, and each of those rewards something specific that a student can be shown in their own draft. Reflection in particular is marked and is routinely treated as decoration.

This is also where travel plans matter most for households in these communities. A fortnight lost in DP1 term one is absorbed; the same fortnight lost three weeks before the school's deadline is not. Plan the trips against the exploration dates rather than the other way round, and send the dates in advance so the tutoring slot moves rather than disappears.

sections.heading: Which paper to practise, and when
paragraphs: Paper practice is not one activity. Standard Level students sit two written papers and Higher Level students sit three, and each rewards a different thing, so practising them in the wrong order wastes the fourth term.

Paper 1 first, always. Sat without a calculator, it exposes fluency directly: exact values, surds, clean algebraic manipulation under time pressure, and method shown so partial credit survives a wrong answer. It responds faster to drilling than anything else in the subject, which makes it the right opening move in any paper block however short.

Paper 2 second, and the work there is a rule rather than a topic. With a calculator available, students stop writing method down, and method marks go with it. The fix is to practise writing the substitution or the rearrangement even when the answer is already on the screen, until it happens without thinking. That is behaviour, and behaviour needs weeks of correction rather than an explanation.

Paper 3 is Higher Level only and is the clearest case of a format problem rather than a content problem. It is an extended scaffolded investigation, and a student meeting that structure for the first time in the examination loses marks to the shape of it. Two or three past investigations, attempted properly and reviewed, removes most of that. Confirm current component structures and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning around them.

Two full timed papers belong in the last six weeks, and not more than two. The purpose of a full paper is not revision; it is data about pace and triage, which is why it has to be sat under something close to real conditions and then reviewed for where the time went rather than only for the mark. A student who discovers they spend eleven minutes on a six-mark question has learned something a hundred individual questions would not have told them, and two such papers is enough to learn it.

sections.heading: The May session, and why no date appears on this page
paragraphs: UAE Diploma schools sit the May session. That is the useful, stable thing to say, and it is as far as this page will go on dates, for a reason worth explaining.

The IB's own website returns an error to automated checking, which means no IB examination or results date in this project has been verified against the IB itself. Secondary sources exist and they converge, but converging secondary sources are not a source for a date a family acts on. A parent who books a flight or plans a revision block around a date taken from a tutoring page has been given something nobody checked.

So the instruction here is specific. Get your session dates from your school's IB coordinator, who holds the school's own examination timetable, or from ibo.org directly. Write them down, and then plan the fourth term backwards from the first paper rather than forwards from the mock. If any tutoring provider, including one quoting this page, gives you an IB date, ask where it came from.

For comparison, dates from the other boards are sourced and can be used with their own framing. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs its IGCSE and International A Level examinations in June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable. Those are useful for a sibling on a British-curriculum route, and they are not IB dates.

sections.heading: The course and level decision, and the window on it
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard: four courses, one decision, and a window that closes earlier than most families realise. It is the highest-leverage calendar item on this page because it is the only one that cannot be fixed later by working harder.

The two courses are not easy and hard versions of each other. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy and is commonly expected by engineering, physics and mathematics degrees. Applications and Interpretation is a modelling and data course with a heavier statistics load, accepted widely for business, social science and design routes and by fewer engineering ones. A student who picks on comfort in DP1 and discovers in DP2 that a target degree wants the other one has a problem no amount of tutoring solves cheaply.

Requirements vary by university and change between admission cycles, so the only reliable method is reading the specific entry page for each specific course. Do that in DP1 term one, with two or three target courses, and the decision becomes evidence-based rather than a guess. Then take marked papers to the school's coordinator if a change looks necessary, because the decision is the school's to make and evidence is what moves it.

A tutor's useful contribution here is diagnostic rather than advisory. Six weeks of marked work shows whether a struggling Higher Level student has a content gap that will close or a genuine mismatch with the level, and that distinction is worth more to the conversation than anybody's opinion about how hard the course is.

sections.heading: What the two years cost, term by term
paragraphs: Families think about an hourly rate and pay a two-year bill, so the honest way to present the money is across the timeline. Every figure below was read on the provider's own public page and is attributed; none is an IB Gram rate.

The published Dubai bands are these. EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya's panel starting lower. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, the premium inside it being a drive out past Mirdif through afternoon traffic.

Across the timeline the shape of the spend matters more than the band. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support. A weekly hour held from DP1 term one sits in the middle band for most of its life and rises only in the final term; an arrangement started in DP2 sits in the exam-year band for its whole life, and is shorter.

That is the actual argument for acting early, and it is arithmetic rather than persuasion. The same total outlay, spread from DP1 term one, buys more sessions at a lower monthly rate and buys them at the points on the timeline where they change something. Started in DP2 spring, it buys fewer sessions at a higher rate at the only point where nothing structural can still be changed.

sections.heading: Mocks, predicted grades and the conversation they trigger
paragraphs: The mock is the most consequential assessment of the two years, and not because it counts. It counts for nothing directly. It matters because it is the evidence a school uses when setting a predicted grade, and a predicted grade is what a university offer is made against.

That gives the mock a specific place on the timeline. Support in the weakest paper should already be running before it, not arranged after it. A family who starts looking for a tutor in the fortnight after mocks has arrived at the busiest point in the local market with the least time, which is the worst combination available.

If a predicted grade comes back below a university requirement, the useful response is evidence rather than argument. A predicted grade a band low usually reflects two or three repeating errors across past papers rather than a general gap, and one diagnostic session with a marked paper identifies them. From there, two sessions a week to the papers, spent almost entirely on timed work marked against published criteria, is the shape that moves marks. Then show the school the improved marked work, because predicted grades are theirs to revise on evidence.

Nobody can promise a grade, a band of improvement or a specific point total, and anybody who does is telling you about themselves. What is reliable is that repeating errors can be named and drilled out, and that a student who stops losing four marks a paper to invisible method is a different candidate by the final series.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the exploration, at every point in the year
paragraphs: The exploration is where the UAE tutoring market behaves worst, and the pressure peaks in the weeks before a school deadline, which is exactly why this belongs on a page about timing.

The boundary does not move. A tutor may explain the criteria, model method on a different example, teach technique on comparable problems, ask questions about the student's draft and point out where the mathematics does not support a claim. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of the exploration, including the reflection.

The test a parent can apply needs no mathematics. Ask to see the feedback. If it reads as sentences your child could paste into the document, the line has been crossed. If it reads as questions they have to go and answer, it has not. That test works in DP1 term one and it works three days before the deadline.

One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the student carries the finding through an appeal, a university application and sometimes a whole qualification, while the seller carries nothing. We also do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes; those belong to the IB and reach a student properly through the school.

Parents occasionally worry that holding this line disadvantages their child against classmates who are not holding it. It might, briefly, on one document, and the trade is still not close. A malpractice finding follows a student through an appeal, a university application and sometimes the whole qualification, and it is not something a fee refund repairs. Tell your child the line in DP1 term one, tell the tutor the line at the first lesson, and ask to see the feedback rather than only the finished draft. All three take minutes and none of them has to be repeated.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will say about the term you are in
paragraphs: Send four things: the course and level, which term the school is in, a photograph of a marked paper, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The second item is what makes the recommendation specific rather than generic.

The free trial lesson runs about forty minutes on a past question from your child's own course, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Afterwards you receive a written read on whether the difficulty is content, algebra or technique, and what the term you are in can realistically do about it. Nothing is owed if you stop there.

We will sometimes say that the term you are in does not support what you want. A family in DP2 spring asking for the exploration to be improved is asking for something that was decided in DP1, and saying so is more useful than taking the booking. A family in DP1 term one asking for intensive paper work is being offered the wrong thing too, and we would rather sell the weekly slot that actually matters.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: course, level, term, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the term
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, and which of the four terms the school is in. Those three together decide the shortlist and the shape of the work, and the term is the one families leave out.

process.title: Write down the school's own deadlines
process.description: The exploration deadline and the mock dates come from the school, and the examination dates come from the IB coordinator or ibo.org. Write them down once; every decision on this page is made by counting backwards from them.

process.title: Send a marked paper
process.description: A photograph of a marked test or mock shows a specialist the pattern in two minutes: method not shown, radians handled in degrees, interpretation sentences missing, or a genuine content gap in one topic.

process.title: Interrogate the exploration topic early
process.description: In DP1, ask your child what the mathematics in their topic actually is and listen for whether the answer names techniques. A topic too thin to reach the higher bands cannot be rescued by careful writing in the final fortnight.

process.title: Set a slot the commute can hold
process.description: Al Mizhar students on Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais routes arrive home late, so 5.30pm is the earliest realistic weekday slot and 6.30pm or a weekend morning is better for the longer routes.

process.title: Take the free trial, then review on the term's cycle
process.description: Forty minutes on a past question from the right course. Review at six lessons in a weekly DP1 arrangement and weekly in a fourth-term paper block, because the time available to correct a wrong approach differs completely.

whyPoints.title: The work is matched to the term
whyPoints.description: DP1 term one is for course choice, level and the exploration topic. The fourth term is for Paper 1 technique and timed papers. Selling the same hour all year round is how a reasonable spend produces no visible movement, and we will say which term supports what you are asking for.

whyPoints.title: No invented IB dates
whyPoints.description: UAE Diploma schools sit the May session, and that is as far as this page goes. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB date here has been verified at source. Get yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, and ask any provider quoting a date where it came from.

whyPoints.title: The exploration is timed, not rescued
whyPoints.description: Topic choice is DP1 work and sets the ceiling on twenty per cent of the grade. We interrogate the topic while it can still change, respond to drafts with questions, and write no part of any submission, including the reflection.

whyPoints.title: The cost argument is arithmetic
whyPoints.description: A weekly hour from DP1 term one sits in the mid-tier monthly band for most of its life and buys seventy or more sessions. The same outlay started in DP2 spring sits in the exam-year band and buys fewer, at the only point where nothing structural can still change.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is attributed
whyPoints.description: Each rate here was read on the provider's own public page and credited to them, and none is an IB Gram price. Three of the best-ranking pages on these searches publish no price at all, and a checkable number is worth more than a reassurance.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, ever
whyPoints.description: Nobody can promise a grade, a band of improvement or a point total. What is reliable is that repeating errors can be named and drilled out, which is a different and more honest claim, and it is the one our written notes are designed to let you check.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should we start maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: The first term of DP1, or the summer before it. That is the only window in which the decisions that matter are still open: whether the student is on the right course and level, whether the exploration topic has enough mathematics in it, and whether the habit of writing method down gets built from scratch rather than retrofitted. A weekly hour started then sits in the mid-tier monthly band for most of its life and buys seventy or more sessions. Started in DP2 spring, the same money buys fewer sessions at a higher rate.

faqs.question: What exactly should the first term of DP1 be spent on?
faqs.answer: Two decisions and one habit. The decisions are course and level, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Higher or Standard, checked against the published entry requirements for two or three target university courses rather than against how DP1 feels. And the exploration topic, interrogated for whether it contains real mathematical techniques. The habit is writing the substitution or rearrangement down before reaching for a calculator, because method marks live there and it takes a term of weekly correction to become automatic.

faqs.question: Which maths paper should be practised first in the final term?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, without exception. Sat without a calculator, it exposes fluency directly through exact values, surds and algebraic manipulation under time pressure, and it responds faster to drilling than anything else in the subject. Paper 2 comes second and the work there is a rule rather than a topic: write the method even when the answer is on the screen. At Higher Level, Paper 3 comes third and needs two or three past investigations so the extended format holds no surprises in the examination.

faqs.question: This page names the May session but gives no dates. Why not?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them at source. The IB's own website returns an error to automated checking, so no IB examination or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources converge, and converging secondary sources are not good enough for a date a family plans a revision block or a flight around. UAE Diploma schools sit the May session; get the specific dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org, and ask any provider quoting a date where theirs came from.

faqs.question: How late can we change from Applications and Interpretation to Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Realistically DP1 term one, and it gets difficult quickly after that. The two are not easy and hard versions of each other: AA is algebraic and proof-heavy and is commonly expected by engineering, physics and mathematics degrees, while AI is a modelling and data course with heavier statistics, accepted widely elsewhere. The decision belongs to the school, and what moves it is evidence rather than preference, so take marked papers to the coordinator. Check the published entry requirements for specific target courses first.

faqs.question: When does the exploration have to start?
faqs.answer: The criteria conversation in DP1 term one and the topic choice in term one or two, because the topic sets the ceiling on a component worth twenty per cent and careful writing afterwards cannot raise it. Writing happens in terms two and three against the school's own internal deadlines, in drafts, with a tutor responding through questions. The reflection is assessed rather than decorative and is routinely treated as paperwork. Ask your school for its internal dates and work backwards from them rather than forwards from today.

faqs.question: We are travelling for three weeks. When is the worst time for that?
faqs.answer: The three weeks before the school's exploration deadline, and the final six weeks before the papers. A fortnight lost in DP1 term one is absorbed because the content is still being taught and there is room to catch up; the same fortnight lost close to a deadline is not recoverable. Plan trips against the school's own dates rather than the other way round, and send us the dates in advance so the slot moves rather than vanishes. Online lessons follow a student to another time zone with the slot adjusted.

faqs.question: My child's predicted maths grade is below a university requirement. What is the sequence?
faqs.answer: Diagnose, drill, then show the school. A predicted grade a band low usually reflects two or three repeating errors across past papers rather than a general gap, and one session with a marked paper in front of a specialist identifies them. From there, two sessions a week to the final papers spent almost entirely on timed work marked against published criteria is the shape that moves marks. Then take the improved marked work back to the school, because predicted grades are theirs to revise on evidence rather than on request.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying maths tutoring in the summer before DP1?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and most under-used point on the entire timeline. Six to ten sessions, uninterrupted by homework or assessment weeks, aimed at exactly what the student is arriving with: proof, radians, function notation and the habit of justifying a method if they come from IGCSE Extended, or algebraic fluency if they come from standard MYP mathematics. Local availability is also at its widest in the summer, so the choice of tutor is real rather than whoever is still free after mocks.

faqs.question: What does a weekly maths arrangement cost across the two years?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates from Bestimate's Dubai table run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, per subject. A weekly hour held from DP1 term one sits in the middle band for most of its life and rises only in the final term. Hourly, the market runs from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik up to AED 650 at BartyED, with TutorChase at AED 270. None of those is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: Should we switch to two sessions a week, and when?
faqs.answer: In DP2, and only with a stated reason. The pattern that works is one weekly session held across both years, with a second added for a defined block when there is something specific to do: the exploration in DP1, Paper 3 format work before the final papers, or recovery after a predicted grade that blocks an offer. Two sessions a week sustained across the whole Diploma is a large commitment, and households that start there usually cut back by the second term, often at the worst possible moment.

faqs.question: Does Paper 3 really need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the clearest format problem in the subject. Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level students and is an extended scaffolded investigation, so the mathematics is familiar while the structure is not. A student meeting it for the first time in the examination loses marks to the shape of the paper rather than to the content, which is an avoidable and expensive way to lose them. Two or three past investigations attempted properly in the fourth term removes most of that. Confirm the current structure with your IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of the exploration if the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: No, and the date changes nothing. A tutor may explain the criteria, model method on a different example, teach technique on comparable problems, question your child's draft and point out where the mathematics does not support a claim. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of it, including the reflection. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which is an IB malpractice trigger, and the student carries it while the seller carries nothing.

faqs.question: What time can a maths lesson run from Al Mizhar in term time?
faqs.answer: 5.30pm at the earliest for a child at a Mirdif school, and 6.30pm or a weekend morning for one on an Al Warqa, Al Qusais or Al Khawaneej route. Those collecting routes can take the better part of an hour, and calculus attempted by a student who walked in twenty minutes ago produces noticeably less than the same hour after food and a break. Set the slot from the worst afternoon rather than the best, because across four terms a slot that fails monthly loses around thirty sessions.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first maths lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. The course and the level. Which of the four terms the school is in, which is what makes the recommendation specific. A photograph of a marked test or mock. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. We will sometimes tell you that the term you are in does not support what you are asking for, which is more useful than taking the booking. The privacy link explains what is held under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingHeading: Find your term, then buy for it
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mizhar.closingBody: Diploma mathematics runs over four terms and each one has a different job, so the first useful question is not which tutor but where on that timeline your child is standing. In DP1 term one you can still change the course, the level and the exploration topic, and build the method-writing habit from scratch. In the fourth term you can convert understanding into marks through Paper 1 fluency and Paper 2 discipline, and nothing structural is still open. Write down the school's deadlines and the session dates from your IB coordinator, send us the course, the level, the term and a marked paper, and take the free trial lesson.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach one IB mathematics course at one level: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. That distinction is the whole job, because the two courses examine different mathematics with different tools.

intro.heading: Two courses, not one subject with two difficulty settings
paragraphs: IB mathematics is two separate courses. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with a Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics, technology-permitted throughout. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, which gives four distinct courses with four syllabuses, four sets of past papers and four sets of expectations. A parent in Al Muteena asking for a maths tutor is asking about one of four things, and the first job is to establish which.

The difference is not a matter of difficulty ranking. Applications Higher Level contains statistical and modelling content that Analysis Standard Level never touches, and Analysis Higher Level contains proof, complex numbers and calculus that Applications students are never examined on. A student moved between courses mid-year arrives having been taught topics that are not on their paper and never taught topics that are. This happens more often than schools like to admit, usually because a Year 12 timetable constraint forced the move.

The second thing to establish is which paper is losing the marks, because the three papers reward different behaviours. Paper 1 in Analysis is sat without technology, so algebraic fluency is the gatekeeper and a student who relies on a calculator for routine manipulation is exposed. Paper 2 permits technology, which changes the question style towards interpretation and setting up rather than executing. Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper that asks a student to work through a developed investigation under time pressure, which is a skill in itself.

Third comes the exploration, the internally assessed piece every mathematics student writes. It is marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic that cannot support genuine mathematics, which caps two criteria regardless of how well the student writes. That decision is made early and is almost impossible to recover from later.

Fourth, and least discussed, is the calculator. Both courses specify permitted graphical display calculator models and the IB prohibits others. Students who have learned a different model's menus, which happens constantly when a family moves between countries, lose time in Paper 2 and in Applications generally. An hour of model-specific practice is one of the cheapest marks available in the subject and almost nobody does it.

Everything below is organised around those four questions: which course, which paper, which exploration topic, which calculator. A tutoring plan that answers them in the first session is worth more than one that starts by asking what topic the student finds hard, because the answer to that question is usually a symptom rather than a cause. A fifth question is worth adding for families in this district specifically, because Diploma mathematics cohorts here are small and often taught by one teacher across two courses at once: how much individual attention is realistically available in class? Where the answer is very little, the tutoring is not a supplement to teaching but the only place a student's own working gets looked at closely, and the session should be built accordingly.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: Mathematics sits differently in each programme a Dubai student might be on, and the route choice made at sixteen is the one that constrains everything afterwards.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes a mathematics course, which is unusual among post-16 systems and the reason mathematics generates more Diploma tutoring demand than any other subject. The choice is between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level, and it is made in Year 12 with consequences at university application.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, where International Baccalaureate students are roughly seven per cent of private-school enrolment, cohorts in each of the four mathematics courses are small. A school may run Analysis Higher Level with a handful of students, which is why a Standard Level student rarely gets to move up and a struggling Higher Level student rarely gets individual attention within the class.

programmes.name: MYP mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than papers, with Standard and Extended pathways in the later years. Criterion B, investigating patterns and justifying a general rule, is the strongest predictor of how a student will cope with Analysis and Approaches, because it rewards the same instinct towards proof.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that run MYP then Diploma make the mathematics transition internally, which usually works. Students arriving into Diploma mathematics from IGCSE instead, which is the common route near Al Muteena, meet algebraic demands at a different pace and need the first term handled carefully.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics as the entry point
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher is the realistic prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches. The Core or Foundation tier omits content the Diploma assumes, and a student entering Analysis Higher Level from a Core background has a gap that shows within weeks rather than months.
programmes.countryNote: Most schools near Al Muteena run IGCSE rather than MYP, so this is the relevant feeder in this district. Families should check the tier as well as the grade: a grade B from Extended and a grade C ceiling from Core are different starting points for Diploma mathematics even where the certificate looks similar.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics as the alternative
programmes.description: The other post-16 mathematics route in Dubai, narrower and deeper, with Further Mathematics available for students aiming at mathematics or engineering degrees. No compulsory mathematics for students who do not choose it, which is the structural difference from the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student needs one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better. No published IB points threshold could be sourced, so none is stated here.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: These are the mathematics topics that generate the most tutoring requests from Dubai Diploma students, described by where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Algebra and proof, Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Sequences, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. Proof is where Higher Level students most often freeze, because it asks for a structured argument rather than a calculation, and the structure itself carries marks.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, graph transformations, rational functions at Higher Level. Marks are lost on domain and range statements that students treat as decoration, and on sketches missing asymptotes or intercepts the mark scheme expects to see labelled.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: HL and SL, both courses, deeper in AA
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration techniques, with Analysis Higher Level extending to implicit differentiation, integration by parts and differential equations. The commonest loss is an unstated substitution or a missing constant of integration in a question where every later mark depends on it.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: HL and SL, dominant in AI
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and regression, with Applications treating these as the core of the course. Students lose marks by giving a conclusion without referring to the significance level or the context, which the scheme requires explicitly.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations, vectors at Higher Level in Analysis, and three-dimensional geometry in Applications. Radians versus degrees is a recurring avoidable loss, usually because the calculator was left in the wrong mode.

subjects.name: Number and algebra, Applications
subjects.description: Financial mathematics, approximation and error, and at Higher Level matrices and complex numbers in applied contexts. Percentage error and rounding questions look trivial and are marked precisely, which catches confident students.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual written investigation marked against five criteria. Topic choice determines the ceiling: a topic with no mathematics beyond arithmetic cannot earn the use-of-mathematics marks however well it is presented, and no amount of later work rescues that.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3
subjects.description: An extended problem-solving paper built as a developed investigation with scaffolded parts. It rewards students who have practised sustained unfamiliar problems under time pressure, and penalises those who have only drilled routine question types.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.levels: All courses where technology is permitted
subjects.description: Solving equations numerically, finding intersections, running regressions and statistical tests on the permitted model. Students who learned a different model's menus lose minutes per question, and minutes are marks on a paper where technology is expected to be fast.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: how to decide properly
paragraphs: The choice is made in Year 12 and it constrains university options two years later, which is why it deserves more than a conversation about which one the student prefers. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic, proof-oriented and sits closer to a traditional mathematics course. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with technology throughout, and is a genuinely rigorous course rather than an easier one, aimed at different destinations.

The deciding input should be the university prerequisite, and that means reading actual entry requirements rather than assuming. Several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a student who chose Applications for comfort can find a course closed in Year 13 when there is no way back. Equally, a student heading for design, social sciences, business or medicine may be better served by Applications, where the statistical content is more useful and the grade more attainable.

The second input is the student's existing instinct. A student who enjoyed proving a result in MYP Criterion B, or who liked algebraic manipulation at IGCSE Extended, usually takes to Analysis. A student who liked data handling, modelling and context, and who found abstract algebra arbitrary, usually does better in Applications and often scores higher. Scoring higher matters: a 6 in the right course is worth more than a 4 in the prestigious one.

The third input is honest capacity. Analysis Higher Level alongside two other demanding Higher Level subjects and an Extended Essay is a heavy load, and it is a load a student carries for two years. Raising that in month two of Year 12, while a change is still administratively possible, is far more useful than noticing it after the first mock series when the school's timetable has hardened.

sections.heading: Three papers, three different skills
paragraphs: Students revise mathematics as one activity and then sit papers that reward three different things. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is taken without a calculator. That single rule reshapes the preparation: exact values, surds, algebraic manipulation and differentiation by hand all have to be fluent, and a student who has leaned on technology for routine work discovers it in the hall rather than in revision.

Paper 2 permits technology, which changes the questions rather than making them easier. With a calculator available, the paper stops testing execution and starts testing setup and interpretation: can the student turn a described situation into an equation, use the tool efficiently, and then say what the answer means in context. Students who solve everything by hand out of habit run out of time, and students who press buttons without setting up correctly get precise wrong answers.

Higher Level Paper 3 is different again. It is an extended problem-solving paper, built as a developed investigation with parts that lead into one another, and it cannot be prepared by drilling standard question types. What prepares a student is working long unfamiliar problems to time, learning how to make progress on an opening part they do not recognise, and learning to bank partial credit rather than stall. Most students practise this least and it carries meaningful marks.

A plan that treats these separately looks different from week to week. A non-calculator session is pencil and paper with the calculator physically away from the desk. A Paper 2 session works on reading a context and choosing a method. A Paper 3 session needs a long uninterrupted block, which for an Al Muteena student bussed back from Oud Metha usually means a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening.

sections.heading: Where maths marks are lost even when the mathematics is right
paragraphs: The most expensive habit in IB mathematics is doing work mentally and writing only an answer. Mark schemes award credit for the method and the substitution separately from the final value, so a student with sound mathematics and one transcription slip loses everything on a question where a student who showed their working would have kept most of it. The fix is mechanical: state the relationship, substitute, evaluate, and write the units or the context where the question asks for them.

Second is notation treated as decoration. Domain and range statements, the constant of integration, the limits on a definite integral, labelled axes and asymptotes on a sketch: each of these carries marks explicitly, and students who regard them as tidiness lose a steady trickle across every paper. A single session spent marking a student's own past paper against the published expectations usually makes this visible in a way no amount of being told does.

Third is the calculator, in both directions. Left in degrees for a radians question, or in radians for a degrees one, is a classic and costly error. So is using the tool to solve something the paper wanted solved algebraically, in Analysis Paper 2 where a method mark depends on the manipulation. And in Applications, failing to use the tool for a regression or a test the paper expects to be done with technology wastes minutes that are not available.

Fourth is context. In statistics questions the scheme frequently requires a conclusion stated in the context of the problem, referring to the significance level. A student who writes reject the null hypothesis and stops has given a mathematically correct answer that does not earn the final mark. These four together account for most of the gap between what a competent student knows and what their paper mark says.

sections.heading: The exploration: five criteria, and the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics student writes an exploration, an individual investigation assessed against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. It is internally marked and externally moderated, and it contributes a published share of the subject grade. Because it is written over months with feedback permitted within limits, it is the most controllable part of a mathematics grade, and it is routinely the least controlled.

The ceiling is set by the topic. A topic that cannot generate mathematics beyond arithmetic cannot earn the use-of-mathematics marks, and no quality of writing recovers that. A topic that is far too ambitious produces a student describing mathematics they do not understand, which the criteria punish differently but just as firmly. The sweet spot is a question the student can genuinely do the mathematics for, at a level consistent with their course, with something to explore rather than merely report.

Reflection is the criterion most often thrown away. The descriptors want the student to consider the limitations of their approach, the validity of their assumptions and what they would do differently, in substance rather than as a closing paragraph of apology. A student who writes about why a model broke down where it did is writing exactly what the criterion asks for, and most students never realise that is what is wanted.

The honesty boundary here is absolute. A tutor can teach the mathematics involved, question whether the topic can support the work, read each criterion with the student, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, cannot do the mathematics for it, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply a model exploration. Operations selling finished Internal Assessments exist in the Gulf market, and the consequences of using one fall on the student as a malpractice matter, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Coming into Diploma mathematics from IGCSE in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Most schools near Al Muteena run IGCSE rather than MYP, so the typical local Diploma mathematics student arrives from Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 rather than from MYP criteria work. That route has a specific profile: good examination technique, comfort with routine question types, and less practice at sustained independent work or at writing about mathematics, which the exploration demands.

The tier the student came through matters more than the grade. Extended or Higher tier IGCSE covers algebraic content that Analysis and Approaches assumes from the first week. A student arriving from Core or Foundation has not merely been assessed more gently, they have not been taught several topics, and in Analysis Higher Level that gap surfaces within the first month. Where the gap exists, the right response is a short intensive block on the missing algebra rather than general Diploma support.

The second common issue is pace. IGCSE mathematics is taught over two years with substantial repetition; Diploma mathematics covers more ground faster and does not revisit. A student who coped by catching up after each topic finds that strategy stops working, and the first mock is where it becomes visible. Starting support in term one of Year 12 rather than after that mock is the difference between a short intervention and a long one.

Students arriving from MYP have the mirror-image profile: comfortable with investigation and process, unpractised at writing complete solutions to a clock. For them the exploration is often straightforward and Paper 1 is the problem. Naming which of the two profiles a student has in the first session shapes the next eight weeks accurately, and it is a question that takes two minutes to answer.

sections.heading: What IB mathematics tutoring costs in Dubai, and what the specialist band buys
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai divide into bands worth understanding before shortlisting. Specialist work is where mathematics mostly sits: Bestimate's rate study puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, TutorChase lists around AED 270, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. Below that, qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. In-home visits are published at AED 180 to 500 with travel included.

What the specialist band buys in mathematics specifically is course-level precision. A capable graduate can teach calculus. Fewer can tell a student which parts of the calculus they have been shown are not examinable in Applications Standard Level, or that a particular manipulation must be shown by hand in Analysis Paper 2 even though the calculator could produce the answer. That knowledge comes from teaching one course repeatedly, and it is the thing worth paying for.

The monthly view governs the household decision. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For a mathematics-only arrangement the sensible shape is usually one weekly specialist session for the whole of Year 13, with a short exploration coaching block in Year 12 and a Paper 3 block before the session for Higher Level students. That is a predictable monthly line rather than a crisis purchase, and it costs less overall than three months of intensive work after a bad mock.

sections.heading: Online delivery for a subject that lives on paper
paragraphs: Mathematics tutoring raises a fair objection to video lessons: the work is handwritten, so how does a tutor see it. The answer in practice is a shared screen with a writing surface, a document camera or simply a phone propped over a page, and the student writing while the tutor watches the working appear line by line. That is closer to what a tutor needs than looking at a finished answer, because the error is usually in the third line rather than the last.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Muteena or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work and AED 200 to 450 for specialists.

For Diploma mathematics the selection argument is strong because the cohorts are small. There may be no tutor in the Deira grid who teaches Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, a course with a small national cohort, whereas online there are several teaching it weekly. For a student whose problem is specifically that course's statistical content, that is the difference between help and sympathy.

The format also fits the paper discipline. A non-calculator Paper 1 session works better when the tutor can see the calculator is genuinely off the desk and the student is working by hand. A Paper 3 block needs a long uninterrupted slot, which is easier to schedule when nobody is driving. And a session can shift to a weekend morning for a full timed paper without writing off a journey, which for a student bussed home late from Oud Metha is the only way a full paper gets sat properly at all.
