sections.heading: The year planned around internal deadlines, not the examination
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is structured by school deadlines rather than by the examination window. The exploration has a school submission date and usually a draft date before it, mocks sit in the winter of Year 13, and the paper phase occupies the final term. A family that knows those dates can plan; a family that does not spends two years reacting to whatever is due next week.

We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be correct. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; confirm the window and results dates with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any third-party calendar as a prompt to check.

Where dates can be stated with confidence is for Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sat alongside. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, with the February/March series offered to India only. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Ramadan sits inside the Diploma's heaviest stretch and should be planned rather than absorbed. Sessions in this district commonly move to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month, which online delivery makes a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. A Higher Level student with a Paper 3 block and an exploration deadline in the same term should map the Ramadan weeks explicitly, because the exploration is always the thing that slips.

process.description: Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, and which of the three papers the marks are being lost on. Those three facts shape the entire plan, and a tutor who starts without them will teach mathematics the student may not be examined on.

process.description: If the exploration is still open, the first coaching goes there, because topic choice sets the ceiling on two criteria and nothing later recovers it. A viable topic plus the five criteria read properly is worth more than months of polishing a weak one.

process.title: Separate the paper types in the weekly plan
process.description: Non-calculator work is done with the calculator off the desk; Paper 2 work is context-to-equation and tool efficiency; Paper 3 work needs a long block at a weekend. Treating them as one activity is why practice can rise while marks stay flat.

process.title: Measure on raw paper marks
process.description: Progress is checked on marks from papers sat to time, not on how the student feels about a topic. Every few weeks the plan is reweighted towards whichever paper is furthest from target, and untaught syllabus content is listed as a named risk.

whyPoints.title: Four courses treated as four courses
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Applications at Higher and Standard are four syllabuses with four sets of papers. A tutor who knows which one a student sits can say what is not examinable, which saves more hours than any revision technique.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 practised without a calculator
whyPoints.description: Analysis Paper 1 is non-calculator, so the preparation is too. It is the simplest honesty in mathematics tutoring and the one most often skipped, because working by hand is slower and less satisfying than getting answers.

whyPoints.title: Method marks made visible
whyPoints.description: Mark schemes credit the relationship and the substitution separately from the answer. Marking a student's own working line by line shows them where credit stopped, which is a different lesson from being told to show more working.

whyPoints.description: Topic viability and the five criteria, read in full, before any drafting. We give feedback on the student's own drafts and do not write, calculate for, or complete any part of the work.

faqs.question: My son is in IB Analysis and Approaches and sinking. Should he move to Applications?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the question to answer first is what he intends to study. Several engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, sometimes at Higher Level, so a move can close doors. If his destinations accept Applications, a 6 there is worth more than a 4 in Analysis, and Applications is a rigorous course rather than a soft option. Raise it in term one of Year 12 while the school timetable can still absorb a change. Collect two marked papers first so the conversation rests on evidence rather than on how hard it feels.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: They are two separate courses. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator and Higher Level including proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with technology permitted throughout, and treats statistical inference as core rather than secondary. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct syllabuses. A student moved between them mid-course has been taught content not on their paper and missed content that is.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks in IB maths when her answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Usually because the working is not on the page. Mark schemes credit the relationship and the substitution separately from the final value, so sound mathematics plus one transcription slip loses marks a student with visible working would have kept. Notation is the second cause: domain and range statements, the constant of integration, limits on a definite integral, labelled axes and asymptotes all carry marks explicitly. Marking her own past paper against published expectations, line by line, makes both visible faster than being told to show more working ever does.

faqs.question: How should a Higher Level student prepare for Paper 3?
faqs.answer: Differently from Papers 1 and 2. Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper built as a developed investigation with parts that lead into one another, so drilling routine question types does not prepare for it. What does is working long unfamiliar problems to time, developing a method for making progress on an opening part the student does not recognise, and learning to bank partial credit instead of stalling on one step. It needs a long uninterrupted block, which usually means a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Does the calculator model my child uses actually matter?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most families expect. The IB specifies permitted graphical display calculator models and prohibits others, and a student who learned a different model's menus loses minutes per question on the papers where technology is permitted. Minutes are marks on a paper designed around fast tool use. An hour of model-specific practice, finding intersections, solving numerically, running a regression or a test, is among the cheapest mark gains available in the subject, and almost nobody schedules it deliberately.

faqs.question: How do we choose an exploration topic that can actually score well?
faqs.answer: Test it against the use-of-mathematics criterion before anything else. A topic that cannot generate mathematics beyond arithmetic cannot earn those marks however well it is written, and a topic far beyond the student's course produces a report describing mathematics they do not understand. The workable zone is a question the student can genuinely do the mathematics for, at a level matching their course, with something to explore rather than report. Decide this early; it sets a ceiling that later effort cannot lift.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on an exploration draft, and what must they refuse?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can teach the mathematics involved, question whether the topic can support the work, read each of the five criteria with the student, and give feedback on drafts the student has written themselves. A tutor cannot write it, cannot do the mathematics for it, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply a model exploration. Operations selling finished Internal Assessments exist in this market, and the malpractice consequence lands on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: My child came from IGCSE Core maths into the Diploma. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches, yes, and it surfaces quickly. Core or Foundation tier omits algebraic content the Diploma assumes from the first week, so the student has not merely been assessed more gently, they have not been taught several topics. The right response is a short intensive block on the missing algebra rather than general Diploma support, and it works far better in term one of Year 12 than after the first mock. For Applications the gap is smaller but the statistical demand is still new.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Diploma student in Al Muteena usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session sustained across Year 13 beats three a week for a month after a bad mock, and costs less overall. The shape that works for most is a single specialist session each week on the paper furthest from target, a short exploration coaching block in Year 12 at the decision points, and a Paper 3 block before the session for Higher Level students. More than that is rarely sustainable alongside two other Higher Level subjects, the Extended Essay and the mandatory UAE subjects Dubai schools deliver.

faqs.question: What does specialist IB maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put specialist work at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above in Bestimate's rate study, with TutorChase listing around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for premium named tutors. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. Qualified tutors working online are AED 150 to 300, and at the budget end EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. These are the providers' own figures.

faqs.question: How does a maths tutor see handwritten working over video?
faqs.answer: Through a shared writing surface, a document camera, or a phone propped over the page while the student writes. That is actually better than reviewing a finished answer, because the error in a mathematics solution is usually in the third line rather than the last, and a tutor watching the working appear can intervene at the line where it went wrong. It also makes a non-calculator Paper 1 session honest, because the tutor can see the calculator is genuinely off the desk.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a maths tutor to our flat in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma mathematics the online pool matters more than usual because the cohorts are small: there may be nobody in the Deira grid teaching Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, while several tutors teach it weekly online. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: When do Dubai Diploma students sit their maths papers?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Confirm the window and results dates with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge qualifications sat alongside, UAE centres sit the June and November series, and Cambridge warns that the correct administrative zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: Does my child need a maths tutor if the school already runs extra classes?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and it is worth checking before paying. School support sessions cover the syllabus for a group and are genuinely useful for content gaps. What they cannot usually do is work on one student's specific pattern of mark loss across three different papers, because the session is paced for the room. Look at a marked paper: evenly spread losses suggest the school sessions are the right answer, while a clear pattern, unwritten method, calculator mode, uncontextualised statistical conclusions, needs individual attention.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan and exam term fit together for a Diploma maths student?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, or badly. Ramadan falls inside the Diploma's heaviest stretch, and in this district sessions commonly move to after Iftar or to weekend mornings for the month, which online delivery makes a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. The thing that slips is always the exploration, because it has no weekly external pressure. A Higher Level student with a Paper 3 block and an exploration deadline in the same term should map those weeks explicitly before the month begins rather than hoping to absorb them.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free who teaches our exact maths course?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level in particular has a small cohort, so a specific course at a specific hour does occasionally come up empty, especially in the weeks before the session. The honest options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the paper plan, or a wait with a date attached. A tutor teaching the wrong one of the four courses will cover content the student is not examined on, which costs a term.

intro.heading: Four courses, one job title, and where the supply actually fails
paragraphs: The reason an Al Nahda parent struggles to find a maths tutor who seems to know the course is that there is no such thing as the course. IB Diploma mathematics is four distinct syllabuses sharing a timetable line: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. They share five topic areas by name and diverge sharply in emphasis, in papers, in calculator rules and in what the examination rewards. A tutor can be genuinely excellent at one and a poor fit for another.

Supply is uneven in a predictable pattern. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the most widely taken course in many Dubai cohorts and the easiest to staff. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is well covered. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is tighter, because it needs somebody comfortable with proof, a non-calculator Paper 1 and the extended Paper 3 build. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is the scarcest of the four, because matrices, graph theory and statistical inference in applied form are a specific skill set that few tutors have taught recently.

Al Nahda adds geography to that. The neighbourhood sits across the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, with Dubai-side schools under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Sharjah-side schools under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The Diploma cohorts nearest here sit mainly in Al Mamzar, Al Garhoud and Festival City, so students travel to school and the tutors who live close by have often never taught the Diploma at all. A filter based on distance from Al Nahda Road therefore returns the wrong kind of shortlist.

What works instead is a filter based on the course plus twenty minutes of testing. The tests are in this page and they require no mathematics from you - you are watching whether a tutor can do a specific thing and whether they say plainly when something is outside what they teach. Ask an AA HL candidate to differentiate from first principles and talk through why it works. Ask an AI candidate to interpret a chi-squared result in the context of data. Ask either to walk through a Paper 3 question as one build rather than four parts. The answers separate people quickly.

IB Gram delivers maths tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the named course and level. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Where the right specialist is not free in your window we say so at the match stage, with the options and a date, rather than placing an AI SL tutor with an AA HL student and letting a term pass before a mock paper explains it.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.programmesIntro: Maths support gets asked for at three points in an IB education, and the scarcity of the right tutor differs at each. Here is where the pool is deep and where it thins.

programmes.name: Diploma mathematics, the four courses
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches is algebra, functions, proof and calculus led, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and applied technique led, with a calculator permitted throughout. Higher Level in either route adds a third paper worth a fifth of the grade and roughly ninety hours of additional content depth, all of it examined.
programmes.countryNote: Not every school within reach of Al Nahda offers all four courses, and some run AI SL as the default with AA HL by application. If the course your child needs is not timetabled, that is a staffing and numbers constraint set by the school, and it is worth asking the IB coordinator in writing before Year 11 choices are signed.

programmes.name: MYP mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria out of eight each: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The scarce skill here is criterion literacy rather than advanced content. A student fluent in calculation can sit in the 3-4 band on investigating patterns for three reporting cycles without anyone diagnosing why.
programmes.countryNote: Standard and extended MYP maths streams exist in many Dubai schools, and which stream a student is in shapes their Diploma options. Send the four criterion scores rather than the overall grade when you brief a tutor, because the scores are what can be worked on.

programmes.name: IGCSE maths as the route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Most Diploma maths students in this catchment arrive from Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 rather than from MYP. Neither covers calculus to the depth Analysis and Approaches assumes from the first weeks, and the gap is specific: differentiation from first principles, radian measure, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws and the language of proof.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge now sets a non-calculator paper on both 0580 tiers, which has narrowed one part of that gap for students on that board. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, so students arriving from it feel the AA Paper 1 demand more sharply in term one.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: Within IB mathematics, Al Nahda families name a small number of specific problems. These are the ones that come up most, with a note on how hard each is to staff properly.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL: proof and Paper 3
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, counterexample and induction, plus the extended scaffolded Paper 3 build. Tight supply, because teaching the shape of a proof is a different skill from teaching the content being proved. This is the request where a geographic filter costs the most.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches: non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Surds, indices, logarithm laws, exact trigonometric values, partial fractions, differentiation by rule. The most trainable thing on the course and the most common October problem for students arriving from a calculator-permitted IGCSE route. Widely available and cheap to fix.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches: functions and calculus
subjects.description: Domain, range, composite and inverse functions, transformations, differentiation and integration techniques. Well supplied. The marks lost here are usually in the first third of a paper rather than the last, which a marked paper identifies immediately.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL: matrices and graph theory
subjects.description: The scarcest content area in all four courses. Matrices, transition models, graph theory and complex numbers in applied form. A tutor who has not taught AI HL recently will be learning it alongside your child, and should say so if asked directly.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation: statistical inference
subjects.description: Chi-squared tests for independence, t-tests, correlation and regression, and the interpretation sentence that carries the final mark. Reasonably supplied, but the marks sit in the hypothesis statement and the conclusion in context rather than in the calculator work.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator fluency

sections.heading: Twenty minutes of test tasks that identify a real maths specialist
paragraphs: Qualification lists do not distinguish an AA HL specialist from a competent maths graduate, so set tasks instead. Each of these takes a few minutes on a first call, requires nothing from you beyond listening, and produces an answer you can judge. Use them on any maths tutor in Dubai, including ours. What you are watching for is whether the tutor does the specific thing asked, explains while doing it, and says plainly when something is outside their experience.

For an Analysis and Approaches candidate: ask them to differentiate from first principles and explain why the limit process gives the gradient, out loud, as they would to a Year 12. Then ask them to prove a simple statement by contradiction. A tutor who teaches AA does both without hesitation and talks about where students go wrong. A tutor who knows the content but has not taught the course will produce correct mathematics with no teaching commentary at all, which is a different product.

For an Applications and Interpretation candidate: give them a short set of data and ask them to run a chi-squared test for independence, state the hypotheses properly, and write the concluding sentence in the context of the data. The last part is where the marks are and where most tutors stop. Then ask what students most commonly lose marks for in AI Paper 2. An honest answer names rounding too early, units omitted, and conclusions that restate the calculator output.

For either, ask them to walk through a Paper 3 question as a single build rather than four separate parts, explaining how the earlier results feed the later ones. This is the task that most reliably separates Higher Level experience from Standard Level experience. Finally, ask what they would refuse to do on an Exploration. The right answer is explicit: not write it, not redraft it to completion, not choose the topic and not supply the mathematics.

sections.heading: Choosing between the four courses, and why the choice outranks the tutor
paragraphs: Before buying any hours, confirm your child is on the right course, because that decision has more effect on a grade than the identity of a tutor. Analysis and Approaches suits students heading towards engineering, physics, mathematics or a selective economics programme where a calculus prerequisite is stated. Applications and Interpretation suits design, psychology, business, biology and most social sciences. Level then follows the rest of the subject block and the student's capacity, because Higher Level adds a third paper worth a fifth of the grade.

The weightings differ in a way that changes revision priorities. At Standard Level both routes sit two papers worth 40% of the grade each, with the Exploration at 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers - two longer ones at 30% each and the shorter Paper 3 at 20% - plus the same Exploration at 20%. That means an HL student who ignores Paper 3 has written off a fifth of their grade, and Paper 3 is precisely the component most often left until the final term.

The calculator rule is the difference students notice first. AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, so algebraic manipulation is examined directly. Every AI paper permits a graphic display calculator, which moves the difficulty from manipulation to selection and interpretation. A student arriving into AA SL from Pearson 4MA1, where a calculator is permitted on both papers, feels this sharply in October - and that single fact explains a large share of the tutoring enquiries we take from this catchment each autumn.

Switching course after Year 12 begins is possible and the window belongs to the school. Ask the IB coordinator in writing for the switch deadline and for a list of the content a student would need to make up. If the destination university route is the reason for the question, check the requirement on that university's own admissions pages rather than relying on a general statement, because requirements are set by programme and revised periodically. Nothing on this page should be treated as a university's requirement.

sections.heading: The graphic display calculator: the examinable skill almost nobody teaches
paragraphs: Every one of the four courses assumes graphic display calculator fluency, and no course teaches it systematically. Students acquire it from a classmate, a teacher's aside or a video, and the result is a two-year drag on their marks that nothing in a report explains. This is one of the easiest things to fix and one of the most reliably neglected, so it is worth asking any prospective tutor how they handle it.

The skills are concrete and listable. Solving an equation numerically when an algebraic route is not required. Finding intersections and using them to answer a question about two models. Running a regression and extracting the coefficients with the right number of significant figures. Using distribution functions rather than tables. Navigating the statistics menus without hunting. Storing an unrounded intermediate value instead of retyping a rounded one, which is where a surprising share of AI marks go.

The course changes which of those matter. AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so an AA student needs the device for Paper 2 and, at Higher Level, Paper 3 - which means fluency matters but non-calculator discipline matters more. An AI student uses the calculator on every paper, so for them it is close to a core skill and deserves two or three dedicated sessions early in Year 12 rather than a scramble before mocks.

A practical point for an Al Nahda family: this is one of the areas where an online lesson is genuinely better than an in-person one, because the tutor can share their screen with an emulator or the student can share theirs and the keystrokes are visible to both. Two people peering at one small handheld screen across a kitchen table is the worst possible arrangement for teaching it, and it is what an in-home session usually amounts to.

sections.heading: Exploration topics that fail, and the hour that prevents it
paragraphs: A fifth of every maths grade comes from the Exploration, and the most expensive mistakes happen before any writing. Marked out of 20 across five criteria, with presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics each carrying their own share, the component rewards a question with real mathematical content that the student genuinely owns. Most of the failures we see in Year 12 drafts from this catchment trace back to the topic rather than to the writing.

The commonest failure is a topic with no mathematics at the right level. A student writes an interesting investigation using arithmetic and a graph, and the use-of-mathematics criterion caps it regardless of how well presented it is. The second is a borrowed topic, where the question comes from a list online and the personal engagement criterion has nothing to reward. The third is a topic that depends on data the student cannot actually obtain, which surfaces three weeks before the deadline.

The fourth is more subtle: a topic so large that the report becomes a survey rather than an investigation. Reflection is impossible when nothing specific was attempted, and reflection plus personal engagement together carry a meaningful share of the marks - the cheapest ones on the component to recover and the ones most often left behind. A narrow question with a real answer scores better than a broad one with a summary.

Screening the topic takes one session and saves a term. Does the question require mathematics from the student's own syllabus or just beyond it? Is there a real model or real data rather than a restatement of someone else's result? Can the student say in one sentence what they are trying to find out, and does the answer matter to them? If all three are yes, the writing is a manageable job. If any is no, change the topic now rather than rescuing it in Year 13.

sections.heading: Bridging into the Diploma from IGCSE or MYP, and when to do it
paragraphs: Most Diploma maths students in this catchment arrive from Cambridge IGCSE 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 rather than from MYP, and the gap into Analysis and Approaches is specific rather than general. Neither IGCSE specification covers calculus to the depth AA assumes within its first weeks. The named items are differentiation from first principles, radian measure, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws, binomial expansion and the vocabulary and structure of proof. That list is closable in eight to twelve focused hours.

The board the student came from changes the emphasis. Cambridge 0580 now sets a non-calculator paper on both tiers, so those students arrive with some hand-arithmetic discipline already built. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, so students from that route feel the AA Paper 1 demand much more sharply. Ask which board and tier your child sat before planning any bridging work, because the two routes need different weighting.

Students arriving from MYP have the opposite profile. They have usually met investigation, generalisation and justification - the substance of the investigating patterns criterion - and have less experience of timed written papers, method marks and recall without resources. For them the bridging job is format rather than content: timed practice, showing working for credit, and speed. That is a different eight hours from the IGCSE version.

The right time for either is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12. There is no competing homework, no mandatory-subject load and no commute, and the work sits in a block rather than being squeezed into the two usable windows a term-time week in Al Nahda offers. It is also the most frequently wasted window in the entire Diploma, because nothing is formally due in it and so nobody plans it.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what we say when the right specialist is not free
paragraphs: Published Dubai market rates give an Al Nahda family something checkable to reason from, and each figure here can be verified at its source. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table placing specialist exam-year support in that region. BartyED published AED 650 at the premium end. Budget platforms advertise from around AED 33 to 52 with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik.

For AA HL and AI HL specifically, the budget band is a poor buy and it is worth saying so rather than leaving a parent to discover it. Proof technique, the Paper 3 build, matrices and graph theory are not things a capable undergraduate has necessarily taught. For non-calculator drilling, basic functions work and homework supervision, the budget band is perfectly reasonable, and a family can sensibly split a budget between the two rather than averaging across everything.

In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500. For an Al Nahda family that premium buys a tutor selected by willingness to drive to the Sharjah boundary in the evening peak, which is the opposite of the selection criterion this page argues for. All figures above were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers that published them; none is an IB Gram price.

Our availability position, stated before any payment. AI SL and AA SL matches are usually available within a few days. AA HL takes longer, particularly in October and before mocks. AI HL is the scarcest of the four and sometimes carries a genuine wait. In each case you are told at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right specialist, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot, or a wait with a date against it. We will not put an SL tutor with an HL student and hope.

sections.heading: Verification, honesty and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated and the position is public. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published - Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties - so any figure circulating as the penalty should be treated as unverified, and we publish none. Ask any tutor the permit question, ours included; it costs nothing to hold, so there is no cost reason for an evasive answer.

On regulators: Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, while Sharjah's answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education there and which, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of those bodies, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the Emirates and send no tutor to a UAE address. We publish no success rate, star rating or student count, because none could be produced with its sample size, date and method if you asked - and research into this market found pages showing two different review scores within one document.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a maths tutor in Al Nahda knows my child's actual course?
faqs.answer: Set a task rather than reading a profile. For Analysis and Approaches, ask them to differentiate from first principles out loud and explain why the limit gives the gradient, then to prove something by contradiction. For Applications and Interpretation, give them a small data set and ask for a chi-squared test with the hypotheses stated and the conclusion written in context. For either Higher Level course, ask them to walk a Paper 3 question as one build. A specialist teaches while doing it; a generalist produces correct mathematics silently.

faqs.question: Which of the four IB maths courses is hardest to find a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, by a clear margin. Matrices, graph theory and statistical inference in applied form are a specific skill set that relatively few tutors have taught recently. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is next, because proof technique and the extended Paper 3 build are different skills from the content they rest on. Both Standard Level courses are comfortably supplied. If your request falls in the scarce group we say so at the match stage, with a date.

faqs.question: My child is on AI SL but wants to study engineering. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It may be, and it is worth settling now rather than in Year 13. Engineering programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches because of a calculus prerequisite, but requirements are set per programme and revised periodically, so check the admissions page of each university your child is considering rather than relying on any general statement. If a switch is needed, the window belongs to the school: ask the IB coordinator in writing for the switch deadline and for the content that would have to be made up.

faqs.question: Why does AA Paper 1 cause so much trouble in October?
faqs.answer: Because it is sat without a calculator and most students arrive from a route where one was always available. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both its papers, so students from that board meet genuine hand-manipulation demands for the first time in Year 12. Surds, index laws, logarithms, exact trigonometric values and clean handling of negatives are all examined directly. It is the most trainable thing on the course: six to ten weeks of short, frequent, marked drills changes Paper 1 performance measurably.

faqs.question: Does graphic display calculator skill really affect a maths grade?
faqs.answer: Noticeably, and it is taught systematically almost nowhere. Students pick the device up from classmates and then lose minutes a paper to hunting through menus, plus marks to rounding an intermediate value instead of storing it. For Applications and Interpretation the calculator is used on every paper, so fluency is close to a core skill and deserves two or three sessions early in Year 12. It is also one of the few topics genuinely easier to teach over a shared screen than in person.

faqs.question: What makes an Exploration topic fail before any writing starts?
faqs.answer: Four things, in rough order of frequency. Mathematics below the level of the course, which caps the use-of-mathematics criterion whatever the presentation. A topic borrowed from a list online, which leaves personal engagement with nothing to reward. Data the student cannot actually obtain, which surfaces weeks before the deadline. And a topic so broad that the report becomes a survey, which makes genuine reflection impossible. One screening session at the start prevents all four and is the best-value hour on the component.

faqs.question: How many hours does bridging from IGCSE into Analysis and Approaches take?
faqs.answer: Eight to twelve focused hours for most students, aimed at a specific list: differentiation from first principles, radian measure, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws, binomial expansion and the structure of proof. Students from Cambridge 0580 arrive with some non-calculator discipline because that board now sets such a paper on both tiers; students from Pearson 4MA1 generally need more of it. The right window is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, which is also the most consistently wasted block in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Is a nearby maths tutor ever better than a course-matched one online?
faqs.answer: In two situations. A younger student who needs company and supervision rather than specialist teaching, where presence does most of the work. And a household whose broadband cannot carry a reliable video lesson, in which case a dropping connection is worse than no lesson. For a Year 12 or Year 13 on a named Diploma course, the specialism matters more, and a tutor willing to drive to the Sharjah boundary at peak has been selected for willingness to travel rather than for knowing AA HL.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tutoring cost for a family in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Budget platforms advertise from around AED 33 to 65. In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. We quote against the course, the level and the weeks remaining rather than from a rate card.

faqs.question: Is a budget online tutor acceptable for IB maths?
faqs.answer: For part of the work, yes. Non-calculator drilling, basic functions practice and supervised homework are reasonable uses of the AED 33 to 65 band that Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise. Proof technique, the Paper 3 build, matrices, graph theory and marking an Exploration against descriptors generally are not, because those are things a capable undergraduate has not necessarily taught. Splitting a budget between a cheap drilling slot and a specialist slot for the two or three things that decide the grade usually beats averaging across everything.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week should a Diploma student have?
faqs.answer: One is right for a student who is coping and wants to move from a 4 or 5 to a 6, provided the homework between sessions is actually done. Two suits a student with a diagnosed content gap, a Paper 3 problem at Higher Level, or an Exploration running behind the school's internal deadline. Three is an intensive block before mocks rather than a steady arrangement. The question that matters more is how many days pass between the lesson and the work it was meant to fix.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's Exploration draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, against the published descriptors, and that is one of the more useful things a tutor does. A tutor may screen the topic, question whether a step follows, point out that a graph is unlabelled, mark a draft criterion by criterion and state plainly that a section is below standard. A tutor may not write any part of it, redraft it to completion, choose the topic or supply the mathematics. The work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and a breach puts the student's diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Do you send maths tutors to homes in Al Nahda or Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. For maths specifically the online format loses very little: a shared whiteboard, the student's own working photographed and annotated live, and a screen-shared past paper reproduce what matters, which is watching the working appear line by line and stopping at the wrong line.

faqs.question: What happens if no AA HL or AI HL specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the match stage, before any payment, with three options. A different time slot with the right specialist, which usually means shifting an hour earlier or later in the Gulf evening. A tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot for you. Or a wait with a date attached, so you can decide rather than guess. Demand concentrates in the same two evening hours and fills in October and before mocks, so sometimes the honest answer is a wait.

intro.heading: Three moments when an Al Quoz family needs a maths tutor
paragraphs: IB Mathematics is the subject Al Quoz parents ask about most, and the request arrives at predictable points in the two-year cycle. The first is the term the route is decided, at the end of Year 11, when Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is chosen and almost nobody has checked it against the degree the student might apply for. The second is the term the exploration is due, when a research question that cannot be developed mathematically has already eaten six weeks. The third is the eight weeks before the papers, when the content is known and the marks still are not arriving.

Those three moments need three different tutors in effect, or at least three different plans. Route choice is a conversation about fit and prerequisites, and it takes one or two sessions. The exploration is process coaching against lettered criteria. Pre-session work is timed past papers marked against mark-scheme wording, with an error log. Treating them as the same product is how families end up paying for a weekly session that is aimed at none of the three.

The calendar decides which one you are in, so this page is organised around it. You will find the five syllabus topics with how each route weights them, the component weightings including Paper 3 at Higher Level, the exploration criteria with the marks attached, the maths year counted backwards, and an honest account of what each stage costs in time and money. The thing a family most often tells us afterwards is that they wish they had seen the weighting table a year earlier.

The Al Quoz practicalities are quickly stated. The district holds its housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with the rest given over to warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces. Children travel outwards to school in several directions, so a weekday session realistically starts between 5pm and 5.30pm, with weekend mornings carrying the second session when a pre-paper block needs two.

There is a fourth moment that families rarely plan for, and it is the cheapest of all: the summer between Year 11 and DP1. Four to six sessions there on notation, proof conventions and sheer algebraic speed address exactly what the Diploma assumes and IGCSE never had to teach. Nobody books it, because in July nothing is wrong yet, and that is precisely why it works.

One premise, because the rest depends on it. IB Gram delivers one-to-one mathematics tuition into Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics in particular this is an advantage rather than a compromise, because a shared screen with live annotation is a better working surface for algebra than a kitchen table and one sheet of paper.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: Mathematics support in Al Quoz is requested across three IB stages and one transition. Each is described by what the assessment actually requires, because that is what the sessions are built from.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The proof, calculus and algebraic route, at Higher and Standard Level. Higher Level is the most demanding mathematics course in the Diploma and adds Paper 3, a longer two-part investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade. Algebraic fluency is assumed rather than taught, so a student who is slow at manipulation spends their thinking time on mechanics instead of on the problem.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route Al Quoz families most often need help with, and the pattern is consistent: a student who did well in IGCSE Extended Mathematics meets Higher Level in DP1 and finds that correct answers without justification score less than they used to. That is a technique problem rather than an ability problem, and it is cheapest to fix in the first DP1 term.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The statistics, modelling and technology route, also at Higher and Standard Level, with Paper 3 again at Higher Level. Fluent graphical display calculator work is expected throughout, and the marks sit heavily on interpreting output in context rather than on producing it. Students lose marks by giving a technically correct value with no sentence explaining what it means.
programmes.countryNote: Applications is frequently chosen for comfort and then questioned when university prerequisites appear. It is a strong route for a student who thinks in data and context, and a poor one for a student who wanted engineering, so the decision belongs with the Mathematics department before the school's confirmation deadline.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than by percentage, covering knowledge and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The investigating-patterns criterion is the one that most directly rehearses the Diploma exploration, and it is the one most students treat as an optional extra.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where exploration skills are either built or not. A student who has learnt to generalise a pattern and justify it in Year 10 writes a far better exploration in DP1. For Al Quoz families this is the cheapest mathematics intervention available, and almost nobody books it.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma mathematics transition
programmes.description: The gap between IGCSE Extended or Higher tier mathematics and Diploma Higher Level is wider than the content list suggests, because what is rewarded changes. IGCSE pays for correct method; the Diploma pays for justified reasoning, correct notation and the ability to explain why a method is valid.
programmes.countryNote: A summer block between Year 11 and DP1 is the single most effective use of a holiday for a prospective Higher Level Analysis student in Dubai. Four to six sessions on notation, proof conventions and algebraic speed prevents the first-term drop that most families then spend a year repairing.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: Mathematics support is best organised by syllabus topic and component rather than by subject name, because that is how the marks are allocated. Below is what each part actually demands and where Al Quoz students most often lose marks in it.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms and, at Higher Level in Analysis, proof and complex numbers. Fluency decides everything downstream: a student slow at rearranging an expression spends their working memory on mechanics and has none left for the actual question.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Transformations, inverses, rational and composite functions, and in Analysis a heavier treatment of function behaviour. Marks are lost on domain and range stated carelessly, and on graph sketches that are qualitatively right but missing the labelled features the question asked for.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations in Analysis, with vectors at Higher Level; more applied geometry and three-dimensional work in Applications. The common failure is working in the wrong angular measure, which produces a confidently wrong answer that looks like a careless slip and is actually a habit.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Light in Analysis, central in Applications, where distributions, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing carry heavy weight. Students lose marks by running the right test and then not stating the conclusion in context, which is where the interpretation marks live.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, far deeper in Analysis Higher Level, where techniques of integration and differential equations appear. Applications treats calculus more instrumentally. Lost marks cluster around unjustified steps and omitted constants rather than around misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: A written paper that tests method and reasoning across the syllabus, with technology permitted or not depending on route and current specification. Timing is the usual limiting factor rather than knowledge, and the fix is timed practice marked to scheme wording.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Longer structured questions where the graphical display calculator is central. The characteristic error is a correct calculator result reported without the supporting line of reasoning, which forfeits method marks even when the final value is right.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: A two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade, requiring sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar context. Schools frequently reach it late in DP2, so it is the component students have practised least relative to its weight.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Internally assessed coursework carrying 20 marks across lettered criteria, including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The commonest structural failure is a topic the student likes that offers no mathematics to develop.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator and toolkit skills
subjects.description: Not a topic in itself and worth marks throughout. Knowing which function to use, how to report what it returned, and when a sketch is required rather than a value, is a trainable skill that students are typically left to pick up by accident.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Al Quoz actually needs to know
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Al Quoz means, in practice, one-to-one Diploma mathematics teaching that happens at home on a weekday evening. IB Gram delivers that as a live online session into Al Quoz homes on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

The first question any competent maths tutor should ask is which route the student is in. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation share five syllabus topics and weight them completely differently, and a tutor who treats them as the same subject will spend sessions on statistics an Analysis student barely needs, or on algebraic proof an Applications student will never be examined on. The second question is the level, because Higher Level adds Paper 3 and 20 per cent of the grade with it.

The third question is which component is losing marks, and it is the one that most changes the plan. A student who cannot do the mathematics needs teaching. A student who can do the mathematics and writes answers that do not earn the method marks needs a different and much shorter intervention. A student who runs out of time on every paper needs neither; they need timed practice and a pacing strategy. Those are three plans of three different lengths, and guessing between them wastes a term.

Mathematics is also the subject where online delivery is most clearly better rather than merely equivalent. Working is shared on screen and annotated live, the whole session is visible to both people at once, and nothing depends on who happened to be free to drive across Al Khail Road at five o'clock.

sections.heading: The five topics, and how each route weights them
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses are built from the same five topic areas, which is why the names sound interchangeable and the experience is not. What differs is depth and emphasis, and the difference is large enough that a student in the wrong route can be simultaneously capable and underperforming.

Analysis and Approaches concentrates on number and algebra, functions, trigonometry and calculus, with statistics present but lighter. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers, vectors and substantially harder integration. Applications and Interpretation inverts the balance: statistics and probability carry heavy weight, modelling runs through everything, and the graphical display calculator is a working tool rather than a checking device.

The table below sets the emphasis out so a family can see which route their child's strengths actually fit. Read it alongside one piece of evidence: a timed paper from the route in question, taken recently and marked honestly. A conversation about which course sounds harder produces worse decisions than a single paper does.

Two cautions. First, both routes are real mathematics and neither is a soft option; Applications Higher Level is a demanding course. Second, university prerequisites are set by programme rather than by subject area, so verify them with the institutions on your child's list, including UAE universities, rather than relying on a general statement from any tutoring page.

There is a practical reason the emphasis table is worth reading even after the route is fixed. It tells you where a tutor's hours should go. An Analysis student needs competence in statistics and depth in calculus, functions and algebra; an Applications student needs the reverse. A tutor who divides session time evenly across the five areas has not read the course your child is sitting, and that is a question worth asking in the first conversation.

sections.heading: Component weightings, and why Paper 3 is the one to worry about
paragraphs: Weightings are the fastest way to find out where a student's revision time should go, and most students have never seen them laid out. The internally assessed exploration and, at Higher Level, Paper 3 together account for a substantial share of the grade, and both are usually the last things a school reaches.

Paper 3 deserves separate attention because of the mismatch between what it is worth and how much practice it gets. It is a two-part extended investigation requiring sustained reasoning in an unfamiliar context, it carries 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade in both routes, and schools frequently arrive at it late in DP2 when everything else is competing for time. A student who has attempted two Paper 3s has a measurable advantage over one who has attempted none, and that is entirely a scheduling fact rather than an ability one.

The exploration is the other half of the mismatch. It is marked by the school against lettered criteria and moderated, and the marks are available months before the examinations, at a point when the student has more time than they will ever have again. Families who treat it as a chore to be completed quickly are leaving marks on the table that cannot be recovered in the examination hall.

Confirm the current weightings and durations against the subject guide your child's school holds, because the IB revises specifications and we do not republish their documents. What the table gives you is the shape of the decision: where the marks are, and therefore where the hours should go.

sections.heading: The exploration: criteria, marks, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one names a single internal assessment criterion. For mathematics that is a serious omission, because the exploration is marked out of 20 against lettered criteria and a student who does not know what each letter rewards is writing blind into a fifth of their grade.

The criteria cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and they do not carry equal marks. Use of mathematics carries the largest share, which means the decisive question is whether the chosen topic contains mathematics at the right level to develop. Presentation and communication together carry a substantial block that is almost entirely technique: consistent notation, defined variables, labelled graphs, no unexplained jumps.

Personal engagement and reflection are the criteria students treat as decoration and examiners treat as evidence. Engagement means the student's own thinking is visible in the choices made; reflection means they can say what their mathematics did and did not establish. Both are written, both are marked, and both are impossible to add convincingly at the end, which is why they belong in the plan from the first session.

The boundary matters most here of anywhere in mathematics. A tutor may test whether a topic yields mathematics, teach what a criterion rewards, show a worked example on unrelated data, read a draft and say which criterion it currently fails and why. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the exploration. The test after a session is whether the student could explain and defend every change in their own words. Confirm the current criteria and mark totals in the subject guide your school holds.

sections.heading: The maths year counted backwards
paragraphs: Mathematics has more hard internal deadlines than most Diploma subjects, and they are almost all set by the school rather than by the IB. Counting backwards from the May session is how a family finds out whether they are early, on time or in triage, and no competitor page in this market does it.

The route decision sits furthest back and matters most. It is confirmed at the end of Year 11 to a school deadline, and after that point it is effectively fixed. Next comes the DP1 work where algebraic fluency is either built or quietly skipped. Then the exploration topic, which should be interrogated for mathematical content before a word is written, and the exploration draft, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit. Then the mock window, then Paper 3 practice, then the session.

For a family deciding when to start, the honest rule is eight weeks of runway to change one component, and a whole term to change a habit. Algebraic slowness is a habit; it takes a term of short regular work and it cannot be fixed in a fortnight. A pattern of reporting calculator results without reasoning is a technique, and four sessions will shift it. Knowing which of the two you are dealing with is the entire value of the first diagnostic session.

IB session and results dates are not independently verified in this project, because ibo.org blocks automated access. UAE schools sit the May session, and anything more specific should come from your child's IB coordinator rather than from any tutoring page.

sections.heading: What maths tutoring costs, and what the alternative costs
paragraphs: Most families compare tutoring rates against each other. The more useful comparison is against the cost of not doing it, because in mathematics the downstream consequences are unusually concrete: a capped route, a prerequisite unmet after offers, or a resit year. Framed that way, a short targeted block looks different from an open-ended weekly commitment.

The market figures, attributed and dated October 2026. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour; IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Budget online provision starts far lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is appropriate for practice supervision and not for diagnosing why Paper 2 method marks are being forfeited. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

Now the arithmetic that actually decides the plan. Six sessions aimed at one identified component is a defined, finite cost. Two years of weekly mathematics bought because nobody diagnosed the problem is roughly fifteen times that, and often achieves less, because the sessions were not aimed at anything. The waste in this market is almost never the hourly rate; it is buying breadth when the problem had a location.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, which is the argument for a plan with a stated end rather than for the cheapest hour available.

sections.heading: Where Al Quoz students actually lose maths marks
paragraphs: After enough marked scripts the failures become repetitive, and almost none of them is a failure of mathematical ability. The dominant one is method marks forfeited by omitted working. A student who can see the answer writes the answer, and the scheme pays for the steps. This is the single most common and most fixable problem in Diploma mathematics, and it is usually worth more marks than any new topic.

Second is calculator work reported without reasoning. In Paper 2, a correct value produced by a calculator with no supporting line is frequently worth less than a wrong value with correct method shown. Students find this unjust, which is precisely why it persists: they argue with it rather than adapting to it. Four sessions of marking their own work against the scheme usually ends the argument.

Third is angular measure, which sounds trivial and is not. Working in degrees where radians are required produces an answer that is confidently wrong and looks like carelessness. It is a habit formed at IGCSE and it survives into DP2 unless someone names it. Fourth is timing, which masquerades as content weakness: a student who scores well with unlimited time and poorly under examination conditions does not need more teaching.

Fifth, and specific to the exploration, is a topic chosen for interest rather than for mathematical content. A student fascinated by a question that offers nothing to develop will spend six weeks producing work that cannot reach the upper bands on use of mathematics, which is the heaviest criterion. That one is free to avoid and expensive to discover late.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Quoz, and what will not be promised
paragraphs: Send four things: the route, the level, the school, and the last two marked pieces of mathematics, which may be papers or an exploration draft. A specialist reading those can usually name the failing pattern in one sentence, and the free trial lesson exists to produce that diagnosis before any payment is made.

What will not be said on the call: no grade promise, because nobody can make one honestly, and no claim that tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or progression, because that is a false claim about a regulatory process. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office or centre. There are no satisfaction percentages on this page, because publishing a statistic without its sample, date and method is just decoration.

A disclosed limit: Higher Level Analysis specialists at early-evening hours are genuinely constrained in the weeks before the May session, when much of Dubai's DP2 cohort wants the same slot. When that happens you are told, offered the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic view of when the slot opens. Nobody is quietly substituted.

Two facts to carry into any conversation with any provider. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. And we do not supply IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because that material is the board's copyright; we cite and link the official source instead.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should my child in Al Quoz choose?
faqs.answer: Decide it with evidence rather than with a conversation about which sounds harder. Take a recent timed paper from the route you are considering and mark it honestly. Analysis and Approaches is the proof, calculus and algebra route; Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and calculator-led interpretation. Both are real mathematics at both levels. Then check the prerequisites with the specific university programmes on your child's list, including UAE institutions, because requirements are set by course and change. The deadline for confirming is the school's.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor come to our home in Al Quoz?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are live one-to-one video sessions into Al Quoz homes on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For mathematics specifically this is usually better rather than merely equivalent, because both people see the same working surface at once instead of leaning over one sheet of paper at a kitchen table.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 3 such a problem for Higher Level students?
faqs.answer: Because of a scheduling mismatch rather than a difficulty one. Paper 3 is a two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade in both routes, and it requires sustained reasoning in an unfamiliar context. Schools frequently reach it late in DP2 when every other deadline is competing for time, so students arrive at it with the least practice relative to its weight. Two full attempts under timed conditions, started early, is a measurable advantage that costs only planning.

faqs.question: How many marks is the maths exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks, awarded against lettered criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the marks are not evenly spread. Use of mathematics carries the largest share, which is why the decisive question is whether the chosen topic contains mathematics at the right level to develop. Confirm the current criteria and totals in the subject guide your child's school holds, because the IB revises specifications and we do not republish their documents.

faqs.question: My child has an exploration idea they love. How do we know it is viable?
faqs.answer: Test it for mathematical content before a word is written, which is one of the most valuable things a tutor does, because a bad topic cannot be rescued later. The tutor interrogates the student's ideas for mathematical content, asks what could actually be developed and at what level, and keeps asking why this question until the answer is the student's own. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or complete any part of the exploration. After each session your child should be able to explain and defend every change themselves.

faqs.question: My child gets the right answers but loses marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly method marks forfeited by omitted working, and calculator results reported without the supporting line of reasoning. The scheme pays for steps; a student who can see the answer writes the answer and is paid for one line instead of four. In Paper 2 a correct calculator value with no evidence of method can score less than a wrong value with correct method shown. It is usually a four-session fix: mark their own scripts against the scheme until they can predict the mark.

faqs.question: When should an Al Quoz student start Higher Level maths support?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the best block available, and it is almost never used. Four to six sessions on notation, proof conventions and algebraic speed address what the Diploma assumes and IGCSE never taught, which is the cause of the first-term drop that families then spend a year repairing. Starting in the first DP1 term is the next best option. By the second term of DP2 the same gap costs considerably more hours and buys less, because the deadlines have stacked up.

faqs.question: Is the degrees and radians problem really worth a session?
faqs.answer: It is worth part of one, and it is worth naming because of how it presents. Working in the wrong angular measure produces a confidently wrong answer that looks like carelessness and is in fact a habit carried from IGCSE. Nobody corrects it because each instance looks like a slip. Across a paper it can cost several marks, and in trigonometry and calculus questions it cascades into later parts. One session of deliberate practice and an error log usually ends it.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child has a content problem or a timing problem?
faqs.answer: Give them a past paper twice: once under strict examination timing, once with unlimited time and no notes. If the untimed score is much higher, the problem is pacing and the plan is timed practice with a per-question time budget, not more teaching. If both scores are low, it is content or technique, and the marked script shows which. This takes one evening at home and saves families a term of tutoring aimed at the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Are statistics a waste of time for an Analysis and Approaches student?
faqs.answer: No, but the proportions differ sharply between the routes. Statistics and probability are present in Analysis and lighter than in Applications, where distributions, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing carry heavy weight. So an Analysis student needs competence rather than depth there, and session time is better spent on calculus, functions and algebraic fluency. A tutor who allocates equal time to all five topic areas regardless of route has not read the course.

faqs.question: What does a short maths block actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The market, attributed and dated October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Budget online provision starts at AED 33 to 65. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. The more useful number is the block: four sessions for a method-marks problem, four to six for the exploration, four to eight for Paper 3 technique.

faqs.question: Does online maths tutoring work as well for a struggling student?
faqs.answer: In mathematics it is generally stronger, because the work is visual and shared. Both people see the same annotated working at the same time, every step is legible, and the session can be paused on one line until it is understood. What matters more than format is whether the tutor teaches the route your child sits and diagnoses the actual failing component. A session in the room aimed at the wrong problem is worse than a session on screen aimed at the right one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Maths and Physics for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the overlap is real: a student who cannot rearrange an equation fluently struggles in both subjects, and the same algebraic work pays twice. But the test remains component-level competence in each subject separately, including the Physics internal assessment and Paper 3 for that subject. If a candidate is strong on Analysis Higher Level and vague about Physics paper structure, two specialists serve the student better than one convenient diary.

faqs.question: Before we spend anything on maths support, what should we gather?
faqs.answer: Three facts and one piece of evidence. The route and level your child is actually in, which is stated on the school's subject paperwork. The next mathematics deadline the school has set, which is usually an exploration checkpoint or a mock. And the last two marked scripts, photographed. With those in hand, a free trial lesson can tell you whether you are looking at a four-session technique fix or a term of fluency work, which is the only question that matters before you spend anything.

sections.heading: What a parent in Al Quoz 4 is actually asking for
paragraphs: The search phrase is an IB maths tutor in Al Quoz 4, but the question underneath it is narrower. A parent typing that has usually seen one of three things: a mock paper score that does not match the effort going in, an exploration deadline approaching with no topic chosen, or a DP1 report saying the Higher Level pace is a problem. The phrase is about location only because location is how people search for services. The actual requirement is a person who has taught the exact course.

That matters because IB Mathematics is not one subject. A tutor who is strong in Applications and Interpretation statistics may be genuinely weak on Analysis and Approaches proof by induction, and the two courses do not even share a paper structure. A general maths tutor advertising IB experience will usually have taught SL content to a GCSE-trained standard, which is adequate for a struggling SL student and useless for an HL student stuck on Paper 3. Asking which course and which level a tutor actually teaches separates the two in about thirty seconds.

The second thing underneath the search is time. Al Quoz 4 is a short drive from the industrial blocks and a long one from most of the schools its children attend, and a parent who has already lost the 4pm to 5.30pm window to a bus route has less flexibility than the booking page of an agency assumes. Any plan that needs a tutor to be physically present adds that person's commute to your constraint list.

So the honest answer to the search is this. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to the hour that works in your house. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and no page on this site will tell you otherwise. What you get instead is a choice of specialist by syllabus rather than by distance, which on a subject this segmented is the variable that moves a grade.

paragraphs: Work backwards from the door, not forwards from the bell. A school in Al Barsha finishing at 3.05pm puts a bus on the road at about 3.20pm once registration and loading are done. That bus serves Al Barsha South, parts of Al Quoz 1 and then the Al Quoz 4 compounds, and the last stop is reached between 3.50pm and 4.20pm. Add a fifteen-minute decompression and a snack, which every parent eventually accepts is non-negotiable, and the earliest honest start for anything cognitive is 4.45pm.

Then subtract homework. A Diploma student at a Dubai school carries roughly two hours of evening work in DP1 and more in DP2, spread across six subjects. If maths tuition sits before homework, the homework gets done at 9pm badly. If it sits after, the tutoring happens at 8.30pm to a student who has stopped absorbing. The slot that survives both is 6pm to 7.30pm, which is precisely the window an in-home tutor crossing Al Khail Road at rush hour cannot reliably promise.

Finish times are the standard published day for secondary year groups and will shift for activities, Friday timings and Ramadan. The point is not the exact minute. The point is that the gap between the bell and a usable session is between ninety minutes and two hours, and that an online session is the only kind that can be booked at the far end of it without a travel buffer.
