sections.heading: Mathematics AA or AI: the choice that sets the next two years
paragraphs: Of every maths question an Al Quoz 4 family brings, this is the one with the longest consequences, and it is usually decided in a fifteen-minute options meeting in Year 11. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic course: proof, calculus, sequences and series, and at Higher Level complex numbers and vectors. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling course: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, and at Higher Level graph theory, matrices and a far heavier statistical load than its reputation suggests.

The common error is to read AI as the easier option. It is easier to begin, because technology is permitted throughout and there is no non-calculator paper demanding hand manipulation. It is not easier to finish. AI Higher Level statistics, including hypothesis testing and the chi-squared distribution applied to unfamiliar data, defeats a steady stream of students every year who chose it to avoid calculus and met a different kind of difficulty instead.

The university consequence is the part parents are rarely told clearly. Engineering, mathematics, physics and most economics degrees at competitive universities expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some list it explicitly. Medicine and life sciences are generally satisfied with either at the right level. Business, psychology and social sciences will usually accept AI HL and sometimes prefer the statistical content. Check the specific course page at the specific university rather than trusting a general rule, because the exceptions are real and they change.

For a student already in DP1 and struggling, the useful question is not which course is better but whether a move is still possible. Schools in Dubai will normally allow an HL to SL move within the same course well into DP1 and a course change only very early, because the syllabus overlap is small. A tutor who has taught both can tell you within two sessions whether the problem is the course or the technique, which is a cheaper diagnostic than a term of guesswork.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: where the IB Mathematics marks sit
paragraphs: A surprising number of students in DP2 do not know how their maths grade is assembled, and neither do their parents. Knowing it changes what you practise. At Standard Level there are two examination papers and the exploration. At Higher Level there are three papers and the exploration, and the third paper is a different kind of assessment from the other two, which is why it is the one most often left until the spring.

The weightings are fixed and public. At SL, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each worth 40 per cent of the examination component and the exploration is 20 per cent of the overall grade. At HL, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each 30 per cent of the grade, Paper 3 is 20 per cent and the exploration is 20 per cent. The arithmetic worth noticing is that an HL student who ignores Paper 3 and the exploration has written off 40 per cent of the grade before entering the examination hall.

Each paper fails students in its own way. Paper 1 at AA punishes students who have never worked without a graphic display calculator, because the algebra has to be driven by hand and under time pressure. Paper 2 punishes calculator inefficiency, where a student knows the method but spends ninety seconds per question navigating menus. Paper 3 punishes students who have only practised short structured questions, because it asks for sustained reasoning through one unfamiliar investigation with later parts depending on earlier ones.

The tutoring implication is that these are four separate skills and a single weekly session cannot drill all of them. A sensible plan allocates them: non-calculator technique in the autumn, calculator efficiency alongside it, exploration work in a defined block, and Paper 3 investigation practice from the start of DP2 rather than the end.

sections.heading: The five places Al Quoz 4 students lose maths marks
paragraphs: These are diagnosable, which is the useful part. The first is notation. IB examiners award method marks for clearly communicated working, and a student who writes a correct answer with no visible chain of reasoning loses marks that were already earned in their head. This shows up as a student who is convinced they have been marked unfairly, and it is the fastest thing to fix: two sessions of writing solutions out properly usually recovers several marks a paper.

The second is the non-calculator paper at Analysis and Approaches. Students at Dubai schools are fluent with a graphic display calculator from MYP onward, and that fluency hides a gap. Factorising a cubic, rationalising a surd, differentiating a product by hand and simplifying a trigonometric expression are all Paper 1 skills, and all of them decay without deliberate practice. The symptom is a student whose Paper 2 scores are consistently eight to twelve marks above their Paper 1 scores.

The third is command-term blindness. Show that, hence, deduce, justify and verify ask for different things, and a student who treats them all as solve will lose the final mark on question after question. Hence in particular means the previous part must be used, and a student who starts again from scratch is throwing away the connection the examiner is testing. The fourth is units and significant figures, which costs a mark at a time and is almost pure carelessness, correctable with a checking routine rather than more teaching.

The fifth is the exploration, treated as an essay rather than a piece of mathematics. Students pick a topic because it sounds interesting, discover it supports only two pages of real mathematics, and then pad. That failure happens at topic selection, weeks before any writing, which is why exploration support that starts after a draft exists is support arriving too late to matter.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by letter
paragraphs: The exploration is 20 per cent of the maths grade at both levels and the single most mishandled component in the course. It is a twelve to twenty page individual investigation on a topic of the student's own choosing, marked by the school against five criteria and then externally moderated. Moderation matters: a school's generous mark can be pulled down across a whole cohort, and the student who suffers is the one whose work was weakest against the published descriptors.

The criteria are lettered A to E and they carry different weights. A rewards presentation and coherent structure. B rewards correct and consistent mathematical communication, which means notation, symbols and terminology used properly throughout rather than approximately. C rewards personal engagement, which is the criterion most commonly misread, because it is about genuine independent thinking rather than about choosing a topic connected to a hobby. D rewards reflection, which means critical commentary on the mathematics as it develops, not a concluding paragraph that says the investigation was interesting. E, use of mathematics, carries the most marks and is where a weak topic becomes unrecoverable.

What a tutor may legitimately do here is narrow and worth stating plainly. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, show a worked example built on a completely different topic, ask questions about the student's own draft, and point out where notation is inconsistent or where the mathematics stops short of the level claimed. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot supply the topic's mathematics, and cannot edit it into shape. IB academic-honesty rules make the student responsible for the work, and a student found to have submitted assistance as their own faces a malpractice finding.

The practical consequence for a DP1 family in Al Quoz 4 is timing. Topic screening in the spring of DP1 is worth more than any amount of help in the autumn of DP2, because the single decision that determines the mark ceiling is which topic the student commits to.

sections.heading: Online teaching against a tutor driving to Al Quoz 4
paragraphs: Set aside the preference question for a moment and look at what the in-home premium is actually buying. The gap between a qualified online tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 an hour is not a teaching-quality gap. It is a travel-cost gap, plus the scarcity premium that comes from only being able to hire from a twenty-minute radius. For Al Quoz 4, a pocket with few resident subject specialists, that radius is the binding constraint.

The things an in-home visit genuinely does better are worth naming. A young child who cannot yet self-manage a screen benefits from an adult in the room. A student with specific access needs may find a physical presence easier. A household with unreliable connectivity has a real problem with video lessons. None of those describe a typical Diploma maths student, who already does most of their work on a laptop and whose school runs its own learning platform.

Against that, online delivery wins on four measurable things for a Diploma student. The tutor pool widens from whoever lives nearby to whoever knows the course, which on a subject split into AA and AI at two levels is decisive. Sessions start on the minute, because no one is in traffic on Al Khail Road. The whiteboard, the graphing software and the past paper are all on screen and the recording or notes survive the session, which a kitchen-table lesson does not. And the rate does not carry a travel premium.

IB Gram's position, stated plainly: we do not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutors are not sent to addresses in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the country, and home tutoring is a service we provide in India only. Every lesson for an Al Quoz 4 family is one-to-one over live video. If your requirement is genuinely a person in the room, the right answer is an independent local tutor with a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and the next section explains how to check that.

sections.heading: Permits, legality and what a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and parents are entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The official route is the MoHRE service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two working-day completion time listed.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any page quoting a specific amount is quoting something it cannot source, and this one will not. Tutoring is not optional to regulate and the permit is not optional to hold; those are both things a competitor page in this market gets wrong in one direction or the other.

A separate thing entirely is a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not claim one, because it does not operate premises in the UAE. Any platform describing its tutors as approved by a regulator is describing something that does not exist in that form, and the phrase should make you ask for the permit number.

One more rule worth knowing before you hire locally. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document, but do not go looking for your child's own class teacher as a paid tutor.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a maths tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This section exists because one page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. It is worth being explicit about the line, because the consequences of crossing it land on the student rather than on the tutor. Under IB rules the exploration must be the student's own work, the school signs a declaration to that effect, and a malpractice finding can cost a candidate the diploma. No grade is worth that exposure.

A tutor may teach the mathematics a student needs in order to attempt a topic. A tutor may explain what each exploration criterion rewards and in what proportion. A tutor may demonstrate a full worked investigation on an entirely different topic so the student can see the shape of a strong piece. A tutor may read the student's own draft and respond with questions: why is this variable defined this way, what justifies that assumption, where does this notation break down. A tutor may point at a section and say the mathematics here is below the level you are claiming.

A tutor may not choose the topic for the student, supply the mathematical content, write or rewrite any passage, edit a draft into shape, or produce material the student then submits. Those are not grey areas and they are not services IB Gram offers at any price. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the MYP Personal Project. We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because reproducing them is a copyright matter; the official sites are the place to get them and your child's school already has access.

The useful by-product of this boundary is that work produced under it survives scrutiny. A student who can explain every line of their own exploration in a viva with their coordinator has nothing to defend. One who cannot is in difficulty regardless of the mark the work would otherwise have earned.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the course, the level, the school and the problem as you see it. We propose a tutor who teaches that exact course, with the trial slot timed to the window that works after the Al Quoz 4 school run. The trial runs forty-five minutes over live video, with no card details taken, and your child does some actual mathematics in it rather than a sales call. Afterwards you get a plain note on what the tutor found and what they would do over the first month.

Availability is where most platforms go quiet, so here is the honest version. A specialist in Mathematics AA Higher Level at a 6pm Gulf Standard Time slot is a narrower pool than a Standard Level tutor at 4pm, and in the eight weeks before the May session that pool is at its tightest. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour, we will say so and offer the nearest slot, a different tutor with the right course, or a date when the slot opens. We will not put an Applications and Interpretation tutor in front of an Analysis and Approaches student and hope.

If a match is wrong, say so after the first paid session and we change it. The reasons a match fails are usually not about competence: a pace mismatch, a personality mismatch, or a student who needs to be asked questions rather than shown methods. Those are visible in one session and worth acting on immediately rather than three months in.

One last note on the calendar, since it drives everything. Cambridge IGCSE and O Level examinations run in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai parent reading a page that quotes it is reading a page written for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session; confirm every specific IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than with us, because those dates are revised and we do not publish them.

faqs.question: Is there an IB maths tutor near Al Quoz 4, or will my child be taught from somewhere else?
faqs.answer: Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, so the tutor's physical location stops mattering. Some of the tutors teaching Dubai families are UAE-based and some are not; what we match on is whether the person has taught Mathematics AA or AI at the level your child is sitting. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE at all, so a search for someone nearby is answered by a wider choice of specialist instead. For Al Quoz 4 specifically, where few resident Diploma maths specialists live, that trade is strongly in your favour.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session start if the school bus reaches Al Quoz 4 at 4pm?
faqs.answer: Plan for 6pm. A 4pm door time needs fifteen minutes to decompress and a snack, then homework has to fit somewhere, and a session placed before homework pushes the homework to 9pm. The window that reliably survives a full term is 6pm to 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time, and an online session can hold that start exactly because nobody is driving across Al Khail Road at 5.40pm to reach you. On activity days a shorter 7.15pm session works better than a cancelled one.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics AA or Mathematics AI at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, not on which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches HL is expected for engineering, mathematics, physics and most competitive economics courses, and some universities name it explicitly. Applications and Interpretation HL is accepted for business, psychology and social sciences and carries statistical content those degrees value. AI is easier to start, because technology is permitted throughout, and harder to finish, because HL hypothesis testing and graph theory defeat students who chose it to avoid calculus. Check the specific course page at the specific university before deciding.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Mathematics tutor cost per hour around Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market puts a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed. Budget online options run from AED 45 to 150. Those are other providers' published figures. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Mathematics exploration without writing any of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version of exploration support we offer. A tutor explains what criteria A to E reward and in what proportion, screens a proposed topic for whether it can carry enough mathematics to satisfy criterion E, demonstrates a complete worked investigation on a different topic, and reads your child's own draft to ask questions about assumptions, notation and level. A tutor will not choose the topic, supply the mathematics, write a passage or edit the draft into shape. The exploration must be the student's own work and a malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and failing the AA HL tests. Is it too late to change course?
faqs.answer: Probably not, but the window is narrow and the school decides. Dubai schools will usually allow a move from Higher to Standard Level within the same course well into DP1, because the content overlaps substantially. A switch between AA and AI is normally only possible very early, since the syllabuses diverge quickly. Before escalating it, get a diagnostic: two sessions with a tutor who teaches both courses will usually show whether the problem is the course, the examination technique, or the gap left by standard rather than extended MYP mathematics.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week do Al Quoz 4 families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One sixty-minute session a week is the common starting point in DP1 and for a drifting rather than collapsing grade. Two sessions a week are worth it in DP2, in the run-up to a mock window, or when a student is carrying both a weak paper technique and an exploration deadline. More than two rarely helps during term, because the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time rather than taught hours. Start at one, review at four weeks, and add only if the review says to.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a MoHRE private tuition work permit to teach my child online?
faqs.answer: A person providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. If you hire a tutor independently in Dubai, ask to see the permit and check the name matches the person teaching.

faqs.question: Which Al Quoz and Al Barsha schools teach the IB Diploma Mathematics courses?
faqs.answer: Schools in and around this corridor that run the Diploma include Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, North London Collegiate School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Raffles World Academy, with British-curriculum schools such as Kings' School Al Barsha and Jumeirah College taking students to IGCSE before an A Level or Diploma split. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25. Named schools describe the local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any of them.

faqs.question: What happens to our 6pm maths slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan, which moves the door time in Al Quoz 4 earlier and changes the whole evening shape. Most families either pull the session forward into the early afternoon or move it to a post-Iftar slot, and both work on video in a way they would not with a tutor driving across town at Iftar. Tell us which pattern your household keeps and the slot is rebuilt for the month rather than suspended. Revision plans in DP2 should assume the Ramadan weeks will be lighter and front-load accordingly.

faqs.question: Will the tutor use my child's own school worksheets or a separate scheme?
faqs.answer: Your child's own, in term time. A session that repairs the misunderstanding in this week's class topic is worth several that teach a parallel syllabus well, and the tutor works from the school's scheme of work and the student's own marked assessments. For examination preparation the balance shifts toward past papers under timed conditions and an error log the student keeps. What we will not do is supply syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those belong to the boards; the official sites and your school hold them.

faqs.question: Does the exploration get marked by our school or by the IB?
faqs.answer: Your school marks it against the published criteria, then the IB moderates a sample externally. Moderation can move a whole cohort's marks if the school's application of the criteria was generous, and the students hit hardest are the ones whose work sat weakest against the descriptors. That is the practical argument for working on criterion E, use of mathematics, early rather than polishing presentation late: a topic with genuine mathematical depth survives moderation, while a well-presented thin topic does not.

faqs.question: Does Mathematics AI Higher Level close any university doors?
faqs.answer: For some degrees, yes. Engineering, mathematics, physics and the more quantitative economics courses at competitive universities generally expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a number of them say so on the course page. Business, management, psychology, geography and most social sciences accept AI HL and sometimes value its statistical content. Medicine and the life sciences usually accept either at the required level. The only reliable method is to open the entry-requirements page for the exact course at the exact university, because general guidance in this area is wrong often enough to matter.

faqs.question: How does a graphic display calculator work in an online maths lesson?
faqs.answer: Two ways, and both are better than they sound. The student keeps their own handheld model in front of them, which is the one they will sit the examination with, while the tutor shares an emulator or the matching software on screen so keystrokes can be demonstrated step by step. For Paper 2 efficiency work this is more useful than sitting side by side, because the tutor's screen shows the menu path at a readable size. For Paper 1 at Analysis and Approaches the calculator goes away entirely and the work is done by hand on a shared whiteboard.

The tutor sets a short diagnostic, usually a past-paper question at your child's level, then watches how the student works rather than only whether the answer arrives. You get a plain written note afterwards on what the tutor found and what the first month would cover. The point of the trial is to test the match, so if your child finds the tutor's pace or style wrong, say so and we propose someone else.

intro.heading: The 15:40 problem, and why it decides who teaches your child maths
paragraphs: Most families in Al Qusais start this search in the same half hour of the day. School has finished, the bus has turned off Damascus Street, and a Year 12 student is sitting at the kitchen table with a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches problem set that neither parent can help with. The question that gets typed into Google is about location, because location is how people think about help. The honest answer is that location is the least useful filter available for IB Diploma maths, and in Al Qusais specifically it is the filter that costs you the most.

Al Qusais sits on the Deira side of the city, strung along Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road with the Green Line running underneath it and Al Ittihad Road feeding the Sharjah border a few minutes north. That geography is excellent for getting a child to school and poor for getting an adult to your door at 16:00. An independent tutor crossing from Jumeirah, Barsha or Dubai Marina in the afternoon peak is budgeting forty to seventy minutes each way on a good day, and that travel is billed to you whether anyone mentions it or not. Market in-home rates in Dubai run higher than online rates for exactly this reason.

The second cost is narrower and more expensive. IB Diploma Mathematics is not one subject. It is four separate courses - Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level - with different content, different papers and different calculator rules. A tutor who is strong on AA HL calculus may be the wrong person for an AI SL student building a regression model, and the reverse is equally true. Filter for the ten-minute radius around Al Qusais and you are choosing from whoever happens to live nearby. Filter for the course, and you are choosing from everyone who teaches it.

So this page answers the search literally, then answers the question underneath it. You will find what the Dubai market charges for maths support at each tier, which schools around Al Qusais, Al Nahda, Al Mamzar and Al Garhoud your child's cohort comes from, how the five criteria of the Mathematics Exploration are actually marked, where Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks are lost, and what time of day a session can realistically run once the school bus, Arabic homework and the mandatory UAE subjects have taken their share of the week.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and we say so on every page rather than letting a parent find out after the deposit. What that buys an Al Qusais family is a specialist in the specific course your child sits, booked at 16:00 or 20:00 Gulf Standard Time, with no travel time inside the fee and no reason to cancel because Al Ittihad Road has stopped moving.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-qusais.programmesIntro: An IB maths tutor in Al Qusais is usually asked for at one of four moments: the MYP report that drops a band, the Year 11 course choice, the first Diploma internal exam, or the Exploration deadline. Each needs a different kind of help, so here is what the programmes actually demand.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two routes, two levels. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-heavy route, with calculus at its centre and a non-calculator Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led, statistics-heavy and calculator-permitted throughout. Both run five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Higher Level adds a third paper and roughly ninety extra teaching hours of content depth.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools around Al Qusais split differently on this. Some British-track schools offer only AA at both levels; some offer AI SL as the default and AA HL by application. If your child's school does not run the course they need, that constraint is set by the school's own timetable and staffing, and it is worth asking the IB coordinator in writing before Year 11 subject choices are signed off.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight each: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is the one that surprises families, because it asks a student to find a pattern, describe it in general terms and justify it - closer to proof than to arithmetic. A child can be fluent in calculation and still sit in the 3-4 band on B and C.
programmes.countryNote: MYP reports in Dubai arrive as four criterion scores plus a 1-7 overall, and the conversion is set by the school, not by a published national table. That is why an Al Qusais parent comparing two children at two schools cannot compare the numbers directly. Ask for the criterion scores, not the overall, when you brief a tutor.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics as the route in
programmes.description: Most Al Qusais students arriving into the Diploma come through Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE 4MA1 rather than through MYP. Both end at sixteen and neither covers calculus in the depth AA HL assumes from week one. The gap is real, specific and closable: differentiation from first principles, radian measure, binomial expansion and the language of proof.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge restructured 0580 so that both tiers now sit a non-calculator paper, which changed what an Al Qusais Year 11 needs to practise. Students who arrive in the Diploma from the Extended tier generally cope with AA SL; those from Core more often fit AI SL. Check which tier your child was entered for, because the entry decision was made by the school.

programmes.name: Maths alongside Career-related and mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Diploma maths is rarely the only pressure on the week. In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and those lessons occupy timetable space that in other countries would be free. A maths plan that ignores them produces a schedule a student abandons in week three.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA sets mandatory-subject instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met. In practice this means the realistic homework window on a school night in Al Qusais is shorter than parents assume, and a single focused 60-minute maths session usually beats two scattered 45-minute ones.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Families search for an IB maths tutor in Al Qusais and then describe a much narrower problem once a tutor is on the call. These are the ten requests that come up most from this part of Dubai, with what each one actually involves.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers plus the Exploration. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where fluency in algebraic manipulation either holds or collapses. Paper 3 is a two-part extended problem built on unfamiliar ground, and students lose marks there by answering part (a) and then abandoning the thread the question was building.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers and the Exploration. The common failure is not calculus but functions: domain, range, composite and inverse functions, and transformations asked in unfamiliar notation. A student who can differentiate reliably and still scores 4 is usually losing marks in the first third of each paper, not the last.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, matrices, graph theory and complex numbers in applied form, with a calculator permitted on every paper. The difficulty is interpretation rather than technique: choosing a test, stating a hypothesis properly, and writing a conclusion in context that earns the final mark rather than restating the output.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: The most commonly taken maths course in many Dubai cohorts. Financial mathematics, descriptive statistics, regression, probability distributions and basic calculus. Marks are lost through calculator discipline - unrounded intermediate values, wrong distribution chosen, answers given without units or without a sentence of interpretation.

subjects.name: The Mathematics Exploration
subjects.levels: HL and SL, all four courses
subjects.description: Marked out of 20 across five criteria and worth a fifth of the final grade. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a draft, point to a weak justification and model what reflection looks like. A tutor may not write it, redraft it to completion or supply the mathematics. We say that plainly because this SERP contains sellers who do otherwise.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: The GDC is examinable in practice if not in name. Solving numerically, finding intersections, running regressions, using distribution functions and reading statistics menus cleanly saves minutes per paper. Students who learned the device from a classmate rather than methodically lose marks to it for two years.

subjects.name: Non-calculator algebra for AA Paper 1
subjects.description: Surds, indices, logarithms, partial fractions, exact trigonometric values, factor and remainder theorem. This is the single most trainable thing on the course and the thing Al Qusais students arriving from a calculator-permitted IGCSE route most often lack. Six weeks of daily short drills changes a Paper 1 score measurably.

subjects.name: Proof and mathematical reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction, counterexample and proof by induction at HL. Students write something true and still earn nothing because the logical structure is missing. Teaching the shape of a proof - what must be assumed, what must be shown, what closes it - is a different lesson from teaching the content it proves.

subjects.name: Statistics and hypothesis testing
subjects.description: Chi-squared tests for independence, t-tests, correlation and regression, and the interpretation sentences that carry the marks. The method is calculator work; the marks sit in the hypothesis statement, the degrees of freedom, the comparison with the critical value and the conclusion written in the context of the data.

subjects.name: MYP to Diploma maths bridging
subjects.description: A six to ten week block that closes the gap between a criterion-based MYP course and a paper-based Diploma one. Timed practice, written method, algebraic fluency and the habit of showing working for marks rather than for the answer. Most useful across the summer before Year 12 rather than in the first term of it.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Al Qusais costs, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest thing in the market and work up, because that is the order in which a parent's options actually appear. Budget online tuition, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from the low double digits an hour: Tutopiya's published rates began around AED 33 to 52 when read in October 2026, and EdFlik listed sessions from AED 45 to 65. Those figures are real and they buy supervision - someone sitting with a child while they work - rather than subject expertise in a named Diploma course.

The next band up is where most Al Qusais families end up. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted between roughly AED 150 and 300 an hour across the Dubai market; Unitors published IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. For a named IB or IGCSE specialist the published range widens to about AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table putting specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450-plus. At the top, BartyED published AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visits are the band that matters for this page, because they are the thing the search phrase implies. Dubai in-home one-to-one is quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate's table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The difference between those two numbers is not better teaching. It is a car on Al Ittihad Road at 16:30.

Every figure above is a market rate published by somebody else and read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. We do not publish an hourly rate on these pages because the right answer depends on the course, the level and how many weeks are left; the free trial lesson exists so that a family can judge the tutor before any fee is discussed, and its only condition is that it is one lesson with one tutor.

sections.heading: The Al Qusais week, hour by hour, and where a maths session actually fits
paragraphs: This is the part of the decision nobody publishes, and it is the reason the school-run angle matters more here than in a villa community with a short internal commute. Private schools across this part of Dubai finish the academic day between roughly 14:30 and 15:15. Bus routes out of Al Garhoud, Al Mamzar and Oud Metha into Al Qusais 1, 2 and 3 take a further twenty to forty minutes depending on the loop, so the practical arrival window at home is 15:00 to 15:45, later for students at the southern end of the catchment.

What follows is not free time. A Dubai private-school student also carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies as mandatory subjects alongside the licensed international curriculum, and those subjects set homework like any other. Add a co-curricular commitment two afternoons a week and the genuinely available slots on a school night narrow to two: an early one from about 15:45 to 17:00, and a late one from about 19:30 to 21:15 after the family has eaten.

An in-home tutor has to land inside one of those two windows having crossed the city. The early window collides with the worst of the outbound afternoon traffic and the late window asks someone to drive to Al Qusais at 19:00 and home again at 21:30. That is why in-home maths tutoring in this part of Dubai is quoted high, cancels often and tends to settle on Friday and Saturday rather than on school nights - which is the worst time for maths, because the gap between the lesson and the homework becomes six days.

An online slot removes the travel from both sides of the hour. It also lets a family use the short Tuesday window and the long Saturday morning differently: diagnosis and marking in the long slot, drilling and correction in the short one. sections.heading: Four courses, not one subject: choosing between AA and AI at HL and SL
paragraphs: The single most consequential maths decision an Al Qusais family makes is not which tutor to hire. It is which of the four Diploma maths courses the student takes, and it is usually made in Year 11 with incomplete information. Analysis and Approaches is the route for students heading towards engineering, physics, mathematics, economics at a selective university or anything with a calculus prerequisite. Applications and Interpretation is the route for students heading towards design, business, biology, psychology, social sciences and most medicine applications that do not specify AA.

The levels then change the weightings rather than only the volume. At Standard Level in both routes there are two examination papers worth 40% of the grade each, plus the Exploration at 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers - two long ones at 30% each and a shorter Paper 3 at 20% - plus the same Exploration at 20%. Paper 3 is the component HL students underestimate: a small number of extended, scaffolded problems on unfamiliar ground, where a student who stops after the first part loses most of the available marks.

The calculator rule is the practical difference students feel first. AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator in both levels, which means algebraic fluency is examined directly. Every AI paper permits a graphic display calculator, which shifts the difficulty from manipulation to selection and interpretation. An Al Qusais student arriving from a calculator-permitted IGCSE route into AA SL therefore faces a specific, trainable shock in term one, and that is one of the most common reasons a family starts looking for a tutor in October.

Switching between courses after Year 12 has begun is possible but costly, and the window is set by the school's own internal deadlines rather than by any public rule. If the question is live in your household, ask the IB coordinator in writing for the school's switch deadline and the content a student would need to make up. The table sets out what the four courses differ on.

table.caption: IB DIPLOMA MATHEMATICS - THE FOUR COURSES COMPARED

sections.heading: The Mathematics Exploration, criterion by criterion, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: One fifth of the final maths grade comes from a piece of coursework the student writes themselves, and it is marked out of 20 across five criteria. Criterion A, presentation, carries 4 marks and rewards a report with a clear aim, a logical structure and a conclusion that answers the aim it set. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries 4 marks for correct notation, defined variables, labelled graphs and consistent symbols. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries 3 marks for genuine ownership of the question rather than a borrowed topic. Criterion D, reflection, carries 3 marks for critical discussion of what the mathematics did and did not show. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6 marks and is the largest single block.

Knowing those letters changes how a student spends their time. The most common pattern we see in Al Qusais Year 12 drafts is a report that is strong on E - the mathematics is competent and at an appropriate level - and weak on C and D, because the student treated reflection as a closing paragraph rather than as a thread running through the work. Those two criteria are worth 6 marks between them, the same as the entire use-of-mathematics block, and they are the cheapest marks on the whole component to recover.

The second pattern is a topic chosen because it sounded interesting rather than because it contains enough mathematics at the right level. A topic screen at the start costs one session and saves a term. Does the question require mathematics from the student's own syllabus or beyond it? Is there real data or a genuine model, rather than a summary of somebody else's result? Can the student say in one sentence what they are trying to find out?

The boundary matters more than the technique. Under IB academic-honesty rules the Exploration must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the criteria, ask why a step follows, point out that a graph is unlabelled, mark a draft against the descriptors and say that a section is not yet at the standard. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite it to completion, choose the topic on the student's behalf or supply the mathematics. There are sellers in this search result who offer completed Internal Assessments. Buying one risks the student's diploma, and we will not do it.

sections.heading: Where Al Qusais students actually lose maths marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Diagnosis beats volume. A marked past paper tells you more in forty minutes than a term of general revision, and the patterns across this cluster are consistent enough to predict. The first is arithmetic and algebraic slips under time pressure on AA Paper 1 - sign errors in expanding brackets, lost negatives when differentiating, surds left unsimplified. These are not conceptual failures and they do not respond to re-teaching the topic. They respond to short, frequent, non-calculator drills with immediate marking.

The second is method marks never earned because working was not shown. A student who writes a correct final answer with no line of reasoning collects the answer mark and forfeits everything else; a student who writes clear working and reaches a wrong answer often keeps most of the marks. Dubai students arriving from a background where the answer is the deliverable take a term to internalise this, and it is worth more than any single topic.

The third is interpretation in AI. A chi-squared test completed correctly on the calculator earns the technique marks and loses the final ones because the conclusion restates the p-value instead of answering the question about the data. The fix is a sentence template the student writes themselves, applied to twenty past-paper conclusions until it is automatic.

The fourth is Paper 3 at Higher Level, where the structure of the question is the question. These are extended problems that build, and the later parts are often more accessible than the middle once the earlier results are in hand. Students who treat Paper 3 as four unrelated questions leave marks on the table. Practising the whole paper under time, twice, usually fixes it faster than practising the topics inside it.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma calendar counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the IB Diploma in the May session, and almost every deadline that matters to a maths student sits months before it. Working backwards is more useful than working forwards, because it shows which term the Exploration actually has to be finished in rather than when it is theoretically due. Note that IB session and results dates are published by the IB itself and are not restated here; confirm every date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it.

The shape of the two years is stable even when the dates move. Year 12 term one establishes the course and exposes the gaps. Term two is the natural window for the Exploration topic to be screened and the data or model to be chosen. Term three carries the first full internal examination, which is the first realistic grade signal a family gets. The summer between the years is the only long block available for bridging content, and it is the block most often wasted.

Year 13 term one is when the Exploration is drafted, reviewed and submitted to the school's internal deadline, which the school sets earlier than the IB's own upload deadline. Term two is mocks, and the mock grade is what universities see in a predicted grade. By the time the May session arrives, there should be nothing left to learn - only timed practice and error correction. Families who start tutoring in the final eight weeks are usually buying exam technique rather than content, and that is a legitimate but much narrower purchase.

For students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications on the way in, the published pattern is different and better documented. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: KHDA, your child's school report, and what a tutor can and cannot read from it
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects on a published six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the rating belongs to the school rather than to any department inside it. A school rated Very Good can still have a stretched maths department, and a school rated Good can be excellent at AA HL. Parents in Al Qusais comparing two schools for maths specifically will get more from asking which of the four courses each school actually runs than from the inspection band.

The regulator map matters here because Al Nahda sits on the Sharjah boundary. Dubai schools answer to KHDA; Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. A family moving one street can change regulator, inspection framework and fee-approval process at once.

Two pieces of KHDA policy change what a maths plan has to accommodate. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

On fees, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. That is the right anchor for any conversation about tutoring cost: school fees are flat, so the tutoring line in a household budget is the part a family still controls. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no accreditation and no relationship with any regulator named here - we are describing what these bodies do, not claiming their endorsement.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens when no AA HL specialist is free
paragraphs: The process is short and the first step is diagnostic rather than commercial. Tell us the school, the exact course - AA or AI, HL or SL - the year group, the most recent grade or criterion scores, and the two time windows on a school night that genuinely work for your household. That last item is the one families leave out and the one that determines whether a schedule survives past week three in Al Qusais.

We then match a tutor to the course rather than to the subject, and the first lesson is a free trial with that tutor, one lesson, no fee discussed beforehand. If the fit is wrong - and sometimes it is, for reasons that have nothing to do with competence - say so and we match again. A student who does not want to talk to their tutor will not learn maths from them, and that is worth discovering in week one rather than in month three.

Transparency on availability is the part most providers skip. Demand for AA HL and AI HL specialists concentrates in the same two hours of the Gulf evening, and in October and in the weeks before mocks those hours fill. If no UAE-based specialist in your child's exact course is free in your window, we say so and offer the alternatives honestly: a different slot with the right specialist, a different tutor with adjacent expertise now, or a wait with a date attached. What we will not do is put an AI SL tutor in front of an AA HL student and hope.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, for every family in the UAE. We do not operate an office, a centre or a branch in the Emirates, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated: individuals providing private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor you consider - ours or anyone else's - whether they hold it.

process.title: Tell us the course, not just the subject
process.description: AA or AI, HL or SL, year group, school and the most recent grade. If you have a marked paper or a report with criterion scores, send it. The difference between a useful first lesson and a wasted one is almost entirely in this message.

process.title: Name your two real time windows
process.description: One short weekday slot and one longer weekend one, in Gulf Standard Time. Al Qusais arrival times after the school run sit between 15:00 and 15:45, so tell us whether 15:45 is comfortable or whether your household only works after 19:30.

process.title: Meet the matched tutor in a free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, one tutor, no fee agreed in advance. The tutor teaches something real rather than interviewing your child. You and the student both say afterwards whether the explanation landed, and that answer decides whether anything continues.

process.title: Start with a marked paper, not a syllabus
process.description: The first paid session is diagnostic: a past paper or a section of one, marked against the real scheme, turned into a written list of three to six named weaknesses. Everything after that is aimed at the list rather than at the course.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the clock
process.description: Checkpoints sit against the school's internal dates - internal exams, the Exploration deadline, mocks - rather than at an arbitrary number of sessions. When the list is closed and the next deadline is clear, we say so instead of renewing by default.

whyPoints.title: The course, not the postcode, picks the tutor
whyPoints.description: Searching for an IB maths tutor in Al Qusais by distance limits you to whoever lives nearby. Matching by course opens the whole pool of AA HL or AI SL specialists and gives an Al Qusais family the same choice a Dubai Marina family has.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the fee
whyPoints.description: Dubai in-home rates are quoted from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online. The gap is a car crossing the city twice, and online delivery removes it from both the price and the cancellation risk.

whyPoints.title: Honesty about the Exploration
whyPoints.description: We teach the five criteria, question drafts and refuse to write any of it. This SERP contains providers selling completed Internal Assessments. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is a malpractice risk carried by the student, not by the seller.

whyPoints.title: Slots that match the Al Qusais school day
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled against bus arrival and the mandatory-subject homework load, not against a generic afternoon. A 15:45 start and a 19:45 start are different lessons, and we plan them differently rather than pretending they are interchangeable.

whyPoints.title: Sourced figures, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is a published market rate attributed to its source and dated. We publish no success percentage, no star rating and no student count, because none of those can be shown to you on request, and a number you cannot check is worth nothing.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in your child's exact course is free in your window, you are told at the match stage with the alternatives and a date, rather than after a deposit. A disclosed wait is cheaper for a family than a mismatched tutor.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB maths tutor in Al Qusais who comes to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Every UAE lesson we arrange runs one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. The Dubai market does supply in-home maths tutors, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel according to published rate tables read in October 2026. What you give up by choosing in-home in Al Qusais is choice: you are selecting from tutors willing to cross the city in the afternoon peak rather than from everyone who teaches your child's exact Diploma course. For AA HL in particular, that narrows the pool sharply.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session realistically start in Al Qusais on a school night?
faqs.answer: Two windows work. School days across this part of Dubai end between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, and bus routes into Al Qusais 1, 2 and 3 put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45. That makes a 15:45 or 16:00 start viable for a short focused block. The second window opens after the family has eaten, from about 19:30 to 21:15, and tends to be the more reliable of the two during term because nothing else competes for it. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework usually takes the gap between them.

faqs.question: Which of the four IB maths courses should my child in Al Qusais take?
faqs.answer: It follows the university destination rather than the current grade. Analysis and Approaches suits engineering, physics, mathematics and selective economics, where a calculus prerequisite is stated. Applications and Interpretation suits design, psychology, business, biology and social sciences. Level then follows workload and the rest of the subject block, because Higher Level adds a third paper worth a fifth of the grade. Ask your child's IB coordinator which of the four courses the school actually runs, in writing, before Year 11 choices close - not every Dubai school offers all four, and that constraint decides the question for many families.

faqs.question: My child came from Cambridge IGCSE 0580 into AA SL and is struggling. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is the most common October call we take from this cluster. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics ends at sixteen without the calculus depth AA assumes from the first weeks, and the non-calculator demand of AA Paper 1 lands hard on students used to a calculator being available. The gap is specific and closable: differentiation from first principles, radian measure, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws, binomial expansion and the language of proof. Six to ten weeks of short, frequent, marked drills changes Paper 1 performance measurably. It is a bridging problem, not a sign the course was the wrong choice.

faqs.question: How is the IB Mathematics Exploration marked, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It is worth 20% of the final grade in all four courses and is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation (4 marks), mathematical communication (4), personal engagement (3), reflection (3) and use of mathematics (6). A tutor may teach those criteria, screen a topic for viability, question a step, mark a draft against the descriptors and say when something is below standard. A tutor may not write it, redraft it to completion, pick the topic or supply the mathematics. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work must be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student.

faqs.question: How much do Al Qusais families typically pay for IB maths support per month?
faqs.answer: The market rather than our price list: Bestimate's Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages seen in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers that published them. IB Gram quotes against the course, the level and the weeks remaining rather than from a fixed table.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Qusais actually run the IB Diploma maths courses?
faqs.answer: The Diploma cohorts closest to Al Qusais sit mainly in Al Mamzar, Al Garhoud and Festival City - schools such as Al Ittihad Private School Al Mamzar, Deira International School and Universal American School run the programme through to examination. Al Qusais and Al Nahda themselves are dominated by Indian-curriculum and British-track schools, so many Diploma students from this neighbourhood commute ten to twenty minutes each morning. Confirm current programmes directly with the school and against KHDA's own school listing; we name these schools as neighbourhood context and claim no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Is my child's maths tutor in Dubai legally allowed to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: Ask and expect an answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AA Paper 1 and AA Paper 2 for an Al Qusais student?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, and that single difference reshapes what each paper examines. Paper 1 tests algebraic fluency directly: surds, exact values, logarithm manipulation, differentiation by rule, clean handling of negatives. Paper 2 tests selection and modelling, where the calculator does the arithmetic and the marks sit in choosing the right approach and interpreting the output. At Standard Level each carries 40% of the grade; at Higher Level each carries 30% with Paper 3 taking a further 20%. Most students need separate practice regimes for the two.

faqs.question: Does online maths tutoring actually work for a student who prefers face-to-face teaching?
faqs.answer: For maths specifically it transfers well, because the work is written. A shared whiteboard, a photographed problem set annotated live and screen-shared past papers reproduce the part of a lesson that matters - watching a student's working appear line by line and interrupting at the line where it goes wrong. What a parent should insist on is a trial lesson with the actual matched tutor, not a sales call, because the variable that decides this is the tutor's habit of asking rather than telling. If the student talks for less than half the lesson, the format is not the problem.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an Al Qusais Diploma maths student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session suits a student who is coping and wants to move from a 4 or 5 to a 6, provided the homework between sessions is actually done. Two a week suits a student with a diagnosed content gap, a Paper 3 problem at Higher Level, or an Exploration running behind the school's internal deadline. Three a week is an intensive block before an internal exam or mocks, not a steady state, and we would say so rather than sell it. The number that matters more is how many days pass between the lesson and the homework it was meant to fix.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IB maths and IB physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The overlap is real - kinematics leans on calculus, fields on vectors, uncertainties on algebraic manipulation - so a tutor who teaches both can use physics problems to repair maths and vice versa. The risk is dilution: a tutor strong in AA HL and merely competent in Physics HL will quietly spend the physics hour on maths. Our preference is one specialist per subject with the two aware of each other's diagnosis, unless a single tutor can show depth in both at the level your child sits.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until internal exams. Is it too late to start maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough to change exam technique and close three or four named weaknesses. It is not enough to re-teach two years of content, and any provider who says otherwise is selling you something. The honest plan starts with a marked past paper in session one, produces a short written list, and spends the remaining weeks on timed practice and correction against that list rather than on syllabus coverage. Students in this situation often gain more from method-mark discipline and rounding control than from new topics, because those losses are spread across every question.

faqs.question: Do sessions continue through Ramadan and the Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed rather than the frequency. During Ramadan school days shorten and the useful study window shifts to the late morning or to after Iftar, so sessions typically move earlier in the day or to roughly 21:00 onwards by agreement. School holidays are the opposite case: long uninterrupted blocks with no competing homework, which is why the summer between Year 12 and Year 13 is the best bridging window in the whole Diploma and the one most often lost. Tell us your family's preference and we schedule against it rather than against a default.

Send us those, plus a marked paper if you have one, and the first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, with the fee discussed only afterwards. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody drives anywhere, and the full hour is teaching.

intro.heading: What two years of IB maths support actually costs a family here
paragraphs: Most pages about IB maths tutoring in Dubai decline to mention a price. That is a strange way to answer the question a parent is holding, which is almost never "is maths tutoring good" and almost always "what is this going to cost me, and is it worth it". So the money comes first on this page, with every figure attributed to whoever published it so you can go and read it yourself.

Think in months rather than hours, because that is how a Diploma Programme is actually paid for. A weekly hour across the two years of the DP is somewhere between seventy and eighty sessions. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for an exam-year specialist. Monthly packages advertised in this market sit at around AED 799 for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. Those are the numbers a two-year commitment is built from, and the spread between the cheapest and the dearest version of the same arrangement is large enough to pay a term of school fees.

Where families in Al Rashidiya waste money is predictable, and it is rarely the hourly rate. It is paying specialist rates for the wrong course, because nobody checked whether the student is on Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. It is a weekly hour of general maths in a student's strongest paper while the paper they are failing goes untouched. It is buying twelve sessions in April when the exploration was due in January. It is the travel premium: in-home one to one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and the difference buys a car journey through the Garhoud interchange rather than better teaching.

IB Gram's own model is online one to one, in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the course and the paper. Home visits are an India-only service; nobody is driving to an Al Rashidiya address for a lesson. That is not a limitation we are apologising for on a maths page: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 is a narrow specialism, and the pool of people who have taught it well is spread across the world rather than clustered near Dubai International Airport.

What follows is the detail behind the money. The course choice and what it costs you to get wrong. The three papers and where the hours have to go. The exploration, which is twenty per cent of the grade and the cheapest twenty per cent to protect. The arithmetic of one session a week against two. And the honest account of what a tutor may do with an exploration, because this is the part of IB maths where the market behaves worst.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: An Al Rashidiya student arrives at Diploma maths from MYP or from IGCSE, and the gap between those two starting points is the single biggest predictor of how many tutoring hours the first year needs. These are the stages we cover.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. Five topic areas run through both: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, with the balance between them differing sharply by course. Assessment is two written papers at Standard Level, three at Higher, plus the mathematical exploration. Confirm the current structure with your school's IB coordinator before planning around it.
programmes.countryNote: Al Rashidiya's nearest IB continuum option is Uptown International School, with further Diploma provision in the Al Garhoud and Mirdif clusters. Because the IB accounts for roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum, Diploma maths specialists are genuinely thinner on the ground here than IGCSE ones, and that is reflected in what the local market charges for them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D rather than by paper marks, with extended and standard routes in the later years. MYP maths builds investigation and modelling habits that serve Applications and Interpretation well and Analysis and Approaches less well, because AA assumes a fluency with algebraic manipulation that criterion-based tasks do not always force. Extended MYP maths is the sensible route for a student aiming at AA Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: For a family in Al Rashidiya the decision point is MYP Year 5, where the choice between standard and extended maths quietly sets which Diploma courses stay available. A student in standard MYP maths who later wants AA Higher Level is looking at a summer of bridging work, and buying that bridging in advance is cheaper in both money and stress than buying remediation in DP1.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma bridging
programmes.description: The crossing most Dubai students actually make, because UK-curriculum schools dominate enrolment. IGCSE Extended maths leaves a student well drilled in technique and short on proof, on radians, on function notation and on the expectation of justifying a method rather than producing an answer. A focused block of six to ten sessions in the summer before DP1 removes most of the first-term shock.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Rashidiya student moving from a British-curriculum school in Mirdif or Al Qusais into a Diploma Programme in Al Garhoud is a routine local case. The expensive version of this transition is discovering the gap in November of DP1 and buying emergency sessions at exam-year rates; the cheap version is ten summer sessions at ordinary rates.

programmes.name: University entry and course choice
programmes.description: What the maths course on the transcript opens or closes. Engineering, physics, economics and computer science degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, while many business, social science and design routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Requirements vary by university and by year, so the only safe method is to read the specific entry page for the specific course.
programmes.countryNote: Check requirements directly with the universities your child is considering, including the UAE institutions, rather than relying on any summary. IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or accelerate Ministry of Education equivalency, and there is no verified IB points threshold for equivalency published on ministry sources, so ask moe.gov.ae or your school registrar for that figure rather than trusting a tutoring page.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: IB maths tutoring is bought by course, but it is spent on topics. These are the areas where Al Rashidiya families most often find the hours going, with what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and proof-heavy route, expected by most engineering and physical science degrees. Standard Level is already a serious course; Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and a substantially harder calculus load, and carries a third paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and data route, with a technology-assumed approach and a heavier statistics weighting. Accepted by many business, social science and design degrees and by fewer engineering ones. Students underestimate it: the Higher Level course is demanding, and the statistics is not a soft option.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponentials and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at AA Higher Level proof by induction and complex numbers. This is where IGCSE-trained students are strongest and where MYP-trained students most often need rebuilding before anything else works.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational functions, and the graphing fluency the whole course rests on. Marks go missing on domain and range, on sketching without a calculator, and on reading a transformation in the wrong order.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Radians, identities, equations and, at AA Higher Level, vectors in three dimensions. Students who learned trigonometry in degrees at IGCSE lose a surprising number of marks simply from not working comfortably in radians, and that is a drill, not a concept.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and regression, weighted much more heavily in Applications and Interpretation than in Analysis and Approaches. The common loss is interpretation: the calculation is right and the sentence explaining what it means in context is missing or wrong.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration and their applications, reaching considerably further at AA Higher Level, where integration techniques and differential equations appear. The non-calculator paper is where calculus fluency is exposed, because there is nowhere to hide an unlearned derivative.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A piece of independent written mathematics carrying twenty per cent of the final grade, assessed on criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. A tutor may teach the criteria and question a draft. A tutor may not write any part of it.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, no calculator
subjects.description: A separate skill from knowing the maths. Exact values, surds, algebraic manipulation under time pressure and the discipline of showing a method that earns method marks even when the final answer is wrong. Pure practice, and the cheapest grade movement available in this subject.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving, Higher Level only
subjects.description: An extended, scaffolded investigation sat only by Higher Level students, where the mathematics is familiar and the format is not. Students who have never seen a Paper 3 before the examination lose marks to the structure rather than the content, which makes it the clearest case for targeted work.

subjects.name: IGCSE and MYP maths foundations
subjects.description: Where a Diploma problem usually began. A DP1 student failing Paper 1 often has an unresolved weakness in index laws, surds or rearranging formulae, and three sessions on those is worth ten on calculus. We diagnose backwards before teaching forwards.

subjects.name: Further maths and bridging to university
subjects.description: For students heading into engineering or mathematics degrees who want the first-year step reduced. Covers proof technique, linear algebra foundations and the habits of rigour that a Diploma course touches but does not drill, usually as a short summer block rather than an ongoing arrangement.
