sections.heading: The calculator, the formula booklet and the things schools assume
paragraphs: A surprising share of lost marks in IB mathematics trace back to equipment and documents rather than to understanding. The graphic display calculator is required in Paper 2 and Paper 3 and prohibited in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1. Schools issue a model, teach to it, and assume the student has explored it. Most have not. A pupil who cannot find the numerical solver, the stored-variable list or the distribution functions under time pressure is paying for the calculator twice: once in money and once in the minutes spent hunting through menus.

The formula booklet is provided in the examination and is a document in its own right. It contains what it contains, and the commonest discovery in a first session is that a student has been memorising a result that was printed on page four all along, while not knowing that a result they assumed was printed is not. Twenty minutes spent reading the booklet with a tutor, marking what is there and what must be known, converts directly into time saved in the paper.

Alongside all of this, pupils in Dubai private schools carry the mandatory UAE subjects regardless of the international curriculum their school is licensed for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in Dubai private schools, KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. That is real weekly load, and it is load a maths plan has to be built around rather than on top of.

The practical consequence for a Satwa family is that the week has less slack in it than the timetable suggests. Two forty-five minute maths sessions, the set work between them, and the mandatory subject homework is a realistic ceiling for most pupils during term. Anyone proposing four sessions a week in October is proposing something that will be abandoned by November, and planning for the pattern that survives is worth more than planning for the pattern that looks committed.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the school, the route and level, and what the last marked piece of work said. We look for an online one-to-one tutor who teaches that route, and we book a free trial lesson before anything is paid. The trial is a working lesson, not a sales call: the tutor should come out of it able to name the two or three topics that need attention and the single habit that is costing the most marks.

Availability is where most platforms go quiet, so here is the honest position. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level with Paper 3 experience, and exploration feedback in the weeks before an internal deadline, are the two things most in demand and most often unavailable at the exact hour a family wants. When that happens we say so, offer the nearest slot that exists, and where no UAE-based specialist covers the route we are open that the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is told a specialist is available when one is not.

There is also a question of fit that no matching process solves on paper. Some pupils need a tutor who moves fast and says little; others need one who narrates every line. If the trial lesson does not work, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking the child to adapt. A mismatch found in week one costs a week. A mismatch tolerated politely costs a term, and in DP1 a term is a substantial fraction of the whole course.

Finally, timing. The best moment to start is the first term of DP1, when the route can still be tested and a weak foundation can still be rebuilt. The second best moment is immediately after the first mock, because a marked script is the most useful document a tutor can be given. The worst moment is six weeks before the examination with no script and no exploration, and even then a short intensive block can repair accuracy, method visibility and command-term reading. What it cannot do is build two years of calculus, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something.

Exploration time is spent reading the student's own draft against criteria A to E; Paper 3 time is spent on extended problems that build towards something unseen, which no normal school week rehearses.

faqs.question: My child is choosing between Maths AA and Maths AI next term. How do we decide?
faqs.answer: Decide on two pieces of evidence rather than on reputation. First, what the child can do on paper under time: work through a past Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 with no calculator and see what happens, because that paper is where the route becomes real. Second, the published entry profile of the courses they might apply to, since engineering and quantitative economics departments often expect the Analysis route while business, psychology and design frequently accept Applications. A strong IGCSE grade alone is weak evidence for Higher Level. A timed diagnostic hour in the first term of DP1 costs far less than switching route in DP2.

faqs.question: Is a 5pm maths lesson realistic if the school bus reaches Satwa at about 4.40pm?
faqs.answer: It is tight but workable, and the twenty minutes matter. A lesson that begins while a child is still putting a bag down is spent settling rather than working. For a 4.40pm arrival we would normally book 5.00pm at the earliest and prefer 5.15pm, with the session shortened to forty-five minutes rather than stretched. Because lessons are online there is no travel to protect, so the start time can move by fifteen or twenty minutes on the day if the coast road has been slow. That flexibility is the practical reason online delivery suits this neighbourhood.

faqs.question: How many marks is the mathematical exploration worth, and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It carries a fifth of the final grade at Standard and Higher Level, on both routes, and it is marked out of twenty against five criteria lettered A to E. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four marks each. Personal engagement and reflection carry three marks each. Use of mathematics carries six, the largest single allocation, and it asks for mathematics at the level of the course, correct and relevant to a stated aim. Internal marks are externally moderated. Most of the outcome is decided at topic choice, weeks before the writing starts.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my daughter's exploration draft without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is worth stating plainly. A tutor reads the draft she has written, points at a specific criterion, and explains what that descriptor asks for which the draft does not yet show. That is teaching and it is allowed. What a tutor must not do is choose the topic, supply the mathematics, or edit the prose into a finished state, because IB academic honesty rules require the work to be the student's own and a breach puts her Diploma at risk rather than ours. Ask any tutor to describe that boundary before you book.

faqs.question: Does Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches really allow no calculator at all?
faqs.answer: Correct, at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and Paper 2 is sat with one. Applications and Interpretation permits a calculator in every paper, which is one of the clearest practical differences between the routes. The consequence for a pupil who has typed every calculation into a screen since Year 7 is a genuine problem in DP1 term one, and it is a fixable one: short weekly by-hand accuracy work, exact values rather than decimals, and the habit of checking a line before building on it.

faqs.question: My son is at a well-inspected school but stuck at a 4 in Maths HL. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: School quality and individual outcome come apart more often than parents expect, and in Higher Level maths the usual cause is not teaching. It is one of four things: arithmetic slips early in long questions that then carry forward, correct answers written with no visible method so the method marks are lost, command terms read as suggestions rather than instructions, or two or three topics quietly avoided since DP1. All four are invisible in classwork and obvious in a timed paper. That is why a first session should be short questions under time rather than a conversation about confidence.

faqs.question: How long before the May session should Higher Level maths revision start?
faqs.answer: Treat the exploration and Paper 3 as the long-lead items and work backwards from the school's internal deadlines, not from the examination. A realistic pattern is exploration drafting and feedback running through DP2 term one, Paper 3 rehearsal starting as a separate strand once the course content is largely delivered, and full past-paper work in the final months. Starting a Paper 3 strand only after the mock is the commonest timing error we see. IB session and results dates should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator, since we do not publish unverified ones.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 look like and which students sit it?
faqs.answer: Higher Level candidates only, on both routes. It presents two extended questions, each building through several parts towards something the student has not been taught directly, and it carries a fifth of the Higher Level grade. In Analysis and Approaches the parts are problem-solving; in Applications and Interpretation they are modelling investigations. The skill being tested is persistence inside a structure: treating part (a) as a hint about part (d), and carrying on when a middle part has not resolved. Very few school weeks rehearse it, which makes it high-yield tutoring time.

faqs.question: Is an IB maths tutor in Al Satwa cheaper online than in the home?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is travel rather than teaching. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, while published online rates for qualified subject tutors start lower, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Part of the in-home premium is a journey with no teaching inside it, and in Satwa at 5pm that journey is slow. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE at all; that service exists only in India, so our UAE delivery is online one-to-one.

faqs.question: We live in Satwa but my child's school is in Al Barsha. Does that commute matter for online lessons?
faqs.answer: It matters for when, not for whether. The return leg from the inland schools along Sheikh Zayed Road at peak is the longest of the routes Satwa families use, which typically pushes a weekday session to around 6.00pm or onto a weekend morning. What the commute no longer affects is tutor choice. Once a lesson is online, the pool is every tutor who teaches your child's route on Gulf Standard Time rather than every tutor who could reach Satwa by six, and on a Higher Level course that is the difference that shows up in marks.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week do Diploma families in this area usually start with?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions on non-consecutive days is the pattern that survives a term, typically forty-five to fifty minutes each. The gap between them is the point: it is where the set work is attempted and where the real error pattern surfaces. One ninety-minute session a week suits DP2, when the exploration and Paper 3 both need sustained attention. Four sessions a week proposed in October is a plan that gets abandoned by November, because the mandatory UAE subjects and school homework already fill more of the week than the timetable suggests.

faqs.question: Does my child need a maths tutor who is a current IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and examiner status is harder to verify than it sounds. What actually predicts useful teaching is assessment literacy: can the tutor name which of the four IB maths courses your child is on, describe what Paper 3 contains, say which exploration criterion a draft is weakest against, and explain why a 'show that' question scores nothing without a derivation. Any tutor can be asked those four questions in a trial lesson. We do not describe tutors as examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner status never implies access to marking or boundaries.

faqs.question: Will maths tutoring have to compete with the Arabic and Islamic Education timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the plan should account for it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. That is real weekly load carrying its own homework. Two maths sessions plus set work is a sensible ceiling during term, and building around the mandatory load works better than stacking on top of it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist is free when we ask?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. The two things most often in short supply are Higher Level tutors with real Paper 3 experience and exploration feedback in the weeks before an internal deadline. When that is the case we offer the nearest slot that genuinely exists, and we are explicit that a specialist may be based outside the UAE and teaching on Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is describe a generalist as a route specialist, because the cost of that lands on your child in week four.

faqs.question: Can the maths slot move to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in this neighbourhood ask for exactly that. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window shifts into the evening, so a post-Iftar session often works better than an afternoon one. Because the lesson is online there is no journey to arrange around prayer or meal times, and the slot can move for the month and move back afterwards without losing the tutor. Shorter, more frequent sessions tend to hold up better than long ones during Ramadan, particularly for by-hand accuracy work that depends on concentration.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Al Sufouh who knows this course?
paragraphs: The honest answer is: a few, and fewer than the search results suggest. Al Sufouh is a narrow strip between Dubai Knowledge Park and the sea, with Dubai College inside it, GEMS Wellington International School inside it, and the Al Barsha and Greens schools a short run inland. The catchment generates real IB Diploma demand. What it does not generate is a deep local supply of people who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level through a full two-year cycle, marked a Paper 3 to the published markbands, and supervised an exploration from a blank page to a submitted twenty-mark piece.

Those are three different competences and most advertisements collapse them into one word. A tutor who teaches A Level Mathematics well is not automatically equipped for AA HL, because A Level does not contain an exploration, does not contain a Paper 3 of that character, and does not demand the proof work that AA HL carries in its first topic. A tutor who teaches IGCSE 0580 Extended confidently is further away still. Both can be excellent teachers and still cost a family a term while they learn the course alongside the student.

So the question a parent should ask is not whether a tutor is near Al Sufouh. It is: which course, which level, and have you taught it. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with separate syllabuses, separate paper structures and different technology assumptions. Each runs at Standard and Higher Level. That is four distinct teaching jobs, and a tutor who has done one of the four is not interchangeable with a tutor who has done another. The HL variants add a third paper worth a fifth of the final grade.

This is where a geographic search works against a family. Restricting the pool to people who can reach Al Sufouh 2 at 5pm on a Tuesday removes most of the people who have taught AA HL to a full cohort. The published in-home rate band in Dubai runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and at the top of that band a family is paying specialist money for whoever is geographically available. The specialist money is not the problem. The geography is.

IB Gram's position is fixed and it is the reason this page exists. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. A student in Al Sufouh therefore gets matched to an AA HL teacher because that is the course they sit, not because that teacher happens to live in New Dubai. That is the whole argument, and it is a scarcity argument rather than a convenience one.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through the IB continuum, and the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools offering the Diploma generally feed into it from their own Middle Years Programme or from an IGCSE route. The three bands below behave differently enough that support for each is a different job.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one mathematics course from group five, choosing Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Standard or Higher Level. Both courses cover the same five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The depth and the balance between those topics differ sharply. Standard Level is assessed by two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty. Higher Level splits as thirty, thirty and twenty across three papers, with the exploration again at twenty.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh's Diploma cohort is small enough that a single school set can contain both AA HL and AI SL students taught in the same room at different times. Families here frequently discover in Year 12 that the course chosen in May does not suit the student, and a route change after the first term is a real piece of work rather than a form.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than against a paper: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-world contexts. Each is marked out of eight against level descriptors. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the route that prepares a student for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the gap between standard and extended MYP is the single best predictor of whether AA HL will be comfortable.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai a student may move from an MYP school in Al Sufouh to a Diploma at a school in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills, or from an IGCSE route into a Diploma inside the same catchment. Those two entry routes arrive at AA HL with different gaps: the MYP student usually needs algebraic fluency, the IGCSE student usually needs investigation and communication skills.

programmes.name: IGCSE into Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: Students entering the Diploma from Cambridge 0580 Extended, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics or Pearson 4MA1 Higher arrive with solid procedural technique and no experience of an extended piece of independent mathematical writing. The first term of AA HL exposes that immediately, because the proof work and the functions topic move faster than any IGCSE paper does. The 0607 route arrives better prepared for the technology-assisted papers, having assumed a graphic display calculator throughout.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of private enrolment against 7 per cent for the International Baccalaureate, so the IGCSE-to-Diploma crossover is common in Al Sufouh rather than exceptional. A student making that move in the same summer is doing a route change and a school change at once, and the mathematics is usually the part that shows the strain first.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on a timetable and four distinct courses in practice, and the related subjects below are the ones Al Sufouh families most often request alongside it. Each note names where marks are actually lost rather than describing the topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route, with proof, sequences and series, and a heavier calculus load at Higher Level. Standard Level Paper 1 is sat without technology, which punishes students who have learned every method through a calculator. Marks leak in unsimplified exact forms, in differentiation of composite functions, and in proof questions answered by example rather than by argument.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Paper 3
subjects.description: A one-hour paper carrying twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, built from two extended problem-solving questions that develop an unfamiliar idea in stages. It rewards reading the scaffolding and using part (a) in part (c). Students who treat it as a harder Paper 2 lose marks by abandoning the thread, and the fix is practice with whole papers rather than with topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with technology assumed on both papers. Content is broad rather than deep: regression, hypothesis testing, graph theory and voronoi diagrams at Higher Level. Students lose marks by giving calculator output without interpretation, and by failing to state what a result means in the context the question built.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: An independent piece of mathematical writing, typically twelve to twenty pages, assessed on five criteria worth twenty marks in total. The most common failure is a topic that produces description rather than mathematics. The second is reflection written as a conclusion, which costs marks on criterion D. Topic choice decides the ceiling before a word is written.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Requested alongside AA HL more than any other subject, because the mechanics and the fields work share mathematical machinery. Students who can differentiate in a maths lesson and cannot recognise a gradient as a rate in a physics graph have a transfer problem rather than a content problem, and it is cheaper to fix once than twice.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The quantitative sections reward exactly the fluency AA builds: rearranging expressions, handling logarithms in pH work, and propagating uncertainties without losing significant figures. A student strong in maths and weak in chemistry is usually weak on the descriptive organic and energetics material rather than on calculation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject expecting essays. Diagram accuracy with correctly labelled axes, and calculation shown rather than asserted, are both reliable marks. The evaluation command terms are where strong mathematicians most often cap out, because a judgement is required rather than a result.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paired with AA HL by students heading towards engineering or data courses. The algorithms and complexity material rewards mathematical reasoning; the paper technique rewards precise use of pseudocode conventions. Marks are lost to answers that describe what a program does instead of tracing what it outputs.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge TOK examines, and students taking AA HL are often asked to write about it. A tutor can discuss the knowledge questions and interrogate an argument. A tutor cannot write the essay or the exhibition commentary, and the distinction should be stated before the work begins.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed curriculum, including IB Diploma schools. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsTitle: Where Al Sufouh maths students actually come from
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsIntro: These are the communities that feed Diploma mathematics sets in and around Al Sufouh. Each note is about tutor supply and session timing in that specific place, because those are the two things a location genuinely changes.

regions.name: Al Sufouh 1 and Al Sufouh 2
regions.note: The coastal strip holding Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School, with villa streets behind the main road. Walkable school runs, so a 4.30pm maths session is realistic here in a way it is not further inland. The local AA HL tutor supply is still thin, because supply follows the whole emirate rather than the postcode.

regions.name: Dubai Knowledge Park
regions.note: Apartment blocks and university campuses, with many households where both parents work past five. Diploma students here tend to want a later slot and to want it fixed, because an inconsistent weekly time is what breaks an exploration timetable more often than difficulty does.

regions.name: Al Barsha 1
regions.note: Inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy and Kings' School Al Barsha. Diploma mathematics demand here is substantial, and families from Al Sufouh and Al Barsha regularly end up competing for the same handful of local AA HL tutors.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Compact low-rise communities with Regent International School inside the Greens. Short internal distances make in-home tutoring look efficient, but the people who have actually taught Paper 3 are not distributed by community, so the apparent convenience buys nothing on the scarce courses.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and the Springs
regions.note: Villa districts served by Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, the latter running the Diploma. Generous distances mean an in-home tutor fits two students into an evening at most, which is exactly the constraint that sets the local rate.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Towers immediately west with heavy evening congestion on limited access roads. Diploma students here lose sessions to traffic rather than to unavailability, and a fixed online slot is the simplest fix for a two-year course that depends on continuity.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Internet City
regions.note: Workday-dominated apartment districts on the inland edge. A 4pm start is unrealistic for most households; 6.30pm or later is normal. Online delivery is what makes that time available at all, since a visiting tutor's last booking of the day sets a hard ceiling.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: The Jumeirah side, villa-heavy with a mix of British and IB schools. Travel from here into Al Sufouh crosses two major junctions, and the premium a visiting tutor adds for that crossing is logistics rather than teaching.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the Knowledge Park edge
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside or bordering Al Sufouh. Between them they run the British pathway to A Level and the IB Diploma, which is why a single catchment produces demand for AA HL and for A Level Further Mathematics in the same week. Current programme detail should be confirmed against each school's own KHDA listing.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The nearest large cluster inland, reachable across Sheikh Zayed Road. American and British curricula dominate, with several schools running the IB Diploma alongside their main pathway, so group five mathematics demand here spans AA and AI at both levels.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills and the lakeside communities
schoolClusters.note: Inland of the Greens, drawing from the Springs, the Meadows, the Lakes and Emirates Hills. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is a long-established Diploma school, and students who move into Al Sufouh mid-phase often arrive from these sets.

This is the only format in which Paper 3 gets taught properly, because Paper 3 technique needs months of whole-paper practice rather than a sprint.

The tutor interrogates the topic, questions the mathematics, asks what a reflection would actually say and gives feedback on the student's draft. The tutor does not write it, draft it or edit it to completion, and says so to the student at the outset.

Less efficient per mark than year-round work, and sometimes the only option left.

sections.heading: The four courses behind the phrase "IB maths"
paragraphs: A family asking for an IB maths tutor in Al Sufouh is asking for one of four things, and the four are not substitutes. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the same course at Standard Level, Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level. All four share five topics. None of the four shares a paper structure with another, and the technology assumptions differ in a way that changes how every single lesson is taught.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-calculus route. It carries proof, sequences and series, and a substantial calculus load that deepens considerably at Higher Level. Its Standard Level Paper 1 is sat without technology, which matters enormously for a student who learned every method with a graphic display calculator in hand. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling-and-statistics route, with technology assumed throughout and a broader, shallower content spread that reaches graph theory and voronoi diagrams at Higher Level.

The Higher Level variants of both add Paper 3. One hour, two extended problem-solving questions, twenty per cent of the final grade. It is a different examination from Papers 1 and 2 in character as well as in length: each question builds an unfamiliar idea in stages and expects the candidate to carry part (a) into part (c). A tutor who has not taught it tends to treat it as a harder Paper 2, which is the specific error that leaves students abandoning question two halfway through.

So the first conversation with any prospective tutor should establish the course, the level and whether they have taught that combination through a full cycle. If the answer is vague, the family will spend the first month paying for the tutor's own orientation. That is the real cost of a mismatch, and it is larger than the difference between any two rate bands in this market.
bullets: AA HL, AA SL, AI HL and AI SL are four courses, not four difficulty settings
AA SL Paper 1 is sat without technology; AI assumes technology on both papers
Paper 3 exists at Higher Level only and carries 20 per cent of the grade

sections.heading: Analysis or Applications: the route decision that precedes the tutor decision
paragraphs: Most families in this catchment meet the AA-or-AI question in the spring of Year 11, make it on partial information, and then meet its consequences in Year 12. It is worth separating the two things the decision controls. The first is what the student will enjoy and cope with for two years. The second is what university courses will accept afterwards, and that second one is where the regret usually sits.

Analysis and Approaches is the conventional prerequisite route for mathematics, physics, engineering and most economics degrees that require mathematics, and Higher Level is what the more selective of those ask for. Applications and Interpretation is a legitimate and demanding course that suits students heading towards design, business, social sciences, architecture and many life science routes. It is not a lesser course, but it is not read as equivalent by every admissions office, and the only safe method is to check the stated entry requirements of the specific courses and universities a student is targeting, including the UAE institutions, rather than relying on general advice.

The practical teaching difference is easy to state. AA rewards algebraic fluency and the ability to construct an argument. AI rewards interpretation, modelling choices and saying what a number means. A student who is quick and accurate but dislikes explaining is usually happier in AA; a student who reasons well about context but finds manipulation laborious is usually happier in AI. Higher Level in either course is a serious commitment, and a Standard Level student who copes comfortably is in a better position than a Higher Level student who is drowning.

A route change after the first term of Year 12 is possible at many schools and is never trivial. It means covering missed content in a new course while keeping up with the current one, and it resets the exploration planning. If the question is live in your household, the cheapest intervention available is one diagnostic session on a past paper from each course before the school's deadline, which turns an opinion into evidence.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, paper by paper
paragraphs: The five topics are shared, so a conversation about content is less useful than a conversation about papers. Standard Level is two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty. Higher Level is three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty, plus the exploration at twenty. Paper durations differ between the levels: the Standard Level papers are ninety minutes each, the Higher Level Papers 1 and 2 run two hours each, and Paper 3 runs one hour.

Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is the one families underestimate, because it is sat without technology. A student who has graphed every function on a screen for two years meets a sketching question and produces an outline rather than a sketch with intercepts, asymptotes and turning points identified. Exact-form answers are the other recurring loss: a decimal where a surd or a logarithm was required scores nothing even when the method is perfect.

Paper 2 allows technology, and the losses shift. Students solve numerically where an exact method was expected, present calculator output without the working that earns method marks, or round early and lose accuracy marks at the end. In Applications and Interpretation the equivalent failure is giving a regression equation or a test statistic and never saying what it means in the context of the question, which is the interpretation the paper was built to assess.

Paper 3 at Higher Level has its own failure mode and it is structural rather than mathematical. The two extended questions scaffold deliberately, and part (c) usually depends on part (a). Students who treat each part as independent lose the thread, run out of time and leave the second question largely blank. The remedy is not more topic revision. It is whole papers, sat timed, marked, and then talked through with attention to where the thread was dropped.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion, and the honesty line
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is twenty per cent of the grade at both levels and it is the component where a good tutor adds the most value and where the rules are tightest. It is assessed on five criteria worth twenty marks in total, and the mark allocations are uneven in a way that should shape how a student spends their time. Criterion A, presentation, carries four marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries four. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries three. Criterion D, reflection, carries three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six and is the largest single block.

Reading those allocations changes behaviour. Criterion E being the heaviest means the mathematics has to be genuinely at the level of the course and used correctly, which rules out topics that produce a tour of a subject rather than a piece of work. Criterion D being worth three marks and being the one most often answered badly means a paragraph labelled conclusion does not earn it; reflection means interrogating the method, the limitations and what a different approach would have produced. Criterion A rewards a focused aim and a structure that serves it, not a long introduction.

The honesty line is not negotiable and it is worth stating to the student before any work starts. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and say which ones are likely to cap out. A tutor may question whether a method is appropriate, point at an unjustified step, ask what a result means, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or produce the exploration, and must not edit it until the mathematical voice is no longer the student's. Where a school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it.

This matters in the Dubai market more than it should. One operator in this search landscape advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying that does not transfer the risk to the seller; it places a malpractice exposure on the student, and malpractice findings at Diploma level are not small. A family paying for exploration support should expect a tutor who states this boundary unprompted at the first session.

sections.heading: When a maths session can realistically start in Al Sufouh
paragraphs: Scarcity of specialists is the main argument on this page, but scheduling is what actually ends arrangements. Al Sufouh school days finish somewhere between two o'clock and half past three depending on the school and the phase, and Diploma students usually have commitments after that: a creativity, activity and service obligation, a sports fixture, a subject clinic, or the bus. A session slotted at four o'clock on paper is frequently a session attended on paper.

Geography does the rest. A student living in Al Sufouh 2 and attending a school in the same strip can be at a desk by half past four. A student commuting back to Media City or Internet City, or inland to Al Barsha, is realistically available from six. Households in Dubai Marina and JBR add the evening congestion on the access roads. None of this is exotic; it is simply the reason a fixed weekly time matters more for a two-year course than for a short block.

Online delivery is what makes the later slot available at all. A visiting tutor's day has a hard ceiling set by their previous booking and the drive after it, which is why in-home availability thins sharply after seven. An online slot at seven or eight in the evening, Gulf Standard Time, costs nothing extra to supply, and for a Diploma student juggling six subjects plus the core that flexibility is usually worth more than proximity ever was.

Ramadan reshapes the week for many households here, and it falls in the UAE academic year. School hours shorten, and evening study migrates to after Iftar. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards. Planning that in advance rather than improvising it mid-month protects the exploration timetable, which is the piece of Diploma mathematics most easily derailed by three disrupted weeks.

sections.heading: What a mathematics specialist costs, and why scarcity sets the price
paragraphs: Rates in this market are a function of supply, and nowhere is that clearer than in Diploma mathematics. The people who have taught AA HL through a full cycle and marked Paper 3 responses are a small subset of the people advertising maths tuition in Dubai, and the published bands reflect it at the top end. Read in October 2026, the market splits roughly as follows: budget online tutoring from AED 33 to AED 65, usually delivered by current university students; qualified subject tutors online from AED 150, with Unitors publishing AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB; specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate placing specialist exam-year work in that band; premium named tutors at AED 500 to AED 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500.

Those are the market's figures, attributed to the providers who publish them, and they are not an IB Gram price list. What they show is that the in-home band and the online specialist band overlap almost completely. A family paying AED 300 an hour for a visit and a family paying AED 300 for an online AA HL specialist are spending the same money, and only one of the two has selected for the course.

The scarcity premium behaves differently from the travel premium. Travel is a fixed overhead that produces no teaching, and it vanishes when the lesson runs online. Specialism is the thing you are actually trying to buy, and it is worth paying for precisely because it is rare. The mistake families in this catchment make is paying the top of the in-home band and receiving the middle of the generalist pool, because that is who was free on Tuesday within fifteen minutes of Al Sufouh.

Monthly context, because hourly numbers mislead over a two-year course. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A Diploma family should budget across the whole course rather than per hour, because the exploration period and the final term both need more contact than the middle of Year 12 does.

sections.heading: Verifying the claim: permit, paper and syllabus
paragraphs: Because specialism is what you are buying and specialism is hard to see from an advertisement, verification matters more here than in a general tutoring purchase. Three checks cover most of it, and none of them is difficult.

The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

The second is the paper. Ask a prospective tutor to mark one past Paper 3 response, or one exploration draft section, and to show the markbands they used. This is the fastest way to distinguish somebody who has taught Higher Level from somebody who is competent at mathematics. A tutor who has done it will reach for criteria and markbands without being prompted; a tutor who has not will talk about the mathematics being correct, which is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.

The third is the claim set. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and claims none. Any provider describing itself as approved by one of those bodies should be asked to produce the permit or centre number. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; that is a specific document and it either exists or it does not. Equally, nobody should be described as an IB examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking or boundaries.

sections.heading: Why "near me" stops mattering once the pool opens
paragraphs: The search phrase is a proxy. A parent typing an IB maths tutor in Al Sufouh is not really asking for a neighbour; they are asking for somebody reachable who is competent in this specific course. Proximity is just the only filter a search box offers. Once the delivery format removes distance from the problem, the filter that remains is the one that mattered all along: which of the four courses has this person taught, and can they prove it.

That is why IB Gram states its UAE model plainly rather than burying it. Lessons are one-to-one online over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai and does not dispatch tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is an India-only service. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where delivery actually happens, which is the opposite approach.

What a family in Al Sufouh gains is specific. The AA HL match is made on the course rather than on the drive. The slot can sit at seven in the evening without a tutor's previous booking deciding it. A road closure on Al Sufouh Road does not cancel the session. Session continuity across a two-year course, which is the real variable in Diploma mathematics, stops depending on logistics. And the travel component of the rate, somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour on published bands, is simply absent.

What a family loses is presence, and that loss is real for some students. A fourteen-year-old who will not engage with a screen is a different case from a sixteen-year-old working through Paper 3 questions with a shared whiteboard. For Diploma mathematics specifically, the shared screen is often better than a kitchen table: the past paper, the markscheme, the graphing software and the student's working all sit in one visible place, and the session can be recorded for revision. That is not a consolation; for this subject it is an advantage.

process.title: Name the course and the level, not the subject
process.description: Tell us whether it is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and whether it is Standard or Higher Level. That single sentence is what allows a match to a tutor who has taught that combination rather than to somebody who teaches mathematics in general, and it takes the guesswork out of the first paid hour.

process.title: Send one piece of real work
process.description: A marked school assessment, a past paper attempt or an exploration draft section tells us more than a description of the difficulty does. It shows whether the problem is content, notation, technique or timing, and those four need different tutors and different session structures to fix.

process.title: Use the free trial on the hardest thing
process.description: One lesson, one subject, booked before any payment is taken. Spend it on the topic the student least wants to look at, not on the one they can already do. The point of the trial is to find out whether this tutor can teach this student the difficult part, and that is not visible in a comfortable session.

process.title: Fix the slot around the real school day
process.description: Al Sufouh school days end between two and half past three, and Diploma students have commitments afterwards. Pick a time the student will be functional at rather than the earliest one available. Online slots run into the evening and can move post-Iftar during Ramadan without losing continuity.

process.title: Put the exploration on the calendar in Year 12
process.description: The exploration is twenty per cent of the grade and the component most often left until it collides with everything else. Agree in the first month which weeks will be spent on topic choice, which on the mathematics and which on the draft, and align those with the school's own internal deadlines.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one of four courses, before booking
whyPoints.description: AA HL, AA SL, AI HL and AI SL are separate teaching jobs with different papers and different technology assumptions. The match is made on the course and the level, which is the step that stops a family paying for a tutor's own orientation during the first month of lessons.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own examination
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level third paper carries twenty per cent of the grade and fails students structurally rather than mathematically, because its parts build on each other. It needs whole timed papers over months, not topic revision in a fortnight, and Higher Level matches are made with that in mind.

whyPoints.title: Exploration support that works to the letters
whyPoints.description: Feedback references criteria A to E and their mark allocations rather than general quality. Criterion E carries six marks and criterion D three, and knowing that changes where a student spends their remaining time. The boundary on what a tutor will not do is stated at the first session.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown as the market's, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or research that published it, read in October 2026. Three of six ranking competitors in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family budgets in.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated without hedging
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is offered only in India. That is on this page because a parent should know the delivery model before the first conversation, not after it.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates published that have not been verified
whyPoints.description: Specific IB examination and results dates are not stated on this page, because they could not be confirmed from the IB's own published source at the time of writing. Session planning here is relative rather than dated, and a family should confirm dates with the school's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB maths tutor near me in Al Sufouh who has taught AA HL?
faqs.answer: Within a twenty-minute radius, a few, and fewer than the advertisements suggest. Teaching Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level through a full two-year cycle, marking Paper 3 against the markbands and supervising an exploration from blank page to submission are three distinct competences that most listings collapse into the word maths. Restricting a search to people who can drive to Al Sufouh at your child's free time removes most of them. Online delivery removes the radius instead, so the match is made on the course rather than on the commute.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Maths AA and Maths AI for my child?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, proof and calculus route, with Standard Level Paper 1 sat without technology. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with technology assumed on both papers and content reaching graph theory and voronoi diagrams at Higher Level. Both cover the same five topics at different depths, and both weight the exploration at twenty per cent. The decision that usually matters is university entry: check the stated requirements of the specific courses your child is targeting rather than relying on general advice.

faqs.question: How is IB Mathematics assessed at Higher Level compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Standard Level is two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty, with each paper running ninety minutes. Higher Level is three papers plus the exploration: Papers 1 and 2 at thirty per cent each running two hours apiece, Paper 3 at twenty per cent running one hour, and the exploration at twenty. The exploration therefore carries the same weight at both levels. Paper 3 is the component with no Standard Level equivalent, and it is the one families most often discover late in Year 13.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 need separate preparation from Papers 1 and 2?
faqs.answer: Because it fails students structurally rather than mathematically. Its two extended questions develop an unfamiliar idea in stages, and part (c) usually depends on part (a). A candidate who treats the parts as independent loses the thread, spends too long recovering and leaves the second question largely blank. Topic revision does not fix that. Whole papers sat under timed conditions, marked, and then discussed with attention to where the thread was dropped does. At one hour for twenty per cent of the grade, the return on that practice is high.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths specialist cost in Dubai, and why is it more than general maths?
faqs.answer: Read in October 2026, specialist rates in Dubai run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 for premium named tutors. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted from AED 200 for IB by Unitors. The premium reflects supply: the subset of maths tutors who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is small. Those are market figures from the providers who publish them rather than an IB Gram price list. The travel element of an in-home rate, by contrast, buys no teaching at all.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go on the maths exploration before it stops being the student's work?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a line that should be stated before the work starts. A tutor can discuss candidate topics and say which will cap out, question whether a method suits the level, point at an unjustified step, ask what a result means and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or produce the exploration, and should not edit it until the mathematical voice is no longer the student's. Where the school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it. Nobody else can.

faqs.question: What are the exploration criteria and how many marks does each carry?
faqs.answer: Five criteria for twenty marks in total. Criterion A, presentation, carries four. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries four. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries three. Criterion D, reflection, carries three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six and is the largest block. Those allocations should direct a student's remaining time: criterion E rewards mathematics genuinely at the level of the course, and criterion D rewards interrogating method and limitations rather than writing a paragraph labelled conclusion.

faqs.question: My child is moving from Cambridge 0580 into AA HL. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Procedural technique usually transfers well; three other things do not. The first is pace, because the functions and proof work in the opening terms of Higher Level moves faster than any IGCSE paper. The second is extended independent writing, which IGCSE does not require and the exploration does. The third is non-calculator fluency in exact forms, which a student who graphed everything on a screen has not built. Students arriving from Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics are better prepared for the technology-assisted papers, having assumed a graphic display calculator throughout.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Sufouh Diploma student realistically start a maths session?
faqs.answer: Al Sufouh school days end roughly between two o'clock and half past three depending on the school and the phase, and Diploma students usually have a creativity, activity and service commitment, a clinic or a fixture afterwards. A student walking home within Al Sufouh can be at a desk by half past four. A household commuting back to Media City, Internet City or Al Barsha is realistically available from six. Online slots run into the evening in Gulf Standard Time, which is the main practical reason they survive a two-year course.

faqs.question: Does my child's school decide whether AA HL or AI HL is available?
faqs.answer: Largely, yes. Schools offer the group five options their staffing and cohort support, and not every Diploma school in Dubai runs all four combinations in a given year. Ask the Diploma coordinator directly which courses and levels will run, and whether a block timetable restricts the combination with your child's other subjects. That answer changes the whole plan, and it is better obtained in Year 11 than discovered in September. It is also the question that determines whether a route change is even possible later.

faqs.question: Should one tutor take both AA HL and Physics HL for an Al Sufouh student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it can be efficient where the student's problem is transfer rather than content. A student who differentiates confidently in a maths lesson and cannot read a gradient as a rate in a physics graph has one problem appearing twice, and a tutor who teaches both can close it once. Where either subject is at Higher Level and genuinely weak, two specialists usually beat one generalist. The honest test is whether the person has taught both at the level required, which is a question worth asking plainly.

faqs.question: Do IB maths tutors in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows Higher Level mathematics?
faqs.answer: Ask them to mark one past Paper 3 response or one section of an exploration draft, and to show you the markbands or criteria they used. Somebody who has taught Higher Level reaches for criteria without prompting and talks about where marks were available rather than only about whether the mathematics is correct. Somebody who has not will discuss correctness, which is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. This single test costs one trial lesson and settles the question faster than any credential list.

faqs.question: Will online maths tuition work for a student who prefers a person in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma mathematics it usually works well, and sometimes better. The past paper, the markscheme, the graphing software and the student's own working all sit on one shared screen, which is hard to replicate at a kitchen table, and sessions can be recorded for revision. For a much younger student who will not engage with a screen, presence is a genuine requirement and a local arrangement is the right purchase. IB Gram delivers UAE lessons online only; home visiting is a service offered in India, not here.

faqs.question: When should exploration work start if my child is in Year 12 now?
faqs.answer: Topic exploration should begin well before the school's first internal deadline, because topic choice sets the ceiling on criterion E before a word is written. A workable pattern is a few weeks testing two or three candidate topics against the level of mathematics they would require, then the mathematical work, then the writing, then reflection as a separate pass rather than a final paragraph. Confirm every date with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than with any published general calendar, and build the plan backwards from their deadline.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education required at an IB school in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, including IB Diploma schools, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and any mandatory subject lesson is advised to run at least twenty-five minutes.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB maths tutor in Al Sufouh, the fastest route to a useful answer is three short steps. Tell us whether it is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and whether it is Standard or Higher Level. Send one marked assessment, past paper attempt or exploration draft. Then take the free trial lesson on the hardest topic rather than the comfortable one. One subject, one hour, no payment taken beforehand. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is matched to the course your child actually sits.

intro.heading: Where does maths practice fit into an Al Twar school week?
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where tutoring most often fails for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. A tutor can explain integration by substitution impeccably at eight in the evening, and if the student does not attempt six questions on it within two days the explanation evaporates. Maths is learned in the practice, not in the lesson, and the practice has to have somewhere to live in the week. In Al Twar, where the bus arrives late and the evening is short, that is a scheduling problem before it is a mathematical one.

Start with the clock. Schools serving this cluster finish between roughly 2pm and 3.30pm, and Al Twar sits towards the end of most bus loops, so add thirty to forty-five minutes. Allow for changing, eating and the school's own set work and it is approaching a quarter to five. That leaves an early window of about ninety minutes before the evening meal and a shorter window after it, running to around nine. Families with a school place in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City should assume the early window does not exist at all.

Now place the maths. The lesson wants the earlier window, because new technique needs attention a nine o'clock student does not have. The practice wants the following afternoon, not the same evening, because consolidation works better after a night's sleep than after a long day. And the check on whether the practice worked wants to be the first five minutes of the next session rather than a question asked three weeks later. Set out like that, a weekly maths arrangement becomes a seven-day cycle rather than a one-hour appointment.

The second structural fact to get right early is the route. IB mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at Higher and Standard Level, and the choice shapes two years of work and some university applications. It is made in Year 11 or at the start of DP1, often with limited information, and it is genuinely difficult to change later. We devote a section of this page to it because it is the decision that most affects what tutoring will be needed.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Maths tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for worked algebra, graphs and graphic display calculator work. For a subject whose success depends on holding a weekly rhythm through a term, that reliability is the point: the session starts when it says it will, and a week that goes wrong can be rescheduled rather than lost.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Standard Level is assessed by two written papers and the exploration; Higher Level by three papers and the exploration, with the exploration worth about a fifth of the grade at both levels.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Standard and Extended routes in the later years, assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Only the first of those is the kind of work a conventional maths tutor usually drills.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 gives solid algebra, trigonometry and graph work. Neither covers calculus, formal proof, or the vector and statistics depth that Higher Level assumes from the first weeks.

The honest test is whether algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than merely correct, because Higher Level offers no time to think about it.

programmes.name: The mathematical exploration
programmes.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing, internally assessed and externally moderated, worth about a fifth of the final grade at both levels. Assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Twar consistently resource this last, which is the wrong order given its weight. dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: Maths is usually tutored alongside something, and the overlaps are specific. These are the subjects Al Twar families combine with it and what each one shares.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus, vectors at Higher Level, and formal proof. Marks go in algebraic slips inside otherwise correct methods and in Paper 1 work attempted without the calculator students have come to rely on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, financial mathematics and graph theory at Higher Level, with technology permitted throughout. Lost marks sit in interpretation: a correct regression with no statement of what it means in context earns less than it should.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The closest overlap. Rearrangement, graph gradients, trigonometry and calculus all appear in both, and a physics problem is very often a maths problem the student did not recognise as one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Logarithms for pH, exponentials for rate work and proportional reasoning throughout. A student weak in logs will appear weak in acid-base chemistry, and the correct diagnosis is maths.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram and gradient work, elasticity calculation and data interpretation. Students who are confident in maths often lose economics marks by calculating without explaining what the figure implies.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Break-even analysis, investment appraisal and ratio work. Arithmetic is rarely the problem; stating a judgement from the number is, and that is a writing skill rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking and complexity. The habit of defining each step before computing transfers directly into multi-step maths questions, where most errors are sequencing errors.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Statistical tests, standard deviation and interpretation of error bars. A student who can calculate but cannot say what a result supports is losing biology marks for mathematical reasons.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Often the subject a maths-strong student neglects, and the one whose writing discipline the exploration depends on. A clear argument is assessed in the exploration as well as correct mathematics.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive components, each needing separate practice. Commonly taken alongside maths in this cluster and commonly tutored too generally to help.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay. Mathematics is unusually rich ground here: whether mathematical truth is discovered or invented is a knowledge question a maths student can answer with real examples.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Mathematics
subjects.description: A supervised research essay. Mathematics titles fail on scope more than on difficulty, and the early session that narrows the question is worth more than several later ones on technique.

sections.heading: A maths week that fits the Al Twar afternoon
paragraphs: The ordinary arrangement, a single tutoring hour dropped into whichever evening slot is free, works badly for mathematics specifically. The reason is that the session produces understanding and understanding decays unless it is converted into fluency within a day or two. A student who is taught the chain rule on Tuesday and next touches it on Sunday has to be taught it twice, and the second teaching is billed at the same rate as the first.

So design the week rather than the hour. Put the teaching in the early window, roughly 5pm to 6.30pm, or on Saturday morning if the afternoon is gone. Put the question set on the following day, when the student is fresher and the method is still recent. Keep it short, six to ten questions, because a set that looks like an evening's work does not get started. And open the next session by marking it, which both checks the learning and tells the tutor exactly where to begin.

The practical constraint in Al Twar is the arrival time. Being late on the bus loop costs this district thirty to forty-five minutes relative to the school gate, and families with a cross-district place in Mirdif or Al Garhoud lose the early window entirely. For those households the Saturday pattern is not a compromise; it is the only version that holds for a whole term. The households that struggle most are the ones trying to defend a 5pm weekday slot that the traffic makes unreliable.

The table below sets out the cycle as a week rather than as an appointment. It is the thing we try to agree in the first conversation, before any tutor is matched, because a well-matched tutor in a badly designed week will still produce a disappointing term.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that shapes the next two years, and it is frequently made on reputation rather than on fit. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytical route, built around functions, trigonometry, calculus and formal reasoning, with proof as a visible strand at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistical route, with technology permitted throughout, covering regression, probability distributions, financial mathematics and, at Higher Level, graph theory and more advanced statistics.

Neither is the easier course. They are differently demanding, and students fail in different ways on each. On Analysis and Approaches the common failure is algebraic fluency: a student who can do each step but not quickly enough, and who therefore runs out of time on Paper 1, where technology is not permitted. On Applications and Interpretation the common failure is interpretation: a student who produces a correct statistical result and then does not say what it means in the context of the question, which is where a large share of the marks sit.

For university planning the sensible instruction is to check rather than assume. Many engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees express a preference for Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while a wide range of other courses accept either. Requirements differ between institutions and between faculties within the same institution, and they are revised. Read the course page for the specific universities your child is considering, including UAE institutions, and if the answer is ambiguous write to admissions. Do not let a tutoring page, including this one, be the source of a prerequisite claim.

What the choice means for tutoring is concrete. An Analysis and Approaches student needs volume: enough practice that manipulation becomes automatic rather than merely possible. An Applications and Interpretation student needs calculator fluency and writing practice, because the technology does the computation and the marks are in the explanation. Those are different kinds of session, and a tutor should be able to say which one they are running.

sections.heading: Papers, weightings and where the hour should go
paragraphs: Knowing the assessment shape tells you where tutoring is worth most. Standard Level is assessed by two written papers plus the exploration. Higher Level adds a third paper, shorter than the others, built around extended problem-solving on unfamiliar material. The exploration is worth about a fifth of the grade at both levels, which makes it the largest single assessment object in the course and the one families resource last.

The weightings have a direct consequence. At Standard Level, with two papers of roughly equal weight and the exploration at a fifth, a student who neglects the exploration is capping themselves before they sit a paper. At Higher Level the third paper is both the least familiar and the least practised, because its questions are extended investigations rather than topic exercises and ordinary topic teaching does not build the stamina for them. A Higher Level student who has never completed a full Paper 3 under timed conditions is in for an unpleasant surprise.

Within the papers, the split on technology matters more than most parents realise. On Analysis and Approaches one paper is sat without a calculator, and students who have learned the course with a graphic display calculator permanently in hand find their algebra is slower than they thought. This is a practice problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it responds quickly to being named: a weekly set of calculator-free questions for a term changes performance on that paper measurably.

Confirm the exact weightings and durations against your child's own subject guide or the school's IB coordinator before planning around them. Assessment detail is revised between guides, the IB publishes the authoritative version, and this page would rather be checkable than confident. The table gives the shape as currently taught in this cluster.

sections.heading: The exploration: a fifth of the grade and a deadline that arrives quietly
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is an individual piece of writing in which a student investigates a question of their own choosing, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. It is worth about a fifth of the final grade at both levels and it is marked by the school and moderated externally. Almost every family in this district treats it as a side task until the internal deadline is three weeks away.

The single highest-value intervention comes first and takes one session: turning a topic into a question. A student who announces they will write about cryptography has a subject area, not an exploration. A student who asks whether a specific modular-arithmetic method remains secure under a defined constraint, and can compute something about it, has a piece of work with marks attached. Narrowing that early is worth more than any amount of later help, and it is cheap because it is one conversation.

The second is the use of mathematics itself. Explorations lose marks for being either trivially simple relative to the course level or so ambitious that the student cannot actually do the mathematics they have committed to. A Higher Level exploration that only uses Standard Level technique is self-limiting; one that requires university-level analysis produces a description of mathematics rather than mathematics. A tutor who knows the course can calibrate that in one reading of a plan.

What a tutor may not do is produce it. We will not write, draft, restructure to completion or supply mathematics for an exploration, and any service offering that is selling your child a malpractice risk rather than a shortcut, because the consequence falls on the student and can reach the whole Diploma. Legitimate supervision is questioning the question, pointing out where a claim is not supported by the working, and giving feedback on the student's own draft. We say this to students at the first exploration session rather than leaving it implied.

sections.heading: Where Al Twar maths students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Very little of it is conceptual. The largest single source of lost marks in both routes is algebraic slips inside correct methods: a sign dropped, a bracket not expanded, a fraction inverted. The student understands the question, selects the right approach, and arrives at a wrong number. More teaching does nothing for this. What works is volume with marking, enough practice that the manipulation stops consuming attention, which is why the practice between sessions matters more in maths than in any other subject.

The second is timing, and it is concentrated on the technology-free paper for Analysis and Approaches students. A student who learned the course with a graphic display calculator in hand can do every question on that paper and cannot do them fast enough. The diagnosis is easy and parents rarely hear it, because a tutor who only sees untimed work will report that everything is fine. Timed sets from early in DP1 prevent the discovery happening in a mock.

The third is interpretation, which belongs mostly to Applications and Interpretation students. The calculator produces a regression line, a probability or a financial value, and the answer stops there. The marks are in saying what the figure means for the situation described, with the correct units and an appropriate degree of confidence. This is a writing skill, it is taught rather than absorbed, and it is the most commonly untouched source of easy marks in that route.

The fourth is specific to students arriving from an Indian-curriculum background, which in Al Twar and Al Qusais is a large share of the cohort. That preparation builds impressive computational strength and a habit of complete textbook-style answers. The Diploma rewards something narrower: the method the question asked for, shown clearly enough to award method marks, with no surrounding material. Shifting that habit takes a few weeks of deliberate work and a tutor who recognises it rather than reading it as carelessness.
