dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches children move through several programmes before they reach Diploma maths, and the maths demand changes at each handover. These are the stages that matter for a family planning support, with the specific Dubai detail that applies to each.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics is compulsory: every Diploma candidate takes either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level. That makes maths the one subject no student can avoid, and the one where a route chosen badly in Year 11 follows a student for two years.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a KHDA-inspected market, and KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7% of enrolment. Diploma cohorts are therefore small relative to the British-curriculum majority, which is precisely why a single school rarely has spare capacity in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level when a student needs extra hours.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics in the Middle Years Programme is assessed against four criteria rather than by examination: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students are graded 1-8 per criterion and the totals convert to a 1-7 subject grade. Standard and extended mathematics streams exist in MYP 4 and 5, and the stream a child sits in at fifteen quietly predicts which Diploma course will fit.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools in the Dubailand belt, including Fairgreen International School in the Sustainable City and GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate, run the Middle Years Programme straight into the Diploma. Students arriving in DP1 from that route have strong investigation and communication habits and often a thinner procedural base than an IGCSE cohort, so their first weeks of Higher Level maths need different support.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE, as the route into DP maths
programmes.description: Most Arabian Ranches secondary students sit IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme, because British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment. Extended Mathematics, and in particular Additional Mathematics, is the best single predictor of whether a student will cope with Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. A student who found Extended algebra uncomfortable is being set up to fail by that choice, however good the rest of the report looks.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches runs the British curriculum through to post-16, and several nearby schools offer the Diploma alongside or instead of A Level. Families here are therefore making a real choice at sixteen rather than following a single track, and the maths question is usually the deciding one. Check the post-16 pages of your own school before assuming a route is available.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with mathematics taught through transdisciplinary units rather than as a separate timetabled block in the early years. Number sense, pattern and measurement are developed in context. Parents sometimes read that as mathematically light, which it is not, but it does mean a Primary Years Programme child arriving in a British-curriculum Year 7 can look behind on written method while being ahead on reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: Ranches Primary School and the primary phase at Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches draw from inside the community, while continuum Primary Years Programme provision sits further out towards Dubai Hills Estate and the Sustainable City. Families moving a child between the two at Year 6 or Year 7 should expect a written-method gap that takes a term of short, regular work to close.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches.subjectsIntro: On a maths page the useful subject list is not every Diploma course on offer. It is the courses where mathematics decides the grade. Each entry below names the maths actually demanded and where it bites, so a parent can see whether a maths tutor is the right fix for a grade that is slipping in a different subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route. Proof, functions, trigonometric identities, calculus by hand. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations. Paper 1 bans technology at both levels, which is the single feature that catches students out most often.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route. Data, regression, financial mathematics and technology throughout. Standard Level includes Voronoi diagrams, the chi-squared test for independence and Spearman's rank. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory, non-linear regression and hypothesis testing. Every paper allows a graphic display calculator, which changes how practice has to be structured.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Diploma subject with the highest hidden maths load. Rearranging before substituting, logarithmic linearisation of graphs, propagating uncertainty through a calculation, and vector resolution. Students who lose physics marks on algebra rather than on physics are common, and the fix is a maths fix.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, dilutions, equilibrium constants, Gibbs free energy and pH all sit on index laws and logarithms. A student who cannot handle a negative exponent cleanly will drop marks across every calculation question, and the error will be recorded as a chemistry weakness on the report.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries genuine calculation: elasticities, marginal and average cost curves, the money multiplier. Quantitative questions are where Higher Level economics grades are made and lost, and they are maths questions with economics vocabulary on top.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary and hexadecimal conversion, Boolean logic, recursion and complexity reasoning. The algorithmic thinking rewarded here overlaps heavily with Analysis and Approaches, and students taking both often find each subject makes the other easier.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ratio analysis, break-even, investment appraisal and cash-flow forecasting. The arithmetic is not hard but the interpretation marks depend on getting it right first, so a small percentage slip costs the whole chain of a long-answer question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Statistics decide the data-analysis marks: standard deviation, error bars, correlation and the difference between a significant result and an interesting-looking graph. The internal assessment is where this matters most, and it is often the first place a student meets real statistical reasoning.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Scale, tolerance, material properties and basic stress calculation. Students choose this course expecting it to be practical and then meet quantitative questions in the papers, which is a predictable place for a maths-driven grade drop.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Population models, flow diagrams with quantified inputs and outputs, and data interpretation under time pressure. A popular choice for students who want to limit their maths exposure, and still a course where the numerical questions separate a 5 from a 7.

sections.heading: What a parent in Arabian Ranches is really asking when they search for an IB maths tutor
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Arabian Ranches teaches either Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level, one-to-one over live video. Market rates in Dubai for a genuine International Baccalaureate subject specialist run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour as published by other providers in October 2026. IB Gram delivers these lessons online to Arabian Ranches rather than by sending a tutor to a villa, and the reason is supply rather than cost.

Behind the search there is almost always a specific document. Sometimes it is a DP1 report with a 4 in Higher Level maths and a comment about needing to show more working. Sometimes it is a mock paper with eleven marks out of forty on Paper 1 and a note that the student ran out of time. Sometimes it is an email from the maths teacher about an exploration draft that has no mathematics in it yet. A tutor is useful in proportion to how precisely that document is read, which is why the first session should be spent on evidence rather than on introductions.

The second thing behind the search is a timing problem that is specific to this part of Dubai. Arabian Ranches is a villa community in the Dubailand belt, and the secondary cohort is dispersed across Motor City, Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate and the Sustainable City. A child is rarely home before 15:30, and a tutor crossing the city at that hour is rarely reliable before 18:00. The practical consequence is that the available pool of in-home Diploma maths specialists for this neighbourhood is small, and it shrinks further once you specify Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than maths in general.

That is the honest case for online delivery, and it is worth stating as a trade rather than as a benefit. You give up the physical presence of a person in the room. You gain access to a tutor who teaches your child's exact course, a session that starts on time whatever Al Qudra Road is doing, a shared screen on which a graph can be built and rebuilt in seconds, and a recording of the worked solution to go back to on Thursday night.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that sets the next two years
paragraphs: The two Diploma maths courses are not an easy version and a hard version. They are different subjects that share five syllabus topics. Both run at Standard and Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic method, proof and calculus done by hand; Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, data and technology. Teaching time is 150 hours at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level in both courses, so the difference is in what those hours contain.

The feature that decides most cases is Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches, which permits no technology at either level. Every paper in Applications and Interpretation allows a graphic display calculator. A student who relied on a calculator through Extended IGCSE and who has never practised simplifying a surd or differentiating from first principles without one is walking into a paper worth 40% of a Standard Level grade or 30% of a Higher Level grade with a tool they cannot use. That is not a talent problem, but it does take a term of deliberate work to repair.

The second deciding factor is the Higher Level content. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers including De Moivre's theorem, three-dimensional vectors with lines and planes, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation and differential equations solved by separation of variables and by Euler's method. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, non-linear regression, transition matrices and formal hypothesis testing. A tutor who knows one of those lists well does not automatically know the other, which is why the match has to be to the course rather than to the subject.

The honest advice to an Arabian Ranches family making this choice in Year 11 is to look at the IGCSE evidence rather than at ambition. A student who enjoyed Additional Mathematics, or who scored well on the algebra and calculus-adjacent questions of Extended Mathematics, belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who was strong on statistics, probability and contextual questions and uncomfortable with abstract manipulation belongs in Applications and Interpretation, and will very likely get a better Diploma total there. Course requirements for specific university programmes differ by department, so check the published entry requirements of the actual course before the decision is locked.

sections.heading: The papers, the durations and the weightings, set out properly
paragraphs: Both courses are assessed on written papers plus one internal assessment. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three. The exploration is worth 20% at both levels in both courses, which means a fifth of the grade is decided before the student walks into an examination hall. A great many Diploma families do not know this until DP2, by which point the opportunity to take it seriously has largely gone.

At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each an hour and a half and each carries 40%. At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 are each two hours and carry 30% apiece, and Paper 3 is one hour carrying 20%. Paper 3 is the component most students meet last and prepare least. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions, and it tests something the other papers do not: sustaining a single unfamiliar problem across many parts, where a wrong answer in part (b) poisons parts (c) through (f).

A formula booklet is supplied in every paper. The skill it demands is knowing what is not in it. Students lose marks waiting to find a result they are expected to know, or using a listed formula without recognising which variable in the question maps to which symbol. Working through the booklet deliberately, early in DP2, and annotating it with what each entry is actually for, is twenty minutes that pays back repeatedly.

Calculator discipline is the other recoverable loss. A graphic display calculator is required for Analysis and Approaches Papers 2 and 3 and for every Applications and Interpretation paper. Angle mode left in radians when the question is in degrees, a stored variable from the previous question, and a regression run on the wrong column have all cost students more marks than any topic gap. These are mechanical errors with mechanical fixes, and they are worth checking before the final eight weeks, not during them.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go: method marks, reasoning marks and the words that tell you what to do
paragraphs: Diploma maths mark schemes award marks for method, for accuracy and for reasoning separately. A student who writes only a final answer to a six-mark question and gets it wrong scores zero, where a student who sets up the same question correctly and then slips in arithmetic can score four. Teaching a student to write the setup line before touching the calculator is the single highest-yield habit change available in DP1, and it is almost entirely a habit rather than an ability.

The command terms are instructions with mark-scheme consequences, not stylistic preferences. Show that means the answer is given and the marks are entirely in the derivation, so a student who writes down the given answer scores nothing. Hence means the previous part must be used, and a fresh approach that reaches the same answer can be refused the marks. Hence or otherwise permits any valid method. Justify and determine require a stated reason. Write down signals that no working is expected and that spending four minutes on it is time stolen from a later question.

Topic-level losses are predictable enough to diagnose from one marked paper. In Analysis and Approaches the recurring failures are index and surd manipulation under no-calculator conditions, the chain rule inside a product, trigonometric identities applied in the wrong direction, and integration by substitution where the limits are not transformed. In Applications and Interpretation the recurring failures are interpreting a regression coefficient in context, stating hypotheses in the right form, confusing correlation strength with model suitability, and rounding too early in a financial calculation so that the final figure drifts.

The practical routine that fixes this is unexciting. Sit a paper under timing. Mark it against the published scheme rather than by feel. Write each lost mark against a cause: did not know it, knew it but misread, knew it and ran out of time, arithmetic slip, or no working shown. Then spend the next session on the two largest categories. Three cycles of that in DP2 move more marks than three months of re-teaching content the student already knows.

sections.heading: The maths exploration, criterion by criterion with the marks named
paragraphs: The exploration is a piece of independent written mathematics, recommended at 12 to 20 pages, carrying 20% of the Diploma maths grade at both levels and in both courses. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and almost no commercial tutoring page in this market names a single one of them. Knowing the letters and their mark allocations changes how a student spends their time, because the largest single block of marks is not where most students think it is.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks: the mathematics must be relevant, correct, and commensurate with the level of the course or beyond it. That is the heaviest criterion and the one most often undersold by students who choose an enormous topic and then run only a surface treatment of it. Criterion A, presentation, and criterion B, mathematical communication, carry four marks each. Criterion C, personal engagement, and criterion D, reflection, carry three each. Reflection must be critical rather than descriptive, which in practice means writing about what the mathematics failed to capture, not summarising what was done.

The commonest failure pattern in a Dubai Diploma cohort is a topic that is too large. A student proposes to model traffic flow on Al Qudra Road, collects nothing usable, and writes eleven pages of description with two equations in it. A narrower question with real mathematics in it scores better every time: the optimal angle for a single shot, the cooling curve of one drink in one room, the geometry of one specific roof. Narrowing is the first conversation in any exploration clinic, and it is usually the only one that matters.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and the boundary should be stated plainly. A tutor may teach the mathematics a student needs, discuss whether a question is answerable, ask what a paragraph is trying to say, point out that notation is inconsistent, and explain what a criterion rewards. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or complete any part of the exploration, and may not supply text for the student to adopt. The work must be the student's own, and under International Baccalaureate academic honesty rules anything else puts the whole Diploma at risk.

The number that moves most between models is not the headline hourly rate but what the hour contains. An in-home visit in Dubailand prices the tutor's drive into the hour you pay for, and on a Thursday afternoon crossing from Al Barsha that drive can be forty minutes each way. sections.heading: The Diploma maths year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan Diploma maths is to count backwards from it rather than forwards from September. The table below is deliberately built around who sets each date, because families routinely assume the International Baccalaureate sets the deadline that is actually set by their own school, and then miss it. Exact session and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate and administered through your child's Diploma coordinator; confirm them with the school rather than with any tutoring page, including this one.

The dates that genuinely bind a student are mostly internal. The school sets the exploration topic deadline, the draft deadline and the final submission date, and it sets them months before the examination session because the teacher has to mark and the work has to be uploaded. By the time a family starts worrying about exams in February, the exploration mark is usually already fixed. That is the single most useful thing a DP1 parent in Arabian Ranches can know, and it is the reason the exploration work belongs in DP1.

The mock window, typically January into February of DP2, is the other date worth protecting. Mocks are the only realistic rehearsal of the full paper set under timing, and at Higher Level they are often the first time a student sits Paper 3 for real. A student who treats mocks as a diagnostic rather than as a verdict gets eight to ten weeks of precisely targeted work out of them. A student who treats them as a verdict loses two weeks to demoralisation and then starts late.

Ramadan falls inside the Diploma preparation window in the current cycle, and it changes when revision can actually happen in a UAE household. School hours shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a 17:00 session may need to move to late evening or to the early afternoon. Planning that shift in advance, rather than cancelling four weeks of sessions and resuming in a panic, is one of the quiet advantages of a fixed online slot that can be moved in a day.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, tutor permits and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Three things in this market are worth being blunt about, because competitors are not. The first is academic honesty. Pages in this search sell completed internal assessments. A completed exploration bought from a third party is malpractice under International Baccalaureate rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A tutor teaches the mathematics, questions the reasoning, explains what a criterion rewards and reads what the student has written. A tutor does not write it. Saying so is not a disclaimer; it is the difference between support and a risk to the whole Diploma.

The second is permits. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. Dubai's private schools are regulated by KHDA, which is an authority to understand rather than an endorsement anyone can claim: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate or Cambridge accreditation, and neither do most of the pages implying otherwise.

The third is availability, which nobody in this search discloses. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists are a narrow pool, and demand concentrates in the eight weeks before the May session. There are weeks when no UAE-based tutor for a specific course and level is free at the slot a family needs. When that happens we say so, and the options are an alternative slot, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus over the same live video, or a wait with a date attached. What we do not do is substitute a generalist and describe them as a specialist.

The same transparency applies to delivery. IB Gram does not run a UAE office, and does not offer home visits in the UAE; those are an India-only service. Every Arabian Ranches lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details taken.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should a JESS Arabian Ranches student pick, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Decide on IGCSE evidence rather than on ambition. A student who enjoyed Additional Mathematics, or who scored well on the algebra and manipulation questions in Extended Mathematics, generally belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who was strong on statistics, probability and contextual questions but uncomfortable with abstract algebra will usually score higher in Applications and Interpretation. Check the published entry requirements of the university courses your child is considering, because some engineering, physics and economics departments name Analysis and Approaches specifically, while a growing number accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. Confirm what your own school offers before assuming both courses run at both levels.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Mathematics internal assessment worth at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The exploration is marked out of 20 and carries 20% of the final maths grade, at Higher Level and at Standard Level, in both courses. The 20 marks are split across five criteria: presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, and use of mathematics 6. Use of mathematics is the heaviest single criterion, which is why a narrow topic treated thoroughly beats an ambitious topic treated superficially. Your child's teacher marks it and the International Baccalaureate moderates. Because the school's internal deadline falls months before the examination session, the exploration mark is usually settled before exam revision begins.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 ask for in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level. It lasts one hour, carries 20% of the grade and contains two extended problem-solving questions set in unfamiliar contexts. A graphic display calculator is required. The skill it tests is sustaining one long problem across many parts, where part (a) sets up a structure that parts (b) to (f) depend on. Students who have only practised short exam questions find it disorientating, and most schools cover it late in DP2. A block of six to eight weeks working only Paper 3 style questions under timing is usually the highest-yield single intervention available in the second Diploma year.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose method marks even when the final answer is right?
faqs.answer: Diploma mark schemes award method, accuracy and reasoning marks separately, and a correct answer with no visible working can still forfeit most of them. This is particularly common with calculator papers, where a student types a long expression and writes only the output. The fix is mechanical: write the setup line, with variables defined and the substitution shown, before touching the calculator. It takes about fifteen seconds and protects the majority of the marks on a six-mark question. Command terms matter here too. Show that gives the answer away deliberately, so every mark lives in the derivation and writing the given result scores nothing.

faqs.question: Is a graphic display calculator allowed in every IB maths paper?
faqs.answer: No. Paper 1 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches permits no technology at either level, while Papers 2 and 3 require a graphic display calculator. Every paper in Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation allows one. This single difference catches out more Dubai students than any topic. A child who passed Extended IGCSE with a calculator in hand needs deliberate no-calculator practice on surds, indices, exact trigonometric values and differentiation from first principles, starting in DP1. Leaving it until the mocks means discovering the problem with ten weeks left rather than ten months, which is a far more expensive place to start.

faqs.question: Which Analysis and Approaches topics cause the most trouble in DP2?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Index and surd manipulation under no-calculator conditions, where a weak foundation from IGCSE shows immediately. The chain rule used inside a product or quotient, where students apply one rule and forget the other. Trigonometric identities applied in the wrong direction, because the student has learnt them as facts rather than as tools. Integration by substitution where the limits are not transformed, which costs the final accuracy mark on an otherwise correct solution. At Higher Level, proof by induction and Maclaurin series are the usual additions. All five are diagnosable from one marked paper, which is why the first session should be spent on evidence.

faqs.question: How long should the maths exploration be, and can a tutor write it?
faqs.answer: The recommended length is 12 to 20 pages, and a tutor cannot write any of it. What a tutor may do is teach the mathematics required, discuss whether a research question is answerable in that space, ask what a paragraph is trying to say, point out inconsistent notation, and explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor must not do is draft, restructure or supply text, because the exploration must be the student's own work under International Baccalaureate academic honesty rules. Pages in this market sell completed internal assessments. That is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Analysis and Approaches HL down to SL mid-course?
faqs.answer: It is often possible, it is a school decision rather than a tutoring one, and it has a deadline. The school's Diploma coordinator has to confirm subject levels with the International Baccalaureate well before the examination session, so a change needs to be requested early rather than after the DP2 mocks. The practical consideration is university requirements: some courses name Higher Level mathematics, so check the published entry requirements for the actual course before moving. A term of focused algebra work in DP1 sometimes makes the move unnecessary, which is a better outcome than either dropping down or struggling on.

faqs.question: What does a 7 in IB Mathematics actually require on the papers?
faqs.answer: Grade boundaries are set by the International Baccalaureate for each session and are not fixed in advance, so no tutor can tell you a percentage that converts to a 7, and nobody can promise your child a grade. What is visible is the shape of the work a top grade needs: near-complete method marks because setup lines are always written, confident no-calculator work in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, a Paper 3 technique that survives an unfamiliar context at Higher Level, and an exploration scoring well on use of mathematics. Those four are trainable. Treat any page that promises a specific grade in advance with real scepticism.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB maths tutor cost for a family in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, put generalist online tutors at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, and International Baccalaureate specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, BartyED AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 and price the tutor's drive into your hour. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. IB Gram starts with a free first lesson and a consultation, because the right plan depends on the course, the level and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: What evening session times work with an Al Qudra Road school run?
faqs.answer: Most Arabian Ranches families settle on 17:00 or 17:30 on weekdays. A child at Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches is usually home by about 15:45, which leaves time to eat before a session. Families in Arabian Ranches 2, Mudon, DAMAC Hills and Town Square typically need 17:30 or 18:00 because the run is longer. Saturday mornings work well for intensive blocks in the final weeks before the May session. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the start time depends only on when your child is at a desk, not on when a tutor can cross Dubai.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not usually the same tutor at Higher Level. The two Higher Level syllabuses diverge sharply: one adds proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations, while the other adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, non-linear regression and hypothesis testing. A tutor who is genuinely fluent in one of those lists is not automatically fluent in the other. We match to the exact course and level your child sits. At Standard Level the overlap is larger and a strong tutor can cover both comfortably.

faqs.question: Which UAE universities expect Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by individual departments and change between admission cycles, so the only reliable answer is the published entry requirements on the course page itself. The general pattern is that engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics programmes most often name Analysis and Approaches, while business, design, life-science and social-science routes accept either, with Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level increasingly accepted. Check the specific programme at the specific university before locking a Year 11 decision, and ask your school's university counsellor, who tracks this annually. No tutoring page should be your source for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session should past-paper work start?
faqs.answer: Timed full papers should start about twelve weeks out, and ideally earlier at Higher Level because Paper 3 needs its own practice. The useful pattern is a cycle rather than a count: sit a paper to time, mark it against the published scheme, sort every lost mark by cause, then spend the following session on the two biggest causes. Three complete cycles move more marks than three months of re-teaching familiar content. Before twelve weeks out, the work is content and technique. Papers used too early, before the syllabus is covered, tend to teach discouragement rather than exam craft.

faqs.question: What happens if no Analysis and Approaches HL specialist is free this term?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date, rather than quietly matched to a generalist. Higher Level specialists are a narrow pool and demand concentrates in the weeks before the May session, so there are genuinely weeks when no UAE-based tutor for a specific course and level is available at the slot you want. The options are then an alternative time, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the identical syllabus over the same live video, or a wait with a named start date. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which does not mean they do not have one.

intro.heading: The maths hour has to survive the drive home first
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 has no secondary school inside the gates. Every Diploma student in Casa, Rosa, Palma, Lila, Camelia, Azalea, Reem, Yasmin and Rasha is bussed or driven out, most often to Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha South or the Sustainable City. School days in that catchment end between roughly 15:00 and 15:30. Buses that loop through Dubailand communities put children back inside the gates somewhere between 15:45 and 16:30, and a Year 12 or Year 13 who has sat two double periods and a mock does not arrive ready for calculus.

This is why a search for an IB maths tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 so often ends in a slot that does not work. The obvious booking is 16:15, straight off the bus, because it looks like the gap. It is the worst hour of the day for the kind of maths that matters most. Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches forbids technology: it is pure method, algebraic manipulation and reasoning written out by hand, and it is the thing that goes wrong first when a student is tired. Scheduling it into the lowest-energy ninety minutes of the week is a common and expensive mistake.

The alternative is to stop treating a tutoring session as one undifferentiated hour. Diploma maths work divides into at least four kinds: new content, worked examples with a tutor driving, timed non-calculator practice, and exploration or reflection work. Those four have completely different energy requirements. A tired student can still follow a worked example on a shared screen and ask questions. A tired student cannot produce clean algebra under time pressure, and making them try teaches them that they are bad at it.

So the plan this page argues for is a week rather than a lesson. One substantial mid-week session for content and worked method, placed late enough that the child has eaten; one short weekend slot for timed non-calculator work, placed in the morning when it is actually possible; and exploration work in the holidays and the long gaps, where it belongs. Families here who fix the timetable usually find they need fewer paid hours, not more, because each hour is spent on work the child could actually do at that moment.

IB Gram delivers Diploma Mathematics support to Arabian Ranches 2 one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The practical consequence for this community is that the 16:00 to 17:00 hour, which an in-home tutor loses to Al Qudra Road traffic, stays available to you, and the tutor you get is chosen for having taught your child's course rather than for living three communities over.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-.programmesIntro: Three stages matter for maths in this community: what the Middle Years Programme left behind, which Diploma course the school has already placed your child in, and what the universities they are applying to expect to see.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses, each at Standard and Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches is the proof-and-method route with a non-calculator Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling-and-statistics route where technology is permitted throughout. Both carry a 20% exploration. Content is organised into number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools place students into these courses at the end of Year 11, usually on IGCSE performance and the school's own assessment. By the time a family in Arabian Ranches 2 searches for a tutor, the placement has normally already happened, so the live question is rarely which course but whether the level is survivable and what the deadline is for changing it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight each: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Strong criterion A and weak criterion B is the commonest profile, and it is the profile that predicts trouble in Diploma maths, because investigating patterns is the skill the exploration and Paper 3 both rest on.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving from an MYP school in Dubailand into the Diploma often report a sharp drop in maths marks in DP1 term one. The usual cause is algebraic fluency rather than ability: MYP assessment rewards process and reflection, and the Diploma assumes manipulation that is fast enough to be invisible.

programmes.name: The Year 11 route into Diploma maths
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum students in this catchment arrive from Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher. Neither includes calculus, and neither requires the sustained algebraic work Analysis and Approaches demands in the first term. Additional Mathematics 0606 does, which is why students who took it tend to land in Analysis HL more comfortably.
programmes.countryNote: The gap is specific and closable: index laws and surds at speed, algebraic fractions, completing the square, and the habit of writing a method that another person can follow. Ten to fifteen hours in the summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the cheapest intervention available to a family in Arabian Ranches 2, and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: What the next step expects
programmes.description: Engineering, economics, computer science and the physical sciences generally expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is accepted widely for business, social sciences, design and many health-science routes. Requirements are published per university and per programme and change between admission cycles.
programmes.countryNote: Check the published entry requirement for each named programme rather than relying on a general rule, including for universities inside the UAE. Where a course is ambiguous about which maths it accepts, the admissions office answers in writing, and that written answer is worth more than any tutor's opinion about what is usually accepted.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranches-.subjectsIntro: Diploma maths splits into course, level and component, and a tutoring plan should name all three. The entries below are the units of work a session is actually built from in this community.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Paper 1 at two hours without technology, Paper 2 at two hours with it, each 110 marks and 30% of the grade, plus a one-hour Paper 3 worth 20%. Proof, sequences, complex numbers and the harder calculus are where DP2 students stall. Needs the most weekend time of any maths option in this list.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 at ninety minutes and 80 marks each, 40% apiece, with the same non-calculator rule on Paper 1. The commonest course in this catchment and the one where tired-evening scheduling does the most damage, because almost half the grade is handwritten method under time pressure.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Technology permitted in every paper, with the same two-hour, two-hour, one-hour structure as Analysis HL. Statistics, modelling and the graph-theory content carry the difficulty, and the common failure is treating a calculator as a substitute for setting the problem up correctly.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two ninety-minute papers at 80 marks and 40% each, both with technology. Suits students who reason well in context and manipulate algebra slowly. Sessions here are most productive when built on real data sets rather than textbook exercises, which also makes them easier to run late in the day.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, carrying 20% of the final grade. Twelve to twenty pages is the recommended length. A tutor may teach the mathematics and give feedback on the student's own draft; no tutor may write the exploration.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: One hour, 55 marks, two extended problem-solving questions that build in stages, technology permitted. Students who can do every topic separately still lose heavily here because the paper tests holding a long argument together. It rewards practice on whole past Paper 3s more than any other component in the course.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.description: The specific skills Paper 1 tests and nothing else does: exact values, surd manipulation, algebraic fractions, differentiation and integration by hand, and the discipline of showing a method a marker can follow. Best practised in short timed blocks in the morning, which is a scheduling point as much as a teaching one.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator fluency
subjects.description: Knowing which function to reach for, and reaching for it in seconds rather than in a minute. Solver, regression, numerical integration and distribution functions all save time in Paper 2 and Paper 3. Twenty minutes of deliberate practice a week is worth more than an hour of reading the manual.

subjects.name: Mock-to-final gap work
subjects.description: The programme of work built from a marked January mock script: error categories counted, the two biggest fixed first, and progress measured on timed questions rather than topic tests. This is the single most useful shape for a DP2 family in this community and it needs a marked paper to exist at all.

sections.heading: What this search is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB maths tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 is usually asking two questions at once. The first is whether anyone competent is reachable from this community. The second, less conscious, is whether the week has room for one more commitment. The answer to the first is yes, but not by distance; the answer to the second is yes, but only if the slot is chosen on the basis of what the student can actually do at that hour.

Taking them in order. Diploma Mathematics is taught in Dubai by a reasonable number of specialists, but they are concentrated where the IB schools are, and their free hours are concentrated in the same 16:00 to 19:00 window every family wants. A tutor who is physically near Arabian Ranches 2 and free at your preferred time and has taught your child's specific course and level is a narrow intersection. Widening it is the entire argument for online delivery: the course and level filter stays, and the geography filter goes.

On the week, the useful reframing is to stop asking when is the tutor free and start asking when is my child capable of this particular kind of maths. A DP2 student at 16:15 after a long bus run from Nad Al Sheba can follow a worked integration and ask good questions. The same student cannot sit a timed non-calculator section and produce work that tells anyone anything true. Booking the wrong task into the wrong hour produces two bad outcomes: wasted money, and a child who concludes they are worse at maths than they are.

IB Gram's position on delivery is fixed and worth stating plainly before anything else. Diploma maths support for Arabian Ranches 2 runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer in-home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. What this community gets in exchange is the 16:00 to 17:00 hour back, and a tutor selected for the course your child is sitting.

sections.heading: Which maths task fits which hour of a Dubailand week
paragraphs: Treat the week as a set of slots with different capacities rather than a search for one free hour. The table below is the version this community's travel actually supports, built from finish times between 15:00 and 15:30 and bus arrivals between 15:45 and 16:30. It is not a theory about learning styles; it is an observation that handwritten algebra under time pressure fails first when a student is tired, and that is exactly what Analysis Paper 1 consists of.

The highest-value realisation for most families is that the weekend morning is not a last resort. It is the only hour in the week when a Diploma student in Arabian Ranches 2 can do timed non-calculator work in a state that resembles the exam. A forty-five minute Saturday slot used for one Paper 1 section, marked immediately, does more for an Analysis grade than two tired weekday hours of the same material.

The second realisation concerns the exploration. It is 20% of the grade and it needs continuous, quiet, slightly experimental thinking. Scheduling it into a weekday evening is why so many explorations end up as a tidy write-up of a textbook example rather than something the student actually found interesting. Holidays and the post-examination gap in DP1 are where that work belongs, and planning for it in advance removes the panic that produces weak personal engagement marks.

None of this requires more paid hours. A common outcome of rearranging the week is the same total hours producing noticeably better data, because the student is now being tested when testing means something and taught when teaching is what is needed. Families who fix the timetable before buying more time usually stop buying more time.

sections.heading: Your child's course was chosen in Year 11, and that changes the question
paragraphs: By the time a parent in Arabian Ranches 2 starts looking for help, the school has already placed the student in Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level, usually on IGCSE performance and an internal assessment. Advice written as though the choice were still open is not much use. The live questions are different: is the level survivable, what is the deadline for changing it, and what work closes the gap if it stays.

The level question has a hard edge to it. Moving from Higher to Standard Level inside the same course is an administrative change with a registration deadline attached, set by the IB and administered by the school's Diploma coordinator. It is not a decision a family can make quietly in March of DP2. Any family with real doubts about an HL maths placement should be asking the coordinator for the actual deadline in DP1, not in the final term, because after it passes the only remaining option is to sit the paper.

The gap question is more tractable. A student struggling in Analysis HL is almost never struggling with the HL-only content first. They are struggling with speed: index laws, surds, algebraic fractions and factorising that are not yet automatic, which makes every HL question twice as long and leaves no capacity for the actual difficulty. Fixing fluency looks like going backwards and is the fastest route forward. It is also work that can be done in short bursts, which suits this community's timetable.

For Applications students the equivalent failure is different. Technology is permitted in every paper, so nobody is slowed by arithmetic, and the losses move to problem setup: choosing the right model, defining variables, interpreting a regression output in the context the question actually asked about. That is a thinking skill rather than a fluency one, and it responds well to the longer mid-week slot where a tutor can work through a full question aloud.

sections.heading: The four papers, the calculator line and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Diploma maths assessment is simpler than it looks, and knowing the shape changes how a week gets planned. At Standard Level there are two papers of ninety minutes and 80 marks, each worth 40% of the grade, with the exploration taking the remaining 20%. At Higher Level there are three: two papers of two hours and 110 marks at 30% each, and a one-hour Paper 3 of 55 marks at 20%, with the exploration again at 20%.

The one asymmetry that matters for scheduling is technology. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 forbids a calculator at both levels. Every other paper in both courses permits one. That single rule is why an Analysis student needs protected fresh time for handwritten work and an Applications student does not, and it is the fact most often missed by a tutor who has taught A Level mathematics but not the Diploma.

Paper 3 deserves separate attention because it is where Higher Level grades are quietly lost. Two extended problem-solving questions, built in stages, where part (d) depends on having got part (b) right and the whole thing depends on holding an argument together for twenty-five minutes. Students who can do every topic in isolation still score poorly, because the skill being tested is stamina and structure. The only effective preparation is whole past Paper 3s, worked and marked, which is a weekend job.

The exploration completes the picture at 20% of the grade in every course and level. Twenty marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Personal engagement and reflection are where marks are most commonly thrown away, and they are the two criteria a rushed final-term write-up cannot rescue.

sections.heading: The exploration gets written in three weeks of DP1, usually the wrong three
paragraphs: The exploration is a fifth of the maths grade and it is handled worse than any other component in this catchment, for a reason that is organisational rather than mathematical. Schools set an internal deadline, often in the final term of DP1 or early DP2. Students interpret that as a deadline for starting. The result is a document produced in a fortnight, about a topic chosen because it was available, with reflection sections written after the mathematics rather than during it.

The criteria punish exactly that. Personal engagement asks for evidence that the student cared about and owned the question, which is impossible to fake at the end. Reflection asks for thinking that happened while the work developed, including about what did not work. A student who gathered data, found the first approach failed, tried another and wrote about both has material for those criteria. A student who picked a textbook topic on a Sunday has none.

The practical fix is calendar work, and it suits this community well because it uses time Arabian Ranches 2 families already have: the winter and spring breaks and the gap after DP1 examinations. In those windows a student can genuinely explore - test an idea, abandon it, keep notes. Two or three concentrated sessions with a tutor across those breaks produce a better exploration than eight tired weekday hours in the term the deadline falls.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else in the course, so it is worth being exact. A tutor may teach the mathematics the student needs, explain a technique, point at a flaw in reasoning, ask whether a claim is supported, and comment on a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write the exploration, draft any section of it, or supply text that ends up in the submission. That line is not ours; it is the IB's academic-honesty requirement, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

sections.heading: Why the January mock misleads families in this community
paragraphs: Mock results arrive in January of DP2 and are treated as a prediction. They are better understood as a diagnosis, and reading them as a prediction causes two specific errors in Arabian Ranches 2 households. The first is panic-buying intensity in February at specialist rates, when the actual problem is a two-hour fix. The second is relief at a decent mock grade that was earned on a paper the school marked generously, followed by a worse result in the real session.

What makes a mock useful is the script, not the number. Error categories can be counted on a marked paper in about twenty minutes: arithmetic slips, method marks lost through unwritten working, questions misread, questions not attempted, and genuine content gaps. The proportions tell you what to buy. A script with eleven unwritten-method losses and one content gap does not need a term of teaching; it needs somebody to sit with the student while they rewrite six solutions properly.

The blank-final-questions pattern is the one most often misread as weakness. A student who answers the first two thirds of a paper well and leaves the last questions empty has a pacing problem, and pacing is trainable in short timed blocks. Buying content teaching for a pacing problem is the most common waste of money in a DP2 spring, and it is also demoralising, because the student is being taught things they already know.

This is the point in the two years where the weekend slot earns its place. Timed sections, marked immediately, with the error categories counted each time, give a family real data every week instead of one data point in January. That is also the honest way to decide whether paid support should continue, because the measure is marks on timed work rather than how the lessons felt.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and the maths that has to move
paragraphs: Dubai's academic year carries scheduling realities that a generic tutoring plan ignores. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the usable part of the day moves. For many families in Arabian Ranches 2 the practical session window shifts to after Iftar, and for students who are fasting the morning timed-practice slot becomes considerably less useful than it is for the rest of the year.

The sensible response is to move the type of work rather than cancel the week. Content teaching and worked examples survive a post-Iftar slot perfectly well. Timed non-calculator practice does not, and pretending otherwise produces scripts that measure fasting rather than mathematics. Shifting timed work into the weeks either side, and using the Ramadan weeks for content and exploration progress, keeps the plan intact without producing misleading data.

The second calendar fact is the mandatory UAE subject load, which occupies real timetable space alongside the Diploma. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. KHDA calculates mandatory instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory subject lesson should run under twenty-five minutes.

For a DP student that load competes for exactly the hours a tutoring plan wants. It is also why the holiday windows matter so much here: the terms are fuller than families moving from a UK school expect, and the weeks that look empty on a calendar often are not. Plan the maths year around the school's published calendar, get the Diploma coordinator's internal deadlines in writing, and treat the breaks as working time rather than slack.

sections.heading: What a Diploma maths specialist costs near Arabian Ranches 2, and what travel buys
paragraphs: Start with the question families actually have about in-home tutoring: what does the premium buy. Published Dubai in-home rates run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting ordinary in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car, a journey down Al Qudra Road in evening traffic, and the tutor's time in it.

What that premium genuinely buys is a person in the room. For some students that changes behaviour: a child who will not engage with a screen, or who needs physical proximity to stay on task, is worth paying for it. For a DP2 student working through marked scripts and timed papers, the value is much harder to see, and the cost is the 16:00 to 17:00 hour that the journey consumes at both ends of the day.

The rest of the market ladder, for context: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly figures are easier to budget against: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, while Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 a month for weekly mid-tier support and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

Every number above belongs to whoever published it and is quoted here as the market, not as our price list. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson first, one per student, taken before any payment and with no card details collected at that point, followed by a rate agreed in writing with the shape of the week attached. Where a figure matters to a decision, ask whether it is per hour or per lesson and what it includes, because those two questions resolve most apparent price differences in this market.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches HL is the hardest Diploma maths option to staff in any market, and the 17:30 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time window is the busiest hour of the week. Those two facts collide regularly, and the honest response is to say so rather than to fill the slot. If no Analysis HL specialist is free for your preferred time, we will tell you that, offer the alternatives with the rate attached, and let you decide. Three options usually exist: a different time with the right tutor, a weekend slot, or a specialist whose working hours sit outside the Gulf window.

What we will not do is put an Applications SL tutor in front of an Analysis HL student because the hour was available. The courses differ most in exactly the places HL students struggle - proof, non-calculator method, Paper 3 structure - and a tutor who has not taught those will teach the content competently and prepare the wrong skills. Course and level go on the booking, and they are matched before anything else.

On the legal position, private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit and the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no official fine schedule is published.

One arrangement is ruled out regardless of availability. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So your child's own maths teacher, privately, is not an option we will arrange. Nor does IB Gram hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the licence a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires, because we do not operate premises here.

process.description: Analysis and Approaches HL, Analysis SL, Applications HL or Applications SL. Four different jobs behind one word. The non-calculator Paper 1 exists only in Analysis, and Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, so the match starts here rather than with availability.

process.title: Send the bus arrival time, not the school finish time
process.description: A 15:15 finish in Motor City can mean a 16:20 arrival in Camelia. We plan the slot from when your child is actually home and fed, which is why so many families end up with a 17:30 weekday session and a short weekend morning one.

process.title: Send the last marked maths paper
process.description: A mock script with a teacher's marks on it lets a tutor count error categories before the first lesson: arithmetic slips, unwritten method, misread questions, blanks and genuine gaps. That count decides the first four sessions far better than a conversation about topics does.

process.title: Take the free trial and agree the week
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, before any payment and with no card details taken. It ends with a written plan: which slot carries content, which carries timed work, when exploration time is blocked out, and what progress by session four would look like.

process.title: Measure on timed work, review at six
process.description: Progress is counted on timed questions marked against the real criteria, not on how a lesson felt. At session six we look at the numbers together, change tutor if the match is wrong, and say plainly if the remaining problem is pacing, sleep or workload rather than mathematics.

whyPoints.title: The 16:00 hour stays yours
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor spends the start and end of your evening in traffic between the city and Dubailand, and the rate carries it. Online delivery returns the window that an Arabian Ranches 2 family loses to the school run at both ends, which in a DP2 spring is the scarcest resource in the house.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and level first
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Applications diverge most exactly where students struggle: proof and non-calculator method in one, modelling and interpretation in the other. We match on the course and level printed on your child's timetable before we look at who happens to be free.

whyPoints.title: Slots planned around capacity, not availability
whyPoints.description: Timed non-calculator work goes into a fresh weekend morning. Content and worked method go into the late weekday slot. Exploration work goes into the breaks. The same number of paid hours produces better data when each hour carries work the student can actually do.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the exploration
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the mathematics, questions the reasoning and comments on the student's own draft. No part of a submitted exploration is written or supplied by us. That boundary is the IB's, the consequence of crossing it lands on the student, and we would rather lose the booking than blur it.

whyPoints.title: Published rates, named sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, Unitors, TutorChase, EdFlik, Tutopiya, BartyED. Three of six competitor pages measured for this project published no rate at all, which makes a sourced band more useful than any claim about value.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: Analysis HL at 18:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest intersection in this market. When it is not available we say so and give you the alternatives with rates, rather than filling the slot with a tutor who has taught a different course.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session realistically start for a student living in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Plan from the bus, not the bell. Schools this community feeds finish between roughly 15:00 and 15:30, and Dubailand bus loops put students back inside the gates between 15:45 and 16:30. A 17:30 or 18:00 start is the reliable weekday window: fed, settled, and still capable of new content. The 16:15 slot that looks like the obvious gap is the one to avoid, particularly for Analysis Paper 1 work, because handwritten method under time pressure is the first thing to fail in a tired student.

faqs.question: When should my child do timed non-calculator maths practice if evenings are this tight?
faqs.answer: Weekend mornings, and nowhere else. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 forbids a calculator at both levels and is worth 40% of a Standard Level grade or 30% at Higher. It tests exact values, surd work and handwritten method under time, which is exactly what a tired student cannot produce after a long bus run. A forty-five minute Saturday or Sunday morning slot with one timed section, marked immediately afterwards, generates more usable information than two weekday hours on the same material.

faqs.question: Does my child's maths course have a paper without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Only if they are taking Analysis and Approaches. In that course Paper 1 forbids technology at both Standard and Higher Level, while Paper 2 permits it. In Applications and Interpretation, technology is permitted in every paper at both levels. This single difference should change how the week is organised: an Analysis student needs protected fresh time for handwritten work, an Applications student needs longer sessions for problem setup and interpretation. A tutor who cannot state this rule has not taught the course.

faqs.question: How are the Diploma maths papers weighted at each level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level there are two papers of one hour thirty minutes and 80 marks each, worth 40% apiece, with the exploration taking the final 20%. At Higher Level there are three papers: Paper 1 and Paper 2 at two hours and 110 marks each, worth 30% each, and Paper 3 at one hour and 55 marks, worth 20%, again with a 20% exploration. Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and consists of two extended problem-solving questions that build in stages.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well on topic tests but badly on Paper 3?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 3 is not testing topics. It sets two extended questions in which later parts depend on earlier ones, over one hour and 55 marks, so the skill being measured is holding an argument together for twenty-five minutes without losing the thread. A student can know every topic and still score poorly. The only effective preparation is whole past Paper 3s, worked under time and marked properly, which makes it weekend work rather than something to attempt at 19:30 on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Can we move my child from Higher Level maths down to Standard Level mid-course?
faqs.answer: It is possible, but it is an administrative change with a registration deadline attached, set by the IB and handled by the school's Diploma coordinator. The mistake families in this community make is leaving the conversation until DP2, by which point the deadline may have passed and the only remaining option is to sit the paper. If there is genuine doubt about a Higher Level maths placement, ask the coordinator for the actual deadline in DP1 and get the answer in writing.

faqs.question: My child was strong at IGCSE maths and is struggling in DP1. What changed?
faqs.answer: Usually speed rather than ability. Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher contain no calculus and do not require the sustained algebraic work the Diploma assumes from term one. Index laws, surds, algebraic fractions and completing the square need to be automatic; when they are merely known, every Diploma question takes twice as long and there is no capacity left for the part that is genuinely hard. Fixing fluency feels like going backwards and is the fastest route forward.

faqs.question: How should I read my child's January mock maths script rather than the grade?
faqs.answer: Count error categories instead of reading the number. On a marked paper you can usually sort losses in twenty minutes into arithmetic slips, method marks lost because working was not written, questions misread, questions left blank, and genuine content gaps. The proportions tell you what to buy. Eleven unwritten-method losses and one content gap does not need a term of teaching; it needs somebody sitting with the student while six solutions get rewritten properly.

faqs.question: My child leaves the last maths questions blank. Is that a knowledge problem?
faqs.answer: Rarely. A paper answered well for two thirds and then abandoned is usually a pacing problem, and pacing is trainable in short timed blocks rather than through more content teaching. Buying weekly content lessons for a pacing issue is a common and demoralising waste, because the student spends the hour being taught things they already know. Check the script for whether the abandoned questions were hard or simply late in the paper, and treat those two findings very differently.

faqs.question: When should the maths exploration actually be started and worked on?
faqs.answer: In DP1, during the breaks, long before the school's internal deadline. The exploration carries 20% of the grade across five criteria, and two of them, personal engagement and reflection, reward thinking that happened while the work developed. A student who tested an idea in the winter break, found it did not work and tried another has evidence for both. A student who began a fortnight before submission has a tidy write-up and no engagement marks. Holidays and the DP1 post-examination gap are the right windows.

faqs.question: Exactly what can a tutor do on my child's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the mathematics involved, explain a technique, point out that a claim is unsupported, ask whether the data actually shows what the student says it shows, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor may write the exploration, draft any part of it, or provide text that ends up in the submission. The boundary is the IB's academic-honesty requirement rather than a company policy, and the consequences of crossing it fall on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change when maths tutoring should happen in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful change is to the type of work rather than the amount. School hours shorten and for many families in this community the practical session window moves to after Iftar. Content teaching and tutor-led worked examples run perfectly well in that slot. Timed non-calculator practice does not, particularly for a student who is fasting, because the resulting script measures fatigue rather than mathematics. Move timed work into the weeks either side and use the Ramadan weeks for content and exploration progress.

faqs.question: How much does an online Diploma maths specialist cost compared with one who visits?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures, October 2026: qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. The in-home premium pays for the drive, not better teaching. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so no travel line appears in a rate we quote.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children if they are in different maths courses?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is worth asking, because a tutor who has taught both Analysis and Applications is common enough. What does not work is a shared session: an Analysis HL student and an Applications SL student need different hours doing different work, and splitting one hour gives each of them half a lesson. Two consecutive short slots with the same tutor usually suits families in Rosa and Lila better than a shared hour, and it keeps the reporting separate for each child.

faqs.question: What happens if no Analysis and Approaches HL tutor is free at our preferred time?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and give you the real alternatives with their rates: a different weekday slot with the right specialist, a weekend morning slot, or a tutor whose working hours sit outside the Gulf evening peak. What we will not do is give an Analysis HL student a tutor who has taught Applications SL because the hour was available. The courses differ most precisely where Higher Level students struggle, so course and level are matched before the time slot is.
